title: reset.sh's limactl delete --force never kills the hostagent process — orphaned hostagent squats on the kubelet port for hours across multiple resets (root cause of BadSignature failures)
description:
scripts/conformance/reset.sh:129, teardown_vm():

  echo "[reset] Deleting $vm VM (full disk wipe) ..."
  limactl delete --force "$vm" 2>/dev/null || true

stderr is silenced and any failure is unconditionally swallowed by '|| true'. If 'limactl delete --force' fails (VM busy, held mount, hung hostagent, etc.), the echo line still prints as if it succeeded, and the OLD VM is left completely intact — including its kubelet's existing TLS serving certificate. Meanwhile step 2 (host state wipe, lines 100-105) unconditionally removes $WORKDIR, so the next run regenerates a FRESH cluster CA (ca.key/ca.crt) independent of whether the VM teardown actually happened. If lima-start.sh's subsequent provisioning then detects the VM already exists and reuses it rather than recreating it, the result is a kubelet serving a certificate signed by a now-defunct prior CA key, verified against the new run's CA.

CONFIRMED via live forensics on a run started 2026-08-03 ~10:34 UTC (operator-initiated re-run, --reset --extra-node lima-node-3):
- lima-node kubelet cert (openssl s_client 127.0.0.1:10250 -showcerts): notBefore=Aug 3 07:06:39 2026 (3.5h before this run's provisioning)
- lima-node-3 kubelet cert (127.0.0.1:10261): notBefore=Aug 3 10:40:04 2026 (matches this run's provisioning exactly)
- openssl verify -CAfile temp/u7s/ca.crt against lima-node's cert: 'certificate signature failure' (exact match to the apiserver's repeated 'invalid peer certificate: BadSignature' — 438+ occurrences and counting in this run's apiserver.log)
- openssl verify against lima-node-3's cert: OK

This is 100% deterministic per-node, not load/concurrency-dependent: every exec/log call routed to lima-node's kubelet fails identically; every call to lima-node-3 succeeds. In a 2-node run with pods scheduled roughly evenly, this alone explains a large, non-flaky fraction of kubelet-exec/log-dependent conformance test failures (see mayor-6pygt, now corrected/retitled — originally misdiagnosed as a load-dependent apiserver TLS-dial reliability bug; the apiserver's rejection of the mismatched cert is CORRECT behavior, not a bug).

Also plausibly explains part of the earlier 157-failure regression (mayor-rqqee, temp/e2e/0803-1011-conformance) though that run's VM has since been re-reset so its specific cert timestamps can no longer be directly checked — the mechanism is identical (same reset.sh, same swallowed-failure pattern) and worth treating as the leading explanation pending any contradicting evidence.

Fix direction: teardown_vm() must fail loud (Rule 12) rather than swallow the delete failure. Options: (a) remove '|| true', let 'set -euo pipefail' (line 20) abort the whole reset on a real delete failure — simplest, matches project's fail-loud stance; (b) after delete, verify via 'limactl list' that the VM is actually gone before proceeding, retry once, then fail loud if still present — more robust against transient delete flakiness (e.g. a busy hostagent) but more code. Given Rule 2 (simplicity), lean (a) unless delete failures are known to be transiently self-resolving (unconfirmed — no evidence either way yet).

Regression test: scripts/conformance/ has existing shell-level tests per test-watchdog-logic.sh precedent — a fix here should include a test exercising teardown_vm with a mocked/stubbed 'limactl' that returns nonzero on delete, asserting the script now exits nonzero instead of proceeding silently.
notes:
DEFINITIVE ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED 2026-08-03 (operator-driven diagnosis via interrupted.log + live process forensics):

lsof -nP -iTCP:10250 -sTCP:LISTEN shows PID 60703 (limactl hostagent ... lima-node) holds the listen socket, started 12:47:36 PM local (elapsed 7h12m at time of check), reparented to launchd (PID 1) -- a fully orphaned process, disconnected from Lima's own bookkeeping (its own ha.pid/vz.pid entries were silently overwritten by a NEWER hostagent, PID 30695, spawned by the current run's provisioning -- confirmed via 'cat ~/.lima/lima-node/ha.pid' returning 30695, not 60703).

Mechanism, fully confirmed: 'limactl delete --force lima-node' in teardown_vm() updates Lima's instance state/config enough that a subsequent 'limactl start' creates a genuinely fresh disk+guest+kubelet-cert every time (confirmed via temp/e2e/interrupted.log showing legitimate 'Provisioning VM lima-node (first run, takes ~5 min)' full boot + 'Kubelet serving cert generated' for the run that was just aborted) -- but it does NOT reliably terminate the underlying hostagent OS process. That process just keeps running, orphaned, still bound to 127.0.0.1:10250 via its own now-stale guest. Every apiserver dial to 127.0.0.1:10250 (exec/log/attach proxy calls only -- NOT general API/watch traffic, which explains why failures were narrowly concentrated on kubelet-exec/log tests and nothing else) has been hitting this same zombie for at least 7+ hours across multiple --reset cycles (confirmed run #1 ~09:18 UTC and run #2 ~10:34 UTC both affected). The freshly-provisioned guest from each run is fully joined and healthy -- it is simply never reachable on that port because the zombie already won the bind.

Separate, secondary bug also visible in interrupted.log: teardown_vm()'s in-VM 'limactl shell $vm pkill -f kubelet' etc. fail with 'Operation not permitted' -- these run as the unprivileged 'lima' user against root-owned processes, missing 'sudo'. Real bug, but does not explain the port-11250 zombie (that's host-side, not guest-side); worth fixing in the same pass since it's the same function.

CONCRETE FIX, now well-scoped (no further reproduction needed -- mechanism is proven, not hypothesized):
1. In teardown_vm(), after 'limactl delete --force $vm', explicitly find and kill any lingering 'limactl hostagent ... $vm' process by argument match (e.g. pgrep -f "limactl hostagent.*--socket .*/$vm/ha.sock" or similar unambiguous match on the vm name) and SIGKILL it if found -- do not trust limactl's own delete to have handled it.
2. Verify port liberation: after cleanup, confirm nothing is LISTENing on the VM's forwarded kubelet port (lsof -nP -iTCP:$port -sTCP:LISTEN) before declaring reset complete; fail loud if still occupied.
3. Add 'sudo' to the in-VM pkill commands (kubelet/kube-controller-manager/sonobuoy all run as root).
4. Remove blanket '2>/dev/null || true' from the delete line -- surface real failures now that the actual cleanup is verified rather than assumed.

Regression test: a script-level test (matching test-watchdog-logic.sh precedent) that stubs 'limactl hostagent' as a long-running dummy process, runs teardown_vm() against it, and asserts the dummy process is actually dead afterward -- not just that the function returned 0.

title: fix(conformance): namespace stuck in terminating — svc-latency hang blocks full conformance run
description:
A full conformance run started 2026-06-11 14:26 UTC hung indefinitely (8+ hours). The svc-latency-6252 namespace is still present and stuck Terminating in the cluster after the run was aborted. This blocks every future full conformance run from completing — sonobuoy waits for namespace cleanup before reporting results.

Root cause hypothesis: the Service or Endpoint object in the svc-latency namespace has a stuck finalizer, or the namespace controller's drain logic is not completing (similar to prior teardown hangs fixed in #508). The namespace DELETE handler must drain all objects and clear the namespace finalizer; if any subresource (e.g. Endpoints, Service with finalizer, or a watch stream that never closes) blocks the drain, the namespace stays Terminating forever.

Observed: namespace svc-latency-6252 present in cluster after 8+ hour hang. No log output from the svc-latency test in temp/e2e-job-c77fffa5.log — sonobuoy was blocked waiting when log was extracted.

Acceptance criteria: a full conformance run (or focused run covering sig-network Services) completes without hanging; the svc-latency namespace is fully deleted within 2 minutes of test teardown.
notes:
Root cause: 3 of 201 services never got EndpointSlices. KCM EPS controller POSTed their EPS (tracker recorded it) but the ADDED watch event was never delivered back to the KCM's global EPS watch stream. After 15 retries at up to 1000s backoff the controller gave up (StaleSlices check). Test watches endpointslices waiting for all 201 ready endpoints — never completes. Watch event delivery miss under burst load (249 rapid EPS creates) is the root cause. Fix: reliable watch event delivery — likely same channel-buffer issue as mayor-p97u.
PR #515 merged: global bookmark race fixed. Rebuild and rerun svc-latency to confirm.
close_reason: svc-latency conformance test passes 20/20 after PR #515 + #516 (watch dedup race fixes). No services missing EndpointSlices.

title: SqliteStore::push_event_locked global-bookmark broadcast is #1 allocation site (694MB/5.80% of 11.95GB in 0810-0107 run); design fan-out reduction that preserves KCM EnsureReady contract
description:
## Summary

`SqliteStore::push_event_locked` (crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:257-276) sends TWO broadcast messages on the shared `tx` channel per write: the specific event, then unconditionally a global bookmark (key="") delivered to EVERY open watch stream regardless of resource-type prefix. This unconditional global fan-out is now the **single largest allocation site in the whole apiserver**.

## Evidence

dhat 0810-0107 conformance run, sorted by total bytes: `push_event_locked`'s global-bookmark send resolves to **694 MB / 4.58M blocks / 5.80% of total 11.95 GB** across ~1,877 calls/sec sustained over 40.67 min.

This ALSO explains why `h2`/`hyper` (+6.33pp) and `rustls` (+2.58pp) category shares grew vs the 08-06 baseline: their top allocation sites all resolve to the same `ndjson_bookmark`/`ndjson_event_value`/`Bytes::from(Vec<u8>)` fan-out, not three independent issues.

Every watcher with `allowWatchBookmarks=true` materializes the bookmark into `ndjson_bookmark()` (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs:1209-1230).

## Why it exists

The doc comment at sqlite.rs:258-262 explains: the global bookmark advances all informers' sync RVs to meet KCM's `EnsureReady()` cross-resource-RV contract. Removing it wholesale would break that contract.

## Open design question

Can the global bookmark be **throttled or coalesced per shard** while still meeting KCM's cross-resource-RV contract? Options to explore:
- Coalesce at emit time (e.g. rate-limit to N/sec globally, latest-wins)
- Coalesce at receive time (per-watcher debounce; risk: increases informer sync latency)
- Emit only when a shard's revision moves relative to global revision (needs shard-aware bookmark tracking)

Requires a scout to prototype and measure — scout does NOT ship a fix, just quantifies which option preserves the EnsureReady contract at least cost. Findings-doc-first.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT delete the global bookmark unconditionally. KCM EnsureReady must remain met.
- Do NOT couple this to mayor-drs2a's ring/deletion_log sharding directly — sharding those does not reduce this fan-out cost. Separate axis.
- Do NOT reduce watcher-side allocation by removing the bookmark encoding; that's a downstream symptom.

## Cross-refs

- mayor-drs2a — ring/deletion_log sharding. Complementary but NOT overlapping. This bead's fan-out will remain after drs2a ships.
- memory-management-state.md — this bead is the currently-#1 allocation site.
- Evidence source: mayor-ddcyx audit (closed) findings ai/findings/memory-audit-2026-08-10-run.md

title: refactor(apiserver): add OwnerReference typed struct + type-migrate GC cascade-delete and generic LIST/CRUD envelope (child of mayor-0bd14)
description:
PARENT: mayor-0bd14 (typed-struct EPIC). Findings: ai/findings/typed-migration-scout-2026-08-10.md, Group B.

PREREQUISITE FINDING: ObjectMeta (types.rs:439-476) has NO ownerReferences field at all (grep-verified: zero hits of ownerReferences/OwnerReference in types.rs besides a comment). This is a live landmine: handlers/cr.rs:516-540 (stamp_cr_fields) has to manually `let saved_owner_refs = obj["metadata"]["ownerReferences"].clone()` BEFORE converting to ObjectMeta and restore it AFTER, specifically because ObjectMeta would silently drop the field otherwise.

SITES (file:line):
- types.rs:439-476 ObjectMeta -- missing ownerReferences field (add here first)
- resource.rs:3302-3360 strip_or_delete_dependent -- reads/filters/writes obj["metadata"]["ownerReferences"] array by .uid for GC cascade-delete. Doc comment at 3290-3301 explicitly warns: "a foreground/background cascade... silently destroys still-owned dependents" if the live-owner check is wrong.
- generic.rs:550-582 build_list_response -- kind/apiVersion/metadata.resourceVersion/continue/remainingItemCount envelope
- generic.rs:586-612 apply_delete_policy -- finalizers/deletionTimestamp/status.phase
- generic.rs:614+ stamp_metadata -- uid/creationTimestamp

REASONING VERB: mutate (envelope stamping) + dispatch (GC: strip-reference-vs-hard-delete decision).

TYPE SHAPE: add `pub owner_references: Option<Vec<OwnerReference>>` to ObjectMeta, with a new `OwnerReference { api_version, kind, name, uid, controller: Option<bool>, block_owner_deletion: Option<bool> }` (matches upstream 1:1, no `rest` needed -- it's a closed upstream type). This removes the cr.rs save/restore workaround entirely (see sibling bead for cr.rs migration, sequenced after this one) and lets strip_or_delete_dependent operate on meta.owner_references instead of indexing.

ALLOCATION COST (dhat 0810-0107 run, u7s-attributed frames, floor not ceiling): build_list_response 46,250,837 B/1,327,416 blk + list_resource closures 61,104,874 B/877,542 blk + delete_collection_namespaced_resource closures 34,663,208 B/419,430 blk + list_pods closures 39,264,438 B/679,155 blk + core_list_resource closure 18,382,857 B/229,382 blk + create_namespaced_resource closure 11,203,408 B/68,674 blk = ~210.9MB / 3.60M blocks (1.76% / 4.28% of total run). types::Object::from_bytes itself (shared root helper feeding this and other groups) adds 53,220,583 B/551,443 blk indirectly.

CORRECTNESS RISK: HIGH -- this is the garbage-collector cascade-delete path. A silently-dropped or mis-filtered ownerReferences entry is a DATA-LOSS class bug (orphan or premature-delete a resource), not cosmetic. The cr.rs workaround proves the current ObjectMeta gap is already a live landmine other code has to route around.

MIGRATION RISK: must confirm no caller relies on ownerReferences entries with fields upstream doesn't define (CRD-authored owner refs are still standard shape, low risk); confirm `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` keeps wire format identical when absent.

TEST HOOKS: fail-on-revert -- round-trip a Pod with 2 ownerReferences (one Job, one ReplicaSet) through ObjectMeta directly (not just via the handler) and assert both survive; existing GC cascade-delete conformance coverage should start failing if the field silently vanishes during migration.

EST LOC: ~250-350 (new struct + 3 files' worth of callsite updates).

SEQUENCING: this bead's ObjectMeta.owner_references addition is a prerequisite for the CR envelope migration bead (Group F in the findings doc) -- file/dispatch that one after this lands.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1079. Added OwnerReference typed struct + ObjectMeta.owner_references field. Migrated resource.rs::strip_or_delete_dependent (GC cascade-delete) and generic.rs::{build_list_response,apply_delete_policy,stamp_metadata} envelope stamping to operate on typed views. Round-trip + GC-cascade + LIST-envelope + wire-format-identity tests fail-on-revert verified. mayor-0bd14.6 (CR envelope) is now unblocked — cr.rs workaround can be removed in that follow-up.

title: refactor(watch): type-migrate watch event stamping & PartialObjectMetadata projection (child of mayor-0bd14)
description:
PARENT: mayor-0bd14 (typed-struct EPIC). Findings: ai/findings/typed-migration-scout-2026-08-10.md, Group A.

SITES (file:line):
- handlers/watch.rs:124-151 prepare_live_event (label/field-selector match on raw Value)
- handlers/watch.rs:155-161 to_partial_object_metadata (GC metadata-only projection)
- handlers/watch.rs:168-177 finish_deleted_event (resourceVersion/apiVersion/kind stamp on tombstones)
- handlers/watch.rs:189-278 encode_watch_event (ADDED/MODIFIED/DELETED/BOOKMARK dispatch; re-stamps apiVersion/kind unconditionally -- in-code comment documents a real historical wedge bug: an object stored without TypeMeta makes client-go's watch decoder fail and RetryWatcher loop forever)
- handlers/watch.rs:301+ fetch_initial_events (sendInitialEvents snapshot-to-ADDED-events conversion)

REASONING VERB: filter-watch (label/field selector) + mutate (resourceVersion/apiVersion/kind stamp, metadata-only projection).

TYPE SHAPE: reuse existing ObjectMeta/TypeMeta-equivalent for to_partial_object_metadata and finish_deleted_event's stamping (currently obj["metadata"]["resourceVersion"] = ... raw-indexed). Selector matching (object_matches_label_selector/object_matches_field_selector) stays Value-based -- it must match against arbitrary field-selector paths across arbitrary kinds, a generic capability. Do not attempt to type that part.

ALLOCATION COST (dhat 0810-0107 run, u7s-attributed frames only -- floor not ceiling, see findings doc caveat on depth-truncation): watch_generic_impl closures 160,736,254 B/2,013,238 blk + prepare_live_event 108,686,707 B/1,342,379 blk + to_partial_object_metadata 13,336,469 B/184,672 blk + fetch_initial_events closure 14,562,456 B/138,734 blk = ~297.3MB / 3.68M blocks (2.49% / 4.37% of total run tb/tbk).

CORRECTNESS RISK: HIGH -- this is the exact mechanism that has already caused one documented client-go-decode wedge bug (comment at watch.rs:238-249); selector-match drift silently breaks watch filtering (a client stops receiving events it should get, or receives events it shouldn't).

MIGRATION RISK: encode_watch_event's stamping must remain unconditional (per its own comment) regardless of typed vs raw implementation -- do not accidentally make it conditional during migration.

TEST HOOKS: a fail-on-revert test constructing a stored object missing apiVersion/kind (the documented historical trigger) and asserting the emitted DELETED event still carries both, would have caught the original bug; add equivalent fail-on-revert tests for ADDED/MODIFIED stamping (currently only forward-asserting).

EST LOC: ~150-200.

NON-GOALS: do not touch object_matches_label_selector/object_matches_field_selector's generic Value-based matching logic itself -- only the stamping/projection call sites around them.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1080. Migrated watch event stamping (encode_watch_event's fallback/synthetic-DELETE tombstone construction via a new build_tombstone_object helper, finish_deleted_event's resourceVersion patch, prepare_live_event/finish_live_event's live ADDED/MODIFIED stamp path) and PartialObjectMetadata projection (to_partial_object_metadata) to typed ObjectMeta-backed envelope structs. Selector-match logic (object_matches_label_selector/object_matches_field_selector) left Value-based per non-goal. Pre-existing historical-wedge regression test (deleted_watch_event_stamps_api_version_and_kind_when_stored_body_lacks_them) already covered the DELETED path; added its ADDED/MODIFIED live-path counterparts (prepare_live_event_added_/_modified_stamps_api_version_and_kind_when_stored_body_lacks_them) plus a PartialObjectMetadata projection round-trip test (to_partial_object_metadata_projects_metadata_only_and_drops_spec_status). Unconditional-stamping invariant on encode_watch_event's DELETED path confirmed preserved. Fail-on-revert verified for all 3 tests (reverted each invariant, confirmed red, restored, confirmed green). Deliberately kept to_partial_object_metadata's metadata field as an opaque Value passthrough rather than a full ObjectMeta round-trip, since ObjectMeta does not yet model ownerReferences (landing in parallel via mayor-0bd14.2) and a full round-trip would silently drop it, breaking GC.

title: scheduler doesn't enforce PV spec.nodeAffinity when filtering nodes for pods with bound (Immediate-mode) PVCs
description:
## Summary

`crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs`'s Filter path (`node_qualifies_for_pod`, lib.rs:1419-1443) does not consult the `spec.nodeAffinity` of PVs backing a pod's already-bound PVCs. Consequence: for any StorageClass with `volumeBindingMode: Immediate` (the default, and what CSI hostpath uses), the scheduler can bind a pod to a node whose labels do not satisfy the PV's own topology constraints. Kubelet then blocks forever on `MountVolume.NodeAffinity check failed ... no matching NodeSelectorTerms`, the pod never reaches Running, and the test times out at the watchdog reap (~10 min) with no progress.

## Concrete failure

**Test:** `[sig-storage] CSI Volumes [Driver: csi-hostpath] [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] read-write-once-pod [It] should block a second pod from using an in-use ReadWriteOncePod volume on the same node`

**Run:** `temp/e2e/0809-0954--driver-csi-hostpath/`, namespace `read-write-once-pod-9029`

**Wall-clock cost:** **622.994s per occurrence** — hits the 10m watchdog force-delete threshold. The only INDEPENDENT (non-#1072, non-snapshot-CRD) failure in the 41-spec run that reached the watchdog. All other watchdog reaps in that run are #1072's propagation cascade.

**Trace:**
- `host-logs/scheduler.log:204-205` — u7s scheduler binds `csi-hostpathplugin-0` (the driver StatefulSet, per-test) → `lima-node`. Driver reports `topology.hostpath.csi/node=lima-node` via `NodeGetInfo`; csi-provisioner stamps that on the PV's `spec.nodeAffinity`.
- `host-logs/scheduler.log:206-207` — u7s scheduler binds the test's workload pod `pod-0b8fc375-...` → `lima-node-3`, which does NOT carry that topology label.
- `host-logs/kubelet-lima-node-3.log:4962` — kubelet retries `MountVolume.NodeAffinity check failed for volume ... no matching NodeSelectorTerms` continuously until the watchdog force-deletes the namespace at 10m.

The pod's own `nodeSelector`/`nodeAffinity` are empty, so `node_qualifies_for_pod` accepts every node — including `lima-node-3`, which cannot serve the bound PV. The scheduler had already committed the binding by the time kubelet tries to mount, so there is no recovery.

## Root cause

`node_qualifies_for_pod` (`crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs:1419-1443`) enumerates:

1. `node_selector_matches` — pod's own `nodeSelector`
2. `node_affinity_matches` — pod's own `nodeAffinity`
3. `node_taints_tolerated` — taints/tolerations
4. `unschedulable` guard

There is no fifth check for PV-backed constraints. The only volume-topology logic in the scheduler is `selected_node_patches` (`lib.rs:2503-2550`), which is scoped by construction to unbound (`info.volume_name.is_empty()`, line 2529) `WaitForFirstConsumer` PVCs (`mode != "WaitForFirstConsumer"`, line 2538). `Immediate`-binding PVCs — which have already been bound to a specific PV before the pod is scheduled — fall through with zero enforcement.

Upstream Kubernetes's default `VolumeBinding` Filter plugin (`kubernetes/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding/volume_binding.go`) fetches the PV for each of a pod's `PersistentVolumeClaim` volumes and evaluates `spec.nodeAffinity` as part of node filtering. u7s's scheduler skips this entirely.

## Impact scope

Any driver that stamps `spec.nodeAffinity` on dynamically-provisioned PVs — which is every topology-aware CSI driver, i.e. essentially all real-world drivers — is exposed. The failure mode is:

- Multi-node cluster (this project's 2-node lima setup already qualifies)
- Any pod with a bound PVC whose PV has non-trivial `nodeAffinity`
- Scheduler picks a node that satisfies the pod's OWN affinity constraints but not the PV's
- Pod hangs 10+ minutes at the mount stage until forcibly killed

Symptom for future triage: `MountVolume.NodeAffinity check failed for volume` in kubelet logs, retrying forever, with the pod stuck ContainerCreating.

## Fix

Extend `node_qualifies_for_pod` (or add a new filter step in its callers `select_node_with_capacity` / `find_preemption_plan`) to consult the PV `spec.nodeAffinity` for each of the pod's bound PVCs and reject nodes whose labels don't satisfy it.

Shape roughly:

```rust
// After existing checks in node_qualifies_for_pod, or via a new predicate
// composed with it in select_node_with_capacity.
for pvc_name in pod_bound_pvc_names(pod) {
    let Some(pv) = pv_lookup_for_bound_pvc(pvc_name) else { continue };
    if let Some(affinity) = pv.spec.node_affinity.as_ref() {
        if !node_matches_pv_node_affinity(&node.metadata.labels, affinity) {
            return false;
        }
    }
}
```

`node_matches_pv_node_affinity` mirrors upstream's `helper.MatchNodeSelectorTerms` — an OR of `NodeSelectorTerm`s, each an AND of `matchExpressions`/`matchFields` (same operators as pod nodeAffinity: `In`, `NotIn`, `Exists`, `DoesNotExist`, `Gt`, `Lt`).

Fetching the PV requires a lookup: either extend the existing PVC lookup in `select_node_with_capacity` to also GET the bound PV, or maintain a cache. Upstream uses its informer cache; u7s will need whatever equivalent it already uses for PVC lookups (see `fetch_pvc_binding_info`, `lib.rs:2564+`).

## Regression tests

1. **Pure filter test** — construct a `NodeItem` without the topology label, a `PendingPod` with a bound PVC whose PV has `spec.nodeAffinity` requiring that label, assert `node_qualifies_for_pod` (or its successor) returns `false`. Fail-on-revert proven.
2. **Integration**: mirror the CSI e2e "read-write-once-pod" scenario at the scheduler-crate level — verify the workload pod gets bound to the node the driver landed on, not a different one.

## Acceptance

1. Filter and integration tests above pass, fail-on-revert proven.
2. `cargo test -p u7s-scheduler` fully green; `cargo clippy -p u7s-scheduler --tests -- -D warnings` clean.
3. Live verification: rerun `sonobuoy --focus 'should block a second pod from using an in-use ReadWriteOncePod'` — completes in < 2 min (was 622s / reaped), no `MountVolume.NodeAffinity check failed` messages in kubelet log.
4. Spot-check a second bound-PV test: any `[Testpattern: Dynamic PV ...]` test that provisions and consumes a PV on a specific node should NOT show scheduler binding the pod to a different node in `scheduler.log`.

## Non-goals

- Do not touch `selected_node_patches` — it handles a different case (unbound WaitForFirstConsumer PVCs) correctly.
- Do not implement PV nodeAffinity mutation or rebinding — this is Filter-side only.
- Do not introduce a full VolumeBinding-plugin replica — the minimal fix is one predicate.

## Cross-refs

- Discovered during: 0809-0954 CSI e2e run root-cause analysis. Only independent (non-#1072-cascade, non-snapshot-CRD) watchdog-reaped failure in the 41-spec set.
- Related — #1072 / [[mayor-a2ysh]] (merged): fixed 30 of 41 failures via protobuf `mountPropagation` decode. This bead covers 1 of the remaining 4 non-#1072 failures — the biggest wall-clock hogger of that set.
- Related — [[mayor-ifrs4]]: separate apiserver protobuf-decode gap on PVC spec fields discovered in the same analysis.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1076. node_qualifies_for_pod now consults bound-PV spec.nodeAffinity (fetch_bound_pv_node_affinities, extracted node_selector_spec_matches shared helper). Regression tests fail-on-revert (verified: 2 unit tests + 1 integration test flip when the conjunct is reverted). kubectl-level A/B repro confirms wrong-node-then-right-node placement. title: gen_persistent_volume_claim_to_json silently drops PVCSpec fields 4/7/8/9 (selector, dataSource, dataSourceRef, volumeAttributesClassName) on protobuf decode
description:
## Summary

`gen_persistent_volume_claim_to_json` in `crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs:2911-2949` silently drops four fields from `PersistentVolumeClaimSpec` on protobuf decode:

- field 4 `selector` (LabelSelector) — bind-selector for pre-provisioned PV matching
- field 7 `dataSource` (TypedLocalObjectReference) — clone-from-PVC / restore-from-VolumeSnapshot pointer
- field 8 `dataSourceRef` (TypedObjectReference) — successor to `dataSource`, required for cross-namespace populators
- field 9 `volumeAttributesClassName` (string) — VAC identifier used by the VAC modify controller

Same bug class as [[mayor-b0dxd]] / PR #1072 (VolumeMount.mountPropagation/recursiveReadOnly), [[mayor-l8g29]] / PR #1050 (missing csi arm in `gen_pod_spec_to_json`), and the other ~10 documented `gen_*_to_json` field-omission instances (see bd memories `content-type-determines-decode-path`, `protobuf-status-decode-bug-class`).

## Evidence

**Current decoder** — `crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs:2916-2949` decodes only `accessModes` (1), `resources` (2), `volumeName` (3), `storageClassName` (5), `volumeMode` (6). No mention of fields 4/7/8/9 anywhere in the function.

**Verified against proto** — `crates/apiserver/proto-include/k8s.io/api/core/v1/generated.proto:3221-3305` (`message PersistentVolumeClaimSpec`) confirms all four missing fields exist upstream. Cross-checked `TypedLocalObjectReference` at `generated.proto:6835-6847` and `TypedObjectReference` at `generated.proto:6849-6869` for target-type shape.

**No Sentinel coverage** — `sentinel_completeness_gen_pod_spec_to_json` (core_gen_adapter.rs:6541) and `sentinel_completeness_gen_container_to_json` exist, but there is no equivalent `sentinel_completeness_gen_persistent_volume_claim_to_json`. That is why the gap survived — the systematic detector added by [[mayor-3s9hf]] doesn't reach this function.

**Same call site shared by StatefulSet** — the doc comment at line 2908 notes `gen_persistent_volume_claim_to_json` is also invoked from `apps_gen_adapter.rs` for `StatefulSetSpec.volumeClaimTemplates`. So the same drop silently corrupts every StatefulSet with a VCT that specifies any of these four fields — no separate fix needed there once this is resolved.

## Impact — known-failing e2e tests

From the 0809-0954 CSI e2e run (`temp/e2e/0809-0954--driver-csi-hostpath/plugins/e2e/results/global/e2e.log`), the following failing specs are plausibly caused (or additionally aggravated) by the `dataSource`/`dataSourceRef` drop rather than the mountPropagation drop that #1072 fixed:

- `[Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] provisioning [It] should provision storage with pvc data source` (needs `dataSource: PersistentVolumeClaim` clone)
- `[Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] provisioning [It] should provision storage with pvc data source in parallel [Slow]`
- `[Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] provisioning [It] should provision storage with snapshot data source [Feature:VolumeSnapshotDataSource]`
- Same three under `[Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)]`

The `volumeAttributesClassName` drop breaks the entire `volume-modify [FeatureGate:VolumeAttributesClass]` family — 5 specs in the failing set — since the VAC modify controller has nothing to reconcile if the field is stripped on PVC create:

- `[It] should create a volume with VAC`
- `[DeferCleanup (Each)] should modify volume with no VAC`
- `[DeferCleanup (Each)] should modify volume that already has a VAC`
- `[DeferCleanup (Each)] should recover from invalid target VAC by updating PVC to new valid VAC`
- `[It] should be protected by vac-protection finalizer`

The `selector` drop is less likely to surface in the CSI test set (dynamic provisioning ignores `selector`) but silently breaks any user-facing pre-provisioned-binding workflow.

## Fix

Add the four field decodes to `gen_persistent_volume_claim_to_json`, mirroring the existing `volumeMode` pattern. Rough shape:

```rust
if let Some(sel) = spec.selector {
    spec_json["selector"] = gen_label_selector_to_json(sel);  // reuse existing helper
}
if let Some(ds) = spec.data_source {
    spec_json["dataSource"] = gen_typed_local_object_reference_to_json(ds);
}
if let Some(dsr) = spec.data_source_ref {
    spec_json["dataSourceRef"] = gen_typed_object_reference_to_json(dsr);
}
if let Some(v) = spec.volume_attributes_class_name.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
    spec_json["volumeAttributesClassName"] = v.into();
}
```

Confirm each helper exists (or add one — `gen_typed_local_object_reference_to_json`/`gen_typed_object_reference_to_json` likely don't exist yet; they're 3 and 4 fields respectively so they're one-liners).

## Regression tests

Two flavors, both belong:

1. **Targeted red-then-green tests** in the style of `generated_pod_spec_preserves_volume_mount_propagation` (core_gen_adapter.rs:4214) — one test per field, each with a `Why:` comment explaining the concrete failure mode a user would hit. Confirm they fail against pre-fix code before landing.
2. **Sentinel completeness test for `gen_persistent_volume_claim_to_json`** — mirror the pattern at core_gen_adapter.rs:6541. This catches whichever `PersistentVolumeClaimSpec`/`PersistentVolumeClaimStatus` field is missed next, without anyone having to think about it. This is the more valuable addition long-term.

## Acceptance

1. All four fields survive a protobuf-encode → `decode_persistentvolumeclaim_proto_gen` → JSON round-trip.
2. Sentinel completeness test for `gen_persistent_volume_claim_to_json` exists, is fail-on-revert proven, and passes.
3. `cargo test -p u7s-apiserver` fully green; `cargo clippy -p u7s-apiserver --tests -- -D warnings` clean.
4. Live spot-check: after fix, `sonobuoy --focus 'should provision storage with pvc data source$'` and `--focus 'should create a volume with VAC'` both pass against a fresh cluster on current main.

## Non-goals

- Do not touch StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplate handling separately — it shares this function, so it's fixed transitively.
- Do not backfill sentinel completeness across every other `gen_*_to_json` function in this PR (worthwhile, but scope-creeps this fix). File as a follow-up if desired.

## Cross-refs

- Same bug class: [[mayor-b0dxd]] (PR #1072, merged), [[mayor-ow10r]] (superseded by same PR), [[mayor-l8g29]] (PR #1050)
- Sentinel infrastructure: [[mayor-3s9hf]]
- Discovered during: 0809-0954 CSI e2e run root-cause analysis (mountPropagation branch fixed by #1072; this bead covers a separately-discovered decode gap in the same file, surfaced while enumerating other candidate root causes)
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1074. Adds decode for spec.selector, spec.dataSource, spec.dataSourceRef, spec.volumeAttributesClassName. Sentinel-completeness test added (scoped to .spec). Regression tests fail-on-revert verified. Filed mayor-ovni7 as follow-up for the pre-existing PersistentVolumeClaimStatus decode gap (accessModes/capacity/allocatedResources/allocatedResourceStatuses/currentVolumeAttributesClassName/modifyVolumeStatus), which is out of scope for this fix.

title: apiserver silently drops VolumeMount.mountPropagation (+recursiveReadOnly) on protobuf decode — root cause of block-volmode CSI hang, NOT upstream
description:
## Corrected root cause for mayor-07zb7 (CLOSED with the WRONG conclusion — see that bead's notes for the superseded reasoning)

mayor-07zb7 closed with: "driver's `mount -o bind` creates a PRIVATE mount... structurally incapable of propagating to kubelet namespace at ANY time... Not a u7s bug. Fix locus: upstream csi-hostpath driver or upstream kubelet."

**That conclusion is wrong, and self-contradicted by its own evidence**: the same finding doc also recorded that a HEALTHY block-volmode pod shows byte-identical `devtmpfs[/loopN]` propagation between the driver container and host — i.e. propagation demonstrably DOES work via the exact same driver/kubelet code path. A "structurally incapable, permanent" mechanism cannot also work correctly sometimes on unmodified upstream binaries.

## Actual root cause

`crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs::gen_container_to_json` (the function that decodes a protobuf-encoded `Container` into u7s's internal JSON representation — this is the path `extract_body`/`decode_pod_proto_gen` route every protobuf-Content-Type Pod/PodTemplateSpec write through) builds each `VolumeMount` JSON object from only `name`, `mountPath`, `readOnly`, `subPath`, `subPathExpr` (lines 806-822 pre-fix). It never reads `mount_propagation` (VolumeMount proto field 5) or `recursive_read_only` (field 7) off the decoded struct at all.

`client-go`'s typed Clientset — which the Kubernetes CSI e2e storage-test framework uses to create a **fresh csi-hostpathplugin StatefulSet for every single test** — defaults to `Content-Type: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf`. Manual `kubectl create`/`apply` sends JSON, which bypasses this decoder entirely (JSON bodies pass through `extract_body` untouched).

Consequence: every ginkgo-driven block-volmode CSI test creates its own driver StatefulSet with `mountPropagation: Bidirectional` on its `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins` and `/var/lib/kubelet/pods` volumeMounts — and that field is silently discarded on write. The driver container's own copy of those mounts is therefore set up as **plain private mounts** (confirmed directly: raw `/proc/<driver-pid>/mountinfo` from the mayor-07zb7 scout's own transcript shows `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins` inside the driver container with NO `shared:`/`master:` peer-group tag). Any bind mount the driver later performs under that tree (the loop-device bind for a block-volmode PV) can then never propagate into kubelet's mount namespace. Kubelet's own follow-up bind-mount reads the stale placeholder file the driver created, and `remove()`/`unlink()` EBUSYs forever on pod delete — deterministically, no race, no kernel/timing/upstream involvement required.

This exactly explains the evidence that broke the old conclusion: **0/4 manual kubectl repro attempts reproduced the hang; every ginkgo `--focus` run reproduces it 100%.** Manual kubectl (JSON) never drops the field; every client-go-driven (protobuf) driver-pod creation does, every time.

## This is a known recurring bug class in this codebase, not a one-off

See bd memories `content-type-determines-decode-path`, `dispatch-proto-decode-drop-check`, `protobuf-status-decode-bug-class`, `protobuf-decode-defaults-break-workload-template-equality`, `protobuf-reflip-2026-07-14-terminationgraceperiod-drop` — this is at least the 10th field-omission instance in the `gen_*_to_json` adapter family, and the first specifically in `VolumeMount`.

## Fix (already drafted, currently only in a local patch, NOT committed to any branch)

Add to `gen_container_to_json`'s VolumeMount-building closure, right after the existing `subPathExpr` handling:

```rust
if let Some(v) = vm.mount_propagation.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
    m.insert("mountPropagation".to_string(), serde_json::Value::String(v));
}
if let Some(v) = vm.recursive_read_only.filter(|s| !s.is_empty()) {
    m.insert("recursiveReadOnly".to_string(), serde_json::Value::String(v));
}
```

No response-side fix is needed — per `protobuf-path-masked-in-harness`, u7s always serves JSON responses regardless of request Accept header, so once the field is captured on decode it round-trips normally.

`apps_gen_adapter.rs` delegates to `core_gen_adapter::gen_pod_template_spec_to_json` (which calls this same `gen_container_to_json`), so this one fix also covers Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet pod templates — no duplicate fix needed there.

## Regression test (drafted, proven to fail against pre-fix code)

Added to `core_gen_adapter.rs`'s test module: construct a `core_v1::Pod` with one `Container` whose `VolumeMount` has `mount_propagation: Some("Bidirectional")`, encode via prost, decode via the real `decode_pod_proto_gen` entry point, assert `result["spec"]["containers"][0]["volumeMounts"][0]["mountPropagation"] == "Bidirectional"`. Confirmed failing pre-fix: `left: Null, right: "Bidirectional"`. Add a matching test for `recursiveReadOnly`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests above pass.
2. `cargo test -p u7s-apiserver` fully green.
3. Live verification: rebuild the apiserver with the fix, bring up a fresh stack, run `sonobuoy --focus 'Verify if offline PVC expansion works'` (the test mayor-07zb7's scout used for its live capture) — pod must complete create/resize/delete cleanly with NO EBUSY retry loop in kubelet's log. Ideally also spot-check 1-2 of the other 6 known-fail block-volmode tests from cv3jo's original list.
4. Live-capture `/proc/<driver-pid>/mountinfo` for the driver's `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins` mount during the run — must now show a `shared:`/`master:` peer-group tag, confirming the mechanism directly (not just the symptom).
5. Update `ai/findings/0807-block-volmode-bind-mount-source-wrong-file-07zb7.md` (or supersede it) with the corrected root cause once verified live.

## Do NOT re-litigate

The kernel mount-propagation-semantics rabbit hole in mayor-07zb7 (H1/H2, "private by default", peer groups) is a red herring caused by this bug, not an independent kernel/driver issue. Do not re-open that investigation thread.
close_reason: PR #1072 opened. Fix + regression tests: cargo test -p u7s-apiserver green (2804 tests), clippy clean. Live verification on fresh lima-node-6 stack: --focus 'Verify if offline PVC expansion works' (the exact mayor-07zb7 repro test) against the real upstream csi-hostpath v1.17.1 driver (auto-deployed by ginkgo's own embedded manifests) now passes with 0 EBUSY in kubelet.log (was 20+ pre-fix, per finding doc), run twice for reproducibility. Live /proc/<driver-pid>/mountinfo capture confirms shared:1 peer-group tag now present on /var/lib/kubelet/plugins (was completely absent pre-fix). Also spot-checked a 2nd test from the original 7-failure list ('should create a volume with VAC', block volmode) — passed, 0 EBUSY. Remaining 5 of 7 not individually re-run (budget) but share the identical mechanism, high confidence fixed too. VM torn down cleanly, no orphaned processes/state. Supersedes mayor-07zb7's wrong 'not a u7s bug, upstream driver/kubelet' closure; ai/findings/0807-block-volmode-bind-mount-source-wrong-file-07zb7.md updated with live verification results.

title: apiserver: cross-namespace pods LIST (/api/v1/pods) mis-parses multi-term fieldSelector, returns unfiltered list (breaks kubectl describe node)
description:
Root-caused via mayor-6ii27 Shape 3 audit (scout agent-a40060153c1ac9cf5, 2026-08-07). Deterministic proof from code trace + upstream selector-string verification; no live cluster repro needed to confirm (existing borrowed stack was torn down; proof is confidence-independent of that gap).

## Symptom

`kubectl describe node <name>` returns the SAME unfiltered pod list for every node. Bead mayor-6ii27 documented this observationally 2026-08-07 during csi-hostpath OOM investigation. Every node's describe output includes every pod in the cluster.

## Root cause (proven)

Two separate pods-LIST entry points in u7s:
- `/api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods` → `handlers::pods::list_pods` (lib.rs:566). Uses `pod_store_field_selector`/`filter_pods_by_field_selector` (pods.rs:100). Comma-aware, first-equality-term extraction. **Works correctly** — verified by existing test `list_pods_with_field_selector_filters_pods` (pods.rs:11738).
- `/api/v1/{resource}` (matches `/api/v1/pods`) → `handlers::core::core_list_resource`, special-cased for `plural == "pods"` (core.rs:36-45).

The `core_list_resource` `plural == "pods"` case has TWO branches:
- **watch/sendInitialEvents branch** (core.rs:81-107) — correctly reuses `pod_store_field_selector` + `filter_pods_by_field_selector`. ✅
- **plain (non-watch) LIST branch** (core.rs:133-178) — incorrectly calls `generic::parse_field_selector` (generic.rs:393). ❌

`parse_field_selector` is a single `key=value`/`key!=value` parser tested only for one clause (generic.rs:1179-1226). It does `s.split_once("!=")` on the WHOLE selector string. For `kubectl describe node`'s selector `spec.nodeName=<name>,status.phase!=Succeeded,status.phase!=Failed`:
- First `!=` occurs inside `status.phase!=Succeeded`.
- `parse_field_selector` extracts `field="spec.nodeName=<name>,status.phase"`, `value="Succeeded,status.phase!=Failed"`, `negated=true`.
- Neither the bogus field nor value matches any sqlite fast-path (metadata.name/metadata.namespace/spec.nodeName), so it falls to `sqlite.rs:831-878`'s generic scan.
- `json_path_equals` can't resolve the dotted bogus field → returns `false`.
- Negated `true` → **every pod matches, for every node**.

## Upstream selector shape (verified via cached source)

`kubectl` `NodeDescriber.Describe` (k/k `release-1.36`, cached at `temp/research/kubectl-describe-node-release-1.36.go`, lines 3435-3453):
```go
fieldSelector := fields.AndSelectors(
    fields.OneTermEqualSelector("spec.nodeName", node.Name),
    fields.OneTermNotEqualSelector("status.phase", string(corev1.PodSucceeded)),
    fields.OneTermNotEqualSelector("status.phase", string(corev1.PodFailed)),
)
```
- `node.Namespace` is `""` (Nodes are cluster-scoped) → uses all-namespaces `/api/v1/pods` route (not the namespaced one).
- `andTerm.String()` (`apimachinery/pkg/fields/selector.go:240-246`) joins with `,`.
- Chunking (`getPodsInChunks`/`FollowContinue`) preserves the FieldSelector unchanged across pages — bug fires on page 1 already.

## Fix

Replace `parse_field_selector` + raw store filter in `core_list_resource`'s plain-LIST branch (`core.rs:133-178`, `plural == "pods"` case) with the SAME pattern the watch/sendInitialEvents branch two branches above already uses:

```rust
let store_selector = pod_store_field_selector(&query.field_selector.unwrap_or_default());
// ... store LIST call passing store_selector ...
let filtered = filter_pods_by_field_selector(pods, &query.field_selector.unwrap_or_default());
```

The exact call shape lives at core.rs:81-107 — mirror it. No new logic; move the working pattern into the missing branch.

## Test predicate (fail-on-revert)

Add integration test in `crates/apiserver/src/handlers/core.rs` (or `pods.rs`, wherever core_list_resource's existing tests live):
- Seed pods across multiple `spec.nodeName` values (e.g. `worker-1`, `worker-2`, `worker-3`) and different `status.phase` values (Running, Succeeded, Failed).
- `GET /api/v1/pods?fieldSelector=spec.nodeName%3Dworker-1%2Cstatus.phase%21%3DSucceeded%2Cstatus.phase%21%3DFailed`
- Assert response contains ONLY the Running/Pending pods on `worker-1`; excludes worker-2/3 pods AND excludes Succeeded/Failed pods on any node.
- Message: "cross-namespace pods LIST with multi-term fieldSelector must filter correctly; `kubectl describe node` breaks otherwise — kubectl issues exactly this selector shape (upstream describe.go:3435-3453) to list only Non-terminated pods on the given node."
- Must fail on revert (currently returns all pods regardless of any of the three terms).

## Priority

**P1** (upgraded from mayor-6ii27's P2 per scout recommendation):
- Core kubectl command silently returns wrong data for every node — usability + trust regression.
- Cross-tenant information exposure potential — an operator with `list pods` cluster-scope but limited namespace scope would see pods in unintended namespaces.
- Deterministic; hits every time.
- Trivial to trigger.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT rewrite `parse_field_selector` — the fix is in `core_list_resource`'s wrong-branch call, not in the generic parser. `parse_field_selector` should stay tested for its own scope (single-term).
- Do NOT touch `handlers::pods::list_pods` — it's the working path.
- Do NOT change the watch/sendInitialEvents branch — it's already correct.
- Do NOT change kubectl's client-side behavior — we don't ship kubectl.

## Cross-refs

- Scout audit findings: this bead's description
- Related class (silent-noop-filter): bd memory `silent-noop-filter-looks-like-flaky-timing`
- Related bead: mayor-tv4ob (CR watch field-selector, needs cross-version conversion in watch path — DIFFERENT class, not the same bug)
close_reason: PR #1065 opened. core_list_resource's plain-LIST branch for pods now uses pod_store_field_selector + filter_pods_by_field_selector (matching the watch/sendInitialEvents branch two above). Fail-on-revert integration test added covering the exact kubectl describe node selector shape.

title: block-volmode PVC hostpath: /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/volumeDevices/<pv>/dev/<pod-uid> bind-mount remains busy 9+ minutes after pod delete, blocks kubelet UnmapVolume forever
description:
Supersedes mayor-cv3jo (closed as baggage-heavy; scout v2 & v3 writeups linked below explored two wrong root-cause hypotheses each with useful negative results, but never answered THIS bead's central question). File-new was preferable to reopening cv3jo yet again.

## Central question

**Why does a hostpath-CSI block-volmode volume's per-pod bind-mount at `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/volumeDevices/<pv>/dev/<pod-uid>` remain busy 9+ minutes after pod delete on u7s, when the same test passes upstream on the exact same kubelet + CRI-O version?**

The test is a simple write-then-read-back: it should hold the volume for seconds. Something on u7s is either (a) holding a fd/lock on that file, (b) leaving something mounted underneath it that prevents `unlink()`, or (c) not releasing the loopback device the file is backed by — none of which happen upstream.

## What's known (from scout v2 aeb8eb33400d53867 + scout v3 2026-08-07 postmortem)

Confirmed by direct evidence:
- Kubelet enters `blkUtil.DetachFileDevice`'s `remove()` retry loop within seconds of pod delete, EBUSY every time.
- Backoff plateaus at 2m2s, retries forever (retry-loop diarrhea, no forward progress — this is a HANG, per `watchdog-thresholds-are-final-do-not-raise` memory).
- `NodeUnpublishVolume` and `NodeUnstageVolume` on the csi-hostpathplugin sidecar are NEVER called during the hang — kubelet's pre-CSI cleanup is what's stuck.
- KCM's AttachDetachController correctly refuses to detach because kubelet is still reporting the volume as mounted (upstream-correct behavior, gated on kubelet's own unmount report).

Ruled out by evidence:
- **Not an apiserver signal-drop bug.** Scout v3 verified across the entire hang window: zero 5xx, zero WARN/ERROR, the one VolumeAttachment PATCH that mattered (`csi-attacher → /apis/storage.k8s.io/v1/volumeattachments/csi-b8eb.../status`) got 200 at 07:52:58.686. No further PATCH was ever due because KCM correctly waited on the (never-arriving) kubelet unmount signal.
- **Not a scheduler / bind-path bug.** Pod was bound and running normally before the delete request landed.
- **Not the watchdog.** Watchdog reaped at 604s AFTER the hang was already 10 minutes old. Reaping cascades to killed sidecars → orphan PVs → 20m PV-delete-wait timeout, which is a separate visible failure mode but not what caused the original hang.

## Investigation direction — LIVE-STACK REPRO REQUIRED

Scout v3 explicitly stated logs alone cannot resolve this. Needed:

1. **Live-VM inspection while the pod is stuck.** Trigger the failing test (see reproduction hint below), wait for the EBUSY loop to start (few seconds after pod delete), THEN:
   - `mcp__lima-node-<slot>__run_shell_command` running: `sudo lsof /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/volumeDevices/<pv>/dev/<pod-uid>` — WHO holds the fd?
   - `sudo fuser -m /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/volumeDevices/<pv>/dev/<pod-uid>` — same question, alt tool
   - `mount | grep <pod-uid>` — is anything ELSE mounted underneath the bind-mount?
   - `losetup -a | grep <pv>` — loopback device state?
   - `sudo cat /proc/mounts | grep <pv>` — same, canonical
   - `sudo cat /proc/<hostpathplugin-pid>/mounts | grep <pv>` — is the driver container's mount namespace holding something?
   - `strace -p <kubelet-pid> -e trace=unlink,unlinkat,umount 2>&1 | grep <pod-uid>` — see the exact syscall failing
2. **Compare mount namespace layout to upstream.** The hostpath driver runs in a container. Does u7s's CRI-O + kubelet arrangement produce a mount namespace layout that differs from upstream stock Docker/containerd — e.g. mount propagation flags (private/shared/slave), overlay mount ordering, or the loop device visible in the wrong namespace?
3. **CRI-O configuration audit.** u7s uses CRI-O + crun (see `scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh` and the CRI-O config drop-ins the script writes). Any config divergence from a stock CRI-O install that could affect block-volmode mount propagation?
4. **Systemd cgroup / mount unit involvement.** Lima's systemd may be mounting or holding something under `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/volumeDevices/`.

## Reproduction hint (from scout v3)

The exact failing test from the 2026-08-07 operator repro was:

```
--focus '\[sig-storage\] CSI Volumes \[Driver: csi-hostpath\] \[Testpattern: Dynamic PV \(block volmode\)\(allowExpansion\)\] volume-expand \[It\] Verify if offline PVC expansion works'
```

The bead's original 7 failing tests are ALL block-volmode variants of VAC-modify or volume-expand — every one hits the same class. Repro takes ~10-15 minutes wall-clock (pod is stuck the whole time; you don't need to wait for the DeferCleanup timeout to observe the mount state).

## Prior artifacts (do NOT re-litigate these, use for grounding only)

- `temp/e2e-memory-samples/scout-cv3jo-v2/findings.md` — scout v2's kubelet-blame writeup (wrong on ROOT CAUSE, correct on mechanistic timeline: MapPodDevice → 1.4s → first EBUSY at UnmountVolume start)
- Scout v3 findings recorded in-line in cv3jo's close note (2026-08-07)
- Post-mortem run: `temp/e2e/0807-0818-verify-if-offline-pvc-expansion-works/` (host-side logs from operator's live cv3jo repro — mount inspection was NOT captured here; that's why this needs a fresh live-stack scout)

## Related beads NOT to conflate

- mayor-cv3jo (closed 2026-08-07, superseded by this bead)
- mayor-51z5g (closed WON'T FIX — watchdog is correct; not the cause here)
- mayor-ivcy3 (P2 open — CSI driver-namespace topology fix; prevents the CASCADE on already-failing tests but not the primary hang)
- mayor-rcujn (P1 open — pod-exec mount visibility; MAY share a root cause with this bead, worth checking after)
- mayor-xbfm0 (P2 open — VAC finalizer gap; independent, orthogonal)

## Priority

P1. This is now the primary open cv3jo-class question. Blocks 7+ block-volmode conformance tests. Not user-facing but blocks the "pass conformance for block volmode" milestone.

## Cross-refs

- mayor-cv3jo (closed, superseded 2026-08-07)
- bd memory: `watchdog-thresholds-are-final-do-not-raise` (why the watchdog cascade isn't the root cause)
- bd memory: `upstream-tests-passing-means-bug-is-ours` (why "upstream kubelet bug" is the wrong default suspicion)
- bd memory: `mayor-does-not-do-scout-work-in-band` (this needs a proper scout dispatch, not mayor cycles)
