title: conformance harness silently permits host-port collision on 127.0.0.1:10250 kubelet forward (root cause of mayor-ag0e5)
description:
Conformance harness silently permits multi-stack host-port collisions on 127.0.0.1:10250 (kubelet forward). Fix: auto-allocate or hard-fail.

## Root cause context (from mayor-ag0e5 scout v2 aa82864c86ab81711, 2026-08-07)

`scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh:75` defaults `KUBELET_PORT` to `10250` when `--kubelet-port` isn't explicitly passed.
`lima-start.sh:94-96` only patches the VM's `lima-config` `hostPort` away from 10250 when a non-default `--kubelet-port` IS passed.

Consequence when two u7s stacks run concurrently and both default to `--kubelet-port`:
- Both VMs try to forward host `127.0.0.1:10250 → guest :10250`.
- Whichever hostagent boots first WINS the bind silently.
- The second VM's kubelet forward silently fails.
- The second VM's apiserver tries `exec/log/attach` to `127.0.0.1:10250` and reaches the FIRST VM's kubelet instead.
- Since every u7s stack's CA uses the same hardcoded `Subject: CN=u7s-ca` (`crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs:179`), rustls's WebPkiServerVerifier finds a name-matching trust anchor and tries crypto verification against a leaf signed by a different stack's CA — `BadSignature`.
- Diagnosis took hours because the error surfaced as a cryptic TLS rejection rather than "your port forward doesn't reach your kubelet".

Live evidence (mayor-verified):
- `lsof -n -i :10250` shows `limactl 56482` (lima-node's hostagent) holding the port since ~10:37AM.
- `openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:10250` returns CN=lima-node's serving cert — NOT lima-node-4's, even though only lima-node-4's kubectl is being invoked.

## Fix approach

Modify `scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh` and possibly `run-all.sh` so that when `--kubelet-port` is not explicitly passed, the script:

- **Option A (preferred): auto-allocate**. Detect a free host port in some sane range (e.g. 10251-10299) via `lsof -n -i :$P` or `nc -z` probing. Bind the VM to that port. Print the chosen port so downstream scripts and the operator see it.

- **Option B (safer): hard-fail on collision**. Before booting the VM, check if `127.0.0.1:$KUBELET_PORT` is already bound (any hostagent). If yes, exit with a clear error like:
  ```
  ERROR: host port 127.0.0.1:10250 already in use by lima VM 'lima-node' (hostagent PID 56482).
  Pass --kubelet-port <N> to assign a different port (10251-10299 recommended).
  See ai/prompts/vm-operations.md for the standard slot table.
  ```

Option B is simpler and preserves the "operator explicitly chooses" convention already documented. Option A is friendlier for scout dispatch but adds discovery logic.

Also consider: apply the same pattern to any OTHER default-port script that could collide. Grep `run-all.sh`, `01-build.sh`, `02-start-apiserver.sh`, `add-node.sh` for other silent-default-port patterns.

## Acceptance

- `shellcheck scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh` clean.
- New behavior test: start two VMs both defaulting to --kubelet-port, second one should either auto-allocate to a free port OR fail with the clear error above (depending on option chosen).
- Existing single-VM path unaffected (default lima-node with --kubelet-port unpassed still works).

## Non-goals

- Do NOT change the standard slot table in `ai/prompts/vm-operations.md` (per-slot kubelet ports are documented and canonical).
- Do NOT rename `--kubelet-port` or change its semantics.
- Do NOT fix the CA-CN-uniqueness issue in the same bead (separate follow-on).

## Cross-refs

- Root cause: mayor-ag0e5 scout v2 aa82864c86ab81711, closed 2026-08-07
- Related follow-on (diagnostic improvement): unique CA CN per stack (separate bead)
- Related diagnostic: mayor-qq14v (pod_log silent-fail warning) — independent low-priority diagnostic improvement
- Priority P1: this is the direct cause of a class of investigation-blocking failures that took hours to diagnose the first time.
notes: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-07: Option B (hard-fail). Rationale: preserve the 'operator explicitly chooses' convention — us controlling the ports is the source of truth. Auto-allocation would break that model (operator couldn't answer 'which ports are free?' without runtime probing). Bead is now ready-to-dispatch as Option B.
close_reason: PR #1054 opened. Option B (hard-fail) implemented per operator decision (2026-08-07). Detection in scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh via lsof-based pre-flight check before each limactl start call site (skipped when target VM already Running, since that path never attempts a new port bind). Verified live against the real 10250 collision held by mayor's own hostagent.

title: apiserver exec/log/attach proxy rejects kubelet TLS with BadSignature on fresh --reset stack (blocks ALL exec/log/attach e2e traffic)
description:
u7s apiserver's exec/log/attach proxy REJECTS every kubelet-side TLS handshake with BadSignature on freshly --reset stacks. Blocks ALL exec/log/attach-based e2e tests.

## Reproduction (100% on fresh --reset lima-node stack, per mayor-rcujn v2 scout 2026-08-07)

1. scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --reset --stack-only --vm lima-node-4 --port 6446 --workdir ./temp/scout-rcujn-v2 --verbose
2. Wait for stack ready. Deploy any test pod.
3. kubectl --kubeconfig ./temp/scout-rcujn-v2/kubeconfig exec <pod> -- ls
4. Fails with:
   apiserver.log: 'WARN u7s_apiserver::handlers::proxy: exec proxy error: kubelet exec connect failed: IO error: invalid peer certificate: BadSignature'
   kubectl-side: BadGateway 502.

## Blast radius

Every exec, logs, attach, port-forward call fails. Any e2e test that verifies workload behavior via 'kubectl exec' or that streams logs cannot pass. This is upstream of mayor-rcujn's original 14 failures (those show cat RUNNING and returning 'No such file'; here exec never connects). Independent of the mount-visibility race hypothesis.

## Evidence collected (mayor-rcujn v2 scout)

- apiserver.log at /Users/balint.erdos/u7s/temp/scout-rcujn-v2/apiserver.log shows BadSignature failures at multiple timestamps (grep 'BadSignature' returns 4+ hits within a few minutes).
- Manual repro 3/3 against a different pod. kubectl logs fails identically.
- 'openssl verify -CAfile ca.pem kubelet-serving.crt' returns OK.
- ca.crt (DER) and ca.pem decode to identical CA (ecdsa-with-SHA256, P-256, matching serial).
- Kubelet's live-presented cert on :10250 matches the on-disk file byte-for-byte.
- Every openssl-level check says the chain is valid. Yet rustls WebPkiServerVerifier rejects it every time.

## Suspect code paths (from scout)

- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs:485 (build_kubelet_tls_config call site)
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs:580-624 (build_kubelet_tls_config -- constructs the WebPkiServerVerifier)
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs:1119 (connect_async_tls_with_config in run_exec_proxy)
- crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs:127-212 (load_or_generate_ca -- CA reload path)
- crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs:172 -- explicit comment 'We cannot round-trip from DER/PEM back to CertificateParams'

## Candidate mechanisms (unproven, need in-band investigation)

1. rustls/webpki-vs-LibreSSL strictness difference: rustls's WebPkiServerVerifier applies stricter validation than openssl (e.g. name-constraints, EKUs, signature-algorithm allowlist). If kubelet's cert or the CA has a field openssl accepts but webpki rejects, this fires.
2. Plumbing bug for state.cluster_ca_der: the DER passed to build_kubelet_tls_config might not match what's on disk.
3. CA reload path bug: load_or_generate_ca's own comment admits it reconstructs only a 'minimal' CertificateParams on reload. No test covers a sign-after-reload round-trip (generate_tls_writes_ca_files_to_disk at tls.rs:1189 only covers first-run). Kubelet's cert is signed by host openssl (not rcgen), so this reload path is a flagged code smell, not a confirmed cause -- but worth investigating.
4. --reset-specific vs standing regression: unknown. The scout only observed on a freshly --reset stack. Previous scouts (mayor-4w0j5, mayor-f4ml4, mayor-rcujn v1) on a REUSED stack did NOT hit this. Suggests something --reset-triggered.

## Fix approach (direction only, worker discretion)

Minimal isolated Rust repro exercising load_or_generate_ca reload + build_kubelet_tls_config verification against a real externally-signed kubelet cert. Compare against a rustls-official validation path. If rustls/webpki is intentionally rejecting for a legitimate reason (e.g. ecdsa-with-SHA256 signature but P-256 curve mismatch, name-constraint violation), we need to either regenerate certs to match rustls expectations OR use a differently-configured verifier.

If this turns out to be a --reset regression (fresh CA generation produces certs webpki rejects) rather than a design bug, the root cause might be in load_or_generate_ca's rcgen-generated CertificateParams -- something in the reconstruction path that produces a subtly-invalid signature.

## Acceptance

- kubectl exec against any pod on a freshly --reset lima-node stack SUCCEEDS
- kubectl logs against a running pod streams output SUCCEEDS
- No 'BadSignature' warnings in apiserver.log during normal traffic
- Fail-on-revert regression test in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs or crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs

## Non-goals

- Do NOT investigate the mount-visibility race in the same worker (that's mayor-rcujn's continued scope; this bead is upstream of it)
- Do NOT touch the cert rotation path in general (would scope-creep to a design decision)

## Cross-refs

- Discovered: mayor-rcujn v2 scout 2026-08-07 (a55410d90496425dc)
- Related open: mayor-rcujn (14 mount-visibility failures) -- likely blocked from further scout-based investigation until this exec-proxy bug is fixed
- Reproduction data: temp/scout-rcujn-v2/apiserver.log, temp/e2e-memory-samples/scout-rcujn-v2/findings.md
- Not affected by this bug: prior scouts on REUSED stacks (mayor-4w0j5, mayor-f4ml4, mayor-rcujn v1 — worked fine)
notes:
MAYOR CORRECTION-OF-CORRECTION 2026-08-07 (scout ab955e6c574403b9f verified my prior 'deprioritize' correction was wrong):

MY EARLIER GREP WAS SLOPPY. The pattern 'method=(GET|POST).*(exec|log|attach)' matched ANY line where those strings appeared ANYWHERE in the URL, which caught kubelet PATCHes to pods in namespaces containing 'log' as a substring (nslookup-*, svc-latency-*, etc). The 'so-called 115 successes' were unrelated traffic.

CORRECT count using tight regex 'uri=[^ ]*/(exec|log|attach)\?[^ ]*': 22 total exec/log/attach requests in scout-rcujn-v2 apiserver.log, ALL FAILED (18x 502, 4x 101-then-BadSignature). ZERO successes.

Scout ALSO live-tested (30+ min after prior scout ended, apiserver still running, no --reset): kubectl exec against a healthy unrelated pod (exectest) reproduces BadSignature. kubectl exec csi-hostpathplugin-0 reproduces BadSignature. 2/2 live repros. THIS IS DETERMINISTIC AND STACK-WIDE, NOT POD-SPECIFIC.

RESTORED TO P1. mayor-rcujn IS blocked by this after all — reopening the 'blocked' framing.

SCOUT'S POSITIVE FINDINGS (kept for the next investigation round):
1. Not the CA-reload path (tls.rs:127-212). Log shows CA loaded exactly once at process start (06:07:22); zero reload events in 4200+ subsequent lines. Failure reproduces byte-identically with no intervening reload.
2. Not cert rotation. Only one kubelet-serving cert pair exists (single mtime 15:03:38). The '-2' suffix scout dispatch mentioned is per-node naming, NOT rotation counter (confirmed via scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh:388-390).
3. Not a plumbing bug in cluster_ca_der DER handling. Two independently-implemented rustls consumers (build_kubelet_tls_config at proxy.rs:580-624 for exec/attach; the pooled kubelet_client at state.rs:658-685 for /log) both fail identically. A bug local to one path wouldn't explain both failing the same way.
4. BEST-SUPPORTED (unconfirmed): --reset-specific bring-up race producing a webpki-rejected (but openssl-valid) cert pair. Operator's temp/e2e/0806-1542-conformance was ALSO a --reset run and had zero BadSignature, so the differentiator is BETWEEN bring-ups, not intrinsic to --reset.
5. rustls-vs-openssl strictness: openssl verify and openssl verify -x509_strict both pass on this stack's certs. No malformed-encoding anomaly visible at CLI level. Scout could not find byte-level trigger without a minimal rustls/webpki reproducer binary (outside read-only tooling).

PREVENTION RECS FROM SCOUT (act on independently of root cause):
1. IMMEDIATE (before evidence lost): snapshot ca.key/ca.crt/kubelet-serving.crt/.key from lima-node-4 (do NOT reset). Diff structurally + byte-wise against a fresh --reset pair from lima-node-2 to isolate differentiating bytes.
2. DIAGNOSTIC FIX (low-risk, useful regardless of root cause): pod_log's non-websocket error path at proxy.rs:310-324 swallows the underlying reqwest/rustls error into a bare 502 with no tracing::warn!. Exec's on_upgrade closure DOES log. That's why 18/22 failures had no error detail. File as a separate small bead.
3. TEST GAP: tls.rs:1189 generate_tls_writes_ca_files_to_disk only covers first-run generation; no test exercises a real rustls handshake against openssl-signed leaf certs across multiple --reset generations.
close_reason:
Scout v2 aa82864c86ab81711 ROOT-CAUSED with grep-verified evidence chain. NOT a rustls/webpki/cert-code bug — it's a host-port collision in conformance tooling.

MECHANISM: mayor-rcujn v2 scout invoked run-all.sh --reset --stack-only --vm lima-node-4 --port 6446 WITHOUT --kubelet-port. Per scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh:75, KUBELET_PORT defaults to 10250. Per lima-start.sh:96, the VM's lima-config hostPort is only patched when --kubelet-port is non-default. Result: lima-node-4's kubelet forward CONFLICTED with lima-node's (operator's healthy stack, holding 127.0.0.1:10250 since ~4h earlier via PID 56482 hostagent). Operator's stack won the bind race; lima-node-4's forward silently failed.

CONSEQUENCE: apiserver on lima-node-4 tries to exec into pods on lima-node-4, connects to 127.0.0.1:10250, but reaches lima-node's kubelet instead. That kubelet presents CN=lima-node's serving cert signed by lima-node's CA key. Because every u7s CA is minted with the SAME hardcoded Subject CN=u7s-ca (crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs:179), lima-node-4 apiserver's rustls WebPkiServerVerifier finds a name-matching trust anchor in its root store and attempts cryptographic verification. But the leaf was signed by a DIFFERENT stack's CA private key — legitimate BadSignature. Rustls is behaving correctly.

VERIFIED (mayor grep-checked scout's claims):
1. tls.rs:179 + tls.rs:192 both hardcode 'u7s-ca' as Subject CN. Confirmed.
2. lima-start.sh:75/94-96 gate hostPort patching on --kubelet-port being non-default. Confirmed.
3. lsof -n -i :10250 shows lima-node's hostagent PID 56482 holding the port. Confirmed live.

SCOUT EVIDENCE:
- Phase 1 cert-diff: affected/healthy CA + leaf certs structurally identical. openssl verify -x509_strict passes on affected pair. NO structural anomaly to blame.
- Phase 2 minimal rustls reproducer (rustls 0.23 + aws-lc-rs, mirrors build_kubelet_tls_config exactly): affected cert pair VERIFIES OK in isolation. Contradicts live failure -> forces the pivot.
- Live: openssl s_client -connect 127.0.0.1:10250 returned CN=lima-node cert with serial af:a1:c6:a3:10:33:a1:3f = byte-identical to temp/u7s/kubelet-serving.crt. Apiserver was talking to wrong VM entirely.

NOT A u7s CODE BUG (in tls.rs/proxy.rs/rustls consumers). Rustls is validating exactly correctly. The bug is in conformance tooling that lets two concurrently-running stacks silently collide on host port 10250.

FIX RECOMMENDATIONS (from scout, all valid):
1. HIGH: file bead to make run-all.sh/lima-start.sh auto-allocate or hard-fail on port collision instead of silently succeeding. Prevents recurrence.
2. MEDIUM: give each stack's CA a unique Subject CN so future misroute surfaces as legible UnknownIssuer instead of opaque BadSignature. Diagnostic improvement.
3. LOW: regression test in conformance tooling (verify effective host-port binding matches intended VM). NOT in tls.rs/proxy.rs.

mayor-qq14v (pod_log tracing::warn) is STILL VALID as an independent diagnostic improvement — this incident took hours to root-cause partly because the log path swallowed errors silently.

BEAD CLOSED as NOT-A-u7s-CODE-BUG. Follow-on beads filed separately for the port-collision-prevention (P1) and CA-CN-uniqueness (P2) improvements. Scout findings memo: temp/e2e-memory-samples/scout-ag0e5-v2/findings.md.

title: feat(scheduler): stamp volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node on unbound WaitForFirstConsumer PVCs at bind time (suf4l Bug 2)
description:
Implement scheduler VolumeBinding: stamp volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node on unbound WaitForFirstConsumer PVCs at pod bind time.

## Bug (verified via mayor-suf4l scout adde8650380bb7f3f, 2026-08-07)

crates/scheduler has NO logic to stamp pvc.metadata.annotations['volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node'] at pod bind time. Grep confirms zero references to 'selected-node', 'WaitForFirstConsumer', or 'VolumeBinding' anywhere in crates/scheduler/*.rs.

Upstream kube-scheduler's VolumeBinding plugin does this: when a pod is bound to a node, if the pod references any unbound PVC whose StorageClass has volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer, the scheduler PATCHes pvc.metadata.annotations['volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node'] with the chosen node's name. This is the signal that external-provisioner sidecars are waiting for -- without it, the PVC stays Pending forever, and the pod stays ContainerCreating until it hits the 900s PodStart ceiling.

This affects ANY WaitForFirstConsumer PVC (direct or ephemeral-derived), not just the ephemeral-volume tests. The scout hit it via Generic Ephemeral tests (9 failures) but the bug is more general.

## Fix (direction only — worker implements)

In the scheduler's bind path (crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs; the current bind_pod / select_node_for_pod / select_node_with_capacity family), add logic:

1. Before/during bind, enumerate the pod's volumes for PVC references (spec.volumes[].persistentVolumeClaim.claimName + spec.volumes[].ephemeral (for ephemeral-derived PVCs, name is <pod-name>-<volume-name> per upstream convention)).
2. For each referenced PVC, look up its StorageClass and check .volumeBindingMode. If == "WaitForFirstConsumer" AND the PVC is unbound (spec.volumeName empty), PATCH pvc.metadata.annotations to add 'volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node' = chosen-node-name.
3. Do this AT or IMMEDIATELY BEFORE the pod bind PATCH so external-provisioner sees the signal before deciding whether to provision.

Upstream reference: kubernetes/kubernetes pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding/binder.go BindPodVolumes (bind_pod_volumes stage of the scheduler framework).

## Fail-on-revert test

Ideally: two-part test.
1. Unit: given a fake apiserver client, a pod with an ephemeral volumeClaimTemplate whose StorageClass is WaitForFirstConsumer, and a bind attempt to node X, assert the scheduler issues a PATCH to the PVC's annotations with selected-node=X.
2. Integration (if the scheduler has an integration harness): stand up a minimal apiserver + scheduler + upstream external-provisioner, create WaitForFirstConsumer StorageClass, create ephemeral-templated pod, assert PVC gets Bound within a reasonable window.

If the integration harness is absent or costly, unit test suffices.

Verify fail-on-revert: revert the annotation-stamping call, run the unit test, confirm it fails. Restore, confirm it passes.

## Acceptance

- cargo test --workspace green
- cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings clean
- Fail-on-revert unit test verified
- Manual live-verify: create a WaitForFirstConsumer StorageClass + a pod with ephemeral volumeClaimTemplate; confirm PVC becomes Bound within seconds and pod reaches Running (rather than sitting at ContainerCreating).

## Non-goals

- Do NOT touch the apiserver core_gen_adapter csi arm (mayor-suf4l Bug 1, filed separately) — different surface.
- Do NOT implement the entire upstream VolumeBinding plugin surface (topology-aware scheduling, delayed provisioning of pre-existing PVs, etc.). Just the selected-node stamping.
- Do NOT change the scheduler's node-selection algorithm — the fix is a PATCH after node selection, not a change to how nodes are picked.

## Cross-refs

- Parent triage bead: mayor-suf4l (14 failures, this bug accounts for 9 of them; the CSI-Ephemeral filed-separately covers 4; 1 unclassified 300s RWOP failure is separate).
- Scheduler current entry points: crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs (bind_pod, select_node_for_pod family). None currently touch PVCs.
- Related closed bug bead: none — this is a genuinely new gap.
- Memory reference: u7s-kubelet-is-stock-upstream-not-u7s-code (kubelet is upstream; the bug is on the u7s side that fails to signal it correctly).
close_reason: PR opened at https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/1051; scheduler stamps volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node on unbound WaitForFirstConsumer PVCs (direct + ephemeral-derived) at bind time via new stamp_selected_node_for_pvcs, invoked from bind_reserved_node before the pod bind POST.

title: fix(apiserver): add csi arm to gen_pod_spec_to_json (silent drop of spec.volumes[].csi on protobuf decode) (suf4l Bug 1)
description:
Add csi match arm to crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs gen_pod_spec_to_json to fix silent drop of spec.volumes[].csi on protobuf-decoded pod CREATE.

## Bug (verified via mayor-suf4l scout adde8650380bb7f3f, 2026-08-07)

crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs gen_pod_spec_to_json (~lines 1094-1259) has match arms for hostPath, emptyDir, secret, persistentVolumeClaim, downwardAPI, configMap, projected, image, ephemeral -- but NO arm for csi. The csi field EXISTS on the generated proto struct but is never read on decode.

Since e2e test framework's typed clientset defaults to protobuf, ANY pod with an inline CSI volume (spec.volumes[].csi.{driver, volumeAttributes, ...}) submitted via protobuf gets that volume source silently dropped. Kubelet then hangs to the 900s PodStart ceiling waiting for an unresolvable volume.

## Fix (mirrors two already-fixed sibling bugs in the same function)

Same bug class as:
- image (already fixed in same function)
- ephemeral (already fixed at core_gen_adapter.rs:1228-1246 with explicit comment: "client-go clientsets ... send protobuf by default ... without this branch the derived PVC template is silently dropped on decode"), with regression test at core_gen_adapter.rs:5234-5307

Add a csi match arm to gen_pod_spec_to_json. The csi handling for PersistentVolumeSource already exists elsewhere in this same file (~lines 2690-2797 in decode_persistentvolume_proto_gen) — mirror its structure.

Fields to handle for spec.volumes[].csi (from upstream Kubernetes CSIVolumeSource):
- driver (string, required)
- readOnly (bool)
- fsType (string)
- volumeAttributes (map[string]string)
- nodePublishSecretRef (LocalObjectReference: name)

## Fail-on-revert test

Add to the existing test module in core_gen_adapter.rs. Test shape (matches the ephemeral test at 5234-5307):
- Construct a pod proto with spec.volumes[].csi populated (driver, volumeAttributes, etc.)
- Decode via decode_pod_proto_gen
- Assert decoded pod.spec.volumes[0].csi contains ALL fields set

Verify fail-on-revert: revert the new csi arm, run just this test, confirm it fails. Restore, confirm it passes.

## Acceptance

- cargo test --workspace green
- cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings clean
- Fail-on-revert test verified via revert step
- LoC: expected <50 for the csi arm (~30 lines matching the ephemeral arm shape) + ~40 lines for the test

## Non-goals

- Do NOT touch the scheduler-side Generic Ephemeral bug (mayor-suf4l Bug 2, filed separately) — different surface, different fix.
- Do NOT touch decode_persistentvolume_proto_gen's csi handling — that already works and is not the bug.
- Do NOT extend beyond the csi arm — no scope creep into other missing/incomplete arms.

## Cross-refs

- Parent triage bead: mayor-suf4l (14 failures, this bug accounts for 4 of them)
- Related closed scouts: mayor-6q2v2 (triage), mayor-4w0j5, mayor-f4ml4
- Sibling bug (separate bead to file): scheduler VolumeBinding for WaitForFirstConsumer / selected-node stamping
- Precedent fix pattern: core_gen_adapter.rs:1228-1246 (ephemeral arm) + test at 5234-5307
close_reason: PR opened at https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/1050; added csi match arm to gen_pod_spec_to_json (core_gen_adapter.rs) mirroring the ephemeral arm, with a fail-on-revert regression test. cargo test --workspace and cargo clippy --workspace --tests -D warnings both green. Filed mayor-jacaa for an unrelated pre-existing flaky test discovered during verification (build_aggregated_discovery_increments_discovery_build_total races on a shared global counter).

title: [triage] ephemeral/inline-volume pods never reach Running, hit PodStart ceiling (14 failures)
description:
Signature: test framework's pod-Running/Ready wait times out before the pod ever reaches the expected phase. Two ceiling variants of the same mechanism:
  (a) `[FAILED] waiting for pod with inline volume: Timed out after 900.0XXs.` (15-minute ceiling; CSI/Generic Ephemeral-volume inline tests) -- 13 occurrences
  (b) `[FAILED] failed to wait for pod1 running status: Timed out after 300.001s.` (5-minute ceiling; ReadWriteOncePod test) -- 1 occurrence

14 failing tests (temp/csi-p4-failed-tests.txt, e2e.log block-start line):
1. L6461  [Testpattern: Generic Ephemeral-volume (block volmode) (late-binding)] ephemeral should support two pods which have the same volume definition
2. L7133  [Testpattern: Generic Ephemeral-volume (default fs) (late-binding)] ephemeral should create read-only inline ephemeral volume
3. L7481  [Testpattern: CSI Ephemeral-volume (default fs)] ephemeral should create read-only inline ephemeral volume
4. L8416  [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] read-write-once-pod should block a second pod from using an in-use ReadWriteOncePod volume on the same node (the 300s variant -- pod1, not the blocking pod, never reaches Running)
5. L9024  [Testpattern: Generic Ephemeral-volume (default fs) (late-binding)] ephemeral should create read/write inline ephemeral volume
6. L10874 [Testpattern: Generic Ephemeral-volume (block volmode) (late-binding)] ephemeral should support expansion of pvcs created for ephemeral pvcs
7. L11218 [Testpattern: Generic Ephemeral-volume (default fs) (late-binding)] ephemeral should support two pods which have the same volume definition
8. L11583 [Testpattern: CSI Ephemeral-volume (default fs)] ephemeral should support two pods which have the same volume definition
9. L12406 [Testpattern: CSI Ephemeral-volume (default fs)] ephemeral should support multiple inline ephemeral volumes
10. L12719 [Testpattern: Generic Ephemeral-volume (default fs) (late-binding)] ephemeral should support multiple inline ephemeral volumes
11. L15308 [Testpattern: Generic Ephemeral-volume (block volmode) (late-binding)] ephemeral should support multiple inline ephemeral volumes
12. L17748 [Testpattern: CSI Ephemeral-volume (default fs)] ephemeral should create read/write inline ephemeral volume
13. L18573 [Testpattern: Generic Ephemeral-volume (block volmode) (late-binding)] ephemeral should create read/write inline ephemeral volume
14. L18935 [Testpattern: Generic Ephemeral-volume (default fs) (late-binding)] ephemeral should support expansion of pvcs created for ephemeral pvcs

Sample failure bodies:
  e2e.log line 6680: [FAILED] waiting for pod with inline volume: Timed out after 900.005s.
    In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/storage/testsuites/ephemeral.go:426
  e2e.log line 8660: [FAILED] failed to wait for pod1 running status: Timed out after 300.001s.
    Expected Pod to be in <v1.PodPhase>: Running ... In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/storage/testsuites/readwriteoncepod.go:206

Suspected u7s mechanism: durations cluster tightly at 902-905s (i.e. right at the 900s/15min PodStart ceiling, meaning the pod NEVER became ready and the test waited the full timeout) -- this is not a slow-but-eventually-successful start, it's a hang. Per memory upstream-test-timeouts-are-ceilings-not-targets: these ceilings exist for legitimately slow environments, not as a target; a healthy stack should have these pods Ready in well under a minute. Ephemeral (inline CSI) volumes use a DIFFERENT provisioning path than Dynamic PV (no PVC/PV objects, volume is provisioned inline via the pod spec's `csi` volume source and a NodePublishVolume call keyed off the pod UID) -- since Dynamic PV tests in this same run DO succeed in provisioning within seconds, the bug is likely specific to the inline/ephemeral volume attach-and-mount path. Candidate u7s code path: kubelet's inline CSI ephemeral-volume handling (the code path that skips the PVC/PV/attach-detach-controller machinery and calls NodePublishVolume directly from the pod admission/sync loop) -- unconfirmed, needs a scout to trace one of these pods from creation to timeout via apiserver.log + kubelet log, the same methodology mayor-4w0j5 used for the Dynamic PV case.

Related beads/memories: same investigative approach as mayor-4w0j5 (timestamp reconstruction via apiserver.log) is the recommended next step; not yet attempted for the ephemeral-volume path specifically. Per u7s-is-default-suspect and upstream-tests-passing-means-bug-is-ours: default suspect is u7s kubelet's ephemeral-volume attach path, not the csi-hostpath driver (which is proven to work for Dynamic PV in the same run).

Reproduction hint: `--focus '\[sig-storage\] CSI Volumes \[Driver: csi-hostpath\] \[Testpattern: CSI Ephemeral-volume \(default fs\)\] ephemeral.*should create read-only inline ephemeral volume'`
notes:
SCOUT RESULT (adde8650380bb7f3f, 2026-08-07): Two data-locked root causes verified in u7s, csi-hostpath driver exonerated. Matches predicted 2-sub-mechanism split.

BUG 1 (CSI Ephemeral-volume inline, 4 failures):
- crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs gen_pod_spec_to_json (~lines 1094-1259) has match arms for hostPath, emptyDir, secret, persistentVolumeClaim, downwardAPI, configMap, projected, image, ephemeral — but NO arm for csi.
- Mayor VERIFIED: grep confirms the arms present and csi absent.
- Field exists on generated proto struct; never read on decode.
- Same bug class as two already-fixed siblings in same function: image and ephemeral (ephemeral fix at core_gen_adapter.rs:1228-1246 has explicit comment 'client-go clientsets... send protobuf by default... without this branch the derived PVC template is silently dropped on decode', with regression test at core_gen_adapter.rs:5234-5307).
- Since e2e test framework's typed clientset defaults to protobuf, inline CSI volumes get silently dropped on every Testpattern: CSI Ephemeral-volume test.
- Fix: add csi match arm to gen_pod_spec_to_json mirroring csi handling already present for PersistentVolumeSource in decode_persistentvolume_proto_gen (~lines 2690-2797). Fail-on-revert test in same style as the ephemeral test at 5234-5307.

BUG 2 (Generic Ephemeral-volume late-binding, 9 failures):
- Real upstream KCM's ephemeral-volume-controller correctly auto-creates the derived PVC within 3ms of pod create (u7s does NOT reimplement this — real KCM runs alongside u7s's own smaller controller-manager).
- BUT u7s scheduler binds pod directly with ZERO PVC interaction. Grep confirms no selected-node / WaitForFirstConsumer / VolumeBinding references anywhere in crates/scheduler/.
- Upstream kube-scheduler's VolumeBinding plugin stamps pvc.metadata.annotations['volume.kubernetes.io/selected-node'] at bind time — the signal external-provisioner needs before it provisions a WaitForFirstConsumer volume.
- Without it, any late-binding PVC (ephemeral-derived or plain) is permanently Pending → pod stuck ContainerCreating → 900s ceiling.
- Fix: scheduler bind path detects unbound WaitForFirstConsumer PVCs (direct or ephemeral-derived) and PATCHes selected-node before/at bind.

BEAD SHOULD BE SPLIT: these are 2 distinct fixes on different surfaces (apiserver core_gen_adapter vs scheduler), best filed as separate implementation beads. Bead ID mayor-suf4l should remain as the umbrella tracking; children file separately.

title: [triage] apiserver allows PVC size update when AllowVolumeExpansion=false (2 failures)
description:
Signature: `pvc "<name>" should not be allowed to be updated` -- the test creates a StorageClass with `allowVolumeExpansion` unset/false, creates a PVC from it, then attempts to PATCH the PVC's requested storage size upward, and asserts the API rejects that update. u7s's apiserver ACCEPTS the update instead of rejecting it.

2 failing tests (temp/csi-p4-failed-tests.txt):
1. e2e.log L8784  [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] volume-expand [It] should not allow expansion of pvcs without AllowVolumeExpansion property
2. e2e.log L18098 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] volume-expand [It] should not allow expansion of pvcs without AllowVolumeExpansion property (this one is compound: after the immutability assertion fails, cleanup ALSO hits the mayor-51z5g PV-still-exists-20m0s symptom -- see e2e.log line 18424)

Sample failure body (e2e.log lines 9010-9016, default-fs variant):
  [FAILED] Expected
      <*errors.StatusError | 0x...>:
      failed to expand PVC size (check logs for error): pvc csi-hostpathc6f5c should not be allowed to be updated
  In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/storage/testsuites/volume_expand.go:203

Block-volmode variant (e2e.log lines 18557-18563) is byte-for-byte the same shape of assertion failure against a different PVC name.

Suspected u7s mechanism: this is a genuine apiserver validation/admission gap, NOT csi-hostpath-specific. Upstream Kubernetes rejects a PVC `spec.resources.requests.storage` increase at admission time when the bound StorageClass has `allowVolumeExpansion: false` (or is unset, which defaults to false) -- this is core PVC immutability validation, unrelated to the CSI driver's plugin capabilities. u7s's apiserver is letting the PATCH through. Candidate u7s code path: PVC update/admission validation (likely near crates/apiserver's handlers for persistentvolumeclaims update, wherever immutable-field checks for PVC spec live -- e.g. handlers/pvc.rs or a shared validation module; the researcher did not have time to confirm the exact file, this needs a scout to grep for existing PVC immutable-field checks such as volumeName/storageClassName and find why storage-size-increase-without-allowVolumeExpansion isn't checked alongside them).

Priority rationale: P1 despite being only 2 CSI-hostpath failures -- this is a base apiserver admission bug that could affect ANY storage-class-driven PVC resize test, not just csi-hostpath, and represents a real conformance gap (PVC validation, not a CSI plugin behavior).

Related beads/memories: none pre-existing. This was called out in mayor-6q2v2's brief as an expected ~2-count cluster ("pvc ... should not be allowed to be updated: u7s apiserver not enforcing a PVC immutability constraint") and this triage confirms it exactly as predicted.

Reproduction hint: `--focus '\[sig-storage\] CSI Volumes \[Driver: csi-hostpath\] \[Testpattern: Dynamic PV \(default fs\)\] volume-expand.*should not allow expansion of pvcs without AllowVolumeExpansion property'`
close_reason: PR opened at https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/1048; added AllowVolumeExpansion admission check to PUT (replace_namespaced_resource) and PATCH (do_patch) PVC write paths in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs, matching upstream PersistentVolumeClaimResize admission plugin's 403 Forbidden message.

title: [triage] pod won't terminate within 5min in VAC/volume-expand DeferCleanup, cascades to PV 20m timeout (7 failures)
description:
Signature: DeferCleanup(Each) fails with `pod "<name>" was not deleted: expected pod to not be found: Timed out after 300.001s` (5-minute pod-delete ceiling), which then cascades into the SAME test's PV wait also hitting `PersistentVolume ... still exists within 20m0s` (see mayor-51z5g). All 7 occurrences are in the VolumeAttributesClass (volume-modify) or volume-expand [DeferCleanup]/[It] families for BLOCK volmode -- never seen in the default-fs variants of the same test names.

7 failing tests (temp/csi-p4-failed-tests.txt, e2e.log block-start line):
1. L7828  [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] volume-modify [FeatureGate:VolumeAttributesClass] [DeferCleanup (Each)] should modify volume that already has a VAC
2. L9389  [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)(allowExpansion)] volume-expand [DeferCleanup (Each)] should resize volume when PVC is edited while pod is using it
3. L13313 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] volume-modify [FeatureGate:VolumeAttributesClass] [DeferCleanup (Each)] should modify volume with no VAC
4. L14194 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] volume-modify [FeatureGate:VolumeAttributesClass] [DeferCleanup (Each)] should recover from invalid target VAC by updating PVC to new valid VAC
5. L15666 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)(allowExpansion)] volume-expand [It] should resize volume when PVC is edited and the pod is re-created on the same node after controller resize is finished
6. L16268 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] volume-modify [FeatureGate:VolumeAttributesClass] [DeferCleanup (Each)] should create a volume with VAC
7. L17151 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)(allowExpansion)] volume-expand [It] Verify if offline PVC expansion works

Sample failure body (block L7828, e2e.log lines 8265 and 8152):
  [FAILED] DeferCleanup callback returned error: pod "pod-045a0b3d-e49f-48f0-99cb-6a3b57de9ecb" was not deleted: expected pod to not be found: Timed out after 300.002s.
  ... (later in the same block)
  persistent Volume pvc-fcf7d436-3f00-49d8-9132-f4548d229001 not deleted by dynamic provisioner: PersistentVolume pvc-fcf7d436-3f00-49d8-9132-f4548d229001 still exists within 20m0s

Suspected u7s mechanism: unlike mayor-51z5g's already-diagnosed mechanism (sonobuoy watchdog externally PATCHing deletionTimestamp on the CSI-driver NAMESPACE after 10 minutes Active), this cluster's PROXIMATE failure is the TEST POD itself not terminating within 5 minutes -- before the watchdog's 10-minute window would even be reached in most of these (durations here are 1500-1600s total, i.e. ~5min pod-delete-timeout + ~20min PV-delete-timeout, not a namespace reap). This looks like a genuine pod-termination hang specific to block-volmode volumes under VolumeAttributesClass modification / controller-resize flows: something (kubelet's SIGTERM/finalize path, or the CSI NodeUnstage/NodeUnpublish being blocked by a still-attached block device) is preventing the pod object from being removed, which then blocks the CSI external-provisioner's DeleteVolume call, which then blocks the PV finalizer removal for the full 20 minutes on top.

Candidate u7s code paths (unconfirmed -- needs scout with in-band inspection of pod deletion for a repro of one of these 7):
- kubelet pod-termination / volume-teardown ordering for block-mode devices specifically (does u7s kubelet wait correctly for CSI NodeUnstageVolume completion before finalizing pod deletion, or can it deadlock if the device is still considered "in use" by a resize/modify operation in flight?)
- crates/apiserver PVC/PV finalizer removal path interacting with an in-flight VolumeAttributesClass modification
This is "unknown -- needs scout with in-band inspection," not yet root-caused to a specific file:line.

Related beads/memories: mayor-51z5g (P1, open) diagnoses the TERMINAL symptom (PV still-exists-20m0s) via a DIFFERENT proximate cause (harness watchdog reaping the CSI driver namespace at 10min for [Slow]-tagged multiVolume tests). This cluster shares the terminal symptom but has direct evidence of a DIFFERENT proximate cause (pod won't delete at the 5-minute DeferCleanup ceiling, in non-[Slow] volume-modify/volume-expand tests). Do not conflate the two mechanisms when working mayor-51z5g -- recommend mayor-51z5g's fix (bump watchdog Active threshold) will NOT resolve this cluster.

Reproduction hint: `--focus '\[sig-storage\] CSI Volumes \[Driver: csi-hostpath\] \[Testpattern: Dynamic PV \(block volmode\)\] volume-modify \[FeatureGate:VolumeAttributesClass\].*should create a volume with VAC'`

title: [triage] pod-exec can't see mounted volume content/device right after (re)mount (cat/dd/test-b/subPath) (14 failures)
description:
Signature: kubectl exec into a csi-hostpath-mounted pod fails with a "No such file or directory" style error reading content or checking a device node that a prior step in the SAME test already created/wrote. Three surface variants of one mechanism:
  (a) `cat <path>/index.html` -> `cat: <path>: No such file or directory` / `command terminated with exit code 1`
  (b) `dd if=<path>/file1.txt ... | sha256sum | grep -Fq <hash>` -> `command terminated with exit code 1`, stderr `dd: can't open '<path>': No such file or directory`
  (c) `test -b <path>` (block volmode device-node check) -> `should succeed, but failed with exit code 1`
  (d) subPath variant: `open /test-volume/test-file: no such file or directory` on pod re-create

14 failing tests (from temp/csi-p4-failed-tests.txt, run 0807-0450, e2e.log line numbers of the block start):
1. L9  [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (filesystem volmode)] multiVolume [Slow] should concurrently access the volume and its clone from pods on the same node [Feature:VolumeSourceXFS] -- cat /mnt/volume1/index.html
2. L339 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] provisioning should provision storage with pvc data source in parallel [Slow] -- cat /opt/0/index.html (5 pods: hostpath-0..4-client, ALL 5 fail identically)
3. L808 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (filesystem volmode)] multiVolume [Slow] should access to two volumes with the same volume mode and retain data across pod recreation -- dd/sha256sum on /mnt/volume1/file1.txt
4. L1485 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] multiVolume [Slow] should concurrently access the volume and restored snapshot from pods on the same node [Feature:VolumeSnapshotDataSource][Feature:VolumeSourceXFS] -- test -b /opt/0
5. L2405 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (filesystem volmode)] multiVolume [Slow] should concurrently access the single volume from pods on the same node -- dd/sha256sum on /mnt/volume1/file1.txt
6. L3420 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] provisioning should provision storage with snapshot data source [Feature:VolumeSnapshotDataSource] -- test -b /opt/0 (NOTE: reaches this check at all, meaning it got PAST the snapshot-datasource step -- does not hit the mayor-cst7t 404; anomalous, worth a follow-up read of provisioning.go's snapshot-data-source path for block volmode)
7. L3697 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] provisioning should provision storage with pvc data source -- test -b /opt/0
8. L4147 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] multiVolume [Slow] should access to two volumes with the same volume mode and retain data across pod recreation -- test -b /mnt/volume1 (compound: ALSO hits PV-still-exists-20m0s x2 afterward, see mayor-51z5g cross-ref)
9. L5429 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] multiVolume [Slow] should concurrently access the volume and its clone from pods on the same node [Feature:VolumeSourceXFS] -- test -b /opt/0 (compound with PV-still-exists)
10. L5934 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] multiVolume [Slow] should access to two volumes with different volume mode and retain data across pod recreation -- test -b /mnt/volume1 (compound with PV-still-exists)
11. L10024 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] volumes should store data -- cat /opt/0/index.html (THIS IS THE mayor-4w0j5 TARGET TEST, default-fs variant)
12. L11947 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] subPath should support existing directories when readOnly specified in the volumeSource -- open /test-volume/test-file: no such file or directory on pod re-create
13. L16877 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] provisioning should provision storage with pvc data source -- cat /opt/0/index.html
14. L19258 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] volumes should store data -- test -b /opt/0 (block-volmode sibling of mayor-4w0j5's target test; ALSO compounds into PV-still-exists-20m0s, see mayor-51z5g cross-ref)

Suspected u7s mechanism: mayor-4w0j5 (closed, P1) already produced hard evidence for the default-fs "volumes should store data" case: pod1 writes index.html, pod1 is deleted+unmounted, pod2 mounts the SAME volume_id and SAME staging_target_path (confirmed identical at the CSI gRPC layer), and pod2's cat fails with "No such file or directory" 43.8s into the test. mayor-f4ml4 (closed) tried to reproduce this manually via kubectl on the same VM/stack and could NOT reproduce it -- data persisted correctly, no admission/defaulting mutation found in a fresh gRPC diff. f4ml4's closing note: the original failure had only ~0.93s between NodePublishVolume success and the test's exec+cat, while the manual repro had >15s dwell time before the cat -- suggesting a **timing-sensitive race between kubelet's Ready-signal for the new mount and bind-mount visibility inside the container**, not a deterministic data-loss or path-mutation bug. That hypothesis is UNPROVEN, not disproven. The dd/checksum and test -b variants in this cluster are the same shape of failure (exec into pod immediately after a mount-related step fails to see expected content/device) and should be treated as more data points for the SAME race, not separate bugs, until proven otherwise.

Candidate u7s code paths (unconfirmed, needs a scout with in-band inspection immediately around a NodePublishVolume-success -> kubelet-Ready -> pod-exec sequence, sub-second resolution):
- kubelet mount-propagation / bind-mount setup timing (do we ack "container Ready" before the bind mount is fully visible in the container's mount namespace?)
- crates/apiserver's pod status PATCH path -- does u7s's kubelet report Ready before or after CSI NodePublishVolume's mount is guaranteed visible?
This is explicitly flagged as "unknown -- needs scout with in-band inspection," per mayor-f4ml4's own next-step recommendation (scripted sub-second cat immediately after pod Ready to try to trigger the race).

Related closed beads / memories: mayor-4w0j5 (closed, positive finding, default-fs variant), mayor-f4ml4 (closed, negative manual repro, timing-race hypothesis). Memory: manual-kubectl-repro-can-fail-to-reproduce-tight-timing-races. Per u7s-is-default-suspect framing: do NOT conclude "csi-hostpath driver bug" -- driver is LAST suspect and f4ml4's gRPC diff already showed the driver was asked for consistent volume_id/staging paths.

Reproduction hint: `--focus '\[sig-storage\] CSI Volumes \[Driver: csi-hostpath\] \[Testpattern: Dynamic PV \(default fs\)\] volumes should store data'` (simplest repro, matches mayor-4w0j5's original target).

title: Triage all 49 failures from csi-hostpath --procs=4 run (0807-0450). Cluster by signature, file one bead per cluster
description:
GOAL: Triage all 49 test failures in temp/e2e/0807-0450--driver-csi-hostpath/plugins/e2e/results/global/e2e.log. Cluster by shared error signature. File ONE bead per distinct signature cluster (do NOT file 49 individual beads — that's noise; do NOT file one monolithic bead — that's unhelpful). Each bead's description enumerates the failing tests in that cluster + captures the shared error mechanism + names candidate u7s code paths responsible.

## Source data (all in mayor checkout, gitignored)

- Full e2e log: `temp/e2e/0807-0450--driver-csi-hostpath/plugins/e2e/results/global/e2e.log` (19765 lines, 49 FAILED blocks)
- Deduped test names list: `temp/csi-p4-failed-tests.txt` (49 distinct names)
- Per-test artifacts (per-test csi-driver logs, pod events): `temp/e2e/0807-0450--driver-csi-hostpath/plugins/e2e/results/global/_sig-storage_CSI_Volumes/<test-name-normalized>/...`
- Prior investigation: `temp/e2e-memory-samples/scout-csi-slow/timeline.txt` (mayor-4w0j5's data-integrity finding for `volumes should store data`, 43.8s pod2-cat-fails)
- Prior investigation: `temp/e2e-memory-samples/scout-csi-remount/findings.md` (mayor-f4ml4's manual-repro NEGATIVE result — same scenario passed at leisure; possible timing-sensitive race)
- Test source (cache to temp/research/ if not present): fetch each failing test's ginkgo `It` block from upstream `kubernetes/kubernetes@release-1.36` (paths visible in the failure lines, e.g. `k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/storage/testsuites/multivolume.go:297`)

## Rough signature clustering (mayor's initial pass, verify)

- **~17 "PersistentVolume ... still exists within 20m0s"**: the PV cleanup timeout. Test framework's `WaitForPersistentVolumeDeleted` at framework/podlogs. Related to mayor-51z5g symptom (watchdog reaps CSI namespace) but the ROOT is upstream — see mayor-4w0j5 timeline for data-persistence-across-remount hypothesis (pod2 cat fails after pod1 delete).
- **~11 "command terminated with exit code 1"**: pod exec failure — usually `cat` or similar shell command returning non-zero. Same fingerprint as mayor-4w0j5's finding.
- **~2 "pvc ... should not be allowed to be updated"**: u7s apiserver not enforcing a PVC immutability constraint.
- **~13 duration-clustered at ~904 seconds (15 min)**: likely PodStart wait timeout — pods that never became Ready.
- **Multiple fast failures (10-80s)**: real assertion failures. Read the failure body to categorize.
- **Snapshot family (~6)**: likely blocked on VolumeSnapshot API gap (mayor-cst7t, already scoped). Do NOT re-file — reference mayor-cst7t.
- **VolumeAttributesClass family**: likely blocked on missing FeatureGate:VolumeAttributesClass (upstream feature u7s doesn't implement). File one bead per distinct missing-feature signature.

## Framing (STRICT — do not deviate)

**u7s is DEFAULT SUSPECT** (apiserver, KCM, scheduler, kubelet, conformance harness). csi-hostpath driver is LAST suspect. See memories `upstream-tests-passing-means-bug-is-ours` and `upstream-test-timeouts-are-ceilings-not-targets`.

**Do NOT propose timeout bumps.** Do NOT reach for "test is unrealistic."

## Per-cluster memo — what each bead needs

Each filed bead (`bd create` with `--description-file /path/to/tempfile`) MUST include:

1. **Title**: `[triage] <one-line signature> (N failures)` — short, actionable, avoids the generic "csi-hostpath failure" phrasing.
2. **Type**: `bug`.
3. **Priority**: P1 if the cluster has ≥5 failures OR the mechanism looks likely to affect non-csi-hostpath tests too (e.g. base handler bug). P2 for smaller / more contained clusters. P3 for known-scoped (e.g. deferred snapshot feature).
4. **Description**:
   - **Signature**: exact error line format (e.g. "PersistentVolume PVC-UID still exists within 20m0s")
   - **N failing tests**: enumerated list of test names (from `temp/csi-p4-failed-tests.txt` matches).
   - **Sample failure bodies**: grep 2-3 representative test blocks from `e2e.log` and include the first ~20 lines of each (via `Read`; keep the raw form).
   - **Suspected u7s mechanism**: 1-2 candidate hypotheses with concrete file:line pointers in u7s code (`crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs`, `handlers/defaults.rs`, etc.) OR "unknown — needs scout with in-band inspection". Do NOT speculate wildly; if you don't have evidence, say so.
   - **Related closed beads / memories**: reference mayor-4w0j5, mayor-f4ml4, mayor-51z5g, mayor-cst7t where applicable.
   - **Reproduction hint**: the `--focus` string that would isolate ONE test in the cluster for future debugging.

## Cross-reference guidance

If a failing test is already covered by an existing open bead (e.g. `mayor-cst7t` for VolumeSnapshot failures), do NOT file a new bead for it — add the test name(s) to the existing bead's notes via `bd update <id> --notes "..."`.

Existing beads relevant to this triage:
- **mayor-cst7t** (P3) — VolumeSnapshot API gap (all snapshot-related failures likely go here)
- **mayor-51z5g** (P1, revised notes) — watchdog symptom, NOT the fix
- **mayor-4w0j5** (closed) — data-integrity finding for "volumes should store data" at 43.8s
- **mayor-f4ml4** (closed) — manual repro of that finding failed to reproduce; likely timing-sensitive
- **mayor-4dtlb** (P2, queued) — Phase-3 --procs override, blocked on PR #1047

## Time budget

**90 minutes wall-clock TOTAL.** Reading 49 failure bodies + clustering + per-cluster memo writing is the core work. Bead-filing is fast at the end.

## Deliverable — return format (under 800 words)

```
# csi-hostpath --procs=4 (run 0807-0450) triage -- 2026-08-07

## TL;DR
N clusters filed as beads, M pre-existing bead updates, K failures deferred (why).

## Clusters filed
- mayor-<id>: <one-line signature> — <count> failures, priority P<n>, top candidate mechanism
- (repeat per cluster)

## Existing beads updated
- mayor-<id>: added <N> failing test names, adjusted description if needed

## Failures not filed (with reason)
- <test name>: <why not filed — e.g. one-off, out of scope, already covered>

## What I could NOT determine
- Which clusters need in-band investigation (mayor-4w0j5-style) to root-cause the mechanism, vs which have obvious mechanisms readable from the failure body alone.
```

## Constraints

- Read-only investigation until you file beads at the end.
- File beads via `bd create --description-file /path/to/tempfile` (avoids shell escaping issues with long descriptions).
- Do NOT edit any repo code. Do NOT commit or push.
- Do NOT close any existing beads.

title: Scout: root-cause the mayor-4w0j5 pod2-cat-fails failure - is it u7s path-mutation, apiserver defaulting, or actual data-loss?
description:
GOAL: Root-cause the specific failure captured by scout mayor-4w0j5: `[Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] volumes should store data` fails at 43.8s because pod2 cats `/opt/0/index.html` (written by pod1) and gets "No such file or directory".

Prior scout captured the STEP-BY-STEP timeline in `temp/e2e-memory-samples/scout-csi-slow/timeline.txt`. That timeline SHOWS the driver logs claim "SAME staging_target_path, SAME volume_id 3489bcdd-9217-...-b612ee8ff7f5" for both pod1 and pod2. But the timeline was reconstructed from what the driver LOGGED, not from ground-truth apiserver payloads and container-side introspection.

## Framing (STRICT — do not deviate)

**Default suspect ordering (operator direction 2026-08-07)**:
1. u7s apiserver (defaulting, admission, mutation) — MOST likely
2. u7s KCM/scheduler wiring — plausible
3. Test setup / u7s conformance harness — plausible
4. csi-hostpath driver itself — LAST suspect; upstream-known-good. Only consider this after 1-3 have been affirmatively ruled out with evidence.

Anti-patterns:
- Do NOT assume "the driver is buggy" without ruling out u7s first.
- Do NOT propose bumping timeouts or delays.
- Do NOT reach for "test is unrealistic" — this test passes upstream.
- Do NOT commit to a specific mechanism until the write-vs-read evidence is captured.

## Key questions to answer (in order)

### Q1: Is the SAME volume actually mounted for pod2 as pod1?

**Two independent verifications required**:

(a) **Compare gRPC-level payloads at the u7s wire**. Look at the csi-provisioner sidecar log AND the hostpath-plugin container log for both pod1's and pod2's NodeStageVolume/NodePublishVolume calls. Extract: `volume_id`, `staging_target_path`, `target_path`, `volume_attributes` (JSON map), `pv_or_volume_context`. If ANY field differs between pod1 and pod2, that's a genuine "u7s asked for a different mount" -- the driver is doing what it's told, u7s asked wrong.

(b) **Verify the api-payload side**. Check the apiserver.log entries for what kubelet's csi-node-driver-registrar published: the pod spec's `spec.containers[].volumeMounts[].mountPath` on pod1 and pod2. If u7s defaulting mutated pod2's mountPath, the container is looking in a different place inside its filesystem than where the file was written.

**If Q1 shows same-in-all-fields**: the u7s-side plumbing is symmetric. Move to Q2.
**If Q1 shows any drift**: file the drift as the primary finding. That's the bug.

### Q2: If the same volume is asked for, is the DATA actually gone?

**Approach**: reproduce the test manually, but with in-band inspection between steps:

1. Kick off the test via `run-all.sh --focus '\[sig-storage\] CSI Volumes \[Driver: csi-hostpath\] \[Testpattern: Dynamic PV \(default fs\)\] volumes should store data'` OR construct an equivalent 2-pod PVC scenario yourself via kubectl manifests (simpler for observation).

2. Between pod1 write and pod1 deletion: `limactl shell lima-node-4 sudo ls -la /var/lib/csi-hostpath-data/<volume_id>/` (or wherever csi-hostpath stores its backing data on the node -- may need a `find /var/lib -name 'index.html' 2>/dev/null` to locate). Confirm the file exists here on the node's local disk.

3. After pod1 delete, before pod2 mount: same ls. Is the file STILL there in the driver's backing store, or has NodeUnpublishVolume / NodeUnstageVolume cleared it? This SHOULD show the file still present -- csi-hostpath's unstage cleans up the STAGING mount, not the underlying data.

4. After pod2 mount, before pod2 exec: same ls at the SAME driver-backing-store path. Is the file gone (data loss)? Is the file present but at a different path than pod2's container sees (path-mismatch)?

Correspondingly, DURING pod2's mount but BEFORE the cat, `limactl shell lima-node-4 sudo find /var/lib -path '*csi-hostpath*' -name 'index.html' 2>/dev/null` should show WHERE the file actually is on the host filesystem.

Match that against pod2's actual mount tree: `kubectl exec pod2 -- mount | head`, `kubectl exec pod2 -- ls -la /opt/0/`.

### Q3: If Q2 shows the file exists on-disk but pod2 can't see it, IS u7s mangling paths?

**Check for u7s force-defaulting** (operator's specific concern about "different driver plugin" or path mutation):

- What CSIDriver object exists in the cluster? `kubectl get csidriver -o yaml`. Is u7s picking the right one for the pod's PVC binding?
- Does pod2's spec at ADMISSION time (before it hits kubelet) match what the test framework POSTed? Extract from apiserver.log the exact JSON body of the pod2 POST + any subsequent PATCH modifications. Compare against what the ginkgo source's `create-pod-with-pvc` helper actually built.
- Does u7s have a mutating webhook / defaulting handler that could rewrite volumeMounts? Grep `crates/apiserver/src/handlers/defaults.rs` and `handlers/pods.rs` for mountPath, volumeMounts, subPath rewriting logic.

### Q4: Is there an admission or defaulting difference between pod1 and pod2?

- Both pods are ephemeral test pods created back-to-back in the same namespace. What's the exact ginkgo helper source that creates them? Fetch: `test/e2e/storage/testsuites/volumes.go` (or wherever this test lives — `Testpattern: Dynamic PV volumes should store data` is somewhere in test/e2e/storage/).
- Extract the POST body for both pod creations from apiserver.log. Diff them structurally. Are they identical apart from name/uid/timestamps?
- If different: what's different, and is u7s the source of the difference?

## Investigation methodology

**This is a live-verify scout, not a memo scout**. You'll need to:
- Bring up a stack on lima-node-4 (Running per limactl list; reset only if needed)
- Reproduce the test (via `run-all.sh --focus` or manual manifests)
- Do in-band inspection between test steps (kubectl exec, limactl shell filesystem checks)
- Read apiserver.log for the specific request-ids
- Read csi-hostpath plugin logs
- Cross-ref u7s source when a hypothesis lands

## Assigned resources

- **VM**: lima-node-4 (Running from prior scout). Port 6446, kubelet port 10253. Workdir: `temp/scout-csi-remount/` (isolate; do NOT reuse temp/scout-csi-slow/ which may have leftover state).
- **Do NOT touch**: lima-node (operator run), lima-node-3 (operator extra-node), lima-node-5 (mp7z1's 12GiB VM, still up).
- **Time bound**: 60 minutes wall-clock TOTAL.

## Tooling rules (mandatory)

- One command per Bash call. Never chain unrelated commands with && ; |
- Never inline env vars or `export`. First token allowlisted binaries only: git, cargo, gh, kubectl, bd, limactl, jq, rustc, rustup, scripts/...
- kubeconfig: pass `--kubeconfig <path>` as a flag, never `export KUBECONFIG`.
- Do NOT start a call with `cd`. Use `git -C <path> ...` or CWD.
- Use `jq` for JSON. Never `python3 -c`.
- Use `Read` for file reads. Never `cat`, `head`, `tail` via Bash.
- Use `Grep` for search. Never shell `grep`/`find` for file I/O.
- `mcp__mcpls__*` LSP tools available for u7s Rust source navigation.

title: Scout: root-cause csi-hostpath slowness via single --focus on 'Dynamic PV (default fs) volumes should store data' - simplest test no Feature deps
description:
GOAL: Root-cause the u7s slowness that makes csi-hostpath e2e tests take 10+ minutes when upstream Kubernetes completes them in 2-3 minutes. Do this via targeted --focus runs on ONE specific, simple, well-defined test first.

## Framing (STRICT — do not deviate)

The current csi-hostpath run (temp/e2e/0807-csi-hostpath-streamed-e2e.log) shows 42 distinct failing test names. Many hit a "PersistentVolume ... still exists within 20m0s" error via a per-test-namespace CSI driver getting reaped by the u7s watchdog after 10 minutes -- see mayor-51z5g's revised notes.

**The 10-minute watchdog reap is a SYMPTOM, not the root cause.** These tests should complete in 2-3 minutes on a healthy stack (upstream does). Something in u7s is 3-5x slower than expected. Your job is to find WHAT is slow, WHY, and WHERE (which u7s code path is at fault).

Anti-patterns to AVOID:
- Do NOT propose bumping any u7s timeout (watchdog thresholds, sonobuoy plugin timeouts, KCM controller sync period, etc.) to accommodate the slowness. Timeouts are ceilings, not targets. See memories: upstream-test-timeouts-are-ceilings-not-targets, upstream-tests-passing-means-bug-is-ours.
- Do NOT assume "the test is unrealistic" or "cloud environments are different." Read the test's actual assertion path from upstream source before making any such claim.

## Assigned resources

- **VM**: lima-node-4 (currently Running, previous scout left it up; verify state and reuse OR reset via run-all.sh --reset). Port 6446, kubelet port 10253. Do NOT touch lima-node, lima-node-2, lima-node-3, lima-node-5, lima-node-smoke.
- **Workdir**: temp/scout-csi-slow/ (isolated from mayor's temp/u7s and other scouts).
- **Time budget**: 60 minutes wall-clock TOTAL.

## Primary target: ONE test, deeply investigated

Focus regex (ginkgo): `[sig-storage] CSI Volumes \[Driver: csi-hostpath\] \[Testpattern: Dynamic PV \(default fs\)\] volumes should store data`

This is the simplest possible csi-hostpath test: create PVC (dynamic provision) -> pod mounts it -> writes data -> reads it back -> cleanup. If THIS is slow, the entire csi-hostpath cascade is caused by whatever is slow here.

## Approach

### Phase 0: Setup (~10 min)

1. Read ai/prompts/vm-operations.md IN FULL before invoking run-all.sh. Cite it in return, don't restate.
2. Verify lima-node-4 state. If dirty, reset via `scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --reset --stack-only --vm lima-node-4 --port 6446 --workdir ./temp/scout-csi-slow --verbose`. If clean (single-node stack ready, no leftover sonobuoy resources), use as-is.
3. Verify apiserver logging is at INFO level with request timestamps (--verbose enables this).

### Phase 1: Run the ONE test in isolation (~10 min)

```
scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --vm lima-node-4 --port 6446 --workdir ./temp/scout-csi-slow --focus '\[sig-storage\] CSI Volumes \[Driver: csi-hostpath\] \[Testpattern: Dynamic PV \(default fs\)\] volumes should store data'
```

Expect: this test SHOULD complete in 2-3 minutes on a healthy stack. If it takes >5 minutes OR hits the 20m0s PV-deletion timeout, that's the reproduction.

Capture wall-clock time from ginkgo output.

### Phase 2: Timestamp reconstruction (this is the actual investigation)

The apiserver log (temp/scout-csi-slow/apiserver.log OR the equivalent under your workdir; verify path) is the source of truth. Extract the request-id chain for the PVC/PV lifecycle:

1. Test creates namespace (POST /api/v1/namespaces/...)
2. Test creates CSI driver StatefulSet in <basename>-<suffix> namespace
3. Kubelet reports csi-hostpathplugin-0 Ready (kubelet PATCH pod status)
4. Test creates StorageClass
5. Test creates PVC in test namespace (POST persistentvolumeclaims)
6. csi-provisioner sidecar issues CreateVolume gRPC to the hostpath driver -- observable via csi-provisioner PATCH on PV
7. u7s apiserver + KCM PV-binder bind PVC to PV (PATCH pvc/status setting VolumeName; PATCH pv/status setting ClaimRef)
8. Pod created (POST pods)
9. Scheduler binds pod to node
10. Kubelet pulls container image (visible via events + kubelet log if --verbose)
11. Pod becomes Ready (PATCH pod/status)
12. Test writes data, reads data (Exec into pod)
13. Test deletes pod (DELETE pods/...)
14. Test deletes PVC (DELETE pvcs)
15. csi-provisioner observes PV Released, calls DeleteVolume gRPC, PATCH removes external-provisioner finalizer
16. PV disappears (kubernetes.io/pv-protection finalizer clears)

For EACH step, extract the timestamp from apiserver.log. Compute the delta between steps. Identify the STEP with the largest delta.

Store the timeline in temp/e2e-memory-samples/scout-csi-slow/timeline.txt. Concrete format:

```
step  timestamp                    delta_ms  description
1     2026-08-07T12:00:00.000Z          -    namespace created
2     2026-08-07T12:00:01.234Z       1234    CSI driver StatefulSet POST
3     2026-08-07T12:00:15.678Z      14444    csi-hostpathplugin-0 first Ready
...
```

The line with the biggest delta is the primary bottleneck. Investigate it further.

### Phase 3: Root-cause the biggest delta (~20 min)

Once you know WHERE the time goes, ask WHY:
- Is it apiserver latency? (grep the log for the specific request-ids' latency_ms field)
- Is it KCM controller cycle time? (KCM logs live in `temp/scout-csi-slow/kcm.log` OR similar; read for controller-reconcile events)
- Is it kubelet lifecycle latency? (kubelet log via limactl shell)
- Is it external-provisioner sidecar not observing an event? (csi-provisioner logs via `kubectl -n <driver-ns> logs csi-hostpathplugin-0 -c csi-provisioner`)
- Is it CSI driver-side (hostpath-plugin) taking too long on CreateVolume? (kubectl logs, same pod, `-c hostpath` container)

The candidate bottleneck sites, ranked by "if I were designing u7s I'd worry about these first":
- **Watch event delivery lag**: does external-provisioner see the PV Released event within seconds, or minutes? Compare apiserver.log timestamp of pv/status write to csi-provisioner-side log timestamp of the reconcile.
- **Missing defaulting or webhook step**: does u7s apiserver skip a field-defaulting step that upstream does, so the CSI driver receives an object it can't act on until some other controller fills in the field?
- **Missing event emission**: many controllers wait for specific Events. If u7s doesn't emit an event upstream KCM/csi-provisioner watches for, the reconciler stays quiet until its resync period (often minutes).
- **KCM PV binder retry loop**: if the initial bind fails or races, KCM backs off exponentially. First retry might be seconds, second minutes.

### Phase 4: Cross-reference upstream expected behavior

If the biggest delta is on a specific step (e.g. "PVC bind takes 90 seconds instead of 500ms"), fetch the upstream code for that specific path:
- external-provisioner: https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/external-provisioner
- kube-controller-manager PV binder: k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume
- CSI hostpath driver: https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-driver-host-path

Cache fetched files into temp/research/ (already the project convention). Grep locally.

Compare what upstream expects u7s to do vs what u7s actually does (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/*, crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs).

### Phase 5: Report (findings memo)

Deliverable: temp/e2e-memory-samples/scout-csi-slow/findings.md AND a memo returned in your final message.

title: watchdog in 06-run-sonobuoy.sh reaps CSI-driver namespaces mid-[Slow]-test, orphans PVs, causes 32+ false-positive still-exists-within-20m0s failures
description:
Root cause of the ~32 "PersistentVolume ... not deleted by dynamic provisioner: still exists within 20m0s" failures on the 0807 csi-hostpath --procs=4 run (temp/e2e/0807-csi-hostpath-streamed-e2e.log). NOT a u7s apiserver bug -- a u7s conformance HARNESS bug in scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh watchdog_loop().

## Mechanism (confirmed via apiserver log 2026-08-07)

Upstream csi-hostpath test framework deploys per-test-namespace the CSI driver StatefulSet into namespace <basename>-<random-suffix>. Example: multiVolume test creates namespace multivolume-3161 (test namespace) AND multivolume-3161-7041 (CSI driver namespace) via storageframework. The driver namespace hosts the csi-hostpathplugin-0 StatefulSet including the external-provisioner sidecar.

Tests can legitimately take >10 minutes. Examples:
- [sig-storage] CSI Volumes [Driver: csi-hostpath] multiVolume [Slow] should concurrently access the volume and restored snapshot from pods on the same node [Feature:VolumeSnapshotDataSource]

The current watchdog_loop in 06-run-sonobuoy.sh reaps ANY non-system namespace after 10 minutes in Active phase. Timeline for one failure (confirmed via apiserver.log):

- 01:50:44Z: multivolume-3161-7041 created, csi-hostpathplugin-0 running
- 01:50:46Z: pvc-9ad38927 dynamically provisioned by csi-hostpath-multivolume-3161
- 01:50:xx through 02:01:xx: test runs, ~10 min 31 sec
- 02:01:15.338Z: kubectl-patch on namespaces/multivolume-3161-7041 (user_agent=kubectl/v1.36.1 darwin/arm64) sets deletionTimestamp -- this is the WATCHDOG
- 02:01:15.4xxZ: kubelet emits container-death events, csi-hostpathplugin-0 gone
- 02:01:15.620Z: kubelet GET csi-hostpathplugin-0 -> 404
- ~02:15:56Z: test cleanup runs CleanupResource, deletes PVC, waits for PV -- PV never deletes because external-provisioner is gone
- 20m0s later: WaitForPersistentVolumeDeleted times out
- Test fails with "PersistentVolume pvc-9ad38927... not deleted by dynamic provisioner: PersistentVolume pvc-9ad38927... still exists within 20m0s"

Resulting orphaned PV state: Released, reclaimPolicy: Delete, finalizers=[external-provisioner.volume.kubernetes.io/finalizer, kubernetes.io/pv-protection]. 17 such PVs visible in the cluster at investigation time. Total failure count from streamed log: 32 (many tests deploy multiple PVs per spec, each becoming a distinct failure aggregate).

## Contribution to overall csi-hostpath failure rate

This ONE bug likely accounts for the majority of --focus '[Driver: csi-hostpath]' failures in this run. Not all failures share the pattern (some csi-hostpath specs will fail for genuinely-missing u7s features like snapshot API -- see mayor-cst7t), but the "still exists within 20m0s" cluster is 32 of the observed failures as of the streamed log check.

## Root cause in the watchdog code

scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh:104-116 watchdog_loop() logic:

    if [ "$phase" = "Active" ] && [ "$age_s" -ge 600 ]; then
      should_delete=1
      reason="Active for ${age_s}s (>= 10m threshold)"

The 10-minute Active threshold is too tight for [Slow]-tagged csi-hostpath tests. The lines 55-73 comment block explicitly recognizes the trade-off with the CronJob test but sizes for the CronJob's 5-minute internal check, not for [Slow]-tagged tests that run 10-20 min.

Additionally, the 15-minute any-phase threshold at line 108 (`elif [ "$age_s" -ge 900 ]`) would reap ANY namespace including a still-alive CSI driver namespace at 15 min -- doesn't help because the reap already fires at the 10-min Active gate first for slow-but-healthy tests.

## Proposed fix approaches (operator to choose)

(a) Bump the Active threshold to 20 or 25 minutes -- matches the upstream PV-delete-slow timeout that tests already tolerate. Simplest change, one line. Downside: genuine hangs take longer to catch.

(b) Distinguish between "test namespaces" (created by ginkgo, safe to reap) and "CSI-driver-deploy namespaces" (created by test framework's storageframework, must be preserved until CSI resources drained). Difficult without extra labels or naming conventions; sonobuoy/ginkgo don't tag test namespaces distinctly.

(c) Introspect the namespace: if it contains a live CSI driver StatefulSet OR any PV binding to a driver identity based on the namespace's name, don't reap. More correct, more code, brittle to storage framework internals.

(d) Increase the 10-minute threshold ONLY for namespace patterns matching known slow-test suffixes. Fragile.

(e) Skip the reap if any external-provisioner finalizer references the namespace's CSI driver identity. Requires cross-referencing PV finalizers, more surgery.

Recommend (a) as the immediate fix. Simplest, targeted at the actual failure mode we've observed, keeps the watchdog's original leak-catcher purpose. Downside is acceptable given the failure mode being fixed is a false positive that MASKS real bugs.

Longer-term: consider (c) or (e) if the harness needs to become more robust to real CSI driver lifecycle.

## Acceptance for the fix

- Existing scripts/conformance/test-watchdog-logic.sh unit test still passes.
- New test case: a namespace matching pattern <basename>-<5-digit-suffix> that hosts a StatefulSet with csi-hostpathplugin pod: watchdog should NOT reap it before 20+ minutes (or whichever threshold picked).
- Re-run --focus '[Driver: csi-hostpath]' at --procs=4 with the fix and count the "still exists within 20m0s" failures: should drop meaningfully.

## Non-goals for this bead

title: task
description:
Phase-1 of mayor-f5sv4 fix. Scout memo: ai/findings (not stored -- see scout return in mayor session).

## Background

mayor-f5sv4 forensic proved the sonobuoy e2e-job container runs BestEffort with no memory bound. Under --focus=[Driver: csi-hostpath] the ginkgo --procs=16 fan-out consumes ~2.78 GiB anon-rss across 19 processes in ~42 seconds. Kernel currently handles this via CONSTRAINT_NONE global oom-search: it picks the e2e cgroup as victim by oom_score, but next roll of the dice could pick kubelet/crio and take down the node.

Second live measurement (2026-08-07 00:32Z lima-node-3): kernel dmesg shows 19 processes killed, summed anon-rss 2847700 kB = 2780 MiB, per-process 139-187 MiB. VM survived by luck, not design.

## Fix

Convert sonobuoy's default --plugin e2e (named-plugin form, resources: {}) to a file-based plugin (-p <yaml>) with explicit requests+limits producing Guaranteed QoS. Operator-chosen values:

  e2e container:
    requests: { memory: 1Gi, cpu: 500m }
    limits:   { memory: 1Gi, cpu: 500m }
  sonobuoy-worker sidecar:
    requests: { memory: 128Mi, cpu: 100m }
    limits:   { memory: 128Mi, cpu: 100m }

Rationale for 1Gi:
- Conformance measured: 150 MiB anon peak (~5x headroom)
- csi-hostpath measured: 2.78 GiB anon peak (WILL breach 1Gi → deterministic per-cgroup OOMKill, constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMCG)
- Failure mode changes from 'kernel scans everything and picks a random victim' to 'the offending container gets killed with exitCode:137 reason:OOMKilled and a clear cap it breached'
- csi-hostpath's own memory demand will be fixed separately via Phase-3 (Option 1: focus-conditional --procs reduction)

## Implementation

1. Generate the default e2e plugin YAML in-VM: sonobuoy gen plugin e2e --show-default-podspec (worker to verify exact flag name on v0.57.3; alternative: sonobuoy gen plugin e2e). Confirm it emits a full plugin spec including the e2e container + sonobuoy-worker sidecar structure.
2. Save as scripts/conformance/sonobuoy-plugin-e2e.yaml (checked into repo). Edit to add requests/limits per above.
3. Update scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh:190 -- change SONOBUOY_BASE_ARGS to reference the file:
   from: run --plugin e2e --wait --kubeconfig /tmp/sonobuoy-kubeconfig
   to:   run -p /tmp/sonobuoy-plugin-e2e.yaml --wait --kubeconfig /tmp/sonobuoy-kubeconfig
4. Add a limactl copy step near lines 133-134 (where sonobuoy-kubeconfig is copied): limactl copy scripts/conformance/sonobuoy-plugin-e2e.yaml ":/tmp/sonobuoy-plugin-e2e.yaml"
5. Update scripts/conformance/test-all-e2e-timeout-logic.sh (shadow-test that mirrors build_filter_args / build_sonobuoy_args) in lockstep -- scout flagged this as project convention.

## Sidecar compatibility smoke test (mandatory before push)

Scout flagged that sonobuoy might inject the worker sidecar differently for a --plugin e2e run vs a -p <file> run. Verify:
1. Bring up stack via scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --stack-only --vm lima-node-2 --port 6444
2. Run sonobuoy with -p using the new yaml, --focus 'should apply a namespace' (1 spec)
3. kubectl -n sonobuoy get pod -l ... -o yaml -- compare the resulting pod spec against a --plugin e2e run's pod spec (structural diff, ignoring container image tags / random names). MUST see: sonobuoy-worker sidecar present, aggregator health-reporting works, e2e container has the resource block set.
4. kubectl -n sonobuoy get pod -l ... -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.qosClass}' MUST print 'Guaranteed'

## Acceptance

- cargo test --workspace green
- cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings clean
- shellcheck scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh clean
- shadow test scripts/conformance/test-all-e2e-timeout-logic.sh green
- QoS smoke test: Guaranteed confirmed
- Sidecar smoke test: sonobuoy-worker sidecar behaves identically to --plugin e2e run

Post-merge verification (operator will run before merging PR, per operator direction 2026-08-07): a --focus '[Driver: csi-hostpath]' run should now OOMKill the e2e container deterministically (kubectl get pod shows reason:OOMKilled, exitCode:137, cgroup dmesg shows constraint=CONSTRAINT_MEMCG NOT constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE) rather than triggering global oom scan. This is a BEHAVIOR CHANGE we EXPECT to see; it confirms Option 2 worked.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT fix csi-hostpath's underlying memory demand (that's Phase-3 / Option 1).
- Do NOT modify --procs=16 default.
- Do NOT bump VM RAM (contradicts project stance).

## Cross-refs

- Parent: mayor-f5sv4 forensic
- Scout: scout memo from 2026-08-07 (mayor session; not stored to ai/findings/, contents captured in this description)
- Direct precedent: sonobuoy v0.57.3 CLI has no resource flag (confirmed via cmd/sonobuoy/app/args.go@v0.57.3)
- Successor bead (to file later): Phase-2 empirical --procs bisect under the new 1Gi cap for csi-hostpath focus; Phase-3 focus-conditional --procs=N override in 06-run-sonobuoy.sh

WORKER FINDING (2026-08-07, lima-node-2 smoke test) -- STOPPING before push/PR, needs mayor decision.

Empirically confirmed (live pod capture on lima-node-2, both --plugin e2e baseline
and -p <file> new run) plus sonobuoy v0.57.3 source (pkg/plugin/driver/base.go
CreateWorkerContainerDefintion, pkg/plugin/driver/job/job.go createPodDefinition,
pkg/plugin/manifest/manifest.go Manifest schema, gh api @v0.57.3):
