title: Delete abandoned proto-reencode Value parsing in content_type.rs:207-231 -- 15 LoC removes 1.06GB/8.25M-block cost per conformance run
description:
SIGNAL

JSON serde scout ai/findings/json-serde-optimization-scoping-2026-08-06.md identified this as the single biggest quick win in the whole apiserver, unambiguous by every metric:

- File: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/content_type.rs, function reencode_proto_response, lines 207-231.
- Behavior: parses the ENTIRE JSON response body into a serde_json::Value tree solely to extract kind for a tracing::debug! line. Then unconditionally returns the untouched original bytes. Proto re-encoding was ABANDONED per the functions own doc comment.
- Firing rate: on every non-chunked GET response to a protobuf-preferring client - essentially every kubelet request.
- Cost per 60min conformance run 0806-1102: approximately 1.06GB total bytes allocated, 8.25 million allocation events. That is 6.25 percent of total allocation bytes and 6.67 percent of total events, all for a debug log line.

FIX

Delete the Value parsing. Keep the debug log or drop it entirely. The function still returns the original bytes unchanged either way.

Scope: approximately 15 LoC deletion in one file. Near-zero risk since output bytes are identical before and after; only the debug log-line content changes.

TESTS

Existing tests should already cover the return-value bytes-identical property. Add a regression test that instruments allocation count via dhat or a simpler cfg-test AtomicUsize counter around content_type middleware and asserts a call does not allocate a Value tree.

If test dhat integration is not clean, an alternative is: cfg-test spy that wraps serde_json::from_slice or Value construction and increments a counter - assert counter stays zero across a middleware invocation that previously would have incremented it. Reverse-fail: restore the deleted Value::from parse call and confirm the counter goes non-zero.

VERIFICATION

- Cargo tests all green.
- Optional but recommended: post-merge dhat A/B against the 0806-1102 baseline showing reencode_proto_response no longer appears in the top-N JSON allocators. Operator can run this in a 20min conformance suite per bd memory conformance-suite-is-iterable-for-profiling-purposes.

WIRE COMPATIBILITY

None affected. Output bytes are identical.

title: u7s-scheduler missing NodeUnschedulable filter: spec.unschedulable field ignored, breaks kubectl cordon and causes deterministic conformance failures
description:
SIGNAL AND EVIDENCE

Flake investigation (ai/findings/flake-0806-1102-investigation-2026-08-06.md, bead mayor-aa3f10 closed) root-caused the 1-failure in the 0806-1102 dhat conformance run. NOT a race, NOT accepted-flake, NOT test-setup: a real deterministic u7s scheduler bug.

The failing test: sig-network Networking Granular Checks: Pods should function for node-pod communication: http [LinuxOnly] [NodeConformance] [Conformance]. Test failed because its unconstrained pod (test-container-pod) was bound to e2e-fake-node-d6rwq, a fake node upstream sig-node Node Lifecycle test creates with Spec.Unschedulable: true SPECIFICALLY so the scheduler will not select it.

Damning quote from upstream (test/e2e/node/node_lifecycle.go:58-67 release-1.36):
    Create a fake node with a ready condition but unschedulable, so it wont be selected by the scheduler

Upstream ships NodeUnschedulable as an always-on default Filter plugin (pkg/scheduler/apis/config/v1/default_plugins.go:36). u7s does not implement this plugin equivalent.

Root cause:
- crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs:738-742 NodeSpec struct deserializes taints only, never unschedulable. The field is not in u7s NodeSpec at all.
- crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs:1351-1359 node_qualifies_for_pod is structurally incapable of checking a field the type does not include.
- Consequence: u7s scheduler cannot see spec.unschedulable. Every conformance run against 2-node cluster deterministically binds unconstrained pods to the transient fake node during its ~1.2s lifetime (scheduler.log:264-311 confirms 3-for-3 pods landed, not 1-in-3).

IMPACT

- Deterministic conformance failure on the sig-node Node Lifecycle plus any concurrent unconstrained pod test (--procs=16 makes concurrent test ordering random which makes THIS specific overlap intermittent, but the underlying scheduler behavior is deterministic when the overlap happens).
- kubectl cordon is broken end-to-end. cordon sets spec.unschedulable: true. u7s scheduler ignores it. Any operator or admin cordoning a node expecting evacuation-plus-no-new-pods gets evacuation only, u7s keeps scheduling fresh pods onto the cordoned node. This is a real product bug beyond conformance.

FIX SPECIFICATION

1. Add unschedulable: Option bool field to crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs NodeSpec struct (line ~738-742), deserialize from both JSON and protobuf (verify wire coverage - see evidence gap below).
2. In node_qualifies_for_pod at lib.rs:1351, reject nodes where spec.unschedulable == Some(true) UNLESS the pod carries a toleration for node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable NoSchedule taint. Upstream allows this override via toleration (verified in flake investigation).

Match upstream NodeUnschedulable plugins semantics. See pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodeunschedulable/ in kubernetes/kubernetes release-1.36 for reference.

REGRESSION TEST (fail-on-revert mandatory per Rule 9)

- Assert that node_qualifies_for_pod returns false for a pod with no unschedulable-tolerating tolerations against a node with spec.unschedulable=true EVEN when its the only or least-loaded candidate.
- Assert that a pod WITH the tolerating toleration IS scheduled to that node.
- Both tests must fail if the fix is reverted.

EVIDENCE GAP TO CLOSE AT FIX TIME

The flake investigation noted an evidence gap: does apiservers JSON response actually carry spec.unschedulable on the wire when a node is created with it set? This is moot for the fix (scheduler struct drops the field regardless today so wire presence is irrelevant to the current bug), but the regression test needs the wire round-trip to be meaningful. Worker should either verify with a live kubectl create/get on the current apiserver OR construct the Node object directly in-test to sidestep the wire path.

VERIFICATION

- Cargo tests pass.
- Small live kubectl repro on the worker VM: kubectl cordon lima-node-N, then kubectl create a pod, observe it does NOT land on lima-node-N.
- Optional but recommended: post-merge, an operator-driven 2-node certified-conformance re-run (20 min per bd memory conformance-suite-is-iterable-for-profiling-purposes) with the sig-node Node Lifecycle test in scope, observe the sig-network pod-http test no longer fails.

CROSS-REFS

- Investigation: ai/findings/flake-0806-1102-investigation-2026-08-06.md
- Prior scout (partially-wrong): ai/findings/flake-0806-1102-2026-08-06.md (mechanism narrative correct, verdict wrong)
- Baseline: temp/e2e/0806-0917-conformance (this test passed 14s but on a different test-firing order)
- The failing dhat run: temp/e2e/0806-1102-conformance

SCOPE ESTIMATE

~20-40 LoC production plus ~30-60 LoC tests. Shape-1 solo dispatch.

title: u7s apiserver exec-proxy drops kubelet exit-status frame -- every nonzero-exit kubectl exec falsely reports exit 0
description:
SIGNATURE and ROOT CAUSE (HIGH-confidence scout, 2026-08-06)

crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs line 1057, function is_exec_status_frame, is inside run_exec_proxy at lines 1070-1150. It unconditionally drops kubelet's WebSocket channel-3 or channel-4 exec status frame regardless of payload content. Both success frames like status Success and failure frames like status Failure with reason NonZeroExitCode are silently discarded, and no replacement frame is ever synthesized or forwarded.

Consequence: client-go remotecommand sees a clean WebSocket close with no in-band failure signal, and reports err == nil, meaning the client interprets every exec as exit 0. Every kubectl exec of a command that actually exited nonzero appears to succeed. This is a cluster-wide correctness defect affecting any conformance test that asserts on exec exit-code semantics.

Introduced by commit bd2b58cc on 2026-05-30, which was a narrower fix that overcorrected and started swallowing failure frames along with success frames.

EVIDENCE

- Full scout doc: ai/findings/csi-block-volmode-failure-scout-2026-08-06.md
- Confirmed 12 of 16 visible FAILED-in-It markers in temp/e2e/0806-e2e-streamed.log (operator --procs=4 csi-hostpath run today) show the exact should fail with exit code 1, but exit without error pattern
- Direct disproof of the mayor initial hypothesis at temp/e2e/0806-e2e-streamed.log lines 311 through 317, showing a real write and read at /opt/0/index.html on a filesystem-mode PVC immediately followed by test -b /opt/0 falsely succeeding, physically impossible unless exit-code reporting itself is broken
- The bug spans fixtures.go 536 and 547, multivolume.go 510 and 619, and utils.go 564 in the upstream test bodies

IMPACT

Not just CSI. Any test in any e2e area that uses the test -X, sh -c exit 1, or negative-assertion pattern with kubectl exec will silently pass a test that should fail. Historic --all-e2e archives may have false-passing tests for this reason. This is a P1 correctness defect.

FIX SPECIFICATION

File: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs
Functions: is_exec_status_frame at line 1057, run_exec_proxy at lines 1070-1150

Approach: instead of blanket-dropping channel-3 and channel-4 frames, parse them. If the frame carries status Failure with reason NonZeroExitCode, translate that to the correct client-facing signal (this may mean forwarding the frame as-is, or emitting a websocket close-with-status carrying the exit-code payload -- the fix worker must read the client-go remotecommand.StreamExecutor code path to determine which representation client-go expects on a nonzero-exit close). Continue dropping true success frames only.

CRITICAL: the fix worker MUST read the original commit bd2b58cc to understand what problem it was solving. Do not simply revert -- the commit was fixing a real (different) issue. The correct fix preserves the original commit intent for success-frame handling while restoring failure-frame propagation.

VERIFICATION

Small kubectl repro without needing a full conformance run:

  kubectl exec pod -- sh -c 'exit 1'; echo $?

Should print 1; currently prints 0 under u7s. Test both success (exit 0) and failure (exit 1, exit 2, exit 127) cases in an integration test.

RELATED

title: ginkgo --procs=16 in a resource-unbounded BestEffort e2e-job container consumed ~3.1GiB (81% of 4GiB VM), the dominant cause of the csi-hostpath-focus OOM
description:
FORENSIC FINDING (read-only investigation, temp/e2e/0806-0217--driver-csi-hostpath, lima-node-smoke, 2026-08-06). See full writeup: ai/findings/oom-forensic-0806-0217-2026-08-06.md (worker worktree agent-a3b4a8a7be7a222d8).

kubelet.log:1412 only logs ONE cAdvisor-summarized OOM victim line ("VictimContainerName":"/"), which is what mayor-kkbe6/mayor-5v9gl's prior investigations relied on. Pulling the RAW kernel ring buffer on the still-live VM (`limactl shell lima-node-smoke sudo dmesg | grep -i oom`) reveals the full picture cAdvisor hid:

  oom-kill:constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE,...,global_oom,task_memcg=/kubepods.slice/kubepods-besteffort.slice/kubepods-besteffort-podbc24d529_761d_4cda_920d_49c0b2c00726.slice/crio-b1fbd0c89ba34d20123f49f566641571dd4ed201a2d438ae63bf09b17f09e9cd.scope/container,task=e2e.test,pid=10550
  Tasks in .../crio-b1fbd0c89...scope/container are going to be killed due to memory.oom.group set
  Out of memory: Killed process 10516 (run_e2e.sh) anon-rss:896kB
  Out of memory: Killed process 10526 (ginkgo) anon-rss:8912kB
  Out of memory: Killed process 10532 (ginkgo) anon-rss:8912kB
  ... 19 more "Killed process NNNNN (e2e.test) anon-rss:1xxxxx-2xxxxxkB" lines ...

memory.oom.group killed 22 processes total, ALL within the sonobuoy e2e-job pod's own `e2e` container cgroup (confirmed: crio-b1fbd0c89... is exactly the e2e container's containerID per resources/ns/sonobuoy/core_v1_pods.json). Summed anon-rss across all 22 = 3,176,128 kB ~= 3.10 GiB, against VM total 3997056 kB ~= 3.81 GiB (/proc/meminfo). ONE BestEffort container consumed ~81% of the whole VM's RAM.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed in source, not inferred):
1. scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh:182,187 and run-all.sh hardcode `E2E_EXTRA_GINKGO_ARGS=--procs=16` unconditionally (shipped via PR #966 / bead mayor-v59ym).
2. lima-node-smoke has 8 vCPUs (`limactl shell lima-node-smoke nproc` = 8; kubelet's own manager.go:218 confirms NumCores:8) -- --procs=16 is already 2x CPU-oversubscribed.
3. Ginkgo's --procs=N forks N FULL e2e.test binary processes (each the complete compiled k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e suite + client-go caches), not lightweight goroutines. Each costs 116-216 MB anon-rss (measured directly from the dmesg kill list above).
4. The sonobuoy e2e-job pod's `e2e` container has `"resources":{}` (zero requests/limits) and `qosClass:BestEffort` (resources/ns/sonobuoy/core_v1_pods.json) -- nothing bounds how much memory this fan-out can consume.

WHY THIS IS NEW (not a duplicate of mayor-5v9gl or mayor-kkbe6): mayor-5v9gl's open bead attributes the OOM primarily to "~25 stuck ImagePullBackOff pod cgroups x 100MB, hours later ~= 2.5GB at OOM time" -- an estimate extrapolated from a LATE, post-hoc systemd-cgtop measurement. I independently re-verified live: all 25 of those pods are now Ready/Running (fully recovered, zero currently stuck) -- the pileup was real but far smaller at the actual 02:11:39 OOM instant than the "hours-later" arithmetic implies (pause containers are ~1-2MB each; 15-16 of them is tens of MB, not gigabytes). The dmesg evidence captured here, from the literal instant of the kernel OOM, shows the dominant mass was the ginkgo/e2e.test fleet itself (~3.1 GiB, ~75-85% of the total memory pressure), not the sidecar pileup (~2-5%).

This ALSO refines mayor-l6ojx's closed "16-way fits, 24/32-way OOMs" bisection: that experiment only tested --focus '[Conformance]' (~450 lighter specs, no per-spec StatefulSet driver deployment). The SAME --procs=16, applied to --focus '[Driver: csi-hostpath]' (which additionally deploys 15-16 concurrent 7-container CSI StatefulSets + triggers PVC-provisioner churn + 274 pull-QPS-exceeded retries -- see mayor-5v9gl), tips the previously-"safe" 16-way ceiling into an OOM. The margin is much thinner than previously measured and is test-family-dependent, not just process-count-dependent.

Project stance note: u7s targets resource-starved tiny VPS; a hardcoded, unbounded, 2x-CPU-oversubscribed parallelism default that can single-handedly consume 81% of a 4GiB VM's RAM is a P1 resource-efficiency defect per project triage rules (every reproducible defect is at minimum P2; this blocks --focus runs entirely and is reproducible on any fresh 4GiB VM per mayor-kkbe6's original framing).

Reproducible: every --focus '[Driver: csi-hostpath]' run (and plausibly other storage-heavy/StatefulSet-heavy --focus patterns) on a fresh 4GiB VM will hit this, per the same mechanism mayor-kkbe6 originally documented (before being mis-attributed to pull-QPS-exceeded as sole cause).

No fix proposed here (out of scope for this read-only forensic pass) -- needs its own scout to evaluate options (lower --procs for storage-heavy focus patterns, set memory limits+requests on the e2e-job container so oom-killer scoping stays contained rather than system-wide, bump VM RAM, or make --procs adaptive to nproc/available memory).
close_reason: Scout complete + operator-approved fix design. Fix work continues as mayor-o4fmo (Phase-1: Guaranteed QoS bounded cap at 1Gi for e2e container, 128Mi for sonobuoy-worker sidecar). Follow-ons will be Phase-2 (empirical --procs bisect under the new cap for csi-hostpath focus) and Phase-3 (focus-conditional --procs override). Ground truth: csi-hostpath run 2026-08-07 00:32Z on lima-node-3 killed 19 processes summed to 2780 MiB anon-rss in 42 seconds under CONSTRAINT_NONE global_oom; Conformance run 2026-08-07 00:16Z stayed under 150 MiB anon peak.

title: u7s apiserver missing imagePullPolicy default causes silent unconditional re-pulls (defeats PR #1011 cache, amplifies pull-QPS-exceeded)
description:
Discovered 2026-08-06 by mayor-5v9gl scout (bed a45455da, doc ai/findings/mayor-5v9gl-pull-qps-scout-2026-08-06.md).

PR #1011 (commit 07205b64) pre-pulls e2e-test-images (including all CSI sidecar images) into the VM base image at provisioning time. This is confirmed working: crio.log shows the pre-pull operations SUCCEED during VM boot.

HOWEVER: during the operator's 0806-0217 csi-hostpath focus run, when real test pods first needed those same images post-boot, kubelet fetched them FRESH (200ms-1.2s each) instead of using the pre-pull cache. Evidence: crio.log around 02:10:48+ shows PullImage operations for csi-attacher/csi-provisioner/csi-resizer/etc. with actual network-fetch timings, not cache-hit timings.

CONSEQUENCE: PR #1011's pre-pull mechanism is providing zero actual speedup for the very scenario it was designed to accelerate. Cache-miss also means the 274 pull-QPS-exceeded errors (mayor-5v9gl) are STRUCTURALLY UNAVOIDABLE without either fixing the cache-hit path or a separate concurrency knob.

ROOT MECHANISM: not conclusively isolated (scout was read-only, no VM access allowed). Possible causes to investigate:
- Image tags in the pre-pull don't exactly match what tests request (SHA mismatch, tag drift between PR #1011's pre-pull list and current csi-hostpath test images).
- cri-o's image cache is being cleared during VM boot / kubelet startup and pre-pulled images are evicted.
- Pre-pull uses one image storage layer, test pods request from a different one (unlikely but worth checking).
- The pre-pull writes to an ephemeral overlay that gets thrown away.

Fix scope requires a scout to identify which of the above is happening. Then the fix itself is probably small (correct tag pin, or preserve the cache location across VM boot).

VALUE PROP: fixing this cache-miss would substantially reduce (possibly eliminate) mayor-5v9gl's pull-QPS-exceeded pressure without needing to bump QPS or serialize tests. Alignment with u7s's resource-efficiency stance is high.

Cross-references:
- PR #1011 (commit 07205b64): the pre-pull implementation
- mayor-5v9gl: pull-QPS-exceeded, which this cache-miss AMPLIFIES
- mayor-w44wg: DiskPressure investigation, which was inconclusive partly because of the same cascade
- Scout doc: ai/findings/mayor-5v9gl-pull-qps-scout-2026-08-06.md

Priority: P2. Not blocking anything urgent (mayor-5v9gl serialize-CSI-tests fix is proceeding independently), but if fixed would elegantly solve multiple related issues.
notes:
SCOUT LANDED 2026-08-06 (bed a5e90314). ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED with HIGH confidence. Full doc: ai/findings/mayor-xv1pk-prepull-cache-miss-scout-2026-08-06.md.

REAL ROOT CAUSE (not what this bead's original title said):

PR #1011's pre-pull is NOT broken. Instead, u7s's apiserver never defaults `imagePullPolicy` for containers that omit the field. Upstream apiservers do (SetDefaults_Container at pkg/apis/core/v1/defaults.go:82-93 -- if tag==latest then Always else IfNotPresent). u7s's apply_pod_spec_defaults() at handlers/pods.rs:4179-4360 has NO imagePullPolicy default (grep-verified).

Kubelet's imagePullPrecheck (image_manager.go:117-127) is a switch over PullAlways/PullIfNotPresent/PullNever with no default case. Empty policy falls through to what functionally = PullAlways behavior -- no cache check, unconditional re-pull on every container start.

DIRECT CONTROL-GROUP PROOF (crio.log): csi-external-health-monitor-controller (explicit IfNotPresent in manifest) was pulled EXACTLY ONCE. hostpathplugin (no explicit policy) was pulled 29 TIMES with identical digest. Same digest across all pulls proves it wasn't a cache-invalidation issue.

CROSS-CUTTING IMPLICATIONS:
- Bead retitled: this is now "u7s apiserver missing imagePullPolicy default", not "PR #1011 cache miss."
- Direct fix pattern IDENTICAL to closed mayor-6xl44 (Pod schedulerName/restartPolicy defaults, PR #1017) and mayor-7ab6g (HPA defaults, PR #1016). Same class of defaulting-gap.
- Impact spans BEYOND csi-hostpath: any test with implicit imagePullPolicy re-pulls unnecessarily. That's a resource-efficiency defect (u7s's core value prop). VPS-target users would be gigabytes of unnecessary pulls out of pocket.
- Contributor to mayor-5v9gl (pull-QPS-exceeded): re-pulls amplify pull demand 7-9x per StatefulSet, continuous for whole run. Fixing this bead directly reduces mayor-5v9gl's cascade.
- Plausibly contributor to mayor-w44wg (DiskPressure): each re-pulled image consumes fresh overlay-fs storage between de-dupe passes.
- Plausibly contributor to mayor-f5sv4 (OOM): re-pulls consume kubelet/cri-o memory during pull-in-progress state.

PRIORITY RAISED P2 -> P1 (2026-08-06). This is a resource-efficiency defect against u7s's raison d'etre (VPS-target). Fix is IMMEDIATELY dispatchable: ~15-25 LoC in handlers/pods.rs, pattern already established by PR #1016/PR #1017.

FIX SPECIFICATION (from scout, verbatim):
- For each container in containers/initContainers/ephemeralContainers, if imagePullPolicy is null/empty, parse the image tag:
  - If tag is "latest" or absent: set "Always"
  - Otherwise: set "IfNotPresent"
- Mirrors upstream SetDefaults_Container semantics exactly.
- Unit test: Pod with container having no imagePullPolicy + non-latest tag → gets IfNotPresent.
- End-to-end verification: re-run csi-hostpath focused suite, confirm each CSI sidecar pulled EXACTLY ONCE.

CAVEAT: this fix eliminates repeated-re-pull. First-wave 14-16 StatefulSet initial pulls can still saturate the 5-QPS/10-burst token bucket if they land in the same instant. This fix removes 7-9x amplification, not first-wave saturation. mayor-5v9gl remains a valid complementary bead (but its Option C fix direction is retracted per the mayor's [Serial] correction; needs re-scoping AFTER this bead's fix lands).
close_reason: PR #1024 opened — imagePullPolicy defaulting added to apply_pod_spec_defaults(), VM-verified on lima-node-2 (crio ImageStatus-only on second create, no repeat PullImage RPC)

title: sonobuoy e2e container OOM-killed during ginkgo spec enumeration on 4 GiB VM (blocks --focus runs)
description:
Observed 2026-08-06 during operator's csi-hostpath repro (temp/e2e/0806-0217--driver-csi-hostpath, on lima-node-smoke VM with 4 GiB RAM).

The sonobuoy e2e container is killed by the kernel OOM killer ~60 seconds after start, before ginkgo completes spec enumeration. The container has no memory limit, is BestEffort QoS, and belongs to a Job with restartPolicy: Never. Symptom: no tests run, no junit produced, sonobuoy plugin marked failed. This blocks ANY --focus run against a fresh 4 GiB VM.

DEFINITIVE EVIDENCE:
1. plugins/e2e/errors/global/error.json: "Container e2e is in a terminated state (exit code 137) due to reason: OOMKilled"
2. kubelet.log:1412 -- "Got sys oom event" event={"Pid":10550,"ProcessName":"e2e.test","TimeOfDeath":"2026-08-06T02:11:39.522490712Z","ContainerName":"/","VictimContainerName":"/","Constraint":""}
   VictimContainerName:"/" = ROOT cgroup. This is SYSTEM-WIDE VM memory exhaustion, not a cgroup limit hit. The kernel picked e2e.test as the victim because it was the largest allocator at OOM time.
3. e2e.txt truncated at 14 lines (line 15 is the SSSSS spec-enumeration marker) -- ginkgo was still enumerating the 7579 specs when killed.
4. Pod status: restartPolicy: Never, QoS: BestEffort, no resources.limits set. exitCode=137, reason=OOMKilled.
5. Timeline: 02:10:39 container start, 02:11:39 kernel OOM (60s elapsed). Ran only long enough to load spec metadata into memory.

MECHANISM:
- Lima VM (base config) has 4 GiB RAM total.
- ginkgo's `-v=6 --procs=16` mode loads all 7579 spec metadata into RAM for enumeration/filtering before it starts dispatching them.
- Simultaneously, kubelet is initiating pulls for 8 sidecar containers PER csi-hostpath test namespace (324 test namespaces = ~2600 pulls queued).
- BestEffort e2e pod has no memory guarantee. Once system-wide pressure crosses kernel OOM threshold, kernel picks the largest RSS as victim.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR OUR FOCUS PATTERN:
- Every --focus '\[Driver: csi-hostpath\]' or --all-e2e run on a 4 GiB VM will hit this.
- Certified-conformance (--mode=certified-conformance) may escape it because that mode filters to ~450 specs before enumeration (fewer to hold in memory). Not verified.

FIX DIRECTIONS (needs its own scout to evaluate):
A. Set memory request+limit on the e2e container (via sonobuoy plugin manifest override).
   - Upside: bounds ginkgo's blast radius so kernel oom-killer targets ginkgo cgroup, not system-wide.
   - Downside: sonobuoy plugin config lives in ConfigMap templated by sonobuoy generate; not obviously operator-tunable.
B. Bump lima VM RAM from 4 GiB to 8+ GiB.
   - Upside: fixes ALL memory-constrained test paths, not just this one.
   - Downside: shifts the "u7s targets tiny VPS" story. But smoke VMs are already dedicated test infrastructure, not the deployment target — worth clarifying: is 4 GiB a hard constraint on VM smoke infrastructure, or only on the eventual deployment target?
C. Reduce ginkgo memory pressure via --procs=<lower> or streaming enumeration.
   - Upside: no infra change.
   - Downside: unclear if ginkgo supports streaming enumeration; --procs=<lower> would slow every subsequent run.
D. Do fewer things concurrently: pre-pull common CSI sidecar images so kubelet doesn't have 2600 pulls queued.
   - Upside: reduces the "second half" of the memory pressure.
   - Downside: doesn't fix ginkgo's own RSS.

RELATED BEADS:
- mayor-5v9gl (pull QPS exceeded) -- downstream symptom of the same pressure. Note-corrected 2026-08-06.
- mayor-hmvl8 (sonobuoy progress feed silent) -- DIFFERENT bug: hmvl8 is about a run that eventually completed with valid junit but had broken progress reporting. This bead is about a run that never got past enumeration. Different failure modes; do not conflate.

Reproducible: EVERY --focus run against a fresh 4 GiB VM will hit this. Not flaky.
notes:
SUPERSEDED CORRECTION 2026-08-06 (third attempt): my prior closure reason ("superseded by mayor-5v9gl, primary cause is pull-QPS-exceeded cgroup pileup") was ALSO WRONG.

The exhaustive OOM investigation (mayor-a3b4a8a7 scout, ai/findings/oom-forensic-0806-0217-2026-08-06.md) ran kernel dmesg and found:

REAL primary cause: ginkgo --procs=16 fan-out in the unbounded BestEffort e2e-job container consumed ~3.1 GiB (81% of the 4 GiB VM) all by itself. kernel `memory.oom.group` killed 22 processes in that ONE container together (1 sh + 2 ginkgo + 19 e2e.test workers). This is mayor-f5sv4 (P1, filed by the scout).

pull-QPS-exceeded / cgroup pileup that this bead and mayor-5v9gl focused on: only ~2-5% of the actual OOM cause. Real but SECONDARY. Verified live by the scout that the "25 stuck pods holding 100 MB each" I claimed had already recovered to Running -- they weren't stuck at OOM time, my extrapolation was invalid.

CORRECT closure: this bead's TITLE ("sonobuoy e2e container OOM-killed during ginkgo spec enumeration on 4 GiB VM") was actually CORRECT -- the OOM is real, it does affect --focus runs. The FRAMING (root cause) was wrong. The real fix is mayor-f5sv4.

This bead remains closed as superseded, but the correct supersedor is mayor-f5sv4 (not mayor-5v9gl). Fix mayor-f5sv4 to unblock --focus runs on 4 GiB VMs.

TRIAGE LESSON (banked as bd memory dmesg-first-for-oom-investigation): I should have run `sudo dmesg | grep oom` on lima-node-smoke as the FIRST diagnostic step. Two consecutive misdiagnoses of the same OOM (this bead + mayor-5v9gl escalation) could have been avoided.
close_reason:
DOUBLE-CORRECTION 2026-08-06 (operator challenge to the initial framing):

My earlier "4 GiB too small for ginkgo spec enumeration" claim was WRONG. Operator's instinct was correct: 4 GiB should be plenty for 320 tests, and the e2e.test binary itself is not multi-GB. VM currently (post-run) shows 1.9 GiB used / 3.8 GiB total with u7s stack running — plenty of headroom for a normal ginkgo workload.

REAL causal chain (verified live on lima-node-smoke VM 2026-08-06):

1. sonobuoy launched sidecars for 324 csi-hostpath test namespaces near-simultaneously.
2. kubelet started admitting them all → each pod got its own cgroup + pause container.
3. cri-o hit registryPullQPS gate (274 "pull QPS exceeded" errors, per mayor-5v9gl) → sidecar container images kept ErrImagePull.
4. Pods stayed Pending indefinitely — cgroups NOT torn down, kubelet state per pod retained.
5. Kubelet cgroup accounting shows STILL right now, hours after the run: 25+ pod cgroups in kubepods-besteffort.slice, each holding 70-107 MB (pause container + kubelet per-pod state + partial CSI-plugin bootstrap state).
6. Estimated at OOM time (60s in): 30+ stuck pods × 100 MB = ~3 GB pods + kubelet 150 MB + crio 140 MB + system ~600 MB = ~4 GB total → kernel OOM triggers.
7. Kernel OOM-killer picked e2e.test as victim because it had the highest RSS among MOVABLE processes at that moment (e2e.test cgroup ~105 MB).

So mayor-5v9gl IS the primary root cause. mayor-kkbe6 (this bead) was mis-framed as an independent OOM issue when it's actually the DOWNSTREAM SYMPTOM of pull-QPS-exceeded → cgroup pileup.

CORRECTION IMPLICATIONS:
- mayor-5v9gl (P2) SHOULD BE RAISED to P1 — it's the actual blocker.
- mayor-kkbe6 (this bead) SHOULD BE CLOSED as duplicate/superseded by mayor-5v9gl.
- Fix directions from mayor-5v9gl apply: pre-pull CSI sidecars into base VM, or bump registryPullQPS, or serialize CSI-hostpath test execution.

TRIAGE LESSON LEARNED (bank as memory): when investigating a "container OOMKilled" event, verify the memory picture at the cgroup level for the WHOLE VM before concluding "the killed container was the memory hog." Kernel OOM-killer picks the highest RSS among movable processes, which is often NOT the process actually causing memory pressure. Cgroup-level pod accounting (systemd-cgtop) is the actionable signal.

title: apiserver: single-object GET handlers never check wants_partial_object_metadata (blocks vendored kcm GC)
description:
DISCOVERED 2026-08-06 by mayor-uuk51 Phase-1 audit (bed a16edec8, doc ai/findings/mayor-uuk51-phase1-audit-2026-08-06.md).

Single-object GET handlers in u7s NEVER check `wants_partial_object_metadata()` for ANY resource type. Affected:
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs::get_resource
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs::get_namespaced_resource
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs::get_cr
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs::get_cr_namespaced
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs::get_pod

Impact (live, verified in temp/e2e/0805-2202-conformance/host-logs/kcm.log): vendored kube-controller-manager's Garbage Collector uses metadata-only informers plus per-owner GET calls for owner-reference verification (`garbagecollector.go:434-444` `isDangling`). These GETs get typed responses (full Pod/Deployment/ReplicaSet/PVC/EndpointSlice objects with `apiVersion: v1`, `kind: Pod` etc.) instead of `PartialObjectMetadata`, and client-side decode fails.

Failure mode is fail-safe (retries forever, does NOT incorrectly delete live-owned objects) — but permanently blocks garbage collection of newly-orphaned objects across ALL owner types. This is a silent, ongoing GC leak.

SCOPE overlap with mayor-uuk51: mayor-uuk51 is about LIST/WATCH. This bead is about single-object GET. Both stem from the same missing check (`wants_partial_object_metadata()`) at their respective handler paths. Fix pattern is identical: detect Accept, if PartialObjectMetadata requested, wrap the response as `meta.k8s.io/v1 PartialObjectMetadata` with only `.metadata` populated.

Recommendation: fix as a SIBLING bead to mayor-uuk51 (both live in the same class), potentially clustered into a single PR. The GET-path fix is SMALLER than the LIST/WATCH fix (no streaming/watch-event machinery) — likely ~15-25 LoC per handler * 5 handlers = ~75-125 LoC, sub-day.

Test coverage recommendation:
- One test per handler: GET with `Accept: application/json;as=PartialObjectMetadata;g=meta.k8s.io;v=v1` → response body is `{"apiVersion":"meta.k8s.io/v1","kind":"PartialObjectMetadata","metadata":{...}}` with NO `spec`/`status`.
- One integration test that reproduces kcm's isDangling call pattern (GET owner via metadata-only) and asserts it decodes correctly.

Cross-references: mayor-uuk51 (LIST/WATCH sibling), 0805-2202 kcm.log (235x `"no kind PodList"` LIST failures + per-owner GET failures — mixed evidence in the same log).
notes:
PRIORITY RAISED P2 -> P1 (operator direction 2026-08-06).

Rationale: u7s exists specifically for extreme resource efficiency (goal: run on resource-starved tiny VPS). A permanent garbage-collection leak that lets newly-orphaned objects accumulate indefinitely is DIRECTLY antagonistic to that raison detre. This is not a "kcm compat gap" (P2 framing) -- it is a resource-hygiene defect that erodes the projects core value proposition.

The fail-safe nature (retries forever, does not incorrectly delete live-owned objects) is a mitigation for correctness only, not for resource footprint. Every long-running u7s cluster leaks storage/memory for orphaned Pods, EndpointSlices, ReplicaSets, PVCs, Deployments -- the entire owner-reference-tracked object graph.

Cross-references: mayor-uuk51 (LIST/WATCH sibling, still P2 -- narrower impact than the GET path which affects EVERY owner-reference lookup for GC).

DISPATCH DECISION 2026-08-06: fix mayor-uuk51 + mayor-bvnmr as a Shape-2 cluster (same missing check, adjacent handlers, one VM verification catches both). Combined scope ~115-195 LoC, sub-day. Prioritized ahead of other queue items given the leak framing.
close_reason: PR #1022 opened

title: Pod spec.schedulerName / spec.restartPolicy missing from apply_pod_spec_defaults
description:
u7s's apply_pod_spec_defaults (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs) implements 3 of the 5 fields set by upstream pkg/apis/core/v1/defaults.go's SetDefaults_PodSpec (release-1.36, lines 211-232): dnsPolicy, securityContext, terminationGracePeriodSeconds. It is missing the other 2 sibling fields from the SAME upstream function: spec.schedulerName (default "default-scheduler") and spec.restartPolicy (default "Always").

Upstream:
  if obj.DNSPolicy == "" { obj.DNSPolicy = v1.DNSClusterFirst }               // u7s: implemented
  if obj.RestartPolicy == "" { obj.RestartPolicy = v1.RestartPolicyAlways }   // u7s: MISSING
  if obj.SecurityContext == nil { obj.SecurityContext = &v1.PodSecurityContext{} } // u7s: implemented
  if obj.TerminationGracePeriodSeconds == nil { ... = 30 }                    // u7s: implemented
  if obj.SchedulerName == "" { obj.SchedulerName = v1.DefaultSchedulerName }  // u7s: MISSING

Consumer for schedulerName: real vendored kube-scheduler's pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go:456-458 responsibleForPod() calls profiles.HandlesSchedulerName(pod.Spec.SchedulerName), which in pkg/scheduler/profile/profile.go:68-71 does `_, ok := m[name]; return ok` against a map keyed by each profile's SchedulerName (defaults to "default-scheduler", never ""). A Pod stored with schedulerName:"" is therefore invisible to real kube-scheduler and never gets scheduled.

Currently masked: scripts/conformance/run-all.sh step 5 launches u7s's own crates/scheduler binary (u7s-scheduler), not vendored kube-scheduler. grep of crates/scheduler/src/{lib,main}.rs for "schedulerName"/"SchedulerName" returns zero hits — the custom scheduler binds every unassigned pod regardless of this field, which is why the gap doesn't currently show up in the 446/446 conformance run. ai/extended-context/project-context.md:41 ("External kube-scheduler binary for Phase 3 conformance") is stale relative to the actual conformance script. This bug becomes live the moment anything points real vendored kube-scheduler at a u7s apiserver, which is squarely inside the project's kubectl/API-compat goal.

Consumer for restartPolicy: kubelet's ShouldContainerBeRestarted (pkg/kubelet/container/helpers.go:86-122) only special-cases RestartPolicyNever and RestartPolicyOnFailure+exitcode0, falling through to `return true` (restart) for anything else including "" — so the specific restart-decision path tolerates the missing default (behaves like "Always"). Not exhaustively verified against kubelet's pod-phase computation (GetPhase) or other RestartPolicy switches, so residual risk is unquantified there.

No known upstream kubernetes/kubernetes issue number for this specific case (unlike HPA's #107038) — found via direct code audit (mayor's schema-defaulting-audit-2026-08-06, dispatched after mayor-7ab6g's HPA nil-deref bug), not a reported incident.

Suggested fix scope: add the two missing `if pod["spec"]["schedulerName"].is_null()/empty { = "default-scheduler" }` and `if pod["spec"]["restartPolicy"].is_null()/empty { = "Always" }` checks to apply_pod_spec_defaults in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs, mirroring the existing dnsPolicy/securityContext/terminationGracePeriodSeconds pattern in the same function.
