title: --all-e2e skip filter runs Beta+ FeatureGate tests we don't support, causing surprise kcm crashes (fix via ginkgo --label-filter, not --skip regex)
description:
During temp/e2e/0805-2202-conformance (--all-e2e run), a Beta-gated test ([FeatureGate:HPAConfigurableTolerance]) crashed vendored Go kcm 14 minutes into a 12.6-hour run (see mayor-7ab6g). The current sonobuoy skip filter (scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh:179) is only  -- every FeatureGate test that upstream ships as Alpha/Beta/dev runs against u7s, which does not claim FeatureGate support for anything beyond GA.

Straight-forward fix considered and REJECTED: add [FeatureGate:*] to --skip regex. NOT SAFE -- 1 real Conformance overlap: [sig-storage] VolumeAttributesClass at conformance.yaml:3952-3961. u7s implements this API and needs the coverage.

Correct fix (per audit ai/findings/featuregate-conformance-resolution-2026-08-06.md):

Use ginkgo v2's native --label-filter instead of --skip regex. Every FeatureGate label is registered as a structured Ginkgo Label (test/e2e/framework/ginkgowrapper.go:271-274). Filter expression:

  --label-filter='FeatureGate: isSubsetOf {VolumeAttributesClass}'

isSubsetOf semantics: empty label set (i.e. unlabeled tests) always matches; a test with [FeatureGate:X] passes only if X is in {VolumeAttributesClass}. Composes safely with the existing --e2e-skip='\[Flaky\]' (ginkgo ANDs all CLI filters, confirmed in onsi/ginkgo source).

Why this is materially better than a regex denylist:
- Degrades safely: any NEW Alpha/Beta gate (or newly-added stale-tagged GA gate) is auto-skipped by default. No dashboard bloat, no per-minor curation cycle.
- Structured, not string-matched: no RE2 negation contortions.
- Grows the allow-set explicitly with documented gates u7s intends to cover.

Landscape stability check: 3 of top 4 FeatureGate labels changed stage 1.34->1.36; a new gate (DRAResourcePoolStatus) debuted Alpha in 1.36. Landscape is unstable enough that regex-based skip would need constant maintenance.

WIRE-UP:
Reachable via sonobuoy today with  plus  (to protect the embedded space). Verified from source (conformance image go-runner/cmd.go) but NOT runtime-tested in the audit pass. Worker MUST verify sonobuoy wire-through with a small --focus run before merge (recommend: --focus '[FeatureGate:HPAConfigurableTolerance]' + label-filter set; expect zero specs run because the label doesn't match the allow-set).

Bonus insight: the [FeatureGate:VolumeAttributesClass] tag is actually STALE (gate is GA-since-1.34-locked-since-1.36 per pkg/features/kube_features.go:2100-2105) -- the label persists because upstream's ginkgowrapper only emits [Alpha]/[Beta] suffixes when PreRelease != empty, and the WithFeatureGate() call hasn't been removed yet. Same pattern as SELinuxChangePolicy which has an explicit '// remove in 1.39' comment. 5 of top 11 FeatureGate labels in test/e2e are already GA-with-stale-tag. Fix should account for this: the ONLY reason we need VolumeAttributesClass in the allow-set today is upstream's slow tag cleanup.

FILE: scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh (near line 179 where --e2e-skip is set + wherever --plugin-env args are passed)
SIZE: script edit + verification run + doc-comment explaining the label-filter semantics
notes:
OPERATOR DESIGN DECISION 2026-08-06: --focus semantics = STACK + explicit --unsafe-focus escape hatch. Symmetric for --skip (whatever answer for label-filter applies to --skip too -- filters compose or they do not, coherent mental model).

Concrete semantics:
- run-all.sh --focus <regex>                     -> label-filter + --skip STILL APPLY (safe default). Named test that carries a filtered-out label runs 0 specs, forcing a deliberate two-step action to add it to allow-set.
- run-all.sh --focus <regex> --unsafe-focus      -> label-filter + --skip WIPED for THIS INVOCATION ONLY. Escape hatch; requires operator to explicitly acknowledge bypass.
- All other invocations (--all-e2e, default certified-conformance): filters always apply; --unsafe-focus not meaningful without --focus.

Rationale: safe by default so operator cannot accidentally re-trigger a known-crashing test (e.g. the HPAConfigurableTolerance panic that killed the 0805-2202 run) by naming it in --focus; explicit --unsafe-focus preserves iteration ergonomics for the rare case where a filtered test needs to actually run once (e.g., to reproduce a bug on record). Consistent with mayor-method Rule 2 (foot-guns should require a deliberate opt-in).

Implementation guidance for worker: --unsafe-focus is a boolean flag parsed by run-all.sh, propagated to 06-run-sonobuoy.sh, which then either passes --plugin-env e2e.E2E_EXTRA_GINKGO_ARGS=... (with label-filter) OR omits it, depending on the flag. The --e2e-skip=\[Flaky\] handling should mirror: pass it unless --unsafe-focus is set.

Sonobuoy wire-through verification (per prior audit caveat) remains a MUST before merge: worker runs a --focus check that exercises the label-filter path (e.g. --focus [FeatureGate:HPAConfigurableTolerance] should return 0 specs with default label-filter, and >0 with --unsafe-focus). This closes the "verified from source not runtime" gap.
close_reason: PR #1019 opened

title: kube-controller-manager has no crash supervision — a single panic silently blacks out control-plane function for hours
description:
In temp/e2e/0805-2202-conformance (--all-e2e run, 2026-08-05), kube-controller-manager
panicked and exited at 09:36:43Z (see companion bead mayor-7ab6g for the panic
itself), 14 minutes into a 12h37m run. It was never restarted: kcm.log
(host-logs/kcm.log on the mayor checkout) has zero further log lines for the
remaining ~12h22m of the run.

Root cause of the "never restarted" part: scripts/conformance/04-start-kcm.sh
starts kube-controller-manager as a bare backgrounded process on the lima VM host
(nohup-style launch, PID captured via $!, no supervisor, no restartPolicy). There is
no systemd unit, no static-pod-with-restartPolicy:Always, and no watchdog that
notices the process is gone.

Because kube-controller-manager owns ServiceAccount auto-provisioning (among many
other controllers: ReplicaSet/Deployment reconciliation, endpoints, PV/PVC binding,
GC, node lifecycle), its silent death meant every subsequent e2e test's shared
[BeforeEach] setup (create namespace, wait ~120s for its "default" ServiceAccount)
timed out — for roughly 2400 consecutive specs across the remaining ~12 hours. This
is why the run's final tally (61 passed / 2401 failed) looks like near-total product
breakage when it is actually the blast radius of one already-dead process.

Compounding gap: meta/clusterhealth.json's node_health block reported both nodes
"healthy":true for the ENTIRE run — cluster health checks in this environment
apparently don't probe kube-controller-manager's liveness at all, so there was no
operator-visible signal of the outage until the junit/e2e failure count was
examined after the fact, ~12 hours later.

New finding, not a duplicate of any known-open bead.

Suggested fix directions (pick at least one):
1. Give kube-controller-manager (and other bare-process control-plane components
   started by scripts/conformance/0*-start-*.sh) a restart-on-crash supervisor
   (e.g. a small wrapper loop, or run under systemd with Restart=on-failure) so a
   single panic degrades gracefully instead of blacking out the control plane for
   the rest of an unattended run.
2. Add kube-controller-manager (and scheduler) liveness to whatever produces
   clusterhealth-equivalent signal in this environment, so "kcm has been silent for
   N minutes" is surfaced immediately instead of discovered via a wall of unrelated
   e2e failures many hours later.
close_reason: PR #1018 opened: kcm-supervisor.sh crash-supervisor with backoff + circuit breaker

title: kube-controller-manager nil-pointer panics reconciling HPA configurable-tolerance test, crashing the whole process
description:
During temp/e2e/0805-2202-conformance (--all-e2e run, 2026-08-05), kube-controller-manager
panicked and exited 14 minutes into a 12.6-hour run:

  E0805 09:36:43.011997 9154 panic.go:336 "Observed a panic"
  panic="runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference"
  ...
  k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/controller/podautoscaler.(*HorizontalController).stabilizeRecommendationWithBehaviors
    k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/controller/podautoscaler/horizontal.go:1213
  k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/controller/podautoscaler.(*HorizontalController).normalizeDesiredReplicasWithBehaviors
    k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/controller/podautoscaler/horizontal.go:1103
  k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/controller/podautoscaler.(*HorizontalController).reconcileAutoscaler
    k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/controller/podautoscaler/horizontal.go:928

Full trace: temp/e2e/0805-2202-conformance/host-logs/kcm.log:238467-238542 (this file
is on the mayor checkout, gitignored under temp/).

Because apimachinery's runtime.HandleCrash defaults ReallyCrash=true, the recovered
panic re-panics and kills the whole kube-controller-manager process (confirmed:
kcm.log has zero lines after 09:36:43, for the remaining ~12h22m of the run).

Test in flight (apiserver.log:292102, user-agent tag on the watch request):
  [sig-autoscaling] [Feature:HPA] [Slow] [FeatureGate:HPAConfigurableTolerance] [Beta]
  Horizontal pod autoscaling (configurable tolerance) with small scale-up, large
  scale-down tolerances should scale up but should not scale down
Immediately preceding log line (kcm.log:238466):
  "Proposing desired replicas" desiredReplicas=0 ... scaleTarget="Deployment/horizontal-pod-autoscaling-3265/consumer"

Hypothesis: this is upstream Go kube-controller-manager code (vendored, not u7s Rust
code), but it is very likely triggered by u7s's apiserver/metrics-server returning
some HPA status/metrics shape that upstream's stabilization-window recommendation-
history logic doesn't expect (e.g. a nil/empty recommendation entry, or an
unexpected zero-replica transition). This HPA code path was only newly exercised
after this session's metrics-server deployment work (PR #1014 / cecbc570), so this
is plausibly a regression surfaced by that change rather than a pre-existing dormant
bug.

Impact: catastrophic in this run specifically because kube-controller-manager has
no restart-on-crash supervision in this environment (see companion bead for that
gap) — this panic alone cascaded into ~2400 downstream e2e failures, since
ServiceAccount auto-provisioning (also owned by kcm) died with it.

New finding, not a duplicate of any known-open bead (mayor-jo7cb/mayor-drs2a/mayor-uuk51
are unrelated: port-forward, watch sharding, metrics-server PartialObjectMetadata watch).

Suggested fix direction: reproduce the HPA configurable-tolerance test in isolation
against u7s, capture the HPA object's .status (recommendations/conditions) right
before the crash, and compare against what upstream's stabilizeRecommendationWithBehaviors
expects (likely a nil slice/pointer in ScaleTargetRef or recommendation history).
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (HIGH confidence) 2026-08-05 (research bed a1811b65):

The panic is NOT in the HPAConfigurableTolerance feature-gate code path. It is in a shared code path that any HPA with a non-nil `spec.behavior.scaleUp` reaches, and it exposes a defaulting-invariant violation in u7s.

Exact nil-deref (horizontal.go:1213 @ release-1.36):
  upDelaySeconds := *args.ScaleUpBehavior.StabilizationWindowSeconds

Confirmed via pointer arithmetic in the panic args: ScaleUpBehavior is a non-nil valid heap addr, but its `StabilizationWindowSeconds *int32` field (offset 0) is nil.

Upstream invariant: once hpa.Spec.Behavior != nil, both ScaleUp and ScaleDown are guaranteed fully-defaulted -- ScaleUp.StabilizationWindowSeconds is never nil. Upstream apiserver enforces this via `SetDefaults_HorizontalPodAutoscalerBehavior` -> `GenerateHPAScaleUpRules` -> `copyHPAScalingRules`, which deep-copies a fully-populated default (StabilizationWindowSeconds=&0) and overlays only caller-set fields. ScaleDown is intentionally left for kcm runtime defaulting (`maybeInitScaleDownStabilizationWindow`), but ScaleUp has NO runtime fallback -- upstream relies entirely on apiserver-side defaulting.

u7s violates this invariant. `crates/apiserver/src/handlers/defaults.rs:9-88` (`apply_defaults` dispatcher) has ZERO dispatch arm for `(autoscaling, horizontalpodautoscalers)` -- every other resource type has a `default_*` call; HPA gets none. And `crates/apiserver/src/autoscaling_gen_adapter.rs:337-359` (`gen_hpa_scaling_rules_to_json`) is pure pass-through: fields serialize only if `Some(v)`. So u7s stores what the client sent, verbatim, forever, on every GET/watch.

Known upstream pattern: issue kubernetes/kubernetes#107038 ("Nil pointer dereference in KCM after v1 HPA patch request") -- exact same panic function and mechanism, previously triggered by an obscure v1-annotation-patch that bypassed v2 defaulting. u7s reproduces the same class of bug via a blanket lack of HPA defaulting rather than an obscure edge case.

PR #1014 (metrics-server deploy) is NOT causal for this bug but plausibly the TRIGGER that exposed it: before #1014, resource HPAs got permanent 404 from metrics.k8s.io and reconcileAutoscaler likely never reached stabilizeRecommendationWithBehaviors; #1014 unblocked metrics -> the reconcile loop ran far enough -> hit the pre-existing dormant defaulting bug for the first time.

FIX SCOPE: u7s-side, bounded. Add an HPA case to `apply_defaults` implementing equivalent of upstream `SetDefaults_HorizontalPodAutoscalerBehavior`/`GenerateHPAScaleUpRules`/`GenerateHPAScaleDownRules`:
  - When hpa.Spec.Behavior.ScaleUp is non-nil but StabilizationWindowSeconds is unset, default to Some(0).
  - Set SelectPolicy=Max, default Policies list, when unset.
  - For ScaleDown, apply same field-level defaulting EXCEPT StabilizationWindowSeconds (intentionally left for kcm).

Full analysis + citations: ai/findings/mayor-7ab6g-hpa-panic-rootcause-2026-08-06.md (mayor checkout, gitignored).

Caveat: apiserver.log does not log request bodies; the "u7s serves null" conclusion is derived from source-code inspection + panic-arg pointer layout, not from a captured wire payload.
close_reason: PR #1016 opened: added default_hpa to apply_defaults, porting upstream SetDefaults_HorizontalPodAutoscalerBehavior/GenerateHPAScaleUpRules/GenerateHPAScaleDownRules to prevent kcm nil-deref at horizontal.go:1213

title: fix(conformance): --all-e2e silently drops [Conformance]-tagged tests that are also [Slow]/[Disruptive]/[Flaky]
description:
scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh's --all-e2e branch (around line 155-167) runs sonobuoy with --e2e-focus=.* --e2e-skip=\[Disruptive\]|\[Flaky\]|\[Slow\]. Ginkgo's --skip is an unconditional regex match against the full spec text -- it has no awareness of whether a spec is ALSO tagged [Conformance]. Confirmed concretely: the upstream StatefulSet Burst-scaling test is framework.ConformanceIt with f.WithSlow(), producing a spec whose text contains both [Slow] and [Conformance] (see mayor-w4rp7's own evidence, spec name literally sig-apps StatefulSet Basic StatefulSet functionality Burst scaling should run to completion even with unhealthy pods [Slow] [Conformance]). This test -- and any other [Conformance]-tagged test that also carries [Disruptive]/[Flaky]/[Slow] -- is silently EXCLUDED from --all-e2e runs, while the SAME test IS included under --mode=certified-conformance (the other branch, which applies no such skip).

This directly contradicts the script's own documented intent: run-all.sh's --all-e2e doc comment (around line 26) says 'Widen sonobuoy beyond the default --mode=certified-conformance' -- i.e. --all-e2e is supposed to be a strict superset of certified-conformance, covering everything certified-conformance covers PLUS the broader ~7500-spec ginkgo set. As currently implemented it is NOT a superset -- it trades away an unknown number of [Conformance]-tagged tests in exchange for the broader net, which is backwards from the stated design and means historical --all-e2e clean-run claims (e.g. any session's 'N/N passed' from an --all-e2e invocation) did not actually cover the full certified-conformance suite.

Fix direction (not decided/implemented here -- needs real design, not a one-line change): ginkgo/RE2 has no negative-lookahead, so a single --e2e-skip regex cannot express 'skip Slow/Disruptive/Flaky UNLESS also Conformance'. The standard correct approach is a two-pass merge: Pass 1 = --e2e-focus=\[Conformance\] with NO skip (equivalent to --mode=certified-conformance, guarantees full conformance coverage including Slow/Disruptive/Flaky conformance tests). Pass 2 = --e2e-focus=.* --e2e-skip=\[Conformance\]|\[Disruptive\]|\[Flaky\]|\[Slow\] (the broader non-conformance net, explicitly excluding conformance specs already covered by pass 1 to avoid double-running them). Aggregate/merge both passes' results for the final --all-e2e report. Whoever picks this up should verify whether sonobuoy's e2e plugin/run_e2e.sh supports running twice into one aggregated result cleanly, or whether this needs two separate sonobuoy runs merged after the fact by 06-run-sonobuoy.sh.

Severity: HIGH/P1 -- this affects the fundamental scope guarantee of a mode this project has used repeatedly for discovery/perf-baseline runs, and the fix is nontrivial (needs a real two-pass restructure, not a regex tweak).
notes:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-05: fix simplified after checking actual overlap against upstream's canonical conformance.yaml (446 tests, fetched release-1.36, cached temp/research/conformance.yaml). Overlap counts: [Flaky] x [Conformance] = 0 (structurally impossible -- a certified suite can't be tagged known-unreliable). [Disruptive] x [Conformance] = 2 (both NoExecuteTaintManager eviction tests). [Slow] x [Conformance] = 6 (API-chunking continuation, 2x CronJob, 2x StatefulSet burst/predictable-order, VolumeSubpathEnvExpansion).

No two-pass merge needed. Simple fix: change --e2e-skip=\[Disruptive\]|\[Flaky\]|\[Slow\] to --e2e-skip=\[Flaky\] only, in the --all-e2e branch of scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh. Dropping Slow/Disruptive from the skip means ALL such tests run (conformance-tagged or not) -- a real superset via a one-line change.

Two objections in the original bead's fix-direction section are WITHDRAWN: (1) wall-clock growth is not a concern -- the overwhelming majority of current wall-clock is watchdog-reaped hangs, not legitimate slow tests, and the default Conformance suite (which already includes Slow tests) completes in ~20min with the current setup. (2) The '[Disruptive] needs multi-node infra our lima setup lacks' rationale in the original script comment is STALE/FALSE -- this project has had 2-node VM support for weeks (--extra-node/--extra-kubelet-port flags in run-all.sh, used throughout this session's own conformance runs). Since --all-e2e must already be a superset of Conformance (which includes 2 Disruptive tests), --all-e2e already implicitly requires 2-node capability regardless of this fix.

Dispatch as a straightforward Solo fix: change the skip pattern, verify the two previously-excluded Disruptive conformance tests and six Slow conformance tests now run under --all-e2e with --extra-node, update/remove the now-inaccurate script comment about --all-e2e's exclusions.
PR #1013 opened with the code fix (e2e-skip narrowed to just Flaky in the --all-e2e branch), stale Disruptive-needs-multi-node comment corrected in both 06-run-sonobuoy.sh and run-all.sh, and a new deterministic regression test test-all-e2e-skip-logic.sh pinning the argv skip pattern - all green (bash -n, all shell logic tests, cargo test/clippy via pre-push hook). LIVE 2-node sonobuoy verification of the 8 target tests could NOT be completed: SSH connectivity to lima-node-smoke and lima-node-3 is refused despite limactl list showing both Running, and the SAME symptom affects the mayor's own lima-node VM (unreachable too) while lima-node-2/4/5 are fine - a pre-existing host-level Lima networking issue unrelated to this change, not something I introduced or could safely fix as a sandboxed worker. Full details and a ready-to-run focus command for re-verification once VMs are healthy are in the PR body. Leaving this open rather than self-closing since the live-verification step of the dispatch is incomplete - mayor should re-run the targeted focus once lima-node-smoke/lima-node-3 recover, then close.
LIVE VERIFICATION COMPLETE 2026-08-05 (after mayor's VM power-cycle fix). Brought up real 2-node stack (lima-node-smoke + lima-node-3, --reset --stack-only), both Ready. Temporarily narrowed --e2e-focus to the 8 target tests and ran the real --all-e2e branch twice via run-all.sh --all-e2e: BEFORE (old skip pattern) all 8 confirmed status=skipped in the JUnit report; AFTER (fixed skip pattern) ginkgo reported Ran 8 of 7579 Specs, 7 Passed, 1 Failed, 7571 Skipped - all 8 were genuinely selected and executed. The 1 failure (NoExecuteTaintManager Multiple Pods eviction) failed on dial tcp 10.96.0.1:443 no route to host mid-test, correlated with a SECOND recurrence of the exact same host-sleep SSH-tunnel-death symptom that had just been power-cycled away, not a fix regression - the sibling Disruptive test (NoExecuteTaintManager Single Pod removing taint cancels eviction) passed cleanly on the same 2-node setup. Reverted the temporary focus-narrowing edit; git diff confirmed clean against the committed fix. PR #1013 body updated with full before/after evidence. Closing this bead with PR #1013 as the resolution.
close_reason: PR #1013 opened and merged-ready: --all-e2e's --e2e-skip narrowed to \[Flaky\] only, stale multi-node comment corrected, regression test added, live 2-node before/after verification confirms all 8 previously-excluded Conformance tests are now genuinely selected/executed (7/8 passed; 1/8 flaked on an unrelated, documented host-sleep SSH-tunnel infra issue).

title: kubectl port-forward completely broken: fabricated WebSocket subprotocol 'v5.portforward.k8s.io' doesn't exist upstream
description:
Live-confirmed 2026-08-04 on lima-node-2 (fresh --reset stack, single pod, isolated repro,
no HPA test involved): plain `kubectl port-forward pf-test 18080:8080` against a Running
agnhost netexec pod fails immediately with:

    error: error upgrading connection: unable to upgrade connection: Request method must be `GET`

This is NOT narrow to HPA. It is a total, unconditional break of port-forward for every
client and every conformance test that uses it (the `sig-cli` "Kubectl Port forwarding"
test class, all currently silently SKIPPED rather than exercised in recent runs because
of unrelated --focus scoping, so this has not been surfacing as its own failure cluster).
It was independently rediscovered while investigating a `sig-autoscaling` HPAScaleToZero
failure (signature #3 of the HPA investigation) whose external-metrics-server probe uses
the same client-go port-forward dialer and hit the identical error text.

ROOT CAUSE (verified against real k8s 1.36 source, `gh api` cached to temp/research/):

crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs's `pod_portforward` handler advertises WebSocket
subprotocol `"v5.portforward.k8s.io"` (proxy.rs:1266, and again on the outbound leg to
kubelet at proxy.rs:1303). This subprotocol name does not exist anywhere in upstream
Kubernetes. The real upstream protocol names (apimachinery
`pkg/util/portforward/constants.go` release-1.36) are:

  - `portforward.k8s.io`          — the only real port-forward protocol name (there is no
                                     v1/v4/v5 versioning for port-forward; that's an
                                     exec/attach-only concept, being confused with here).
  - `SPDY/3.1+portforward.k8s.io` — the WEBSOCKET-TUNNELED-SPDY subprotocol prefix used by
                                     client-go's PRIMARY port-forward dialer
                                     (`portforward.NewSPDYOverWebsocketDialerForStreaming`,
                                     staging/k8s.io/client-go/tools/portforward/tunneling_dialer.go).
                                     This carries REAL SPDY framing (stream multiplexing,
                                     CreateStream with StreamType=error/data headers, a
                                     2-stream pair per forwarded port) INSIDE the websocket
                                     bytes — it is not a plain byte-splice protocol.

Client-go's `test/e2e/framework/pod/dial.go` (same setup code kubectl's own
`pkg/kubectl/cmd/portforward/portforward.go` uses) always tries the SPDY-over-websocket
tunneling dialer FIRST (a GET request), and falls back to legacy raw SPDY-over-HTTP (a
POST request) only if that fails. u7s's router maps BOTH GET and POST for
`/api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/portforward` to the same `pod_portforward` handler
(proxy.rs:2405-2406), which uses axum's `WebSocketUpgrade` extractor — GET-only. So:

  1. The primary GET/tunneling attempt fails (wrong subprotocol offered — no match on
     `SPDY/3.1+portforward.k8s.io` — and even if subprotocol matched, u7s's `splice()`
     implementation does a raw 1:1 byte passthrough, not real SPDY multiplexing, so it
     could not actually carry the SPDY-framed error+data stream pair the client sends).
  2. That failure triggers client-go's fallback to the POST/legacy-SPDY dialer.
  3. The POST hits the same GET-only `WebSocketUpgrade` extractor and axum rejects it
     with its generic, unhelpful "Request method must be `GET`" — which is the exact
     error surfaced to the user/test.

There is a SECOND, independent bug on the outbound (apiserver -> kubelet) leg: u7s
connects to the kubelet's real `wss://.../portForward/...` endpoint using the SAME
fabricated `"v5.portforward.k8s.io"` subprotocol. Real kubelet (cri-streaming
`pkg/streaming/portforward/websocket.go`, confirmed release-1.36 source) DOES support a
native (non-SPDY) websocket port-forward path via `handleWebSocketStreams`, but the
correct subprotocol for that is `"v4." + wsstream.ChannelWebSocketProtocol` i.e.
`"v4.channel.k8s.io"` (reusing the exec/attach channel-multiplexing protocol family,
always v4 — v5 is exec-only, added later for the stdin-close signal, per PR #991 /
mayor-v3bm9). Kubelet's native protocol ALSO requires: one (data, error) channel pair per
forwarded port, and kubelet writes the port number as a little-endian uint16 as the FIRST
2 bytes of each new data/error stream so the client can demux — none of which u7s's
current raw-splice `portforward_proxy` implements.

WHY THIS WASN'T CAUGHT: the "networking-websocket-decision-2026-05-22" memory (and its
originating bead mayor-2d7p, PR #178) recorded the premise "WebSocket only, no SPDY at
any layer... kubelet also speaks WebSocket in 1.34+" as justification for skipping SPDY
support entirely. That premise is INCOMPLETE: kubelet's native websocket path exists but
is only reachable by a client that speaks the exact `v4.channel.k8s.io` protocol AND
correct channel/port-preamble framing — NOT by the subprotocol name u7s actually chose,
and NOT by real kubectl, which (per verified client-go source) only ever offers SPDY
(tunneled-over-websocket or raw) to the apiserver leg, never a bare native protocol
directly. So the "no SPDY at any layer" design cannot interoperate with any real kubectl
client on the client-facing leg, no matter what kubelet supports internally.

SCOPE — NOT attempting this fix in-session (too large to be a bounded, surgical change):
implementing real SPDY-over-websocket tunneling for the client-facing leg (frame-level
SPDY stream multiplexing, not just a subprotocol string) is a genuine protocol
implementation task comparable in size to the original PR #178, not a one-line rename.
Fixing only the kubelet-facing leg's subprotocol name (`v5.portforward.k8s.io` ->
`v4.channel.k8s.io`) without also implementing kubelet's channel/port-preamble framing
would still not produce a working end-to-end path, and would not fix the client-facing
break at all (that's the leg the "Request method must be `GET`" error comes from).

SUGGESTED NEXT STEPS for whoever picks this up:
  1. Decide the architecture: (a) implement genuine SPDY-over-websocket tunneling on the
     client-facing leg (matches how upstream kube-apiserver bridges old SPDY-only clients
     to new kubelets), or (b) confirm whether kubectl 1.36 has since gained a true native
     `v4.channel.k8s.io`-only port-forward client path that could be targeted instead
     (re-verify client-go portforward.go for the exact version in use — this bead's
     research used release-1.36; a newer kubectl minor might differ).
  2. Either way, the outbound (apiserver->kubelet) leg needs its subprotocol corrected to
     `v4.channel.k8s.io` AND the channel-multiplexing / port-preamble framing implemented
     per cri-streaming's `handleWebSocketStreams` (constants and wire format cited above,
     cached at temp/research/kubelet_portforward_websocket.go if still present in a
     worktree, otherwise re-fetch via `gh api .../staging/src/k8s.io/cri-streaming/pkg/streaming/portforward/websocket.go?ref=release-1.36`).
  3. Correct the "networking-websocket-decision-2026-05-22" memory once the real
     interoperability story is nailed down — its "no SPDY at any layer" premise misled
     the original implementation.
  4. Regression gate: `kubectl port-forward <pod> <local>:<remote>` against a real
     listening pod (e.g. agnhost netexec) must succeed end-to-end, plus the `sig-cli`
     "Kubectl Port forwarding" conformance test class via `--focus "Port forwarding"`.

Cross-references: mayor-v3bm9/PR #991 (analogous exec v4/v5 channel subprotocol fix —
same bug family, different subresource). mayor-2d7p/PR #178 (original, now-shown-incomplete
implementation). Filed from the sig-autoscaling/HPA failure-cluster investigation (signature
#3 of that investigation, `[FAILED] Timed out after 120.001s ... unable to upgrade
connection: Request method must be \`GET\`` for
"[sig-autoscaling] [Feature:HPA] [FeatureGate:HPAScaleToZero] ... should scale down to
zero and back up based on external metric value").
notes:
CRATE DECISION LANDED 2026-08-06 (bed a36138b5). Verdict: BYTE-PUMP ONLY, ZERO NEW SPDY CRATES.

Byte-pump sufficiency confirmed from IMPLEMENTER PERSPECTIVE (not just apiserver-source inspection): apimachinery/pkg/util/proxy/upgradeaware.go tryUpgrade @ release-1.36 is what pkg/registry/core/pod/rest/subresources.go:310 actually wires up on the kubelet-facing leg. Its flow: dial() opens raw net.Conn via DialURL and writes outbound HTTP/1.1 upgrade with req.Write(conn), no SPDY object. getResponse() parses only HTTP/1.1 response headers via http.ReadResponse+TeeReader (preserving over-read bytes). On 101 Switching Protocols (L388-410), hijack client connection, replay over-read rawResponse bytes, then PURE bidirectional io.Copy (L419-445) until either side closes. NO SPDY frame (SYN_STREAM, PING, or otherwise) ever constructed by apiserver in this role.

Important framing refinement: client-go/transport/spdy/spdy.go RoundTripperFor (PingPeriod: 5s, feeds NewClientConnectionWithPings which runs a full spdystream.Connection engine and sends periodic keepalive PINGs) is NOT the code path apiserver-proxy uses to reach kubelet. That machinery is for genuine SPDY protocol peers (kubectl-as-client, in-cluster clients using client-go remotecommand/portforward directly). Apiserver, in middleman role, never instantiates it.

CRATE SURVEY: 3 relevant candidates on crates.io (spdy-mux GPL-3.0 blocker, kube-portforward GPL-3.0, spdystream-rs Apache-2.0 but 0 stars/dormant/single-author). All three solve HARDER problem than u7s needs (full multiplexer-peer). None fit the initiator+byte-shuttle shape. h2 crate wire-incompatible with SPDY/3.1 (different frame header layout + zlib-dictionary vs HPACK) and moot anyway.

RECOMMENDATION: byte-pump only. Wins every axis (memory perf, maintainability, fit, effort):
- MEMORY: no per-connection frame buffering/allocation; streams not buffers; stuck peer blocks one io::copy direction, cleaned up by existing timeout/close.
- MAINTAINABILITY: zero new deps; code already exists (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/stream.rs BiStream/splice, 80% present); u7s owns 100%.
- FIT: exact match to u7s role (initiator + shuttle, no server-side SPDY, no multiplexed-session ownership).
- EFFORT: ~200-400 LoC, mostly HTTP-upgrade plumbing.

CAVEAT: "zero crates" depends on u7s NEVER becoming a genuine SPDY protocol peer. If a future requirement needs u7s to terminate SPDY itself (connection pooling to kubelet across client sessions, independent kubelet-endpoint health-checking, etc.), spdystream-rs (Apache-2.0) is the fallback candidate over spdy-mux (GPL-3.0 blocker). Neither is needed today.

Full analysis + citations: ai/findings/spdy-crate-decision-2026-08-06.md (mayor checkout, gitignored).

READY FOR DISPATCH. All research complete, no further research needed. Fix scope: swap wire protocol on both legs of pod_portforward + node_portforward in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs, using existing BiStream/splice for byte-pump. No new crates. ~200-400 LoC. VM verification required (touches network handlers; sonobuoy smoke path exercises port-forward via [sig-cli]).
close_reason: PR #1021 opened — implemented SPDY-tunneled-websocket + legacy raw-SPDY-over-HTTP wire protocol per follow-up research (superseding original v4.channel.k8s.io ground truth). 45/47 sig-cli Port forwarding specs pass on sonobuoy; remaining 2 (native v4.channel.k8s.io websocket client, not kubectl) filed as mayor-zfgar.

title: Stage 2: shard SqliteStore's ring/compaction_horizon/broadcast channel by resource-type prefix (mayor-jzlon Stage 1 proven insufficient)
description:
mayor-jzlon shipped Stage 1 (PR #978, merged 2026-08-03): bumped RING_CAPACITY 1000->100_000 as a low-risk stopgap, explicitly deferring Stage 2 (per-resource-type sharding) with its own close reason saying 'file follow-up bead if/when Stage 1 proves insufficient.' mayor-nlkyd's investigation (2026-08-04) is that trigger case, with real quantified evidence -- filing this as the follow-up Stage 2 bead mayor-jzlon called for.

ROOT MECHANISM (from mayor-nlkyd's investigation): crates/store/src/sqlite.rs's SqliteStore is a SINGLE global instance for the whole apiserver (crates/apiserver/src/lib.rs:202) shared by every resource type. Its ring buffer, compaction_horizon, and broadcast channel (tx, capacity 2048) are global and unsharded. watch()'s initial-connect replay (sqlite.rs ~L1238-1245) and its broadcast-Lagged recovery scan (sqlite.rs ~L1373-1383) both do a full linear .iter().filter(prefix).cloned() over the ENTIRE ring while holding a synchronous std::sync::RwLock read lock -- O(total ring occupancy), not O(matching events).

QUANTIFIED (throwaway, uncommitted microbenchmark): watch-open latency for a prefix with ZERO matching events scaled ~61x from 1k ring occupancy (10.9us) to 100k/full occupancy (670.8us avg over 200 reps).

SYMPTOM THIS EXPLAINS: mayor-nlkyd -- 21 real conformance failures, 'wait for service account default: timed out', clustering entirely in the FINAL ~40 minutes of a 4h29m run (zero occurrences in the first 3h50m), ruled out as apiserver/store request latency (flat <100ms throughout). Plausible compounding mechanism: KCM's serviceaccount/token/root-ca controllers each hold ONE long-lived watch since startup, filtered client-side to their own prefix, but every event from EVERY resource type in the cluster flows through their receiver on the shared broadcast channel -- a slow-consumer moment trips broadcast::error::Lagged, triggering an O(ring) rescan that blocks a tokio worker thread synchronously; as the ring fills toward 100k over a long high-churn run, each rescan gets more expensive and blocks longer, making the NEXT Lagged event more likely -- fits 'fine for 3h50m, then a cluster of failures in the final 40min' well. NOT verified end-to-end via live VM repro (blocked on VM availability during investigation, see mayor-nlkyd's notes) -- verified at the store-layer mechanism level only.

SCOPE (per mayor-jzlon's own Stage 2 description, still accurate): shard the ring/compaction_horizon/deletion_log by resource-type root prefix (same string as crates/apiserver/src/keys.rs::group_list_prefix) instead of one global ring. Requires threading a resource-type-prefix argument through Store::put/delete/create_if_namespace_active/delete_namespace_resources (trait in crates/store/src/lib.rs, impl in crates/store/src/sqlite.rs, ~48 call sites in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/*.rs, plus ~10 mock Store test impls needing the same signature update). watch()'s own prefix argument needs no change -- a namespace-scoped watch prefix is already a sub-prefix of its resource-type root, so it only ever scans one shard. Must preserve the lock-ordering invariant on push_event_locked (broadcast order must match revision-assignment order under write_conn) per-shard. The global bookmark mechanism (key == "") is shard-independent already.

Genuinely large (~300-500 LoC across many files) -- needs proper scoping/sub-issue breakdown before implementation dispatch, not a single bounded fix. Cross-reference: mayor-jzlon (Stage 1, closed), mayor-nlkyd (symptom, closed pointing here), mayor-itre2 (original watch-ring scoping audit).
notes:
SCOPE UPDATE 2026-08-06 (from mayor-1z6hw investigation, findings at ai/findings/stamp-resource-version-growth-investigation-2026-08-06.md):

Stage-2 sharding MUST cover BOTH structures in the SqliteStore's ring/broadcast subsystem, confirmed same subsystem, not two separate concerns:

1. ring: Arc<RwLock<VecDeque<Arc<InternalEvent>>>> (crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:48, 181) — the primary retention structure. RING_CAPACITY=100_000 (sqlite.rs:20). Populated by push_event_locked on every write.

2. deletion_log.by_key: HashMap (crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:32) — sibling structure populated by the same push_event_locked call chain. Grew hashbrown::RawTable::reserve_rehash 811KB in the 0806-1102 dhat run — confirmed as the same subsystem, not a separate concern.

Prior analysis had these as potentially separate; the scout confirmed they share the write path. Any Stage-2 sharding design must partition BOTH by resource-type prefix, not just the ring.

Also from operator direction 2026-08-06: the RING_CAPACITY=100_000 was measured against ~20k ring-pushes across a full 60.5min conformance run. The 100k cap is likely overkill by 5x. A separate bead is being filed (mayor-brxsc or similar) to reduce to 10k and measure — this is orthogonal to Stage-2 but affects the memory calculus underneath it. If cap reduction lands first, Stage-2's per-shard memory budget shifts proportionally.
EVIDENCE ADD 2026-08-10 (memory audit of 0810-0107 conformance run, ai/findings/memory-audit-2026-08-10-run.md, worker worktree agent-a1692f374ff3b3b59, read-only Shape-3 audit mayor-ddcyx):

1. NEW #1 hotspot: push_event_locked (sqlite.rs:257-276) sends TWO broadcast messages per write on the shared `tx` channel -- the specific event, then unconditionally a global bookmark (key="") delivered to EVERY open watch stream regardless of resource-type prefix ("Broadcast a global bookmark... to advance all informers' sync RVs", sqlite.rs:258). Every watcher with allowWatchBookmarks=true materializes this into ndjson_bookmark() (handlers/watch.rs:1209-1230). dhat jq (sort .pps by -.tb, resolve .fs[1]) shows this is now the SINGLE LARGEST allocation site in the whole apiserver: 694,089,088 B / 4,579,223 blocks (5.80% of total 11.95GB tb this run) -- ~1,877 calls/sec sustained over the 40.67min run. This also explains why h2::/hyper:: (+6.33pp) and rustls (+2.58pp) category shares grew in this run vs the 08-06 baseline: top pps in both categories resolve to the SAME ndjson_bookmark/ndjson_event_value/Bytes::from(Vec<u8>) sites, i.e. the wire-encoding growth is downstream of this same broadcast fan-out, not 3 independent issues.

OPEN QUESTION for Stage-2 scoping this raises, not currently addressed by the existing scope: does the global bookmark still need to fan out to every watcher on every single write once shards exist, or can it be throttled/coalesced per shard while still meeting KCM's EnsureReady() cross-resource-RV contract (sqlite.rs:259-262, the reason the global bookmark exists at all)? Sharding the ring alone does not obviously reduce this fan-out cost since cross-shard consistency is the whole point of the global bookmark.

2. delete_sync's Row::get "zero-free" pattern (dhat-triage-2026-08-06-run.md fix target #4, which called for "a new bead" after a source read) -- READ crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:469-532 this run: delete_sync reads the deleted object's full JSON body and immediately moves it into Bytes::from(...) as its return value, which the caller threads into InternalEvent.deleted_body -- retained BY DESIGN in deletion_log.by_key so a reconnecting watcher can still get a correct DELETED event body for an object deleted before ring compaction. This is NOT a bug, it's the same deletion_log/ring subsystem already in Stage-2's scope (confirmed, matches the 2026-08-06 stamp_resource_version-growth doc's finding that ring and deletion_log share the same write path). mb=11,263,970 this run, essentially unchanged from baseline's 11.11MB -- stable, not growing. The 08-06 doc's "new bead needed" call for this specific site is superseded/retracted by this read.

3. RING_CAPACITY=10,000 (mayor-h3zlt, PR #1037) confirmed LIVE and SAFE in this run: grep -c "ring buffer compacted" host-logs/apiserver.log = 19,856 compactions; grep -c "Lagged" = 0; the 82 status=410 responses are all attributable to CRD-deletion namespace-controller cleanup + the API-chunking conformance test's own intentional-410 assertion (test name literally "if the original version has been compacted away"), not ring-truncation. No regression from the cap reduction. BUT: the ring filled to its 10k cap in only ~13.5 minutes this run (first compaction at 00:40:33, process start 00:27:04) at the observed ~12.3 writes/sec rate (19,856+10,000=29,856 pushes / 2440s) -- roughly DOUBLE the 5.6/sec rate mayor-h3zlt's own bead body used to project a ~29-minute retention window. Push rate has measurably grown since that sizing was done (2026-08-06 -> 2026-08-10). Still safe today (0 real watch 410s from ring truncation), but the safety margin has shrunk by roughly half in 4 days. Relevant to Stage-2's per-shard capacity sizing: a shard serving a hot resource type at 12+/sec on its own would fill a proportionally-sized shard ring even faster than the current global ring does.

title: u7s apiserver: Pod delete (grace-period=0, no finalizers) never purges object from store
description:
Discovered while doing mandatory live verification for mayor-805ga (06-run-sonobuoy.sh retrieval fix). Confirmed reproducible against the live lima-node/lima-node-3 apiserver instance at /Users/balint.erdos/u7s (long-running, >1h uptime).

Symptom: `kubectl delete pod sonobuoy -n sonobuoy --grace-period=0 --force` returns a success message ("pod ... force deleted"), sets deletionTimestamp + deletionGracePeriodSeconds=0 on the object, but the Pod is NEVER actually removed from the store -- `kubectl get pod` keeps showing it (STATUS Terminating) 9+ minutes later. `metadata.finalizers` is null (no finalizer is blocking it). `crictl ps -a` on the node confirms no real container was ever created for this pod (it was stuck Pending) -- so this is not a kubelet/CRI-side issue, it's the apiserver/store itself failing to purge a deletable object.

Downstream effect: any workflow that deletes-then-recreates a namespace+objects with the same names (e.g. `sonobuoy delete --all --wait` followed by a fresh `sonobuoy run`) hits "the server reported a conflict" on every object whose stale copy is still silently present in the store, and namespace deletion itself hangs indefinitely in "Terminating" waiting for content that was supposedly already deleted.

Reproduction: real 2-node lima-node/lima-node-3 cluster, delete a Pod with --grace-period=0 --force via kubectl, then poll `kubectl get pod` -- it keeps showing Terminating far past any reasonable delay, despite no finalizers and no real container.

Impact: blocks reliable sonobuoy re-runs against a long-lived apiserver without manually deleting every stale object by hand across multiple resource kinds (namespace, serviceaccount, clusterrole, clusterrolebinding, configmap, secret, service, pod) -- confirmed needing manual cleanup across ALL of those kinds during this investigation.

Not fixed here -- out of scope for mayor-805ga (which is about 06-run-sonobuoy.sh's retrieval-sequence timeout/node-search bugs only). Filing separately per Rule 12 (surface, don't silently work around).
notes: PR #995 opened. Confirmed does NOT reproduce on a bare fresh instance (kubelet-alive scheduled pod completes ~3s via kubelet's own follow-up DELETE; unscheduled pod completes ~16s via KCM pod-GC gcUnscheduledTerminating). Reproduces reliably once the pod's assigned node's kubelet is dead/unresponsive, because scripts/conformance/04-start-kcm.sh disables node-lifecycle-controller entirely -- nothing ever fires the confirming second DELETE for a pod stuck on a dead-but-not-deleted node. Root cause: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs delete_pod (~line 950) and delete_collection_pods only hard-deleted on an already-Terminating object or a second call, never on the first call even when the caller explicitly requested gracePeriodSeconds=0. Genuinely SEPARATE mechanism from mayor-1920p: that bug lives entirely in namespaces.rs's cascade-delete (store-level, already unconditionally hard-deletes finalizer-free objects) and is a TOCTOU race with a concurrent finalizer-clearing PATCH -- a code path this bug's direct single-pod delete never goes through. No shared root cause, no namespaces.rs changes needed. Fix: delete_pod/delete_collection_pods now hard-delete immediately on the first call when gracePeriodSeconds=0 is explicitly requested and no finalizers are present (finalizers still block regardless of --force). Verified live on a fresh 2-node lima-node/lima-node-3 cluster: pre-fix pod on dead-kubelet node stuck Terminating 15+ min across an apiserver restart; post-fix identical scenario purges within ~3s of the single DELETE call, confirmed via apiserver access log showing exactly one DELETE then a 404 GET. Filed mayor-pqw78 for an unrelated pre-existing flaky test found during verification.
close_reason: PR #995 opened - fix + regression tests + live before/after verification on fresh 2-node lima cluster

title: 06-run-sonobuoy.sh results retrieval fails silently -- hardcoded to primary VM_NAME, no timeout on any blocking call
description:
Live incident 2026-08-04 ~17:48 JST: operator ran a targeted --focus test (2-node, --extra-node lima-node-3), sonobuoy completed cleanly ('Sonobuoy has completed'), but 06-run-sonobuoy.sh's retrieval logic produced ZERO output after echoing 'Retrieving results...' (temp/e2e/0804-0848-terminal.log:461, last line) and the run-all.sh process returned control with no results file ever written to temp/e2e/. Manually recovered via the standard crictl/emptyDir playbook -- confirmed the sonobuoy pod was scheduled onto lima-node-3 (the EXTRA node), not lima-node (the primary VM_NAME), and the results tarball genuinely existed the whole time at /var/lib/kubelet/pods/<uid>/volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir/output-volume on lima-node-3. Recovered results archived at temp/e2e/0804-0848-focus-recovered/ -- both targeted tests failed as expected (pre-fix baseline, consistent with mayor-ax87f).

TWO confirmed/suspected bugs in the retrieval sequence (06-run-sonobuoy.sh:179-214):

1. CONFIRMED: line 202-204's 'limactl shell "$VM_NAME" sudo find /var/lib/kubelet/pods/${POD_UID}/volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir -name "$TARBALL_NAME"' searches ONLY $VM_NAME (the primary node). It never checks $EXTRA_NODE. Sonobuoy's own scheduler can and does place the aggregator pod on either node in a 2-node run -- when it lands on the extra node, this find always returns empty on the wrong VM.

2. STRONGLY SUSPECTED (matches every observed symptom -- total silence, no error message despite the script having explicit 'error: tarball not found...' >&2 exit paths at both failure branches, script apparently returning control with nothing printed): NONE of the blocking external calls in this sequence -- kubectl logs (line 184), kubectl get pod ... jsonpath (line 198), limactl shell ... find (line 202), limactl copy (line 220) -- have any timeout wrapper. If any one of them stalls (transient SSH/konnectivity hiccup, VM briefly unresponsive), the whole script hangs indefinitely with zero diagnostic output, violating Rule 12 (Fail Loud). The existing 'error: tarball not found' messages only fire if the commands actually RETURN (even if empty) -- they provide no protection against a call that never returns at all.

FIX NEEDED:
- Wrap every blocking call in this retrieval sequence with an explicit timeout (with a clear, actionable error message identifying WHICH call timed out) so a stall surfaces loudly instead of silently.
- Search for the results tarball across ALL nodes in the run ($VM_NAME AND $EXTRA_NODE if set), not just the primary -- mirroring how other parts of this script family already iterate NODES=("$VM_NAME" ${EXTRA_NODE:+"$EXTRA_NODE"}) (see line 237-238 for the existing pattern used for host-logs collection).
- Regression test per Rule 14, matching the existing test-teardown-vm-logic.sh / test-port-kill-logic.sh pattern in this same directory (real spawned processes, not just string logic) -- demonstrate the old buggy behavior (wrong-node search fails; a hung call blocks forever) vs the fixed behavior (correct node found; a stalled call times out loudly).
- MANDATORY VERIFICATION per mayor policy (bd memories fix-verification-required-before-merge): re-run a real small --focus test with a 2-node setup and confirm automatic retrieval succeeds without manual intervention -- this exact failure mode is now trivially reproducible on demand.
notes:
Fixed both bugs in scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh's retrieval sequence: (1) tarball search now loops over NODES ($VM_NAME + $EXTRA_NODE), and the subsequent stage/copy steps target the node where it was actually found (fixing just the search wasn't enough); (2) all 5 blocking calls (kubectl logs, kubectl get pod, limactl shell find, limactl shell cp, limactl copy) wrapped in a new run_with_timeout() helper that kills a stalled call and prints which one timed out.

Regression test: scripts/conformance/test-sonobuoy-retrieval-logic.sh, matching sibling test conventions (real spawned processes, RUN_OLD_BUGGY_VERSION=1 toggle). 9/9 assertions pass.

Notable implementation detail: run_with_timeout() polls via 'kill -0' rather than backgrounding a second 'wait'-based watchdog -- the watchdog approach hung indefinitely under this script's own 'set -e' in bash 3.2 (macOS's shipped /bin/bash). Confirmed and fixed during development.

Live verification: ran the fixed script against the assigned lima-node + lima-node-3 topology. Confirmed the fail-loud path works correctly in a real run (lima-node's SSH broke mid-run from ambient host flakiness -- also independently reproduced on lima-node-5 -- and the script correctly caught it, printed the graceful degradation warning, and exited cleanly instead of hanging silently). Did NOT achieve a full green sonobuoy pass: discovered and filed a separate, serious bug (mayor-6sv46) where a deleted Pod (grace-period=0, no finalizers) is never purged from the apiserver's store, poisoning every subsequent run with "server reported a conflict". Out of scope for this bead, not fixed here.

title: service-account provisioning timeouts cluster entirely in final ~40min of long run -- controller backlog, not apiserver latency
description:
Full audit of the 0804-focus run (temp/e2e/0804-focus-recovered/, findings: ai/findings/focus-run-91pct-failure-and-spec-count-discrepancy-2026-08-04.md, worker worktree agent-ad38ea32d61fce94d) found 21 failures with signature:

  [FAILED] wait for service account "default" in namespace "<ns>": timed out waiting for the condition
  In [BeforeEach] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework/framework.go:372

Extracting the embedded timestamp from all 21 failures shows a striking pattern: ALL 21 occur in the FINAL ~40 minutes of a 4h29m run (05:52:03 UTC through 06:32:07 UTC -- the run ended at 06:32:08 UTC), at a regular ~2-minute cadence, with ZERO occurrences in the first ~3h50m. This is not a general "service account bootstrap is broken" capability gap -- new namespaces successfully got their default SA provisioned for the entire first 87% of the run.

Checked and RULED OUT as apiserver request-latency: apiserver.log shows flat, fast (<100ms for 99.996% of requests) latency for the ENTIRE run window, including the final 40 minutes where these failures start appearing. If apiserver itself were the bottleneck, request latency would show it; it doesn't.

This points at a CONTROLLER-side backlog or degradation that builds up over a long, high-namespace-churn run (thousands of e2e test namespaces created over 4.5h, each needing a default ServiceAccount + token + kube-root-ca.crt configmap from kube-controller-manager) -- most likely kube-controller-manager's serviceaccount-controller, token-controller, or root-ca-cert-publisher-controller falling behind (growing work-queue depth, or some resource exhaustion in KCM itself) rather than anything in the apiserver/store request path.

Needs: check KCM's own logs/metrics for this run's final ~40 minutes (host-logs/kcm.log if captured) for work-queue depth growth, error rates, or resource pressure in the serviceaccount/token/root-ca controllers specifically. Consider whether this generalizes to any sufficiently long/high-churn run (would affect full, non-focus conformance runs too, just later in their longer wall-clock).
notes:
INVESTIGATION (2026-08-04): synthetic repro NOT attempted end-to-end -- code-level root cause found first, with high confidence, so no VM-based repro was forced (see env-note below). Root cause: crates/store/src/sqlite.rs's SqliteStore is a SINGLE global instance for the whole apiserver (crates/apiserver/src/lib.rs:202, one store for every resource type). Its ring buffer, compaction_horizon, and broadcast channel (`tx`) are likewise global and unsharded by resource type -- confirmed by reading watch() (sqlite.rs ~L1227-1390): every watch-open (initial connect, sqlite.rs:1238-1245) AND every broadcast-Lagged recovery scan (sqlite.rs:1373-1383) does a full linear `.iter().filter(prefix).cloned()` over the ENTIRE ring while holding a synchronous (non-async, no spawn_blocking) std::sync::RwLock read lock -- cost is O(total ring occupancy), not O(matching events), regardless of how few events actually match the watcher's own resource-type prefix.

Quantified via a throwaway #[tokio::test] microbenchmark (not committed): watch-open latency for a prefix with ZERO matching events scaled ~61x from 1k ring occupancy (10.9µs) to 100k/full occupancy (670.8µs; avg 241.5µs over 200 reps) -- confirms real O(ring-size) scaling, not just a theoretical concern.

This is the EXACT unaddressed gap flagged (Stage 2, "per-resource-type ring sharding") when mayor-jzlon shipped Stage 1 (PR #978, RING_CAPACITY 1000->100_000, merged 2026-08-03): "Ring is still global; a busy resource can still evict a quiet one but with 100x more headroom... file follow-up bead if/when Stage 1 proves insufficient." Mechanism fits mayor-nlkyd's symptom well: KCM's serviceaccount/token/root-ca controllers each hold ONE long-lived watch since startup, filtered client-side to their own prefix, but every event from EVERY resource type in the whole cluster (pods, events, leases, configmaps, etc., all sharing the one broadcast channel, capacity 2048) flows through their receiver -- a slow consumer moment (GC pause, CPU contention) trips broadcast::error::Lagged, triggering an O(ring) rescan that blocks a tokio worker thread synchronously; as the ring fills toward 100k over a long, high-namespace-churn run, each rescan gets more expensive and blocks longer, making the NEXT Lagged event more likely -- a plausible compounding-backlog mechanism matching "fine for ~3h50m, then a cluster of failures in the final ~40min."

Did NOT attempt the full synthetic namespace-churn VM repro from the original task: lima-node-4 (my VM assignment) was occupied by a fully orphaned stack (apiserver PID 69871 port 6446, KCM PID 4318 in-VM, scheduler, konnectivity-server) from a worktree (agent-abe69abb4643ef481) that no longer exists on disk (confirmed via ls/git worktree) -- both `reset.sh --vm lima-node-4` and a direct `kill` of the specific orphaned PIDs were denied by the session's auto-mode safety classifier as workload-interference risk, even with this evidence presented. Given the code-level finding was already strong and quantified, I did not force a new VM to complete the live E2E repro (would cost significant additional token/wall-clock budget for a live-run confirmation of a mechanism already demonstrated at the unit level) -- flagging this as unverified end-to-end, verified at the store-layer mechanism level.

Separately, note lima-node-4 needs manual operator cleanup (orphaned stack from a deleted worktree) before its next assignment.

title: scheduler treats a 409 'already assigned' bind rejection as a genuine scheduling failure, incorrectly marking a running pod Unschedulable
description:
Discovered live 2026-08-04: a --focus run (temp/e2e/0804-0057-focus, testing '\\[sig-storage\\].*(csi-hostpath|csi-mock|Ephemeral|nfs3|local)|\\[sig-node\\].*DRA|\\[sig-autoscaling\\]' on the 2-node lima-node+lima-node-3 setup, post mayor-pxm9c + mayor-6oqbd) produced no usable results -- sonobuoy reported the e2e plugin as failed despite the pod's containers genuinely running the whole time.

Root cause chain, fully confirmed via apiserver.log:
  00:28:38.246  POST .../sonobuoy-e2e-job-.../binding  status=201  (genuine first bind, succeeds)
  00:57:03.059  POST .../sonobuoy-e2e-job-.../binding  status=409  (mayor-4526p's periodic ~30min duplicate-bind fires again, correctly REJECTED by mayor-6oqbd's new already-assigned guard)

The 409 is correct apiserver behavior (mayor-6oqbd working as designed). But the recovered plugins/e2e/errors/global/error.json shows the pod's PodScheduled condition got flipped to False/Unschedulable with the 409's conflict message as the reason -- despite both containers (e2e, sonobuoy-worker) showing state.running the entire time, per the SAME error.json's containerStatuses. The pod was never actually unschedulable; it was already running successfully when the spurious duplicate-bind attempt fired.

Traced to crates/scheduler/src/main.rs: bind_reserved_node (line ~40) propagates ANY error from the bind call uniformly as anyhow::Error. Its caller in handle_pod_event's outcome match (line ~620-651) folds every Err(e) into the SAME 'FailedScheduling' path regardless of cause -- it calls failed_scheduling_status_patch and PATCHes PodScheduled=False onto the pod, with no special case for 'the bind was rejected because the pod is already correctly bound elsewhere' (409/Conflict, semantically a benign no-op) versus 'no viable node was found' or 'the apiserver call itself failed' (genuine scheduling failures worth reporting).

Impact: this is not a NEW regression from mayor-6oqbd -- the scheduler's naive error handling always existed, it just had no legitimate way to observe a bind rejection before that fix existed (previously the apiserver silently accepted every duplicate bind with 201, so the scheduler never received an error to mishandle). Now that the apiserver correctly rejects duplicates, this latent gap actively corrupts the PodScheduled status of any pod that mayor-4526p's periodic duplicate-bind bug touches -- which, per mayor-4526p's own findings, is EVERY pod in the cluster, roughly every 30 minutes, for the life of the scheduler process. This directly caused THIS test run's failure to produce results (sonobuoy's own monitoring almost certainly treats PodScheduled=False as 'plugin never started properly'). Likely still causing incorrect status/events for other long-running pods too, not just sonobuoy's own job pod.

Fix: bind_reserved_node / bind_pod (the scheduler's own HTTP client function, not the apiserver handler of the same name) needs to distinguish a 409 Conflict specifically (ideally by status code, or the 'already assigned to node' message if status code isn't easily threaded through the current anyhow::Error type) from other bind failures. On that specific outcome, treat it as a benign no-op: do NOT patch PodScheduled=False, do NOT emit a FailedScheduling event, and do NOT remove the pod's reservation from NodeTally (it's already correctly bound and counted from the FIRST successful bind -- removing it now would under-count that node's real usage). This likely needs a new error variant/enum case threaded through bind_reserved_node's Result, mirroring how PickNodeError/PreemptionFailure already distinguish failure kinds elsewhere in this same file.

Regression test: a bind attempt returning 409 'already assigned' must result in no PodScheduled patch, no FailedScheduling event, and no NodeTally removal -- distinct from a bind attempt failing for any other reason, which must still patch PodScheduled=False as today.
close_reason: PR #990 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/990

title: kubectl exec with stdin (tar streaming, e.g. kubectl cp) hangs indefinitely after channel opens
description:
During the --all-e2e conformance run (temp/e2e/0803-1624-conformance,
2026-08-03), namespace kubectl-9853 ("[sig-cli] Kubectl client Simple pod
should return command exit codes should handle in-cluster config") was force-
deleted by the 10-minute conformance watchdog after going completely silent
(zero further apiserver requests of any kind from the e2e.test client) for
~9m47s.

Sequence from host-logs/apiserver.log (all against pod kubectl-9853/agnhost,
user_agent=kubectl/v1.36.0):
  15:07:20.561  exec printenv KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST      -> status=101 (ok, completes)
  15:07:20.803  exec printenv KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT       -> status=101 (ok, completes)
  15:07:21.032  exec test -d /tmp                           -> status=101 (ok, completes)
  15:07:21.313  exec tar -xmf - -C /tmp  (stdin=true)        -> status=101 (channel opens)
  [... nothing at all from the test until 15:17:08 ...]
  15:17:08  watchdog force-deletes namespace kubectl-9853 (Active for 600s)
  15:17:09  KCM garbage-collects the now-orphaned pod
  15:17:49  the test's own AfterEach finally resumes, all its cleanup calls
            return 404 (resources already gone, reaped by the watchdog)

The 4th exec (tar with stdin=true, used to stream a kubectl binary/kubeconfig
into the pod for the "in-cluster config" check — kubectl cp-style usage)
successfully upgrades the connection (HTTP 101) but the data transfer never
completes and control never returns to the caller. This is not a "test is
slow" pattern (no incremental apiserver activity of any kind occurs during
the gap, unlike the ephemeral/provisioning storage-testsuite cases which show
continuous background traffic) — it is a genuine hang in u7s's exec/stdin
plumbing (apiserver exec handler and/or its CRI-O attach implementation) that
only resolves when the pod is force-killed out from under it.

Needs a focused repro: kubectl exec into a pod with --stdin and pipe a tar
stream (`tar cf - <path> | kubectl exec -i <pod> -- tar xf - -C /dest`) and
confirm whether the write-side of the stdin stream is dropped, never signals
EOF to the container process, or the exit-status frame never gets sent back
to the client. Check crates/apiserver's exec/attach handler and the crio
attach forwarding path.

Findings doc (not committed, local only):
ai/findings/all-e2e-watchdog-reap-analysis-2026-08-04.md, section 4b.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #991: kubelet-side exec subprotocol was hardcoded to v4.channel.k8s.io while kubectl's real client only negotiates v5 (which carries the stdin CLOSE signal). Root-caused and live-reproduced before/after on lima-node-5.

title: HPA Scale subresource hardcodes status.selector="" — every HorizontalPodAutoscaler permanently fails to compute metrics
description:
During the --all-e2e conformance run (temp/e2e/0803-1624-conformance,
2026-08-03), all 5 horizontal-pod-autoscaling-* test namespaces reaped by the
conformance watchdog show the identical failure in host-logs/kcm.log: the HPA
controller logs "selector is required" / event reason FailedComputeMetricsReplicas
every ~15s continuously from shortly after the HPA is created until the
namespace is force-deleted at the 10-minute watchdog threshold. No HPA test
in this run ever computed a desired replica count.

Root cause, confirmed by reading crates/apiserver/src/handlers/scale.rs:
build_scale() (the handler backing GET/PUT/PATCH .../scale for Deployments,
ReplicaSets, StatefulSets, and ReplicationControllers) hardcodes:

    "status": { "replicas": status_replicas, "selector": "" }

status.selector is ALWAYS an empty string, regardless of the workload's own
spec.selector. Upstream's HPA controller
(pkg/controller/podautoscaler/horizontal.go:397-403,
validateAndParseSelector) treats an empty selector string as a hard,
unrecoverable error and never proceeds to metric collection — so no
HorizontalPodAutoscaler can ever converge against u7s, independent of
[Slow]/[Flaky] tagging. This also breaks real (non-test) HPA usage, not just
conformance.

No existing helper in the codebase converts a workload's spec.selector
(LabelSelector) into the string form (comma-separated key=value / set-based
expressions) that the Scale subresource's status.selector field requires —
grepped crates/ for label_selector_to_string / selector_to_string style
helpers, found none.

Fix: build_scale (or its callers in scale_get_impl/scale_put_impl/scale_patch_impl)
needs to read the stored workload's spec.selector and serialize it to a label
selector string, then populate status.selector with that value instead of "".

Evidence path: temp/e2e/0803-1624-conformance/host-logs/kcm.log, search
"horizontal-pod-autoscaling-7446" for a representative example (created
14:50:44 UTC, HPA created 14:51:04, first "selector is required" at 14:51:19,
repeats every ~15s until watchdog reaps the namespace at 15:01:13).

Findings doc (not committed, local only):
ai/findings/all-e2e-watchdog-reap-analysis-2026-08-04.md, section 4a.

title: Instrumented Guestbook conformance run + cross-VM contention root-cause under vzNAT-primary
description:
Follow-on to mayor-b3ns9 (measurement-only, no PR).

mayor-b3ns9 confirmed lima-node is now vzNAT-primary (no lima0 interface at
all; host.lima.internal -> 192.168.104.2 via eth0). Synthetic burst probes
against the shared apiserver (host.lima.internal:6443/healthz) from idle
VMs lima-node-2/lima-node-4 (substituted for the originally-scoped
instrumented Guestbook conformance run, which was skipped for budget - no
idle VM had a running stack and this worktree had no pre-built binaries)
found:

1. vzNAT does NOT eliminate the SYN-blackhole pathology class documented by
   mayor-biy31/mayor-mjt51 under usernet. Solo single-VM bursts up to N=5000
   are always clean (0 failures, all nstat/netstat/apiserver-log counters
   zero); N=10000 solo produces 0.02-0.44% curl-side connection timeouts
   with zero counter visibility anywhere (guest kernel, Mac kernel,
   apiserver's own 429/5xx log) - same "invisible blackhole" signature as
   the usernet case, confirmed via source-port+TCP-seq SYN-cascade pcap
   analysis (35 groups with 3+ retransmits, 114 first-retries clustered in
   a single second, 2 flows fully exhausted tcp_syn_retries=6 with no
   SYN-ACK ever received - matches curl's reported failure count 1:1).

2. UNEXPECTED and NOT YET EXPLAINED: simultaneous N=5000+N=5000 bursts from
   TWO DIFFERENT idle VMs (lima-node-2 + lima-node-4) against the same
   shared apiserver produced a combined 9.84% failure rate (984/10000) -
   roughly 20-40x higher than the same total volume (10000) concentrated in
   a single VM (0.02-0.44%). This is strong evidence of a shared bottleneck
   across concurrently-running VMs that vzNAT does not eliminate, directly
   contradicting the hypothesis that per-VM vzNAT interfaces give each VM
   an independent path to the host. Candidates not yet distinguished:
   Apple Virtualization.framework's own NAT implementation being a
   shared/serialized resource across VMs, vs. plain Mac-host CPU contention
   across 5 concurrently-running VMs during simultaneous fork-storm bursts.

3. Retry-timing anomaly (also unexplained): the guest kernel's SYN
   retransmit cadence for fully-exhausted flows was near-constant ~1.0-1.03s
   for 5 successive retries then a single ~2x jump, NOT the standard Linux
   RFC6298 exponential doubling (1,2,4,8,16s) despite
   sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_syn_retries=6 confirmed default. Possible guest-
   scheduler-under-load artifact or vzNAT-side retiming effect.

Task:
- Run the originally-scoped instrumented `--focus 'Guestbook application
  should create and stop a working application'` conformance capture
  (scripts/conformance/instrument-vip-capture.sh + tcpdump) on an idle VM
  freshly provisioned with vzNAT-primary, to see whether REAL conformance
  watch-reconnect traffic reproduces the same pattern as this synthetic
  curl-burst substitute, or something different/worse (real kubelet watch
  reconnects are less uniform than curl bursts).
- Investigate the Phase 6 cross-VM interference finding specifically - it
  is the most actionable and surprising result and needs root-causing
  (Mac host CPU/scheduler contention vs. shared vzNAT/Virtualization.
  framework internals) before concluding whether vzNAT is actually better
  or worse than usernet for OUR multi-VM conformance workload.

This bead's dispatch (today) inherited that stale premise without re-verification -- mayor error, not the worker's. Both assigned VMs (lima-node-2, lima-node-4) confirmed live on plain user-v2/usernet, not vzNAT, contra the bead's stale premise. Reframed remaining work around current operational risk under usernet. Findings (worktree-only, not on main): ai/findings/vznat-cross-vm-contention-2026-08-05.md in worktree agent-acaa52c79ef6b2543. Key results: (1) structurally confirmed the shared bottleneck candidate is a single host-wide 'limactl usernet' Go process backing every concurrently-running VM's networking (its lease table lists all 6 running VMs); (2) solo N=10000 burst baseline reproduced (0.11% failure, matches prior 0.02-0.44% range), with failures clustering tightly at the burst's peak per-second connection-attempt rate (~700-800/s), not spread by elapsed time or generic host CPU business alone; (3) attempted replication of mayor-b3ns9's simultaneous 5000+5000 cross-VM burst (9.84% reported) instead measured 0.06% combined failures -- did NOT reproduce the 20-40x amplification; shared-usernet-process CPU profile was similar between solo/cross-VM runs in this attempt.
