title: Experiment: test vzNAT Lima network driver vs usernet SYN-drop baseline (correct mayor-1pj1u scoping)
description:
Correction to mayor-1pj1u scoping and mayor-jh31w experiment: both erroneously
treated 'no VM-to-VM path' as a disqualifier for vzNAT. But per mayor-jh31w's
actual live experiment, Lima network drivers ADD an interface (lima0), they
don't REPLACE the default (eth0) — meaning vzNAT would run alongside Lima's
default network, not instead of it, and VM-to-VM cross-node pod traffic could
continue using whatever handles it today.

Also: Lima's docs (https://lima-vm.io/docs/config/network/vmnet/) explicitly
say vzNAT is the recommended choice for VZ instances for guest-to-host
performance. That's exactly the traffic pattern (kubelet -> apiserver,
cri-o -> registries) causing our SYN blackholes.

## Experiment scope (matches mayor-jh31w shape)

Same measurement approach as mayor-jh31w:
1. Provision a fresh test VM with `networks: - lima: vzNAT`
2. Verify Phase 3 correctness: VM-to-VM ping (via whatever interface),
   host.lima.internal (should now route over vzNAT for VZ instances per
   the docs), guest OS reachability
3. Attach instrument-vip-capture.sh + tcpdump
4. Run --focus '[Conformance]' via run-all.sh
5. Compare SYN cascades against mayor-biy31 attempt-2 baseline (usernet)
   AND against mayor-jh31w's socket_vmnet result:
   - usernet: 1x 36.1s single-flow + 1x ~20s mass event
   - socket_vmnet shared (mayor-jh31w): 24 events, max 67.9s, 158/481 fails
6. Cleanup: delete test VM.

Absolute constraint (same as mayor-jh31w): NO PR from this experiment.
Findings + follow-on bead only. Operator approves any driver switch after
seeing measured evidence.

## Why redo this

Prior scoping (mayor-1pj1u) dismissed vzNAT based on unmeasured architectural
assumption ('no VM-to-VM path') that mayor-jh31w's shared-mode experiment
subsequently invalidated as a valid disqualification pattern (Lima drivers
add, not replace). Direct measurement will settle it.
close_reason: Measured: vzNAT (networks: - vzNAT: true) attaches as a second interface (lima0) exactly like socket_vmnet shared did — host.lima.internal still resolves on eth0's subnet and 'ip route get' confirms eth0 carries the traffic despite lima0 having a better default-route metric. Disqualified, same class as socket_vmnet (mayor-jh31w). Findings: ai/findings/vznat-experiment-results-2026-08-03.md (worker worktree). No PR, no follow-on bead (2nd of 2 Lima network-driver candidates to fail the identical structural test — line of investigation closed).

title: PR #980 pre-pull breaks Lima provisioning — 'e2e-test-images conformance set is pre-pulled' probe times out on fresh VMs
description:
Operator hit this immediately after PR #980 merged: multiple --reset runs
failed with:
  INFO[0106] [hostagent] Waiting for the optional requirement 6 of 6:
    "e2e-test-images conformance set is pre-pulled"
  ... [tries several times over ~10 min] ...
  FATA[0603] did not receive an event with the "running" status

## Root cause

PR #980 (mayor-5fkx5) put the 10-image pre-pull loop inside lima/kubelet.yaml
mode:system provisioning block, coupled to Lima's own "e2e-test-images
conformance set is pre-pulled" probe. Any failure or slowness in the ~1GB of
image pulls (usernet burst-drop, mirror lag, transient DNS, or simply
first-time-on-a-Mac cold pulls) either:
  (a) Aborts the provisioning script via set -euo pipefail, leaving cache
      incomplete → probe never satisfies → 10min timeout, or
  (b) Takes longer than Lima's 10min provision timeout even on a happy path
      if the Mac's first-ever pull of these images is genuinely slow

## Worker verification was incomplete

The worker (a0298869dc4dad845) verified with a scoped Guestbook run on a
newly-created isolated VM (lima-node-a0298869). But that VM was probably not
starting from a truly-cold state OR the worker's specific network condition
happened to complete pulls fast enough. On the operator's machine now,
--reset runs fail consistently.

## Fix options

A. Move pre-pull OUT of the Lima provisioning probe and into
   scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh AFTER Lima has come up. Failures become
   script warnings, not VM lifecycle failures. Provision succeeds; if some
   images aren't cached, tests still run and possibly fail (same as before
   PR #980).

B. Pre-pull only during the run's setup phase (scripts/conformance/06-run-
   sonobuoy.sh or a new step in run-all.sh), not at VM provision at all.
   Adds ~1-2 min to run time but doesn't couple to VM lifecycle.

C. Revert PR #980 entirely and go back to relying on kubelet's per-test
   pulls (unblocks operator; doesn't solve mayor-n4c6b).

## Immediate action

Ship revert (Option C) NOW to unblock the operator's --reset workflow.
Follow-up PR does Option A or B properly with real cold-start verification.
close_reason: Revert shipped as PR #981 (merged 2026-08-03). lima/kubelet.yaml restored to pre-#980 state. VM provisioning now completes normally. Original goal (avoid runtime image-pull SYN-drops from usernet) remains open — tracked in mayor-5fkx5's ready-queue status for the correct implementation (Options 2a/3a/4a from mayor's analysis).

title: replace_namespace (PUT /api/v1/namespaces/{name}) never strips/restores .status
description:
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/namespaces.rs:338-392 (replace_namespace, the bespoke PUT handler for /api/v1/namespaces/{name}) never fetches the stored object and never strips or restores `.status`. Whatever `status` (e.g. `status.phase`) the client PUT body carries is written verbatim via `state.store.put(...)`.

This is the same class of bug fixed for Pod in mayor-mlyfr (replace_pod). Namespace has a real status subresource (has_status_subresource=true per patch_namespace at namespaces.rs:409) with a dedicated /status endpoint, but the main PUT handler does not protect it — a plain `kubectl replace`/client-go `Update()` on a Namespace (e.g. any controller/test helper doing a metadata-only update) can silently reset `status.phase` from Terminating back to Active or vice versa, or clobber status.conditions.

Spotted while implementing mayor-mlyfr; not fixed there per scope (surgical, pods.rs only). Fix should mirror the same strip-on-decode/restore-after-write pattern used in resource.rs:1958-1964/2162-2173 and now replace_pod, plus a regression test analogous to put_pod_ignores_body_status_uses_stored_status but for Namespace.
close_reason: PR #986 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/986

title: replace_pod (PUT /pods/{name}) never strips/restores .status — silently clobbers observedGeneration and other status fields
description:
## Root cause (verified via mayor-82wpg re-investigation, see
ai/findings/pod-put-status-clobber-2026-08-03.md, worker/agent-aa8e9a6ae4ebc7f81)

crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:651-758 (`replace_pod`, wired to
`PUT /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}` at crates/apiserver/src/lib.rs:543)
is Pod's own bespoke PUT handler — NOT routed through the generic
`replace_namespaced_resource` in resource.rs. It restores
`metadata.generation` (line 692-693) and
`metadata.deletionTimestamp`/`deletionGracePeriodSeconds` (line 701-709)
from the stored object before writing, but never strips the client-sent
`.status` nor restores the server's current stored `.status`. Whatever
`status` the client's local (possibly stale) object carries gets written
verbatim via `state.store.put(...)` at line 749-753.

This is the exact protection that:
- the generic `replace_namespaced_resource` implements for every other
  status-subresource resource (resource.rs:1958-1964 strip on decode,
  resource.rs:2162-2173 restore after webhooks), with a regression test
  (`put_statefulset_ignores_body_status_uses_stored_status`,
  resource.rs:13973-14064), and
- ANOTHER Pod-specific handler in the same file already implements
  correctly (pods.rs:1049,1064: `current_obj.body["status"] = stored_status;`).

## Verified failure trace (0802-2344-conformance run)

Pod pod-generation-03ea861d-c578-49a2-b781-87a979686849, ns pods-2545:
- 23:21:07.890 apiserver: kubelet's status PATCH lands with top-level
  `"observedGeneration":5` (confirmed in raw patch body, kubelet.log).
- 23:21:10.516 apiserver (request_id=28f8dc9c, method=PUT, status=200,
  latency_ms=15): e2e test's annotations-only `podClient.Update()` PUT
  to the main /pods/{name} endpoint commits successfully (store CAS
  confirms this was NOT a stale/conflicting write — legitimate commit,
  corrupt content).
- All subsequent GETs (23:21:11 through the reported 25.138s timeout)
  return `pod.Status.ObservedGeneration == 0`
  (test/e2e/framework/pod/wait.go:335 checks the top-level scalar, not
  status.conditions[].observedGeneration).
- Post-failure pod dump confirms status.conditions[].observedGeneration
  is still correctly 5 for every condition — ONLY the top-level scalar
  field was lost, consistent with the whole `.status` object being
  overwritten by a stale/zero client copy rather than restored from the
  store.

## Blast radius

Any client doing a plain `kubectl replace` / client-go `Update()` (not
`UpdateStatus()`) on a Pod for a spec-only or metadata-only change (many
e2e test helpers and some controllers do this) can silently reset
pod.status — observedGeneration, conditions, podIP, phase, hostIP,
qosClass, etc. — to whatever stale copy the client held. Broader than the
observedGeneration symptom alone.

## Fix scope

Mirror the strip-on-decode + restore-after-webhooks pattern from
resource.rs:1958-1964 / 2162-2173 into replace_pod
(crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:651-758):
1. Strip `obj.body["status"]` from the incoming PUT body right after
   decode (or simply never read it).
2. After admission webhooks + generation increment, restore
   `obj.body["status"] = stored_obj.body["status"].clone()` (stored_obj
   is already fetched at line 684 for spec_before/generation — no extra
   read needed).

Regression test: mirror
`put_statefulset_ignores_body_status_uses_stored_status`
(resource.rs:13973-14064) but for `replace_pod`, asserting
`status.observedGeneration` (and ideally another field like `podIP`)
survive a plain metadata-only PUT with a stale/zeroed `status` in the
request body. Must fail if the fix is reverted (Rule 14).

## NOT in scope for this bead

- mayor-i9d54 (`gen_pod_status_to_json` drops observedGeneration on
  protobuf status decode) is a separate, narrower gap in the /status
  subresource protobuf-PUT decode path; confirmed unrelated to this bug
  (this bug is in the *main* resource PUT handler, and status decoded
  from the client body is discarded here regardless of what it contains
  once the fix above lands).
- The "executable file 'pause' not found" CrashLoopBackOff seen in the
  same failing test run is expected upstream test behavior (agnhost's
  NewAgnhostContainer defaults Args=["pause"], test only swaps .Image to
  nginx, nginx has no "pause" binary) — not a u7s bug, no action needed.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/979 (branch worker/agent-af29a3aa80b021dd6). Fix + regression test (replace_pod_ignores_body_status_uses_stored_status) verified fail-on-revert. Local Guestbook conformance run: Ran 1 of 7579 Specs SUCCESS. cargo test/clippy clean. Do not close — mayor closes after merge. Sibling bug found in replace_namespace (namespaces.rs), filed as mayor-r3z74, not fixed here.
close_reason: Shipped as PR #979 (merged 2026-08-03). replace_pod now preserves .status via the strip/restore pattern matching resource.rs:1958-1964+2162-2173 and pods.rs:1049,1064. Regression test replace_pod_ignores_body_status_uses_stored_status added, fail-on-revert verified per Rule 14. Sibling bug found in replace_namespace filed as mayor-r3z74 (P1).

title: Bump RING_CAPACITY + design per-resource-type ring sharding (staged A→B, per mayor-itre2 scoping)
description:
Implement the staged fix recommended by the Shape 3 scoping audit for mayor-itre2
(watch-history ring buffer premature-410 bug). Findings doc:
ai/findings/watch-ring-redesign-scoping-2026-08-03.md (worktree agent-a99959602427c3b62).

Stage 1 (ship first, small/low-risk):
- Bump crates/store/src/sqlite.rs RING_CAPACITY from 1000 to a value derived from the
  observed 16-way conformance burst rate (~36 events/sec cluster-wide) with a wide safety
  margin (e.g. 100,000 gives ~46 min retention). Consider also bounding eviction by
  wall-clock age in addition to count.
- Verified: no existing test scales real store.put() I/O by RING_CAPACITY (the two
  DELETION_LOG_CAP-scaled tests use the cheap in-memory push_event() helper), so this bump
  should not blow up test-suite runtime.
- Add/update a test documenting the derivation of the new capacity value.

Stage 2 (structural fix, do after Stage 1 ships):
- Shard the ring/compaction_horizon/deletion_log by resource-type root prefix (the same
  string as crates/apiserver/src/keys.rs::group_list_prefix(group, plural, None)) instead of
  one global ring, so a busy resource type's write volume cannot evict an unrelated, slow-
  moving resource type's watch history.
- Requires threading a resource-type-prefix argument through Store::put/delete/
  create_if_namespace_active/delete_namespace_resources (trait in crates/store/src/lib.rs,
  impl in crates/store/src/sqlite.rs, ~48 call sites in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/*.rs,
  plus ~10 test fault-injection mock Store impls that need the same signature update).
  watch()'s own prefix argument needs no change — a namespace-scoped watch prefix is already
  a sub-prefix of its resource-type root, so it only ever scans one shard.
- Must preserve the lock-ordering invariant documented on push_event_locked (broadcast order
  must match revision-assignment order under the write_conn mutex) per-shard. The global
  bookmark mechanism (key == "") is shard-independent already and needs no change.

Do NOT implement Option C (persistent sqlite-backed watch history) — deferred per the
scoping doc's recommendation; it has no current consumer at u7s's single-process deployment
shape and adds write-path I/O under the already-contended write_conn mutex.
notes: Stage 1 shipped: PR #978 bumps RING_CAPACITY 1000 -> 100_000 with WHY comment + regression tests (ring_capacity_retains_far_more_than_the_old_1000_entry_window fails on revert to 1000; ring_buffer_caps_at_ring_capacity_and_advances_horizon_on_evict verifies cap+horizon mechanism). Guestbook conformance scoped run green (Ran 1 of 7579 Specs SUCCESS). Stage 2 (per-resource-type ring sharding) remains open -- do not close this bead until Stage 2 merges too.
close_reason: Stage 1 shipped as PR #978 (merged 2026-08-03). RING_CAPACITY: 1000 → 100_000, ~46 min retention at observed 16-way conformance write rate. Regression test ring_capacity_retains_far_more_than_the_old_1000_entry_window fails-on-revert verified per Rule 14. Stage 2 (per-resource-type sharding, ~300-500 LoC) NOT implemented — file follow-up bead if/when Stage 1 proves insufficient. Ring is still global; a busy resource can still evict a quiet one but with 100× headroom.

title: fix(scheduler): in_flight dedup releases pending pod before its deferred preemption bind resolves, letting it be double-scheduled
description:
## Summary

u7s-scheduler's `in_flight` dedup set (crates/scheduler/src/main.rs) releases a
pod's key as soon as `preempt_and_pick_node` returns `Ok(())` — i.e. the moment
victims have been evicted — even though the actual bind for that pod is
DEFERRED until `NodeTally::apply_event`'s DELETED-branch hook confirms the
victim is physically gone (see `PreemptionWaiters`). Because the key is
already gone from `in_flight`, a second, fully independent scheduling attempt
for the SAME still-unscheduled pod (spec.nodeName still empty; the pod is only
distinguishable by a nominatedNodeName set by the first attempt) can start
before the first attempt's deferred bind ever completes. That second attempt
runs its own `pick_node`/`find_preemption_plan` cycle, typically lands on a
DIFFERENT node (since the first attempt's chosen node's in-memory tally hasn't
freed up yet from this second attempt's point of view, or simply because
node-candidate order differs), evicts an INNOCENT bystander pod that should
never have been touched, and eventually double-binds the same pod to two
different nodes once both deferred binds resolve.

This produces exactly the "Pod ... not found" failures in
`k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/scheduling/preemption.go` at lines 206 and 304 —
NOT because of a hard-delete/grace-period bug (that was already fixed via
mayor-u0dpc/mayor-krae9/mayor-i4mwr/mayor-kn79c, 2026-07-30/31), but because
the test's OWN survivor-pod loop (`for i := 1; i < len(pods); i++ { ... Get
... ExpectNoError ... DeletionTimestamp must be nil }`) observes a pod that
was wrongly, extraneously preempted by the scheduler's SECOND, spurious
preemption plan.

## Evidence (run 0802-1400-conformance, host-logs/scheduler.log + kubelet-lima-node-3.log)

Two "unscheduled pod detected" events for the SAME key
(`sched-preemption-7359/preemptor-pod`), 900ms apart, each independently
running preemption on a DIFFERENT node:

```
13:52:01.770736  unscheduled pod detected: sched-preemption-7359/preemptor-pod
13:52:01.774153  pick_node: no node had capacity pod=preemptor-pod candidates=2
13:52:01.776235  preempting 1 pod(s) on lima-node to schedule higher-priority pod sched-preemption-7359/preemptor-pod
13:52:01.778741  skipping duplicate scheduling request for sched-preemption-7359/preemptor-pod   <- in_flight already cleared, this is a LATER redundant watch tick being correctly deduped, not the race itself
13:52:02.670627  unscheduled pod detected: sched-preemption-7359/preemptor-pod    <- SECOND independent attempt, in_flight had already been cleared after the FIRST attempt's preempt_and_pick_node returned Ok(())
13:52:02.672057  pick_node: no node had capacity pod=preemptor-pod candidates=2
13:52:02.673294  preempting 1 pod(s) on lima-node-3 to schedule higher-priority pod sched-preemption-7359/preemptor-pod   <- evicts pod1-1-sched-preemption-medium-priority, a pod the test never expected to be touched
13:52:02.690410  deferred bind for sched-preemption-7359/preemptor-pod: victim confirmed gone — attempting bind to lima-node
13:52:02.692973  bound pod sched-preemption-7359/preemptor-pod -> node lima-node
13:52:02.889689  deferred bind for sched-preemption-7359/preemptor-pod: victim confirmed gone — attempting bind to lima-node-3
13:52:02.891661  bound pod sched-preemption-7359/preemptor-pod -> node lima-node-3    <- SAME pod bound TWICE, to two different nodes
```

kubelet-lima-node-3.log confirms `pod1-1-sched-preemption-medium-priority`
(one of the pods the test's survivor loop expects to remain untouched) was
genuinely, gracefully evicted with its own `spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds
= 1` (upstream's `initPausePod` sets this explicitly — this part of the
graceful-delete path is correct and NOT the bug):

```
13:52:02.714551  "Pod terminating with grace period" pod=.../pod1-1-... gracePeriod=1
13:52:02.714579  "Killing container with a grace period override" gracePeriod=1
13:52:03.271255  "Pod fully terminated and removed from etcd" pod=.../pod1-1-...
```

e2e.test's own follow-up Get on `pod1-1-...` at 13:52:03.826788 legitimately
gets 404 (the pod really is gone by then, per its own 1s grace period) —
the test failure is correct given the pod state; the BUG is that this pod was
ever selected as a victim at all.

The second failing test (`validates lower priority pod preemption by critical
pod`, preemption.go:304) shows the identical pattern at 13:56:30–13:56:34 for
`sched-preemption-4353/preemptor-pod` (also 2 nodes, also a spurious second
victim: `pod0-1-sched-preemption-medium-priority`).

## Code location

`crates/scheduler/src/main.rs`, `handle_pod_event` (~line 363-622):

```rust
Ok(()) => {
    // Victims evicted; the bind itself is deferred
    // until `apply_event`'s DELETED-branch hook
    // confirms they're actually gone ...
    // Nothing to report yet — no Scheduled/FailedScheduling event, `key`
    // stays out of `in_flight` below exactly as it
    // would on any other "wait for the next tick"
    // outcome.
    return None;
}
```
...
```rust
// Always remove the key, whether binding succeeded, failed, or was skipped.
in_flight_clone
    .lock()
    .expect("in_flight lock poisoned")
    .remove(&key);
```

The doc comment's reasoning ("stays out of in_flight ... exactly as it would
on any other wait-for-next-tick outcome") does not hold for this specific
outcome: unlike the transient-GET-failure retry case (where NOTHING has
happened yet and re-scheduling is genuinely safe), `Ok(())` here means a real,
state-changing side effect (victim eviction) has already started and a
deferred-bind waiter has already been registered in `NodeTally`
(`register_preemption_waiter`). Releasing `in_flight` at this point makes the
pod look "not currently being scheduled" to the dedup check even though a
whole preemption+bind sequence is still in flight for it.

`attempt_deferred_bind` (main.rs ~line 262) is never passed `in_flight` at
all, so there is no mechanism to keep the key reserved until the deferred bind
actually resolves (bind success, bind failure, or plan abandonment via
`NodeTally`'s waiter-drop path).

## Suggested fix shape (not attempted here — needs careful design + guardrail tests, same class of work as mayor-krae9/mayor-kn79c)

Keep `key` in `in_flight` across the `Ok(())` / deferred-bind branch instead
of releasing it immediately. Thread `in_flight` (or just the single `key`)
into `attempt_deferred_bind` (and into whatever path abandons a plan, e.g. a
reconnect that drops `PreemptionWaiters` — see that struct's doc comment) so
the key is only removed once the deferred bind truly resolves one way or the
other. Needs a guardrail test analogous to mayor-kn79c's: a pod with an
in-flight deferred bind must never pass the `in_flight` dedup check for a
second, concurrent scheduling attempt.

## Related / prior context

- mayor-h61va (closed 2026-07-31 as "unreproducible environmental flake") is
  almost certainly THIS exact bug, hit under different timing. Its notes
  already named "cross-node critical-pod preemption" and the deferred-bind
  chain as the "LIKELY MECHANISM" but two scout re-runs at lower load could
  not reproduce it. This bead's evidence (0802-1400-conformance, HTTP/2-era
  higher-throughput run) is the first concrete repro with full log evidence
  pinpointing the exact race window (900ms between two "unscheduled pod
  detected" events for the same key).
- mayor-krae9/mayor-i4mwr/mayor-kn79c hardened the VICTIM side of concurrent
  preemption (double-targeting the same victim, fast-path/slow-path
  divergence). This bug is the mirror-image gap on the PENDING/preemptor pod
  side: the same pod being independently re-scheduled while its own deferred
  bind is still outstanding.
- mayor-zl9ku (this bead was discovered investigating that one) hypothesized
  a hard-delete/grace-period bug in `delete_pod`. That mechanism was already
  fixed 2026-07-30 (mayor-u0dpc, PR #954) and is confirmed correct by direct
  log evidence in this same run (`gracePeriod=1` honored exactly per the
  victim's own spec, single graceful DELETE, real kubelet-driven hard-delete
  only after actual container termination). mayor-zl9ku's cited test failures
  are actually caused by THIS bug, not a grace-period bug.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/977 (not merged yet — mayor to review/merge and close).
close_reason: Shipped as PR #977 (merged 2026-08-03). Fix: introduced SchedulingOutcome::{Deferred, Skipped, Done} in handle_pod_event so only Deferred skips the in_flight release. attempt_deferred_bind now takes in_flight and releases the key on every exit path — sole releaser for a deferred plan. Second bug discovered and fixed in the same PR (Rule 8 read-before-write): NodeTally::clear / PreemptionWaiters::clear now return abandoned plans' pod keys so main.rs releases in_flight on watch reconnect — without this, holding in_flight across deferred bind would create stuck-forever pods. Two regression tests, both fail-on-revert verified per Rule 14. Scoped Guestbook conformance passed. Expected effect: [sig-scheduling] SchedulerPreemption tests (which failed in run 0802-1400 via double-scheduling → innocent bystander eviction) should now pass.

title: [Conformance] regressed to 10 failures after HTTP/2 (#975) — 5x '300s timeout' cluster in 15s, apiserver traffic 3-4x baseline
description:
First 16-way [Conformance] run after PR #975 (HTTP/2 landed): 436 pass / 10 fail.
Prior runs 445-479 pass / 1-5 fail. Regression is real.

## Failure breakdown

**5x "Timed out after 300s" (all pod-Ready-waits, all within 15s window
13:39:23-38 UTC, across 5 unrelated test suites):**
  - lifecycle_hook.go:140
  - configmap_volume.go:220
  - namespace.go:530
  - downwardapi (pod-secrets)
  - output.go:263 (twice)
  - output.go:281
These are all waiting for their own pod to become Ready. All timed out
simultaneously = ONE systemic event, not 5 separate bugs.

**2x container-probe restart-count wrong** (same class as prior runs;
now amplified: one expected 0 got 2 -- previously we saw 0->1)

**2x preemption "Pod not found"** (new class, scheduler race)

**1x VIP i/o timeout** (was 1-3 in prior runs; HTTP/2 dropped this to
essentially just 1)

## Cross-signal (verified)
- apiserver.log: 678 MB (vs ~94 MB prior comparable run, i.e. 7x volume)
- Per-minute peak: 726k lines at 13:34 = ~12k req/sec sustained
- 4x status=5xx and 2x status=429 (all in the AdmissionWebhook family --
  those tests configure webhooks that call BACK into apiserver, hit their
  own timeouts under the new load)
- 1x InflightLayer 429 (Wave 2 caps holding)
- Server-side latency at the failure moment: single-digit ms per request
- Apiserver process itself is healthy and fast

## Working theory (unverified)

HTTP/2 removed HTTP/1.1's accidental request-rate throttle. Every client
(kubelet, KCM, scheduler) can now stream requests at wire speed over
multiplexed connections. Apiserver serves each request in single-digit ms,
so individual requests are fine. BUT the resulting load stretches:
  - Pod-startup latency (scheduler → apiserver → kubelet → CRI-O chain)
  - Watch reconcile times
  - Controller reconcile loop cadence

Which turns "300-second pod-Ready wait" tests into simultaneous failures.

Likely next-tier bottleneck candidates:
  1. mayor-itre2 (RING_CAPACITY=1000 watch ring) -- 3-4x more writes/sec
     means faster ring cycling, more 410s, more watch retries
  2. Controllers/scheduler overwhelmed by high pod-churn
  3. Kubelet resource exhaustion on the VM (CPU/memory contention with
     all the new activity)

Investigation needed:
  - Correlate pods that timed out at 13:39:23-38 against their entire
    lifecycle in apiserver.log + scheduler.log + kubelet.log
  - Check for 410s in the same window (mayor-itre2 signal)
  - Check kubelet's own CPU/memory during the peak
  - Compare AdmissionWebhook 5xx pattern against prior runs -- may be

The reaped namespace was reaped ~10 min AFTER the 5-fail cluster at 13:39:23-38Z, so it's unrelated. That means the 5-simultaneous-timeout cluster is NOT namespace-teardown-related. Namespace GC is working normally in this run. Working theory revised: the 5 pods were healthy from the apiserver's perspective (kubelet was PATCHing their status at 13:34-13:39 UTC repeatedly with 0-13ms latency) but did NOT become Ready within the test's 300s. Something in the pod-startup path (kubelet → CRI-O → CNI → container-start → probe) is stretched, but the apiserver is not the bottleneck. Look at kubelet.log + crio.log for the 5 specific pods around the 13:34-13:39 window. Pod IDs: downwardapi-volume-c756b823, pod-d8703e25, pod-secrets-656f4e5d, plus the lifecycle/configmap/namespace tests' pods (need to extract from e2e.txt bodies).

Root cause #1 (7-8/10 failures, the 300s-timeout cluster + both container-probe restart-count failures): kubelet's upstream-default --serialize-image-pulls=true single-worker queue got hit with a ~260-request burst in 70s (13:33:25-13:34:35) that HTTP/2 (#975) no longer paces; queue took ~5min to drain, straddling the tests' 300s timeout (confirmed via crio.log: RunPodSandboxRequest to CreateContainerRequest gap was ~5m00s-5m05s for 3 traced pods, CRI-O itself served each request in <20ms once received). Not a u7s bug -- infra/config tuning gap, follow-on mayor-w98yt. Root cause #2 (2/10, SchedulerPreemption 'Pod not found'): u7s-scheduler's preemption path hard-deletes the victim pod (scheduler.log: delete_pod DELETE completed -> 404 on e2e's Get ~1.1s later) instead of a graceful delete -- genuine scheduler bug, unrelated to HTTP/2 load, follow-on mayor-zl9ku. Theories A (kubelet OOM/pressure - partial: coredns OOMKilled at 13:39:17Z but no node pressure conditions, ruled out as primary), B (410/watch-ring amplification - ruled out, only 125 410s over 18min, no spike at 13:39), C (CRI-O choking - ruled out, CRI-O fast once it received requests) all addressed with evidence in the doc. title: Enable HTTP/2 (ALPN h2) support in apiserver TLS listener to reduce kubelet watch-reconnect SYN bursts
description:
Follow-on to mayor-mjt51's usernet-mitigation audit (findings:
ai/findings/usernet-mitigation-audit-2026-08-02.md, worker worktree
agent-a16f32c3c371fb6b8, not committed -- ai/findings/* is gitignored).

The apiserver never negotiates HTTP/2 today:
- crates/apiserver/Cargo.toml: `hyper = { version = "1", features =
  ["http1"] }` -- the http2 cargo feature is not enabled.
- crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs `generate_tls()`: the rustls ServerConfig
  never sets `.alpn_protocols` -- server sends no ALPN extension.
- crates/apiserver/src/lib.rs `serve_tls()` (~line 3573): hardcodes
  `hyper::server::conn::http1::Builder::new().serve_connection(io,
  service).with_upgrades()` -- HTTP/1.1 only, by construction.
- `git log --all -S 'http2' -- crates/apiserver/**/*.rs
  crates/apiserver/Cargo.toml` -> zero commits; never attempted before.

Because HTTP/1.1 cannot multiplex concurrent requests on one TCP
connection, every kubelet watch reflector opens its own dedicated TCP
connection. mayor-biy31's live pcap capture caught ~150-200 of these
reconnecting together within under 1 second after a synchronized ginkgo
teardown, producing a SYN burst that (by elimination across every other
instrumented layer) overwhelms some capacity limit inside the shared
`limactl usernet` process, causing a ~20s mass SYN-blackhole event.

Kubelet's client-go stack does NOT need any config change: Go's
net/http.Transport auto-negotiates HTTP/2 via ALPN by default (confirmed:
no DISABLE_HTTP2/GODEBUG=http2client=0 set anywhere in
scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh's kubelet systemd drop-in). If the
server offered h2, client-go would multiplex many concurrent watch
streams from the same kubelet process over a small pool of shared HTTP/2
connections instead of one-TCP-connection-per-watch, collapsing the SYN
burst regardless of usernet's actual internal limit.

## Scope
- Add hyper's `http2` cargo feature (crates/apiserver/Cargo.toml).
- Set `alpn_protocols = vec![b"h2".to_vec(), b"http/1.1".to_vec()]` on the
  rustls ServerConfig in generate_tls() (crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs).
- Replace `hyper::server::conn::http1::Builder` in serve_tls()
  (crates/apiserver/src/lib.rs) with `hyper_util::server::conn::auto::Builder`,
  which dispatches h1 vs h2 per-connection based on the negotiated ALPN
  protocol.

## Regression risk -- must be covered by tests, not assumed safe
- exec/attach/portforward use HTTP/1.1 `Connection: Upgrade` (websocket).
  The existing `.with_upgrades()` comment in serve_tls() documents that
  this path is fragile ("Without it, hyper sends the 101 Switching
  Protocols response but never hands the connection off... kubectl times
  out with 'unexpected output from server'"). HTTP/2 does not support the
  same Upgrade mechanism (would need RFC 8441 Extended CONNECT, which
  hyper_util::server::conn::auto's HTTP/2 path may not support out of the
  box) -- verify these clients still negotiate http/1.1 via ALPN (most
  exec/attach client libraries prefer h1 for upgrade-based streaming) or
  explicitly confirm/implement Extended CONNECT support before shipping.
- Add a test that opens N concurrent watch connections from a single
  client and asserts they land on a bounded number of underlying TCP
  connections when h2 is negotiated (the actual regression-relevant
  behavior this bead exists to fix).
- Add/keep a test that exec/attach/portforward still complete successfully
  end-to-end (conformance or integration) after this change.

Do NOT ship this as a quick config flip -- it changes the connection-
serving path for every client. Full test coverage of both the
multiplexing win and the upgrade-path regression risk is required before
merge.
notes: PR #975 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/975 — implements HTTP/2 (ALPN h2) support per scope. Local scoped conformance run + ALPN wire verification both passed. Awaiting mayor review/merge.
close_reason: Shipped as PR #975 (merged 2026-08-02). Apiserver now negotiates HTTP/2 via ALPN. Changes: hyper gains http2 feature, hyper-util gains server-auto, tls.rs sets alpn_protocols=[h2, http/1.1], lib.rs replaces both http1::Builder sites with hyper_util::server::conn::auto::Builder::serve_connection_with_upgrades() for per-connection ALPN dispatch. Verified end-to-end: openssl s_client -alpn h2,http/1.1 reports 'ALPN protocol: h2'; ss -tnp on guest shows kubelet holds exactly ONE established TCP connection to apiserver in steady state (multiplexing works live); scoped Guestbook conformance test passed. Regression tests: new http2_alpn_negotiated_and_multiplexes_concurrent_requests_on_one_connection (20 concurrent requests over shared h2 SendRequest with Barrier proves genuine multiplexing, fail-on-revert verified per Rule 14); existing serve_connection_with_upgrades_allows_websocket_handler_to_run updated to use production auto::Builder path. Expected effect on next 16-way [Conformance]: kubelet SYN burst on synchronized reconnect collapses from ~150-200 to a handful, eliminating usernet mass-blackhole trigger.

title: lima-start.sh silently swallows ipset install failure → kube-proxy crashloops → VIP dead; killed run 0802-0742 after 1h
description:
Root-caused 2026-08-02T07:41Z: the conformance run that was started at ~06:46Z
hung for 55 min because the sonobuoy aggregator couldn't reach the apiserver via
the kubernetes Service VIP (10.96.0.1:443). Every request from the aggregator
timed out with 'dial tcp 10.96.0.1:443: i/o timeout'.

Direct root cause:
  - lima-start.sh:636 runs `apt-get install -y ipset` but pipes through
    `2>/dev/null | tail -1 || true` — silently swallows any failure.
  - On this run, the install failed (transient apt / lock / cache issue —
    running the same command manually just now succeeded, so it's timing-
    related at provision time). ipset ended up NOT installed.
  - kube-proxy in IPVS mode requires ipset. It crashlooped immediately with
    "can't use the IPVS proxier: error getting ipset version, error:
    executable file not found in $PATH" (kube-proxy log confirms).
  - IPVS was never programmed, so the kubernetes Service VIP had no backend.
  - Every packet to 10.96.0.1:443 died silently. Sonobuoy aggregator hit
    its 30s dial timeout on every attempt, gave up after ~4 min, then
    'no-exit was specified, sonobuoy is now blocking' and hung indefinitely.

This is the SAME failure family mayor-odt6u audited (VIP i/o timeout), but
this instance is a PERSISTENT infra failure caused by the missing ipset,
not the intermittent race that audit chased. mayor-odt6u's diagnosis was
correct for that class; this instance is a different, deterministic mechanism
that ALSO produces the same observable symptom (SYN gets no response) because
kube-proxy is dead.

Bigger issue this reveals: lima-start.sh has many `|| true` and `2>/dev/null`
suppressions on operations that are actually load-bearing. Any of them could
silently break the run the same way. Worth a follow-up audit.

Fix scope:
  1. Prepend `apt-get update` before `apt-get install -y ipset` (fresh
     Ubuntu often has stale cache).
  2. Remove the `2>/dev/null | tail -1 || true` from the ipset install so
     failure is loud (script exits, run-all fails immediately).
  3. Also install `conntrack` (mayor-biy31 found this missing too — needed
     for network diagnostics AND for the mayor-biy31 instrumentation script
     to work out of the box).
  4. Add post-restart kube-proxy health check: wait up to ~15s, verify
     `systemctl is-active kube-proxy` returns `active` (not `activating` or
     `failed`), fail loud otherwise. Without this check, ANY failure mode
     that puts kube-proxy in crashloop state passes silently.

Also file a follow-up bead: audit lima-start.sh for other `|| true` /
`2>/dev/null` swallows on load-bearing operations.
notes: PR opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/974. Not closing — mayor closes after merge per instructions. Follow-up audit bead filed: mayor-qt39k.
close_reason: Shipped as PR #974 (merged 2026-08-02). scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh now: (1) apt-get update before install, (2) unconditional apt-get install -y ipset conntrack (no more || true error swallow), (3) post-restart kube-proxy health check that polls systemctl is-active up to 15s and dumps journalctl on failure. Verified locally: --reset + --focus 'Guestbook application should create and stop a working application' completed 5m40s end-to-end with Ran 1 of 7579 Specs SUCCESS! Follow-up mayor-qt39k (P2) filed for auditing other silent-swallow patterns in lima-start.sh.

title: apiserver TCP listener has no explicit backlog; host somaxconn=128 may drop SYNs under 16-way conformance load
description:
Audit mayor-odt6u root-caused the VIP i/o-timeout family (see
ai/findings/vip-timeout-rootcause-2026-08-02.md). Strongest surviving
candidate: an accept-queue overflow somewhere between the guest kube-proxy
DNAT/IPVS path, the shared limactl usernet host proxy, and the apiserver's
own TCP listener at crates/apiserver/src/lib.rs:365
(TcpListener::bind(&args.listen).await?) — which sets no explicit backlog.
The live host's kern.ipc.somaxconn=128, a low, silently-clamping ceiling
that applies regardless of what backlog tokio requests.

Evidence: primary repro (0802-0447-conformance, kubectl-1759 @ 04:27:58.731
UTC, dial tcp 10.96.0.1:443: i/o timeout) shows the apiserver's own request
loop had zero gaps >727ms throughout the 30s blackout (6077 requests
completed in the window) — the server process was alive and responsive,
so if this is the mechanism, the drop happens upstream of accept(), most
likely at an OS-level or usernet-level queue capacity limit.

Fix candidates (need to be evaluated, not blindly applied):
- Explicitly raise the listen backlog via socket2 when constructing the
  TcpListener (e.g. listen(1024) explicitly rather than relying on OS
  defaults).
- Document/raise kern.ipc.somaxconn as a conformance-host prerequisite
  (analogous to the existing ulimit -n guidance in scripts/u7s-start.sh).

This is a hypothesis with strong circumstantial support, not a proven
mechanism — mayor-9v0eu (live capture) is the way to get definitive
confirmation of which layer actually drops the SYN. This bead is the
actionable fix path regardless of that outcome, since a wider backlog is
low-risk and directly addresses this candidate class.
close_reason: Shipped as PR #970 (merged 2026-08-02T~05:47Z). Explicit socket2-based bind_listener() with LISTEN_BACKLOG=4096, plus runtime clamp detection via /proc/sys/net/core/somaxconn (Linux) or sysctl -n kern.ipc.somaxconn (Mac) that emits tracing::warn! when OS clamps below the requested value. Regression tests: 3 unit tests for backlog_clamp_warning decision logic + 1 tokio::test for the end-to-end bind path. Defense-in-depth: apiserver is no longer part of the accept-queue overflow question; residual layer (limactl usernet vs guest IPVS/conntrack) tracked in mayor-biy31.

title: VIP 10.96.0.1:443 i/o timeout — kubectl and pod-VIP connections drop SYNs under 16-way conformance load (reproduces across runs)
description:
Reproducible across at least 2 independent 16-way [Conformance] runs, always as 'dial
tcp <IP>:<port>: i/o timeout' (SYN got no response), always to a Service VIP or pod IP,
never to the direct 127.0.0.1:6443 loopback listener.

Instances:
  - temp/e2e/0802-0447-conformance @ 04:27:58.731 UTC:
      kubectl 'get pod pause -L testing-label' in kubectl-1759 --
      'dial tcp 10.96.0.1:443: i/o timeout'.
      kubectl-1759 was doing tolerable ops seconds earlier (delete succeeded at
      04:27:58.731). Single failure in a 445/446-pass run.

  - temp/e2e/0802-0140--conformance (mayor-xz6fg, single-node run):
      webhook-6839 BeforeEach @ 01:25:29 -- 'dial tcp 10.96.0.1:443: i/o timeout'
      labeling namespace.
      dns-424 It -- 'dial tcp 10.96.0.1:443: i/o timeout' creating pod.
      container-probe-2549 liveness -- 'dial tcp 10.85.0.51:8080: i/o timeout'
      (pod IP, not VIP -- but same SYN-drop family).

  - temp/e2e/0802-0329-conformance (mayor-pzgzc failure 3):
      container-probe-4965 liveness -- pod IP dial timeout, similar family.

Cross-signal (not exhausted, worth investigating):
  - Apiserver 127.0.0.1:6443 is a host-listener on the Mac, NEVER shows this pattern
    for direct connections (audit's 137-req/200ms burst had zero connect failures at
    the listener level).
  - The failing connections all go through kube-proxy iptables/nftables (Service VIP)
    or CNI-routed pod IPs -- both are inside the VM.
  - kube-proxy runs on lima-node / lima-node-3 (VM-local).
  - VM has 8 vCPUs and 4GiB RAM; under 16-way parallel ginkgo the VM's kernel is
    under real contention.

Possible mechanisms (mutually non-exclusive):
  1. conntrack table saturation or drop -- 16-way parallel = large connection churn.
  2. kube-proxy iptables/nftables rule reconciliation blocks briefly during ns/pod
     churn, drops in-flight SYNs.
  3. Konnectivity's proxy-server-to-proxy-agent path drops the connection under load
     (konnectivity is how apiserver reaches kubelet inside the VM; but VIP traffic
     doesn't necessarily go through konnectivity -- verify).
  4. Kernel accept queue overflow on kube-proxy-side or apiserver-side.
  5. Apiserver's own event loop briefly stalled (e.g. big write, GC pause, semaphore
     contention around InflightLayer -- 15 fires this run) causing accept()s to lag.

This is real, reproducible, and now blocking [Conformance] from reaching 100% pass.
Not conformance-specific: any workload doing kubectl-through-VIP or pod-to-pod
connections under load will hit this.
notes: Audit complete. Findings: ai/findings/vip-timeout-rootcause-2026-08-02.md. Follow-ons: mayor-oxz6w (bug, apiserver listen backlog / somaxconn=128), mayor-biy31 (task, live conntrack/IPVS/usernet capture), mayor-u2x1u (bug, redundant dual-DNAT for kubernetes VIP).
close_reason: Audit complete (read-only, no code changes/PR per task shape). Root-cause verdict: candidates 3 (konnectivity) and 5 (apiserver event-loop stall) ruled out with hard evidence (architectural code trace + 6077 apiserver requests completing with max 727ms gap through the exact 30s VIP blackout). Candidate 1 (conntrack table-full) has no supporting evidence (nf_conntrack_max=262144, zero 'table full' log lines). Candidate 2 (kube-proxy IPVS reconciliation) is real and constant but not shown to touch the specific kubernetes VIP at the failure moment (its IPVS state was programmed once at 04:19:46 and never touched again). Candidate 4 (accept-queue overflow) is the strongest surviving candidate: apiserver's TcpListener has no explicit backlog, host kern.ipc.somaxconn=128, and all conformance traffic funnels through kube-proxy DNAT + a single shared limactl usernet host process before reaching the apiserver socket -- KCM/scheduler share that exact path but use long-lived watches (no comparable connection-churn burst) and show zero timeouts, explaining the asymmetry. Evidence cannot pinpoint whether the drop is at the Mac kernel socket layer, inside usernet, or a stale conntrack/IPVS entry -- that needs a live capture (mayor-biy31). Also surfaced an unlisted 6th mechanism (shared limactl usernet proxy across all 4 VMs) and a redundant dual-DNAT architecture smell (mayor-u2x1u). Fix bead mayor-oxz6w filed for the actionable backlog-tuning candidate regardless of final live-capture confirmation. Findings: ai/findings/vip-timeout-rootcause-2026-08-02.md (worktree-local, not pushed).

title: Watch-history ring buffer (RING_CAPACITY=1000, global) causes premature 410 Expired under concurrent load, breaking list-then-watch
description:
[sig-apps] StatefulSet "should validate Statefulset Status endpoints" (test/e2e/apps/statefulset.go:1205)
failed in the first --procs=16 conformance run (0802-0329), ns statefulset-3257:

  [FAILED] failed to locate Statefulset ss in namespace statefulset-3257: timed out waiting for the condition

Root cause: crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:9 — `const RING_CAPACITY: usize = 1000;` — is a SINGLE
GLOBAL ring buffer (`ring: Arc<RwLock<VecDeque<Arc<InternalEvent>>>>`, sqlite.rs:37) shared
across every resource type and every namespace in the whole cluster. push_event_locked
(sqlite.rs:159-183) evicts the oldest entry and advances compaction_horizon the moment the
ring exceeds 1000 events — regardless of which resource/namespace generated them. Under
16-way parallel conformance, aggregate cluster-wide write throughput (16 namespaces' pods,
services, configmaps, leases, etc. all writing concurrently) blows through 1000 events in
single-digit seconds.

The test does the standard k8s client pattern: LIST (captures ResourceVersion, here 2183),
do a few mutating calls (~10s of Patch/Get/UpdateStatus-with-retry), then start a watch
FROM that captured resourceVersion via `watchtools.Until(ctx, ssList.ResourceVersion, w, ...)`
(statefulset.go:1122-1181) expecting historical replay back to the UpdateStatus event.

Evidence (e2e.txt lines 495-542, sonobuoy-e2e-job-e4e5cc55264946ee/logs/e2e.txt):

  I0802 03:05:52.191362 statefulset.go:1174 updatedStatus.Conditions: [...StatusUpdate...]
  STEP: watching for the statefulset status to be updated @ 03:05:52.191
  E0802 03:05:52.192715 retrywatcher.go:169 "Watch failed" err="too old resource version: 2183 (current compaction horizon: 2275)"
  E0802 03:05:53.193014 ... horizon: 2306
  E0802 03:05:54.193393 ... horizon: 2394
  ... (continues every ~1s) ...
  E0802 03:06:31.332884 ... horizon: 3679

The compaction horizon moved from 2275 to 3679 (1400+ revisions) in 39 seconds — global
cluster-wide write rate under 16-way load. The watch never recovers: client-go's RetryWatcher
(used internally by watchtools.Until) retries the SAME requested resourceVersion after a
"too old" error rather than re-LISTing, which is a reasonable design against a real etcd
backend (5-minute compaction interval, tens of thousands of retained revisions by default) —
but is fatal against a 1000-event global ring that a 16-way conformance run exhausts in
single-digit seconds. The test polled fruitlessly for the full 10-minute statefulSetTimeout
before framework.ExpectNoError failed it at statefulset.go:1205 (03:15:51.913, per e2e.txt
line 1102/1231).

The 410 response itself is correctly formed per spec — see
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs:730-745 (the from_revision < horizon check) and the
existing test watch_410_error_uses_compaction_horizon_not_last_rv (watch.rs:1822). The bug is
retention CAPACITY, not correctness of the 410 semantics.

Impact: this is not conformance-test-specific. ANY client using the standard list-then-watch
or watch-reconnect pattern (client-go Reflector/Informer resync, kubectl --watch after a
network blip, any controller) will get spurious, effectively-unrecoverable 410s once
aggregate cluster write throughput is high enough to cycle 1000 events faster than the
client's own list-to-watch latency. 16-way parallel conformance is the first workload to
expose this, but the bug is a scalability ceiling on writes/sec, not a conformance-only issue.

Suggested fix directions (needs design, not prescribing the exact number here):
1. Raise RING_CAPACITY substantially and/or make retention time-bounded rather than
   count-bounded (real etcd's default is time-based: 5 min compaction interval).
2. Consider per-resource-type or per-prefix rings instead of one global ring, so one busy
   resource type's write volume doesn't evict slow-moving resources' history.

Filed from mayor-pzgzc (Shape 3 audit, read-only, findings doc:
ai/findings/conformance-16way-first-run-triage-2026-08-02.md).
notes: Shape 3 scoping complete (read-only, no code changes): compared bump-constant (A) vs per-resource-type ring sharding (B) vs sqlite-persistent history (C). Findings doc: ai/findings/watch-ring-redesign-scoping-2026-08-03.md (worktree agent-a99959602427c3b62). Recommendation: staged A now (bump RING_CAPACITY, ~1 file, near-zero risk) then B (per-prefix rings, structural fix for cross-resource-type contamination, ~10-14 files/300-500 LoC). C deferred — no consumer at u7s's current single-process deployment shape, highest risk to watch-protocol invariants. Follow-on implementation bead: mayor-jzlon. Leaving this bead open per task instructions; mayor-jzlon tracks the actual fix.
close_reason: Stage 1 shipped as PR #978 (mayor-jzlon, RING_CAPACITY 1000→100k). Stage 2 (per-resource-type sharding) NOT implemented — file follow-up if 100k proves insufficient under future load patterns.

title: InflightLayer 429s under 16-way parallel conformance load: caps too low, rejections invisible in apiserver.log
description:
Two conformance failures in the first --procs=16 run (0802-0329) trace to
crates/apiserver/src/inflight.rs's InflightLayer:

  const MAX_INFLIGHT: usize = 50;   // total concurrent requests, whole apiserver
  const MAX_MUTATING: usize = 20;   // concurrent POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, whole apiserver

Both constants are GLOBAL across the entire apiserver (crates/apiserver/src/inflight.rs:24-25),
sized when conformance ran serially (introduced in #52, before the 16-way default shipped in
PR #966). Under 16-way parallel ginkgo, 16 independent test namespaces' setup/teardown bursts,
plus kube-controller-manager, kubelet, and scheduler background traffic, transiently exceed
these caps.

Evidence (temp/e2e/0802-0329-conformance, temp/u7s/apiserver.log — both in mayor checkout):

- Failure 1: [sig-apps] StatefulSet BeforeEach (test/e2e/apps/statefulset.go:130), ns
  statefulset-3215. e2e.txt line 28-40: POST /services returns
  `{code: 429, reason: TooManyRequests, message: "Too many requests"}` at 03:04:07.403 —
  this exact JSON shape matches inflight.rs:76-93's too_many_requests_response() body.
  apiserver.log shows 137 completed requests logged within the 200ms window
  [03:04:07.300, 03:04:07.499] (`rg -c '^2026-08-02T03:04:07\.[3-4].*INFO
  u7s_apiserver::content_type: request' temp/u7s/apiserver.log` = 137) — consistent with
  transient inflight-limit exhaustion at 16-way concurrency.

- Failure 2: [sig-api-machinery] MutatingAdmissionPolicy DeferCleanup
  (test/e2e/framework/framework.go:506), ns mutating-admission-policy-6217. e2e.txt line 227:
  DELETE ns returns the same 429/TooManyRequests shape at 03:09:42.718. At that exact moment
  apiserver.log shows a burst of ~25 concurrent marker-deployment pod DELETEs from kubelet +
  kube-controller-manager's garbage-collector within a ~250ms window (grep 'method=DELETE.*
  mutating-admission-policy-6217' temp/u7s/apiserver.log, lines 301807-308406) — a textbook
  MAX_MUTATING=20 trip.

CRITICAL COMPOUNDING BUG: apiserver.log's own `status=429` grep only shows 2 total 429s in
the whole ~18min run (both from an unrelated, EXPECTED source: DisruptionController PDB-blocked
evictions at 03:07:56 and 03:08:00, which correctly return 429 by design). Neither failure's
429 appears in apiserver.log's request-completion log at all. Root cause: lib.rs:348-362 wires
InflightLayer OUTSIDE (i.e. runs BEFORE) ContentTypeLayer:

    // Order (outermost first): body_limit → inflight → auth → content_type → handler.
    let app = build_router(state.clone())
        .layer(ContentTypeLayer)
        .layer(AuthLayer::new(...))
        .layer(InflightLayer::new())          // <-- rejects here, before ContentTypeLayer logs
        .layer(axum::extract::DefaultBodyLimit::max(MAX_BODY_BYTES));

InflightLayer's too_many_requests_response() (inflight.rs:76-93) also never calls
`tracing::` at all — the rejection is completely silent. This makes InflightLayer 429s
undiagnosable from apiserver.log in production or CI without correlating against the e2e
client's own error text, as we had to do here.

Fix should address both:
1. Raise MAX_INFLIGHT / MAX_MUTATING (or make them a function of expected concurrent client
   count) so 16-way parallel conformance doesn't trip the same static budget tuned for serial
   testing.
2. Add a `tracing::warn!` (or metrics counter) in too_many_requests_response() (or its call

(both 429s: StatefulSet BeforeEach POST /services, MutatingAdmissionPolicy DeferCleanup DELETE

title: sonobuoy --e2e-parallel=true does NOT propagate E2E_PARALLEL into the plugin container; overnight --all-e2e ran with [Serial] specs INCLUDED (correctness hazard) and unknown actual parallelism
description:
Verified by mayor-zdp6z (dry-run reconciliation, 2026-08-02):

- Our sonobuoy invocation at 06-run-sonobuoy.sh:137 passes --e2e-parallel=true.
- Upstream run_e2e.sh (v1.36.0, test/conformance/image/run_e2e.sh lines 60-66):
    case ${E2E_PARALLEL} in
        'y'|'Y'|'true')
            ginkgo_args+=("--p")                    # auto-detect parallel nodes
            E2E_SKIP="\\[Serial\\]|${E2E_SKIP}" ;;   # prepend [Serial] to skip
    esac
- Our overnight --all-e2e run's effective candidate count was 4475 (verified against
  terminal.log's Remaining:4475).
- Dry-run against the SAME conformance:v1.36.0 image:
    * skip=[Disruptive]|[Flaky]|[Slow] (no [Serial])   -> 4475/7579  ← MATCHES
    * skip=[Serial]|[Disruptive]|[Flaky]|[Slow]         -> 3861/7579  ← does NOT match

Therefore E2E_PARALLEL was NOT actually 'true' inside the plugin container during the
overnight run, despite sonobuoy's --e2e-parallel=true flag being passed. Two independent
consequences:

1. **Correctness hazard**: [Serial] specs (which assume sole-cluster access, no
   concurrent test load) were included in a nominally-parallel run. Their failures
   under load are spurious, and their presence contaminates any per-spec-cost measure.

2. **Unknown actual parallelism**: if E2E_PARALLEL=true didn't reach the case statement,
   the ginkgo command line probably also didn't get --p — meaning our actual runtime
   parallelism is not 8-way as mayor-uixpn assumed, but some unknown value (possibly 1).

Investigation needed:
- Trace what sonobuoy's --e2e-parallel=true actually does inside the e2e plugin container
  (env var? command-line arg? maybe it maps to something OTHER than E2E_PARALLEL in the
  plugin's runtime env). Verify by inspecting the running e2e-job container's env +
  ginkgo process args.
- Determine whether stock sonobuoy 0.57.3's --e2e-parallel flag is even correctly wired
  to E2E_PARALLEL, or if it's been renamed/deprecated in the sonobuoy binary but not
  our script.
- Fix: whatever the correct mechanism is, wire it up so E2E_PARALLEL=true reaches the
  plugin container. Regression test: dry-run the resulting sonobuoy invocation and
  confirm the effective candidate count matches the [Serial]-excluded number (3861 for
  --all-e2e; a different number for other focus regexes).

Note: the in-flight parallelism experiment (mayor-xz6fg, worker aaffefc66bd493ee9) was
told to add a verification step for actual runtime parallelism before running its 16-way
experiment. Its findings may inform this bug.

Downstream: if fixing this raises actual parallelism from 1->8, ALL the per-spec-cost
math in mayor-uixpn's findings needs revisiting.
notes: Verified 2026-08-02 (post-mayor-xz6fg): --e2e-parallel=true has been in 06-run-sonobuoy.sh since commit 6bdd8e0d (2026-05-27, 'feat(test): try running in parallel') but archived 07-30 and 07-31 [Conformance] runs (temp/e2e/0730-1446, 0731-0640) show only 'Ginkgo node 1' (no node 2+), no --p/--nodes/--procs flags anywhere in e2e.txt, and 6297s / 6442s wall-clock (~14.1 s/spec, consistent with serial). Our [Conformance] merge gate has been silently running SERIAL for 2+ months. Root cause: --e2e-parallel=true's hidden-flag path in sonobuoy 0.57.3 sets E2E_PARALLEL=true env, which go-runner (compiled Go binary that replaced the deprecated bash run_e2e.sh in the plugin image) reads and maps to ginkgo's --p auto-detect — but on our VMs the auto-detect apparently resolves to 1 rather than the expected 7 (unclear why: possible container cgroup CPU-count issue, or go-runner's --p path silently no-ops, or some other path failure). Working workaround per mayor-xz6fg: --plugin-env=e2e.E2E_EXTRA_GINKGO_ARGS=--procs=N passes explicit numeric parallelism, verified reaching ginkgo via crictl inspect + /proc/*/cmdline. Fix options: (a) investigate why auto-detect resolves to 1 (would give free future upgrades), or (b) switch to explicit --procs=N in default script (safer, no magic). Downstream: this bug invalidates the perf baseline in mayor-uixpn's arithmetic (its 88s/spec/lane 'at 8-way' was actually 14s/spec/lane at 1-way).
close_reason: Workaround exists and shipped: PR #966 uses --plugin-env=e2e.E2E_EXTRA_GINKGO_ARGS=--procs=16 to bypass the silent no-op path. Actual --e2e-parallel=true propagation bug in sonobuoy/go-runner is not root-caused but no longer blocking anything since the workaround is the default configuration. Reopen only if the workaround ever becomes insufficient.

title: namespace delete: TOCTOU race lets stuck-namespace completion trigger fire before deletionTimestamp is stamped, orphaning Terminating namespaces forever
description:
Live evidence (2026-08-01 audit, mayor-ie8n3): namespace job-8968 has sat in
status.phase=Terminating for 7+ hours with spec.finalizers=[] and zero remaining
objects carrying metadata.finalizers (only a finalizer-less default ServiceAccount
and 2 stale Events remain) — i.e. its own completion condition is currently TRUE,
but nothing will ever re-check it.

Root cause: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/namespaces.rs delete_namespace (line 968)
takes the "no spec.finalizers" branch when the ns itself has no finalizers, and calls
cascade_delete_namespace_resources_until_stable (line 826). If that cascade finds a
contained object (e.g. a Job-owned pod) with metadata.finalizers still set, it
soft-deletes that object and returns CascadeResult::FinalizerPending; ONLY THEN does
delete_namespace's FinalizerPending branch (lines 1056-1078) stamp the NAMESPACE's
own metadata.deletionTimestamp.

Concurrently, the real owning controller (e.g. job-controller) can observe the
object's own deletionTimestamp (stamped by the cascade), PATCH to remove its
finalizer, and hard-delete it via patch_pod's drain-complete path (handlers/pods.rs,
~line 1096), which calls maybe_finalize_terminating_namespace (namespaces.rs:866) to
check whether the namespace can now complete. But maybe_finalize_terminating_namespace
guards on `if ns_meta.deletion_timestamp.is_none() { return; }` (namespaces.rs:881-883)
— and at this point the NAMESPACE's own deletionTimestamp has NOT YET been persisted
by delete_namespace (still in-flight in the same request). The check is a no-op.

By the time delete_namespace finally stamps the namespace's deletionTimestamp, the
blocking object is already gone. maybe_finalize_terminating_namespace is only called
from specific event-triggered call sites (resource.rs:849, pods.rs:745/1096,
cr.rs:1678) — there is no periodic re-check — so a namespace that races this way is
stuck in Terminating permanently even though its completion condition is met.

Confirmed via apiserver.log 2026-08-01T07:37:18.151-.238Z (32ms window): watchdog
PATCH clears spec.finalizers (.151972) -> delete_namespace's cascade soft-deletes
foo-1e005/foo-a76e0 (both had job-controller finalizers) -> job-controller PATCHes
land at .217756 and .227407 (both 200, finalizer removed + pod hard-deleted) -> ns's
own DELETE response completes at .238186, AFTER both pods were already cleared.

Fix direction: stamp the namespace's own deletionTimestamp (and phase=Terminating)
BEFORE running the cascade that discovers per-object finalizers, so any concurrent
completion-trigger sees it's already set and can complete the namespace immediately
once it observes zero remaining finalizer'd objects. Alternatively, re-run the
emptiness check once more directly inside delete_namespace's FinalizerPending branch
after stamping deletionTimestamp, closing the race window without relying on an
external trigger.

Regression test: reproduce the race in a unit/integration test — soft-delete a
namespaced object with a finalizer via cascade, concurrently clear its finalizer via
the normal patch path before the namespace's own deletionTimestamp write lands, and
assert the namespace still completes (does not orphan).

See ai/findings/namespace-force-delete-audit-2026-08-01.md (worker audit doc, not
committed) for full traced evidence.
notes: PR #996 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/996. Implemented fix direction (b) — re-run the emptiness check inside delete_namespace's FinalizerPending branch after stamping deletionTimestamp. Extracted the branch into stamp_terminating_and_recheck_completion() which now calls maybe_finalize_terminating_namespace() right after its own deletionTimestamp write lands, closing the TOCTOU window regardless of which side wins the race. Regression test added (delete_namespace_completes_when_finalizer_cleared_before_own_deletion_timestamp_lands) reproduces the documented interleaving deterministically; confirmed it fails on revert and passes with the fix. Live verification: checked mayor's live running cluster for the job-8968 namespace referenced in the audit (read-only) — no longer present, so no live stuck example remains to compare against; live reproduction of the sub-second race itself was judged impractical (see PR body), regression test used as the documented acceptable substitute.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #996 (merged 2026-08-04). stamp_terminating_and_recheck_completion re-runs maybe_finalize_terminating_namespace immediately after the namespace's own deletionTimestamp write lands, closing the TOCTOU window regardless of which side (namespace's own stamp vs. a controller's finalizer-clear) won the race. Regression test deterministically reproduces the documented interleaving, confirmed to fail on revert. Live reproduction judged impractical (sub-100ms race between concurrent async handlers) -- regression test used as the verification substitute per policy's explicit fallback.

title: Scout: is conformance ginkgo parallelism set high enough for --all-e2e to be feasible in <6h?
description:
Motivating question (operator, 2026-08-01): our overnight --all-e2e run hit
sonobuoy's 6h plugin timeout. Rough math: 450 conformance tests take ~2h ≈
16s/test avg. 4475 total specs × 16s ≈ 20h single-threaded. Even at that pace
6h can't cover the wide focus.

BUT — our VMs run 8 CPU each and e2e tests are heavily I/O-bound, so 8-16x
parallelism should be realistic. If ginkgo is defaulting to serial (-p=1),
we're leaving nearly all of that on the floor. Fixing that could turn a 20h
sweep into 1-2h and change what "6h timeout" even means.

Scout goal (read-only, ~30-60 min budget):

1. Read scripts/conformance/run-all.sh end-to-end. What ginkgo/sonobuoy args
   does it pass today? Is --e2e-parallel or --ginkgo.parallel.total ever set?
   What's ginkgo's default when unset (varies by version)?
2. Read whatever sonobuoy manifest / plugin config we ship. Same questions.
3. Look at upstream k8s CI (kubernetes/test-infra prow configs or
   sig-release job specs) for what --focus=[Conformance] and wider runs
   actually use for parallelism + timeout. Cite exact prow job names +
   parallel counts.
4. Verdict: is our current config expected to finish --all-e2e in any
   reasonable time, or is there a well-known parallelism knob we're missing?

Return: one-page finding with specific file:line for our current config,
specific prow-job cites for the upstream baseline, and a concrete
recommendation (e.g. "add --e2e-parallel=8 to run-all.sh's sonobuoy invocation
at scripts/conformance/run-all.sh:LINE").

No code changes. Read-only. Findings doc under ai/findings/, one follow-on
bead if there's an actionable config change to make.

Context: complements the parallel investigation in mayor-ie8n3 (namespace GC
stalls under load). Both can be true — a parallelism fix may still leave
individual-test stalls that need mayor-ie8n3's fix. This scout tells us the
BUDGET question; mayor-ie8n3 tells us the EFFICIENCY question.
notes:
Follow-on filed: mayor-d8z7g (raise/parametrize sonobuoy --plugin-timeout for --all-e2e)
Follow-on filed: mayor-xz6fg (experiment: raise ginkgo parallelism above auto-detect(8) for --all-e2e, measure per-spec-cost impact)
close_reason: Verdict: both budget-misconfig AND scope-driven, compounding — --all-e2e's own doc comment already expects 6-12h (5.5x more candidate specs than the upstream anchor job by design, since it deliberately doesn't skip [Feature:.+]) but sonobuoy's untouched 6h default was never raised to match; separately, effective parallelism is 3.75x lower than upstream (8 auto-detect vs 30 explicit) and per-spec cost ~2.5x higher, both tracing to driver+cluster sharing one 8-core VM (upstream's driver/cluster never share a core). Raising --p alone only reaches the edge of the 6h ceiling, not comfortably under it. Findings: ai/findings/parallelism-baseline-2026-08-02.md. Follow-ons: mayor-d8z7g (raise/parametrize --plugin-timeout for --all-e2e), mayor-xz6fg (experiment: explicit ginkgo parallelism + measure per-spec-cost/error-rate impact before committing to a number).
