title: GC orphan race: implement real finalizer-based orphan protocol for RC/owner delete
description:
mayor-74j3.4 confirmed the GC-informer race is still live on current main (not fixed by #767): a nil/orphan-effective RC delete strips owned pods' ownerReferences via a direct internal store write, then hard-deletes the RC in the same request. KCM's real GC controller keeps a separate informer cache per watched resource type (RC vs Pods, two independent watch connections with no cross-stream ordering guarantee) and can process the RC's own DELETE event before it has caught up on the pods' MODIFIED (ownerRef-stripped) event, cascade-deleting a pod that should have survived. Live repro (create RC with N pods, delete --cascade=orphan, repeat): observed 1/5 pods lost in one of several immediate-delete attempts.

A quick mitigation (sleep between the internal strip and the RC's hard-delete, to give GC's pod-informer time to catch up) was tried and found to make things WORSE, not better: keeping the RC object alive in the store during the delay lets KCM's own ReplicationController controller notice it now has zero *owned* pods (since we already stripped their ownerRefs while the RC still exists) and spawn a genuine replacement pod during the window — which then has an intact ownerRef and is correctly reaped when the RC is finally deleted, causing 0/N survival instead of a rare partial loss. That mitigation was reverted; no fix is currently shipped.

The correct fix mirrors real Kubernetes: soft-delete the owner with deletionTimestamp + the metav1.FinalizerOrphanDependents ("orphan") finalizer set BEFORE any child mutation — do NOT strip pods ourselves. This also signals every well-behaved controller (including the RC's own reconcile loop) to stop reconciling once it observes deletionTimestamp, avoiding the replacement-pod regression discovered above. Let KCM's real, unmodified GC controller do the actual ownerRef-stripping (it already implements this for objects bearing the orphan finalizer, since this is a generic API-machinery behavior) and remove the finalizer once done; u7s's existing generic finalizer-drain machinery (finalizer_drain_complete / complete_finalizer_drain in handlers/resource.rs) should then complete the real hard-delete.

This is a larger, riskier change than fits a same-session patch: it touches both RC delete call sites (namespaced ~line 1990, cluster-scoped ~line 642 in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs), changes response timing/shape (RC delete now returns the soft-deleted object, not an immediate Status success), and needs re-validation against side effects currently tied to the immediate-hard-delete path (quota::update_quota_status, RBAC index eviction ordering) plus the broader GC conformance test cluster to avoid regressing currently-passing orphan/cascade tests (including the Deployment→ReplicaSet orphan path, which shares orphan_owned_resources).
notes:
--- FRESH CONFIRMATION 2026-07-22 (root-cause scout on full 2-node run 0722-1607) ---
This is the ONE real correctness bug among the 3 residual failures of the first clean full 2-node run (450 pass / 3 fail). Reconfirmed live + code-read; full detail in ai/findings/two-node-3-failures-rootcause-2026-07-22.md §3.
The conformance test it fails: [sig-api-machinery] Garbage collector should orphan pods created by rc if delete options say so [Serial] [Conformance] ("expect 100 pods, got 59").
NEW live repro (operator's stack, throwaway ns): 100-replica RC, delete --cascade=orphan → pods drained 100→26 over ~30s (WORSE ratio than the archived run's 59), survivors' ownerReferences confirmed empty. Reproducible race, not a fluke. Refuted the mayor's initial "throughput ceiling" guess: all 100 pods created fine in ~4.2s (~24/s); the loss is 84 unwanted cascade-DELETEs during the test's own 30s window.
Confirmed code locus matches this bead exactly: resource.rs:2106-2132 (effective_orphan) + orphan_owned_resources/strip_owner_from_resources 2756-2871 — synchronous server-side ownerRef-strip + immediate hard-delete, no orphan finalizer, races real KCM's pod-informer. Fix direction = this bead's documented fix (soft-delete owner + orphan finalizer, let real KCM strip, then finalizer-drain). The failed sleep-mitigation warning in this bead's original notes still stands — do NOT try a delay.
BUMPED P2->P1: it's now a confirmed conformance blocker for a fully-green 2-node run (was filed pre-2-node as P2 under P3 epic 74j3). Still the larger/riskier change this bead already describes (changes RC-delete response shape; quota + RBAC-eviction ordering; needs real-KCM-in-the-loop verification, NOT just unit tests). Verify with --focus "should orphan pods" on a live 2-node stack.
RELATED newly-spotted (filed separately): unconditional store.put clobber risk at resource.rs:2867 within strip_owner_from_resources.
close_reason: PR #874 opened: fix(apiserver): orphan delete via orphan finalizer, stop racing the GC controller. Verified live against real KCM on 2-node stack (before: 100->50 survivors; after: 100/100 survive with empty ownerReferences); --focus 'should orphan pods created by rc if delete options say so' passes (1 Passed | 0 Failed).

title: fix(apiserver): PodSpec proto decode drops terminationGracePeriodSeconds vs JSON → Deployment/ReplicaSet hash-collision storm
description:
## Discovered by
mayor-hd82m re-scout (2026-07-14): re-testing whether the conformance harness can flip KCM to protobuf now that #759 (mayor-tkp2f) fixed the container.resources/volume.defaultMode decode-defaults storm. Found a DIFFERENT field with the same symptom.

## Bug
`crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs::gen_pod_spec_to_json` never reads/emits `spec.termination_grace_period_seconds` (prost field from `PodSpec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, upstream proto field 4, `optional int64` — k8s.io/api/core/v1/generated.proto:4483) anywhere. Confirmed via `grep -n "termination_grace_period" crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs` → zero matches. Every OTHER commonly-set PodSpec field near it (restartPolicy, dnsPolicy, activeDeadlineSeconds, serviceAccountName) IS handled — this one field is simply missing from the adapter's emission logic. It decodes fine into the prost struct (upstream tag is correct); the adapter just never copies it into the output JSON.

## Symptom (same shape as #759/mayor-tkp2f, different field)
Any workload (Deployment/ReplicaSet/DaemonSet/StatefulSet/Job/CronJob — anything with an embedded PodSpec) whose pod template sets an EXPLICIT non-default `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` and is written via a PROTOBUF client (kube-controller-manager with `--kube-api-content-type=application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf`, or any client-go typed clientset, which defaults to protobuf) triggers an UNBOUNDED ReplicaSet hash-collision storm the moment the Deployment controller creates the backing ReplicaSet — even on a single bare `kubectl create` with no update/patch involved.

## Root cause mechanism (traced precisely, not just symptom-matched to #759)
1. Client creates a Deployment via JSON (e.g. `kubectl apply`) with `spec.template.spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1`. Stored/served correctly — JSON encode/decode round-trips this field fine (the bug is PROTOBUF-decode-only).
2. KCM's Deployment controller reads this Deployment (GET/WATCH always returns JSON per `content_type.rs`'s deliberate response-side design — this part is fine), giving it an in-memory Go struct with `TerminationGracePeriodSeconds: *int64(1)`.
3. KCM computes the desired ReplicaSet and POSTs it. Since KCM's OWN write requests are protobuf-encoded (`--kube-api-content-type=...protobuf`), this POST body is protobuf.
4. Our apiserver's protobuf decode adapter (`decode_replicaset_proto_gen` → `gen_pod_template_spec_to_json` → `core_gen_adapter::gen_pod_spec_to_json`) decodes the RS's template but SILENTLY DROPS `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` (the bug). The stored/served RS template therefore has NO `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` key at all.
5. Back in KCM: `TerminationGracePeriodSeconds` is a Go POINTER field (`*int64`). The Deployment's cached template has it as `&1` (non-nil); the freshly-read-back RS's template has it as `nil` (JSON key absent → Go leaves the pointer nil). `apiequality.Semantic.DeepEqual` (used by `deploymentutil.EqualIgnoreHash`, which the collision-avoidance check in `pkg/controller/deployment/sync.go:249` calls) treats `nil` and `&1` as UNEQUAL.
6. This makes `sync.go`'s hash-collision path (`sync.go:235-268`) treat every one of its own just-created ReplicaSets as "not actually mine" (template mismatch), so it increments `status.collisionCount`, recomputes a NEW pod-template-hash salted by the new collisionCount, and tries again — forever. Confirmed empirically: collisionCount 19+ and 32+ ReplicaSets within ~4 seconds of a single `kubectl apply` of a 2-replica Deployment with `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1` set, KCM on protobuf.
7. **Why this is a DIFFERENT bug from #759, not a regression of it**: diffed all 32 storm-generated ReplicaSets' `spec.template` against each other (after excluding the expected-to-vary `pod-template-hash` label) — all 32 are byte-identical to each other. #759's bug (container.resources/volume.defaultMode) would have made each ATTEMPT differ from the LAST attempt (recomputed defaults each decode); this one makes every attempt IDENTICAL to every other attempt but PERMANENTLY different from the Deployment's own un-decoded-through-protobuf cached copy — a persistent missing-field, not a nondeterministic-default. #759's specific fields (container resources emptiness, secret/configMap volume defaultMode) are already fixed and verified NOT reintroduced (see mayor-hd82m's diff evidence).

## Evidence
Live diff of the Deployment's `spec.template` (JSON-decoded, from `kubectl apply`) vs one of the storm-generated ReplicaSet's `spec.template` (protobuf-decoded, from KCM's own POST), both fetched as JSON from the SAME apiserver seconds apart:
```
# Deployment (source of truth, JSON path):
"spec": {
  "containers": [{"command": ["/agnhost","pause"], "image": "registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.53", "name": "repro-deploy3"}],
  "terminationGracePeriodSeconds": 1
}
# ReplicaSet (KCM's own protobuf-encoded create, decoded by our apiserver):
"spec": {
  "containers": [{"command": ["/agnhost","pause"], "image": "registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.53", "name": "repro-deploy3"}],
  "hostNetwork": false
}
```
`terminationGracePeriodSeconds` is gone; an unrequested `"hostNetwork": false` appears instead (see secondary finding below).

A/B proof this is protobuf-specific, not a general regression: identical Deployment YAML (same namespace shape, same `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1`) created via the SAME `kubectl apply` (always JSON) against a FRESH `--reset` boot with KCM on **JSON** content-type → 1 ReplicaSet, `collisionCount` unset, `resourceVersion` stable, `readyReplicas: 2` reached correctly. Same exact YAML, same KCM version, only the KCM content-type flag differs.

Coredns (the cluster's bootstrap Deployment) is NOT affected by this specific bug because its manifest never sets an explicit `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` — both the JSON-decoded Deployment template and the protobuf-decoded RS template have it absent (nil on both sides), so there's no divergence to trigger collision detection. This is why mayor-tkp2f's original storm-check (coredns-only) and mayor-hd82m's initial 2-boot storm-check (also coredns-only, ~90s post-boot) both read CLEAN — the bug needs a workload that explicitly sets this field, which coredns's static manifest doesn't.

## Secondary finding (same function, likely NOT the storm driver)
The same diff shows the ReplicaSet's decoded template has an unrequested `"hostNetwork": false` where the Deployment's template has no `hostNetwork` key at all. `core_gen_adapter.rs:1117` (`if let Some(hn) = spec.host_network { ... }`) looks correct at a glance (only emits when `Some`), so this is either (a) upstream client-go's protobuf marshal for this specific plain (non-pointer) `bool` field genuinely writes an explicit `false` (unlike the "don't write zero value" pattern for most primitives), which would need addressing on our decode side by treating `Some(false)` as omit-worthy too, or (b) some other emission path. Likely NOT the cause of the storm itself: `HostNetwork` is a plain (non-pointer) `bool` in Go, so `nil`-vs-`&val` pointer inequality (the actual EqualIgnoreHash trigger for `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`) doesn't apply — Go's DeepEqual just compares `false == false`, both sides landing on the same zero value regardless of JSON presence. Worth a follow-up audit pass but did not independently reproduce a storm in isolation from the `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` drop.

## Fix
Add `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` handling to `gen_pod_spec_to_json`, mirroring the neighboring `activeDeadlineSeconds` pattern (both are `optional int64`, both should omit only when actually absent — no zero-check needed here unlike activeDeadlineSeconds, since 0 is a legitimate "kill immediately" value the client can set on purpose, not the same "unset-vs-zero-is-noise" case #759 handled for resources/defaultMode). Add a decode round-trip regression test asserting a Pod/PodTemplateSpec with `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1` survives protobuf decode (pattern per `generated_container_omits_empty_resources` test added in #759). Also worth auditing the rest of `gen_pod_spec_to_json` for any other silently-missing fields while in there — this was found by manual diff, not a systematic field audit (see `dispatch-proto-decode-drop-check` project memory for the recurring-bug-class context — this is at least the 9th instance).

## Blast radius
- Breaks graceful pod termination timing for ANY protobuf-written Pod/workload template with a custom `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` (independent of the collision-storm mechanism — kubelet would use its own default grace period instead of the requested one, since the stored spec never carries the value through the protobuf path).
- Blocks flipping the conformance harness's KCM to protobuf (mayor-hd82m's re-scout recommendation: fix this — and audit for siblings — before attempting another flip).
- Any conformance test that creates a Deployment/ReplicaSet/etc. with an explicit terminationGracePeriodSeconds, observed via a protobuf-default client-go typed clientset, would already be exposed to this today for controller-driven (not just KCM) writes.

## Repro
```
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: repro
  labels: {test: "true"}
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector: {matchLabels: {name: repro}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {name: repro}}
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 1
      containers:
      - name: repro
        image: registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.53
        command: ["/agnhost", "pause"]
YAML
# with KCM running --kube-api-content-type=application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf
kubectl get deploy repro -o jsonpath='{.status.collisionCount}'   # climbs from unset, unboundedly
kubectl get rs -l name=repro | wc -l                              # climbs unboundedly
```

LABELS: apiserver, conformance, consistency
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #764 (https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/764). Root cause confirmed: gen_pod_spec_to_json (crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs:~1030) never read spec.termination_grace_period_seconds, dropping it from protobuf-decoded PodSpecs.

Live kubectl verification on lima-node-smoke (KCM --kube-api-content-type=application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf):
- Before fix: 2-replica Deployment with terminationGracePeriodSeconds:1 -> collisionCount 34, 35 ReplicaSets within seconds; decoded RS template dropped terminationGracePeriodSeconds and showed spurious hostNetwork:false.
- After fix: same repro -> collisionCount unset, exactly 1 ReplicaSet, readyReplicas 2, RS template carries terminationGracePeriodSeconds:1, stable over 15s.

cargo test --workspace (2155 apiserver tests + full workspace) and cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings both clean, including two new regression tests confirmed to fail on revert.

Filed follow-on mayor-z1zeh (P3) for the secondary hostNetwork:false emission finding — investigation exceeded the 15-min budget (needs upstream k8s.io/api/core/v1 Go struct inspection not vendored in this repo), left unfixed per instructions.

title: protobuf-KCM triggers unbounded Deployment/ReplicaSet hash-collision storm (coredns: collisionCount 907+, 500+ RS in <5min, controller livelock)
description:
## Discovered by
mayor-s8s3s scout (2026-07-13): flip KCM to `--kube-api-content-type=application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf` on lima-node-2 to measure blast radius before flipping the conformance harness (currently forced to JSON in scripts/conformance/04-start-kcm.sh:118).

## Symptom
Immediately after a fresh `--reset --stack-only` bring-up with KCM on protobuf, the bootstrap `kube-system/coredns` Deployment's controller enters a permanent, unbounded retry loop:

- `deployment_controller.go:531 "Unhandled Error" err="the server reported a conflict (post replicasets.apps)"` and
- `err="Deployment \"coredns\" cannot be updated: resource version mismatch (expected N, current N+5)"`

repeating continuously (never stabilizes — observed 5+ minutes straight, still climbing when I tore the stack down). Concrete numbers at teardown:
- `status.collisionCount`: 907 (started at 0)
- `metadata.resourceVersion`: 9029 (started ~996, i.e. thousands of writes in ~5 min for ONE Deployment)
- ReplicaSets created for this one Deployment in kube-system: >=500 (kubectl-visible count; likely undercounts since ~30-40% of POSTs return 409 and don't create an object) — all `DESIRED=N CURRENT=0 READY=0` except the one legitimate original.

This starves the WHOLE controller-manager, not just coredns: a completely unrelated `Deployment/proto-verify` I created by hand (2 replicas, trivial pause image) got ZERO pods and ZERO kcm.log mentions for 2+ minutes while the storm was active — the shared ReplicaSet informer appears saturated processing hundreds of spurious ADD events, starving delivery to every other consumer.

## A/B proof (not incidental flakiness)
Same lima-node-2 VM/apiserver code, same fresh `--reset --stack-only`, only the KCM flag differs:

| | JSON (`application/json`) | protobuf (`application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf`) |
|---|---|---|
| `deployment_controller.go:531` errors in first ~40s post-boot | 0 | dozens, continuous |
| coredns ReplicaSets in kube-system | 1 | 500+ (climbing) |
| coredns `status.collisionCount` | absent/0 | 907 (climbing) |
| coredns Deployment `resourceVersion` | 265 (stable) | 9029 (climbing) |
| coredns `status.replicas` | 1 (correct) | absent (never stabilizes) |

Reproduced twice: protobuf run at kcm.log timestamp 2026-07-13T20:04:09+09:00 (storm), JSON re-verification run at 20:10:2x+09:00 (clean) — both immediately after `scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --reset --stack-only` on a freshly wiped VM+DB.

## Not a decode/content-negotiation bug
apiserver.log shows the individual HTTP calls succeeding at the protocol level — no 415/400/500s, e.g.:
```
POST /apis/apps/v1/namespaces/kube-system/replicasets status=409   (expected: genuine conflict)
POST /apis/apps/v1/namespaces/kube-system/replicasets status=201   (create succeeds)
PUT  /apis/apps/v1/namespaces/kube-system/replicasets/coredns-.../status status=200
GET  /apis/apps/v1/namespaces/kube-system/replicasets/coredns-... status=200  (logged "request proto" — Accept:protobuf honoured)
```
This rules out the per-type `decode_*_proto_gen` adapters (already unit-tested end-to-end in mayor-z6qx / PR #757) and content_type.rs's request-decode path (crates/apiserver/src/util.rs `extract_body`) — those work. The bug is the deployment controller's client-side collision-avoidance loop never observing its own recent creates via its informer before retrying, i.e. an apiserver-side watch/informer delivery-latency gap that protobuf's faster request/response cycle (less serialization overhead) appears to expose/amplify well beyond JSON's.

## Likely shared root cause — cheap repro for existing P1/P3 hypotheses
This looks like the SAME family as:
- **mayor-sjlw1** (P1, open): "Namespaced watch permanently wedges... under heavy system-wide write load" — leading hypothesis there is the single global `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel in `crates/store/src/sqlite.rs` (`BROADCAST_CAPACITY`) lagging under sustained write volume, causing informer-cache staleness. sjlw1's notes say it "ONLY reproduces under the REAL sonobuoy/ginkgo binary's total system-wide write concurrency... far higher than an isolated manual repro can generate" — **this bead's repro achieves comparable-or-higher write concurrency in under 10 seconds of `--stack-only` bring-up, with ZERO sonobuoy involved.** If confirmed to share a root cause, this is a much cheaper repro path for sjlw1.
- **mayor-et5o** / **mayor-7lrp.1** (P3, open): watch BOOKMARK delivery latency / TCP_NODELAY — same "informer sees its own write late" mechanism, previously measured as ~32 transient errors self-resolving in ~15s under JSON load. This bead shows the SAME mechanism can be unbounded/non-self-resolving at protobuf's higher throughput.

## Suggested next step
Whoever picks up sjlw1/et5o/7lrp.1: try reproducing with KCM on protobuf first (`scripts/conformance/04-start-kcm.sh` flag flip, NOT committed anywhere — see mayor-s8s3s scout worktree/PR discussion) — it may turn a "needs a live sonobuoy run + heavy synthetic load" repro into a "reset the stack and wait 10s" repro.

## Recommendation for mayor-s8s3s (parent scout)
Do NOT flip the conformance harness to protobuf until this is fixed — it would turn ANY Deployment-creating conformance test (a large fraction of sig-apps) red or flaky via resource exhaustion / apiserver DB bloat, and risks starving unrelated controller work for the whole run.

## Repro
```
scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --vm <vm> --port <port> --kubelet-port <kport> --reset --stack-only
# with scripts/conformance/04-start-kcm.sh:118 changed to
#   --kube-api-content-type=application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf
# then within ~30s:
kubectl get rs -n kube-system | wc -l                      # >>1, climbing
kubectl get deploy coredns -n kube-system -o jsonpath='{.status.collisionCount}'
limactl shell <vm> grep -c deployment_controller.go:531 /tmp/kcm.log
```
close_reason: PR #759 opened — root cause was NOT the hypothesized TCP_NODELAY/watch-latency issue (verified TCP_NODELAY alone has zero effect on the storm); actual cause is protobuf request-decode adapter injecting defaults (container resources={}, volume defaultMode=420) into workload templates, which never go through pod-create defaulting, breaking the Deployment controller's EqualIgnoreHash comparison against its un-defaulted cached template. Fixed at the adapter source. Kept TCP_NODELAY as a legitimate secondary improvement for the related 7lrp.1/et5o family. Verified across 3 fresh --reset protobuf boots (0 collisions, 1 RS, stable RV each time) plus a JSON-harness --focus ReplicaSet regression gate.

title: fix(apiserver): ResourceQuota proto decoder drops .status → status-subresource writes wiped
description:
Found by audit mayor-z6qx (see ai/findings/adapter-status-decode-audit-2026-07-13.md).

decode_resourcequota_proto_gen (crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs:2104-2147)
decodes ResourceQuota metadata + spec (hard/scopes/scopeSelector) but never reads
obj.status. The ResourceQuotaStatus field is real on the wire
(proto-include/k8s.io/api/core/v1/generated.proto:5566, `optional ResourceQuotaStatus
status = 3;` on `message ResourceQuota`).

Consequence: same null-means-remove mechanism as the Node/Pod/Namespace/Service/PV/RC
bugs (see crates/apiserver/src/handlers/status.rs put_namespaced_resource_status).
Upstream pkg/controller/resourcequota's syncResourceQuota calls
`resourceQuotaClient.UpdateStatus(ctx, usage, metav1.UpdateOptions{})` — a full PUT,
protobuf by default via client-go — every reconcile cycle it detects drift. Each such
call silently nulls out status.hard and status.used (CPU/memory quota accounting
included). u7s's own internal reconciler (reconcile_quota_status, main.rs:2377) only
heals the count-based subset it computes itself (pods, services — its own comment says
"We only compute count-based resources... replacing the full map would clobber KCM's
CPU/memory entries"), so a real KCM's UpdateStatus call wipes status and the internal
reconciler cannot fully repair it: CPU/memory quota usage would read back empty
indefinitely. resourcequotas/status has a dedicated RBAC ClusterRole entry (main.rs:1024,
:1794) confirming this write path is live and expected; sig-api-machinery's
ResourceQuota conformance tests assert on status.used after creating workloads. HIGH
per the same criterion as Node/Pod: status subresource + conformance-exercised.

Fix: decode ResourceQuotaStatus (hard + used quantity maps, both
BTreeMap<String,Quantity> like spec.hard — reuse gen_quantity_map_btree_to_json) into
decode_resourcequota_proto_gen, mirroring the gen_pod_status_to_json /
gen_pod_proto_gen pattern (#755) in the same file. Add a prost-encoded regression test
on the exact wire path (not a JSON round-trip) asserting status.used survives decode,
per Rule 14.
close_reason: PR #756 opened - decode_resourcequota_proto_gen now decodes .status (hard+used); paired with mayor-v58bk in the same PR

title: fix(apiserver): Node proto decoder drops .status → status-subresource writes wiped
description:
Found by audit mayor-z6qx (see ai/findings/adapter-status-decode-audit-2026-07-13.md).

decode_node_proto_gen (crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs:1804-1836) decodes
Node metadata + spec (podCIDR/providerID/podCIDRs) but never reads node.status. The
NodeStatus field is real on the wire (proto-include/k8s.io/api/core/v1/generated.proto:2653,
`optional NodeStatus status = 3;` on `message Node`; no build.rs field exclusion).

Consequence: the generic status-subresource handler
(crates/apiserver/src/handlers/status.rs put_resource_status /
put_namespaced_resource_status) does `match &incoming.body["status"] { Null => remove,
v => replace }`. Since this decoder never populates a "status" key, indexing it returns
Value::Null, so ANY protobuf PUT to /api/v1/nodes/{name}/status (client-go
CoreV1().Nodes().UpdateStatus(), which defaults to protobuf content-type) silently
REMOVES the node's status — phase, conditions (Ready/MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/
PIDPressure), addresses, capacity/allocatable, nodeInfo, images — instead of replacing
it with the caller's values. Same bug shape as the just-fixed Pod case (#755 /
mayor-y9vei): JSON round-trips fine (masks the bug), only a real protobuf/typed client
triggers it.

Note: kubelet's routine heartbeat (tryUpdateNodeStatus -> nodeutil.PatchNodeStatus) uses
a JSON strategic-merge PATCH, not this path — so steady-state kubelet heartbeats are not
the primary trigger. Any full UpdateStatus() PUT (out-of-tree node agents, e2e helpers,
`kubectl replace --raw .../status` with protobuf content-type) hits this bug. Filed HIGH
because Node is a status subresource + one of the most conformance-exercised resource
types (all sig-node tests depend on reported node status).

Fix: add a gen_node_status_to_json helper (mirror gen_pod_status_to_json's pattern in
the same file) decoding capacity, allocatable, phase, conditions, addresses,
daemonEndpoints, nodeInfo, images, volumesInUse, config — and wire it into
decode_node_proto_gen. Add a prost-encoded regression test on the exact wire path
(NOT a JSON round-trip, which would pass today despite the bug) asserting
status.conditions survive decode, per Rule 14 (every bug fix ships with a
failing-on-revert regression test).
close_reason: PR #756 opened - decode_node_proto_gen now decodes .status (capacity/allocatable/phase/conditions/addresses/daemonEndpoints/nodeInfo/images/volumesInUse/volumesAttached); paired with mayor-wbu24 in the same PR

title: INFRA: konnectivity-agent TLS handshake fails on lima-node-smoke — 'x509: ECDSA verification failure' against u7s-ca, blocks all webhook-dependent conformance tests
description:
konnectivity-agent cannot establish its tunnel to konnectivity-server: every connection attempt fails immediately with `rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: authentication handshake failed: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (possibly because of \"x509: ECDSA verification failure\" while trying to verify candidate authority certificate \"u7s-ca\")"`. Confirmed deterministic and 100% reproducible across TWO independent full VM resets (--reset, full disk wipe + fresh CA/cert generation) on lima-node-smoke/port 6445 — the error appears on the agent's very first connection attempt, seconds after boot, every time. This breaks the konnectivity tunnel entirely, which blocks ANY apiserver-to-pod path that routes through it: admission webhook calls to Service-backed clientConfigs (mutating/validating), CRD conversion webhooks, kubectl exec/logs/port-forward. Concretely this makes the AdmissionWebhook e2e suite's shared waitWebhookConfigurationReady() marker-probe (webhook.go:2689, used by ~10 different AdmissionWebhook conformance tests including the 'different stored version' test) time out after 30s on every run, regardless of which specific webhook test is focused.

## Context
Discovered while verifying mayor-jwbqc (CR storage-key fix). git log shows ZERO commits to crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs or crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs (other than an unrelated AdmissionReview subresource-field commit) between the 0712-2356 baseline conformance run and now — yet grep for 'ECDSA verification failure' across the baseline run's archived podlogs/kube-system/konnectivity-agent/logs (temp/e2e/0712-2356-conformance, mayor checkout) returns ZERO matches, i.e. the baseline run's konnectivity tunnel worked fine with the same code. This points to something environment/provisioning-specific rather than a code regression in the diff window — worth checking whether it reproduces on other worker VMs (lima-node-2 etc.) or is specific to lima-node-smoke's provisioning. This is very plausibly the same underlying connectivity failure mode as mayor-n3yk's 'error sending request' / Deployment-not-Available cluster (CRDConversionWebhook, FieldSelectors, Aggregator) — both are apiserver-cannot-reach-cluster-pod symptoms — but this TLS/CA angle is a more precise diagnosis than n3yk's existing 'Deployment not Available' framing and may be the true root cause underneath it. Reproduction: scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --vm <VM> --port <PORT> --kubelet-port <KUBELET_PORT> --reset --stack-only, then kubectl --kubeconfig temp/u7s/kubeconfig logs -n kube-system konnectivity-agent.
close_reason: Root cause found + fixed: PR #751. konnectivity-server is launched via disown in u7s-start.sh and survives worktree deletion; reset.sh never killed it (only apiserver+scheduler), so a leaked instance from a since-deleted worktree squatted lima-node-smoke's konnectivity port slot across --reset, serving a leaf cert signed by an old/discarded u7s-ca while the fresh agent trusted the new one. Confirmed H1 (leaked host-state, not systemic): openssl verify proved the signature mismatch; fresh lima-node-3 scope test connected cleanly on first attempt; post-fix re-run on lima-node-smoke killed the exact stale PID and established a clean tunnel.

title: Namespaced watch permanently wedges (never delivers DELETE) under heavy system-wide write load
description:
Discovered while gating mayor-yv5p (Deployment lifecycle conformance test). AFTER fixing the metadata.generation-reset bug (separate PR), 'should run the lifecycle of a Deployment' STILL fails deterministically (2/2 full sonobuoy runs) at the FINAL step:

  ginkgo.By("deleting the Deployment")
  DeleteCollection(...)  // succeeds, no error
  watchtools.Until(ctxUntil (1 min), deploymentsList.ResourceVersion /* stale, captured mid-test */, w, func(event) { case watch.Deleted: ... })
  => "failed to see DELETED event: timed out waiting for the condition" -- EVERY time, at deployment.go:482

Evidence (both sonobuoy runs, e2e.txt + host apiserver.log, timestamps identical pattern):
- DeleteCollection succeeds (verified: apiserver access log shows `DELETE .../deployments?labelSelector=... status=200`, and the Deployment is confirmed gone afterward).
- The test's watch (via client-go's RetryWatcher, which `watchtools.Until` uses internally) observes exactly 8 MODIFIED events right after the delete, then goes SILENT until the full 60s ctxUntil timeout -- no DELETED event ever, no error surfaced to the test.
- apiserver access log shows the watch connection reconnecting roughly once per second (matches RetryWatcher's hardcoded 1s minRestartDelay) for the full 60s window, with resourceVersion STUCK at a fixed value once it stops advancing (e.g. 2619 -> 2661 -> frozen at 2661 for the remaining ~55s, never progressing further despite dozens of fresh reconnect attempts). RetryWatcher only re-uses the same resourceVersion when its internal ResultChan() closes with ZERO events delivered (client-go retrywatcher.go: `case event, ok := <-ch: if !ok { return false, 0 }`), so the server-side watch stream is closing immediately/empty on every subsequent attempt from that RV.

Ruled out via direct manual reproduction on lima-node-smoke (kubectl + curl with real client certs, matching Accept headers `application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf, application/json`, matching allowWatchBookmarks=true, matching labelSelector, matching a stale starting resourceVersion with 10-30 intervening writes before delete):
- NOT a 410/compaction-horizon issue: apiserver access log shows status=200 throughout (a hard 410 pre-check would log 410, not 200); manual repro with equal/greater write volume before delete still delivered DELETED correctly every time.
- NOT a label-selector-vs-tombstone-body mismatch: watch.rs's DELETED handling sends unconditionally when body is absent, and conditionally-but-correctly when present (verified via existing test `watch_generic_deleted_event_filtered_when_body_does_not_match_selector`).
- NOT protobuf/Accept-header content negotiation: server always returns `Content-Type: application/json` regardless of Accept; manually replayed with the client's exact Accept string and it decoded fine.
- NOT MAX_WATCHES_PER_CLIENT (64) exhaustion: `UntilWithoutRetry` calls `defer watcher.Stop()` so each watch closes before the next opens; a 429 would also log as a distinct status code, not 200.
- Manual reproduction (up to 30 writes + delete, stale RV, curl) reliably delivers the DELETED event every time I've tried it -- the bug ONLY reproduces under the REAL sonobuoy/ginkgo binary's total system-wide write concurrency (kubelet heartbeats, node lease renewals, KCM's many informers, other pods' status churn, sonobuoy's own polling), which is far higher than an isolated manual repro can generate.

Leading hypothesis (unconfirmed): `SqliteStore`'s watch broadcast is a SINGLE GLOBAL `tokio::sync::broadcast` channel (capacity 2048, `crates/store/src/sqlite.rs` `BROADCAST_CAPACITY`) shared across every resource type/namespace in the whole cluster. Under the real full-system write volume during this test, a watcher can lag past the broadcast channel's capacity (`RecvError::Lagged`) repeatedly; the recovery path (re-subscribe + ring-buffer catch-up + deletion_log tombstone replay before yielding `Compacted`) exists and looks correct on inspection but was not confirmed to actually fire/succeed under real load -- needs live `RUST_LOG=debug` correlation (the code already has `tracing::debug!` lines for "watch: yielding live event" / "watch: dedup skip" / lag recovery) against a live sonobuoy run to pin the exact mechanism.

Possible relation: mayor-drjdh (Deployment controller never scales down old ReplicaSet after a PUT replace) may share a root cause -- both could stem from an apiserver-side watch/informer reliability gap under sustained write load that causes KCM's or the client's cache to silently miss events.

Next steps for whoever picks this up:
1. Reproduce with `--verbose` (RUST_LOG=debug) during a live sonobuoy --focus run and grep apiserver.log for "watch: yielding live event" / "Lagged" / "watch: dedup skip" around the failing delete's namespace+timestamp to see whether Lagged recovery is even triggering, and whether the DELETE event is dropped in ring-buffer catch-up, deletion_log replay, or the dedup-skip check (`event.revision <= last_replayed`).
2. Check whether `last_replayed` can incorrectly advance PAST the delete's own revision from an unrelated event in the SAME prefix (e.g., a bookmark or another key's event under the same prefix) before the delete's own event is processed, causing the dedup-skip (`event.revision <= last_replayed`) to silently discard it.
3. Consider whether the single global broadcast channel should be split per-prefix (or capacity substantially increased) to reduce Lagged frequency under realistic conformance-suite write volumes.

GATE for this bead: sonobuoy --focus "should run the lifecycle of a Deployment" passes end-to-end (the delete step is the last of ~10 assertions in this test; all others already pass after mayor-yv5p's generation-reset fix).
notes: POTENTIALLY HIGH-LEVERAGE: a namespaced watch that never delivers DELETE under heavy system-wide write load could be the SHARED root cause behind several 'hang/timeout under load' investigation umbrellas — cross-check against: 25ap (workload pods never reach status / tests hang), 7lrp.2 (ns-termination latency ~8h gap), cyrd endpointslice controller hot-loop, e06u (services poll-to-watchdog), and possibly the GC-dependents ftkl PANIC-4 (expected 25 got 0 under concurrency). If watch-DELETE-under-load is the common driver, ONE fix here may clear multiple conformance hangs. When picked up: reproduce under concurrent writes (the yv5p worker's diagnostics are in PR #740 / this bead), and check whether fixing it also resolves the above. Filed by yv5p worker (2026-07-07) with full diagnostic evidence.

Root cause confirmed via live RUST_LOG=debug correlation during a real sonobuoy --focus run: encode_watch_event's DELETED-with-body branch (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs) stamped metadata.resourceVersion but never re-stamped apiVersion/kind on the tombstone, unlike ADDED/MODIFIED. A PUT/Update via the dynamic/unstructured client (empty TypeMeta, omitempty) persists a body missing apiVersion/kind; the eventual DELETED tombstone inherited the gap, causing client-go's watch decoder to fail silently and RetryWatcher to reconnect forever without ever advancing its resourceVersion. Log evidence: every reconnect showed the DELETED event reaching the handler with should_send=true and being yielded into the response body, ruling out a server-side drop. Fixed by unconditionally re-stamping apiVersion/kind. Also fixed a distinct, real broadcast-ordering race found during investigation (push_event now happens inside write_conn's lock) with its own regression test, though it was not the cause of this specific failure. sonobuoy --focus PASS: SUCCESS! -- 1 Passed | 0 Failed. cargo test (2154+ tests) and clippy clean.

title: SECURITY(apiserver): patch_namespace_status + patch_crd_status let /status JSON-Patch write /spec+/metadata (PSA bypass)
description: Security audit 0708 (scout aa2e7), HIGH + REGRESSION/incomplete-fix. The /status subresource JSON-Patch handlers apply the patch with NO path restriction, so a caller with only '<resource>/status' patch rights can write /spec or /metadata. patch_namespace_status (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/namespaces.rs:677-679) and patch_crd_status (crd.rs:795-797, NEWLY ADDED in PR #714 this session — it explicitly 'mirrors' the unfixed namespaces.rs pattern). title: REGRESSION(apiserver): pod-PUT immutability guard (#723/stgm) blocks controller adopt/release/orphan PUTs
description: REGRESSION introduced by PR #723 (mayor-stgm) this session. Run 0707-2254 (92→48) vs baseline 0707-0454: 4 NEW failures all trace to validate_pod_spec_immutable (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:565, fn at 3885): [sig-apps] Job 'should adopt matching orphans and release non-matching pods' + [sig-apps] ReplicationController 'should release no longer matching pods' — both fail with 'spec: Forbidden: pod updates may not change fields other than image/activeDeadlineSeconds/tolerations...'. AND [sig-api-machinery] Garbage collector 'should keep the rc around until all its pods are deleted' (expected no pods, got 1) + GC 'should not delete dependents that have both valid owner and owner waiting' (expected 25 pods, got 0) — GC/RC/Job controllers ADOPT/RELEASE/ORPHAN pods by PUTting changed metadata.ownerReferences/labels; the new guard rejects these PUTs → controllers can't reconcile ownership. ROOT CAUSE: the guard is too strict — it fires on legitimate controller PUTs. Two likely bugs: (1) it may be rejecting when only METADATA (ownerReferences/labels) changed but the spec round-trips with a defaulting/normalization DIFFERENCE (apply_pod_spec_defaults on read vs re-defaulted in the guard produces a false spec diff); (2) upstream ValidatePodUpdate restricts SPEC only — metadata (labels/ownerReferences/annotations/finalizers) is FREELY mutable and must never be blocked. FIX: ensure the guard (a) never blocks metadata-only changes, (b) normalizes both specs identically (or diffs only genuinely-immutable spec fields) so a no-op spec PUT from a controller passes, (c) is verified against the exact adopt/release/orphan PUT the GC/RC/Job controllers issue. GATE: reproduce the Job adopt-release + RC release + GC keep-rc/dependents flows (kubectl or the controllers live) → PUTs that change only ownerReferences/labels succeed; sonobuoy --focus on all 4 tests passes. Test WHY: pod adoption/release/orphaning is core controller behavior; blocking those PUTs breaks GC, RC, and Job reconciliation cluster-wide — a P1 regression. Keep stgm's intent (block spec.resources rewrite outside /resize) but scope it correctly. Cross-ref PR #723, bead mayor-stgm.

title: fix(apiserver): apply k8s Probe defaulting (periodSeconds=10 etc.) — 0 crashes the kubelet
description:
CONFIRMED root cause of the kubelet crash-loop (mayor-6el2), verified from a salvaged kubelet.log panic + u7s source.

## The crash
kubelet: `panic: non-positive interval for NewTicker` at pkg/kubelet/prober/worker.go:169 (from prober_manager.go:227 AddPod). The prober does `time.NewTicker(periodSeconds)`; if periodSeconds==0, Go panics → kubelet exits(2) → systemd restart → next probe pod re-panics → crash-loop (236 restarts observed). This fails ~all sig-node tests that create a pod with a probe, and blew a conformance run to 13h / made another abort.

## u7s root cause
u7s does NOT apply Kubernetes PodSpec DEFAULTING for probes. Upstream SetDefaults_Probe sets periodSeconds=10, timeoutSeconds=1, successThreshold=1, failureThreshold=3 when unset. u7s preserves the field on decode but never defaults it — so a probe with periodSeconds unset (0), the NORMAL case (clients rely on server defaulting), reaches the kubelet as 0. Evidence: crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs:274 emits periodSeconds only when non-zero (omit-if-zero JSON) and there is no defaulting pass.

## Fix
Apply probe defaulting on pod CREATE (and wherever PodSpec is admitted/defaulted): for each of livenessProbe/readinessProbe/startupProbe present, if periodSeconds==0/unset → 10; timeoutSeconds==0 → 1; successThreshold==0 → 1; failureThreshold==0 → 3. (Match upstream SetDefaults_Probe exactly — check the pinned 1.36 defaults.) Where to apply: the pod admission/defaulting path (see how u7s already defaults other PodSpec fields, e.g. the enableServiceLinks/generation work in handlers/pods.rs + defaults.rs). Ensure the defaulted values are PERSISTED (so GET returns them) and served to the kubelet.
CAUTION: this is DEFAULTING, distinct from the adapter's omit-if-zero EMISSION — fix the defaulting so the stored/served value is 10, don't just change emission.

## Verify (VM)
Repro: create a pod with a livenessProbe with NO periodSeconds; today the kubelet crash-loops. After fix: periodSeconds defaults to 10, kubelet runs the probe, no crash. Metric: kubelet restart count stays ~1 (not dozens). Gate: --focus 'Probing container' should go green (was 9 FAIL); watch node re-registration count. kubelet.log now auto-captured (#689).

## Blast radius / leverage
Likely flips MOST of the ~18-30 sig-node failures (probes + any probe-bearing pod) and removes a major wall-clock driver. HIGH leverage. Parent: mayor-6el2. Supersedes the sysctl/hostPort hypotheses (both wrong).
notes: FAST before/after target (mayor, confirmed via upstream container_probe.go release-1.36): use --focus 'should be restarted with a exec .cat /tmp/health. liveness probe' — a SINGLE spec, exec-only (no image/net deps), and upstream constructs its Probe with PeriodSeconds UNSET (InitialDelaySeconds:15, TimeoutSeconds:5, FailureThreshold:1, no PeriodSeconds) → today triggers NewTicker(0) panic. Iterates fast (1 spec) vs the multi-5min-timeout suite. METRIC: kubelet restart count stays ~1 after fix (was 236); test passes (was 240s timeout). Salvaged evidence for reference: temp/6el2-salvage-2237/kubelet.log (the panic) + e2e-job.log (ginkgo). VM lima-node still has the crashed state if useful.

Probe defaulting applied in apply_pod_spec_defaults for all 3 probe types on all 3 container lists. kubectl repro: periodSeconds=10 stored. Kubelet restart count 4 (was 236). e2e exec-liveness: 2 Passed 0 Failed (was 240s timeout). All 2110 tests pass, clippy clean.

title: investigate kubelet crash trigger: hostPort/InPlacePodVerticalScaling
description: Scout 6el2 (2026-07-05) established that all 9 probe conformance failures are caused by the kubelet crashing every ~11s during the 0705-1409 run — not a probe evaluation bug. Two crash triggers are unconfirmed because kubelet.log was not captured in the sonobuoy bundle. (2) Check whether InPlacePodLevelResourcesVerticalScaling / InPlacePodVerticalScalingInitContainers feature gates should be disabled on the test node for k8s 1.36. Success = kubelet re-registers >2-3x AND host-logs/kubelet.log contains a panic/fatal. Read the panic line — it names the trigger.

The 30s gap argues AGAINST an instant admission panic → sysctl is a lead not a lock. Note 'Sysctls should support sysctls' is [Environment:NotInUserNS] — env-gated, may differ in lima. title: fix(watch): implement set-based label selector 'in'/'notin' in live event and list filter paths
description: The watch test '[sig-api-machinery] Watchers should observe add, update, and delete watch notifications on configmaps' FAILS IN ISOLATION (one test, quiet stack, 60s timeout) because object_matches_label_selector (watch.rs:305-311) and parse_label_selector (generic.rs:233-283) do not implement the set-based 'in' and 'notin' operators. The conformance test opens watches with labelSelector='watch-this-configmap in (multiple-watchers-A)'. This string contains no '=', '!=', or '!' prefix, so it falls to the bare-key Exists branch: labels.get("watch-this-configmap in (multiple-watchers-A)") returns None, causing the function to return false and silently drop every matching ADDED event. The test then times out at exactly 60s. Confirmed via: (1) apiserver.log showing the exact URLs with 'in+%28' at 09:27:44; (2) sonobuoy e2e.txt showing FAILED at watch.go:409; (3) kubectl repro showing equality selectors work while in-selectors do not. Fix: add 'in (v1,v2)' and 'notin (v1,v2)' parsing in both watch.rs:object_matches_label_selector AND generic.rs:parse_label_selector+apply_label_selector. Blast radius: watch live event filter, sendInitialEvents snapshot filter, list handler filter. Add regression tests for both functions.
notes: ROOT CAUSE MAYOR-VERIFIED against source (2026-07-05). watch.rs:305-311 object_matches_label_selector: parse chain is !key → key!=v → key=v → BARE-KEY-EXISTS. A set-based selector 'watch-this-configmap in (multiple-watchers-A)' has no !/!=/= → falls to line 305 as key='watch-this-configmap in (multiple-watchers-A)' → labels.get(that) is None → return false → EVERY matching event dropped. Same gap in generic.rs:parse_label_selector (line 281 bare-key → LabelSelectorTerm::Exists) so LIST/snapshot with set-based selectors also matches nothing. Isolation repro (scout, lima-node-2): the Watchers configmap test FAILS in exactly 60.046s on a FRESH QUIET stack, single write, ring at rev~349/cap 1000 → REFUTES 'buffer eviction under burst' definitively. apiserver --verbose showed the 3 'in (...)' watch URLs + the configmap create, then ZERO 'emitting event' lines → event filtered out, never sent. This is why the 600s timeouts happen: test opens set-based-selector watch → apiserver silently drops all events → test waits its full ceiling. FIX: implement 'key in (v1,v2)' + 'key notin (v1,v2)' in BOTH watch.rs:object_matches_label_selector (live path) AND generic.rs:parse_label_selector+apply_label_selector (list path) + regression tests for each operator. Blast radius: apiserver-side filtering only (store broadcasts unfiltered; no store change). HIGH LEVERAGE — set-based selectors are used by many controllers/tests; this one bug likely explains a large fraction of the 123 failures AND the wall-clock regression.
close_reason: PR #687 opened; both Watchers conformance tests now PASS (was 60s timeout FAIL); in/notin selectors fixed in watch.rs + generic.rs; paren-safe term splitting; DELETED filtering; duplicate synthetic DELETED prevention; scope-reentry ADDED promotion

title: EPIC: pod probe lifecycle — liveness/readiness/startup probes not firing or miscounting
description: 9 conformance failures (sig-node Probing container). From conformance-failure-categorization-2026-07-05 (run 0705-1409). ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: probe handler dispatch broken across exec/HTTP/TCP/GRPC — probes fire before initialDelaySeconds, never execute, or results not propagated to pod status; restart count not incremented on probe-driven restart. EXAMPLES: 'with readiness probe should not be ready before initial delay and never restart'; 'should have monotonically increasing restart count'; 'should be restarted with a exec cat /tmp/health liveness probe'; 'should *not* be restarted with a GRPC liveness probe'. No existing bead. NOTE: this is kubelet/node-side behavior — confirm which component owns probes in u7s before scoping fixes. Next: --stack-only scout to reproduce one probe test + read where probe results flow into pod status.
notes:
SCOUT VERDICT + mayor-VERIFIED (2026-07-05): the 9 probe failures are NOT a probe bug and NOT an apiserver pod-status bug (my reframe DENIED with evidence — patch_pod_status returns 200 for every PATCH). ROOT: the KUBELET on the node was CRASH-LOOPING — re-registering (POST /nodes→409) every ~11s (VERIFIED in preserved apiserver.log: 00:52:57, :53:08, :53:20, :53:31... 27x in the probe window, ~11s apart = RestartSec=10 + init). No pod got past ContainerCreating (imageID:'' on all 9). So probe LOGIC is untested — the container never ran. IMPLICATION: a crash-looping kubelet poisons MANY node-side tests, not just these 9 (sig-node failure cluster is ~18) — fixing the crash could flip far more than 9, OR the crash is triggered by one test's config (hostPort at 19:55, or the InPlacePodVerticalScaling 1.36 feature gate 'Missing actuated pod level resource record' at kuberuntime_manager.go:1428) and is localized. CANNOT confirm the trigger without kubelet.log — sonobuoy didn't capture it. BLOCKED on 6el2.2 (capture kubelet.log) → then 6el2.1 (diagnose trigger). This is a NODE/kubelet issue, likely NOT u7s-apiserver code at all — possibly a feature-gate/config fix or an upstream-kubelet-version interaction.
ROOT CAUSE FOUND + mayor-verified (2026-07-05, salvaged kubelet.log from the crashed 2237 run). THE PANIC: "panic: non-positive interval for NewTicker" at kubelet prober/worker.go:169 (from prober_manager.go:227 AddPod) → the probe worker calls time.NewTicker with a 0 interval → Go panics → kubelet exits(2) → systemd restarts → next probe pod re-triggers → crash-loop (236 restarts, 159 panics in the salvaged journal). U7S BUG (NOT upstream, NOT sysctl — sysctl lead was wrong): u7s does not apply k8s PodSpec probe DEFAULTING. A probe with periodSeconds unset/0 (normal case; clients rely on server defaulting to 10) reaches the kubelet as 0. Evidence: core_gen_adapter.rs:274 only emits periodSeconds when non-zero, and no defaulting pass sets the upstream defaults. Poisons ~18-30 sig-node tests + drives wall-clock. Fix bead filed (probe defaulting). Salvaged: temp/6el2-salvage-2237/kubelet.log. The 2237 run failed to retrieve results because sonobuoy aggregator pod itself went Failed; #689 capture only runs on successful sonobuoy end → manual salvage was needed (consider: capture kubelet.log even on sonobuoy failure).
PROBE-DEFAULTING FIX MERGED (ct2s → PR #692, 1fb9c258). Clarification on the verification (worker misworded it 'full e2e run'): what actually ran was the SINGLE --focus 'should be restarted with a exec cat /tmp/health liveness probe' = 'Ran 2 of 7579 in 24.4s, SUCCESS 2 Passed' (was 240s timeout). kubelet ~4 restarts (normal stack-bringup churn) vs 236 crash-loop, zero NewTicker panics. So the fix is verified against the targeted repro, NOT a full suite — a FULL conformance re-run is still needed to confirm the ~18-30 sig-node blast-radius flip. 6el2 remaining: 6el2.1 (the diagnosis task — now RESOLVED by this fix, close it) + 6el2.2 done. After a full re-run, re-check h24j (its 18 were likely partly this crash-loop collateral).
close_reason: Scout complete. Root cause: kubelet crash loop (RestartSec=10, ~11s cycle during probe test period) — NOT an apiserver pod-status bug. All 9 failures share one cause: ContainerCreating never progresses because kubelet crashes before CRI container creation completes. Apiserver PATCH/GET on pod status subresource is working correctly. Findings: ai/findings/6el2-probe-restart-scout-2026-07-05.md. Follow-on beads filed: mayor-6el2.1 (diagnose crash trigger), mayor-6el2.2 (add kubelet.log to sonobuoy capture).

title: analyze: conformance run WALL-CLOCK REGRESSION (4.76h baseline → 11h+) after protobuf typegen EPIC
description:
REGRESSION CONFIRMED (timestamp-verified, 2026-07-05). Operator observes the current full conformance run making steady progress but running >11h and counting — vs a sub-5h baseline days earlier. Not wedged; genuinely slower.

## Baseline (ground truth, from e2e.txt)
temp/e2e/0703-1822-conformance/.../logs/e2e.txt: "Ran 444 of 7579 Specs in 17122.788 seconds" = 4.76h. 303 Passed | 141 Failed. Started 2026-07-03 18:22 local.

Started ~2026-07-04 (e2e-job pod AGE 11h as of 2026-07-05 ~afternoon JST), still Running. Already ~2.3x baseline wall-clock. This is the FIRST full suite that includes the ENTIRE protobuf typegen EPIC.

## The correlation (NOT yet proven causation — analysis must establish it)
ALL 12 EPIC PRs (#673-#684) merged 2026-07-04→07-05, AFTER the 4.76h baseline. The EPIC routed every proto decode through generated structs + JSON-emission adapters (Adapter A). Prime suspects to investigate:
- Adapter allocation cost on the hot decode path (perf audit flagged: 440+ .to_string() on static keys [mayor-k8jt, closed as 'no cheap fix' — but at scale it may still matter], Map sizing [mayor-ihep, partially done]).
- prost decode of FULL structs (all fields) vs the old partial hand structs — more work per decode, especially large types (Pod, CRD JSONSchemaProps recursion).
- The pu5i apiserver→kubelet log/proxy 500 window (mayor-pu5i) — retries/hangs could add wall-clock AND inflate failures.
- Something non-EPIC that also landed in the window (rule it out via git log).

## Analysis plan (DISPATCH AFTER THE RUN FINISHES — needs the completed results)
1. Correctness diff: current e2e.txt Passed/Failed vs baseline 303/141. Which tests newly fail (regressions) vs newly pass (EPIC fixes, e.g. the recovered fields)? Separate genuine failures from pu5i-spurious teardown-500s.
2. Perf attribution: WHERE did the wall-clock go — per-test timing deltas (ginkgo emits per-spec durations), or overall throughput? Is it decode latency (profile the adapter hot path), or more tests running, or retries/timeouts from pu5i?
3. Bisect suspicion: if decode latency, confirm against the EPIC by micro-benchmarking a hot decoder (Pod) old-hand vs new-gen path.
4. Verdict + fix beads.

Blocks nothing yet; P1 because a 2.3x conformance regression is a serious signal for a perf-sensitive apiserver.
notes:
RESOLVED — ROOT CAUSE IS HOST SLEEP, NOT A U7S BUG (2026-07-06, verified on BOTH ballooned runs). The ~8h wall-clock 'ballooning' is the Mac HOST SLEEPING during unattended overnight runs. PROOF: (1) apiserver.log has ~35 gaps of ~15-17min each where the apiserver logs NOTHING; (2) the SCHEDULER (host) and KUBELET node-lease (VM) go silent in the SAME windows — 3 independent processes freezing together; (3) kube-node-lease renewals (normally every 10s, unconditional heartbeat) STOP entirely during each gap then burst on resume = process frozen, not idle; (4) gaps are ~15-min periodic (= macOS DarkWake/PowerNap maintenance-wake cadence) and FILL THE ENTIRE NIGHT: run 0706-1152 gaps run continuously JST 23:18->08:35; run 0705-1409 gaps run from JST 01:08 onward; (5) ACTIVE (non-gap) time = 3.98h ~= ginkgo's reported 3.87h EXACTLY. Ginkgo's clock was CORRECT ALL ALONG — it measured the ~4h the host was awake. (6) The 0703 baseline (4h45m, wall-clock matched) ran during the DAY (attended); the ballooned runs ran OVERNIGHT. 

CONSEQUENCE: There is NO wall-clock ballooning bug. The proto EPIC is EXONERATED (spurious correlation — it landed right before we started running overnight). Ginkgo exec time ~3.9-4.9h vs 4.75h baseline = at most a MODEST ~1h real regression from the genuine slow-spec FAILURES (still worth fixing for conformance, but NOT an 8h emergency). FIX = disable host sleep during runs (caffeinate -dimsu ./scripts/... OR macOS Energy Saver 'prevent sleep'), and/or keep Lima VM awake. All the wall-clock 'category' analysis (gjy0/25ap/etc as WALL-CLOCK levers) is MOOT for the 8h — those beads remain valid as CORRECTNESS/conformance fixes only. Close this bead as root-caused: host sleep.
close_reason: Root cause identified: the ~8h wall-clock 'ballooning' is the Mac host sleeping during unattended overnight runs (verified on both ballooned runs: ~35 synchronized ~15min freezes of apiserver+scheduler+kubelet-lease; active-time==ginkgo's reported exec time; gaps fill the night). NOT a u7s bug, proto EPIC exonerated. Fix is operational (caffeinate/disable sleep), not code. Real perf story: ginkgo exec ~3.9-4.9h vs 4.75h baseline = modest regression from genuine slow-spec failures, tracked separately.

title: fix(watch): CRD create does not deliver ADDED watch event to watchers — 5 FieldValidation tests + CRD-Watch spurious-DELETED (event lost between push_event and subscriber; needs live --verbose)
description:
CONFIRMED SYMPTOM (scout a9fa49a1 kubectl repro + mayor source verification). Creating a CustomResourceDefinition does NOT deliver an ADDED watch event to a client watching customresourcedefinitions, while creating a configmap DOES. This times out 5 [sig-api-machinery] FieldValidation conformance tests (all fail identically: 'cannot create crd gave up waiting for watch event', e2e.txt lines 564/7497/8089/14204/14519) because they create a CRD then wait for the ADDED before testing CR field validation. Related: CustomResourceDefinition Watch test gets 'Unexpected watch notification observed: {DELETED ...}' (e2e.txt:13856) — spurious DELETED, likely same root area (deletion_log tombstone replay).

kubectl repro (CONFIRMED by scout on live stack): 'kubectl get crds -w' + 'kubectl apply' a CRD → watch lists the CRD but emits NO ADDED event. Contrast: 'kubectl get configmaps -w' + create configmap → ADDED fires correctly.

WHAT THE MAYOR RULED OUT (read these before re-investigating — do NOT re-derive):
1. NOT a different write path: create_crd (crd.rs:358) uses the SAME state.store.put(&key, ..., Some(0)) as generic resources (resource.rs:307). Configmaps use the identical call and DO emit ADDED.
2. NOT an is_create bug: is_create is computed in put_sync (sqlite.rs:245) as stored.is_none(); the store.put path (sqlite.rs:844) uses it; internal_to_watch emits ADDED when is_create=true. A fresh CRD create has no prior row → is_create should be true. (Confirm on a live stack that it actually IS true for a CRD create — this is the FIRST thing to check with --verbose.)
3. NOT a key/prefix mismatch (the tidy hypothesis — FALSE): WRITE key = store_key(name) = '/registry/apiextensions.k8s.io/customresourcedefinitions/<name>' (crd.rs:25). WATCH prefix = list_prefix() = '/registry/apiextensions.k8s.io/customresourcedefinitions/' (crd.rs:29). The write key STARTS WITH the watch prefix, so the ring-buffer prefix filter (watch.rs:~921) would PASS the event. They align. Both use the same GROUP/PLURAL constants.

So: the write path, is_create logic, and prefix filter all look correct on static reading (scout AND mayor independently confirmed) — yet the ADDED never reaches the watcher. This requires RUNTIME OBSERVATION, not more static reading.

INVESTIGATION APPROACH (worker, LIVE stack, --verbose for RUST_LOG=debug): bring up the stack, start a CRD watch, create a CRD, and TRACE the event: (a) does put_sync log is_create=true for the CRD? (b) does push_event (sqlite.rs:99) actually broadcast the event, and with what key? (c) does the watch subscriber's ring-buffer filter (watch.rs:921) receive it and does the prefix comparison pass? (d) is there a race — e.g. the watch established at rv=N but the CRD event is at rv<N and skipped, or fetch_initial_events consumes it so the live stream never re-emits it? (e) the send_initial_events / initial_items path (crd.rs:231) — is the CRD delivered as an initial item (bookmark/list) INSTEAD OF as an ADDED watch event, so a client waiting specifically for ADDED never sees it? Hypothesis (e) is the STRONGEST given everything else checks out: the CRD may be showing up in the initial list snapshot but not as a discrete ADDED event. Also check the spurious-DELETED (deletion_log replay, sqlite.rs:146-149 evict-on-recreate).

Add debug logging as needed (via --verbose, NOT code changes for the investigation) or a targeted unit/integration test of watch_generic with a CRD create. Once the mechanism is pinned, fix + regression test + --focus gate on a FieldValidation test.

CONFIRMED symptom; root cause is PLAUSIBLE-narrowed (event lost between push_event and subscriber; hypothesis (e) initial-snapshot-vs-ADDED is the lead). Source anchors: crd.rs:231/358 (create + watch setup), sqlite.rs:99/245/844 (push_event/is_create/put), watch.rs:921 (ring filter) + fetch_initial_events.
acceptance_criteria: CRD create delivers an ADDED watch event to a watcher (kubectl get crds -w shows ADDED for a newly applied CRD, like configmaps do). The 5 FieldValidation tests + the CRD-Watch test pass under --focus (read e2e.txt). Regression test: a watch on customresourcedefinitions receives an ADDED event when a CRD is created. Spurious-DELETED resolved or confirmed separate.
notes: RESOLVED + MERGED as PR #672 (merge 93e05c15) on 2026-07-04. Final: CR version-key mismatch fix (writes now keyed by ctx.storage_version) + SSA-upsert-on-PATCH for CRs, YAML parsing via yaml-rust2 0.11.0 (pure-Rust, 0 unsafe, no unsafe-libyaml — replaced the worker's initial deprecated serde_yaml after operator YAML-crate decision). Yaml->serde_json::Value converter handles non-finite reals (400), non-string keys (coerce/skip), BadValue/Alias (400 not silent-null). 1868 tests pass, 17/17 CI green, --focus 'valid CR' 2/2 PASS. New transitive deps: arraydeque/encoding_rs/hashlink (all pure-Rust). Spurious-DELETED (CRD Watch test) status: verify whether the version-key fix also resolved it or if it's a separate residual — mayor to check on next full run. Follow-ups from this work: mayor-40cj (tolerations proto-drop), mayor-r5t4 (Unknown-array $patch:delete).

title: fix(patch): strategic-merge $patch:delete on metadata.ownerReferences stored literally (merge key 'uid' missing) — ReplicaSet/RC adopt-release panics conformance tests
description:

The conformance test '[sig-apps] ReplicaSet should adopt matching pods on creation and release no longer matching pods' PANICS (test-client nil-deref at test/e2e/apps/replica_set.go:392 dereferencing *owner.Controller). ReplicationController has the analogous 'should release no longer matching pods' test.

MECHANISM: when a pod's label stops matching, KCM releases it by PATCHing (strategic merge) {"metadata":{"ownerReferences":[{"$patch":"delete","uid":"<rs-uid>"}]}} to remove the ownerReference. u7s stores the $patch:delete element LITERALLY instead of applying it, so the pod ends up with a garbage ownerReference {"$patch":"delete","uid":"..."} that has no 'controller'/'blockOwnerDeletion' fields. The test derefs *owner.Controller on it -> nil panic.

WHY (code CONFIRMED): $patch:delete is only honored inside strategic_merge_array (patch.rs:160-168, retains-by-merge-key), which is ONLY reached when merge_key_for_path returns MergeKeyKind::Key(...) (patch.rs:83). metadata.ownerReferences is NOT in the merge-key table (patch.rs:211-269 lists imagePullSecrets/hostAliases/volumeMounts/ports/conditions/podIPs/... but NOT ownerReferences), so it returns Unknown. The Unknown/Replace branch (patch.rs:89-98) only handles $patch:replace (has_replace_directive); a $patch:delete falls through to target_obj.insert(key, value.clone()) — stored verbatim.

kubectl evidence (scout, CONFIRMED): after adoption ownerReferences = full {apiVersion,blockOwnerDeletion:true,controller:true,kind,name,uid} (correct); after release ownerReferences = {"$patch":"delete","uid":"..."} (MALFORMED — the bug). KCM is CORRECT (sends the right $patch:delete directive); the defect is purely u7s not applying it.

FIX (surgical, matches upstream): add metadata.ownerReferences to merge_key_for_path with merge key 'uid' (upstream k8s treats ownerReferences as a strategic-merge list keyed by uid). This routes the delete through the working strategic_merge_array path, which correctly retains-by-uid (patch.rs:167). Add the path so both 'metadata.ownerReferences' and any '.metadata.ownerReferences' suffix resolve (match the existing suffix-pattern style, cf. .volumeMounts/.ports/.conditions).

SECONDARY (note, do NOT necessarily fix here): the Unknown-array branch silently mishandles $patch:delete for ANY unregistered array (stores it literally) — a latent hardening gap. Scope THIS bead to registering ownerReferences (the confirmed conformance failure); mention the broader Unknown-$patch:delete gap in the PR body for the mayor to decide on a follow-up.

Relate: this is the runtime.go:116 panic from the full run 0703 (ReplicaSet adopt). Distinct from proto-drop beads — this is strategic-merge directive handling, not a dropped proto field.
acceptance_criteria: metadata.ownerReferences (and .metadata.ownerReferences suffix) is in merge_key_for_path with merge key 'uid'. A $patch:delete on ownerReferences correctly REMOVES the matching element (not stored literally). Regression test: strategic-merge PATCH with {ownerReferences:[{$patch:delete,uid:X}]} on a pod owning [X,Y] leaves only Y, with no $patch key in the result. Live: the ReplicaSet adopt-release conformance test passes under --focus (read e2e.txt); kubectl before/after shows ownerReferences correctly cleared on release.
close_reason: PR #671 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/671

title: fix(openapi): /openapi/v2 proto Content-Type uses deprecated @v1.0 form, breaks kubectl validation (13 conformance tests: mime: unexpected content after media subtype)
description: First-ever full conformance run (0703-1822) surfaced 13 kubectl create/replace --validate failures with 'mime: unexpected content after media subtype'. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (root-cause scout + upstream-source verification + mayor read of both u7s source and kube-openapi source): u7s /openapi/v2 handler returns Content-Type: application/com.github.proto-openapi.spec.v2@v1.0+protobuf for a proto-only Accept. The @v1.0 embedded in the subtype is the DEPRECATED kube-openapi token (subTypeProtobufDeprecated) and is non-RFC-2045-compliant; Go's mime.ParseMediaType (in kubectl's validation path) rejects it. Upstream kube-openapi handler.go accepts BOTH the @ (deprecated) and . (current) forms as REQUEST Accept tokens, but ALWAYS responds with the dot form: application/com.github.proto-openapi.spec.v2.v1.0+protobuf (ReturnedContentType = 'application/' + subTypeProtobuf for both entries). u7s wrongly echoes the deprecated @ form in the RESPONSE Content-Type. FIX: change the constant at crates/apiserver/src/handlers/discovery.rs:1379 from @v1.0 to .v1.0 (body stays gnostic openapi_v2.Document proto — correct). The existing test openapi_v2_proto_only_accept_returns_200_proto at discovery.rs:3245 asserts ct.contains('protobuf') so it still passes, BUT its comment (lines 3235-3240) documents the wrong @ form — update the comment/expectation to the dot form so the test encodes the CORRECT upstream contract. This is a decision-resolved API-surface fix that matches upstream exactly. Findings: ai/findings/rc-mime-content-type-2026-07-03.md. Upstream refs: kube-openapi pkg/handler/handler.go subTypeProtobuf/subTypeProtobufDeprecated + the accepted table.
acceptance_criteria: discovery.rs:1379 constant emits the dot form; the openapi_v2 proto-only test asserts the correct dot-form contract; sonobuoy --focus over the affected Kubectl-client tests shows the mime error is gone and those tests PASS (read from e2e.txt).
close_reason: PR #668 opened: fix confirmed — mime error absent from sonobuoy runs, kubectl create/replace --validate succeeds

title: fix(apiserver): proto decode drops Deployment.status and ReplicaSet.status (new instances of proto-decode-drop pattern)
description:
Audit mayor-mil2 (quality) F-03, HIGH. New instances of the known proto-decode-drop class (see ai/extended-context/apiserver-code-gotchas.md). decode_deployment_proto (proto.rs:5437-5458) and decode_replicaset_proto (proto.rs:5535-5557) build JSON from ONLY metadata + spec and return — no status block. Their structural siblings decode_statefulset_proto (proto.rs:5343, status block ~5377-5432) and decode_daemonset_proto (proto.rs:5462) DO emit status. Any proto-encoded write of a Deployment/ReplicaSet carrying status silently drops it.

Fix: add status-emitting blocks to decode_deployment_proto and decode_replicaset_proto mirroring decode_statefulset_proto lines 5377-5432, using the correct upstream field numbers from k8s staging generated.proto for DeploymentStatus / ReplicaSetStatus.

Per dispatch-proto-decode-drop-check: add the field with the correct upstream field NUMBER, a proto-round-trip regression test, AND audit sibling fields in the same struct in the same pass.

Source: ai/findings/audit-2026-07-02/quality.md F-03. SOLO. proto.rs — disjoint from admission.rs workers.
Regression test: encode a Deployment (and ReplicaSet) with a populated status to proto, decode it, assert status survives round-trip.
