CSINode watch: resource.rs watch path already correctly called fetch_initial_events and watch_generic emits k8s.io/initial-events-end=true BOOKMARK (watch.rs:321) — resolved before PRs #192-#195. RuntimeClass 404: node.k8s.io/v1/runtimeclasses registered in state.rs:420-422 and served by generic handler, returns empty RuntimeClassList (200) not 404, confirmed by test list_resource_returns_empty_list_for_runtimeclasses. All 801 tests pass.

title: Persist TLS CA key+cert across restarts
description: u7s generates a fresh CA keypair on every startup (tls.rs:generate_tls called unconditionally, KeyPair::generate() always runs). The SA key is already persisted with load-or-generate pattern, but the CA is not. After any restart, the kubeconfig/certs distributed to kubelet (or to the lima VM via lima-start.sh) are signed by the old CA; u7s now trusts a new CA; TLS handshake fails; kubelet falls back to system:anonymous; all requests get 403 Forbidden; node never registers. Fix: apply the same load-or-generate pattern from load_or_generate_sa_keys to the CA key+cert. Persist ca.key and ca.crt alongside sa.key/sa.pub (same --db or key directory). On startup, if the files exist, load them; if not, generate and write. This is the primary blocker for stable lima VM + kubelet integration.

title: Pod watch: implement fieldSelector=spec.nodeName filtering
description:
kubelet watches /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods?watch=true&fieldSelector=spec.nodeName={node} to receive only its own pods. fieldSelector is entirely absent from the codebase (zero occurrences). Without it, the server returns ALL pods in the namespace (Axum drops unknown query params silently), causing kubelet to attempt running unassigned pods.

Gap: CollectionQuery in handlers/pods.rs:22-25 has no field_selector field. watch_pods() in handlers/pods.rs:153-265 has no post-filter step. list_pods() similarly.

Fix: 1) Add field_selector: Option<String> to CollectionQuery in pods.rs. 2) In list_pods(), after fetching all pods, filter by spec.nodeName if fieldSelector=spec.nodeName=X is present. 3) In watch_pods(), filter emitted events by spec.nodeName. The watch path is harder: filtering must happen client-side on the stream since the store watch is prefix-based. Emit only events where obj[spec][nodeName] matches.

Severity: HIGH — kubelet pod scheduling model is broken without this; kubelet will attempt to run unscheduled pods.

title: SA JWTs are minted but never validated on inbound requests
description: auth.rs:83-111 authenticate() only checks the static bearer token file. SA JWTs minted by handlers/tokens.rs are never verified on inbound requests — a request with a valid SA JWT header is authenticated as system:anonymous. Fix: add JWT verification path in authenticate(). Load the RSA public key from --sa-pub at startup. On a Bearer token that fails static map lookup, attempt RS256 JWT decode and verify. On success, extract sub (system:serviceaccount:ns:name) as username and construct groups [system:serviceaccounts, system:serviceaccounts:ns]. On failure, return BadToken. The encoding key is already loaded at startup (main.rs:82-96); load the corresponding DecodingKey from sa.pub.
notes: Implemented and committed directly to main (b062670). 5 regression tests added covering: valid JWT authenticates, tampered/expired/wrong-key rejected, static token priority. All 61 auth tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented in commit b062670: authenticate() now chains static-map → RS256 JWT → BadToken; sa_decoding_key loaded at startup; 5 new regression tests all pass (61 total).

title: RBAC index not updated when roles/bindings are written via API
description: The generic handler (generic.rs) writes RBAC objects (ClusterRoles, ClusterRoleBindings, Roles, RoleBindings) to the store but never calls rbac_index.apply_object() or rbac_index.remove_object(). Creating or deleting a ClusterRole via kubectl has no effect on the in-memory RBAC index — policy enforcement is stale until restart (and restart doesn't help either, see mayor-vgr). Fix: after each successful put/delete in the generic handler, check if the key is under /apis/rbac.authorization.k8s.io/ and call apply_object/remove_object accordingly. Depends on: mayor-vgr (startup scan) — both must land together for RBAC to work end-to-end.

title: RBAC index not populated from store on startup — restarts open the cluster

Effect: any RBAC roles and bindings stored on a previous run are invisible after restart — every restart produces an open cluster with no policy. Fix: in AppState::new() (or main.rs boot sequence), list the /apis/rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1/ prefix from the store and call rbac_index.apply_object() for each item. This must run before the server starts accepting requests.

title: Scout: repro mount-race hypothesis under --procs=4+ concurrent load, not isolated --focus
description:
GOAL: mayor-rcujn's isolated single-test scout (5/5 sonobuoy --focus runs of
'[Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] volumes should store data') found
NO failure across a range of Ready-status-PATCH-accept-to-exec-arrival
windows (70ms-1.77s, apiserver's own clock, directly comparable deltas) --
even windows tighter than the ~0.93s window that accompanied the ORIGINAL
failure (mayor-4w0j5) passed cleanly. Full findings and raw evidence:
ai/findings/rcujn-mount-race-scout-2026-08-10.md (see the worktree that
produced it, or ask the mayor to copy it into a new worktree's
ai/findings/).

HYPOTHESIS TO TEST: the mount-visibility race is not a pure timing-window
effect -- it requires actual node/kubelet/CRI-O resource contention, absent
from a solo --focus run. The original 14-failure cluster
(temp/csi-p4-failed-tests.txt) came from a --procs=4 FULL csi-hostpath
suite run (many concurrent volume tests hammering the same node's kubelet,
CRI-O sandbox creation, and CSI sidecar processing simultaneously), not an
isolated single-test run.

METHOD: reuse the SAME apiserver instrumentation this scout added (RCUJN_INSTR
prefix in patch_pod_status @ crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs and
resolve_exec_target @ crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs -- re-add it,
since this scout reverted it per the Shape-3 audit protocol) but run sonobuoy
with a focus regex matching SEVERAL of the 14 originally-failing test names
concurrently (e.g. the whole '[Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)]
volumes should store data|...' cluster, or use --procs=4 against the broader
csi-hostpath suite) so multiple pod1-write/pod1-delete/pod2-mount/pod2-exec
sequences race each other for node resources. Grep apiserver.log for
RCUJN_INSTR lines on a FAILING attempt and compute the same Ready-accept ->
exec-arrival delta; compare against the passing deltas already on record
(70ms-1.77s) to see if a failing run's window is qualitatively different
(e.g. much larger due to contention-induced kubelet sync delay) or if the
apiserver-side ordering itself is violated for the first time.

ACCEPTANCE: either (a) reproduce at least one failure with instrumentation
live and quote the smoking-gun timestamp delta, proving the contention
hypothesis and pointing at the specific mechanism, or (b) run the same
--procs=4-style concurrent load 5x without reproducing, which would argue
the original 14-failure cluster's root cause is environmental/flaky rather
than a deterministic u7s code defect -- file that as the next disproof step.

Do NOT edit kubelet (stock upstream Go). Instrumentation must be reverted
before this scout's own findings doc is finalized, per the Shape-3 audit
protocol (findings-doc-first, no code changes survive the scout).

title: perf(auth): AuthService::call clones request path unconditionally per-request (~1% of apiserver allocation bytes)
description:
SIGNAL

Memory audit of the 0810-0107 conformance run (ai/findings/memory-audit-2026-08-10-run.md, worker worktree agent-a1692f374ff3b3b59) found AuthService::call as a 113.7MB/86,127-block allocation site over a 40.67min run (~1% of total apiserver allocation bytes), via dhat jq query sorting .pps by -.tb and resolving .fs[1] through .ftbl:

  {"tb":113687640,"tbk":86127,"mb":93720,"frame":"<u7s_apiserver::auth::AuthService<S> as tower_service::Service<...>>::call"}

86,127 blocks is within the same order of magnitude as this run's total non-exempt request count (~88k status=200/201 responses per `grep -o "status=[0-9]*" host-logs/apiserver.log | sort | uniq -c`), i.e. essentially once per request.

MECHANISM

crates/apiserver/src/auth.rs:1014:

    let path = req.uri().path().to_owned();

This allocates an owned String on every non-exempt request, unconditionally. Why: req is moved into `Box::pin(async move { ... })` at auth.rs:1033, and `path` is used again AFTER an .await point inside that block (`parse_path(&path)` at auth.rs:1146, and `Some(&path)` at auth.rs:1153 for the non-resource-URL case only). A borrow of req.uri().path() cannot outlive the point where req itself is moved into the same closure, so the current code pays a String allocation to decouple path's lifetime from req's -- on every request, not just the minority (non-resource URLs) that actually need the raw string downstream.

This is NOT the same site mayor-e555b (PR #1038, closed) fixed -- that closed bead replaced object_is_live's full serde_json::Value tree parse for SA-token bound-object liveness. This finding is a plain String clone in the outer auth middleware's Service::call, unrelated to Value/JSON parsing. Not covered by mayor-0bd14 (typed-struct epic) either, since there's no Value involved.

FIX SKETCH

Call `is_exempt(req.uri().path())` and, for non-exempt requests, `parse_path(req.uri().path())` BEFORE `Box::pin(async move {...})` -- both are pure functions of a borrowed &str and involve no .await. Capture the resulting owned ParsedPath (crates/apiserver/src/auth.rs:806-816 -- already owns its own group/version/resource/subresource/namespace/name Strings) directly in the async block instead of the raw path.

For the narrow non-resource-URL case (auth.rs:1152-1153, `if parsed.resource.is_empty() && !path.starts_with("/api") { Some(&path) }`), only clone a separate Option<String> when `parsed.resource.is_empty()` is true -- this only fires for the minority of requests that are actually non-resource URLs (health checks, /openapi, /version, etc.), not every request.

Net effect: removes the unconditional per-request path.to_owned(), replacing it with a conditional clone that only fires for non-resource-URL requests.

SCOPE

Small, single-file (auth.rs), localized to Service::call's synchronous preamble. Estimated ~20-30 LoC restructure. Low risk: is_exempt/parse_path are pure functions already called with &str; moving the call site earlier changes nothing about their behavior, only when the owned data is captured.

TESTS

Existing auth.rs test suite already exercises is_exempt/parse_path/AuthService::call extensively (see auth.rs:1256+ test helpers) -- reverse-fail check: confirm parsed.resource/group/version/name/namespace values are identical before and after the restructure for representative resource and non-resource paths.

CROSS-REF

ai/findings/memory-audit-2026-08-10-run.md (HIGH finding #2), companion sibling to mayor-e555b (closed, PR #1038) and mayor-g7g2m (closed, PR #1036) -- part of the same "second-order allocation cleanup" wave but a distinct site/mechanism (String clone, not Value tree).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1075. AuthService::call preamble restructured: is_exempt+parse_path called on borrowed &str before Box::pin(async move); non-resource-URL raw path clone now conditional on parsed.resource.is_empty(). Reverse-fail check confirmed identical ParsedPath for representative resource + non-resource paths.

title: gen_persistent_volume_claim_to_json drops PersistentVolumeClaimStatus fields accessModes/capacity/allocatedResources/allocatedResourceStatuses/currentVolumeAttributesClassName/modifyVolumeStatus
description:
Discovered while fixing mayor-ifrs4 (PVCSpec.selector/dataSource/dataSourceRef/volumeAttributesClassName decode gap).

gen_persistent_volume_claim_to_json (crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs) only decodes PersistentVolumeClaimStatus.phase and .conditions. Six other status fields are silently dropped on protobuf decode:

- accessModes (actual access modes backing PV has)
- capacity (actual resources of underlying volume)
- allocatedResources (tracks resources allocated including expansion-in-progress capacity)
- allocatedResourceStatuses (per-resource resize status)
- currentVolumeAttributesClassName (VAC modify controller's current-state field)
- modifyVolumeStatus (VAC modify controller's in-progress status)

Impact: volume-expansion and VolumeAttributesClass status reporting is incomplete for any client reading PVC status via the protobuf decode path (client-go typed clientsets, used by controllers by default).

The sentinel_completeness_gen_persistent_volume_claim_to_json test added in mayor-ifrs4 is deliberately scoped to .spec only and documents this gap in a comment, rather than asserting on these fields, to keep that PR's scope to the originally reported spec fields.

Fix: add decode blocks for the six fields to gen_persistent_volume_claim_to_json's status handling, mirroring the existing phase/conditions pattern. Extend the sentinel test to cover .status once fixed.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1077. Six PVCStatus fields decoded (accessModes, capacity, allocatedResources, allocatedResourceStatuses, currentVolumeAttributesClassName, modifyVolumeStatus). Sentinel-completeness test extended to .status; scope-comment removed. Fail-on-revert verified per field.

title: 06-run-sonobuoy.sh: pod-log extraction gated behind JUnit — skipped on timed-out runs (where full logs matter most)
description:
## Summary

`scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh` evacuates the full `/var/log/pods/` tree from every VM node into `temp/u7s/pod-logs-evacuation-<node>.tar.gz` before namespace GC (line 291-297). But the extraction of those tarballs into `$RUN_DIR/pod-logs/` (line 483-489) is nested inside `if [ -f "$JUNIT" ]` (line 458), so when sonobuoy doesn't produce a `junit_01.xml` — which is exactly when Ginkgo times out mid-run — the extraction is silently skipped. The run directory ends up with only sonobuoy's own truncated per-namespace log dumps (fixed 42 lines, teardown only, useless for root-causing hangs), while the full logs sit unextracted on disk under `temp/u7s/`.

## Concrete impact

**Run `temp/e2e/0809-0954--driver-csi-hostpath/`** — timed out, no `junit_01.xml`, no `pod-logs/` dir extracted. Two independent investigations of the block-mode failures had to give up mid-analysis with "csi-hostpathplugin-0/hostpath/logs.txt is truncated to 42 lines, can't confirm NodeStageVolume/NodePublishVolume request bodies." Directly delayed root-cause identification of what turned out to be PR #1072 ([[mayor-a2ysh]], mountPropagation decode drop). The full logs were on disk the whole time — `temp/u7s/pod-logs-evacuation-lima-node-3.tar.gz` had every gRPC call from every driver container — but the pipeline never surfaced them into the run dir because JUnit was missing.

Compare to `temp/e2e/0809-1227-should-delete-volumes-at-scale-.../pod-logs/` — same script, but JUnit WAS produced (test failed cleanly rather than timing out), so extraction ran and `pod-logs/` is present. This is exactly backwards: the timed-out runs — where the failures are most opaque and full logs matter most — are the ones where extraction is skipped.

## Root cause

`scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh:458-508` structure:

```bash
if [ -f "$JUNIT" ]; then
    # ... JUnit parsing, summary print ...
    if [ "${FAILURES:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
      echo ""
      echo "  Failing tests:"
      # ...
      for NODE in "${NODES[@]}"; do
        EVAC_TARBALL="$WORKDIR/pod-logs-evacuation-${NODE}.tar.gz"
        if [ -f "$EVAC_TARBALL" ]; then
          mkdir -p "$POD_LOGS_DIR"
          tar -xzf "$EVAC_TARBALL" -C "$POD_LOGS_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
          HAVE_POD_LOGS=1
        fi
      done
      # ... summary print of pod logs ...
    fi
fi
```

The extraction is triple-guarded: `$JUNIT` must exist, JUnit must parse, `$FAILURES > 0`. All three conditions typically hold when Ginkgo completes; NONE hold when Ginkgo times out. The evacuation itself (line 291) happens unconditionally, so the tarballs are always on disk — they just don't get unpacked into the results tree.

## Fix

Move the tarball-extraction loop OUT of the JUnit-guarded block. Extraction should run whenever the evacuated tarballs exist, independently of whether sonobuoy produced JUnit. The summary-print loop (which iterates over failed namespaces from JUnit) can stay inside the JUnit block — it needs JUnit to know which namespaces were interesting. But putting the raw logs in the run dir shouldn't depend on JUnit at all.

Rough shape:

```bash
# Extract evacuated pod logs unconditionally — the timed-out runs where
# JUnit is missing are exactly the ones where these logs matter most.
POD_LOGS_DIR="$UNPACK_DIR/pod-logs"
HAVE_POD_LOGS=0
for NODE in "${NODES[@]}"; do
  EVAC_TARBALL="$WORKDIR/pod-logs-evacuation-${NODE}.tar.gz"
  if [ -f "$EVAC_TARBALL" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$POD_LOGS_DIR"
    tar -xzf "$EVAC_TARBALL" -C "$POD_LOGS_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
    HAVE_POD_LOGS=1
  fi
done

if [ -f "$JUNIT" ]; then
  # ... JUnit parsing, summary print, uses HAVE_POD_LOGS for tail preview ...
fi
```

`$UNPACK_DIR` is set at line 454 inside the `if [ "$UNPACK" -eq 1 ]` block, so the extraction needs to sit inside that same block (or `$UNPACK_DIR` needs to be set unconditionally). The `--no-unpack` case (line 33) can legitimately skip both.

## Acceptance

1. Deliberately kill a sonobuoy run before Ginkgo can write JUnit (e.g. Ctrl-C the script mid-run, or `--focus` a spec known to hang past `SONOBUOY_ALL_E2E_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`). Confirm `<run-dir>/pod-logs/var/log/pods/` is populated with the full logs.
2. Same for a normal successful run — extraction still runs, no regression.
3. Same for `--no-unpack` — extraction is skipped (correctly, since the whole tarball is left unmoved in that mode).

## Non-goals

- Do not change sonobuoy's own per-namespace log-dump truncation — that's an upstream ginkgo-e2e-framework `AfterEach` timing issue (dump is taken after the driver container starts shutting down), not something u7s can fix from this script. The evacuated `/var/log/pods/` logs are the complete alternative.
- Do not change the summary print (line 490+). It correctly stays JUnit-guarded — it iterates JUnit-listed failures.
- Do not touch the evacuation tar step (line 291) — that already runs unconditionally, which is correct.

## Cross-refs

- Discovered during: 0809-0954 CSI e2e run root-cause analysis; two subagent investigations of block-mode failures explicitly hit and reported the truncation as a blocker.
- Related — [[mayor-a2ysh]] (merged as PR #1072): root cause of that run's failures was identified anyway, but had to be inferred from the sonobuoy-truncated tail plus kubelet host logs. Full driver logs would have surfaced the `NodePublishVolume` gRPC response's own path directly.
- Related — [[mayor-ifrs4]], [[mayor-k8m7p]]: other beads filed from the same investigation.

title: sentinel-completeness tests only check top-level field NAMES, not nested-struct leaf completeness — hardening needed
description:
mayor-a2ysh found that gen_container_to_json silently drops VolumeMount.mountPropagation and recursiveReadOnly. The existing sentinel_completeness_gen_container_to_json test (core_gen_adapter.rs) has "volumeMounts" in its `expected` list and would have PASSED anyway, because assert_fields_present/has_field (util.rs sentinel_test_util) only checks whether a field name appears as ANY path segment ANYWHERE in the decoded JSON tree — it's satisfied the moment one subfield of one VolumeMount (e.g. "mountPath") survives. It does not verify that EVERY leaf field of a nested struct like VolumeMount, VolumeDevice, EnvVar, Probe, etc. individually survives decode.

This is a real coverage gap across every *_gen_adapter.rs sentinel-completeness test (they all use the same shared assert_fields_present/collect_leaf_paths helpers), not just gen_container_to_json.

Proposed hardening: extend sentinel_test_util so nested-struct expected entries can be given as full dotted leaf paths (e.g. "volumeMounts.mountPropagation") and are matched by exact leaf-path membership rather than segment-anywhere, while flat top-level fields keep the existing coarser check. Then audit gen_container_to_json (VolumeMount, VolumeDevice), and spot-check a few other adapters with array-of-struct fields, adding any leaf paths the audit finds missing to each `expected` list — this will likely surface a couple more of the "10th field-omission bug in this family" instances mentioned in dispatch-proto-decode-drop-check before a future scout has to rediscover them the hard way.

Not urgent/blocking — file as P2 quality-of-life hardening, related to (but narrower than) the already-closed mayor-z6qx (which addressed null-vs-omitted correctness, not read-at-all completeness).

title: apiserver test: install a single global tracing subscriber with thread_local per-test buffer routing to eliminate has_just_one callsite-Interest cache race (mayor-pqw78 root fix)
description:
Root cause investigation is complete in `mayor-pqw78`; this is the fix bead following operator's chosen approach (Option 1 of 3 presented).

## Root cause (from mayor-pqw78 investigation, 2026-08-07)

`tracing-core` has a process-global, per-callsite `Interest` cache with a `has_just_one` fast-path (see bd memory `tracing-core-has_just_one-caches-interest-permanently-under-parallel-cargo-test`). Under parallel `cargo test` where different tests install per-test scoped `set_default` subscribers (thread-local): if a callsite (e.g. `debug!("pod list entry")` in `list_pods`) is FIRST hit anywhere in the process while `has_just_one==true` AND the hitting thread has no default subscriber, `Interest::never()` gets cached PERMANENTLY for the whole process lifetime — silently disabling that callsite for every subscriber attached later (thread-local via `set_default` OR future-local via `WithSubscriber` — both downstream of the cache).

Empirically verified: `list_pods_emits_one_debug_event_per_pod_with_lifecycle_fields` (in `crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs`) reproduces ~40% flake rate under `cargo test -p u7s-apiserver --lib handlers::pods::` (scope where pods.rs is the only ever-registered dispatch). NEVER reproduces in full-crate runs (`-p u7s-apiserver --lib`) because `content_type.rs`, `lib.rs`, `inflight.rs`, `resource.rs` also install their own scoped `set_default` subscribers, flipping `has_just_one=false` early and defusing the fast path.

Neither Approach A (`WithSubscriber` future-locality) nor Approach B (test-scope `set_default` variants) can fix this — both are downstream of the callsite-Interest cache. Verified by mayor-pqw78 worker: 25 runs with `WithSubscriber` fix showed statistically-identical ~40% failure rate to baseline.

## The fix (operator-chosen, "Option 1", 2026-08-07)

Install a **single** `set_global_default` subscriber via `Once`, at test-binary init time. Its `MakeWriter` looks up a `thread_local!<Option<Arc<Mutex<Vec<u8>>>>>` for "currently active test buffer." Each debug-capturing test gets an RAII guard at its top that sets the thread-local; the guard drops on scope end.

Structure:
1. **Shared test-utils module** — new file `crates/apiserver/src/test_utils/tracing_capture.rs` (or similar location matching u7s crate conventions). Exports:
   - `install_global_test_subscriber()` — idempotent `Once`-gated function, called from any test that needs to capture events. First call installs the global subscriber; subsequent calls no-op.
   - `TestBufferGuard` — an RAII struct that sets the thread_local buffer on `new(buf: Arc<Mutex<Vec<u8>>>)` and clears it on drop.
2. **Migrate the 4 currently-affected tests** from `set_default` to the new pattern:
   - `pods.rs` — `list_pods_emits_one_debug_event_per_pod_with_lifecycle_fields` (the primary flaky test)
   - `content_type.rs` — the debug-capturing test(s) there
   - `inflight.rs` — same
   - `resource.rs` — same

Grep for `set_default` in `crates/apiserver/src/**/*.rs` to find all sites; each needs migration.

## Why this defuses the race

- Only ONE `Dispatch::new()` ever exists process-wide.
- `has_just_one=true` correctly resolves to "the global subscriber" (which IS the calling thread's current default because it's the only one).
- The global subscriber's `MakeWriter` demuxes to per-test buffers via thread-local lookup.
- No test's events are ever mis-routed because THREAD-LOCAL always correctly identifies which test is currently executing on that thread (thread ≠ test-invocation, but each test's future+guard scope pins the thread-local for the duration of its own captures).

## Non-goals

- Do NOT use `serial_test::serial` (Option 2 rejected): introduces a new crate dep for what should be a test-infrastructure fix, and it only serializes one test — future debug-capturing tests would need the same annotation.
- Do NOT modify production `tracing::debug!` call sites (Option 3 rejected): production code stays as-is; test-side is where the fix belongs.
- Do NOT touch `list_pods` production code or any other handler production code.

## Regression predicate (fail-on-revert)

`list_pods_emits_one_debug_event_per_pod_with_lifecycle_fields` must pass 20+ consecutive runs under `cargo test -p u7s-apiserver --lib handlers::pods::` (the pre-fix ~40% flake scope). If any of the 20 runs fails, the fix doesn't work.

Additionally: after the migration, `cargo test --workspace` must remain green (2795+ passed, unchanged assertion count).

## Cross-refs

- mayor-pqw78 (parent; investigation complete, investigation notes there)
- bd memory: `tracing-core-has_just_one-caches-interest-permanently-under-parallel-cargo-test`
- bd memory: `worker-refused-code-style-violation-2026-08-07` — related discipline note
close_reason: PR #1069 opened. Global test subscriber + thread_local buffer routing installed; 6 tests migrated across 4 files (pods.rs, content_type.rs x3, inflight.rs, resource.rs); 25/25 consecutive runs stable on both the exact test and the true flake-reproducing handlers::pods:: scope; fail-on-revert verified (20/20 fail reverted, 20/20 pass restored).

title: conformance harness watchdog: exempt CSI driver namespaces from reap while parent test namespace exists (matches <slug>-<N>-<M> pattern, checks <slug>-<N> presence)
description:
Supersedes mayor-ivcy3 (closed as SUPERSEDED, 2026-08-07). Operator design chosen over scout's earlier timer-widening proposal.

## The bug (re-established from mayor-51z5g close context and mayor-ivcy3 audit)

Conformance-harness watchdog (`scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh::watchdog_loop`) reaps any non-system namespace at 10m Active / 15m any-phase. Upstream `storageframework` deploys `csi-hostpathplugin-0` StatefulSet into a per-test namespace named `<parent-test-ns>-<random>` — e.g. `multivolume-3161-7041`. When the watchdog reaps this while the parent test is still running/cleaning-up, it kills the CSI driver, orphaning PVs and cascading into 20min PV-delete-wait timeouts.

**Naive fix "raise the threshold" is permanently REJECTED by operator** (see bd memory `watchdog-thresholds-are-final-do-not-raise` — the current 10m/15m values exist ONLY because CronJob suspended-schedule test needs a 5m buffer beyond its own 5m gomega.Consistently check; nothing else legitimately-executing comes close).

## The design (operator, 2026-08-07)

For any namespace matching the pattern `<slug>-<N>-<M>$` (two chained numeric suffixes = driver-namespace shape per audit-scout mayor-ivcy3), check if the parent `<slug>-<N>` still exists:
- **If parent exists**: skip the reap regardless of age (driver is still needed for the parent test's ongoing operations).
- **If parent absent**: fall through to the normal reap logic (both 10m Active and 15m any-phase gates apply unchanged).

**Why this design is better than timer-widening** (my prior recommendation, discarded):
- No threshold values change; aligned with `watchdog-thresholds-are-final-do-not-raise`.
- Gates on the actual CAUSAL condition (parent test needs the driver) rather than a timer.
- Symmetric with real-KCM's namespace-controller semantics (reap when dependency chain is broken, not when timer expires).
- A hung driver-ns whose parent has been reaped still gets caught at the normal 10m/15m gates.
- Aligned with operator's `retry-loops-are-hung` framing: healthy driver-ns finishes fast with its parent; hung driver-ns still gets reaped when it should.

## Regex (verified via audit-scout, 2026-08-07)

`-[0-9]{1,4}-[0-9]{1,4}$` — matches namespace names ending in two chained numeric suffixes. The k/k `release-1.36` chain that produces this pattern was traced by audit-scout:

- `test/e2e/storage/drivers/csi.go:250-253` — `hostpathCSIDriver.PrepareTest` calls `utils.CreateDriverNamespace(ctx, f)`
- `utils.CreateDriverNamespace` calls `f.CreateNamespace(f.Namespace.Name, labels)` — passes the parent test-ns's ALREADY-SUFFIXED name as base
- `framework.go:554-574` → `util.go:323-332` `CreateTestingNS`: `name := fmt.Sprintf("%v-%v", baseName, RandomSuffix())`
- `RandomSuffix()` = `strconv.Itoa(rand.Intn(10000))` — always 1-4 digits

Reference cached in `temp/research/` from prior audit.

## Pre-verify before finalizing the fix (upstream truncation edge case)

Worker MUST verify: does upstream's `CreateNamespace` / `CreateTestingNS` do ANY truncation of long names (e.g. k8s DNS label 63-char limit)? If yes, a driver-ns whose parent had a long name might be constructed differently and NOT match the `<parent>-<random>` invariant. Check `test/e2e/framework/util.go:323-332` in release-1.36 for any length-clamping. Report back if found — may need adjustment to the regex or additional handling.

## Implementation shape

In `scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh`'s `watchdog_loop()`, before the existing `age_s >= 600` / `age_s >= 900` reap-decision logic:

```bash
if [[ "$ns" =~ ^(.+-[0-9]+)-[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  parent_ns="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
  if kubectl --kubeconfig="$kubeconfig" get ns "$parent_ns" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    continue  # parent test-ns still exists → driver-ns is still needed. Skip reap.
  fi
fi
# fall through to existing reap logic
```

Extract into the existing `watchdog_decide` unit-testable function that `scripts/conformance/test-watchdog-logic.sh` already exercises. Add test cases (all against the existing test harness):

1. **Driver-ns pattern + parent exists → NOT deleted** (regression predicate for the actual bug). Test setup creates two namespaces: `multivolume-3161` and `multivolume-3161-7041`, both Active for 11 min. Predicate: `watchdog_decide` for `multivolume-3161-7041` returns "do not delete."
2. **Driver-ns pattern + parent absent → deleted per normal thresholds**. Setup: only `multivolume-3161-7041` (no `multivolume-3161`), Active 11 min. Predicate: `watchdog_decide` returns "delete."
3. **Regular test namespace (single suffix) → deleted per normal thresholds unchanged**. Setup: `multivolume-3161` alone, Active 11 min. Predicate: `watchdog_decide` returns "delete."
4. **Nested-suffix edge case**: `foo-1-2-3` — the regex should match on the LAST two-suffix suffix. Parent lookup would search for `foo-1-2`. Handle whatever falls out; document choice in the test case's assertion message.
5. **Adversarial**: `foo-9999-9999` where `foo-9999` doesn't exist → reaps normally per parent-absence.

Note: the current watchdog logic in `06-run-sonobuoy.sh` iterates inside a shell loop that already has `kubectl` access — adding a `kubectl get ns` per iteration is fine (small O(namespaces) call, fires once per 30s tick).

## Non-goals

- Do NOT change the 10m/15m thresholds. Do NOT make the watchdog "smarter" in any other way (per operator's `watchdog-thresholds-are-final-do-not-raise` memory).
- Do NOT delete the watchdog. Its primary use case (reaping legitimately-leaked namespaces) is real.
- Do NOT extend to any other namespace-pattern exemption without operator go-ahead.

## Acceptance

- `shellcheck scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh` clean.
- All 5 new test cases in `scripts/conformance/test-watchdog-logic.sh` pass.
- Case 1 fails on revert of the parent-existence check (regression predicate).
- `cargo test --workspace` + `cargo clippy` unaffected (shell-only change).

## Cross-refs

- mayor-ivcy3 (closed SUPERSEDED, 2026-08-07)
- mayor-51z5g (closed WON'T FIX; operator's `watchdog-thresholds-are-final-do-not-raise` memory)
- Audit-scout evidence in temp/research/e2e-*-1.36.go (from mayor-ivcy3 audit)
- bd memory: `csi-driver-namespace-name-shape`
close_reason: PR #1068 opened. Parent-existence check added to watchdog_decide per operator's design; driver-ns pattern <slug>-<N>-<M> skips reap while <slug>-<N> exists. Fail-on-revert test added and verified.

title: csi-hostpath: storageframework deploys driver StatefulSet into per-test namespace subject to conformance-harness TTL watchdog; move to stable shared namespace or add exclusion pattern
description:
Follow-on to mayor-51z5g (closed 2026-08-07 as won't-fix — see close reason there and the operator's repeated rejections of raising the namespace-TTL watchdog).

## The real problem (not the watchdog)

Upstream `storageframework` (k/k `test/e2e/storage/framework/`) deploys the csi-hostpathplugin StatefulSet into a namespace named `<driver-basename>-<random>` — e.g. `multivolume-3161-7041`. This namespace:
- Is a first-class per-test namespace subject to conformance-harness cleanup.
- Hosts the driver + external-attacher + external-provisioner + external-resizer sidecars for the WHOLE test's duration, including the PV-delete-wait window at the end (~20 min for `[Slow]` tests).

u7s's namespace-TTL watchdog (`scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh` watchdog_loop, thresholds set to 10m Active / 15m any-phase per commit f1535161) reaps this namespace as soon as it crosses 10 min Active — cutting the CSI driver's legs out from under the still-running test, orphaning PVs, cascading to `WaitForPersistentVolumeDeleted` timing out at 20m.

Naive fix "raise the watchdog threshold" is **rejected by operator, permanently** (see mayor-51z5g close reason + bd memory).

## Fix direction

**Option 1 (topology-side, correct):** Get the storageframework's `csi-hostpath` driver install pattern to deploy the driver StatefulSet into a stable, suite-scoped namespace (e.g. `csi-hostpath` — a plain fixed name, not per-test). System-namespace exclusion in `06-run-sonobuoy.sh` already covers `kube-*`/`sonobuoy`/`default`; add `csi-hostpath` (and any other in-tree e2e driver name that follows the same pattern) to that exclusion list. The upstream `csi-hostpath` install YAML actually uses namespace `csi-hostpath` in a lot of docs — the per-test-random naming is a storageframework wrapper choice, may be overridable via env or the driver-config struct.

**Option 2 (harness-side, easier, less correct):** Add an exclusion regex to the watchdog for namespaces matching a known-CSI-driver-namespace pattern. E.g. exclude namespaces whose OwnerReferences chain leads to a StatefulSet named `csi-hostpathplugin` or whose namespace name matches `^(csi-hostpath|hostpath|multivolume|.*-hostpath)-[0-9]+(-[0-9]+)?$`. Fragile — the naming pattern is not spec, it's storageframework internals.

**Recommend investigating Option 1 first.** Read `test/e2e/storage/framework/testsuites.go` and `test/e2e/storage/drivers/csi.go` upstream (release-1.36) — search for how the hostpath driver is installed and whether the destination namespace is configurable. If yes, override it in u7s's `06-run-sonobuoy.sh` (or wherever the driver install is triggered) to use `csi-hostpath` and add that to the exclusion list. If no, Option 2 is the fallback.

## Scope

Investigation + fix. Read-only investigation first (Shape 3 audit); fix bead(s) follow based on findings. ~1-3 hour dispatch expected — the fix itself is small, but proving the topology-side option is available takes reading upstream source.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT raise any watchdog threshold. This bead exists BECAUSE that path is closed by operator.
- Do NOT make the watchdog "smarter" via cross-referencing PV finalizers, live-CSI-detection, etc. — those are Option (c)/(e) from mayor-51z5g's description, which the operator's reasoning also rejects (they add fragility that masks real hangs).
- Do NOT touch the CronJob suspended-schedule test.

## Cross-refs

- mayor-51z5g (closed won't-fix, root reasoning) 2026-08-07
- mayor-rcujn / mayor-cst7t / mayor-w44wg — downstream symptoms; some may resolve once this is fixed, some are independent (snapshot API gaps, DiskPressure)
- Commit f1535161 (watchdog thresholds 10m/15m, the current + final values per operator)
- Commit cbf70302 (earlier attempt to raise to higher values, REVISED DOWN in f1535161)
- bd memory: watchdog-thresholds-are-final-do-not-raise
close_reason: SUPERSEDED by follow-on bead (see next). Operator (2026-08-07) rejected scout's timer-widening proposal and instead proposed a parent-existence check: for namespaces matching pattern <slug>-<N>-<M>$, look up parent <slug>-<N>; if parent exists, skip the reap (driver-ns is still needed); if parent absent, reap normally. Design pressure-tested and preferred (aligns with retry-loops-are-hung memory: no timer widening; reaps hung driver-ns just as fast as any other; correctly gates on the actual causal condition rather than time).

title: cleanup(prompts): architecture.md §3.4/§3.6/§3.7/§4.1/§7/§8/§9.2 describe fantasy node-agent and TBD-scheduler arrangements superseded by real kubelet + shipped scheduler
description:
Follow-on to mayor-unfxb (PR #1057, 2026-08-07). Worker on unfxb corrected §1/§3.3/§3.5 but held scope; the same drift class is present in seven other sections of the same file.

## Drift catalog (from unfxb worker's return)

Each section describes a fantasy arrangement that the corrected §3.5 (Node Runtime = real kubelet + CRI-O, no u7s node agent) now directly contradicts, OR is stale by shipped-code (scheduler section says TBD but crates/scheduler ships):

- **§3.4 Scheduler**: "internal design is TBD (see §9.3)" — stale. crates/scheduler ships per roadmap.md; the shipped design should be summarised at the same fidelity as the corrected §3.3.
- **§3.6 CRI Shim / Container Runtime Interface**: "The node agent does not call container runtimes directly" — no node agent exists. Real kubelet talks CRI to real CRI-O; there is no u7s CRI shim to describe.
- **§3.7 CNI Integration Point**: "does not implement networking" attributed to the node agent — same class as §3.6. CNI here is the CRI-O bridge conflist rewritten by scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh, not a u7s abstraction.
- **§4.1 Data Flow Diagram**: has "Node Agent on node-1 (watching v1/Pods with spec.nodeName='node-1')" as a labelled arrow — the actor is real upstream kubelet, not a u7s component.
- **§7 Node Agent Design**: entirely fictional per unfxb worker's audit — same shape as the container-runtime.md §5-9 fantasy that mayor-keloo removed. Should be deleted or replaced with a "Node lifecycle" section describing what scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh actually does (kubeconfig injection, CA copy, serving-cert generation, subnet rewrite, static routes).
- **§8 Phase 1/2 Deliverables**: lists a "node agent" phase deliverable that was never built.
- **§9.2 Container Runtime**: same class as §3.6 — describes a u7s-side abstraction that doesn't exist.

## Approach

Prefer one PR that sweeps all seven sections consistently — piecemeal PRs risk landing §3.6's correction before §7's, temporarily leaving the doc more internally contradictory than it is now.

Grounding order:
1. Read the current mayor-unfxb corrections (PR #1057) FIRST so the new sections match their tone and cross-refs.
2. Read `crates/scheduler/src/main.rs` and `crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs` for §3.4 — describe what actually shipped (scheduling gates, bind, PodScheduled patch, etc.), don't reinvent it.
3. Read `scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh` end-to-end for §3.5/§3.6/§3.7 factual grounding (already cited in the corrected §3.5 — reuse those citations).
4. `git log --oneline --grep=keloo` for the deletion pattern established by mayor-keloo (container-runtime.md §5-9 delete-and-replace).
5. Cross-check §8's phase-deliverables against roadmap.md's current phases to see which ones actually landed.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT re-touch §1, §3.3, or §3.5 (mayor-unfxb landed those cleanly).
- Do NOT change the document's overall structure or numbering unless deleting §7 forces a reflow (in which case, note the numbering change in the PR body).
- Do NOT rewrite the scheduler section from scratch as a design proposal — describe what shipped, not what could ship.

## Acceptance

- Every section listed above either accurately describes shipped code+scripts OR is deleted (with a one-line "see §3.5" pointer if the section number is referenced elsewhere).
- No section still uses "node agent" as an actor.
- §3.4's "TBD" wording is gone, replaced with a factual summary of crates/scheduler cross-refing lib.rs/main.rs.
- git grep 'node agent\|Node Agent\|TBD\|internal design' ai/prompts/architecture.md returns only expected residuals (or nothing).

## Priority

P2. Docs-only, correctness-of-onboarding value, no runtime impact.

## Cross-refs

- Parent: mayor-unfxb (PR #1057, corrected §1/§3.3/§3.5)
- Grounding: crates/scheduler/src/{main,lib}.rs; scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh; roadmap.md

title: apiserver bind_pod handler writes spurious reason="PodScheduled" / message="" on PodScheduled=True (upstream writes neither); triggers kubelet needsReconcile spam
description:
## Symptom

Kubelet log spam under sustained load (every ~10s reconcile tick), e.g. `temp/e2e/0807-0450--driver-csi-hostpath/plugins/e2e/results/global/e2e.log`:

```
kubelet[33707]: I0807 08:07:22.042270  33707 status_manager.go:1294] "Pod status is inconsistent with cached status for pod, a reconciliation should be triggered" pod="sonobuoy/sonobuoy" statusDiff=<
        @@ -35,8 +35,7 @@
            "observedGeneration": 1,
            "status": "True",
            "lastProbeTime": null,
        -   "lastTransitionTime": "2026-08-07T07:52:37Z",
        -   "reason": "PodScheduled"
        +   "lastTransitionTime": "2026-08-07T07:52:37Z"
           }
          ],
          "hostIP": "192.168.104.7",
 >
```

Note: `lastTransitionTime` is IDENTICAL on both sides — this is NOT a re-scheduling / re-bind bug. The only field that differs is `reason`.

## Diff arg-order convention (source of truth)

Upstream kubelet `pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go:1294` (release-1.36):

```go
logger.V(3).Info("Pod status is inconsistent with cached status for pod, a reconciliation should be triggered",
    "pod", klog.KObj(pod),
    "statusDiff", diff.Diff(podStatus, &status))
```

Where `podStatus := pod.Status.DeepCopy()` (from apiserver, normalized) is arg 1, and `&status` (kubelet's cached local status) is arg 2. `diff.Diff` renders `-` for arg 1 and `+` for arg 2.

Therefore in the log above:
- APISERVER side (`-`): has `"reason": "PodScheduled"`.
- KUBELET CACHE side (`+`): does NOT have any `reason` field.

## Root cause

`crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs::set_pod_scheduled_true` (line 6602) always writes:

```rust
cond["reason"] = serde_json::json!("PodScheduled");
cond["message"] = serde_json::json!("");
```

when the apiserver's `bind_pod` handler flips the condition to True.

Upstream apiserver (`k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/storage.go:261-264`, release-1.36) writes:

```go
podutil.UpdatePodCondition(&pod.Status, &api.PodCondition{
    Type:   api.PodScheduled,
    Status: api.ConditionTrue,
})
```

No `Reason`, no `Message`. Since kubelet's local cache is populated from what THIS bind path writes back (through its watch of the apiserver, minus any locally-generated fields), kubelet's cache never carries `reason: "PodScheduled"` for the scheduler-bound condition. u7s adds it; kubelet detects the drift on every reconcile and log-spams.

## Consequences

1. Log spam — dozens of these per pod per reconcile cycle under sustained load. Drowns real signal in kubelet logs.
2. Real work: `needsReconcile` returning true causes status-manager to schedule a status re-send back to the apiserver, adding write load that would not exist upstream. Under high-concurrency loads (>16 pods running), this multiplies (each pod's status is re-sent every ~10s reconcile tick until kubelet gives up).
3. Confusion: mimics re-scheduling / re-bind symptoms superficially, wasting mayor cycles investigating scheduler paths.

## Fix

`crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs::set_pod_scheduled_true` should NOT write `reason` or `message` fields when it flips PodScheduled to True. Only `type`, `status`, and `lastTransitionTime` should be written — matching upstream.

Trap: tests at `pods.rs:7786` and around line 6173 actively assert the WRONG behavior (`scheduled["reason"] == "PodScheduled"`). Those must be inverted to assert the field is either absent or empty, per upstream.

Also verify: `merge_conditions` (line 2570) clears stale `reason`/`message` when status flips (see line 2600-2608). Removing set_pod_scheduled_true's spurious reason should not create the inverse bug (stale Unschedulable reason surviving the True flip) — the merge_conditions clearing already handles that case. Cross-check with existing test at line 3773 (status_patch_clears_stale_reason_when_pod_scheduled_status_changes) — that should continue to pass.

## Test evidence (regression)

Live observation on `lima-node-2` during cv3jo repro run (`0807-0450--driver-csi-hostpath/`):
- Every pod in namespaces sonobuoy/, kube-system/ shows this reconcile-diff at every kubelet reconcile tick (~10s).
- Timestamps IDENTICAL on both sides — proves this is not re-transition, it's a stable field-inconsistency.

## Acceptance

- `set_pod_scheduled_true` matches upstream (no `reason`, no `message`) — verified by removing both writes AND by reading upstream `pod/storage/storage.go:261-264`.
- Related tests at pods.rs:6173, 7786 updated to assert new behavior.
- All existing status-patch merging tests (line 3765+) still green.
- Live-verify: on a fresh conformance stack, kubelet journal should NOT show these `status_manager.go:1294` "reason" diffs for stably-bound pods. Some diffs are expected (containerStatuses, timestamps) — the specific `-   "reason": "PodScheduled"` should disappear.

## Priority

P2 — log spam + amplified write load, but not a correctness bug (kubelet's reconcile-and-resend converges eventually). Deprioritize below active P1 correctness work but ahead of P3 cosmetics.

## Cross-refs

- Surfaced by operator, 2026-08-07, cv3jo repro run
- NOT mayor-s0wa3 (that was about a truly missing scheduler write, this is about a spurious apiserver write)
- Related: merge_conditions logic already handles the inverse case (True → False stale-reason clearing)
- Upstream commit history at k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/storage.go
close_reason: PR #1060 opened. Dropped spurious reason/message writes from set_pod_scheduled_true; now matches upstream pod-storage bind path shape (only Type + Status). Also clears stale reason/message on the update-existing-condition branch (upstream's UpdatePodCondition replaces the whole struct), preventing a worse regression (True + stale Unschedulable). Two tests inverted to assert the new correct behavior. cargo test + clippy green.

title: conformance harness: --port (default 6443) and konnectivity ports have same silent-collision class as pre-dda10 --kubelet-port
description:
Follow-on to mayor-dda10 (PR #1054, 2026-08-07).

mayor-dda10 hard-failed silent host-port collisions on `--kubelet-port`'s default 10250. The same silent-default-port class problem remains for `--port` (defaults to 6443, apiserver) and the auto-derived konnectivity-server-port / konnectivity-agent-port (line 84-87 of scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh).

title: hardcoded CA CN=u7s-ca makes cert-misroute failures cryptic (BadSignature) instead of legible (UnknownIssuer)
description:
Every u7s CA hardcodes Subject CN=u7s-ca; makes misrouted-cert failures surface as opaque BadSignature instead of legible UnknownIssuer.

## Context (mayor-ag0e5 scout v2 aa82864c86ab81711, 2026-08-07)

`crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs:179` and `:192` both hardcode `"u7s-ca"` as the CA Subject CN when generating a fresh CA. Every u7s stack ever provisioned uses the SAME Subject CN. Different key pairs (obviously), same DN.

When cert-routing goes wrong (e.g. via mayor-ag0e5's host-port-collision root cause), rustls's WebPkiServerVerifier finds a name-matching trust anchor in the client's root store (matching the wrong stack's CA), tries cryptographic verification against a leaf signed by a DIFFERENT stack's CA key, and returns `BadSignature`. Cryptically. What was really "you're talking to the wrong VM" surfaced as an opaque signature failure that took hours to root-cause.

## Fix

Make the CA Subject CN unique per stack. Options:

- **Option A**: incorporate the stack's VM name into the CN, e.g. `u7s-ca-lima-node-4`. Requires threading VM name / worktree ID into `load_or_generate_ca` (`crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs:127`).

- **Option B**: incorporate a random suffix generated at first-run, e.g. `u7s-ca-a3f7b2` (persisted to disk with the CA). Simpler — no threading needed.

Option B is cleaner (no cross-file coupling), but Option A is more debuggable (you can tell from the CN which stack a leaked cert came from).

Either way: rename the CA Subject at generation time. If the misrouting-to-wrong-stack scenario recurs, rustls's error becomes `UnknownIssuer` (name mismatch during trust-anchor lookup) which is a much more legible failure mode than `BadSignature`.

## Acceptance

- `cargo test --workspace green`.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings` clean.
- Fresh generation of a CA (fresh --reset) produces a CN that is NOT literally `u7s-ca`.
- Regression: an existing CA on disk (pre-fix) still loads without error (load_or_generate_ca reads whatever CN is there).
- Optionally: fault-injection test where two stacks are misrouted at each other; rustls error is `UnknownIssuer`, not `BadSignature`.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT change certificate KEY types, extensions, or validity dates.
- Do NOT change kubelet-serving cert Subject CN (kubelet's CN is per-node, which is already correct).
- Do NOT rename the CA file paths.

## Priority

P2. This is a diagnostic improvement — the actual bug (port collision) is fixed separately at P1. Without the port-collision fix in place, this fix alone would still result in a misrouted apiserver failing to reach its kubelet; the failure would just be more legible. Both fixes together give a robust "impossible-to-misdiagnose" scenario.

## Cross-refs

- Root cause: mayor-ag0e5 scout v2 aa82864c86ab81711, closed 2026-08-07
- Sibling fix (P1): port-collision auto-allocate/hard-fail in conformance harness (separate bead)
- File pointer: crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs:179 and :192 (both need to change together)
close_reason: PR #1061 opened. CA Subject CN is now u7s-ca-<6-hex-suffix> (random at generation, persisted in the cert itself). Existing CAs on disk load unchanged. Regression tests added.

title: flaky: handlers::discovery::tests::build_aggregated_discovery_increments_discovery_build_total races on shared DISCOVERY_BUILD_TOTAL counter
description:
Test snapshots crate::metrics::DISCOVERY_BUILD_TOTAL.with_label_values(["/discovery/v2","true","false"]).get() before calling build_aggregated_discovery once, then asserts the counter increased by exactly 1.

Other tests in the same file (e.g. around discovery.rs:589, :5173, :5222) call build_aggregated_discovery with the same (path="/discovery/v2", include_core=true, has_apiservice=false) label combination. Since cargo test runs tests in parallel threads within one process sharing the global Prometheus registry, if one of those other tests' call lands between this test's before/after snapshot, the counter jumps by more than 1 and the assertion fails.

Observed: reproduced intermittently (~1 in 4-5 runs) via `cargo test -p u7s-apiserver --lib --quiet` on 2026-08-07, both on main (9071c297) and on a branch adding an unrelated test elsewhere in core_gen_adapter.rs (which only shifted test-binary scheduling odds, not root cause). Not related to any change in discovery.rs or metrics.rs.

Fix should isolate the assertion from cross-test interference — e.g. use a unique label value per test run, or serialize tests touching this counter, or assert `after >= before + 1` is insufficient (loses precision); better to make the metric or the test call path deterministic per-test.
notes: PR #1055 (qq14v) worker independently reproduced this flake at origin/main tip and filed mayor-qyi9j (closed as duplicate of this bead 2026-08-07). Fix in flight: worker on mayor-a67fc2bb74b4d7463, using test-unique route label per this bead's option A.
close_reason: PR #1056 opened. Test now uses a test-unique route label (/test-only/discovery-build-total) to avoid parallel-test races on the process-global DISCOVERY_BUILD_TOTAL counter. Verified stable over 10 filtered runs + 4 full unfiltered parallel lib-test runs (2790 passed each) with no flake reproduction.

title: fix(apiserver): reject PVC size contraction (upstream 'field can not be less than previous value')
description:
u7s apiserver silently allows PVC size contraction (shrink). Upstream Kubernetes REJECTS this unconditionally.

## Bug (verified 2026-08-07 via operator question during mayor-65e5w PR #1048 review)

Grep of `crates/apiserver/src/` for shrink/contract validation returns zero PVC-relevant hits. u7s currently accepts a PVC UPDATE that sets `spec.resources.requests.storage` to a LOWER value than the previous request.

## Upstream expected behavior

`kubernetes/kubernetes@release-1.36:pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go:2579-2589`:

```go
if newSize.Cmp(oldSize) < 0 {
    if !opts.EnableRecoverFromExpansionFailure {
        allErrs = append(allErrs, field.Forbidden(
            field.NewPath("spec", "resources", "requests", "storage"),
            "field can not be less than previous value"))
    } else {
        // permits reducing pvc requested size up to capacity recorded in pvc.status
        // so users can recover from volume expansion failure -- but Kubernetes does
        // not actually support volume shrinking
        if newSize.Cmp(statusSize) <= 0 {
            allErrs = append(allErrs, field.Forbidden(
                field.NewPath("spec", "resources", "requests", "storage"),
                "field can not be less than status.capacity"))
        }
    }
}
```

Explicit upstream comment (line 2584-2585): "Kubernetes does not actually support volume shrinking."

## Failure mode this leaves us in

- User submits `kubectl patch pvc X -p '{"spec":{"resources":{"requests":{"storage":"500Mi"}}}}'` on a PVC currently requesting 1Gi.
- Upstream apiserver rejects with `Forbidden: field can not be less than previous value`.
- u7s apiserver ACCEPTS the update. The apiserver-side spec now reads 500Mi.
- CSI driver won't actually shrink the underlying storage (that's what upstream's comment means by "does not actually support") — so u7s ends up in a state where spec.resources.requests.storage=500Mi and status.capacity=1Gi indefinitely. That's a state upstream deliberately prevents.
- Not test-observable in the current csi-hostpath focused failure set (no upstream test intentionally shrinks), but a real production/user-facing gap.

## Fix

Same admission surface mayor-65e5w just added the expansion validation to: `crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs` (per PR #1048), function `reject_disallowed_pvc_expansion` (or add a sibling `reject_disallowed_pvc_shrink`). Extend to also check `newSize < oldSize` and reject with the upstream-matching Forbidden error.

**Optional/harder**: the `EnableRecoverFromExpansionFailure` narrow-shrink-to-status.capacity exception. That's a feature-gate-conditional recovery mechanism — if u7s doesn't already implement that feature gate, don't scope-creep. Just the hard "can't be less than previous" rejection is the baseline.

## Fail-on-revert test

Mirror the tests mayor-65e5w added in PR #1048:
- Create PVC with 1Gi request.
- Attempt UPDATE with 500Mi request.
- Assert Forbidden with the expected error message.

## Acceptance

- cargo test --workspace green
- cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings clean
- Fail-on-revert verified
- Very small LoC delta on top of 65e5w's changes

## Non-goals

- Do NOT touch expansion validation (65e5w PR #1048 covers it).
- Do NOT implement the RecoverFromExpansionFailure feature gate (feature-scope, not this bead).
- Do NOT touch KCM's volume-expansion controller.

## Cross-refs

- Discovered: 2026-08-07 operator question during PR #1048 review
- Sibling bead: mayor-65e5w (expansion validation, PR #1048 open)
- Upstream source: pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go:2579-2589 (release-1.36)
- Related admission plugin (expansion side): plugin/pkg/admission/storage/persistentvolume/resize/admission.go
close_reason: PR opened at https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/1049; extended reject_disallowed_pvc_expansion to also reject shrink unconditionally, mirroring upstream's hard 'no shrink' rule.

title: [triage] VolumeAttributesClass missing vac-protection finalizer (2 failures)
description:
Signature: `[FAILED] vac-protection finalizer was not set for VolumeAttributesClass "<name>"` -- the test creates a VolumeAttributesClass, references it from a PVC, and asserts u7s's apiserver adds a `storage.k8s.io/vac-protection` (or equivalent) finalizer to the VAC object while it's in use. The finalizer never appears.

2 failing tests (temp/csi-p4-failed-tests.txt):
1. e2e.log L3178 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] volume-modify [FeatureGate:VolumeAttributesClass] [Feature:VolumeAttributesClass] [It] should be protected by vac-protection finalizer
2. e2e.log L3945 [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] volume-modify [FeatureGate:VolumeAttributesClass] [Feature:VolumeAttributesClass] [It] should be protected by vac-protection finalizer

Sample failure body (e2e.log line 3411, default-fs variant; nearly identical for block volmode at line 4138):
  [FAILED] vac-protection finalizer was not set for VolumeAttributesClass "volume-modify-8176-e2e-vac-hostpathcbr5x"
  In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/storage/testsuites/volume_modify.go:287

Suspected u7s mechanism: VolumeAttributesClass is a relatively new (beta, feature-gated) upstream API. This looks like a genuine, narrow apiserver feature gap: u7s's admission/controller path for `storage.k8s.io/v1beta1 VolumeAttributesClass` does not add the protection finalizer when a PVC starts referencing it (the analogous behavior for PVs/PVCs -- kubernetes.io/pv-protection, kubernetes.io/pvc-protection -- IS implemented per other passing tests in this run). Candidate u7s code path: wherever u7s implements the PV/PVC protection-finalizer admission plugin (likely near crates/apiserver's admission or defaulting handlers) -- VolumeAttributesClass needs the equivalent, and it is very likely simply missing rather than broken.

Note: this is DISTINCT from mayor-6q2v2's cluster 2 (7 DeferCleanup pod-termination-hang failures in the SAME volume-modify family) -- those 7 tests get PAST VAC creation/finalizer setup and fail later during cleanup; these 2 fail immediately on the finalizer assertion itself.

Related beads: none pre-existing for this specific signature. Cross-ref mayor-6q2v2 cluster 2 (pod-termination hang, same test family, different test names) and mayor-cst7t (unrelated feature-gap precedent: apiserver missing an entire API group vs. missing one finalizer behavior here).

Reproduction hint: `--focus '\[sig-storage\] CSI Volumes \[Driver: csi-hostpath\] \[Testpattern: Dynamic PV \(default fs\)\] volume-modify.*should be protected by vac-protection finalizer'`
notes: CONFIRMED from mayor-cv3jo scout (2026-08-07): VAC is NOT a whole-feature gap. u7s DOES register storage.k8s.io/v1 VolumeAttributesClass (cluster-scoped) in crates/apiserver/src/state.rs:1324-1325 with adapter in crates/apiserver/src/storage_node_flow_gen_adapter.rs. Upstream 1.36 has VAC GA with lockToDefault:true (per temp/research/versioned-feature-list-1.36.yaml:2206-2223). This bead's scope is NARROW: only the vac-protection finalizer is missing (analogous to pv-protection / pvc-protection finalizers that already exist). Fix approach: look at how pv-protection is added by KCM's PVProtectionController and mirror it for VAC. Should be a small addition, no new API-registration work needed.
close_reason: PR #1064 opened. kubernetes.io/vac-protection finalizer now stamped on VolumeAttributesClass at CREATE time (create_resource), mirroring upstream's StorageObjectInUseProtection admission plugin (admitVAC) — verified this is unconditional-at-create, not PVC-reference-triggered as originally hypothesized; the failing conformance test asserts the finalizer immediately after Create(), before any PVC exists. Also confirmed pv-protection/pvc-protection stamping does not actually exist anywhere in u7s today (only referenced in comments/test fixtures) — left untouched, out of scope. Fail-on-revert regression tests added (pure-function + integration).

title: Scout: replicate upstream csi-hostpath e2e resource shape (30-parallel 6Gi req limit) on 12GiB VM
description:
GOAL: mirror upstream Kubernetes CI's proven-working csi-hostpath e2e configuration on a u7s stack (10+ GiB VM, --procs=30, --plugin YAML with requests=limits=6Gi on e2e container) and characterize what actually happens.

Reference upstream CI config: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-slow-beta/2063243433639677952
- Kubernetes CI runs csi-hostpath e2e at --procs=30
- Job pod has resources.requests.memory=6Gi (explicit)

What we want to learn:
- Does the test runner (e2e-job pod) even START and STAY UP at 30-parallel with 6Gi req/limit on a 12GiB VM?
- What is the actual peak memory demand at 30-parallel? (per-worker private-anon x 30 + shared) -- critical data.
- How many test specs run to completion (pass/fail/skip breakdown)? Our csi-hostpath coverage is probably near-zero, so most specs will fail -- but the failure modes ARE the data.
- Enumerate the failing specs by name + short failure reason -- these become follow-on bead sources for --focus zoom-in and future bug fixes.

What we do NOT care about here:
- Whether csi-hostpath specs actually pass. We EXPECT them not to (operator direction 2026-08-07).
- Sizing the Phase-1 fix. That's separately scoped in mayor-4dtlb (Phase-3).
- The VolumeSnapshot API gap (mayor-cst7t, scoping already done).

Assigned resources:
- VM: lima-node-5. Port 6447, kubelet port 10254.
- Do NOT touch: lima-node, lima-node-3 (operator csi-hostpath --procs=4 run in flight), lima-node-2 (worker o4fmo worktree, idle), lima-node-4/lima-node-smoke (prior scout Left Running). Confirm via limactl list before starting.
- Memory: bump the VM's Lima memory allocation to at least 12GiB. See provisioning options below.
- Workdir: temp/scout-nuius-repl/ (isolates from mayor/worker/other scouts).

How to provision a 12GiB VM:
Check if lima-node-5 exists (limactl list --json). If not, provisioning options:
(a) Prefer: scripts/worker-vm.sh start lima-node-5 127.0.0.1 10254 (if that helper exists and accepts memory override).
(b) Fall back: limactl create --name lima-node-5 lima/kubelet.yaml with memory override via --set.
(c) If lima-node-5 already exists with less memory: limactl stop lima-node-5 (if Running), limactl edit lima-node-5 to set memory to 12GiB in the persisted config, restart. limactl edit is out-of-band from the provisioner; no repo revert needed.
(d) LAST RESORT: temporarily edit lima/kubelet.yaml memory (from 4GiB to 12GiB), invoke scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --reset --stack-only --vm lima-node-5 --port 6447 --workdir ./temp/scout-nuius-repl --verbose, then REVERT lima/kubelet.yaml before returning.

Prefer (c) if lima-node-5 already exists, or (a)/(b) if it doesn't.

Custom plugin YAML for 6Gi request/limit:
sonobuoy's default e2e plugin has resources: empty-object. To set 6Gi req/limit, generate a custom plugin YAML:
   limactl shell lima-node-5 sudo sonobuoy gen plugin e2e --kubeconfig /tmp/sonobuoy-kubeconfig
Save that output to a file (e.g. /tmp/scout-nuius-repl-plugin.yaml inside the VM), then edit the e2e container's resources block to:
    resources:
      requests:
        memory: 6Gi
        cpu: 500m
      limits:
        memory: 6Gi
        cpu: 500m

Note: this makes the e2e container Guaranteed-scoped at the cgroup level. Sidecar remains resources:{}. Pod-level QoS will be Burstable (sonobuoy v0.57.3 cannot cap the sidecar per prior investigation).

Invoke sonobuoy with the plugin YAML and --procs=30 for the csi-hostpath focus. Escape the square brackets as ginkgo expects. Example (adjust the exact shell escaping as needed for your invocation form):
   limactl shell lima-node-5 sudo sonobuoy run -p /tmp/scout-nuius-repl-plugin.yaml --wait=false --kubeconfig /tmp/sonobuoy-kubeconfig --plugin-env=e2e.E2E_EXTRA_GINKGO_ARGS=--procs=30 --e2e-focus SQUARE-BRACKET Driver colon space csi-hostpath SQUARE-BRACKET-CLOSE

Test the invocation shape with sonobuoy status --kubeconfig /tmp/sonobuoy-kubeconfig first to confirm the pod is actually running.

Monitoring during the run:
Background sampler at 30s cadence capturing on lima-node-5:
- VM free -m -> available memory trajectory
- e2e-job cgroup memory.current, memory.peak, memory.stat (anon, file)
- Every 60s: ps -eo pid,rss,comm --sort=-rss top-20
- Every 60s: kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=spec.nodeName=lima-node-5 -o wide, count + brief list

Log to temp/e2e-memory-samples/scout-nuius-repl/samples.txt.

TIME BOUND: 45 min wall-clock. Upstream at --procs=30 completes csi-hostpath in ~30-60 min. Our u7s stack will likely fail most specs quickly. If the sonobuoy run is still going at 45 min, initiate sonobuoy delete and capture whatever data is there.

Findings to capture BEFORE writing the memo (save to temp/e2e-memory-samples/scout-nuius-repl/):
1. runner-lifecycle.txt: e2e-job pod's containerStatuses through time -- did it OOMKill? Did the ginkgo test suite complete? Did sonobuoy see a healthy plugin?
2. memory-trajectory.txt: your sampler output (already accumulating).
3. junit-summary.txt: post-run, retrieve the sonobuoy tarball and extract plugins/e2e/results/global/junit_01.xml. Grep for testcase counts + failure counts + skipped counts.
4. failures-list.txt: extract each testcase that has a failure child. Include the test name and a short line from the failure body. This is the payload the operator wants to review.
5. cluster-artifacts.txt: what pods existed at end-of-run (kubectl get pod -A), what namespaces persisted (kubectl get ns), any pods stuck Terminating.
6. dmesg-oom.txt (only if OOM fires): kernel OOM block.

Deliverable -- findings memo (under 800 words):

TL;DR: did the runner start? did it OOM? if it ran, what was the pass/fail rate?

Setup: vm memory, procs, sonobuoy invocation shape, plugin YAML resource shape.

Runner lifecycle: did e2e-job pod stay up for the whole run, or did it die mid-run? containerStatuses evidence.

Memory trajectory: peak memory.current, peak per-worker anon (if sampled), VM free-m low-water-mark, whether any OOM fired.

Test results breakdown: total specs, passed, failed, skipped -- and how long the run took.

Notable failing spec patterns: clusters of failures by root cause if visible: X tests all fail with 'VolumeSnapshotClasses not found', Y tests all fail with pod scheduled but never Ready, Z tests fail with CSIDriver missing capability foo, etc.

Sizing implications for u7s csi-hostpath support: data-locked answer: at N-parallel with M-Gi request the runner is stable; per-worker demand under this load was ~K MiB anon; upstream's 6Gi/30-parallel is/is not consistent with what u7s needs.

Recommended follow-ons (bead-sized items): list of concrete beads the operator could file post-review.

What I could NOT determine: be honest about limits.

Cleanup MANDATORY before return:
- sonobuoy delete --all --wait on lima-node-5
- Leave lima-node-5 Running (mayor decides teardown) but note whether operator-preferred to keep at 12GiB or revert to 4GiB
- If you edited lima/kubelet.yaml (option d), REVERT it before returning
- Confirm all listed data files landed under temp/e2e-memory-samples/scout-nuius-repl/ in the mayor checkout (path-leak check)

Cross-refs:
- Parent: mayor-nuius (root-cause scout, closed) + mayor-o4fmo (PR #1047 pending merge)
- Sibling: mayor-4dtlb (Phase-3 --procs override, blocked on #1047)
- Upstream reference (link at top)
- Prior sampled data: temp/e2e-memory-samples/ (multiple runs, all in mayor checkout, gitignored)

Peak e2e cgroup memory 5729 MiB (93% of 6Gi cap) at ~90s startup burst from 30-worker fan-out, then dropped to ~198 MiB at steady state -- matches mayor-nuius's finding that per-worker ramp is much higher than steady-state. VM-wide low-water was 1550MB free (~13% VM free), driven not by e2e-job cgroup but by ~20+ concurrent CSI-hostpathplugin StatefulSets across test namespaces. One ginkgo failure captured at 42.8s (multiVolume single-volume-concurrent-access) -- SAME test family that hit 20m0s in operator's procs=4 run, but under healthier stack conditions fails on real assertion in 43s. Junit not retrieved (scout stopped run early to stay in budget). Operational findings banked as memory: vm-memory-edit-requires-kubelet-reconnect-not-just-kcm-restart. title: feat(conformance): focus-conditional --procs override for storage-heavy focus patterns (f5sv4 Phase-3)
description:
Phase-3 of mayor-f5sv4. Now that Phase-1 (mayor-o4fmo, PR #1047) is verified and Phase-2 empirical bisect data has landed via mayor-nuius scout, Phase-3 is a small focus-conditional --procs override in 06-run-sonobuoy.sh.

## Data-locked sizing (from mayor-nuius scout, 2026-08-07)

- Per-worker ginkgo ramp-peak for csi-hostpath specs: 155-180 MiB anon-rss (tight spread across 16 independent workers).
- Steady-state settles to ~100 MiB/worker after initial setup phases finish.
- Phase-1 cap: 1 GiB on the e2e container.
- Safe --procs ceiling under the 1 GiB cap: 5-6 (1024 MiB / 180 MiB ≈ 5.7).
- Recommended: --procs=4 to leave headroom for occasional worker-heap spikes above 180 MiB during specific test types.

## Fix

Edit scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh's build_filter_args function to add a focus-conditional override:

    # Storage-heavy focus patterns need lower --procs to fit under the 1 GiB e2e cap.
    # See mayor-f5sv4 forensic + mayor-nuius scout: per-worker ginkgo ramp for these
    # specs is 155-180 MiB, so 16-way would need >2.5 GiB.
    PROCS=16
    if [[ "$FOCUS" =~ (Driver:[[:space:]]*csi-hostpath|Ephemeral|nfs3|VolumeSnapshot|Feature:VolumeSnapshotDataSource) ]]; then
      PROCS=4
    fi

Then substitute $PROCS into the two hardcoded '--procs=16' occurrences.

Also update scripts/conformance/test-all-e2e-timeout-logic.sh (shadow test) in lockstep.

## Focus regex justification

The scout memo shows StatefulSet+CSI-driver deployments amplify the memory pressure. The regex above covers:
- '[Driver: csi-hostpath]' — the direct forensic reproducer
- 'Ephemeral' — inline ephemeral volume tests deploy similar StatefulSet-like objects
- 'nfs3' — NFS driver family, similar sidecar count
- 'VolumeSnapshot' / 'Feature:VolumeSnapshotDataSource' — if we ever get snapshot support (mayor-cst7t)

If future test families surface a similar OOM pattern, extend the regex. Do NOT preemptively add patterns that haven't been measured to spike.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT change --procs for [Conformance] or --all-e2e paths.
- Do NOT add a new sonobuoy flag — this is a script-side computation.
- Do NOT touch the plugin YAML from Phase-1.

## Acceptance

- shellcheck 06-run-sonobuoy.sh clean
- shellcheck test-all-e2e-timeout-logic.sh clean
- Manual verification: launch with SONOBUOY_FOCUS='[Driver: csi-hostpath]' and confirm the sonobuoy invocation carries --procs=4 (via ps or the run's own log).
- Empirical: --focus '[Driver: csi-hostpath]' run must complete without OOMKill on the e2e container. Individual test specs may still fail for csi-hostpath-specific reasons (that's mayor-w44wg / mayor-5v9gl territory) but the JOB pod must not die.

## Depends on

- PR #1047 (mayor-o4fmo) MUST merge first — this bead assumes Phase-1's 1 GiB cap is in place.

## Cross-refs

- Parent: mayor-f5sv4 (closed)
- Sibling Phase-1: mayor-o4fmo / PR #1047 (pending merge)
- Sizing data: mayor-nuius (closed, findings in temp/e2e-memory-samples/scout-nuius/)
- Follow-on to investigate separately: BestEffort workload pod stacking on scheduler's least-loaded-by-requests node (u7s-wide, not csi-hostpath-specific)
notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-07 (post-scout-review): the scout memo mayor-nuius implied 'BestEffort scheduler stacking' was an amplifier. Cross-checked against commit f4c575d6 (fix scheduler spread by pod_count, landed 2026-08-04) AND against the scout's own pods-lima-node-4-at-oom.txt / pods-lima-node-smoke-at-oom.txt files: actual CSI StatefulSet distribution was 7 vs 6 (fair ~50/50 spread), scheduler is working correctly.
