title: Scout: root-cause csi-hostpath --procs=16 OOM mechanism (unexplained ~1.2GiB pressure gap)
description:
GOAL: root-cause the ~1.2GiB unexplained memory pressure that fires the CONSTRAINT_NONE global_oom on the e2e-job pod within ~42s of csi-hostpath focus start at --procs=16.

WHY THIS IS INTERESTING

Measured data-locked facts (2026-08-07 investigation, temp/e2e-memory-samples/):
- Conformance --procs=16: per-worker private-anon ~9 MiB, steady-state ~150 MiB total, no OOM.
- csi-hostpath --procs=4: per-worker private-anon ~100 MiB (Private_Dirty from smaps_rollup), steady-state ~440 MiB total, no OOM, VM shows ~600 MB free.
- csi-hostpath --procs=16: OOMKilled in ~42s. Kernel dmesg shows 19 processes killed, summed anon-rss 2780 MiB, constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE (system-wide OOM scan, not per-cgroup).
- Upstream reference (Kubernetes CI): 30-parallel csi-hostpath e2e-job uses 6Gi memory REQUESTS. https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-ci-logs/logs/ci-kubernetes-e2e-gce-cos-slow-beta/2063243433639677952

INCONSISTENCY

Linear extrapolation from --procs=4 (~440 MiB anon) predicts --procs=16 = ~1.6 GiB anon. Measured is 2.78 GiB summed at kill instant. **Delta of ~1.2 GiB is unexplained.** And more importantly: OOM fires under BestEffort/no-cap, so 'the cap fired' cannot be the explanation -- the VM as a WHOLE ran out (constraint=CONSTRAINT_NONE), not the pod's cgroup (which had no limit).

Candidate mechanisms (test empirically -- do NOT speculate):
(a) Per-worker anon RAMPS during startup to ~250-300 MiB before settling -- 16 workers × 250 MiB = 4 GiB pressure spike during ramp. --procs=4 doesn't hit this because the 4-worker ramp fits.
(b) Concurrent CSI-hostpathplugin StatefulSet deployments cause crio to spike memory during 16-parallel image pulls (each StatefulSet = 8 sidecars; 16 concurrent deployments = 128 concurrent image pulls). Not the e2e-job pod's own memory, but pressure that pushes the VM system-wide over the edge, and BestEffort e2e-job becomes the sacrificial oom_score victim.
(c) The test workload pods land on the same VM as the e2e-job (scheduler picks by requests-tally; BestEffort test pods add no tally weight so pile up), consuming meaningful RAM.
(d) Some combination of a+b+c.

EXPERIMENT DESIGN

Dispatch a worker to bring up a two-node stack (--stack-only, no fix -- BestEffort BASELINE), set up in-VM sampling, then launch csi-hostpath --procs=16 as a raw sonobuoy run. Sample at 5s cadence throughout the entire OOM-to-kill window (~42s). Capture:

1. **e2e-job pod's cgroup memory.current + memory.stat (anon, file, kernel)** every 5s.
2. **Per-e2e.test PID smaps_rollup Private_Dirty** every 5s (shows per-worker ramp trajectory).
3. **VM-wide ** every 5s (proves whether it's system-wide pressure or pod-specific).
4. **Top-10 processes VM-wide by RSS** every 15s (catches crio/kubelet/other spikes).
5. **crio journal for image-pull activity** during the OOM window.
6. **Namespaces created (kubectl get ns) at 5s intervals** -- shows workload deployment rate.
7. **dmesg -T --time-format iso** for the OOM instant, capture the constraint= line, oom-victim rank, and rss_anon of the top-N processes VM-wide right before OOM (kernel logs oom_score_adj + rss for every process in scope).

DELIVERABLE (findings memo)

A memo that DEFINITIVELY answers:
- Was OOM triggered by e2e-job's own cgroup ramp, or by system-wide pressure from concurrent workload?
- Which of (a)/(b)/(c)/(d) above is dominant, with dmesg + free-m trajectory as evidence.
- What's the actual peak per-worker Private_Dirty during the ramp (not just at kill instant)?
- How much of the VM's total ~3.8 GiB was consumed by non-e2e-job processes at OOM time?
- Given the upstream 6Gi request precedent: does the mechanism suggest we should size Phase-1 differently (larger cap, adaptive to VM size), or would a --procs reduction address the root cause more cleanly?

CONSTRAINTS

- Do NOT edit any code. Read-only investigation.
- Do NOT modify the fix branch (--reset expected).
- Do NOT run --focus '[Conformance]' -- that's already measured.
- Assigned VM: worker's own two-node slot (mayor to assign at dispatch time). Isolate from operator/mayor VMs.
- Time bound: 45 min wall-clock from dispatch. If the OOM doesn't reproduce in one attempt, capture what happened + report back rather than retry forever.

CROSS-REFS

- mayor-f5sv4 (closed): original forensic
- mayor-o4fmo (PR #1047 pending): Phase-1 fix
- mayor-sc0h5: imagePullPolicy anchor for future pods.rs cluster (unrelated but recent memory pattern)
- Upstream: 6Gi request precedent (link above)
- Prior sampled data: temp/e2e-memory-samples/{samples.txt,anon-samples.txt,csi-hostpath-verify/,csi-hostpath-procs4/} (all in mayor's checkout, gitignored)
close_reason: Scout complete. Root cause: (a) per-worker ginkgo ramp is dominant magnitude driver (~155-180 MiB/worker at startup ramp, tight spread across all 16); the 'unexplained 1.2 GiB' was an artifact of comparing procs=4 steady-state (~100 MiB/worker) against procs=16 ramp-peak — like-for-like both are ~177 MiB/worker. (c) workload-pod co-location is amplifier: 7 of 13 csi-hostpath StatefulSets scheduled onto e2e-job's own node (BestEffort pods contribute 0 to scheduler tally, so they stack). (b) crio image-pull NOT supported (StatefulSets ready in 40-50s, images pre-pulled). Triggering allocator was kube-proxy iptables (oom_score_adj=-999), proving VM system-wide OOM. Findings memo captured in temp/e2e-memory-samples/scout-nuius/ (dmesg-oom.txt, dmesg-vmwide-proclist.txt, pods-*.txt). Phase-1 cap fixes containment, not magnitude; Phase-3 --procs bisect target is 5-6 (1GiB cap / 180 MiB per-worker ramp).

title: kubectl describe node returns incorrect/unfiltered pod list (same list shown for all nodes)
description:
Observed 2026-08-07 during csi-hostpath OOM investigation on lima-node + lima-node-3.

'kubectl describe node <name>' shows the same pod list for both nodes -- almost certainly the same unfiltered result regardless of which node was named. This is a real u7s apiserver bug.

Expected upstream behavior (kubectl describe node): the Non-terminated Pods section is filtered to just the pods whose spec.nodeName equals the described node. kubectl fetches pods with a fieldSelector like 'spec.nodeName=<name>,status.phase!=Failed,status.phase!=Succeeded' or similar.

Likely mechanism (candidates -- needs a scout to root-cause):
1. Field selector on spec.nodeName is silently ignored by the pods LIST handler (same 'silent no-op filter' bug class as mayor-pgm5q's field-selector issue documented in memory 'silent-noop-filter-looks-like-flaky-timing').
2. The FieldSelector parser accepts the selector but the actual filter isn't applied.
3. Some intermediate transformation (e.g. sonobuoy proxy, kubectl-side reduction) that we don't own -- less likely.

Reproduction:
- Bring up a two-node stack (lima-node + lima-node-3).
- Deploy some pods scheduled to different nodes.
- kubectl --kubeconfig ./temp/u7s/kubeconfig describe node lima-node > /tmp/describe-1.txt
- kubectl --kubeconfig ./temp/u7s/kubeconfig describe node lima-node-3 > /tmp/describe-2.txt
- diff /tmp/describe-1.txt /tmp/describe-2.txt (or eyeball the Non-terminated Pods sections)

Scout steps:
- Confirm the mechanism -- capture 'kubectl -v=9 describe node <name>' to see the exact API URL kubectl issues (specifically, whether the LIST request contains a fieldSelector), then grep the apiserver log for that request-id.
- If apiserver receives a fieldSelector on spec.nodeName and returns unfiltered results -> classic no-op filter bug in pods list handler.
- Cross-ref existing memories: 'silent-noop-filter-looks-like-flaky-timing' (mayor-pgm5q 2026-07-23 lesson).
- Cross-ref existing bead: mayor-tv4ob (CR watch field-selector, needs cross-version conversion in watch path).

Scope: apiserver fix only. Fail-on-revert regression test: LIST pods with fieldSelector=spec.nodeName=X must return only pods whose spec.nodeName=X.

Discovered while running temp/e2e/... csi-hostpath investigation on 2026-08-07 (operator quote: 'kubectl describe node has an incorrect list of pods (or rather, the same possibly unfiltered list for all nodes). This is definitely our bug that needs fixing.').
close_reason: Audit closed 2026-08-07. Shape 3 audit (scout agent-a40060153c1ac9cf5) root-caused deterministically via code trace + upstream verification. Bug is in core_list_resource's plain-LIST branch (core.rs:133-178) using single-term parse_field_selector against kubectl's multi-term selector 'spec.nodeName=X,status.phase!=Succeeded,status.phase!=Failed', producing a bogus split that matches nothing → negated → everything matches. Filed follow-on fix bead (P1 upgrade from original P2 per scout — core kubectl command silently wrong + cross-tenant exposure risk). Watch/sendInitialEvents branch two branches above already uses the correct pattern — fix is one call-site swap. See successor bead for full evidence chain + fix shape.

title: Type build_aggregated_discovery in handlers/discovery.rs: reuse the file's already-existing APIGroup/ApiResourceList typed structs (typed-struct EPIC child 2, cheapest migration in scope)
description:
PARENT

mayor-0bd14 typed-struct EPIC Phase-3 second child. Discovered by Phase-1 scout ai/findings/typed-struct-migration-scoping-2026-08-06.md as the cheapest migration in the entire EPIC — typed scaffolding already exists.

THE SURPRISE

crates/apiserver/src/handlers/discovery.rs already has typed APIGroup / ApiResourceList structs in-file (used at lines 165-260). But the newer build_aggregated_discovery function (lines 288-347, target of mayor-k3pxp discovery-cache bead) bypasses them entirely and rebuilds via raw serde_json::json! macros. Same file, same domain types, ~120 lines apart. Retrofit is straightforward.

WHY THIS IS CHEAP

- Typed scaffolding already exists in-file (APIGroup, ApiResourceList): no new type definitions needed
- Migration is local to one function: build_aggregated_discovery lines 288-347, maybe ~60 LoC of production code
- No new dep
- No wire-format changes: the typed structs already round-trip against real clients (used at lines 165-260 for non-aggregated discovery today)

INTERACTION WITH mayor-k3pxp / mayor-ppcwt

The discovery cache work has TWO complementary paths now:
1. **This bead**: type the assembly, dropping the constant-per-call cost of json! + Value construction
2. **mayor-k3pxp**: cache the assembled result (currently blocked on mayor-ppcwt pre-work for counter + APIService safety design)

Both individually reduce discovery-request cost. Together they compound. But: this bead's migration ALSO shrinks the marginal value of mayor-k3pxp's cache — if per-call cost drops significantly, the cache-hit vs cache-miss delta narrows. That's fine (still a win overall), just something to flag in mayor-k3pxp's re-scoping once this lands.

Recommended order:
1. mayor-ppcwt (discovery counter + APIService safety decision) — pre-work
2. THIS bead (type build_aggregated_discovery) — cheap standalone win  
3. Re-measure via the new counter to see if per-call cost is now low enough that caching is unnecessary
4. mayor-k3pxp cache: dispatch only if step 3 shows cache is still needed

WHAT TO PRODUCE

1. Migrate build_aggregated_discovery (lines 288-347) to construct APIGroup / ApiResourceList instances directly instead of building serde_json::Value trees via json! macros
2. If any fields are needed that the existing typed structs do not cover, extend them (in-file, following the existing pattern) — do NOT split them into a new module
3. Regression tests: build_aggregated_discovery produces byte-identical JSON output to the pre-migration version for a fixed input set. Simplest form: golden-file test with a snapshot of the pre-migration output
4. Fail-on-revert: revert to the json!-macro path, snapshot-test should fail (typed path produces different output ordering? if so, that's the fail signal; adjust the assertion or the migration to preserve exact ordering — Kubernetes discovery responses may have implicit ordering conventions worth preserving)

NON-GOALS

- Do NOT implement mayor-k3pxp's cache — separate bead, separate concern, blocked on mayor-ppcwt anyway
- Do NOT touch handlers/defaults.rs (sibling child bead mayor-ds8hb handles that)
- Do NOT change wire format
- Do NOT change semantics of what discovery returns

VERIFICATION

- cargo test --workspace green
- Cargo clippy clean
- Existing discovery tests continue to pass
- Reverse-fail as described above
- Optional post-merge: dhat re-run should show build_aggregated_discovery drop as a serde_json::Value allocator

CROSS-REFS

- Parent: mayor-0bd14 typed-struct EPIC
- Phase-1 scout: ai/findings/typed-struct-migration-scoping-2026-08-06.md (this is §5 the surprise finding)
- Sibling child bead: mayor-ds8hb defaulting typed migration
- Related open: mayor-k3pxp discovery cache (BLOCKED on mayor-ppcwt), mayor-ppcwt discovery pre-work (P2)
- Related closed: mayor-e555b PR #1038 (recent example of minimal-field-deserialize with existing typed scaffolding)

Shape-1 solo. Estimated ~60 LoC production code plus ~50-100 LoC tests. Cheapest migration in the EPIC — recommended to ship soon to prove the pattern is tractable and provide a datapoint before larger cluster migrations.

title: Type crates/apiserver/src/handlers/defaults.rs default_X functions: replace serde_json::Value wrangling with typed structs (typed-struct EPIC child 1)
description:
PARENT

mayor-0bd14 typed-struct EPIC Phase-3 first child. Scope + prerequisite decisions came from ai/findings/typed-struct-migration-scoping-2026-08-06.md Phase-1 scout.

WHY THIS ONE FIRST

Direct lineage to a real shipped bug: commit 7db94f0c mayor-xv1pk imagePullPolicy silent mis-defaulting (PR #1024 merged). That bug happened SPECIFICALLY because the defaulting code path wrangled a serde_json::Value tree and a field the apiserver was supposed to reason about got silently dropped. This is the exact bug class the operator's typing-guideline exists to prevent.

Each default_X function is independently shallow and testable. 119 grep-hits in defaults.rs (per Phase-1 scout §2, cluster row 1). ~250 LoC of production code change.

DIRECTION

Extend the existing crates/apiserver/src/types.rs module. NOT add k8s-openapi dep. Per Phase-2 operator decision 2026-08-06.

types.rs already has the pattern in use:
- ObjectMeta, PodSpec, NamespaceStatus etc. with minimal typed fields
- #[serde(flatten)] rest: Value on structs where passthrough of unknown fields is desired
- Borrowed lifetimes where possible for zero-copy (see PR #1038 mayor-e555b for a recent auth.rs example)

Extend types.rs with typed structs for each resource-type the default_X functions currently touch as a Value tree. Then migrate each default_X call site to use the typed struct.

WHAT TO PRODUCE

1. **Typed structs for the resources defaulted**: Pod, Service, Deployment, PVC, ConfigMap, Secret, ReplicaSet, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job, CronJob — whatever the default_X functions in defaults.rs actually operate on. Grep defaults.rs to enumerate the full set. Do NOT type resources that are not defaulted here; scope creep kills EPICs.

2. **For each typed struct**: minimal fields the defaulting logic reasons about. Everything else via #[serde(flatten)] rest: Value. This preserves wire-format compatibility across all clients — un-referenced fields pass through untouched.

3. **Migrate each default_X function** to take the typed struct (or Option<TypedStruct>) instead of navigating a Value tree. The function signature may need to change; that ripples to callers. Handle the ripple — should be localized to handlers/*.rs.

4. **Regression tests per typed struct**: (a) fields the default_X function reads round-trip correctly, (b) fields it does NOT read but exist in real k8s wire format pass through via the rest: Value catch-all, (c) missing-required-field behavior matches upstream Kubernetes.

5. **Fail-on-revert test for the imagePullPolicy bug specifically**: construct a Pod with a container that has an empty imagePullPolicy, run through defaulting, assert the result has imagePullPolicy correctly set per upstream semantics. This test would have caught the mayor-xv1pk bug pre-merge if it had existed.

NON-GOALS

- Do NOT touch handlers/discovery.rs (sibling child bead mayor-<Y> handles that).
- Do NOT touch other clusters from the Phase-1 scout (14 clusters total; this bead is cluster 1 only).
- Do NOT add k8s-openapi or any other crate dep.
- Do NOT change wire format — every field currently accepted must still deserialize, every field currently emitted must still emit.
- Do NOT change semantics of any default_X function — this is a type-safety migration, not a behavior change.

VERIFICATION

- cargo test --workspace green.
- Cargo clippy clean.
- Existing defaulting tests continue to pass (may need mechanical updates for new signatures).
- Reverse-fail: revert one default_X (say default_pod_spec) to Value-wrangling, re-run tests, assert new typed test fires. Restore, assert pass.
- Optional post-merge A/B: dhat re-run should show reduced serde_json::Value allocations in the defaulting call chain.

CROSS-REFS

- Parent: mayor-0bd14 typed-struct EPIC
- Phase-1 scout: ai/findings/typed-struct-migration-scoping-2026-08-06.md
- Direct-lineage bug: mayor-xv1pk PR #1024 (silent imagePullPolicy defaulting drop)
- Sibling child bead: mayor-<Y> discovery typing (filed separately)
- Related closed: mayor-e555b PR #1038 (recent minimal-field-deserialize example in auth.rs)
- Bd memory: typing-guideline-no-raw-json-for-reasoned-fields (the original rule)

Shape-1 solo. Estimated ~250 LoC production code plus ~150-300 LoC tests.
close_reason: PR #1046 opened: 19 typed structs added to types.rs, 17 default_X functions migrated in defaults.rs, all 116 pre-existing tests pass unmodified + 10 new wire-format-passthrough tests, reverse-fail verified. Scope finding flagged in PR body: imagePullPolicy anchor bug (PR #1024) lives in handlers/pods.rs (Phase-1 scout cluster 6, deferred own EPIC child), not defaults.rs (cluster 1) -- substituted with an equivalent fail-on-revert test against defaults.rs's own bug class (CSIDriver rest passthrough) instead of expanding scope into pods.rs. CI wall (GHActions outage) not caused by this PR.

title: Discovery pre-work: add u7s_discovery_build_total counter + resolve APIService-token-forwarding cache-safety before mayor-k3pxp dispatch
description:
SIGNAL

Discovery-endpoint usage scout (ai/findings/discovery-endpoint-usage-metrics-2026-08-06.md, agent ace43a8a82bc8a52e) surfaced two blockers that must resolve BEFORE mayor-k3pxp dispatches its cache implementation:

BLOCKER 1: NO METRIC COVERAGE
/api, /apis, /discovery/v2 (every route reaching build_aggregated_discovery) are in is_exempt at crates/apiserver/src/auth.rs:665-680. AuthService::call returns early for exempt paths (auth.rs:997-1000) BEFORE the record_request_total call site fires. Result: apiserver_request_total has ZERO series for these routes.

Consequence: mayor-k3pxp cannot land with a verifiable hit-rate assertion in its PR body. We would be shipping a cache with no way to measure whether it works.

BLOCKER 2: SECURITY HAZARD FROM CALLER-TOKEN FORWARDING
discovery.rs:280-284 forwards the caller's own bearer token to APIService-backed groups so the backend can enforce per-caller authorization on the group's discovery response. The 0806-1102 run registered a live APIService (v1alpha1.wardle.example.com).

A naive shared cache keyed on (discovery_version, include_core) would leak one caller's backend-authorized discovery result to a different caller — a real cross-user data leak, prohibitive risk per operator (2026-08-06 direct quote: 'That is a prohibitive risk.').

Any mayor-k3pxp cache design must EITHER:
- Cache only the core-groups portion (which uses no caller-token forwarding) and pass APIService-backed groups through per-request, OR
- Key the cache on (caller-token-hash, ...) so each caller gets its own entry, OR
- Bypass the cache entirely when any APIService is registered, OR
- Some hybrid the pre-work should explicitly propose and the operator explicitly approve

FIX SPECIFICATION

Two-part pre-work, one PR:

Part 1: Add u7s_discovery_build_total counter.
File: crates/apiserver/src/metrics.rs. Register a new IntCounterVec with labels {version, include_core, has_apiservice}. IntCounterVec register pattern already established (see WATCH_BROADCAST_RECEIVERS, apiserver_watch_events_total, etc.). Increment inside build_aggregated_discovery at crates/apiserver/src/handlers/discovery.rs:288-347 on every call.

Rationale for the specific labels:
- version: which discovery-endpoint variant fired (/api vs /apis vs /discovery/v2 vs a versioned /apis/GROUP/VERSION)
- include_core: whether the response included the core /api/v1 group (potentially different rate distribution vs GROUP-only variants)
- has_apiservice: whether any APIService was registered at call time (cache-safety-relevant per Blocker 2)

Part 2: Document the APIService-cache-safety decision.
Add a code comment at the top of build_aggregated_discovery (before line 288) documenting the caller-token-forwarding constraint AND the deliberate cache-design decision (WHICH of the four options above we chose and why). This is not a runtime enforcement, it is a durable record so a future mayor implementing mayor-k3pxp does not accidentally reintroduce the leak.

Also update mayor-k3pxp's bead body to reference this pre-work and require the cache design to match the documented decision.

TESTS

- Basic unit: register the counter, call build_aggregated_discovery, assert counter incremented with the expected label values.
- No behavioral test for the doc comment.

VERIFICATION

Post-merge, an operator-run 20min certified-conformance suite would populate the counter and let us measure baseline discovery request rate (invocations, distribution across labels) BEFORE mayor-k3pxp caches anything. That baseline becomes the point-of-comparison for mayor-k3pxp's PR to prove the cache actually reduces calls.

CROSS-REFS

- Scout: ai/findings/discovery-endpoint-usage-metrics-2026-08-06.md
- Blocked bead: mayor-k3pxp discovery-doc caching (do NOT dispatch until this pre-work merges + operator sees the counter data from a subsequent run)
- Related: mayor-atemy.1 PR #896 (established the metrics.rs register pattern), mayor-xs7hq PR #932/#933 (generic AuthLayer wiring — which EXPLICITLY exempts discovery, that's how we got here)
- Prior scout doc for the security decision: ai/findings/discovery-endpoint-usage-metrics-2026-08-06.md section 3

Shape-1 solo. LoC: ~30-50 (counter register + increment call + doc comment + one test). No new dep.
close_reason: PR opened at https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/1045; discovery counter + cache-safety doc pre-work complete, mayor-k3pxp bead updated to reference this.

title: Recapture dhat with deeper backtrace to attribute the residual 6.6% (~1.12 GB) of unlabeled churn
description:
SIGNAL

Real dhat profile of 0806-1102 conformance run (ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06-run.md, PID 27958, 60.5min) showed a 4.46GB 'depth-truncated recursion' bucket. Dhat truncates the recorded call stack at a fixed depth by default, so any recursive or deeply-nested code paths collapse into one anonymous rollup.

4.46GB is a large fraction of the total ~19GB dhat-observed churn. If we could de-anonymize that bucket, we would know whether we are looking at a distinct hot subsystem (e.g. deep serde recursion, deep async chain, deep tokio task tree) or just the fatter tail of already-visible callsites.

FIX

Recapture dhat with a higher max-backtrace depth. The dhat crate exposes DHAT_MAX_STACK env var (or its Rust API equivalent), default is 12 frames. Bump to 50-100.

Options for delivering this:
1. Bump the default via crates/apiserver/src/main.rs's dhat::Profiler::builder chain
2. Add a --features dhat-deep Cargo feature that swaps the profiler config
3. Set via env when invoking run-all.sh --binary target/release/u7s-apiserver

Prefer option 1 or 2. Env is fragile.

INTERACTION WITH mayor-vnun4 / mayor-2pio7 (dhat harness bugs)

Do NOT recapture dhat until either those bugs are fixed OR the recapture is done with the operator alongside to manually SIGTERM the apiserver at end-of-run (as they did for run 0806-1102 to produce the good dhat file). Otherwise the recapture may produce the 2.6-second Phase 1 file, wasting the run.

DELIVERABLE

Bump the depth setting via option 1 or 2, then dispatch a new dhat-instrumented conformance run (operator time, iterable at 20 min), then a follow-on scout to re-triage focusing on the previously-truncated 4.46GB bucket.

CROSS-REFS

- Findings: ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06-run.md
- Prior harness bugs: mayor-vnun4 two-phase-startup, mayor-2pio7 missing SIGTERM
- Related profiling tooling landscape: ai/findings/rust-profiling-tooling-survey-2026-08-06.md

Shape-1 for the depth-config change. Follow-on scout separate.

Priority P3 because we already have enough actionable data from the current dhat profile to fill the perf-fix roadmap; de-anonymizing the truncated bucket is a nice-to-have that unlocks more roadmap items but does not block current ones.
notes:
REWRITTEN 2026-08-06: original bead body cited a fabricated 4.46 GB figure. Corrected to the actual residual.

CORRECTED SIGNAL

Real dhat profile of 0806-1102 conformance run (ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06-run.md, PID 27958, 60.5min) categorized ~93.4% of total 17 GB cumulative churn across 7 named subsystems (serde_json 44.2%, h2/hyper 16.8%, rustls 8.6%, watch/ndjson_bookmark 8.2%, u7s_store/sqlite 7.2%, jsonwebtoken 4.4%, num_bigint_dig 4.0%).

Residual: 17.0 GB - 15.88 GB categorized = ~1.12 GB (6.6%) unattributed. This is where dhat's default 12-frame stack truncation loses attribution — the residual is likely a mix of:
- Deep serde-recursion sub-frames that flatten into 'other'
- Deep tokio async-chain sub-frames from the request pipeline
- Deep hyper/h2 sub-frames below the categorized top
- Genuine small callsites that don't cluster into any of the 7 named buckets

OPERATOR JUSTIFICATION 2026-08-06

'We did consider the JWT cache for a <5% CPU improvement. Investigating 6%+ of memory is worth it.'

title: EPIC: restore the typing-guideline discipline: replace serde_json::Value handler-logic with typed structs (94.5 percent of JSON allocation bytes come from this)
description:
PROJECT GUIDELINE (from operator, standing rule, restated 2026-08-06):

If the apiserver has LOGIC about something, that thing must be PROPERLY TYPED end-to-end. Flow it through typed structs. No wrangling serde_json::Value in logic. Raw-map access is acceptable ONLY for pure passthrough fields the apiserver never reasons about.

This rule was set early in u7s history (bd memory typing-guideline-no-raw-json-for-reasoned-fields, banked 2026-06-26). It has been repeatedly forgotten. Every rediscovery of it has been triggered by a bug where JSON-map defaulting or validation silently dropped a field the apiserver was supposed to reason about (e.g. enableServiceLinks 2026-06-26).

Now measured at scale: mayor-7e8jf JSON serde scout (ai/findings/json-serde-optimization-scoping-2026-08-06.md) documented that 94.5 percent of ALL apiserver JSON allocation bytes come from serde_json::Value tree allocations (Object.body = Value at crates/apiserver/src/types.rs:639-642, propagated across 91 call sites). This is BOTH a correctness risk AND a perf tax.

The typing-guideline was violated across most of the apiserver's storage plus middleware layers. Restoring it is a substantial engineering effort.

SCOPE (umbrella, needs child breakdown)

This bead is an EPIC. Its purpose is to scope + plan + eventually track the child beads. Actual implementation work happens in the children.

Phase 1: SCOUT to identify the hot-path callsites that most need typed migration
- Read the JSON serde scout doc top-N list plus the discovery scout results
- Rank callsites by (allocation cost) x (correctness risk if the Value structure changes underneath us)
- Group into work-sized child beads (probably 5-15 children total)
- Deliverable: ai/findings/typed-struct-migration-scoping-2026-08-06.md
- Explicitly out-of-scope for the scout: DO NOT propose full type schemas for every group, DO NOT enumerate every one of the 91 Object.body call sites. Focus on the hot paths where typed-struct migration will PROVABLY help.

Phase 2: OPERATOR PRIORITIZATION
- Which child beads land in what order
- Which are 'nice to have' vs 'correctness-critical'
- Which get shipped as Shape-1 solos vs bundled Shape-2 clusters

Phase 3: IMPLEMENTATION CHILDREN
- Each child implements typed structs for one specific handler / middleware / codec
- Each ships with: typed struct definitions, Serialize/Deserialize impls (borrowed where possible for zero-copy), migration of call sites to use them, tests that would fail if a field silently dropped

WHAT THIS EPIC IS NOT

- NOT a Value-tree elimination project. Value has legitimate uses for genuinely-generic data (e.g. CRD validation, apply-patch merge). Do NOT propose to remove Value entirely from the codebase.
- NOT a prost/protobuf migration. u7s is JSON-only by design (bd memory content-type-determines-decode-path documents the choice). This EPIC does not change wire format.
- NOT time-boxed. Correctness first. Perf gains are the incidental win. Do not rush.

CROSS-REFS

- Bd memory typing-guideline-no-raw-json-for-reasoned-fields (2026-06-26 - the original rule)
- Bd memory dispatch-proto-decode-drop-check (2026-08-06 - documents the class of bugs typed-migration prevents)
- Scout: ai/findings/json-serde-optimization-scoping-2026-08-06.md (the measurement that made this actionable at scale)
- Sibling perf beads that address specific hot paths: mayor-g7g2m (content_type dead parse - Shape-1 quick win), mayor-e555b (auth::object_is_live minimal-field), mayor-k3pxp (discovery-doc caching)

STARTING POINT

File this EPIC. Dispatch Phase-1 scout when the operator is ready. Do not implement anything under this EPIC directly - only file/track child beads.
notes:
GREP-VERIFIED CORRECTION 2026-08-06 (per bd memory statistics-from-findings-docs-must-be-grep-verified-never-recited):

Original bead body cited 91 call sites paraphrased from the JSON serde scout. That figure came from a dhat-backtrace-derived count (10-frame-truncated), NOT a source grep. Actual source-verified numbers:
- Object::from_bytes() literal analog to the pattern: 61 sites across 11 files
- serde_json::Value identifier raw grep: 3139 occurrences
- Of those, 1605 (51%) live in generated *_gen_adapter.rs files — out of scope
- Real actionable surface: ~1534 occurrences across 34 files

Scope is roughly a third narrower than the original bead framing suggested. Good news for feasibility.

PHASE-1 SCOUT COMPLETE

ai/findings/typed-struct-migration-scoping-2026-08-06.md (agent ab3881d00af6741c8, closed) enumerated 14 clusters and recommended:
- Top-1 migration: defaulting logic (handlers/defaults.rs, 119 grep-hits, ~250 LoC) — direct lineage to commit 7db94f0c mayor-xv1pk imagePullPolicy silent mis-defaulting shipped bug
- Prerequisite: extend the existing types.rs module (NOT add k8s-openapi dep). Rationale: types.rs already has ObjectMeta/PodSpec/NamespaceStatus with the minimal-field + #[serde(flatten)] rest: Value pattern
- Genuine surprise: handlers/discovery.rs already has typed APIGroup/ApiResourceList structs in-file (lines 165-260), but build_aggregated_discovery (lines 288-347) bypasses them entirely — CHEAPEST migration in scope, typed scaffolding already exists

PHASE-2 DECISION 2026-08-06

Operator approved:
- Defaulting migration (first child): mayor-<X> to be filed
- Discovery migration (second child, the surprise finding): mayor-<Y> to be filed
- Approach: hand-rolled types.rs extension, no k8s-openapi
- Dispatch pattern: two child beads in parallel if surfaces are disjoint (defaults.rs vs discovery.rs are — verified)

OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS EPIC

- Reserved: pure passthrough Value uses (managedFields, apply-patch, CRD custom-resource bodies with unknown-at-compile-time schemas, aggregated APIService proxy responses) — those legitimately require generic Value
- Not in scope: the 51% of Value grep-hits inside *_gen_adapter.rs boundary code (already-typed prost structs converted to Value only for wire encoding)

STATUS

Phase-1 done. Phase-3 (implementation) starts with children being dispatched. This EPIC stays open as the umbrella.

title: Reduce SqliteStore RING_CAPACITY from 100k to 10k: measured 20k ring-pushes across full 60min conformance run means 100k is 5x overkill
description:
SIGNAL

Real dhat measurement of the 0806-1102 conformance run (60.5 min including 20 min idle, per ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06-run.md and follow-on ai/findings/stamp-resource-version-growth-investigation-2026-08-06.md) confirmed:

- SqliteStore ring is a VecDeque with RING_CAPACITY = 100_000 (crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:20)
- Actual ring-pushes across the FULL 60min run: approximately 20,229 (about 5.6 pushes per second sustained)
- The ring never evicted a single entry - well under the 100k cap

Consequence: the 27.55MB max-live at eb==mb we saw in dhat is NOT a leak but IS an over-provisioned bounded structure. 5x more capacity than the sustained load requires.

Operator direction 2026-08-06: reduce to 10k and prove the necessity of anything larger with hard data before restoring.

FIX

crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:20 - change RING_CAPACITY from 100_000 to 10_000. Update the accompanying doc comment (currently sqlite.rs:16 mentions ~100-200 MB eventual ceiling - this becomes ~10-20 MB).

WHY THIS IS SAFE

The ring serves watch-replay for late-arriving or reconnecting watchers. A watcher missing more than RING_CAPACITY events past the last-seen resource-version gets a 410 GONE and re-lists.

Question the fix must answer with the reverse-fail test: does a 10k cap trigger 410s under normal conformance load? Answer projected from measurement: no. Sustained rate was 5.6 events/sec. A 10k ring holds approximately 29 minutes of history at that rate - far longer than a normal watch-reconnect gap.

TESTS

- Regression: reproduce the eviction path by generating >10k events and verifying pop_front fires correctly.
- Live: full conformance suite run under the new cap, confirm 0 watch 410-Gone responses fired due to ring-truncation. If any 410s fire, that IS evidence the cap needs to be higher and the exact rate observed becomes the sizing data.

If the conformance run trips any 410s under 10k, the resulting bead should be filed as a companion: which specific watch scenario needed more, and what is the observed minimum sufficient cap. Then either restore to a smaller than 100k value backed by that data, OR implement Stage-2 sharding (mayor-drs2a) which would give per-resource-type rings each much smaller than the current global 100k.

RISK

Low-medium. If load spikes beyond 20k events in a 30sec window (~333 events/sec, ~60x observed sustained rate), the ring may evict live-watched events under peak burst. But: the current 100k cap only helps if that burst persists for MORE THAN 30 minutes - a plausible upper-tail cap of 30 minutes of burst history is 600k events, and our 100k already fails to cover THAT hypothetical - so we are not currently defending against sustained bursts, just against short bursts. 10k covers short bursts up to ~30 seconds at 333 events/sec, or ~29 minutes at observed sustained rate. Either bound seems reasonable for u7s pre-alpha.

VERIFICATION

Full conformance suite (iterable at 20min per bd memory conformance-suite-is-iterable-for-profiling-purposes) with the new cap. Zero 410-Gone from watch handlers.

CROSS-REFS

- ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06-run.md (top-1 by max-live: stamp_resource_version -> put_sync 27.55MB, in the ring)
- ai/findings/stamp-resource-version-growth-investigation-2026-08-06.md (verifies ring is the retention structure, not a leak)
- Related but distinct: mayor-drs2a Stage-2 (per-resource-type sharding). If we go with 10k global THEN Stage-2 becomes 10k-per-shard vs 100k-per-shard - much smaller design margin.
- Prior context: mayor-jzlon 2026-08-03 bumped RING_CAPACITY 1k -> 100k for 16-way conformance retention. That bump was speculative given actual measurement now available.

Shape-1 solo dispatch. Minimal LoC change plus regression test.
close_reason: PR #1037 opened: reduced RING_CAPACITY 100k -> 10k with pinned regression test

title: discovery::build_aggregated_discovery: cache the assembled discovery doc with CRD/APIService invalidation
description:
SIGNAL

JSON serde scout ai/findings/json-serde-optimization-scoping-2026-08-06.md identified this as one of three top-3 callsites (per companion beads mayor-g7g2m and mayor-e555b) accounting for 20.7 percent of allocation bytes and 27.7 percent of events in the 0806-1102 conformance run.

- File: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/discovery.rs, function build_aggregated_discovery, lines 288-347.
- Behavior: constructs the full aggregated /apis/... discovery response as a serde_json::Value tree by walking every registered API group and version. Called on every /apis or /api discovery request.
- Waste: the discovery doc changes only when a CRD or APIService is created, updated, or deleted. Between changes it is identical bytes but the function re-builds the Value tree per request.
- Discovery-request rate in conformance is high because every client fresh-starts through discovery.

FIX

Wrap the current build_aggregated_discovery in a cache:

    Arc<RwLock<Option<CachedDiscoveryDoc>>>

Structure of CachedDiscoveryDoc:

    struct CachedDiscoveryDoc {
        content_type_variants: HashMap<AcceptType, Bytes>,  // pre-serialized bytes per Accept negotiation
        version: u64,  // increments on invalidation
    }

Or a simpler variant: cache a single serde_json::Value once and only re-render bytes per request. The bytes-cache is faster but requires knowing the Accept variants; the Value-cache is safer and still saves the tree-construction.

Invalidation: bump a version counter on any CRD create/update/delete AND on any APIService create/update/delete. Cache-hit checks version, cache-miss triggers rebuild.

Implementation notes:
- Cache location: on AppState alongside sa_sig_cache from mayor-6sbvc (state.rs).
- Precedent for RwLock<HashMap> cache pattern: state.rs:149 AdmissionConfigCache.
- Concurrency: reads dominate writes 1000:1 (like the SA sig cache), so std::sync::RwLock (not tokio) is right.
- Do NOT introduce a new dep unless there is a clear reason.

TESTS

- Discovery request returns identical bytes to un-cached version.
- Creating a CRD invalidates the cache (next request rebuilds).
- Concurrent requests during a rebuild block-then-read-current, no torn state.
- Fail-on-revert: instrument a rebuild counter, assert it stays at 1 across N repeated requests. Restore the naive per-request build and confirm the counter climbs.

VERIFICATION

Cargo tests green. Optional dhat A/B: build_aggregated_discovery drops from top-N JSON allocators post-merge.

CROSS-REFS

- Scout: ai/findings/json-serde-optimization-scoping-2026-08-06.md
- Precedent for cache pattern: state.rs:149 AdmissionConfigCache
- Sibling bead: mayor-6sbvc PR #1034 (SA sig cache, same pattern, different subsystem)

Shape-1 solo dispatch. Slightly larger scope than mayor-g7g2m or mayor-e555b - probably 60-100 LoC total including cache module + invalidation hooks + tests.
notes: BLOCKER (Part 1) resolved by mayor-ppcwt PR https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/1045: u7s_discovery_build_total counter (IntCounterVec{version, include_core, has_apiservice}) now measures discovery build rate per route (/api, /apis, /discovery/v2). Cache design MUST match the constraint documented in build_aggregated_discovery's doc comment in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/discovery.rs (four options laid out there; operator has not yet chosen one -- do not pick unilaterally).

title: auth::object_is_live: replace full Value tree parse with minimal-field deserialize for SA-token liveness check
description:
SIGNAL

JSON serde scout ai/findings/json-serde-optimization-scoping-2026-08-06.md identified this callsite as one of three that TOGETHER account for 20.7 percent of all allocation bytes and 27.7 percent of all allocation events in the 60min 0806-1102 conformance run:

- auth::object_is_live at crates/apiserver/src/auth.rs:400-436 - the per-request SA-token bound-object liveness check added by mayor-504t7 PR #910.
- discovery::build_aggregated_discovery at crates/apiserver/src/handlers/discovery.rs:288-347 - separate bead.
- content_type::reencode_proto_response at crates/apiserver/src/handlers/content_type.rs:207-231 - already filed as mayor-g7g2m.

For object_is_live specifically the scout identified that it constructs a full serde_json::Value tree from the store-returned bytes purely to extract a few discrete fields (namespace, name, uid, deletionTimestamp). Value trees are BTreeMap-backed and account for 94.5 percent of ALL JSON bucket allocations across the whole apiserver - so any callsite doing this is paying disproportionately.

FIX

Replace the Value construction with a minimal-field #[derive(Deserialize)] struct like:

    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct LivenessCheckFields<'a> {
        metadata: LivenessMetadata<'a>,
    }
    #[derive(Deserialize)]
    struct LivenessMetadata<'a> {
        name: &'a str,
        namespace: Option<&'a str>,
        uid: &'a str,
        #[serde(rename = deletionTimestamp)]
        deletion_timestamp: Option<&'a str>,
    }

Or the equivalent owned-String form if borrow-lifetime plumbing across the async check is awkward. Borrowed is preferred where possible for zero-copy.

Change scope: probably 20-40 LoC of type definitions plus the call-site swap in object_is_live. Do NOT change any external contract; only the internal deserialization strategy shifts.

TESTS

Existing object_is_live tests should continue to pass unchanged. Add a regression test that confirms:
1. A minimal object body with only the required metadata fields deserializes successfully (proves we do not require any other fields incidentally).
2. Extra fields in the object body do NOT cause failure (serde default is skip-unknown, but verify).
3. Optional: instrument with an allocation counter and assert the count-per-call is significantly lower than the Value baseline. Reverse-fail by restoring the Value parse and confirming the count goes back up.

VERIFICATION

Cargo tests green. Optional: dhat A/B post-merge showing object_is_live drops out of the top-N JSON allocators.

CROSS-REFS

- Scout: ai/findings/json-serde-optimization-scoping-2026-08-06.md
- Related but distinct: mayor-6sbvc JWT sig-cache PR #1034 (also in auth path, orthogonal — cache eliminates repeat verify, this fix reduces per-verify allocation cost)
- Cousin cost callsites: mayor-g7g2m (content_type dead parse, filed), mayor-brxse (discovery-doc, next)

Shape-1 solo dispatch. Fire this after mayor-g7g2m lands to avoid same-file collision - both touch different files but in the same crate.
close_reason: PR #1038 opened: replaced full Value tree parse in object_is_live with minimal borrowed-str struct (uid + deletionTimestamp only — name/namespace unused by the function, dropped from field set). Tests + reverse-fail verified.

title: run-all.sh --profile flag: build --features dhat, stop apiserver post-run, place dhat results with run results
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-06 during dhat conformance run 0806-1102.

MECHANISM

scripts/conformance/run-all.sh completes normally when sonobuoy finishes, prints its results summary, and exits. It does NOT send SIGTERM to the apiserver process it started via u7s-start.sh at the end of the run. The apiserver keeps running indefinitely after run-all.sh exits.

This is fine for normal usage (mayor session leaves the apiserver alive between conformance runs by design; next run cleans up via reset.sh). BUT it breaks any profiling tool that flushes state via Rust Drop semantics on SIGTERM.

For dhat specifically:
- apiserver main.rs:29-33 catches SIGTERM via tokio::select, returns from run(), Profiler::drop fires, dhat writes heap file.
- Without SIGTERM, apiserver keeps running with heap data trapped in-process.
- Observed: after run 0806-1102 completed at 11:02:39, PID 27958 continued running. Operator noticed 20+ minutes later that no dhat file for the real run existed (only the 2.6s Phase 1 file per companion bead), had to manually kill PID 27958 which THEN triggered Profiler::drop and produced the real dhat file (dhat-heap-apiserver-0806-1123.json).

BROADER IMPLICATION

This affects any future profiling integration that relies on graceful shutdown to flush:
- dhat (current use case, confirmed broken)
- pprof-rs (would-be candidate for CPU flamegraphs, same Drop-based flush pattern likely)
- tokio-console (long-lived subscriber connection: may or may not flush on drop -- worth checking if we ever integrate it)
- Prometheus /metrics push-gateway integrations (if any future work uses one)

FIX OPTIONS

Option 1: Add a --stop-on-completion flag to run-all.sh. When set, after sonobuoy retrieval + log evacuation, send SIGTERM to the apiserver + scheduler + konnectivity-server processes, wait for exit (with timeout), then exit run-all.sh.

Option 2: Always SIGTERM at end-of-run. Breaks existing mayor workflow where the stack is left running for kubectl exploration.

Option 3: Add a --profile-cleanup or --dhat-cleanup flag that specifically triggers this only when a profiling feature is active. Narrower, less footgun risk.

RECOMMEND OPTION 1: --stop-on-completion, opt-in flag. Default off (preserves current workflow). Operator or profiling scripts explicitly opt in. Documentation update in ai/prompts/vm-operations.md for the profiling workflow.

SCOPE

Shape-1 solo. LoC: ~20-30 in scripts/conformance/run-all.sh (flag parsing + final teardown block). Regression test: shell test that runs a mock apiserver, run-all.sh with --stop-on-completion, asserts apiserver exits before run-all.sh does.

Companion bead: u7s-start.sh two-phase apiserver overwrites dhat capture (above -- mayor-vnun4). Both should be fixed together in one PR ideally since they address the same class of end-user problem (dhat capture works reliably).

CROSS-REFS

- ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06.md (Phase 1 misleading)
- ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06-run.md (Phase 2 real, only exists because operator manually killed)
- ai/findings/rust-profiling-tooling-survey-2026-08-06.md (broader profiling tooling landscape)
- Companion bead mayor-vnun4 (u7s-start.sh Phase 1 overwrite)

Files: scripts/conformance/run-all.sh.
notes:
OPERATOR REDESIGN 2026-08-06: replaced the naive --stop-on-completion flag with a proper --profile flag that owns the whole dhat workflow end-to-end. Companion bead mayor-vnun4 (two-phase apiserver dhat overwrite) becomes a strict prerequisite/sibling in the same PR.

REDESIGNED SPEC

Add a --profile flag to scripts/conformance/run-all.sh. When set, the flag drives THREE integrated behaviors:

1. **BUILD WITH DHAT**: When --profile is set, the script rebuilds u7s-apiserver with --features dhat before starting the stack. This replaces the operators current manual workflow of cargo build --release --features dhat --bin u7s-apiserver as a separate step.

2. **STOP APISERVER POST-RUN**: After sonobuoy retrieval + log evacuation completes, send SIGTERM to the apiserver (plus scheduler + konnectivity-server for full cleanup), wait for exit (with reasonable timeout, say 10s), then run-all.sh exits. main.rs:29-33 catches the apiserver SIGTERM, returns from run(), Profiler::drop fires, dhat writes heap file.

3. **PLACE DHAT RESULTS WITH RUN RESULTS**: Set U7S_DHAT_HEAP_FILE (or set the dhat profiler builder's output path) to route the heap json into the per-run temp/e2e/YYYY-DDDD-slug/ directory alongside the sonobuoy results, host-logs/, rss.csv, etc. No more manual file-move step from the operator.

MUTUAL EXCLUSIVITY

--profile implies --features dhat build. Do NOT combine with --binary target/release/u7s-apiserver (which points at a possibly-non-dhat binary). If both are given: error out with a clear message.

--profile is orthogonal to --focus and --all-e2e - can be combined with either.

DEFAULT OFF preserves the current workflow (mayor session leaves the apiserver alive for post-run kubectl exploration).

TESTS

Shell tests in scripts/conformance/ verifying:
1. --profile causes a cargo build --features dhat to run before stack bring-up (grep the build command).
2. --profile causes apiserver to be SIGTERM'd after sonobuoy retrieval (grep for the kill call).
3. --profile places dhat-heap-apiserver-*.json under the per-run output dir (not the mayor CWD or /tmp).
4. Without --profile, none of the above three behaviors fire (regression against accidentally enabling always).

WHY THIS SUPERSEDES THE OLD --stop-on-completion DESIGN

Old design: --stop-on-completion was a narrow shell knob. Required the operator to separately run cargo build --features dhat and separately set U7S_DHAT_HEAP_FILE and separately move the resulting file to the run dir - three coupled manual steps that break independently.

New design: one --profile flag captures the WORKFLOW. The three coupled steps become one atomic user gesture. Mistakes (like forgetting the SIGTERM, or forgetting to set U7S_DHAT_HEAP_FILE, or forgetting to move the file) become structurally impossible.

CLUSTER SHAPE

This bead is now the head of a Shape-2 mini-cluster with mayor-vnun4 (two-phase apiserver dhat overwrite). Both are scripts/-scoped, both address the same functional goal (dhat capture works reliably end-to-end). Dispatch as ONE PR.

CROSS-REFS

- ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06.md (misleading Phase 1)
- ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06-run.md (real Phase 2)
- ai/findings/rust-profiling-tooling-survey-2026-08-06.md (broader profiling tooling landscape - future --profile might extend to pprof-rs or tokio-console)
- Companion bead mayor-vnun4 (Phase 1 overwrite - fix together in one PR)

Files: scripts/conformance/run-all.sh (main flag logic), possibly scripts/u7s-start.sh if the CA-generation-Phase-1 handling needs coordination with the --profile output path routing (see mayor-vnun4 fix).

title: u7s-start.sh two-phase apiserver restart overwrites dhat capture with 2.6s bootstrap when --reset + --features dhat
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-06 during dhat conformance run 0806-1102.

MECHANISM

scripts/u7s-start.sh has a deliberate two-phase apiserver startup on --reset:

Phase 1 (line 213): Launch apiserver WITHOUT --konnectivity-proxy-addr (because ca.crt does not exist yet). Apiserver generates ca.crt as part of normal startup.

Phase 2 (lines 278-338): Once ca.crt exists, script generates konnectivity certs and starts konnectivity-server. Then at lines 317-338: kill Phase 1 apiserver with SIGTERM, sleep 1, restart apiserver WITH --konnectivity-proxy-addr.

This is by design for the CA-generation ordering constraint.

INTERACTION WITH DHAT

When the apiserver is built with --features dhat:
- Both Phase 1 and Phase 2 apiservers share the same U7S_DHAT_HEAP_FILE env var (or the default dhat-heap.json in CWD).
- Phase 1 apiserver receives SIGTERM at line 318 -- main.rs:29-33 catches the signal via tokio::select, Profiler::drop fires, dhat writes heap file.
- Phase 2 apiserver starts, allocates for the full run (~40+ minutes), holds heap data in memory.
- IF Phase 2 apiserver is killed with SIGKILL (or the process just exits abnormally), Profiler::drop never fires, Phase 2 heap data is lost, and the on-disk dhat file contains ONLY the ~2.6-second Phase 1 bootstrap data.
- IF Phase 2 apiserver receives SIGTERM (as it did once the operator killed PID 27958 manually), Profiler::drop fires, and Phase 2 heap OVERWRITES Phase 1 heap correctly.

The observed bug in run 0806-1102: initial dhat file (dhat-heap-apiserver-0806-1022.json, PID 27892) contained ONLY Phase 1's 2.6-second bootstrap heap. Phase 2 (PID 27958) never wrote its file because run-all.sh does not send SIGTERM at end-of-run (see companion bead for that half of the problem).

Silver lining: once operator manually killed PID 27958 with SIGTERM, real dhat file was produced (dhat-heap-apiserver-0806-1123.json). See findings docs ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06.md (from the 2.6s file, misleading) and ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06-run.md (from the real 60.5 min file).

FIX OPTIONS

Option 1: Distinct dhat output paths per phase. Phase 1 sets U7S_DHAT_HEAP_FILE=...-phase1.json (or similar), Phase 2 keeps the original path. Only Phase 2 output lands where the operator expects.

Option 2: Skip Phase 1 entirely by pre-generating CA outside apiserver. Bigger refactor, riskier.

Option 3: Add a note to the operator-facing dhat workflow that with --reset, the Phase 1 dhat file overwrites Phase 2 unless SIGTERM is guaranteed. Documentation-only, does not fix the underlying trap.

RECOMMEND OPTION 1: simple env-var manipulation in u7s-start.sh, ~5-10 LoC, no behavioral change to normal (non-dhat) runs.

SCOPE

Shape-1 solo. LoC: ~5-10 in scripts/u7s-start.sh. Regression test: a small script test that runs a mock apiserver binary through the two-phase startup, sets U7S_DHAT_HEAP_FILE, and asserts the FINAL heap file is not the Phase 1 one.

CROSS-REFS

- ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06.md (misleading Phase 1 findings)
- ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06-run.md (real Phase 2 findings, corrected)
- Companion bead: run-all.sh missing end-of-run SIGTERM (below)

Files: scripts/u7s-start.sh:213 (Phase 1 apiserver launch), :317-338 (Phase 2 restart).
notes:
OPERATOR REDESIGN 2026-08-06: this bead is now a strict sibling of mayor-2pio7 (--profile flag). Both fixes must land in the SAME PR since they interlock:

- mayor-2pio7 --profile flag sets U7S_DHAT_HEAP_FILE to a specific path under the per-run output dir. Phase 1's Profiler::drop would OVERWRITE that path with the 2.6-second bootstrap heap if Phase 1 shares the env var.
- mayor-vnun4 must give Phase 1 a distinct output path (e.g., append -phase1 suffix, OR redirect Phase 1's dhat writes to /tmp/dhat-phase1-<pid>.json, OR simply skip dhat instrumentation entirely for Phase 1 since we do not care about its bootstrap heap picture).

RECOMMENDED APPROACH

Best solution: teach scripts/u7s-start.sh to set U7S_DHAT_HEAP_FILE to a distinct scratch path (e.g., /tmp/u7s-dhat-phase1-$$.json or similar) BEFORE launching Phase 1 apiserver, then restore/set the operator-requested path BEFORE launching Phase 2 apiserver.

Alternative approaches:
1. Skip dhat entirely for Phase 1 by unsetting U7S_DHAT_HEAP_FILE and using a stripped-down apiserver binary if --profile is set... too fragile, requires two binary builds.
2. Rename the Phase 1 file after Phase 1 exits and before Phase 2 launches... fragile, race-prone.
3. Have Phase 2's Profiler::drop only trigger if certain conditions... changes apiserver code, out of scope for a scripts/ fix.

Approach 0 is simplest and stays within scripts/. Do this.

CLUSTER

Ship both mayor-vnun4 and mayor-2pio7 in one PR titled something like: fix(conformance): --profile flag for reliable dhat capture (mayor-2pio7, mayor-vnun4). Neither works standalone: --profile without Phase-1-diverted-path still gets overwrites, Phase-1-diverted-path without --profile flag does not solve the missing-SIGTERM problem.

CROSS-REFS

- Sibling bead mayor-2pio7 (the head of the mini-cluster)

- Prior misleading data: ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06.md (the 2.6s Phase 1 file that motivated this bead)

title: stamp_resource_version -> put_sync unbounded growth: 27 MB max-live and STILL climbing at process kill (dhat 0806-1102)
description:
SIGNAL

Real dhat heap-attribution of the 0806-1102 conformance run (PID 27958, ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06-run.md) identified u7s_store::sqlite::stamp_resource_version -> put_sync (SqliteStore::put) as the top single-callsite by max-live bytes: 27.55 MB / 11,611 blocks with eb == mb (end bytes equal max bytes).

The eb == mb signal is CRITICAL: it means this allocation was still growing when the process was killed, never plateaued. NOT a working-set-and-hold pattern (grow to hold new state per test-family, then flat). This is genuinely accretive over the whole 60.5-minute run including the 20-min post-test idle window during which apiserver.log emitted zero lines.

An accretive allocation that survives an idle period is one of two things:
- H1: A retained-forever data structure (leak, or bounded-but-nobody-yet-cleared cache)
- H2: A slow-drip allocation from a background timer / reconciler that fires periodically even when no request traffic is happening

Neither is inherently a bug. But: 27 MB at ~40 minutes of load plus 20 minutes of idle, no ceiling in sight, on u7s (whose north star is small VPS deployments) is suspicious. Also: 20 minutes with zero apiserver.log activity but the allocation still climbing means the drip source is NOT request-driven.

POSSIBLE LINK TO MAYOR-DRS2A

Dhat also showed hashbrown::RawTable::reserve_rehash -> push_event_locked at 811 KB. push_event_locked is the ring / compaction_horizon mechanism mayor-drs2a Stage-2 was originally proposed to shard (sharding case retracted for CPU per samply, then partially revived by dhat on memory grounds). It is possible but NOT CONFIRMED that stamp_resource_version and push_event_locked share the same underlying ring subsystem, in which case a single fix could address both.

INVESTIGATION TASK (Shape 3, findings doc only)

Produce ai/findings/stamp-resource-version-growth-investigation-2026-08-06.md under 700 words. Structure:

1. Read u7s_store::sqlite::stamp_resource_version and put_sync source. What data structure grows here? What is the retention policy? What triggers growth?

2. Identify the growth mechanism. Is it (a) a shared ring/broadcast buffer, (b) an in-memory index/cache, (c) an accumulator like the deletion-log, (d) something else? Cite file:line evidence.

3. Correlate to push_event_locked. Are stamp_resource_version and push_event_locked in the same subsystem? If yes: describe the linkage. If no: describe why they look similar in the profile but are distinct.

4. Determine WHY 20 minutes of idle apiserver still shows growth. What background actor was inserting/appending during idle? Check for periodic timers, watchdog loops, revision-counter mechanisms. See crates/store/src/ + crates/apiserver/src/ for tokio::spawn + interval + sleep patterns.

5. Answer: Is this a bug or a design intent? If bug (leak, unbounded cache), scope the fix. If design intent (e.g., append-only revision log with compaction on a slower cadence than what dhat measured), evaluate whether the growth rate + max size is acceptable for u7s stance.

6. Cross-reference against mayor-drs2a Stage-2. Does this evidence strengthen, refute, or leave-unchanged Stage-2s case?

7. Recommended action. Fix bead + LoC estimate, OR ai/findings/ update + memory bank, OR both.

CROSS-REFS

- ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06-run.md (top-1 by max-live evidence)
- mayor-drs2a Stage-2 (open, RSS-accounting justification only per samply refutation, partially revived by dhat on push_event_locked)
- mayor-pwnz2 PR #1033 (SQLite prepare_cached — a DIFFERENT SQLite code path, invisible to dhat via bundled-C blind spot)

RULES

Read-only. No bd writes. No gh writes. No code edits. Do not disturb JWT worker or PR #1034 which is mergeable now. Use mcpls LSP if up otherwise grep+Read. Cite file:line for every non-trivial claim.

RETURN under 200 words: 1 growth mechanism identified (which data structure), 2 verdict bug or design (with reason), 3 link to drs2a Stage-2 (strengthens/refutes/neutral), 4 recommended action, 5 surprise if any.

Growth is push_event_locked into a bounded VecDeque (RING_CAPACITY=100_000, sqlite.rs:20). Run only produced ~20k pushes over 60min (well under cap), so never evicted — eb==mb is bounded-but-unfilled signature, not accretion. Confirmed subsystem link to push_event_locked (drs2a Stage-2 territory) — hashbrown 811KB site is deletion_log.by_key sibling of ring. title: JSON serde is our top allocator by both bytes 44 percent and events 52 percent -- scout for root cause and optimization landscape
description:
SIGNAL

Real dhat heap-attribution of the full 0806-1102 conformance run (PID 27958, 60.5 min including 20 min idle, findings at ai/findings/dhat-triage-2026-08-06-run.md) revealed the biggest surprise from all profiling this session:

JSON (de)serialization dominates total churn: 44.2 percent of all bytes and 52.6 percent of all allocation events made system-wide over 60.5 minutes.

This is BIGGER than SQLite Rust-side (top single callsite at 27.55 MB max-live). This is BIGGER than watch fan-out. This is BIGGER than JWT verify (which is a scout-recommendation candidate on its own via mayor-6sbvc, in flight as PR #1034). JSON serde is at the very top of the memory-attribution picture, and correlates with samplys writev at 21.6 percent self-time on the CPU side (HTTP response encoding is downstream of JSON serialization).

NON-TRIVIAL COMPOUND CAUSATION

Operator direction: while focusing on finding One True Root Cause, in many cases root causes compound into issues requiring multiple distinct fixes.

For JSON serde specifically, the mayor suspects the observed 44 percent bytes and 52 percent events is a compound of several sub-causes each requiring its own fix. Enumerate hypotheses the scout must investigate:

- H1: We re-encode the same object N times across different code paths (e.g., LIST response encoding + watch event encoding + admission-webhook payload construction each independently serialize the same Pod). If proven, we may need a request-scoped encoded-bytes cache OR a shared Arc-of-encoded-bytes plumbed through the response pipeline.
- H2: Our serde_json usage has unnecessary allocations (String vs Cow, to_vec vs writer, intermediate Value construction). serde-json-core, sonic-rs, simd-json are drop-in candidates for tighter zero-copy paths.
- H3: Every incoming request de-serializes the body into fresh owned types even when we could use zero-copy borrowed views. This is a deserialization not serialization root cause.
- H4: We serialize into intermediate strings and then convert to bytes rather than serializing directly into a byte writer.
- H5: prost is not the answer for u7s (project stance: JSON-only per samply confirmation) but there may be intermediate structural changes -- e.g., serde_json Value vs typed structs at admission-layer boundaries -- that inflate allocation counts.
- H6: One or more upstream JSON contracts we implement (managedFields expansions, ObjectMeta duplication across responses, large watch-event payloads) may be structurally forcing more JSON work than necessary; even a partial reduction would be measurable.

Actual root cause is likely a subset of these plus possibly others. Do not lock in one hypothesis. Enumerate and rank.

SCOUT TASK (Shape 3, findings doc only)

Produce ai/findings/json-serde-optimization-scoping-2026-08-06.md under 900 words. Structure:

1. Verify the dhat top-N allocators mapping to JSON serde. Cross-check by grepping the dhat file for serde_json, serde::ser, serde::de, String from Utf8, Vec push in Rust-serialization contexts. Report the top-N callsites by max-live AND by total-bytes, split by encode-path vs decode-path.

2. Map each callsite to a u7s code location. Which handler / middleware / codec is doing the serialization? Cite crates/apiserver/src/... file colon line evidence via mcp mcpls tools if LSP is up (fall back to grep+Read otherwise -- LSP has been flaky).

3. Enumerate root-cause hypotheses (H1 through Hn above plus any others). For each, cite the evidence for/against. Explicitly rank confidence.

4. Landscape of possible fixes per hypothesis. For each hypothesis, what would the fix shape look like? Rough LoC estimate, structural vs local, risk to correctness, projected win magnitude.

5. Fix-target prioritization. Rank the concrete candidate fixes. Highest-leverage first. Note dependencies between them (e.g., an Arc-of-encoded-bytes cache is easier once serialization is centralized in one place).

6. Anti-recommendations. Things NOT worth doing based on the dhat evidence, even if tempting. Example: switching to prost/protobuf is off-limits per project stance and would not fix the underlying JSON churn anyway since the wire format is JSON either way.

7. Follow-on beads recommended. Do NOT file them yourself. List them so the mayor can decide.

- Samply for CPU cross-signal: ai/findings/samply-triage-2026-08-06.md

- Do NOT file any bead. Do NOT open a PR.

title: Implement SA JWT signature-verify LRU cache (auth.rs:460): cap=512 default, exp-bounded TTL, sha2 key on signature bytes only
description:
SIGNAL AND SCOUT REFERENCE

Samply CPU triage of the 0806-0917-conformance baseline (ai/findings/samply-triage-2026-08-06.md, bead mayor-akyhj) identified num_bigint_dig::biguint::monty::montgomery at 4.4 percent self-time on apiserver. Root cause: every incoming request with a Bearer token re-runs the full RSA modular exponentiation. Same token from same client burns the same modexp hundreds of times per minute.

Full design scoping: ai/findings/jwt-signature-verify-cache-scoping-2026-08-06.md (bead mayor-32uy1). Operator has decided on the shape.

CACHE SHAPE (operator-decided)

- SIGNATURE-VERIFY RESULT ONLY. Do NOT cache decoded claims. Do NOT cache bound-object liveness (mayor-504t7 async DB check stays per-request).
- KEY: [u8; 32] SHA-256 of the JWT signature bytes only. NOT the full JWT string. NOT the kid alone. sha2 is already a workspace dep.
- VALUE Entry: signature_valid bool, kid Option String (currently always None per oidc.rs:66, kept for future rotation), token_exp Instant, inserted_at Instant.
- TTL: strictly min(token.exp - now, some_cap_like_5min). NEVER LONGER THAN token.exp under any circumstance. Operator security invariant.
- SIZE: LRU cap DEFAULT = 512 entries. Reasoning: real 0806-0917 baseline showed 17010 SA-authenticated requests across only 9 unique SA identities; even with token rotation and multi-audience the realistic unique-token cardinality is under 100. 512 gives 5x headroom for a burst of new test-namespace SAs. Memory cost ~75 KB (0.06 percent of 135 MB baseline). See mayor session context 2026-08-06 for the full calculation.
- CONFIGURABLE via CLI arg or env: U7S_SA_SIG_CACHE_SIZE, default 512. Zero cost when defaulted, lets operator tune without a rebuild.
- NEGATIVE CACHING: do NOT cache invalid-signature results under the exp-derived TTL. An unverified tokens exp claim cannot be trusted for TTL. Either skip negative caching entirely or cap negatives with a tiny fixed TTL like 1 second. Prefer skip-negative for MVP simplicity.

CONCURRENCY

std::sync::RwLock HashMap [u8; 32], Entry. No new dep. Strong in-repo precedent: state.rs:149 AdmissionConfigCache chose std::sync::RwLock for the same reads-dominate-writes reasoning.

CALL SITE (from scout)

crates/apiserver/src/auth.rs:460, inside try_verify_sa_jwt at auth.rs:443:

    let data = match jsonwebtoken::decode SaClaims (token, key, and validation)

Change: before the jsonwebtoken::decode call, hash the token signature bytes, check the cache under a read lock, return the cached signature_valid bool if entry exists and now less than entry.exp. Otherwise fall through to the existing decode, then on success cache-insert under a write lock. On failure do not cache.

Threading: instantiate the cache once on AppState alongside sa_decoding_key at state.rs:413. Pass into try_verify_sa_jwt via the existing store threading pattern.

LOCATION

New module: crates/apiserver/src/sa_sig_cache.rs, roughly 80-120 LoC production. Structure it with (a) new_with_capacity(usize) constructor, (b) get(and self, and [u8; 32]) which is a read-lock check plus expiry, (c) insert(and self, [u8; 32], Entry), (d) internal LRU-eviction on insert past capacity.

For LRU: hashlink crate exists but adds a dep. Alternative: use a fixed-size VecDeque plus HashMap for touch-tracking, or a simpler probabilistic scheme. If the eviction algorithm becomes non-trivial in LoC, hashlink LRU may be worth the dep. Worker decides after reading the code and picks the simpler option that fits.

OBSERVABILITY (mandatory per operator: metrics-driven cap tuning beats intuition)

Add three Prometheus metrics to crates/apiserver/src/metrics.rs following the existing prometheus crate pattern:

- u7s_sa_sig_cache_hits_total: IntCounter
- u7s_sa_sig_cache_misses_total: IntCounter
- u7s_sa_sig_cache_size: IntGauge, set on every insert plus eviction

Follows the same pattern as existing u7s_watch_broadcast_receivers etc. See metrics.rs for the register-once idiom.

MANDATORY CORRECTNESS TESTS (4, all per operator security-first stance)

Add tests in sa_sig_cache.rs plus one integration in auth.rs. All must be able to fail-on-revert per Rule 9.

1. valid_token_caches_after_first_verify_and_skips_modexp_on_second: instrument the real RSA verify path with an AtomicUsize counter (or wrap the verify function under test). Call auth once with a valid token, observe counter equals 1. Call auth 100 more times with the SAME token, observe counter still equals 1.

2. cache_entry_expires_at_or_before_token_exp_never_later: use a mock clock or Instant injection. Mint a token with exp equal to now plus 60s. Verify it, cache-populated. Advance the mock clock to now plus 61s. Verify the same token, assert cache miss and real verify fired.

3. tampered_signature_never_gets_cache_hit_shortcut: mint a valid token, verify, cache-populated. Flip one bit in the signature bytes of a NEW JWT string derived from the same header+payload. Verify the tampered one, assert cache miss (different SHA-256 hash key), assert real verify fired and returned Err, assert nothing cached.

4. lru_eviction_under_load_does_not_violate_correctness: create cap plus 100 unique tokens, verify all of them in sequence. First 100 should have been evicted. Verify all cap plus 100 again, assert real-verify counter now equals 2 times (cap plus 100) not just once.

Test helpers exist at auth.rs:1639-1693 (mint_sa_jwt, test_rsa_keypair). Reuse them.

NON-GOALS (per scout)

- Do NOT add kid_change_invalidates_cached_entry. u7s has exactly one static sa_decoding_key at state.rs:413, no kid header is ever set at oidc.rs:66, no rotation path exists at lib.rs:260. Speculative feature per Rule 2. Flag for revisit if key rotation lands.
- Do NOT touch mayor-504t7 bound-object liveness (auth.rs:400). It stays per-request by design.
- Do NOT extend TTL past token.exp under any circumstance.
- Do NOT cache decoded claims.
- Do NOT copy upstream flat-10s TTL. Our exp-bounded design is STRICTER, not weaker. This is by choice.

VERIFICATION

Post-merge, an A/B run of certified-conformance (per bd memory conformance-suite-is-iterable-for-profiling-purposes, iterable at 20 min) with samply should show num_bigint_dig::biguint::monty::montgomery self-time drop from 4.4 percent to well under 1 percent, and u7s_sa_sig_cache_hits_total should show a large majority of authentications hitting the cache (target: 95 percent plus hit rate at cap 512, based on the 9-unique-SA distribution observed in 0806-0917 baseline).

CROSS-REFS

- Scout: mayor-32uy1 (closed after producing findings doc)
- Related closed work: mayor-504t7 (SA token liveness), mayor-akyhj (samply triage)
- Related open: mayor-drs2a Stage-2 (unrelated, watch sharding)

CONVERSATION LEVERAGE

This is a Phase-5 perf fix in the same pattern that shipped as PR #901 (mayor-cef5 F3 apply_label_selector reparse elimination, 94 percent LIST latency reduction). Small measurable-win perf PR with strong before-and-after. The 512 cap + metrics + config option lets the operator tune after landing if the observed hit rate suggests a different sweet spot.
