In a project whose goal is passing as many e2e tests as possible, "flaky is functionally broken" applies to our OWN test suite as much as to upstream conformance.

The bead correctly noted the likely cause on 2026-08-04 (tracing/debug-event capture race when this test global subscriber/layer is exercised concurrently) but was left P3 as if that made it a rounding-error concern. It is not - it is:
- Blocking clean signal on every workspace test run
- Making per-worker "quality gate pass?" checks ambiguous (a green output could mean "genuinely green" OR "the flake happened to not fire this time")
- Every worker pre-commit hook is a coin flip

Fix scope hypothesis (from the original description, still current): the test likely installs a global tracing subscriber/layer that mutates process-wide state, and another concurrent test either reads or overwrites it. Suggested next step: use tracing_subscriber::fmt::TestWriter or per-test scoped subscribers (see tracing_subscriber::with_default) instead of a global one; or serialize the offending test via #[serial] (serial_test crate) as a stopgap.
INVESTIGATION 2026-08-07 (mayor-pqw78 dispatch): revised hypothesis (thread-local set_default racing tokio task migration) REFUTED empirically.

Verified via source read (tracing-core 0.1.36, tracing 0.1.44):
- tracing::subscriber::set_default IS thread-local (tracing_core::dispatcher::CURRENT_STATE is a std::thread_local!). Confirmed.
- BUT #[tokio::test] defaults to RuntimeFlavor::CurrentThread (tokio-macros 2.7.0 entry.rs:91-94), not multi_thread. block_on runs entirely on the calling OS thread - no task migration is possible within this specific test's own runtime. The "future gets polled on a different worker thread" mechanism does not apply here.

Implemented Approach A (WithSubscriber, attaching the Dispatch to the future via .with_subscriber()) exactly as specified. Empirically verified against the ORIGINAL bug report's own repro command (`cargo test -p u7s-apiserver --lib handlers::pods::`, run repeatedly):
- Baseline (unmodified code): 6/15 runs failed (~40%) at pods.rs:11886 (entry_lines.len() != 2).
- With WithSubscriber fix applied: 10/25 runs failed (~40%) at the equivalent assert line. Statistically indistinguishable from baseline. Fix reverted (not committed) since it does not work.
- Full crate suite (`-p u7s-apiserver --lib`, unfiltered, 2792 tests): 15/15 green on baseline, both with and without the fix - never reproduces at that scope in my runs.

Root cause characterized (own analysis, going beyond the brief's 3 approaches): tracing-core's PROCESS-GLOBAL, per-callsite Interest cache (tracing_core::callsite), specifically the `Dispatchers::has_just_one` fast-path optimization (tracing-core src/callsite.rs mod dispatchers). When a callsite (here, the `debug!("pod list entry"...)` in list_pods) is registered for the FIRST TIME EVER in the whole test-binary process, and at that instant `has_just_one==true` (i.e. at most one scoped Dispatch has EVER been created process-wide via Dispatch::new/set_default), the interest computation short-circuits to `dispatcher::get_default(f)` on the CALLING thread - which incorrectly assumes "the one ever-registered dispatch is this thread's active default." That assumption is valid for set_global_default (one dispatch, all threads) but FALSE for set_default (thread-scoped): if callsite C's first-ever hit happens on some OTHER concurrently-running pods.rs test's thread (one that never called set_default), the cache permanently stores Interest::never() for that callsite, silently disabling ALL FUTURE debug! calls at that site for the rest of the process - regardless of what subscriber is later attached to the executing thread/future (thread-local or future-local, both are downstream of this cached short-circuit).

Corroborating evidence: content_type.rs, lib.rs, inflight.rs, and resource.rs in this crate ALSO install their own scoped set_default subscribers in tests. In the full `-p u7s-apiserver --lib` run, those additional concurrent Dispatch::new() calls flip has_just_one to false early (as soon as a 2nd ever-alive dispatch exists anywhere in the process), permanently closing the risky fast path for the rest of the run - explaining why the full-crate run never reproduces while the handlers::pods::-scoped run (where pods.rs's one debug-capturing test is the ONLY ever-registerer in that filtered scope) reproduces reliably. This exactly matches the original bug report's own repro command.

Why A/B (subscriber locality) cannot fix this: the defect is upstream of "is the subscriber attached via thread-local or future-local" - it's a one-time, global, sticky callsite-interest cache corrupted by an UNRELATED concurrently-running test, entirely orthogonal to how this test attaches its own subscriber.

Why C (set_global_default + Once) is NOT a safe drop-in either (agree with brief's caution, but with a sharper reason than "leaks forever"): a global dispatch bypasses has_just_one entirely (get_default's SCOPED_COUNT==0 fast path uses get_global() unconditionally) so it WOULD close this specific race, but doing so naively means every OTHER test's tracing output (from any concurrently or later-run test, for the rest of the process) also gets captured into this test's single SharedBuf - risking both unbounded buffer growth and false-positive content collisions (another concurrently-run test's own "pod-a"/"Pending" strings landing in the same buffer).

Recommended real fix (bigger than a single-test patch, likely its own bead): install ONE tracing_subscriber::fmt subscriber globally, once, via Once-gated set_global_default, whose MakeWriter looks up a thread_local!-scoped "currently active test buffer" set via an RAII guard at the top of each debug-capturing test. This stabilizes the process at exactly one ever-registered dispatch (permanently defusing has_just_one) while still isolating captured output per test. This is shared test infrastructure, not specific to list_pods, and several tests in the crate (content_type.rs, inflight.rs, resource.rs, pods.rs) would likely benefit from/need the same fix.

No code changes committed - reverted the non-working WithSubscriber patch to leave the tree clean. Bead left open pending a decision on the global-subscriber-with-thread-local-routing design (or an accepted narrower mitigation).
close_reason: Root cause fixed by mayor-685aa PR #1069 (global set_global_default subscriber + thread_local demux, defusing tracing-core's has_just_one callsite-Interest cache race). 25/25 consecutive clean runs on the original repro scope (cargo test -p u7s-apiserver --lib handlers::pods::); fail-on-revert confirms the fix is load-bearing.

title: DRA ResourceClaim never allocated/reservedFor'd for count:0 opaque-config claims -- kubelet permanently rejects pod admission
description:
Discovered live during mayor-9qe1t's investigation (PR #993, worktree agent-abe69abb4643ef481), NOT a plugin-registration issue (see that bead's corrected notes).

Repro: --focus '[sig-node] [DRA] control plane must deallocate after use' on a fresh single-node lima-node-4 stack.

The test creates a ResourceClaim named external-claim with spec.devices.requests[0] = {exactly: {count: 0, deviceClassName: <ns>-class}} and a deviceConfiguration.opaque parameter block (no real device needed -- this is a control-plane-only claim-lifecycle test, distinct from the kubelet-plugin-registration path). The claim's status never gains .allocation or .reservedFor. Confirmed via kubectl get resourceclaims -o yaml: only .spec is populated, .status is entirely absent, for the whole run.

Downstream effect: the consumer pod (tester-1) gets scheduled (u7s-scheduler assigns it to the node) but kubelet's dynamic-resources admission then permanently rejects it:

  FailedPrepareDynamicResources: Failed to prepare dynamic resources: prepare dynamic resources: pod tester-1 (uid) is not allowed to use ResourceClaim external-claim (uid)

Pod stays ContainerCreating forever; ginkgo eventually times out ([FAILED] Timed out after 300.001s. at k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/dra/dra.go:1194).

This means: whatever u7s-side component is supposed to allocate ResourceClaims (set .status.allocation and add the consuming pod to .status.reservedFor once the scheduler decides to use this claim for this pod) either doesn't exist, doesn't handle a count:0/opaque-only device request, or isn't wired up to run for this claim at all. Needs investigation into u7s-scheduler's (or wherever DRA allocation lives in this codebase) ResourceClaim-allocation code path -- check whether it's implemented at all, and if so why it never triggers for this claim shape.

Cross-references: mayor-9qe1t (where this was discovered as a red herring -- initially looked like a registration-timeout failure but is unrelated), mayor-5di71 (separate, already-tracked missing-API-resource DRA bug -- this is NOT that; the resourceclaims resource itself works fine here, it's the allocation step that's missing).
close_reason:
Investigated (Rule 6 checkpoint, no code changes -- this exceeds a bounded fix per dispatch instructions point 6). Root cause is NOT a narrow "count:0" edge case: DRA allocation is entirely unimplemented. Exhaustive grep across crates/scheduler and crates/controller-manager finds zero references to ResourceClaim, DeviceClass, ResourceSlice, deviceClassName, reservedFor, or allocation anywhere -- apiserver (state.rs ~1368-1380) registers these Kinds as pure generic CRUD with protobuf-decode adapters only (resource_gen_adapter.rs), no business logic.

The observed "count: 0" is itself a real but separate small bug: upstream defaults ExactDeviceRequest.Count to 1 when unset (staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go doc comment), and u7s never applies that defaulting -- filed as mayor-r5ee3. But fixing that alone would not fix this test: the failing case ([sig-node] [DRA] control plane must deallocate after use, k8s 1.36.2 dra.go:1186, singleNodeTests(withKubelet=false)) requires real structured-parameter allocation -- the test's DeviceClass uses a CEL selector (`device.driver == "<name>"`, test/e2e/dra/utils/builder.go:100-104) matched against devices from a ResourceSlice the test's control-plane-only driver publishes even with no kubelet plugin (dra.go:1456-1458). u7s has no CEL evaluator anywhere (only proto-field pass-through for x-kubernetes-validations, never executed) and no ResourceSlice-aware allocation code, plus no deallocation controller for the second half of this same test.

This is a genuinely large net-new subsystem (device-slice indexing + CEL selector engine + allocation algorithm + scheduler bind-cycle wiring + deallocation controller) equivalent to upstream's dynamicresources scheduler plugin -- not a one-gap bounded fix, and a "count:0 -> trivially allocate" shortcut would build on an already-nonconformant object and not generalize to the real scenario. Scoped out into mayor-8qcaw (epic, full requirements documented there). No PR opened per dispatch instructions.

title: 36.9 core-hours of pure timeout-waiting across 495/517 (95%) of 0804-focus failures — iteration speed is bottlenecked by unfixed root causes, not test count
description:
Measured directly from junit_01.xml's per-testcase time= attribute (all 517 failures, not label-inference): only 26/517 (5%) fail in <10s. 236/517 (46%) take 2-5min, 119/517 (23%) take 5-10min, 38/517 (7%) hit a full 900s+ ceiling. Summed elapsed time across all 517 = 132,793s = 36.9 core-hours; even at 16-way parallelism that's ~2.3h of the observed 4.5h run spent purely on tests hanging out a timeout before reporting failure. Spot-checked the not-yet-root-caused 'connection refused' cluster too (avg ~196s elapsed, only ~16% fail fast) -- the pattern is universal across the whole failure set, not confined to storage/DRA.

This is not a call to retune timeout VALUES (mayor-5j5tx already established that's the wrong lever -- e.g. PodStartSlow's 900s is a legitimate upstream 'just in case' constant, not something to shorten). The actual fix is the underlying root-cause bugs already in flight (mayor-57lng, mayor-9qe1t, mayor-ax87f): once those land, the affected tests should complete in seconds instead of hanging out their timeout, which collapses this 36.9-core-hour figure as a natural side effect.

ACTIONABLE: treat 'now completes in seconds, not minutes' as part of the acceptance bar for each of those fixes, not just 'now passes' -- a fix that makes a test pass but still slow suggests the timeout-driven code path is still being exercised for the wrong reason. Re-measure this histogram after mayor-57lng/mayor-9qe1t/mayor-ax87f all land to confirm the collapse actually happened.
notes: Cross-ref 2026-08-04 (mayor-4mxi3 HPA investigation): confirmed the watchdog-reap theme directly for 2 sampled sig-autoscaling cases by cross-referencing 0804-focus-recovered's own [watchdog] terminal-log timestamps (600s/10m 'Active for' threshold) against the junit's 'Deployment/ReplicaSet not found' failure timestamps -- both lined up within ~20s. 13/31 of that run's HPA failures share this exact shape.
close_reason: Prerequisite fixes (mayor-57lng, mayor-9qe1t, mayor-ax87f) all landed; 0806-1542-conformance run is the re-measurement this bead demanded. Result: 446 passed / 0 failed in 30m11s (was 4.5h with 517 failures). The 36.9-core-hours timeout-hang thesis collapsed as predicted. Goal achieved.

title: GenericEphemeralVolume PVCs never auto-created -- explains 27/31 (87%) of inline-ephemeral-volume timeout cluster, NOT the CSINode/plugin-registration gap
description:
Full characterization of all 31 inline-ephemeral-volume timeout failures from the 0804-focus run (findings: ai/findings/ephemeral-volume-timeout-full-characterization-2026-08-04.md, worker worktree agent-acbbc352c8bf00e14; builds on ai/findings/persistence-failure-common-cause-audit-2026-08-04.md, worktree agent-a6520b6b863de032d, which only sampled 2 of the 31 cases).

TALLY: all 31 pods never reach Running (100%, confirmed via exhaustive last-known-status extraction: phase=Pending, container waiting reason=ContainerCreating, started=false, ready=false in every single case). Breakdown by driver/testpattern:

- csi-hostpath "CSI Ephemeral-volume" (true inline CSIVolumeSource, NO PVC/PV involved at all): 4/31
- csi-hostpath "Generic Ephemeral-volume" (pod's ephemeral.volumeClaimTemplate auto-generates a PVC, standard bind/provision path): 13/31
- nfs3 "Generic Ephemeral-volume" (in-tree NFS mount, no CSI plugin involved in the mount step at all): 7/31
- nfs "Generic Ephemeral-volume" (same): 7/31

Only the first group (4/31, 13%) is consistent with mayor-9qe1t's CSINode/plugin-registration gap (zero PVC involved, so the only path to a mount is kubelet's direct NodePublishVolume against the CSI driver's registered socket -- and CSINode.spec.drivers stays empty all run per mayor-57lng).

THE OTHER 27/31 (87%) -- ALL "Generic Ephemeral-volume" cases across csi-hostpath/nfs3/nfs -- are a DISTINCT, upstream-of-CSI mechanism: the PersistentVolumeClaim these pods require is NEVER CREATED AT ALL.

Evidence (checked 4 independent cross-driver samples: 2 csi-hostpath, 1 nfs3, 1 nfs):
- Zero PVC-creation requests found anywhere in apiserver.log for the expected auto-generated PVC name (<pod-name>-<volume-name>, per real k8s ephemeral_volume controller naming convention -- e.g. "inline-volume-tester-397e6-my-volume-0").
- Zero activity from KCM's ephemeral-volume-controller anywhere in the ENTIRE 5.4GB / ~4.5-hour apiserver.log, beyond its ClusterRole being seeded once at server bootstrap ("seeded ClusterRole: system:controller:ephemeral-volume-controller" at server start, 01:59:11Z). Compare to persistent-volume-binder (a DIFFERENT KCM controller), which is clearly active throughout the log per mayor-57lng's findings -- this rules out "KCM isn't running any controllers" and points specifically at the ephemeral-volume controller's visibility of Pod objects, or how u7s serves pods-with-ephemeral-volumes to that controller's informer.

Since no PVC is ever created, kubelet has nothing to bind/mount -- these pods are permanently stuck at ContainerCreating regardless of CSI driver health. Even a fully-fixed mayor-9qe1t would not fix these 27 cases (14 of them, the nfs/nfs3 ones, don't even use CSI for the mount step -- in-tree NFS mount is a kubelet builtin with zero plugin-registration involvement).

RELATIONSHIP TO OTHER BEADS: same broad "u7s doesn't correctly surface certain Pod/PVC state to specific kube-controller-manager controllers" problem family as mayor-57lng's already-documented §1a/§1b sub-bugs, but a DIFFERENT KCM controller (ephemeral-volume-controller, which creates PVCs from a pod's inline volumeClaimTemplate) and a different failure point entirely (PVC never created at all, vs. mayor-57lng's "PVC/PV created but binder never completes/attempts the write"). Filed as its own bead rather than folded into mayor-57lng since it's a different controller and different code path, even though clearly related.

Needs: root-cause investigation into why u7s never triggers/surfaces the ephemeral-volume-controller's PVC-creation reconcile for pods with inline volumeClaimTemplate volumes -- check whether the Pod objects created by these tests are actually visible via u7s's watch/list to KCM's pod informer at all, and whether the ephemeral-volume-controller's own watch establishes correctly against u7s.
notes: CORRECTION 2026-08-04 (mayor re-verification, post-merge): the csi-hostpath residual failure reported in this bead's close notes ('no volume plugin matched', attributed to 'the already-tracked CSINode/plugin-registration gap') was a STALE-BUILD FALSE ALARM, not a genuinely separate bug. The worker's build (PR #998) was based on commit 63695ed0, which predates PR #997 (merged later the same session) -- and #997 fixed exactly this symptom (missing spec.csi decode in decode_persistentvolume_proto_gen). Re-ran the exact dispatched spec ('[sig-storage] CSI Volumes [Driver: csi-hostpath] [Testpattern: Generic Ephemeral-volume (default fs) (immediate-binding)] ephemeral should create read-only inline ephemeral volume') against current main (post #997 AND #998) on a fresh lima-node/lima-node-3 stack: Ran 38, Passed 38, Failed 0. The csi-hostpath side of this bead's original 27/31 scope is now fully, cleanly resolved -- no further action needed there. The nfs3 side's residual (external-provisioner non-idempotent retry) is a genuinely distinct, still-open issue, tracked separately as mayor-hbr1n.
close_reason: PR #998 opened - fix + regression test + live before/after verification; two dispatched specs still fail on separate, already-tracked downstream bugs (CSINode plugin-registration gap, nfs external-provisioner idempotency race) unrelated to this fix

title: DRA kubelet plugin registration never completes -- 82/517 (16%) conformance failures, FATAL ERROR after 60-80s
description:
Full audit of the 0804-focus run (temp/e2e/0804-focus-recovered/, findings: ai/findings/focus-run-91pct-failure-and-spec-count-discrepancy-2026-08-04.md, worker worktree agent-ad38ea32d61fce94d) found the 2nd-largest failure category: 82 of 517 failures (16%), all from k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/dra/utils/deploy.go, with signature:

  FATAL ERROR:
      Timed out after 60.001s.
      hosts where the plugin has not been registered yet
      Expected
          <map[string][]app.GRPCCall | len:1>: {"lima-node-3": []}
      to be empty
  In [BeforeEach] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/dra/utils/deploy.go:730

Breakdown: 71x "Timed out after 60/60.002s ... hosts where the plugin has not been registered yet", 6x "all kubelet plugin proxies running: replicaset ...", 3x "schedule pod: Timed out after 80s", 2x misc (list pods / get ReplicaSet).

This is a DRA (Dynamic Resource Allocation) test-driver kubelet plugin that deploys as a DaemonSet/pod on each node and is expected to register itself with the kubelet's plugin registration gRPC socket within 60s; u7s's kubelet-plugin-registration path (or whatever u7s-side mechanism surfaces registration status to the DRA e2e test framework's polling) appears to never complete this handshake for lima-node-3 specifically in the example above ({"lima-node-3": []} means zero GRPCCalls recorded for that host).

Checked and RULED OUT as apiserver/store latency (see linked PVC-bind-timeout bead for the same apiserver.log evidence -- request and store-commit latency were flat throughout this run).

Needs: root-cause investigation into u7s's DRA/kubelet-plugin-registration surface -- confirm whether u7s implements the DRA kubelet plugin registration gRPC API path at all, or whether ResourceSlice/plugin-registration status is exposed to the test framework's polling mechanism correctly. Cross-reference with the already-known scheduler DRA gaps if any exist.
notes:
FULL 31-CASE CHARACTERIZATION 2026-08-04 (findings: ai/findings/ephemeral-volume-timeout-full-characterization-2026-08-04.md, worker worktree agent-acbbc352c8bf00e14): the prior audit's 2-sample characterization of the separate 31-count inline-ephemeral-volume timeout cluster left open whether it was "mostly" explained by this bead's CSINode/plugin-registration mechanism. Now fully characterized (all 31, not a sample): only 4/31 (13%, the true "CSI Ephemeral-volume" inline-CSIVolumeSource csi-hostpath cases, which involve zero PVC/PV at all) are actually consistent with this bead's mechanism. The other 27/31 (87% -- 13 csi-hostpath "Generic Ephemeral-volume" + 7 nfs3 + 7 nfs) are NOT explained by plugin-registration at all -- they have a distinct, upstream-of-CSI root cause (the auto-generated PVC for GenericEphemeralVolume pods is never created by KCM's ephemeral-volume-controller, which shows zero activity in the entire run). See new bead mayor-ax87f for that mechanism. Correcting the record here so this bead isn't read as explaining the whole 31-count cluster -- it only explains the smaller inline-CSI-no-PVC slice of it.
LIVE REPRO 2026-08-04 (PR #993, worktree agent-abe69abb4643ef481): the plugin-registration-never-completes hypothesis is DISPROVEN by a fresh single-node repro using the exact dispatched --focus. For CSI-hostpath, BOTH local handshake and CSINode publish succeed: kubelet plugin_watcher detects the reg socket in ~4s, dials it, calls NodeGetInfo, and CSINode.spec.drivers populates correctly with topologyKeys. The real root cause is one level up: kubelet also publishes the driver topology label onto the Node object via PATCH .../nodes/name/status (nodeinfomanager.go PatchNodeStatus, since kubelet only holds nodes/status RBAC), and u7s's generic status-subresource handler silently dropped metadata.labels there for ALL kinds including Node -- wrong per upstream nodeStatusStrategy which only resets .spec on Node status writes. Node never gained its topology label, so external-provisioner failed forever with topologyKeys not found on any nodes -- looks like a registration failure but is actually this. Fixed in PR #993 (merge_incoming_metadata now exempts Node from the labels-protection rule); before/after log evidence in the PR. RESIDUAL: even after this fix the csi-hostpath test in this focus still fails, at a DIFFERENT step -- PV provisions but PVC never reaches Bound within 5m, matching mayor-57lng's already-tracked PV-binder 1a sub-pattern now also seen in dynamic provisioning. DRA test in this focus is NOT explained by plugin registration at all for this exemplar: the driver pod never received any exec call from the test framework; the real failure is kubelet rejecting pod admission because the ResourceClaim status.allocation/reservedFor is never set for a count:0 opaque-config claim -- a separate, previously untracked bug, filed as its own bead. Next investigator: re-sample the 82 DRA failures to see how many actually hit deploy.go:730 vs this ResourceClaim-allocation symptom before assuming the original characterization holds.
New bead filed for the DRA ResourceClaim-allocation gap discovered above: mayor-wp3wj.
close_reason: Investigation complete: the 'plugin registration never completes' hypothesis is disproven by a live repro (PR #993). CSI-hostpath's local handshake AND CSINode publish both work correctly; the actual bug was a level up (Node status-subresource dropping topology labels), now fixed in PR #993 with before/after evidence. The DRA test in the dispatched focus turned out to be an unrelated ResourceClaim-allocation bug, filed separately as mayor-wp3wj. Closing this bead since its core hypothesis is resolved (disproven + real mechanism fixed); mayor-57lng tracks the residual PV-binder issue and mayor-wp3wj tracks the DRA allocation gap.

title: PVC/PV bind-timeout is the dominant conformance failure category (274/517, 53%) across csi-hostpath/local/nfs3 drivers
description:
Full audit of the 0804-focus run (temp/e2e/0804-focus-recovered/, findings: ai/findings/focus-run-91pct-failure-and-spec-count-discrepancy-2026-08-04.md, worker worktree agent-ad38ea32d61fce94d) found PVC/PV bind timeouts are BY FAR the single largest failure category: 274 of 517 failures (53%), an order of magnitude more than the prior quick-pass estimate of ~26 (that estimate apparently only caught one of two distinct message templates).

Breakdown by exact junit failure message:
- 130x "PVC, PV failed to bind: PVC ... not all in phase Bound within <N>" (framework/volume_resource.go / pv.go path)
- 45x "PVC \"pvc-X\" did not become Bound: PersistentVolumeClaims [pvc-X] not all in phase Bound within 3m0s" (storage/persistent_volumes-local.go:813 path -- a DIFFERENT code path/message template than the above, same underlying symptom)
- 7x "Failed to bind pv and pvc: PVC ..."
- 1x "expected all PVCs to be in Bound state within 30m0s" (storage/testsuites/volumeperf.go:209)
- remainder distributed across the driver/testpattern matrix (csi-hostpath, local, nfs3)

This spans multiple different upstream test-framework code paths (volume_resource.go, pv.go, persistent_volumes-local.go, volumeperf.go) all converging on the same root symptom: PVC binding not completing within its wait window for these driver/testpattern combinations under this --focus set.

Checked and RULED OUT as apiserver/store latency: apiserver.log for this run's exact window shows only 2 requests >=1000ms (both watchdog namespace DELETEs, not PVC/PV operations) out of 34M logged requests; store commit elapsed_ms had zero entries >=1000ms. This is NOT a general apiserver-slowness story -- it's either (a) a real gap/bug in PV/PVC binding logic for local-volume and CSI provisioner code paths under this workload, or (b) a controller-side (PV controller / kube-controller-manager) reconcile issue that wouldn't show up as apiserver request latency.

Needs: root-cause investigation into WHY PV/PVC binding doesn't complete for these specific driver/testpattern combinations -- start with the u7s PV controller's bind logic and whether it's actually reconciling these specific volume types (local PVs pre-provisioned by the test, CSI-hostpath dynamic provisioning, nfs3) correctly, and whether watch delivery for PVC/PV changes to the controller is healthy during a long high-churn run.
notes:
csi-hostpath (67) and nfs3 (29) slices RESOLVED via PR #997 (open, awaiting mayor review). Fresh live repro on lima-node-5 DISPROVES the PR #993 hypothesis that this was the same "1a" PV-binds-PVC-never-does mechanism: direct kubectl inspection showed PVC/PV binding itself already working correctly for both drivers (PVC reaches Bound, PV gets claimRef+capacity+nodeAffinity). The actual blockers were three separate, independent apiserver defaulting/decoding gaps that each prevent a PV from ever mounting or being created, all found via live log/crash evidence rather than assumption:

1. decode_persistentvolume_proto_gen (core_gen_adapter.rs) never decoded spec.csi (CSIPersistentVolumeSource) -- every CSI-provisioned PV round-tripped with NO volume source, so kubelet rejected the pod with "no volume plugin matched" even though the PVC was already Bound. PR #992 explicitly scoped its decoder to local/hostPath/nfs only since csi-hostpath never got far enough at the time (blocked by the topology-label bug #993 later fixed) -- once #993 unblocked topology resolution, this gap became the new blocker.
2. apply_defaults (defaults.rs) had no CSIDriver dispatch arm -- spec.requiresRepublish stayed null when a driver's manifest omits it (the common case). Kubelet's unmodified upstream csiPlugin.RequiresRemount (pkg/volume/csi/csi_plugin.go:471) unconditionally dereferences *csiDriver.Spec.RequiresRepublish, SIGSEGV-crash-looping kubelet on every node running a CSI-mounted pod. Confirmed via live kubelet panic/crash-loop log capture.
3. apply_defaults had no StorageClass dispatch arm -- reclaimPolicy stayed null. The nfs-provisioner sidecar (unmodified upstream, pkg/volume/provision.go:226) unconditionally dereferences *options.StorageClass.ReclaimPolicy in Provision(), panicking on every attempt before ever creating a PV -- confirmed via live provisioner panic log capture, explaining nfs3's entire PVC/PV bind-timeout cluster.

Also added nfs-common to scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh's package install (missing /sbin/mount.nfs was blocking nfs3 mounts even after binding succeeded -- unrelated to the apiserver fixes but needed for genuine end-to-end verification).

Mandatory before/after verification (fresh lima-node-5 stack): both "CSI Volumes [Driver: csi-hostpath] ... provisioning should mount multiple PV ..." and "In-tree Volumes [Driver: nfs3] ... provisioning should mount multiple PV ..." went from FAILED (pod never Running / provisioner crash-loop respectively) to a clean 38/38 PASS with 0 failures.

Residual, OUT OF SCOPE finding: the exact originally-dispatched focus test (volume-expand block-volmode allowExpansion offline PVC expansion) still fails even with all 3 fixes -- confirmed via live log to be a THIRD, unrelated, kubelet-internal bug: blkUtil.DetachFileDevice hits a persistent "device or resource busy" EBUSY unmapping a block-CSI volume's loop-device bind file during pod deletion, reproducing identically with and without kubelet crash-looping. This is kubelet's own unmodified upstream Linux syscall-level code running in the guest VM, not a u7s apiserver bug -- not fixed here, flagged for a future investigator if it recurs outside this VM environment.

Regression tests (fail-on-revert confirmed): decode_persistentvolume_proto_gen_preserves_csi_source, csidriver_pointer_fields_default_when_absent, storageclass_reclaim_policy_and_binding_mode_default_when_absent (+ idempotency counterparts).

PR: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/997
close_reason: PR #997 opened — csi-hostpath and nfs3 slices fixed (CSI PV source decode, CSIDriver/StorageClass defaulting), local slice already fixed via PR #992. All three driver slices of the 274-count PVC/PV bind-timeout cluster now addressed.

title: sonobuoy e2e plugin progress reporting completely silent (not just stale) on the OOM-repro --focus regex, reproduced twice
description:
Observed on the specific --focus regex used to target the --all-e2e OOM's in-flight test mix:

  --focus '\\[sig-storage\\].*(csi-hostpath|csi-mock|Ephemeral|nfs3|local)|\\[sig-node\\].*DRA|\\[sig-autoscaling\\]'

Reproduced on BOTH attempts of this exact focus set (temp/e2e/0804-0057-terminal.log, and a live run in progress as of this bead's filing): sonobuoy status/the terminal log's own status dump NEVER shows a Passed/Failed/Remaining count, not even on the very first poll. This is qualitatively different from the already-known 'numbers don't update mid-run, only at completion' behavior seen on other runs all session (full conformance and --all-e2e runs this same session show a populated Remaining:N count from poll 1 onward, e.g. 'Passed: 0, Failed: 0, Remaining: 4475') -- this run shows NOTHING, ever, from the very first poll.

Confirmed via live investigation (operator correctly rejected an initial 'probably a sonobuoy/ginkgo version quirk' hypothesis -- the SAME sonobuoy version has shown normal progress reporting all session on other test selections, so a generic compatibility explanation doesn't fit; something specific to this run or this --focus selection is different):

- The e2e job pod itself is genuinely healthy: 2/2 Running, PodScheduled=True, all conditions True (kubectl get pods -n sonobuoy -o json). This is NOT a recurrence of the bind-conflict/PodScheduled bug fixed earlier tonight (mayor-6oqbd/mayor-llh72) -- that's confirmed closed.
- The e2e container IS genuinely executing real tests: kubectl logs -c e2e shows live ginkgo output, including a real test failure ('[FAILED] PVC, PV failed to bind: PVC "pvc-32a97" did not become Bound ... within 3m0s') and normal skip-marker output. Tests are running; only the STATUS REPORTING is broken.
- The sonobuoy-worker sidecar (kubectl logs -c sonobuoy-worker, running at --level=trace -v=6 --logtostderr, its most verbose setting) shows it started correctly: 'Starting to listen on port 8099 for progress updates and will relay them to https://[10.85.1.3]:8080/api/v1/progress/global/e2e' -- but NO subsequent log line ever shows it receiving a progress POST from the e2e container's ginkgo process (E2E_EXTRA_ARGS=--progress-report-url=http://localhost:8099/progress). At trace level, a received callback should be logged; its total absence means the callback is never arriving, not just going unlogged.

Investigation approach (operator's suggestion, not yet done -- deferred until the current live run completes so as not to disturb it): collate apiserver.log with the sonobuoy-worker sidecar's own log by timestamp, looking for a correlating event around when the progress channel should have started delivering data. Also worth checking: does this focus regex select for a DIFFERENT code path in the e2e binary's own startup (e.g. a different SIG's test files loading, different plugin flags) that could disable or fail to initialize its own progress reporter independent of anything sonobuoy-side? And whether apiserver logs show anything unusual around the pod's own startup window (02:02:57Z-ish based on the worker's startup log line) that might correlate with whatever suppressed the progress callback.

Not yet confirmed whether this prevents final results (junit) from being produced correctly once the run completes normally -- unlike the two prior failures on this same focus set, which were caused by confirmed, now-fixed u7s bugs (mayor-pxm9c OOM/scheduling, mayor-6oqbd/mayor-llh72 bind-conflict-status). If the current live run DOES produce valid final results despite blank live progress, this is a monitoring/observability gap, not a correctness blocker -- downgrade priority accordingly once known. If it does NOT produce valid final results either, treat as equally severe as the bugs already found in this same investigation chain.
notes: Confirmed via post-completion analysis of this same run (temp/e2e/0804-focus-recovered/, full findings: ai/findings/focus-run-91pct-failure-and-spec-count-discrepancy-2026-08-04.md in worker worktree agent-ad38ea32d61fce94d). (1) The run DID complete with fully valid final results despite the silent/broken live progress feed: junit_01.xml is complete and internally consistent (7616 tests, 517 failures, 16 passed, 7046 skipped, all arithmetic closes exactly against 'Will run 3026'), all 16 SynchronizedAfterSuite + 3 ReportAfterSuite entries show status=passed, and the e2e container exited cleanly (exitCode=1, reason=Error -- ginkgo's own 'there were failures' exit, not a kill). So per this bead's own priority guidance: this is confirmed a monitoring/observability gap, NOT a correctness blocker -- downgrade priority accordingly. (2) New data point on the mechanism: 'sonobuoy status' polls in the terminal log show the progress feed isn't just silent -- it's actively WRONG at times. At 13:10:39 JST (~2h07m into a run that ran ~4h29m total) it briefly reported 'Passed: 0, Failed: 0, Remaining: 0' (implying the run was already fully done, which was false -- ~2400 more specs were still to be processed), then reverted to 'Remaining: 3026' by 15:32:10 JST (near actual completion) before the plugin transitioned to complete/failed. So the feed doesn't just fail to update -- it can transiently report an incorrect terminal-looking state mid-run. Worth folding into whatever investigation eventually chases the sonobuoy-worker progress-callback silence, since a 'briefly reports fully-done, then un-reports it' pattern narrows down what kind of race/reset in the callback aggregation path is at play.

title: scheduler re-issues POST .../binding for every pod roughly every 30 minutes, for the life of the process, regardless of whether it's already bound or even still exists
description:
Discovered while re-verifying an audit claim (mayor-puia3) that certain storage tests 'routinely need ~15 minutes' -- that claim does not hold up; this is what was actually happening.

Evidence from temp/e2e/0803-1624-conformance/host-logs/apiserver.log (this run's own archived log, not the live one):

Pod ephemeral-6126/inline-volume-440c6 (a normal e2e test pod, its namespace force-deleted by the conformance watchdog at 14:49:21 UTC):
  14:39:16.619  POST .../inline-volume-440c6/binding  status=201  (bound successfully, first and only real attempt)
  15:07:17.673  POST .../inline-volume-440c6/binding  status=404  (SAME bind re-issued ~28 min later -- pod/namespace already gone)
  15:37:22.649  POST .../inline-volume-440c6/binding  status=404  (again, +30 min)
  16:07:25.652  POST .../inline-volume-440c6/binding  status=404  (again, +30 min)

To confirm this is NOT specific to deleted/reaped pods, checked kube-system/coredns-574db47869-631e7 -- a normal, NEVER-deleted, long-lived system pod:
  14:37:12.638  POST .../coredns.../binding  status=201  (bound successfully)
  15:07:17.653  POST .../coredns.../binding  status=201  (SAME bind re-issued ~30 min later -- apiserver accepts it silently, no error)
  15:37:22.650  POST .../coredns.../binding  status=201  (again, +30 min)
  16:07:25.663  POST .../coredns.../binding  status=201  (again, +30 min)

Both pods show the identical ~30-minute periodic re-bind pattern, confirming this is systemic -- EVERY pod the scheduler has ever bound gets re-bound roughly every 30 minutes, for the entire lifetime of the u7s-scheduler process, independent of whether the pod is still Pending, already Running, or even deleted.

This is NOT the documented 30-SECOND RESYNC_INTERVAL backstop (crates/scheduler/src/main.rs:382, 'flushUnschedulablePodsLeftover'-equivalent) -- that mechanism is explicitly tested to EXCLUDE already-scheduled pods (see pods_needing_resync_excludes_an_already_scheduled_pod, crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs:2758). The ~30-MINUTE period observed here doesn't match that 30-SECOND interval at all, so a separate, currently-unidentified code path is responsible -- most likely a periodic full pod-relist on the scheduler's watch connection (a common client-go informer convention often defaulting to exactly 30 minutes as a consistency safety net alongside an active watch) that does not apply the same already-scheduled-pod filter pods_needing_resync uses. Look at crates/scheduler/src/main.rs's watch-loop/reconnect logic around POD_WATCH_PATH (line ~384) for a full-relist path separate from the tested RESYNC_INTERVAL loop.

Impact:
1. Apiserver load waste that scales with total pod count in the cluster AND scheduler uptime -- every pod ever scheduled gets a spurious rebind call every ~30 min, forever. For a long-running production cluster with many pods this is a real, continuous, unbounded cost.
2. For pods that get deleted before their next resync tick, this generates confusing 404 log noise that can be misread as ongoing test/application activity when it's actually just this bug retrying a stale bind against a gone object -- this is exactly what caused the mayor-puia3 audit to (incorrectly) conclude certain storage tests were 'still making progress' for 15+ minutes; the real test client activity for ephemeral-6126 stopped within ~5 minutes of its namespace being reaped, and everything after that was this unrelated bug.
3. Unclear whether re-binding an already-bound pod causes any side effects beyond wasted work (resourceVersion churn, spurious watch events fanning out to other watchers) -- worth checking once the root cause is found.

Regression test: once the actual relist/reconnect code path is found, a test asserting that a full relist-triggered pod event for an ALREADY spec.nodeName-set pod does not call bind_pod / does not issue a duplicate binding POST.
notes: Related, higher-severity bead filed: mayor-6oqbd (P0) -- bind_pod has NO guard against re-binding an already-assigned pod at all (confirmed missing vs. upstream's explicit 'already assigned to node' rejection, pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/storage.go:238-240). This bead's periodic global re-bind is the currently-known TRIGGER exercising that gap, but mayor-6oqbd is the real safety fix needed regardless of what triggers a duplicate bind call. Fix mayor-6oqbd first/independently -- it closes the actual risk (silent pod reassignment) even before this bead's root cause (the unidentified periodic full-relist path) is found.
close_reason: PR #1003 opened: root cause diverged from the bead's hypothesis (no separate full-relist code path exists; needs_scheduling's already-scheduled filter was already correct) -- the real defect is that POD_WATCH_PATH never carries a resourceVersion, so every watch reconnect (forced by the apiserver's own ~30-min stream_timeout_secs) fell back to from_revision=0, which replays raw ring-buffer write history instead of current state. Fixed by adding sendInitialEvents=true so a reconnect relists current pod state instead. Live-verified on lima-node-4 via a scheduler restart (same code path as the 30-min forced reconnect): repro showed spurious 409 POST .../binding for already-bound pods; fix showed zero.

title: feat(scheduler): enforce hostPort/hostIP/protocol conflict (NodePorts Filter)
description:
u7s's scheduler has ZERO implementation of the NodePorts Filter (hostPort +
hostIP + protocol conflict detection between a pending pod and pods already
on a candidate node). Confirmed via grep across the whole of
crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs for hostport|host_port|nodeports
(case-insensitive): no matches at all. This was not called out in the
originating audit's background (which focused on topologySpreadConstraints
and pod-affinity) -- surfaced during a function-by-function sweep of the
scheduler and flagged per fail-loud discipline rather than dropped as
out-of-scope-as-framed.

CONFORMANCE STATUS (verified against upstream release-1.36 source): this IS
the one item in this audit that IS conformance-tagged upstream --
test/e2e/scheduling/predicates.go:706,
framework.ConformanceIt("validates that there exists conflict between pods
with same hostPort and protocol but one using 0.0.0.0 hostIP") (Release:
v1.16, Testname: "Scheduling, HostPort and Protocol match, HostIPs different
but one is default HostIP (0.0.0.0)"). However, reading the test body
(createHostPortPodOnNode, predicates.go:1197) shows the expectScheduled=false
path calls e2epod.WaitForPodNotPending but discards its error
UNCONDITIONALLY when expectScheduled is false -- so this specific test's
negative assertion (pod5 must NOT schedule) does not actually hard-fail even
if the conflict is never detected by the scheduler. Could not confirm from
static reading alone whether this currently passes in u7s's real conformance
runs (would require an actual harness run, out of scope for a read-only
audit).

Do not assume this is currently red or currently green -- first step for
whoever picks this up should be: run/inspect the existing conformance
harness (scripts/conformance) with --focus on this test name (or check the
most recent full-conformance-suite run's per-test log) to determine current
pass/fail status BEFORE implementing anything. If it's passing today (likely,
given the weak assertion described above, and given the
full-conformance-suite-first-green-2026-07-24 milestone), this becomes a
should-fix-for-correctness item rather than an active red-conformance-test
fix, and priority should be revisited downward.

SCOPE (once verified): add a Filter-phase check in
crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs comparing the pending pod's container
Ports[].hostPort/hostIP/protocol against the hostPort/hostIP/protocol of
containers in pods already tallied on a candidate node (reuse the existing
NodeTally/node-usage infrastructure), with the 0.0.0.0-as-wildcard-hostIP
semantics upstream's NodePorts predicate uses.

title: perf(o11y): implement tiered -v/-vv/-vvv verbosity (apt-style) instead of blanket RUST_LOG=debug on --verbose
description: MEDIUM severity. Follow-on from a clean-run perf audit of temp/e2e/0803-1139-conformance (483/483 passed). scripts/conformance/run-all.sh line 109 sets --verbose to a blanket export RUST_LOG=debug. tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter::try_from_default_env in crates/apiserver/src/lib.rs line 176 applies debug to every crate, not just u7s's own. Measured on the 4,672,104-line, 653MB apiserver.log from this run: h2::codec::* (HTTP/2 frame-level tracing) accounted for 4,199,200 lines, 89.9 percent of the entire file. u7s_apiserver::* was only about 287k lines and u7s_store::* about 106k lines combined roughly 8.4 percent. rustls::* and everything else made up the remainder. This means the debug! calls added by the mayor-o8284 audit follow-ons (request-path timing, storage-write internals, admission-chain latency, scheduler decision cycle) will all be buried under h2 frame noise in every future --verbose conformance run, and every such run produces a 650MB-plus mostly-unusable log file. Fix direction: scope the --verbose RUST_LOG default to target only u7s's own crates, e.g. something like u7s_apiserver=debug,u7s_store=debug,u7s_scheduler=debug,info instead of a blanket debug, while still letting an operator override via an explicit RUST_LOG env var for cases where h2/rustls-level detail really is wanted. Regression test: a focused test asserting the default EnvFilter construction (or the run-all.sh RUST_LOG value) does not enable debug on third-party crates by default. Findings doc: ai/findings/conformance-clean-run-perf-audit-2026-08-03.md in worker worktree agent-a86fbfa20f37d32fa (gitignored).
notes: DECISION 2026-08-03 (operator): tiered --verbose/-vv/-vvv, mapped to broader EnvFilter presets, over the alternative (splitting h2/rustls wire logging into a separate file). Operator's rationale: matches the familiar apt-style -v/-vv/-vvv convention. Fix direction: -v (today's single --verbose) = u7s_apiserver=debug,u7s_store=debug,u7s_scheduler=debug,info; -vv adds hyper=debug,rustls=debug (connection/handshake detail, no per-frame spam); -vvv adds h2=debug (full frame tracing, for exactly the kind of TLS/H2 investigation mayor-zdrjr needed). Repeatable-flag counting (-v vs -vv vs -vvv) needs to be implemented in scripts/conformance/run-all.sh's arg parser alongside the existing single '--verbose) export RUST_LOG=debug' case at line 109 -- other conformance scripts that read VERBOSE/RUST_LOG downstream (e.g. the kube-controller-manager --v=5 bump noted around line 181) should be checked for whether they need their own tiering or can stay as a simple on/off keyed off any -v level >= 1.

title: conformance watchdog 10-min Active-namespace threshold force-deletes legitimately-still-running [Slow] test namespaces
description:
Live-forensics audit (mayor-rqqee, findings doc ai/findings/conformance-2node-novznat-regression-2026-08-03.md in worker worktree agent-a96a37f2aff439554, gitignored) traced the "[sig-apps] StatefulSet Basic StatefulSet functionality Burst scaling should run to completion even with unhealthy pods [Slow] [Conformance]" failure ('[FAILED] Failed waiting for pods to enter running: Namespace "statefulset-4013" not found') from a 157-failure 2-node conformance run (temp/e2e/0803-1011-conformance) to its exact cause.

Traced end-to-end in apiserver.log:
- Namespace statefulset-4013 created 2026-08-03T09:21:46.807Z (test BeforeEach at 09:21:48.754Z).
- 09:31:49.474Z: PATCH .../namespaces/statefulset-4013 clearing spec.finalizers, then 09:31:49.572Z DELETE https://127.0.0.1:6443/api/v1/namespaces/statefulset-4013 status=200 user_agent=kubectl/v1.36.1 (darwin/arm64) — host-side kubectl hitting loopback directly, NOT the e2e test client (which uses user_agent=e2e.test/v1.36.0 (linux/arm64)).
- Ginkgo's own failure fires 11s later at 09:32:00.7.
- 602.7s after creation — crosses scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh's watchdog_loop() (lines 68-117) hardcoded threshold exactly: any Active-phase namespace with age_s >= 600 (10 min, line 96-98) gets `kubectl patch ns ... spec.finalizers:[]` + `kubectl delete ns --grace-period=0 --force` — this IS the observed request signature.
- Confirmed NOT a one-off: the same watchdog pattern (kubectl/v1.36.1 (darwin/arm64) -> 127.0.0.1:6443 DELETE) fired for 5 more still-Active namespaces in this same run: statefulset-793, pod-resize-tests-7620, pod-resize-tests-5256, pod-resize-tests-4558, pod-resize-tests-2063 — all legitimately-running [Slow]/long-pole tests, not leaked/stuck namespaces.

This is the SAME failure class the script's own comment (lines 53-64) already documents fixing once: the CronJob "should not schedule jobs when suspended" test's 5-minute gomega.Consistently check raced a 5-minute Active threshold, which was raised to 10 minutes specifically to clear that test's floor. It is now recurring for OTHER [Slow] tests because this run's overall wall-clock was ~2.4x baseline (2908s vs 1233s baseline) — tests that comfortably finish under 10 min at baseline pace cross the FIXED 10-minute threshold under this run's degraded conditions (plausibly compounded by mayor-6pygt's kubelet proxy TLS flakiness slowing pod-readiness retries, and/or general 2-node scheduling latency under 16-way parallelism).

Explicitly distinct from mayor-1920p (that bead is a TOCTOU race causing namespaces to get stuck in Terminating FOREVER; this is the watchdog PREMATURELY force-deleting a namespace that was never stuck at all — confirmed via full apiserver.log trace, not assumed).

Fix direction (needs a decision, not obviously a bigger threshold bump): a fixed wall-clock Active-threshold is fundamentally fragile against a run's own overall pace varying 2x+ run to run. Consider either (a) making the threshold adaptive/relative to observed run pace so far, (b) checking whether the namespace's pods are still making progress (recent status updates / not stuck in a crash loop) before force-deleting an Active namespace rather than purely gating on age, or (c) accept periodic threshold bumps as tests get slower and treat this as a known tradeoff (simplest, matches the existing single prior fix of this exact class) — but then this WILL recur again the next time overall pace regresses for any reason (including cluster A's own conformance-slowing bugs), so bare threshold-bumping doesn't actually fix the systemic problem, just moves the goalpost.

Regression test: scripts/conformance/test-watchdog-logic.sh already covers the pure decision function (watchdog_decide) with fixed thresholds - a fix here needs a new case demonstrating the previous fixed-threshold logic incorrectly kills a namespace when overall run pace is slower than normal, and that the fix doesn't.

Severity: MEDIUM — confirmed cause of 6/157 failures in this run, and self-amplifying whenever anything else (like mayor-6pygt) makes a run run slower overall.
notes:
MAYOR REJECTED PR #1005 (not merged) after operator correction. Two compounding errors in the original bead + fix: (1) the motivating incident run (0803-1011-conformance) is the SAME run mayor-zdrjr root-caused to a deterministic stale-kubelet-cert bug (fixed via PR #982) that breaks exec/log calls to one node -- and StatefulSet Burst-scaling's own breakHTTPProbe/restoreHTTPProbe exec into pods, exactly that broken path, so the 'still progressing' evidence is likely contaminated, not clean. (2) More fundamentally: upstream's StatefulSetTimeout=10m etc. are FAILSAFE CEILINGS for declaring a hang, not assertions that healthy tests approach them -- properly-progressing tests complete in 1-2 min. A watchdog that gets MORE lenient when multiple namespaces are simultaneously old treats a strong signal of a systemic bug as license to wait longer -- this is exactly backwards, and this session already has a concrete cost example (mayor-puia3: ~40 ephemeral namespaces hung on a permanent CSI image-pull failure burned ~10 CPU-hours before their 15-min reap, because they were never going to complete regardless of how long we waited). Do NOT re-attempt an adaptive/lenient watchdog fix. If premature reaping of a GENUINELY healthy-but-slow test is ever confirmed again (root-caused, not just 'namespace was old and pod events looked non-crashy'), the right fix is understanding why that specific test is slow (probably a real bug), not loosening the global safety net.
Deferred rather than left open in the ready pool -- do not dispatch without new evidence (see prior rejection notes). Re-open only if premature reaping reproduces on a clean run with root-caused evidence a specific test is healthy-but-slow.

title: Experiment: test socket_vmnet (shared) Lima network driver vs usernet SYN-drop baseline
description:
Follow-on to mayor-1pj1u (findings: ai/findings/lima-alt-network-driver-scoping-2026-08-03.md,
worker worktree agent-a942a51ae191d8217). Scoping identified socket_vmnet
(mode: shared) as the top candidate to replace the shared gvisor-tap-vsock
usernet process confirmed as the SYN-drop layer for concurrent-connection
bursts (mayor-mjt51, mayor-n4c6b).

Scope (experiment, not a ship-it):
1. Install socket_vmnet as root (one-time host setup, see Lima docs:
   https://github.com/lima-vm/socket_vmnet, `limactl sudoers`).
2. Provision ONE (or two, to test VM-to-VM) NEW test VM(s) with
   `networks: - lima: shared` instead of `- lima: user-v2`. Do NOT touch
   lima-node/lima-node-2/lima-node-3/lima-node-4 (the mayor's live stack).
3. Confirm VM-to-VM reachability between two such test VMs (unverified
   assumption flagged in the scoping doc — shared mode's docs don't
   explicitly say "VM-to-VM: yes", though it's standard vmnet.framework
   switch behavior).
4. Confirm host.lima.internal / guest->host apiserver connectivity still
   works as expected under this driver.
5. Run scripts/conformance/instrument-vip-capture.sh against a scoped
   --focus 'Guestbook application should create and stop a working
   application' run.
6. Compare SYN cascades to the usernet baseline from mayor-biy31 attempt 2
   (ai/findings/vip-live-capture-attempt-2-2026-08-02.md).

Only propose a driver switch (as its own bead, with a real PR/config change)
if this experiment shows a clear reduction in SYN drops. This bead is the
experiment itself, not a decision to switch.
notes: REOPENED 2026-08-03: worker add8e86fd5ff8eced closed as 'inconclusive — blocked at Phase 1' because socket_vmnet install requires two host-root operations the mayor's shell cannot execute. Findings doc at ai/findings/socket-vmnet-experiment-2026-08-03.md (worker worktree) has the two exact commands for operator.
