No switch recommended. Findings: ai/findings/socket-vmnet-experiment-results-2026-08-03.md (worker worktree agent-a318f30e341497132).

title: Pre-pull e2e-test-images conformance image set into base Lima VM at provision time
description:
Follow-on to mayor-n4c6b (root-cause audit of image-pull TCP timeout that
killed [sig-node] Sysctls should support sysctls in run 0803-0053-conformance).

Root cause (see ai/findings/image-pull-timeout-investigation-2026-08-03.md,
worker worktree agent-a9252419d6269552d, not committed -- ai/findings/* is
gitignored): a ~92s burst-triggered SYN-drop at the limactl usernet layer
(same shared usernet process mayor-mjt51 flagged) black-holed 10 concurrent
outbound image-pull TCP flows to both AWS S3 (ap-northeast-1) and GCP's
registry.k8s.io front door simultaneously. cri-o does not retry internally
(no pull_retry_count knob exists in crio 1.36.2 -- that was a bad assumption
in mayor-n4c6b); kubelet's own backoff loop DID eventually recover the pulls
for most pods within ~75s, but upstream e2e's pod-watch step fails fast on
the first ErrImagePull/ImagePullBackOff event, so the sysctls test died
despite the underlying pull ultimately succeeding for other pods moments
later.

Fix: pre-pull the known e2e-test-images/conformance image set into the base
Lima VM image at provision time (lima/kubelet.yaml or equivalent
provisioning step), so these specific images never need a runtime network
fetch and can't be broken by a transient usernet black-hole.

Concrete image list observed in this single run (15 distinct
registry.k8s.io images; several -- kube-proxy, coredns, etcd,
kas-network-proxy/proxy-agent, pause -- are already baked in for cluster
bootstrap, so the incremental new set is smaller):
  registry.k8s.io/conformance:v1.36.0
  registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/busybox:1.37.0-1
  registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/nginx:1.15-4
  registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.55
  registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.63.0
  registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/glibc-dns-testing:2.0.0
  registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/kitten:1.8
  registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/nautilus:1.8
  registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/nonewprivs:1.4
  registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/sample-apiserver:1.29.2

Note this list is from ONE run (446 of 7579 conformance specs); a full
--all-e2e or full-suite run will touch more of the ~30-image upstream
e2e-test-images set. Cross-check against upstream's documented conformance
image list (registry.k8s.io/conformance docs) before finalizing the
pre-pull list so it doesn't silently drift stale as suite coverage grows.

Estimated cost: ~2GB additional base VM disk. Must keep the tag list in
sync with the k8s/sonobuoy version pin already tracked elsewhere in
provisioning.

Not in scope: fixing the underlying limactl usernet SYN-drop itself (that's
mayor-mjt51 -> mayor-66wxb, apiserver HTTP/2 support). This bead only
removes conformance-test flakiness for the bounded, known e2e-test-image
set that a black-hole can currently break.
notes:
CROSS-REF 2026-08-04 (common-cause audit, ai/findings/persistence-failure-common-cause-audit-2026-08-04.md, worktree agent-a6520b6b863de032d): sampled the inline-ephemeral-volume timeout cluster (31/517) looking specifically for whether image-pull delay is sufficient to explain any of the PVC-bind/DRA-registration/inline-ephemeral failures per the operator's objection that documented image-pull recovery (~3min) is well within all the timeout windows discussed.

Found it is NOT a unifying explanation (ruled out entirely for the "local" PVC-bind majority and the DRA-registration cluster -- see mayor-57lng and mayor-9qe1t notes, neither involves any relevant image pull at all in the sampled failure path) -- but found one concrete inline-ephemeral instance where image-pull unreliability WAS real and NOT resolved within the test's own budget: ns ephemeral-9785, test "ephemeral should support two pods which have the same volume definition", total time 915.19s (i.e. it ran past the full 900s wait). Its csi-hostpathplugin-0 driver pod's event history shows repeated Pulling -> Failed (RegistryUnavailable / Failed to pull image) -> ImagePullBackOff -> BackOff cycles for one of its 7 sidecar images, with the LAST recorded events being BackOff/Failed -- no final "Pulled" event before the test's own 900s timeout fired. This is a genuinely different, more severe case than the previously-documented ~3-minute-recovery instance: here the pull never recovered within the full observation window at all.

This strengthens the case for this bead's pre-pull mitigation as real and worth doing, while being explicit it's a narrow, minority contributor (1 of 2 sampled inline-ephemeral cases this pass; the other sampled case, ns ephemeral-938, was a watchdog-reaped namespace whose driver pod never reached Running at all for an unrelated reason, not image-pull) -- not a explanation for the PVC-bind or DRA-registration clusters, which are proven unrelated to image pull entirely.
close_reason: PR #1011 opened: pre-pulls 25 e2e-test-images/conformance/CSI-hostpath images into base Lima VM at provision time, cross-checked against upstream release-1.36 manifest.go + csi-hostpath-plugin.yaml. Live-verified via --reset --stack-only on lima-node-5 (crictl images shows all present pre-pod). ~2.30GB disk impact. Also fixed a discovered lima boot-timeout regression (10m default too short for the added pull loop; raised to 30m).

title: Scout: root-cause image-pull TCP i/o timeout to AWS S3 (registry.k8s.io backend) on gigabit-capable network
description:
Run 0803-0053-conformance's single failure was a kubelet image-pull timeout:
  Failed to pull image "registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/busybox:1.37.0-1":
  rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = unable to pull image:
  parsing image configuration:
  Get "https://prod-registry-k8s-io-ap-northeast-1.s3.dualstack.ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com/...":
  dial tcp 3.5.157.184:443: i/o timeout

Operator observation: local network can consistently deliver >1 Gbps. Yet
a single TCP connection to AWS S3 (registry.k8s.io's ap-northeast-1 backend)
timed out. This is the SECOND external-infra failure this session (first was
opensuse's cri-o repo returning 503 during CI which repeated on rerun --
mayor-sks04 timeframe).

Investigate:
  1. What is the actual DNS resolution + TCP handshake path from lima-node's
     guest → limactl usernet → Mac host → internet for cri-o image pulls?
     Same shared usernet process we investigated in mayor-mjt51 (which is
     confirmed to have concurrent-connection bottleneck for kubelet watch
     bursts). Could it also drop long-lived outbound TCP under other patterns?
  2. Is cri-o retrying image pulls, or does one dial timeout kill the entire
     pull? Check crio.conf's registries.conf and any retry config.
  3. Are we hitting a specific AWS S3 region issue? 3.5.157.184 resolves to
     ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo). Any AWS status incidents in the region during
     the run window (2026-08-03 00:33 UTC)?
  4. Longer-term: can we pre-pull the standard e2e-test-images set into the
     lima VM at provision time so runtime pulls hit local cri-o cache?
     Upstream sonobuoy conformance-image list is bounded (~30 images) so
     pre-population is a real option. Cost: extra ~2 GB in the base VM disk.
  5. Alternative: run a local registry mirror (docker registry :5000
     transparent-caching proxy for registry.k8s.io) inside the VM or on the
     Mac host. cri-o's registries.conf supports mirror configs.

Findings-only. Compare pros/cons of options 4 vs 5 (plus any others found).
Output: recommend one approach + estimate implementation cost, file follow-on
bead for the fix. Zero code changes in this bead.
close_reason: Root-caused: burst-triggered limactl-usernet SYN drop (~92s, 10 concurrent external image-pull flows, both AWS S3 and GCP registry.k8s.io front door affected simultaneously) killed the pull for one test while kubelet's own retry recovered it ~75s later for others; test failed fast on the first ErrImagePull event per upstream e2e framework behavior. crio has no pull_retry_count knob (bead premise was wrong for crio 1.36.2) -- all retry is kubelet-side. Findings: ai/findings/image-pull-timeout-investigation-2026-08-03.md (worker worktree agent-a9252419d6269552d, gitignored). Recommended option B (pre-pull e2e-test-images into base VM); filed mayor-5fkx5 for implementation. No code changes, read-only audit per bead scope.

title: pod.status.observedGeneration never populated by u7s — breaks [sig-node] auto-restart back-off test
description:
Run 0802-2344-conformance, [sig-node] Pods should have their auto-restart
back-off timer reset on image update (test/e2e/node/pods.go:531), failure at
23:21:37Z:

  Failed inside E2E framework:
    WaitForPodObservedGeneration(...pod-generation-03ea861d..., generation=5, timeout=20s)
  Timed out after 25.138s.
  expected pod generation to be 5, got 0 instead

The test made 5 mutating operations to the pod's spec (each triggering a
metadata.generation bump), then waited for pod.status.observedGeneration to
reach 5. It never advanced past 0.

## Verified

- crates/apiserver/proto/api-core-v1-generated.proto:4821 defines
  observedGeneration on Pod.status. Comment: "The PodObservedGenerationTracking
  feature gate must be enabled to use this field."
- grep -rn "observed_generation|observedGeneration|ObservedGeneration" crates/
  → ZERO hits in Rust code. Field defined in proto but nothing populates it.

## Likely root causes (unverified — needs investigation)

1. u7s apiserver doesn't propagate pod.status.observedGeneration during
   status PATCH (kubelet may be sending it, we may be dropping it in the
   validation/serialization/store-write path).
2. Kubelet requires the PodObservedGenerationTracking feature gate — we
   may not be enabling it in lima/kubelet.yaml (need to check whether the
   gate is default-on in kubelet v1.36.3 or requires --feature-gates).
3. Something in our HTTP/2 path (unlikely — HTTP/2 shouldn't change field
   semantics, just multiplex the transport).

## Fix approach

1. Check kubelet.log for whether kubelet is sending observedGeneration in
   its status PATCH calls. If not — enable the feature gate.
2. If kubelet IS sending it, trace the apiserver status-update path
   (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs) to see where it's dropped.
3. If neither — check the proto → Rust deserialization for the Pod status
   type; the field may be defined but never mapped.

## Priority

P2 — one failing test out of 446, low-blocking. But the fix is likely a
few-line change (enable feature gate, or add field to a status struct in
apiserver). Worth doing cleanly.

Discovered from run 0802-2344-conformance (post PR #976 landing).
notes:
RE-INVESTIGATION 2026-08-03 (worker/agent-aa8e9a6ae4ebc7f81, findings:
ai/findings/pod-put-status-clobber-2026-08-03.md): confirmed root cause,
filed follow-on mayor-mlyfr with exact fix scope.

Two separate things in the failing trace:
1. "executable file 'pause' not found" CrashLoopBackOff is EXPECTED
   upstream test behavior, not a bug — test/e2e/framework/pod/resource.go's
   NewAgnhostContainer defaults Args=["pause"] (agnhost's own subcommand),
   the "updating container image" test step only swaps .Image to nginx
   and leaves Args=["pause"], nginx has no "pause" binary. Happens against
   any CRI runtime including real Kubernetes. Ruled out CRI-O
   pause_image/pause_command misconfig (Sub-4) — this "pause" is agnhost's
   arg, unrelated to the CRI sandbox pause container.
2. THE REAL BUG: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:651-758
   (replace_pod, Pod's own bespoke PUT handler, NOT the generic
   replace_namespaced_resource) never strips the client-sent .status nor
   restores the stored .status before writing. Confirmed via apiserver.log
   + kubelet.log timestamps: kubelet PATCHes status.observedGeneration=5
   successfully at 23:21:07.890, then an annotations-only e2e test PUT
   (legitimate, non-stale per store's CAS check) to the main /pods/{name}
   endpoint at 23:21:10.516 silently resets observedGeneration back to 0
   for the rest of the test (confirmed: status.conditions[].
   observedGeneration stays correctly 5 — only the top-level scalar,
   which is all WaitForPodObservedGeneration checks, is lost). This is
   the exact status-subresource protection every other resource type
   gets via resource.rs:1958-1964/2162-2173 (with regression test
   put_statefulset_ignores_body_status_uses_stored_status) and that
   ANOTHER pod handler in the same file already does correctly
   (pods.rs:1049,1064) — replace_pod alone is missing it.

Not shipping the fix from this bead (touches a core Pod write path,
broader blast radius than just observedGeneration — see mayor-mlyfr).
Leaving this bead open per task instructions; mayor closes after
mayor-mlyfr's PR merges.

mayor-i9d54 and mayor-794xs remain filed separately and are confirmed
unrelated to this root cause.
close_reason: Real root cause was mayor-mlyfr (replace_pod PUT silently clobbers .status), shipped as PR #979 today. Original bead framing 'observedGeneration never populated' was a symptom, not the cause — kubelet was correctly setting observedGeneration=5 via PATCH; the test's own subsequent PUT was clobbering it. Also closes related mayor-i9d54 dependency on this (protobuf-decode path was correct all along; the drop was in replace_pod's Go-side status handling). Next [Conformance] should now pass [sig-node] auto-restart-backoff test.

title: fix(vm-operations): tune kubelet image-pull concurrency to survive HTTP/2-era admission bursts
description: Root cause #1 from mayor-h2u9z forensics (explains ~7-8 of 10 conformance failures in run 0802-1400-conformance: the 5-6x 'Timed out after 300s' pod-Ready cluster plus both container-probe restart-count failures). kubelet runs with the upstream default --serialize-image-pulls=true (MaxParallelImagePulls: null), which funnels ALL container starts through a single-worker FIFO queue before issuing the CRI CreateContainer call -- even for pods whose image is already cached. PR #975 (HTTP/2) removed HTTP/1.1's implicit pacing of pod-admission traffic, letting the 16-way parallel conformance run plus concurrent Deployment-scaling/webhook tests push ~260 'Creating container in pod' events onto a single kubelet within a 70s window (13:33:25-13:34:35 in the run). That queue took ~5 minutes to drain -- confirmed via crio.log: for 3 traced pods (downwardapi-volume, pod-secrets, pod-d8703e25) the gap between RunPodSandboxRequest completing and CreateContainerRequest arriving was ~5m00s-5m05s in every case, while CRI-O itself served each request in under 20ms once received. This straddles the e2e tests' fixed 300s pod-Ready timeout almost exactly. Fix: tune the conformance/e2e VM's kubelet bootstrap flags -- set --serialize-image-pulls=false or --max-parallel-image-pulls=N (N>1) so cache-hit image checks don't serialize behind a single global queue. See ai/findings/http2-regression-root-cause-2026-08-02.md for full evidence.
notes: PR #976 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/976. IMPORTANT deviation from bead's original plan: verified on live kubelet v1.36.3 that --max-parallel-image-pulls is NOT a kubelet CLI flag (kubelet --help has no such flag; crashloops with 'unknown flag' if passed on ExecStart). It only exists as a KubeletConfiguration file field. Fix landed in lima/kubelet.yaml's KubeletConfiguration (serializeImagePulls: false, maxParallelImagePulls: 10) instead of scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh's ExecStart drop-in (unchanged). Verified via scoped Guestbook focus run on lima-node-4: Ran 1 of 7579 Specs SUCCESS. kubelet.log startup config dump confirms both fields live (SerializeImagePulls: false, MaxParallelImagePulls: 10). Not closing per dispatch instructions -- mayor closes after merge.
close_reason: Shipped as PR #976 (merged 2026-08-03). Set serializeImagePulls=false + maxParallelImagePulls=10 in lima/kubelet.yaml (the KubeletConfiguration file, since maxParallelImagePulls has no CLI flag equivalent — verified via kubelet --help). Verified live on lima-node-4: kubelet.log startup config dump shows 'SerializeImagePulls: false, MaxParallelImagePulls: 10'. Scoped Guestbook conformance test passed (Ran 1 of 7579 SUCCESS). Expected effect on next 16-way [Conformance]: the ~5-cluster 'Timed out after 300s' pattern should not reproduce; ~7-8 of the 10 failures from run 0802-1400 attributable to this bottleneck should be gone. Remaining preemption failures (2) tracked separately in mayor-lmr4s (real in_flight dedup race in scheduler main.rs).

title: fix(scheduler): preemption hard-deletes victim pod instead of graceful delete
description: Root cause #2 from mayor-h2u9z forensics. u7s-scheduler's preemption eviction path does an immediate DELETE that removes the victim pod object from the store within ~1s, instead of a graceful delete (respecting terminationGracePeriodSeconds, setting deletionTimestamp, staying Get-able as Terminating until kubelet finishes). Evidence: scheduler.log shows delete_pod: DELETE completed -> evicted pod ... (preemption) at 13:52:02.684, then e2e.test's own Get on that same pod name returns 404 Not Found at 13:52:03.826 (~1.1s later). This breaks k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/scheduling/preemption.go (both 'validates basic preemption works' and 'validates lower priority pod preemption by critical pod' failed this way in the 0802-1400-conformance run). Needs someone to read preemption.go around line 206/218 next to u7s-scheduler's preemption/eviction code to confirm exact DELETE semantics expected, then fix the delete call (or apiserver's handling of it) to go through the normal graceful-termination path.
notes:
FINDING (investigated, no code change made — see reasoning below): the
grace-period/hard-delete hypothesis in this bead's description does not hold
against the current code. `delete_pod` (crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs) has
issued exactly one graceful DELETE since mayor-u0dpc (PR #954, 2026-07-30) —
confirmed by reading the function + its doc comment + git history (no commits
touched it since). The apiserver's `effective_grace_period_seconds`
(crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs) correctly falls back to the pod's own
`spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, defaulting to 30s only if absent.

Direct log evidence from the SAME run this bead cites
(temp/e2e/0802-1400-conformance, host-logs/kubelet-lima-node-3.log) for the
victim `pod1-1-sched-preemption-medium-priority`:

  13:52:02.714551  "Pod terminating with grace period" gracePeriod=1
  13:52:02.714579  "Killing container with a grace period override" gracePeriod=1
  13:52:03.271255  "Pod fully terminated and removed from etcd"

gracePeriod=1 is CORRECT here — upstream's own `initPausePod` test helper
(test/e2e/scheduling/predicates.go:967, fetched from release-1.36 and cached
at temp/research/predicates.go in my worktree) hardcodes
`TerminationGracePeriodSeconds: &gracePeriod` with `gracePeriod := int64(1)`
for every pause pod these preemption tests create. The pod really did finish
its own 1-second graceful termination and get truly removed — that is
expected, upstream-correct behavior, not a scheduler bug.

The actual bug causing both cited test failures
(k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/scheduling/preemption.go:206 and :304): those
lines are the test's SURVIVOR-pod assertion loop (pods[1..], NOT the intended
low-priority victim pods[0]) — it expects those pods to be completely
untouched. Scheduler.log shows the scheduler processed the same pending
preemptor-pod through TWO independent, concurrent scheduling attempts 900ms
apart (an in_flight dedup gap: the key is released as soon as
preempt_and_pick_node returns Ok(()), even though the actual bind is deferred
and still outstanding). The second attempt ran its own preemption cycle on a
different node, evicting an innocent bystander pod that should never have
been touched, and eventually double-bound the preemptor pod to two nodes.
That extraneous eviction is what preemption.go:206/304 catches, and it is
correctly diagnosed as "Pod not found" from the test's point of view but is
NOT a hard-delete-vs-graceful-delete bug.

Filed the real root cause as mayor-lmr4s (P1, discovered-from this bead) with
full log evidence and exact code location (crates/scheduler/src/main.rs,
handle_pod_event's in_flight release timing). Did not attempt that fix here:
it is a nontrivial scheduler concurrency change (same class of work as
mayor-krae9/mayor-kn79c, which needed careful design + guardrail tests) and
is a different code path/mechanism than what this bead was scoped to
investigate. No code change made under mayor-zl9ku since its hypothesized
mechanism does not reproduce. Recommend closing this bead as
"root cause corrected, real issue tracked in mayor-lmr4s" or re-scoping.
close_reason: Verified-already-fixed. The bug described here (scheduler preemption hard-deleting victim) was already fixed on 2026-07-30 in crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs delete_pod (commit 3102308c, mayor-u0dpc, hardened by mayor-krae9/mayor-i4mwr/mayor-kn79c). crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs effective_grace_period_seconds correctly honors spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds. Log evidence from run 0802-1400-conformance actually shows gracePeriod=1 (upstream test's initPausePod fixture at test/e2e/scheduling/predicates.go:967 hardcodes TerminationGracePeriodSeconds=1), so the timeline 'delete → 404 1.1s later' was correct graceful behavior with a very short grace. The REAL bug causing preemption.go:206/:304 to fail is in crates/scheduler/src/main.rs handle_pod_event's in_flight dedup race — filed as mayor-lmr4s (P1). Discovered by worker aeee324f50984dbdc which correctly refused to fix already-correct code (Rule 8: read before you write) and traced the actual mechanism instead.

title: Confirm kubelet's TLS ClientHello offers ALPN h2 via a fresh larger-snaplen capture
description:
Follow-on to mayor-mjt51's usernet-mitigation audit (findings:
ai/findings/usernet-mitigation-audit-2026-08-02.md, worker worktree
agent-a16f32c3c371fb6b8).

The audit found conclusive server-side proof that the apiserver never
supports HTTP/2 (see the companion bead "Enable HTTP/2 (ALPN h2) support
in apiserver TLS listener..."), but could NOT directly confirm from the
existing pcap (/tmp/vip-capture.pcap on lima-node-4, 720MB, from
mayor-biy31 attempt 2) that kubelet's TLS ClientHello actually offers ALPN
h2, because that capture used a small tcpdump snaplen (per
scripts/conformance/instrument-vip-capture.sh, -s 128) -- 128 bytes
truncates the payload at ~76 bytes into a ClientHello, well before
reaching the ALPN extension (this apiserver's ClientHello is ~1523 bytes
due to the ML-KEM-768 post-quantum hybrid key share, serialized after
cipher suites, compression methods, SNI, supported_groups, key_share,
etc.).

This doesn't change the fix's necessity (the server-side gap is
independently conclusive), but it's a residual evidence gap worth closing
cheaply before or alongside the HTTP/2 implementation work, and it
directly validates whether the fix will actually produce the expected
multiplexing win once shipped.

## Scope
- Re-run scripts/conformance/instrument-vip-capture.sh's tcpdump
  invocation with a much larger snaplen (0 or 1600) instead of 128, for one
  short window during kubelet startup (no full conformance run needed -- a
  single kubelet reconnect is enough to see one ClientHello).
- Extract the ALPN extension from the first ClientHello to the apiserver
  port and confirm it lists "h2" (and/or "http/1.1").
- If tshark isn't installed on the target VM, either install it there (a
  test VM, not the mayor's live stack) or work out the byte offset by hand
  from the raw hex dump -- either is fine for a one-off confirmation.
close_reason: Confirmed via fresh -s 0 tcpdump capture on lima-node-4 during a forced kubelet reconnect: kubelet's TLS ClientHello (record length 1523 bytes, matching mayor-mjt51's ML-KEM-768 prediction exactly) carries ALPN extension (type 0x0010) with protocol list [h2, http/1.1] in that wire order (hex: 02 6832 08 68747470 2f312e31). This is client-go's net/http.Transport default ALPN offer, confirmed reaching the apiserver unmodified. Combined with mayor-mjt51's server-side finding (apiserver never configures ALPN, hardcoded http1::Builder), the HTTP/2 fix (mayor-66wxb) is client-ready today. Findings: ai/findings/alpn-check-2026-08-02.md (worker worktree agent-a1ab16ff2fc949aea). Findings-only task, no code changes, no PR.

title: Investigate limactl usernet as confirmed SYN-drop layer for VIP/watch-reconnect timeouts (mitigation options)
description:
Follow-on to mayor-biy31's live-capture attempt 2 (2026-08-02, findings:
ai/findings/vip-live-capture-attempt-2-2026-08-02.md in worker worktree
agent-a17a97c4eb1ea1c29, not committed -- ai/findings/* is gitignored).

Live pcap capture during a real [Conformance] run on lima-node-4 caught two
direct SYN-blackhole events (36.1s isolated flow; ~20s mass event affecting
~150-200 simultaneous new connections from kubelet's non-multiplexed
per-reflector watch reconnects). By elimination across every other
instrumented layer (guest kernel nstat/conntrack/IPVS counters clean
throughout both events across 746 snapshots; apiserver's own request loop
never stalled, 503ms max gap through the 150-conn burst; Mac host's
cumulative `netstat -s -p tcp` "listen queue overflow" stayed at 0 despite
the organic ~150-conn-in-under-1s burst), the shared `limactl usernet`
userspace process -- which bridges all 4 concurrently-running Lima VMs'
virtual networking to the Mac's real TCP/IP stack -- is now the
best-supported single remaining candidate for where the SYN actually gets
dropped.

No code fix is available in the u7s repo for this (it's external Lima /
gvisor-tap-vsock tooling, not our code). Suggested next steps, in
increasing order of effort:
  1. Check the installed Lima version's changelog / issue tracker for known
     usernet burst-capacity or connection-setup-concurrency bugs/fixes.
  2. Try Lima's alternative network drivers (e.g. vzNAT / socket_vmnet)
     if compatible with the current multi-VM (4 concurrent Lima VMs)
     conformance setup, and re-run the same live-capture method to see if
     the blackhole reproduces under a different driver.
  3. Isolation test: run a single VM (no other lima-node-*/2/3 concurrently
     active) through the same live-capture method to see if reducing
     usernet's shared load (currently split across all 4 VMs at once)
     changes the burst-recovery time or eliminates the event.
  4. If none of the above pans out, consider whether kubelet's own
     behavior (opening one TCP connection per watch reflector instead of
     multiplexing over HTTP/2) is the more tractable lever -- reducing the
     size of the "thundering herd" on reconnect would reduce exposure to
     whatever the usernet capacity limit is, even without fixing usernet
     itself. This would need investigation of whether the u7s apiserver
     currently negotiates HTTP/2 for watch connections at all.

Root trigger of the ~150-200-connection mass reconnect (why so many kubelet
watches closed together) was not conclusively identified in the live
capture -- most likely a synchronized ginkgo 16-way-parallel checkpoint
(many workers tearing down namespaces at once), not a u7s server bug
(checked: no max_connections/idle_timeout/watch-duration-cap logic exists
in crates/apiserver/src/*.rs). Worth confirming with another capture if
this bead's mitigation work needs to isolate the trigger further.
close_reason: Audit complete. Sub-question 1 clearly won: the apiserver never negotiates HTTP/2 (hyper Cargo feature=http1 only, no ALPN protocols set in tls.rs, serve_tls() hardcodes hyper::server::conn::http1::Builder), which is what forces every kubelet watch reflector onto its own TCP connection and amplifies reconnects into the ~150-200-connection SYN burst mayor-biy31 caught overwhelming limactl usernet. Kubelet's client-go needs no config change (no DISABLE_HTTP2/GODEBUG set anywhere in lima-start.sh). Sub-questions 2/3 (alt Lima driver, VM isolation) not run per the dispatch's stopping rule. Findings: ai/findings/usernet-mitigation-audit-2026-08-02.md (worker worktree agent-a16f32c3c371fb6b8, not committed). Follow-ons filed: mayor-66wxb (implement HTTP/2 support, primary fix), mayor-lrx6c (confirm kubelet's ALPN h2 offer via larger-snaplen capture), mayor-1pj1u (deferred sub-questions 2/3 as fallback). No PR opened per dispatch guidance -- this is a code change, not a config flip.

title: reconcile redundant dual-DNAT for default/kubernetes VIP (manual iptables rule + kube-proxy IPVS)
description:
Discovered during mayor-odt6u audit (ai/findings/vip-timeout-rootcause-2026-08-02.md).

Two independent, unaudited mechanisms both target 10.96.0.1:443 today:

1. scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh:677-699 installs a hand-rolled
   `iptables -t nat -A OUTPUT/PREROUTING -d 10.96.0.1/32 --dport 443
   -j DNAT --to-destination ${HOST_IP}:${PORT}` once, at node-join time,
   plus a one-time patch of the default/kubernetes EndpointSlice address
   (lima-start.sh:695-699).
2. kube-proxy (running in IPVS mode, confirmed via
   "Syncing ipvs proxier rules" in kube-proxy-lima-node.log) independently
   programs its own IPVS virtual server for 10.96.0.1:443 from that same
   EndpointSlice (proxier.go:1558 "Adding new service"
   virtualServer="10.96.0.1:443/TCP").

Both mechanisms coexist and (per current evidence) produce the same
routing outcome, but nothing in the codebase documents *why* the manual
rule is needed on top of kube-proxy's own IPVS programming, whether it's
a workaround for an IPVS bug/gap, or whether one is now dead weight. The
precedence between a plain iptables nat-table DNAT rule and IPVS's
local-in packet interception is kernel/version-dependent and was not
resolved during the audit (see mayor-9v0eu for the live-capture follow-up
that could disambiguate).

Ask: determine whether the manual rule is still required; if so, document
why (link back to whatever bug/limitation motivated it); if not, remove it
to eliminate a redundant, unaudited code path that any operator debugging
VIP routing would otherwise have to discover by hand.
notes: Outcome A (manual iptables DNAT removed as legacy/redundant). PR #971 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/971. Git-history evidence: manual DNAT (e7a406d5, May 26) predates kube-proxy systemd service (74fad8a3, Jun 3) by over a week; EndpointSlice patch commit (dbd53c27) explicitly says its purpose is feeding kube-proxy's IPVS. Empirically verified on idle lima-node-4: disabled manual OUTPUT+PREROUTING DNAT, curled 10.96.0.1:443 from both VM root netns and a live pod netns (nsenter) -- identical connection-refused behavior with rule present vs removed, proving kube-proxy IPVS alone handles the VIP. VM restored to original state after test. Filed mayor-7tgag as follow-up for the same duplicated pattern found in scripts/kubelet-reconnect.sh (out of this task's named scope). Not closing per task instructions -- mayor closes after merge.
close_reason: Shipped as PR #971 (merged 2026-08-02T05:50:42Z). Removed the legacy manual iptables OUTPUT+PREROUTING DNAT for 10.96.0.1:443 from scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh:673-701. Empirical evidence: manual DNAT packet counters were 0/0 on idle lima-node-4 (kube-proxy IPVS caught traffic first per netfilter ordering); disable-and-test showed identical behavior. Git-history evidence: commit e7a406d5 (May 26) added the manual DNAT when there was no kube-proxy at all; 74fad8a3 (Jun 3) added kube-proxy independently; dbd53c27 (Jun 4)'s commit message explicitly states the EndpointSlice patch's purpose is to feed kube-proxy's IPVS. Kept net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 (IPVS prereq), HOST_IP resolution, and the EndpointSlice patch (load-bearing for kube-proxy). Follow-up mayor-7tgag (P3) filed for the identical duplicate in scripts/kubelet-reconnect.sh:111-123.

title: live conntrack/IPVS/usernet capture during a conformance run to confirm VIP SYN-drop layer
description:
Audit mayor-odt6u (see ai/findings/vip-timeout-rootcause-2026-08-02.md)
narrowed the VIP/pod-IP i/o-timeout family to "somewhere in the guest
kernel DNAT/IPVS path or the shared limactl usernet proxy, before the
packet reaches the apiserver's own listener" but could NOT distinguish,
from static post-hoc logs, between:
  - Mac kern.ipc.somaxconn=128 accept-queue overflow on the apiserver's
    loopback listener,
  - an internal queueing/capacity limit inside the single shared
    `limactl usernet` process (which backs all 4 concurrently-running
    Lima VMs' networking),
  - a stale/desynced conntrack or IPVS real-server entry on the specific
    4-tuple causing every SYN retransmit to be silently dropped
    (nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal=false is the kube-proxy default in this
    run — flags.go:64 in kube-proxy-lima-node.log).

Need, during a live 16-way conformance run, timed to catch a reproduction:
  - `conntrack -L` / `conntrack -S` snapshots on the affected VM around a
    VIP or pod-IP timeout event
  - `ipvsadm -L -n --stats` for the `default/kubernetes` virtual server
  - `ss -s` / `netstat -s | grep -i overflow` on both the guest and the
    Mac host apiserver process
  - ideally a targeted `tcpdump` on the guest's primary interface and/or
    `kube-ipvs0` capturing the exact failing 4-tuple's SYN retransmits

This is the only way to move the mayor-odt6u root-cause from "strongly
implicated candidate" to "proven mechanism." Also apply to the pod-IP
timeout variant (mayor-pzgzc), which is architecturally distinct (kubelet
probing a pod IP entirely within the guest kernel, no usernet/DNAT hop) and
needs its own capture.
notes: Attempt 2 (2026-08-02, worker agent-a17a97c4eb1ea1c29): e2e.txt shows no i/o timeout again (2nd narrow-grep no-repro), BUT direct pcap analysis (grouping SYNs by src-port+seq to isolate genuine kernel retransmit cascades from coincidental port reuse) caught the underlying SYN-blackhole phenomenon live, twice: (1) an isolated 36.1s single-flow blackhole on a kubelet watch-reflector reconnect, bypassing VIP/IPVS entirely (source stayed the guest's own host-netns address); (2) a ~20s MASS blackhole affecting ~150-200 simultaneous new connections at once (kubelet's non-multiplexed per-reflector watches all reconnecting together after ~150 watches closed within the same few seconds). Guest kernel counters (nstat overflow/drop, conntrack -S insert_failed/drop) stayed zero throughout both events across all 746 snapshots; apiserver's own request loop never stalled (503ms max gap through the 150-conn burst); Mac host cumulative 'listen queue overflow' stayed at 0 despite the organic ~150-conn-in-under-1s burst. By elimination across every other instrumented layer, the shared limactl usernet process (bridging all 4 concurrently-running Lima VMs to the Mac's real socket) is now the best-supported single remaining candidate for where the SYN gets dropped -- promoted from untested residual candidate to primary suspect via direct evidence, twice, at two different event scales. No code fix available in this repo for that external process; actionable next steps are investigative (alt Lima network driver, check Lima issue tracker for usernet burst-capacity bugs, isolation test with fewer concurrent VMs). Findings: ai/findings/vip-live-capture-attempt-2-2026-08-02.md + blackhole-evidence.txt (worktree agent-a17a97c4eb1ea1c29, not committed -- ai/findings/* is gitignored).
close_reason: Attempt 2 complete (2026-08-02, worker agent-a17a97c4eb1ea1c29). e2e.txt still shows no i/o timeout by narrow grep, but direct pcap analysis (grouping SYNs by src-port+seq to isolate genuine kernel retransmit cascades) caught the underlying SYN-blackhole live twice in the same run: an isolated 36.1s single-flow event and a ~20s mass event affecting ~150-200 simultaneous connections. By elimination across every other instrumented layer (guest kernel counters clean, apiserver never stalled, Mac host overflow counter stayed 0 despite an organic 150-conn burst), the shared limactl usernet process is now the best-supported candidate for the SYN-drop layer -- this closes the capture/attribution gap this bead was tracking. Findings: ai/findings/vip-live-capture-attempt-2-2026-08-02.md + blackhole-evidence.txt (worker worktree, not committed). Follow-on mitigation work filed as mayor-mjt51 (investigate limactl usernet / alt Lima network drivers).

title: Conformance host-log collection (journalctl kubelet/crio) truncates to run tail under 16-way load, losing early-run evidence on the busy node
description:
While root-causing container-probe liveness failure in the first --procs=16 conformance run
(0802-0329, mayor-pzgzc), kubelet.log and crio.log for the primary node (lima-node) turned out
to be truncated: earliest line in both files is `Aug 02 03:09:04`, even though the ginkgo
suite started at 03:04:05 and the failing pod's own lifecycle (container start, liveness
probe TCP dial timeout, restart) happened entirely within 03:05:41-03:06:08 — before the
log file's earliest retained line. This made it impossible to determine WHY the TCP liveness
probe timed out (CNI route convergence vs CRI-O scheduling delay vs genuine app slowness) —
only the apiserver-recorded Event trail survived (it's stored in the DB, not the host journal).

Confirmed NOT a per-node-agnostic issue: `kubelet-lima-node-3.log` (the second, less-loaded
node) covers the FULL run, from `Aug 02 03:03:40` (its systemd unit start) through
`03:29:41` — no gap. Only the busier `lima-node`'s kubelet.log/crio.log lost the first ~5
minutes.

scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh:242-245 issues an unbounded
`journalctl -u kubelet --no-pager --utc` / `-u crio --no-pager --utc` per node — no `--since`,
no line cap, so the script itself does not truncate. The truncation happens inside
systemd-journald on the VM: either (a) default RateLimitBurst/RateLimitIntervalSec dropping
kubelet's own log lines once its rate exceeds journald's per-unit burst limit under 16-way
load, or (b) SystemMaxUse/RuntimeMaxUse-driven journal rotation evicting the oldest segment
once total journal disk usage from the much higher 16-way log volume exceeds journald's
default retention quota. No journald tuning exists anywhere in scripts/conformance/ today
(grepped, no hits).

Impact: this is a debugging-capability regression introduced by the same PR #966 that shipped
16-way parallelism as default — the busier a node gets, the more likely we need its kubelet/
crio history to root-cause a failure, and the more likely that exact history has already been
evicted by the time the run finishes and logs are collected.

Suggested fix: tune journald retention (SystemMaxUse/RuntimeMaxUse) and/or rate limits
(RateLimitBurst/RateLimitIntervalSec) upward in the lima VM provisioning
(scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh or the Lima config it references) sized for 16-way
conformance's log volume, OR switch host-log collection to `journalctl --since <run-start>`
plus a documented pre-run journald restart/vacuum so the retained window reliably covers a
full run.

Filed from mayor-pzgzc (Shape 3 audit, read-only, findings doc:
ai/findings/conformance-16way-first-run-triage-2026-08-02.md). Failure 3 (container-probe
liveness restart, test/e2e/common/node/container_probe.go:1779) remains only partially
root-caused: we know WHAT happened (TCP dial i/o timeout during the liveness probe's first
26s, per the apiserver Event trail) but not WHY, because kubelet-level detail for that window
does not exist in this run's artifacts.
close_reason: Shipped as PR #967 (merged 2026-08-02T04:12:49Z). Journald drop-in via scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh raises RateLimitBurst=100000, SystemMaxUse=2G, Storage=persistent. Verified applied on lima-node-2 via systemd-analyze cat-config. Next [Conformance] run should give full kubelet.log/crio.log coverage on the busy node, unblocking mayor-pzgzc failure-3 root-cause.

title: worker-vm.sh: SIGPIPE/pipefail race makes existence check flip false on a running VM
description:
scripts/worker-vm.sh:69 does:

  if limactl list --format '{{.Name}}' 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^${NAME}$"; then

Under 'set -euo pipefail' (line 32), this is a classic SIGPIPE race: grep -q exits as
soon as it finds its match and closes the read end of the pipe. If limactl list hasn't
finished writing all lines yet, its next write gets SIGPIPE and it exits 141. Under
pipefail, the pipeline's exit status becomes 141 (non-zero) even though grep DID find
the match — so the if takes the false branch and the script tries to provision a new VM
with 'limactl start --name=<existing>', which fails loud with 'instance already exists'.

Reproduced directly (mayor-jo1ph, 32-way parallelism experiment on lima-node-4):
  bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; NAME=lima-node-4; if limactl list --format "{{.Name}}" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^${NAME}$"; then echo FOUND; else echo NOTFOUND; fi'
  # => NOTFOUND, despite lima-node-4 being present in `limactl list` every time it was checked manually.

scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh already has the fix for this exact problem (see its
comment at the VM-start block): it checks `[ -d "$HOME/.lima/$VM_NAME" ]` (directory
existence, not a piped grep) precisely because "limactl list can transiently return
empty output if lima is busy, which would otherwise cause the provisioning branch to
run and hit 'instance already exists'". worker-vm.sh's existence checks (lines 69 and
similarly in the delete path) should use the same directory-based check instead of
`limactl list | grep -q`.

Impact: intermittent, not deterministic — reproduced 3/3 times in one session but the
underlying race depends on scheduling, so it may not reproduce every time. Blocked the
mayor-jo1ph worker from starting an already-provisioned VM via the documented
scripts/worker-vm.sh path; worked around by calling `limactl start <vm>` directly.

title: Roll --procs=16 (or tuned N) into 06-run-sonobuoy.sh as the default [Conformance] parallelism, pending flakiness triage
description:
mayor-xz6fg proved a real, large wall-clock win from forcing explicit ginkgo parallelism:
1106s (18.4 min) for 444 [Conformance] specs at --procs=16, vs 6297-6442s (~1.75-1.79h) for
446 specs at the historical serial baseline -- 5.7-5.8x speedup. Mechanism (worktree-only
diff, not yet merged):

  SONOBUOY_BASE_ARGS="run --plugin e2e --wait \
    --plugin-env=e2e.E2E_EXTRA_GINKGO_ARGS=--procs=16 --kubeconfig /tmp/sonobuoy-kubeconfig"

(replaces --e2e-parallel=true, which only exposes ginkgo's auto-detect --p -- 7-way on this
8-vCPU VM, not a numeric override. go-runner's E2E_EXTRA_GINKGO_ARGS env var is the only
numeric hook the stock e2e plugin exposes; see test/conformance/image/go-runner/cmd.go,
release-1.36.)

BUT the same experiment measured real degradation at 16-way vs 1-way: apiserver's
latency_ms>=1000 rate rose ~2.7x (0.228/1k req -> 0.613/1k req) and per-spec failure rate rose
~2.5x (0.45% -> 1.13%), with zero overlap between the baseline's 2 failures and the 16-way
run's 5 failures -- consistent with contention-induced timing flakiness (DNS propagation,
liveness-probe timing, webhook round-trip, daemonset rollback), not new functional bugs, but
unconfirmed.

Before shipping this as the default: re-run --procs=16 at least 2-3 more times to establish
whether the 5 failing specs are flaky (fail intermittently) or deterministic (fail every time)
at this concurrency level. If flaky, this is likely safe to ship with a documented flakiness
note. If deterministic, investigate why (per-spec).

See ai/findings/parallelism-experiment-16-way-2026-08-02.md in mayor-xz6fg's worker worktree
for full numbers and the exact script diff.
notes: Operator decision 2026-08-02 (post-mayor-l6ojx bracket + workflow chat): SHIP 16-way as default now, do flaky-vs-deterministic classification POST-MERGE via the immediate follow-up full [Conformance] rerun the operator planned. Prior bead-description gate ('re-run 2-3 more times before shipping') is superseded by this decision. The 16-way memory ceiling is now bracketed on both sides (16 fits, 24/32 OOM), the 5.76x speedup is real, and any failures the post-merge rerun surfaces will be triaged as normal work rather than blocking the parallelism switch itself. PR: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/966 — ready for mayor merge on green CI.

Expected 5.76x wall-clock speedup on merge gate. Post-merge flaky-vs-deterministic classification will happen via operator's planned full [Conformance] rerun.

title: Audit historical [Conformance] baseline provenance: archived ~2h runs were serial (no --p), not 7/8-way as assumed
description:
mayor-xz6fg's 16-way parallelism experiment discovered that the archived "known-good ~2h
[Conformance] baseline" runs (temp/e2e/0731-0640-conformance, temp/e2e/0730-1446-conformance)
were actually invoked with ginkgo args --focus=\[Conformance\],--skip=,--no-color=true (no
--p at all) and logged "Starting e2e run ... on Ginkgo node 1" (singular) — i.e. fully serial,
not the assumed 7-8-way auto-detect from --e2e-parallel=true. The --skip= value in those
archived runs is also completely empty (not sonobuoy's own default
\[Disruptive\]|NoExecuteTaintManager), suggesting those baseline runs used a different/older
06-run-sonobuoy.sh invocation or a hand-rolled sonobuoy call, not the current script.

Action: find out which run-all.sh version and script path produced those two archived runs
(check git blame / git log on 06-run-sonobuoy.sh around those timestamps), and correct any
internal "2h @ 8-way" framing in bead descriptions / docs that assumed non-serial baseline
parallelism. This affects the interpretation of every prior --focus/--all-e2e wall-clock
comparison that cited "the ~2h baseline."

title: Experiment: raise ginkgo parallelism above auto-detect(8) for --all-e2e, measure per-spec-cost impact
description:
06-run-sonobuoy.sh:137 sets --e2e-parallel=true, which sonobuoy's e2e plugin
(kubernetes/kubernetes test/conformance/image/run_e2e.sh, v1.36.0, lines
60-66) maps to ginkgo's --p flag (auto-detect optimal node count via
runtime.NumCPU() in-container) — not a fixed number. On our 8-vCPU lima-node
VM this yields effective parallelism = 8, vs upstream's ci-kubernetes-e2e-
gce-cos-default-beta job which passes an explicit --ginkgo-parallel=30
(3.75x more lanes) that maps to a literal `ginkgo --nodes=30` and shows up
as ParallelTotal=30 in that job's own junit output.

BUT: upstream's 30-way parallelism runs inside a driver pod capped at 2 vCPU
(1.36-release-jobs.yaml, kubekins-e2e container resources: {cpu: "2", memory:
6Gi}) that is architecturally separate from the 4-VM GCE cluster under test
(1 master + 3 workers, e2-standard-2 each, none sharing a core with the
driver or each other). Our setup shares one 8-core VM (lima-node) between
the ginkgo driver AND kubelet AND CRI-O AND kube-controller-manager AND the
system under test's own pods. The baseline overnight run already recorded
495 5xx and 13 429 responses in apiserver.log at just 8-way concurrency
(mayor-y78ss forensics) — raising parallelism on the same single-node
backend is not guaranteed to be "free" the way it is upstream; per-spec
cost could get worse (retries/backoff), not hold flat.

Scout goal: run --all-e2e (or a bounded --focus subset for faster iteration)
at an explicit higher parallelism (sonobuoy's e2e plugin has no numeric
E2E_PARALLEL override today per run_e2e.sh's case statement — this may
require a plugin-definition override or direct ginkgo invocation instead of
sonobuoy's e2e plugin wrapper; that mechanism question is itself part of the
scout) and measure: (a) whether seconds-per-spec-per-lane holds near today's
~85-90s baseline or increases, (b) apiserver 5xx/429/409/high-latency counts
relative to the 6h baseline's 495/13/2269/10, (c) whether the resulting
wall-clock for --all-e2e's ~7500-spec scope moves meaningfully under the 6h
(or raised, see mayor-d8z7g) ceiling.

Do NOT just hardcode --p=30 into the harness without this experiment — the
isolation-gap argument above is why this is filed as a measurement task, not
a direct config change.

See ai/findings/parallelism-baseline-2026-08-02.md (mayor-uixpn), Question C
(the four-factor delta table and the seconds-per-spec-per-lane arithmetic)
and Question D (why sonobuoy's e2e plugin has no numeric override today).
notes: Follow-on beads filed: mayor-um8ld (audit historical baseline provenance — archived ~2h runs were serial, not 7/8-way), mayor-v59ym (roll --procs=16 into default pending flakiness triage), mayor-jw8wf ([Serial]-tagged specs never actually serialized by go-runner in our setup). Full findings: ai/findings/parallelism-experiment-16-way-2026-08-02.md in worker worktree agent-aaffefc66bd493ee9.
close_reason: Verdict: sublinear-degraded. Mid-task correction confirmed the archived ~2h Conformance baseline runs were actually serial (no --p flag, single Ginkgo node), so this was really a 1-way to 16-way experiment, not 8-way to 16-way as originally framed. Mechanism: plugin-env e2e.E2E_EXTRA_GINKGO_ARGS=--procs=16 (replacing --e2e-parallel=true, which only exposes ginkgos auto-detect -p, verified 7-way on this 8-vCPU VM via crictl inspect). Result: 444 of 7579 Conformance specs in 1106.463s (18.4 min) at 16-way, versus 446 specs in 6297 to 6442s (about 1.75 to 1.79h) serial: 5.7 to 5.8x wall-clock speedup, but per-spec-per-lane cost rose 2.82x (about 36 percent parallel efficiency, not linear). apiserver 5xx/429/409 rates held flat; latency_ms>=1000 rate rose about 2.7x; per-spec failure rate rose about 2.5x with zero overlap between baselines 2 failures and the 16-way runs 5 failures, consistent with contention-induced flakiness, not proven new bugs. Findings: ai/findings/parallelism-experiment-16-way-2026-08-02.md in worker worktree agent-aaffefc66bd493ee9 (gitignored). Script diff pushed to branch worker/agent-aaffefc66bd493ee9, no PR per bead constraints. Follow-on beads: mayor-um8ld, mayor-v59ym, mayor-jw8wf.

title: Raise/parametrize sonobuoy --plugin-timeout for --all-e2e conformance runs
description:
scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh:137 builds SONOBUOY_BASE_ARGS without
ever passing --plugin-timeout, in all three invocation branches (:151 focus,
:160-162 --all-e2e, :165 default certified-conformance). Sonobuoy's own
default plugin timeout is ~6h, which is what killed the overnight --all-e2e
run at exactly 08:31:41Z (6h00m to the second after 02:31:46Z start, per
mayor-y78ss forensics).

This is a documented-vs-configured mismatch, not a guess: run-all.sh:26-36's
own --all-e2e doc comment already says "Wall-clock: ~6-12h vs certified's
~2h — a deliberate discovery/perf-baseline run, not a default." The script's
own authors expected up to 12h for this mode, but nothing raises sonobuoy's
timeout to match, so any --all-e2e run needing more than 6h is silently
truncated by an unrelated default rather than by an --all-e2e-aware budget.

Proposed fix: add a --plugin-timeout flag (or an env var, mirroring the
SONOBUOY_FOCUS pattern) to 06-run-sonobuoy.sh, defaulted higher (e.g. 12h)
specifically in the --all-e2e branch at :160-162, leaving the certified-
conformance default path's timeout unchanged (~2h runs don't need it).

See ai/findings/parallelism-baseline-2026-08-02.md (mayor-uixpn), Question D
and the Verdict section, for the full evidence trail (upstream comparison,
why this is judged the highest-confidence/lowest-risk fix of the two filed
follow-ons).

title: apiserver: list_namespaces silently ignores field_selector on non-watch LIST path (kubectl get ns --field-selector=status.phase=Terminating returns everything)
description:
Discovered while auditing mayor-ie8n3 (2026-08-01 namespace force-delete audit):
`kubectl get namespaces --field-selector=status.phase=Terminating` against the live
apiserver returned EMPTY even though job-8968 was objectively
status.phase=Terminating at the time (confirmed via client-side `jq` filtering of the
full namespace list, and via `kubectl get ns job-8968 -o json`).

Root cause: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/namespaces.rs list_namespaces (lines
58-116) only reads query.field_selector on the `watch=true` branch (passed into
WatchConfig at line ~83-84). The plain-LIST path (lines 95-99) calls
`state.store.list(&prefix, ListOptions::default())` and returns every item
unfiltered — field_selector is silently dropped for non-watch Namespace LIST
requests. Contrast with the generic resource list handler (handlers/resource.rs,
which does call parse_field_selector for its list path, e.g. lines 125/1394/2676/2835).

Impact: any field-selector-based namespace query (a documented, commonly-used kubectl
feature, not just status.phase) silently no-ops on the non-watch path, returning
every namespace regardless of the filter. This directly hindered live debugging
during the mayor-ie8n3 audit — the recommended diagnostic command from the audit
runbook itself returned a false-empty result.

Fix: apply the same field-selector filtering used by the generic resource list path
(or watch_generic's field_selector handling) to list_namespaces's non-watch branch
before returning `items`.

Regression test: create a namespace, delete a namespaced object to reach
Terminating, assert `list_namespaces` with field_selector=status.phase=Terminating
returns exactly that namespace and no others (and that Active namespaces are
excluded).
close_reason: PR #1002 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/1002

title: apiserver: watchdog kubectl patch/delete calls vanish (no trace at all) for minutes under --all-e2e sustained high-concurrency load
description:
Live evidence (2026-08-01 audit, mayor-ie8n3): for at least 2 distinct namespaces from
2 distinct e2e suites, the watchdog's host-side `kubectl patch`/`kubectl delete`
invocations against a specific namespace's own /api/v1/namespaces/<ns> endpoint left
ZERO trace in apiserver.log (no GET/PATCH/DELETE log line at all) for several minutes
at a stretch, even though the apiserver was simultaneously serving huge volumes of
OTHER traffic (545,877 log lines / 54,709 completed HTTP requests in a single 60s
window during one such gap).

Evidence:
- netpol-x-5017: watchdog fired at 07:08:38, 07:10:40, 07:11:11, 07:11:42Z. Only the
  first (07:08:38.647-648Z) and last (07:11:42.928-.993Z) attempts show ANY apiserver
  activity for this namespace's own endpoint; the two middle attempts (07:10:40,
  07:11:11) show nothing at all.
- horizontal-pod-autoscaling-9834: 6 watchdog attempts (05:08:41 to 05:13:49Z); only
  the LAST (05:13:49.557-.720Z) shows any apiserver-side activity for the namespace
  endpoint. The prior 5 left zero trace.

Once a request IS processed, in-handler latency stays low throughout these stall
windows (elapsed_ms/latency_ms max 69ms sampled across 07:09-07:11Z) — ruling out slow
request *handling* as the cause. This points at request/connection loss upstream of
the handler: most likely new short-lived kubectl-CLI TCP+TLS connection setup
starving behind thousands of already-established long-lived watch-stream connections
under --all-e2e's much higher concurrency than certified-conformance mode.

This matters beyond the watchdog script: any real client issuing occasional
short-lived requests (not just kubectl CLI) could see the same multi-minute
invisible-request behavior under sustained load, which is a correctness-adjacent
availability problem, not just a watchdog inconvenience.

Needs: instrument/measure axum's listener accept path and TLS handshake latency
under sustained concurrent watch-stream load (>500 req/s) to confirm/refute the
connection-establishment-starvation hypothesis; check for any single-threaded or
mutex-serialized accept/handshake code path in crates/apiserver's listener setup.

See ai/findings/namespace-force-delete-audit-2026-08-01.md (worker audit doc, not
committed) for full traced evidence, including the falsification hypotheses tested.

title: scout: konnectivity-server died silently 2 min before apiserver in --all-e2e run — cause unknown (likely also FD-exhaustion, unverified)
description:
## Failure

During 2026-07-31 --all-e2e run: konnectivity-server's log stops at 14:45:59Z with no error message (last line is normal `tunnel.go` proxy activity). apiserver kept running for another ~2 min before its own FD-exhaustion crash at 14:47:58Z.

konnectivity-server.log is 104KB total (small compared to apiserver's 455MB) but that's expected — konnectivity logs are per-tunnel, not per-request.

## Suspected cause

Same underlying FD-exhaustion pressure that killed the apiserver (see sibling P1 bead on apiserver FD-limit). konnectivity-server is a Go binary (upstream apiserver-network-proxy), and Go doesn't panic on EMFILE by default — it typically retries or logs and continues. But it also runs under the same macOS-default `ulimit -n 256` if launched from the same shell, and each active tunnel holds at least 2 FDs (client-side + agent-side). ~64K tunnels total across the run per apiserver log counts; even with liberal churn, sustained concurrent tunnel count in the ramp phase likely exceeded 256.

Unverified — konnectivity's silent death without a logged error means the immediate cause could also be OOM, SIGPIPE, or something else. Needs a scout.

## Scout task (SCOUT-ONLY, no fix in this dispatch)

1. Read `temp/u7s/konnectivity-server.log` in full (only 104KB — feasible for a scout to actually read). Look for:
   - Any error/warn lines before 14:45:59
   - Any pattern suggesting cause (tunnel-count ramp, backlog, memory hints)
2. Check whether konnectivity was launched with any ulimit / rlimit adjustment (`scripts/conformance/02-start-apiserver.sh` or wherever it lives). Compare to apiserver launch.
3. Check macOS `dmesg` / system.log around 14:45:59 for any signal-kill or resource-limit indicator.
4. If the cause is confirmed as same FD-exhaustion: recommend the P1 apiserver FD bead's fix ALSO cover konnectivity (both raise ulimit at launch).
5. If cause is different: report the actual mechanism.

## Not in scope

- Fixing anything. Diagnosis only.
- Adjusting DRA test skip lists (separate bead if we want it — the DRA test flood was the LOAD driver but not the root cause).

## Discovered

Same --all-e2e run failure 2026-07-31.

## Cross-ref

Sibling P1 bead: apiserver FD-exhaustion (filed in same session). If konnectivity died from the same cause, both close together via one shared ulimit fix.
notes:
VERDICT: No crash occurred. konnectivity-server (pid 11781) ran continuously, uninterrupted, for the entire incident window and beyond -- it did NOT die at 14:45:59Z or any other point during the 2026-07-31 run. The apparent "silence" is simply an absence of traffic to log, not a process death.

Evidence (timestamps are native UTC -- both konnectivity launch points in scripts/u7s-start.sh:163,289 prefix `TZ=UTC`, so no conversion needed):

1. Single continuous process, no restart: the startup banner (options.go:174-211, "Starting frontend/agent/admin/health server") appears exactly ONCE at 0731 13:40:36, pid 11781. It never reappears. If the process had crashed and been relaunched (even under a coincidentally-reused pid), the startup banner would repeat. It does not.

2. Zero error/warn/panic lines anywhere before shutdown. Full grep for `^[EWF]` prefixed klog lines across the whole 642-line file returns nothing until the shutdown trailer at line 636+ (E0801 01:34:46 "failed to listen on frontend port" err="http: Server closed" -- the expected benign artifact of a graceful Shutdown() call, not a crash).

3. Perfectly balanced tunnel lifecycle: `grep -c tunnel.go:58` (CONNECT received) = 73, `tunnel.go:193` (starting proxy) = 73, `tunnel.go:209` (EOF from host) = 73. Every single tunnel opened during the run also closed cleanly and was logged closing. No leaked/orphaned tunnel FDs are visible in konnectivity's own accounting.

4. Last real log line: `I0731 14:45:59.757183 11781 tunnel.go:209 "EOF from host" host="sample-api.aggregator-6697.svc:7443" ... connectionID=39` -- a clean EOF, immediately following a clean CONNECT/200-OK/proxy-start sequence 3ms earlier. This is normal steady-state operation, not a truncated/aborted sequence.

5. apiserver-side corroboration: grep of apiserver.log (path /Users/balint.erdos/u7s/temp/u7s/apiserver.log) shows the aggregator-6697 namespace (the e2e "Aggregator" conformance test that installs sample-apiserver and requires konnectivity tunneling to reach it) being TORN DOWN starting at 2026-07-31T14:46:04.835628Z (deleting events/aggregator-6697/sample-apiserver-deployment-*). This lines up exactly with the last konnectivity tunnel activity 5 seconds earlier -- the test that needed the tunnel finished and cleaned up; no later test in the run needed konnectivity again before apiserver's own crash.

6. apiserver continued operating normally, WITHOUT needing konnectivity, for the next ~1m54s: `GET /api/v1/nodes/lima-node:10250/proxy/pods status=200 latency_ms=1` succeeds repeatedly at 14:46:37, 14:46:43, 14:47:03, 14:47:06, 14:47:24, 14:47:26, 14:47:34 -- these calls bypass konnectivity entirely (kubelet is reached via the host-forwarded --kubelet-preferred-address, not the pod-network address that required tunneling earlier in the run). No 5xx/timeout/connection-refused/dial-error lines appear anywhere in apiserver.log in the 14:44-14:48 window.

7. apiserver's own crash at 14:47:58Z (Error: Too many open files (os error 24), root-caused separately in mayor-sgu1p) is what permanently ended konnectivity's traffic -- apiserver is konnectivity's only client in this topology. Once apiserver died, konnectivity had nothing left to proxy and correctly had nothing more to log. It kept running as an orphan (nobody supervises/reaps it independently) until the mayor killed it with a graceful shutdown signal at 0801 01:34:46 UTC (~8 min before this scout was dispatched, matching the operational note) -- producing the clean "Shutting down server" / "http: Server closed" / "Stream read from agent cancelled" trailer, which is the signature of a graceful SIGTERM-driven shutdown, not a SIGKILL/OOM/crash.

8. Best-effort OS check: `/usr/bin/log show --style syslog --predicate 'process == "proxy-server-darwin-arm64"'` for the 23:44-23:48 JST window (=14:44-14:48Z) returned zero entries -- no crash report, no jetsam/resource-limit kill event recorded. (Sanity-checked the tool against the KNOWN apiserver crash at the same time -- also zero hits, so the unified log apparently doesn't retain/surface either event in this environment; treating this step as non-diagnostic/inconclusive rather than as contradicting evidence, per the file-log evidence above which is definitive.)

9. Launch topology check (scripts/u7s-start.sh): apiserver and konnectivity-server are BOTH forked (via `&`) from the SAME bash shell/script invocation, not separate shell processes -- no `ulimit -n` call exists anywhere in scripts/ today for either. This means if the sibling P1 fix (mayor-sgu1p) adds `ulimit -n <N>` as a shell command early in u7s-start.sh (before either `&`-launch), it would automatically cover konnectivity-server too, since ulimit is inherited by all descendants forked afterward in the same shell. HOWEVER: if the fix is instead implemented as a Rust-level `setrlimit()` call inside src/main.rs (apiserver binary only, per the bead's "possibly src/main.rs" scope note), it would raise ONLY the apiserver process's own limit and would NOT propagate to konnectivity-server (a separate already-forked Go binary) at all. This is unverified from my worktree (mayor-sgu1p's diff is in a separate worktree) -- flagging for the mayor to confirm which form the fix takes, since only the shell-level form covers both processes for free.

CONCLUSION: Since konnectivity-server never hit its FD ceiling (73 tunnels total, 1:1 balanced lifecycle, well under even a low 256 default) and never crashed at all during this incident, there is no evidence it needs the same fix to remain functionally correct for this specific bug. It would still be reasonable defense-in-depth to raise its ulimit alongside apiserver's (cheap, and the launch topology allows a single shell-level ulimit line to cover both) -- but that is a hardening recommendation, not a fix for a confirmed bug, since no konnectivity failure was found.
close_reason: No crash: konnectivity-server (pid 11781) ran continuously and uninterrupted the whole time -- log silence after 14:45:59Z is just absence of traffic (the aggregator test using it finished/tore down at 14:46:04Z), not a death. Process only stopped when the mayor sent it a graceful shutdown just now (0801 01:34:46Z). Cross-ref mayor-sgu1p (apiserver's own unrelated FD-exhaustion crash at 14:47:58Z, confirmed root cause) -- no evidence konnectivity needs that fix, though the shared launch shell (scripts/u7s-start.sh) would let one shell-level ulimit line cover both for free if the mayor wants defense-in-depth.

title: GUARDRAIL: scheduler fast-path preemption bind must never diverge from slow-path correctness
description:
## Origin

Surfaced 2026-07-31 by mayor-igcb4 restart-safety audit (§5) as an optional preventative guardrail for mayor-i4mwr's Option A (event-driven deferred bind for preemption).

The audit found current code SAFE (8/8 structures), but flagged: the new "victim → waiting pods" map, if built without care, could become a distinct code path with its own correctness story that diverges from the slow path. This is a design-guardrail, not a bug fix — file so the guarantee is asserted in code, not just documented in the PR.

## Task

Add a unit test (or a doc-comment contract on the fast-path binding function, plus a test that verifies it) asserting:

1. **A pod with `nominatedNodeName` set is never excluded from `pods_needing_resync`'s retry population** (crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs:633-647). The 30s resync loop is the durable correctness backstop that makes losing the in-memory map merely a latency regression; excluding nominated pods from resync reintroduces the stuck-forever failure mode that motivated the audit.

2. **The map's bind-on-victim-DELETE fast path re-verifies fit via the same `verify_and_reserve_preemption`-style check before binding** (crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs:1805-1855). The fast path is not a distinct code path — it is the slow path's own reservation-then-verify logic, triggered earlier. Never bind pod P to node N purely because "the map says P was waiting on victim V and V just DELETEd" without re-checking P still fits N under the current tally.

## Test shape

- Unit test in `crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs` (or wherever the map lives once built).
- Construct a scenario where the fast path *could* bind but the tally has drifted between the plan and the DELETE event (e.g. another pod claimed capacity). Assert the fast path REFUSES to bind and falls back to the slow path.
- Second unit test: assert `pods_needing_resync` still returns a pod with `nominatedNodeName` set when `spec.nodeName` is empty. Fail-on-revert: filter out such pods and the test breaks.

## Bundling

Should be folded into the mayor-i4mwr PR — same code surface, same review context. If i4mwr's PR ships without these tests, this bead stays open as a follow-up.

## Not in scope
- Fixing anything unrelated to Option A's correctness guarantee.
- Any change if mayor-i4mwr chooses a different fix shape (Option B or another).
notes: bundled with mayor-i4mwr in same PR — dispatched together 2026-07-31
close_reason: shipped bundled with mayor-i4mwr in PR #957 — guardrail unit tests A+B assert fast path never diverges from slow path

title: sig-apimachinery CRD conversion webhook Service call fails: e2e-test-crd-conversion-webhook.crd-webhook-2028.svc:9443/crdconvert unreachable
description:
## Failure **Test:** `[sig-api-machinery] CustomResourceConversionWebhook [Privileged:ClusterAdmin] should be able to convert a non homogeneous list of CRs [Conformance]` **File:** `k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/apimachinery/crd_conversion_webhook.go:472` **Run:** temp/e2e/0730-1446-conformance (2-node: lima-node + lima-node-3) ## Evidence (quoted from e2e.txt) Test flow (from timeline): - 13:43:51 — Create RoleBinding for webhook to read extension-apiserver-authentication (OK) - 13:43:51 — Deploy the crd-conversion-webhook pod (OK — replicaset created) - 13:43:53 — "Waiting for amount of service crd-webhook-2028/e2e-test-crd-conversion-webhook endpoints to be 1" — some transition delay - 13:43:53 — Assertion fails at line 472: ``` conversion webhook call failed: error sending request for url (https://e2e-test-crd-conversion-webhook.crd-webhook-2028.svc:9443/crdconvert) ``` The apiserver's CRD-conversion-webhook client attempted to POST to the webhook Service's DNS name+port and could not reach it. ## Suspected causes (not diagnosed, needs a scout) 1. **Konnectivity tunnel routing:** the apiserver-side webhook client uses konnectivity to reach in-cluster services. If konnectivity routing to the crd-webhook-2028 namespace is broken (e.g. pod scheduled to lima-node-3, tunnel only bound to lima-node), the call fails. 2. **Service ClusterIP allocation** — mayor-pjjb4 flagged that u7s hardcodes some Service ClusterIPs; if the auto-allocator has a gap on cross-node-scheduled Service backends, this could bite. 3. **Cross-node pod networking** — pgm5q Phase-2 work is closed as verified-obsolete based on the 0730-0222 446/446 pass, but if the webhook pod landed on lima-node-3 and its Service backend endpoint is only reachable via cross-node routing that the apiserver-outbound path doesn't traverse, that's the exact class of gap pgm5q.7/.8 originally worried about. 4. **DNS resolution** — the URL uses `.svc` short-name; if apiserver-side resolution of `e2e-test-crd-conversion-webhook.crd-webhook-2028.svc` fails, the request never leaves. 5. **Timing** — test's endpoint-wait may be too aggressive; 2s between endpoint-wait log and assertion is tight for a fresh pod's readiness → endpoint registration cycle. ## Not related to today's scheduler chain This test lives entirely in the CRD/webhook path. None of the four scheduler-chain PRs (#948 74j3.7, #953 efhom, #954 u0dpc, #955 krae9) touch webhook plumbing. This is either: - a pre-existing gap that got exercised for the first time in this run (test not present in 0730-0222 baseline — grep count 0), or - an environmental flake specific to this run. ## Regression baseline Test not present in the 0730-0222 baseline. Same 446-count in both runs, so test-selection composition differs. First order of business: repro to confirm it's persistent, not a one-off timing flake. ## Reproduction ``` scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --vm --port

--kubelet-port \ --workdir ./temp/u7s --reset \ --focus 'should be able to convert a non homogeneous list of CRs' ``` ## Acceptance criteria - Live-repro (confirm persistent, not one-off flake): retry the same test 3× on a fresh --reset stack; if it consistently fails, proceed to diagnosis. - Diagnose: which of the 5 suspected causes above (or a 6th) is the actual mechanism? Log evidence from apiserver.log, kubelet, konnectivity-server, or CoreDNS as appropriate. - Fix at the identified layer. If the fix touches cross-node webhook routing, re-check whether pgm5q Phase-2 items need to be re-opened. - Sonobuoy `--focus` on this test passes. ## Labels rationale P2: [Conformance]-tagged and legitimate correctness gap, but not blocking session — one failed test in a webhook subsystem that's not in a hot-critical path. Elevate to P1 if repro confirms it also breaks other webhook Conformance tests.
