title: scheduler: preemption force-double-DELETE makes victims 404 before graceful-termination pollers ever see DeletionTimestamp
description:
Discovered while verifying mayor-efhom (status.nominatedNodeName on
preemption plan commit) against the real upstream e2e test via sonobuoy,
2026-07-30, VM lima-node-4, focus "validates various priority Pods
preempt expectedly with the async preemption".

The scout (mayor-m6kzq) inferred this test's FIRST blocking assertion
was line 435 (highPod.Status.NominatedNodeName != ""). A real sonobuoy
run against the upstream test (not the scout's simplified 3-pod repro)
shows the test actually fails EARLIER, at preemption.go:402:

  [FAILED] Pod "pod0-0-sched-preemption-low-priority" not found
  In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/scheduling/preemption.go:402

Test flow (test/e2e/scheduling/preemption.go, release-1.36, function
starting at line 319): 10 low-priority pods are created and scheduled
(lines 322-373); 10 medium-priority pods are then created requesting the
SAME scarce resource as the low-priority pods (lines 378-396) -- since
medium priority outranks low, THIS ALONE triggers preemption in u7s's
scheduler (our scheduler does not distinguish "low"/"medium"/"high" as
special-cased tiers, only numeric priority) well before any high-priority
pod exists. The test then polls (lines 400-409) for each low-priority
pod to show `DeletionTimestamp != nil` -- i.e. it expects the victim to
still be GETtable, just marked for graceful termination. Each
low-priority pod carries `TerminationGracePeriodSeconds: 80` and a
`PreStopHookSleepSeconds: 79`, specifically so upstream's real
kube-scheduler (which only soft-deletes and waits out the grace period)
leaves it observable in this state for up to 80s.

u7s's `delete_pod` (crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs) does not implement this:
it issues DELETE twice back-to-back ("equivalent to kubectl delete
--grace-period=0 --force") specifically to bypass any multi-round wait.
Consequently a victim goes from Running to genuinely gone (404) within
about a second of being targeted, never staying observable in a
"DeletionTimestamp set, still Gettable" state long enough for a client
polling once a second (this test's poll interval) to reliably catch the
transition -- confirmed live: pod0-0 got its Scheduled/Pulling/Started/
Pulled events at 11:28:59, medium-priority pods that outrank it were
created at 11:29:05.155, and by the test's very next poll at 11:29:06.222
the apiserver already returned 404 (not "has deletionTimestamp").

This is NOT caused by, or related to, mayor-efhom's fix (status.
nominatedNodeName write) -- that change only adds a PATCH call BEFORE
`evict_victims` runs; `delete_pod`'s own force-double-DELETE eviction
path is untouched by it. Because this failure occurs strictly EARLIER in
the test's chronological flow than the NominatedNodeName wait at line
435, this test cannot currently be used to confirm the NominatedNodeName
fix's effect on the real upstream scenario -- mayor-efhom's fix was
independently, directly verified via a targeted kubectl repro instead
(watching status.nominatedNodeName go non-empty on a pod while
still Pending, i.e. before the eviction+bind cycle completed).

Fix candidates (not scoped/investigated in depth -- pick one after
reading upstream's real Executor.PreemptPod grace-period handling):
1. Make preemption evictions a normal graceful DELETE (respecting
   spec.terminationGracePeriodSeconds, no force-double-DELETE), matching
   upstream kube-scheduler and letting the kubelet's own termination
   lifecycle (including preStop hooks) run to completion before the
   object is actually removed from the store. Removes the "MVP
   explicitly skips that multi-round wait" shortcut noted in delete_pod's
   own doc comment -- re-introduces exactly the wait that shortcut was
   trying to avoid, so needs to be weighed against whatever motivated it.
2. Something narrower and less invasive, e.g. only single-DELETE (soft,
   not force) for preemption evictions specifically, leaving the
   kubelet's normal graceful-termination watch loop to actually remove
   the pod once the container exits -- needs checking whether u7s's
   kubelet-side finalizer/GC path actually handles that correctly today
   (may itself have gaps, since the MVP shortcut exists in the first
   place, presumably to route around one).

Acceptance criteria for the fix:
- Re-run sonobuoy --focus "validates various priority Pods preempt
  expectedly with the async preemption" and confirm the failure point
  moves PAST preemption.go:402 (to line 435's NominatedNodeName wait, or
  further).
- Regression test (unit or integration) asserting a preemption-evicted
  pod remains GETtable with a non-nil deletionTimestamp for some window
  after DELETE, not immediately 404 -- must fail if delete_pod reverts to
  the force-double-DELETE shortcut.
- Understand and document why delete_pod's force-double-DELETE shortcut
  was originally introduced (git blame / bead history) before removing
  it, to avoid reintroducing whatever bug it fixed.
close_reason: Preemption DELETE now respects grace period; victims stay observable with DeletionTimestamp until grace expires (or the container actually exits, whichever comes first). See PR #954: live kubectl+apiserver.log repro on lima-node-4 shows the scheduler's single soft-DELETE at 12:15:17, pod stays 200/Running until the real kubelet issues the completing hard-DELETE at 12:15:42 (after its container exited), then 404 at 12:16:07. Sonobuoy focus 'validates various priority Pods preempt expectedly with the async preemption' still fails at preemption.go:402, but the failure mechanism changed from 'Pod not found' (this bug) to a 5-minute poll timeout caused by a different, already-tracked bug (concurrent preemption plans double-targeting the same victim in find_preemption_plan/select_preemption_victims — mayor-krae9's in-flight surface, same file, out of scope here). Two new regression tests verified to fail on revert: u7s-scheduler::delete_pod_sends_exactly_one_delete_request, u7s-apiserver::single_delete_leaves_pod_gettable_with_deletion_timestamp.

title: scheduler: concurrent equal-priority preemption can double-target victims, causing genuine kubelet OutOfResource rejections
description:
Live-verified while implementing mayor-efhom (status.nominatedNodeName on
preemption plan commit), 2026-07-30, VM lima-node-4.

Once nominatedNodeName is written correctly (mayor-efhom lands), the
SchedulerAsyncPreemption scenario (3 equal-priority low-priority fillers,
1 extended resource unit each, capacity 3; 3 concurrent equal-priority
high-priority preemptors applied simultaneously) now reproducibly fails
2 of 3 preemptors with a genuine kubelet-side admission rejection:

  status:
    phase: Failed
    reason: OutOfscheduling.k8s.io/foo
    message: 'Pod was rejected: Node did not have enough resource:
      scheduling.k8s.io/foo, requested: 1, used: 3, capacity: 3'

This reproduced twice in a row with the mayor-efhom fix applied; a
back-to-back baseline run on the pre-fix scheduler binary (same scenario,
same node, same VM) completed with all 3 preemptors Running. Scheduler
log for a failing run shows all three concurrent preempt_and_pick_node
calls independently plan and commit a reservation for exactly ONE victim
each (filler-0), and all three issue their own DELETE against the SAME
filler-0 (visible as three separate "evicted pod default/filler-0"
lines) -- filler-1 and filler-2 are never evicted. This is the exact
mechanism the scout (mayor-m6kzq, ai/findings/scheduler-async-preemption-
fairness-scout-2026-07-30.md) already named "candidate 2": independent
find_preemption_plan/verify_and_reserve_preemption calls have no
visibility into victims another in-flight (reserved-but-not-yet-evicted)
plan has already claimed, and equal-priority tie-breaking makes every
concurrent plan pick the same cheapest victim. The scout's original repro
called this harmless (idempotent redundant DELETEs, capacity conserved
correctly) because in that run only one plan ever needed exactly one
victim and the others also fit without a real deficit; this run shows
the same overlap can leave real demand unfreed (2 units still needed,
only 1 unit's victim actually evicted) and the two preemptors that don't
fit get force-bound anyway (our tally's optimistic reservation lets them
through) only to be rejected by the real kubelet's own independent
admission check once bound -- a genuine scheduling failure, not just
wasted work.

Root cause (best understanding from log/code review, not from added
tracing -- worth confirming with debug logging before fixing):
verify_and_reserve_preemption's fresh re-check is only atomic with
respect to OTHER verify_and_reserve_preemption calls; it says nothing
about which victims are STILL VALID once a fresher reservation exists.
Because the check only re-verifies aggregate pod-count/resource totals
against the SPECIFIC victim list computed earlier by that same call's
(possibly stale) search phase, it can still pass even when two
concurrent plans have overlapping victims, as long as each call's own
before/after arithmetic happens to balance out against whatever the
tally showed at ITS OWN check instant -- this needs a debug-log-backed
repro to nail down the precise interleaving before designing a fix.
Candidate 2 in the scout's doc already describes the general-shape fix:
track in-flight victim claims in NodeTally so a pod already claimed by
another reserved-but-not-yet-evicted plan is excluded as a candidate in
select_preemption_victims.

Not scoped as "genuine over-subscription" (capacity=3, exactly 3
preemptors, exactly 3 fillers -- the balanced case the scout already
tested) -- this is the SAME balanced case now failing, apparently more
readily reproducible once nominatedNodeName's extra PATCH round-trip is
in the critical path before eviction (not confirmed as causal vs. just a
wider/different race window; needs its own investigation).

Repro (same as scout's, mayor-efhom's fix applied):
```
kubectl apply -f - <<'EOF'
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: low-priority-x}
value: 100
---
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata: {name: high-priority-x}
value: 1000
EOF
kubectl patch node <node> --subresource=status --type=merge \
  -p '{"status":{"capacity":{"scheduling.k8s.io/foo":"3"},"allocatable":{"scheduling.k8s.io/foo":"3"}}}'
# 3x filler pods, low-priority-x, requests/limits scheduling.k8s.io/foo: "1" each, wait Running.
# 3x preemptor pods, high-priority-x, same request, applied simultaneously.
kubectl get pods -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PHASE:.status.phase,REASON:.status.reason
```

Acceptance criteria for the fix:
- The 3-way balanced scenario above ends with all 3 preemptors Running
  (0 Failed/OutOfResource pods), reproducibly across multiple runs.
- Root-cause confirmed with debug-log tracing of the actual
  verify_and_reserve_preemption interleaving (not just log-timestamp
  inference) before choosing a fix shape.
- Regression test on NodeTally/select_preemption_victims covering
  concurrent equal-priority victim selection, mirroring
  verify_and_reserve_preemption_never_double_books_shared_victims's
  real-concurrent-thread style.
- Re-run sonobuoy --focus "validates various priority Pods preempt
  expectedly with the async preemption" and confirm it passes fully (or
  narrow further if a different, later assertion is what's left failing).
close_reason: Fixed via PR #955: NodeTally now tracks in-flight victim claims (reserved_victims set) so concurrent equal-priority preemption plans no longer double-target the same victim; pods_on() excludes claimed-but-unevicted victims from search/re-verify, claim released once eviction finishes/abandons. Also found+fixed a second bug during live confirmation: apply_event wrongly erased assume() reservations on watch-echoes of the nominatedNodeName status PATCH. Live-verified 4/4 clean 3v3 runs (all preemptors Running, zero OutOfResource). 4 new regression tests, all confirmed to fail on revert.

title: feat(scheduler): set status.nominatedNodeName when a preemption plan is committed
description:
Scout mayor-m6kzq found the SchedulerAsyncPreemption e2e test fails
deterministically at its FIRST wait step (line 435 of
test/e2e/scheduling/preemption.go, release-1.36: polls for
highPod.Status.NominatedNodeName != "") because u7s's scheduler never
writes status.nominatedNodeName anywhere -- grep of crates/scheduler/
for "nominated" returns zero hits. This blocks the test at ANY
contention level, not just 10-way; it's a missing-feature gap, not a
subtle race. No feature-gate infra is needed: SchedulerAsyncPreemption
is Beta+Default:true since k8s 1.33, and upstream's WithFeatureGate is
a pure Ginkgo label (test/e2e/framework/ginkgowrapper.go:513-530), not
a runtime cluster-gate check.

Fix: patch the pending pod's status.nominatedNodeName to the planned
node as soon as find_preemption_plan/verify_and_reserve_preemption
succeeds in crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs, called from
preempt_and_pick_node in crates/scheduler/src/main.rs -- BEFORE any
victim is evicted (matches upstream's nominate-then-evict-async
semantics). Mirror the existing disruption_target_patch /
scheduling_gate_status_patch pattern: pure function building the PATCH
body + one call site. No apiserver changes needed --
nominatedNodeName marshalling/field-selector support already exists
(core_gen_adapter.rs:2074, handlers/pods.rs:120).

Acceptance criteria:
- find_preemption_plan's success path results in a PATCH of the
  pending pod's status.nominatedNodeName to the planned node before
  any victim is evicted.
- Unit test on the patch-body builder (pure function, no network,
  mirrors disruption_target_patch's existing test style) -- must be
  a fail-on-revert regression test per project convention.
- Live verification: reproduce the 3-way scenario in the scout's
  findings doc (ai/findings/scheduler-async-preemption-fairness-scout-2026-07-30.md)
  and confirm kubectl get pod <preemptor> -o jsonpath='{.status.nominatedNodeName}'
  is non-empty while eviction is still in flight (not just after bind).
- Attempt sonobuoy --focus SchedulerPreemption and report whether the
  async-preemption test's FIRST failure point moves past the
  NominatedNodeName wait. Full green is NOT required to close this bead
  -- only confirming this specific blocker is gone. If the test still
  fails later (e.g. the "no more than 5*nodeListLen medium pods
  scheduled" assertion, or starvation under genuine over-subscription
  from the scout's candidate 2/3), file a NEW follow-on scout/bead for
  that rather than expanding this one's scope.

Cross-ref: mayor-m6kzq (scout), PR #842 / mayor-ouuo5 (prior preemption
race fix this builds on).
close_reason: status.nominatedNodeName now set on preemption plan commit before any victim eviction, matching upstream nominate-then-evict-async semantics. Live-verified non-empty mid-eviction via targeted kubectl repro. Sonobuoy focus on the real e2e test hits an earlier, unrelated blocker (preemption.go:402, force-delete visibility gap) rather than confirming line 435 directly -- filed as mayor-u0dpc. Also found and filed mayor-krae9 (pre-existing duplicate-victim-targeting race now manifesting as real kubelet rejections). See PR #953.

title: Namespace created via apply/patch-create gets empty status (missing phase:Active default), breaking default-SA reconciliation
description:
Discovered as a byproduct of mayor-effuh's sig-storage live-repro investigation
(see ai/findings/storage-live-repro-2026-07-30.md, "Cross-cutting patterns" for
full evidence). Not one of mayor-effuh's 9 target tests; filed separately.

## Bug

Namespaces created via `kubectl apply` (server-side-apply / create-via-apply
codepath) are persisted with an empty `status: {}`, whereas the same manifest
created via plain `kubectl create` (clientset Create()/POST) correctly gets
`status: {phase: Active}`.

Evidence (same apiserver, ~2s apart):
- `kubectl create namespace repro-plain` -> `.status: {phase: Active}`
- `kubectl apply -f <identical manifest>` (repro-apply) -> `.status: {}`

## Impact

kube-controller-manager's ServiceAccount controller skips reconciling the
default ServiceAccount for namespaces whose status.phase != Active (this
matches real upstream KCM behavior — it is not a KCM bug). Result: any
namespace created via `kubectl apply` (a very common pattern, e.g.
`kubectl apply -f install.yaml` bundling a Namespace + workloads) never gets
its `default` ServiceAccount. Confirmed via 5+ minutes elapsed with zero
`default` SA and zero related KCM log activity for an apply-created
namespace, vs. 3s for a plain-created one.

Any pod in the affected namespace with the pod-spec default
`automountServiceAccountToken: true` gets stuck in ContainerCreating forever.
kubelet logs a misleading cause:
  "Error preparing data for projected volume kube-api-access-*: ... failed to
  fetch token: the API server does not have TokenRequest endpoints enabled"
The real cause is confirmed via `kubectl create token default -n <ns>` ->
`ServiceAccount "default" not found` — TokenRequest itself works fine.

## Suspected root cause

The apiserver's create-via-apply/patch-based object creation path likely
bypasses the same REST "PrepareForCreate" resource-specific defaulting logic
that the plain-create path uses to set Namespace.Status.Phase = Active on
creation. Worth checking whether other resource types have similar
creation-time status defaulting that the apply path also skips.

## Acceptance criteria

- Namespaces created via `kubectl apply` get `status.phase: Active` set at
  creation time, identical to plain `kubectl create`.
- Regression test: apply-create a Namespace, assert status.phase == Active
  immediately (no watch/poll needed since this is a creation-time default).
- Manually verify: apply-create a namespace, confirm KCM creates its default
  ServiceAccount within a few seconds (matching plain-create behavior).
close_reason: Apply-create path now defaults Namespace.status.phase=Active (matches plain-create + upstream). See PR #950 + kubectl live verification quoted in PR body. Related-defaulting sweep found CRD's patch_crd has a distinct/worse gap (no SSA create-on-missing at all, 404s instead) — filed as follow-on mayor-tvhei; CSR and CR resource types confirmed unaffected.

title: fix(scripts): 06-run-sonobuoy.sh pre-check races on SIGPIPE, spuriously fails before sonobuoy launches
description:
Found while running mayor-pgm5q.6 verification (2026-07-30). 06-run-sonobuoy.sh contains a pre-check of the form:

  kubectl get nodes | grep -q "$VM_NAME"

Under 'set -o pipefail', grep exits 0 on match, SIGPIPEs kubectl, and pipefail surfaces kubectl's 141 as the pipeline exit. Result: the pre-check fails ('lima-node-2 not registered') even when the node IS registered — the same command run interactively passes cleanly. Symptom: sonobuoy focus/full runs abort ~3 min into a fresh --reset before the test actually launches, wasting the whole bring-up.

Reproducible in pgm5q.6 verification worktree at 2026-07-30T04:37Z; cluster was healthy at exit time (verified via kubectl get nodes 1h later).

Fix: either drop pipefail for that line, or replace with:
  kubectl get nodes -o name | grep -Fxq "node/$VM_NAME"
with pipefail off around it, or:
  kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}' | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -Fxq "$VM_NAME"

Grep the whole scripts/conformance/ tree for similar 'set -o pipefail' + 'grep -q' patterns before shipping — likely more than one instance.

Acceptance: (1) the check reliably passes when nodes are up; (2) the 2 target pgm5q.6 tests can complete via run-all.sh --focus without hitting this flake; (3) any similar patterns elsewhere in scripts/conformance/ are fixed in the same PR.
close_reason: Fixed 06-run-sonobuoy.sh pre-check SIGPIPE+pipefail bug (and identical sibling in lima-start.sh); grepped scripts/conformance/ for other instances, none found. See PR #945.

title: Investigate: PVC/PV/VolumeAttributesClass delete-confirmation times out at 30s
description:
Found during mayor-rwbd storage/volume audit (ai/findings/storage-volume-audit-2026-07-30.md).

Two sig-storage conformance tests hit an identical symptom: Delete() (or DeleteCollection())
returns success, but the test's follow-up List() (polling up to 30s) still shows the object,
so the test times out waiting for confirmed deletion:
- [sig-storage] PersistentVolumes CSI Conformance should run through the lifecycle of a PV and a PVC
  (temp/research/persistent_volumes.go:536-679, PVC and PV deletion both confirmed this way)
- [sig-storage] VolumeAttributesClass should run through the lifecycle of a VolumeAttributesClass
  (temp/research/volumeattributesclass.go:87-171, both Delete and DeleteCollection variants)

The natural theory — "u7s adds kubernetes.io/pvc-protection / pv-protection / vac-protection
finalizers on create like real kube-apiserver admission does, but no controller ever removes
them, leaving the object stuck Terminating" — was RULED OUT by this audit via code inspection:
`grep -rn "protection" crates/` only turns up these finalizer strings in comments and test
fixtures (e.g. resource.rs:7764 constructs a *test* PVC with that finalizer already present, to
exercise the generic finalizer-drain-via-PUT completion mechanism in isolation) — no
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/defaults.rs code path or admission step actually attaches any of
these finalizers to a real PVC/PV/VolumeAttributesClass on creation. crates/controller-manager/src
has no protection-controller file of any kind (only endpoint_slice_controller.rs,
endpoint_slice_mirroring_controller.rs, statefulset_controller.rs, namespace_controller.rs).
Since nothing injects the finalizer, nothing should be blocking the delete under that theory —
so the real mechanism causing the 30s timeout is unknown.

This bead should start with mayor-effuh's live-repro (does this even still reproduce on current
HEAD?) before any code changes. If it does reproduce:

Acceptance criteria:
- kubectl-repro: create + Delete() a PVC and a VolumeAttributesClass against current HEAD;
  immediately after Delete() returns, `kubectl get <resource> <name> -o yaml` to see actual
  object state (finalizers present? deletionTimestamp set but object still listed? object
  actually gone from the store but stale in a list/watch cache?).
- Identify the actual blocking mechanism (may be: DELETE handler treats these resources as
  needing external confirmation it never gets; a stale list-cache; a resourceVersion/watch
  bookmark race; something else entirely).
- Fix it, or if it does not reproduce, close as stale (same pattern as mayor-25ap/mayor-n3yk).
close_reason: Verified-stale via mayor-effuh's live-repro (2026-07-30). The 2 delete-confirmation-timeout tests this bead was scoped to (PV/PVC lifecycle #7, VolumeAttributesClass lifecycle #9) BOTH pass on current HEAD — kubectl repro shows deletes confirm in the same second they're issued, nowhere near the tests' 30s budget. The 'unknown-mechanism 30s timeout' this bead posited does not exist on HEAD. See ai/findings/storage-live-repro-2026-07-30.md per-test evidence (in worker worktree ai/worktrees/agent-ac2283f1cc9b4b11d/).

title: investigate(apiserver): silent mid-run stop during [sig-node] Pods Extended pod-generation 500-podspec-updates stress test (xi9bd 2026-07-30)
description:
During xi9bd's conformance run on lima-node-smoke, u7s apiserver stopped serving mid-run at 15:59:55.122 UTC. No panic message, no shutdown log, no graceful-shutdown trace — just clean cessation of log output while the last-served request was in the middle of `[sig-node] Pods Extended (pod generation) Pod Generation issue 500 podspec updates and verify generation and observedGeneration eventually converge [MinimumKubeletVersion:1.34] [Conformance]`. VM (lima-node-smoke) stayed alive throughout; only the apiserver process died. Sonobuoy hung for ~5h with no cluster to talk to.

MAYOR'S INITIAL OOM GUESS WAS WRONG per operator: 'There is no way it'd be OOM-killed. We hardly use any memory.' Retracted.

REAL QUESTIONS to answer:
1. What actually killed the apiserver? Check the systemd/lima side: did the apiserver process exit code 0 (graceful) or non-zero (panic/kill)? Check for OOM-killer messages in dmesg/journal despite the operator's expected-low-memory footprint (there could be a leak we don't know about — VERIFY, don't assume). Check for a panic that got swallowed before stderr was flushed to file.
2. Is the failing test (`Pods Extended pod-generation 500 podspec updates`) a reliably-reproducing killer, or was this a one-off? It's a stress pattern (500 PUT /pods/.../status in tight loop) that stresses watch fanout + store write path. Related to prior investigations of watch delivery under load.
3. What's in the last few seconds of apiserver.log before it stopped? Log was actively writing debug (--verbose was on for the xi9bd bench). Was there a specific request pattern immediately before the stop? Any 'connection reset' / stream errors that could correlate with a resource exhaustion different from memory (file descriptors, tokio task budget, sqlite handle limit)?
4. Was this specific test running when the process actually died, or did the process die and the test just happened to have been in flight? (Compare the very last log line's timestamp with any journal/systemd-side timestamp of process exit if we can recover it.)

CONSTRAINT: worktree ai/worktrees/agent-a048b3d2ffe0f8a26 has been REMOVED. Fresh reproduction may need a new worker or the operator's own run.

METHOD: dispatch a targeted --focus run on this specific test (`Pods Extended.*Pod Generation.*500 podspec`) with --verbose on a fresh --reset stack, watch the process closely, capture systemd exit metadata via limactl shell.

LABELS: apiserver, investigation, stability
close_reason:
OPERATOR CORRECTED MAYOR'S FRAMING: the silent apiserver stop was NOT an apiserver bug. Actual mechanism (best explanation, no direct proof): run-all.sh runs the apiserver as a child of the worker session's shell (not systemd, not nohup, not daemonized). When the worker agent 'returned' (either the original xi9bd going idle waiting on sonobuoy, or my resume-check returning after its inspection completed at ~15:18 UTC), its session process group was cleaned up, SIGHUP cascaded to the apiserver, and it died silently — no panic because it was a signal, not a crash. Timing fits: apiserver.log stopped at 15:59:55 UTC, ~40 min after the resume-check ran (which was itself run_in_background=true and just went idle and returned rather than actually waiting on the backgrounded sonobuoy job).

REAL LESSON for the mayor: (1) don't dispatch resume-check workers via run_in_background=true when the goal is to keep a long-lived shell child (apiserver) alive — the resumed agent will complete its check and terminate its session, killing the child; (2) run-all.sh's apiserver-as-shell-child design means the worker MUST stay blocked on the sonobuoy job until it truly completes, not merely 'know it's running and return'. This is a workflow constraint on the mayor, not a bug in run-all.sh or apiserver.

NO further investigation of apiserver stability warranted from this incident. Not filing a follow-on unless the stop reproduces WITHOUT the shell-child mechanism explaining it.

title: investigate(watch): is u7s delivering the EndpointSlice ADDED event to kube-proxy AFTER the test client can already see the Service — event-order suspect from pztio findings
description:
OPERATOR HYPOTHESIS filed 2026-07-29 following mayor-pztio's finding that EndpointSlice ADDED → first konnectivity CONNECT is ~1036ms in passing runs vs ~28.5ms in failing runs (both u7s Lima+arm64 env, 12-core Mac with 48GB, resources should NOT be a bottleneck vs CI running the same test at scale).

If our resources are adequate, the delta must come from event-delivery timing, not raw compute. Hypothesis: u7s might be delivering the same watch event to different consumers OUT OF ORDER — specifically, the test client's 'wait for Deployment ready' loop might observe pod-Ready BEFORE kube-proxy observes the EndpointSlice ADDED event (or its underlying Endpoints ADDED), even though both events fire at the same store revision. If that's happening, the test proceeds to LIST/watch before kube-proxy has been TOLD to program iptables at all, not just before it's had time to.

INVESTIGATION SCOPE:
1. Read u7s watch delivery code in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs and store watch stream code in crates/store/src/sqlite.rs — is there any code path that could deliver a watch event to consumer A (test client's Deployment watcher) before consumer B (kube-proxy's Endpoints/EndpointSlice watcher), even when the events cross the same store revision boundary?
2. Take one passing run (0728-0127) and one failing run (0729-1250). For each, find the EXACT store-write timestamp for:
   - Pod ready-condition update (kubelet PATCH /pods/.../status setting Ready=true)
   - EndpointSlice ADDED (the one for the webhook Service)
   - Deployment status ReadyReplicas=1 (kcm PATCH /deployments/.../status)
   Then for each of these, find WHEN each watcher (test client, kube-proxy) received the event. Compare deltas. Is our fan-out ordered or not?
3. Consider whether the CrConversionCache single-flight (9110c9a4) or the per-request AuthLayer metric (2d1862cd) could have introduced any ordering effect — specifically, do they hold any lock across .await that could stall a watcher fan-out even briefly? (Prior code reviews rr4ja/mo7dk didn't look at this angle.)
4. Check u7s watch fan-out for any 'chatty consumer starves quiet one' pattern where a heavy watch client (like sonobuoy, which is receiving many events) could block delivery to a lighter one (kube-proxy).

CONTEXT — memories worth reading before starting:
- [[kube-proxy-iptables-race-vs-e2e-test-timing-is-the-crfs-driver]] (pztio 2026-07-29 findings)
- [[crd-conversion-webhook-failure-is-cluster-side-9443-not-listening]]
- [[customresourcefieldselectors-line-241-signature-is-first-v2-to-v1-conversion]]
- Any memory tagged with 'watch' or 'fan-out'

Do NOT modify source code in this bead. Diagnostic only. If a fix path emerges, file a follow-on.

LABELS: investigation, watch, apiserver, event-ordering, conformance
close_reason: Operator hypothesis DISPROVEN with concrete log evidence. u7s watch fan-out is concurrent (each consumer independent broadcast::Receiver in own tokio task), unlocked (no cross-consumer lock across .await), sub-millisecond spread across all consumers (measured 385µs on failing 0729-1358 rv=33239, 506µs on failing 0729-1250 rv=20606, 191µs on passing-log 0728-0127 rv=27363 — all 2-3 orders of magnitude smaller than the passing-vs-failing EndpointSlice-ADDED→CONNECT delta driving the CRFS race). Fan-out mechanism at crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:230 (push_event_locked → tokio::sync::broadcast::Sender::send, 2048-slot per receiver). CrConversionCache does NOT touch kube-proxy's builtin-resource watch path (short-circuited at handlers/watch.rs:571-589). No file:line bug found. Full finding banked as memory [[watch-fanout-is-submillisecond-not-the-crfs-driver]]. Verdict: the CRFS-line-241 delta lives ENTIRELY downstream of u7s watch delivery — in kube-proxy's own reconcile→iptables loop — confirming and extending mayor-pztio's root cause. LOW-priority cleanup: rename misleading trace 'watch: CR conversion webhook call completed' at handlers/watch.rs (~line 975) to be gated on cr_fields.is_some() — observability nit, not a bug.

title: audit(upstream): does apiextensions-apiserver retry on transport-level connect errors for CR conversion webhook dispatch? — inform u7s fix scope
description:
READ-ONLY AUDIT. No PR at the end.

CONTEXT: u7s's call_conversion_webhook (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:70-84) is a single-shot HTTP send with no retry on any error class — including transport-layer connect-refused. This makes u7s reproducibly fail (2/3 rate on HEAD, verified by mayor-a8ndi) on the upstream CustomResourceFieldSelectors and CustomResourceConversionWebhook e2e tests due to a well-known race: the tests' webhook Deployment readiness probe hits :9444/readyz which comes up ~199ms before the actual conversion endpoint on :9443 binds. Same failure mode was catalogued as a systematic weakness in mayor-ido0r on 2026-07-25 (five days ago), and 'server-side retry on connection-refused for CRD conversion webhook calls' was surfaced as a candidate follow-on then but never filed.

GOAL: establish, with cited file:line evidence, whether upstream Kubernetes apiextensions-apiserver retries on transport-layer connect errors when dispatching a CR conversion webhook call, and if so, what the retry policy is.

Answer these specific questions:
1. In upstream, where does the CR conversion webhook HTTP dispatch happen? Suspected: staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/conversion/webhook_converter.go (or a nearby file). Cite file:line for the actual .Do() / .Send() / RESTClient invocation.
2. Is the HTTP client used there wrapped in any retry mechanism? Look for backoff, retry, or DoRaw wrappers. Does it use the shared apimachinery webhook client (util/webhook)?
3. If retry exists: what error classes does it retry on? Specifically — does it retry on transport-level connect errors (ECONNREFUSED, dial timeout) vs. HTTP-level 5xx responses vs. context deadline? What is the backoff shape (initial, max, factor, cap)?
4. Does upstream ADMISSION webhook dispatch (staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/generic/webhook.go and dispatcher/) use the same or different retry policy? Note the answer even though this audit is primarily about conversion — informs whether a u7s fix should cover admission as a follow-on.
5. Under what conditions does upstream give up? (max attempts, wall-clock cap, non-retryable classes.)

METHOD: use `gh api -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" "/repos/kubernetes/kubernetes/contents/<path>?ref=release-1.36"` for each file. Cache into temp/research/ (per project convention). Do NOT use WebFetch (blocked for workers).

Suspected files to fetch (verify these are the right ones for release-1.36):
- staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/conversion/webhook_converter.go
- staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apiserver/conversion/converter.go
- staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/webhook/webhook.go
- staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/webhook/client.go
- staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/generic/webhook.go
- staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/mutating/dispatcher.go
- staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/plugin/webhook/validating/dispatcher.go

RETURN under 500 words, structured as:
- **Retry policy for CR conversion webhook** (file:line-cited): does it exist, error classes, backoff shape, max attempts
- **Retry policy for admission webhook** (same shape)
- **Recommended shape for u7s fix bead** based on findings — attempts, backoff, error classes to catch (should we match upstream exactly, or is a narrower defensive fix — e.g., single retry on ECONNREFUSED only — closer to what we need to eliminate the flake?)
- **Whether admission webhook code in u7s (crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs) has the same gap** — grep call_admission_webhook or the equivalent in the same crate and note whether it also lacks retry

LABELS: audit, upstream-parity, apiserver, conversion-webhook, admission-webhook
close_reason: Upstream conversion webhook + admission dispatch are both single-shot RESTClient.Do() calls with no retry wrapper. Confirmed by direct read of upstream-webhook_converter.go:282-283 and upstream-mutating-dispatcher.go:297-302 (release-1.36). The GenericWebhook.WithExponentialBackoff helper (upstream-util-webhook.go:106-117) exists but is NOT invoked from conversion or admission code paths. Recommendation: do NOT add u7s-side retry; the observed 2/3 flake rate on our env reflects genuine upstream-test race + our timing envelope, not a u7s conformance deviation. Full finding cited in mo7dk worker return; audit files at temp/research/upstream-*.go were in the worker worktree only (gitignored, removed with worktree).

title: investigate(apiserver): CustomResourceFieldSelectors + CustomResourceConversionWebhook chronic flake — reproduce via --focus and root-cause
description:
Investigate whether the 0729-1250 conformance failure of `[sig-api-machinery] CustomResourceFieldSelectors ... MUST list and watch custom resources matching the field selector [Conformance]` at crd_selectable_fields.go:241 reproduces on demand or is a flake.

CONTEXT: Failure surfaced in temp/e2e/0729-1250-conformance (445/446 pass). Run history over last 9 conformance runs shows CR-conversion-webhook family tests (this test + `CustomResourceConversionWebhook`) failed in 5/9 runs, all pre-dating recent perf work (#928/#929/#934). Failure mode: apiserver's call to https://e2e-test-crd-conversion-webhook.<ns>.svc:9443/crdconvert fails at ~2s into the test with `error sending request for url (…)` (no upstream cause chained — transport-layer connect failure). The test only waits for Deployment ReadyReplicas=1, but the readiness probe checks :9444/readyz while the webhook binds :9443/crdconvert — classic pod-Ready-vs-app-not-listening race.

APPROACH per operator: dispatch a --focus run on HEAD (a62a009b) to see if it reproduces reliably. If yes, investigate the apiserver-side code path for anything that could contribute (e.g., HTTP client that doesn't retry on connect-refused when target is a fresh Service). If unclear, bisect via git checkout + same --focus run against 67cfe2ba (last passing baseline before #933/#934).

DELIVERABLES:
1. --focus run result on HEAD (PASS/FAIL, wall-clock)
2. If FAIL: apiserver.log excerpt + kubelet.log + a hypothesis on whether a defensive retry (once, on transport-layer connect-refused to a very-fresh Service) would eliminate the flake without changing correctness — or whether the fix belongs entirely in the upstream test (readiness probe port bug)
3. If PASS: file a bd remember memory documenting the flake pattern (5/9 rate, mechanism, that a single --focus reproduction is unreliable) so the next mayor doesn't chase it as a regression
4. Whether it makes sense to bisect further

NON-GOALS: do NOT open a PR yet. This is diagnostic. Any fix comes after we know the failure mode.

LABELS: apiserver, conversion-webhook, flake, e2e
close_reason: Diagnostic complete: reproduced FAIL 2/3 via --focus on HEAD a62a009b. Confirmed pod-Ready-vs-webhook-not-listening race (199ms gap, readyz-probe-success to first failed webhook dispatch). Traced code path to crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs call_conversion_webhook() — single-shot HTTP call, no retry, unlike upstream's exponential-backoff retry for connect-refused. Memory filed: conversion-webhook-flake-2-of-3-fail-missing-retry. No PR (diagnostic-only per bead scope); recommend mayor decide on defensive retry fix given 2/3 rate exceeds 5/9 historical baseline.

title: task
description:
First and load-bearing sub-bead of the zw0ou EPIC (plan at ai/findings/zw0ou-per-version-storage-cacher-plan-2026-07-29.md, ~230-350 LoC total across 4 sub-beads). Adds a CrConversionCache mirroring the CrSchemaCache precedent from mayor-p8vgj (state.rs:200-264) exactly: an Arc<RwLock<HashMap<CacheKey, Arc<Value>>>> keyed on (source resourceVersion, target apiVersion), wired into the single shared convert_cr_list_items helper (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:327-352) that BOTH the LIST path AND the watch fanout path already call.

Fix precedent to mirror: mayor-p8vgj (PR #925) — CrSchemaCache. Same shape: pub struct in state.rs, Arc-wrapped field on AppState, constructor call in AppStateConfig::new_with_config, get/insert/invalidate methods. Zero AppStateConfig plumbing (unconditional construction, like admission_cache and cr_schema_cache).

MANDATORY SCOPE ADDITIONS (folded in from sketched sub-bead 2 per operator recommendation 2026-07-29):
1. Verify the metadata.resourceVersion staleness precondition: does the stored CR object's own .metadata.resourceVersion field match the store's rv counter at write time? If not, the cache key derivation is wrong and would produce stale hits. Read cr.rs's CR write path (create/replace/patch) and confirm. If the precondition doesn't hold, STOP and report — the whole approach depends on it.

Add a WEBHOOK-LATENCY-AWARE benchmark (mocking a realistic 5-20ms round-trip delay across N=1/5/10/20 concurrent watchers on cross-version watches) to complement crates/apiserver/benches/watch_fanout.rs. This is CRITICAL: the 94.5% headroom bench I've been citing measures the wrong thing (µs JSON on no-conversion fast path, not ms webhook). Without this new bench, we cannot verify the claimed win, and the honest possibility (per zw0ou-headroom-bench-measures-wrong-thing memory) is that the win doesn't materialize.

CORRECTNESS INVARIANTS:
- Cache key MUST include target_api_version as an explicit non-optional part (never inferred). Test with TWO different target versions against the same source object to confirm independent cache entries.
- Rule 14 revert-check tests: (a) two watchers same-target-version same-rv share ONE webhook call not two (counter test), (b) two watchers different-target-versions same-rv trigger two separate webhook calls (correctness test — no cross-key collision), (c) same target-version different-rv (write followed by second write) triggers a fresh webhook call (invalidation-by-key test).

FALLBACK: any cache miss falls through to today's behavior (call the webhook), so the risk envelope is 'no worse than today'. See plan doc Q5 Correctness/Performance sections.

If the measured win at N=10 or N=20 is small (<3x, say) despite the extrapolation predicting much larger, that is a signal to reassess whether sub-beads 3-4 are worth doing at all (per plan's 'close as measured, not worth complexity' exit).

title: task
description:
Prompted by operator observation 2026-07-28: an RFC 5322 compliant email regex is ~6500 characters, well over the 512-byte cap I proposed for mayor-cmtwm's ReDoS fix. Before picking a number, verify against evidence.

QUESTIONS (all read-only research, no code changes):

1. Does upstream Kubernetes (release-1.36) enforce ANY length cap on openAPIV3Schema.pattern or patternProperties keys? Check:
   - k/k apimachinery openapi validator source (k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/validation and k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apis/apiextensions/validation)
   - k/k kube-openapi source (k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/validation/validate)
   - k/k apiextensions-apiserver CRD admission (k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/registry/customresourcedefinition)
   Fetch relevant files via gh api pinned to release-1.36, cache in temp/research/.

2. Does OpenAPI 3.0 spec itself impose any length or complexity constraint on 'pattern'? Cite the OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec section.

3. What is upstream K8s's overall CRD manifest size cap (I recall ~3 MB body limit for API requests) — does that implicitly bound the effective maximum pattern size a CRD author could ship?

4. Empirically: what is a realistic length distribution of production-in-the-wild CRD 'pattern' values? Common candidates worth measuring: email (RFC 5322 ~6500 chars, but a 'reasonable email' regex is often only 20-100 chars), URL, semver, k8s resource-name (DNS-1123 subdomain, ~50 chars), UUID (~40 chars), K8s label selectors, cron expressions. If you have access to any operator CRD collection (cert-manager, prometheus-operator, argo-rollouts are all Helm-installable and use CRDs), grep their published CRD YAMLs for pattern: fields and report the observed length distribution — 5-10 concrete data points beats speculation.

5. Given mayor-cmtwm's audit finding (boon O(n^2)): does the 4 MiB MAX_BODY_BYTES on the apiserver's request body already provide any implicit protection? What's the WORST realistic pattern length inside a 4 MiB CRD? The audit says up to ~1 MB of \d repeated could produce minutes of CPU — is that ceiling more like ~500KB (with realistic schema overhead) or is it actually the full 4 MiB?

DELIVERABLE: findings doc at ai/findings/crd-pattern-size-upstream-and-real-world-2026-07-28.md (gitignored). Executive summary should recommend a specific cap value with rationale, or a range to choose from ('anywhere between X and Y works; here's the tradeoff'), backed by evidence from questions 1-5.

TIME BUDGET: single dispatch, ~30 min. Read-only, no code changes. This bead's OUTPUT decides mayor-cmtwm's cap parameter.

FEEDS INTO: mayor-cmtwm (P2 HIGH ReDoS fix, currently decision-blocked). Do NOT dispatch cmtwm before this research completes.
close_reason: Research complete: doc at ai/findings/crd-pattern-size-upstream-and-real-world-2026-07-28.md; recommend cap = 512 bytes (unchanged from mayor-cmtwm's original proposal); feeds into mayor-cmtwm cap parameter.

title: task
description:
Audit: ai/findings/redos-and-user-controlled-pattern-audit-2026-07-28.md, finding F2 (HIGH).

PROBLEM: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs::validate_cr_schema (lines 476-499, called from
8 production CR write paths) compiles the CRD's openAPIV3Schema via boon::Compiler::compile.
For any `pattern` or `patternProperties` key in that schema, boon (v0.6.1) first runs an
ECMA-to-Rust-regex compatibility shim (boon-0.6.1/src/ecma.rs::convert, lines 8-49) BEFORE
calling regex::Regex::new. That shim's translate loop is O(pattern_length^2): each outer-loop
iteration does a full O(n) AST walk (ast::visit) PLUS a full O(n) re-parse
(Parser::new().parse(&updated_pattern)), and only rewrites ONE `\d`/`\D`/`\w`/`\W`/`\s`/`\S`
escape per iteration (Translator::visit_post short-circuits via `if self.out.is_some() {
return Ok(()) }`). A pattern of ~1MB consisting of `\d` repeated ~500,000 times (well within
the apiserver's 4 MiB MAX_BODY_BYTES request-body limit, crates/apiserver/src/lib.rs:61) drives
this loop through ~500,000 iterations of O(n)-cost work each, on the order of 10^11-10^12
character operations -- i.e. minutes of single-core CPU pinned per request. This runs BEFORE
regex compilation, so the regex crate's own size_limit default (which bounds a separate,
lower-severity issue, see companion bead for F1) provides zero protection.

REACHABILITY: a CRD author (privileged, cluster-admin-gated in a well-configured cluster, but
CRDs are also commonly installed from third-party Helm charts/operators an admin may not have
fully audited) sets a `pattern` or `patternProperties` key like this in openAPIV3Schema. Once
installed, ANY principal with mere create/update RBAC on that Custom Resource kind (a much
lower privilege than CRD-create) can retrigger the full O(n^2) cost on every single write,
because validate_cr_schema recompiles the whole schema from scratch every time (no cache --
see companion MEDIUM bead F1). This is worse than upstream Kubernetes: kube-openapi's `pattern`
handling (k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/validation/validate/rexp.go, verified against release-1.36's
kube-openapi dependency, cached at temp/research/kube-openapi-rexp.go) passes patterns straight
to Go's regexp.Compile (RE2) with NO ecma-compat rewrite needed at all, because Go's regexp
already treats \d/\w/\s as ASCII-only by default (matching ECMA 262 semantics natively). The
quadratic cost is specific to u7s's choice of the `boon` crate, not inherited from upstream.

FIX SHAPE: u7s does not control boon's internals, so patch upstream of boon:
1. At CRD admission time (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/crd.rs, the CRD create/update handler),
   walk the submitted openAPIV3Schema and reject any `pattern` string or `patternProperties`
   object key longer than 512 bytes with a 422/400. 512 bytes is generous headroom over any
   realistic hand-written JSON Schema validation regex (worst case cost becomes ~512^2 =
   262,144 char-ops, sub-millisecond).
2. Defense in depth: re-check the same 512-byte bound in validate_cr_schema
   (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs) before calling boon::Compiler::compile, so a CRD that
   bypassed the create-time check (e.g. installed before the check existed, or via direct store
   manipulation / restore from backup) can't still trigger the blowup on CR write.
3. Regression test: a CRD with a >512-byte pattern is rejected at CRD create/update; a CRD with
   a <=512-byte pattern (including one using \d/\w/\s) is accepted and CR validation against it
   still works correctly (exercise the actual ECMA-compat rewrite path, not just the length gate).
4. Recommended (not required for this bead, but do before closing if time allows): empirically
   time boon::Compiler::compile on a ~1MB \d-repeated pattern before and after the fix, to confirm
   the fix actually caps the cost (this audit's own attempt at that timing PoC was blocked by the
   worktree-boundary Write guard and is documented as a static-analysis-only finding in the audit
   doc).

Companion bead: MEDIUM finding F1 (recompile-on-every-CR-write / no schema-compile cache) in the
same audit doc, filed separately.
close_reason: PR #924 opened: 1024-byte cap on CRD pattern/patternProperties keys + defense-in-depth in validate_cr_schema, empirical bounded timing sweep confirms boon O(n^2) audit claim (4x size -> 14.3x time, vs 4x linear/16x quadratic)

title: task
description:
Prompted by an operator concern about a Stack Overflow ReDoS incident, 2026-07-28. u7s's dep tree uses ONLY the standard rust regex crate (guaranteed-linear NFA/DFA, immune to catastrophic backtracking by design) and regex-syntax — no fancy-regex, pcre, or onig. That closes the classic engine-level ReDoS vector but leaves four other classes worth confirming:

  (1) DIRECT regex::Regex::new on attacker-controlled patterns — even linear execution has bounded DFA size, and the regex crate has RegexBuilder::size_limit() / dfa_size_limit(). Any site that compiles a regex from a user/CRD/webhook-config-supplied string without setting a size limit can be DoS'd via memory/CPU on COMPILE (not match). Audit every regex::Regex::new / RegexBuilder::build call site under crates/**/*.rs, tag each: (a) pattern is a compile-time constant → safe; (b) pattern is derived from a config/CRD/user path AND size_limit is set → safe; (c) pattern is derived from a config path AND no size_limit → HIGH.

  (2) regex-syntax used standalone (Parser / ast::parse) — bounded work in-crate but check the call sites; verify no unbounded recursion in a caller that walks the AST.

  (3) HAND-ROLLED pattern matching in hot loops with user-controlled strings. Kubernetes-specific vectors u7s must be checked against: LabelSelector expressions (equality/set-based), FieldSelector parsing, ValidatingWebhookConfiguration rule matching (apiGroups/apiVersions/resources/operations), MutatingWebhookConfiguration URL/name matching, admission webhook 'match conditions' CEL predicates (if u7s implements them), RBAC PolicyRule glob matching, CRD OpenAPI schema pattern validators. Look for nested for-loops on user strings, .split().split() chains, glob-to-regex conversions where the glob is not a compile-time constant.

  (4) SqliteStore predicate/query construction that concatenates a user field-selector/label-selector into a SQL LIKE or GLOB — this is more SQL-injection than ReDoS but the same audit pass should notice.

Deliverable (Shape 3 audit): findings doc at ai/findings/redos-and-user-controlled-pattern-audit-2026-07-28.md with per-site verdict (SAFE / MEDIUM / HIGH), file:line citations, and a per-HIGH-severity follow-on bead with a concrete fix (RegexBuilder::size_limit(N) with an explicit N, or a length pre-check, or refactor to avoid dynamic compilation). Explicit allowance: if the audit finds nothing HIGH, that's a valid clean-bill-of-health outcome — write the doc anyway so a future audit knows what was checked.

Time budget: single dispatch, read-only, no code changes in this bead. Any HIGH findings become their own P1/P2 beads.
notes:
Filed mayor-cmtwm (P2) for finding F2 (HIGH): boon's ECMA-compat regex-rewrite loop is O(pattern_len^2), reachable via CRD pattern/patternProperties, no size_limit protection applies since it runs before Regex::new.
Filed mayor-p8vgj (P3) for finding F1 (MEDIUM): validate_cr_schema recompiles boon Schemas from scratch on every CR write, no cache, unlike upstream kube-openapi's process-wide compiled-regex cache.
close_reason: Audit complete: 1 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM / 9 SAFE findings; doc at ai/findings/redos-and-user-controlled-pattern-audit-2026-07-28.md; follow-on beads: mayor-cmtwm (P2, F2 HIGH - boon ECMA-compat regex-rewrite O(n^2) DoS via CRD pattern/patternProperties), mayor-p8vgj (P3, F1 MEDIUM - no schema-compile cache, recompiles boon Schemas on every CR write). Verdict: not clean - u7s's own code never compiles a regex, but the CRD schema pattern path routes through boon (third-party) and has a genuine HTTP-reachable CPU-exhaustion vector plus an amplification issue that upstream Kubernetes mitigates via a process-wide compiled-regex cache.

title: kcm.log and konnectivity-server.log timestamps are klog local time, not UTC — journalctl --utc fix (mayor-c9hrk) does not cover them
description:
mayor-c9hrk fixed the journalctl wrapper prefix for kubelet.log (--utc) and the
temp/e2e/ run-dir timestamp (date -u), scoped exactly to scripts + docs per its
task description, which asserted apiserver.log/kcm.log/scheduler.log/
konnectivity-server.log were "all UTC" already.

Direct verification on a JST host (lima-node-2 stack-only bring-up, host and VM
both Asia/Tokyo) shows that assertion is only true for the two Rust/tracing-based
logs:
  - apiserver.log: 2026-07-28T13:02:19.573045Z   (true UTC)
  - scheduler.log: 2026-07-28T13:04:31.505364Z   (true UTC)

The two Go/klog-based logs are NOT UTC — they render whatever the process
considers local time, and klog has no --utc equivalent flag at all (unlike
journalctl):
  - kcm.log (in-VM, klog):              I0728 22:04:21.658260  (JST, = 13:04 UTC + 9h)
  - konnectivity-server.log (host, klog): I0728 22:02:17.767012  (JST, Mac host is also Asia/Tokyo)

So on any host/VM that isn't already UTC, kcm.log and konnectivity-server.log
timestamps are silently wrong relative to apiserver.log/scheduler.log — the
exact "9h off, easy to not notice" failure mode mayor-c9hrk was filed to kill,
just in two components the original bead didn't know were affected.

klog has no UTC flag, so the only fix is forcing the *process's own* clock to
UTC via TZ=UTC in the environment each binary launches in:
  - scripts/conformance/04-start-kcm.sh: set TZ=UTC in the env kube-controller-manager
    inherits (it runs inside the lima VM via `limactl shell ... bash -s`).
  - scripts/u7s-start.sh (or wherever konnectivity-server is spawned on the host):
    set TZ=UTC in its process env.
  - kubelet's own embedded klog line (I0728 22:03:51...) inside kubelet.log is
    ALSO local (JST) today, separate from the journal-wrapper prefix already fixed
    by mayor-c9hrk's --utc — same TZ=UTC treatment needed in the kubelet.service
    systemd unit written by lima-start.sh, if this is worth closing all the way.

Scope estimate: 3 small script edits (systemd unit / env block), no Rust changes.
close_reason: PR #914 opened: force TZ=UTC in kcm/konnectivity/kubelet process env, live-verified on lima-node-4 (JST host/VM) — all 5 log files now show UTC-consistent timestamps

title: Unify log timestamps to a single timezone across apiserver, kubelet, kcm, scheduler, konnectivity, and sonobuoy result dir names
description: Currently u7s runtime logs use a mix of UTC and JST which is confusing for debugging even for operators who know what to look for and error-prone for agents doing log correlation. Observed: apiserver.log kcm.log scheduler.log konnectivity-server.log all UTC in ISO 8601 or klog. kubelet.log via systemd journal export has BOTH a journal prefix Jul DD HH:MM:SS in local JST AND embedded klog I0725 HH:MM:SS in UTC on every line. temp/e2e run directory names MMDD-HHMM are local JST end time. When correlating events across files an agent or human can easily compare a journal JST line to an apiserver UTC line and be 9h off. Concrete pain today: multiple full-conformance triage sessions had to redo work after realizing they were comparing across timezones without noticing. DECISION NEEDED: unify to UTC or JST project-wide. UTC is standard for distributed systems, matches k8s conformance conventions and the majority of our components already do it. JST is the operator local convenience. Scope estimate: run scripts/conformance/*.sh to set TZ=UTC or Europe/London for the whole stack, and rename temp/e2e/ result directories to include a UTC suffix or drop the local time prefix. Not a code change to production apiserver etc. NEXT: operator picks tz, then a small scripts-only worker.

title: fix(apiserver): revoked_jtis SA-token revocation set is wired for reads but never populated — leaked tokens cannot be invalidated before 24h expiry
description:
Found by mayor-rl86n (2026-07-24 security reflection audit). Doc: ai/findings/security-review-2026-07-24.md F1.

crates/apiserver/src/state.rs:521 constructs AppState::revoked_jtis (Arc<Mutex<HashSet<String>>>)
empty. crates/apiserver/src/auth.rs:386 (try_verify_sa_jwt) and
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/authorization.rs:631-639 (TokenReview) only ever call
.contains() on it. A full-crate grep for .insert(...) against this set shows it happening
ONLY inside #[cfg(test)] blocks in auth.rs (lines 1742, 1764, 1789) that build a throwaway
HashSet by hand to unit-test the read path. There is no HTTP handler, admin endpoint, or
lifecycle hook (ServiceAccount delete, Pod delete, Secret delete, Namespace delete) anywhere
in crates/apiserver or crates/scheduler that ever inserts a JTI into the real, production
revoked_jtis set. The doc comments on this field (state.rs:253-256, auth.rs:381-389) claim
"this allows immediate token invalidation without waiting for the 24h JWT expiry" — that
mechanism does not exist.

Compounding: handlers/tokens.rs's MIN_JWT_LIFETIME_SECS (86400) floors every minted SA JWT's
real cryptographic validity at 24h regardless of the caller-requested (and clamped-valid,
e.g. 600s) expirationSeconds — the JWT exp claim is always max(requested, 86400) seconds from
mint, while status.expirationTimestamp in the TokenRequest response still reflects the short
requested window. try_verify_sa_jwt also never re-checks that a pod-bound token's
kubernetes.io.pod/.node claim still refers to a live store object — the bound object's
continued existence is never re-verified at auth time, only echoed into TokenReview's extra
fields.

ATTACK SCENARIO / FAILURE MODE: an operator discovers a ServiceAccount token has leaked (e.g.
printed in a CI build log, exfiltrated from a compromised pod). Real Kubernetes' remediations
are: wait out the short TTL, or (for bound tokens) delete the bound Pod/Secret so the next
auth attempt is rejected by bound-object-liveness checking. In u7s NEITHER works: the token's
real lifetime is >= 24h no matter what TTL was requested, and deleting the
Pod/Node/ServiceAccount/Namespace it was bound to has zero effect on try_verify_sa_jwt (it
never queries the store). The only real remedy is rotating the SA signing key
(--sa-key/--sa-pub), which invalidates every SA token cluster-wide, not just the compromised
one.

FIX SHAPE (pick one, or combine):
(a) wire an explicit revoke path (e.g. DELETE .../serviceaccounts/{name}/token or an admin
    endpoint) that inserts the token's jti into revoked_jtis;
(b) make try_verify_sa_jwt's bound-pod/node claims re-checked against the live store at
    verification time (matching upstream BoundServiceAccountTokenAuthenticator semantics) so
    deleting the bound Pod invalidates the token promptly;
(c) if revocation is intentionally out of scope for pre-alpha, remove the dead revoked_jtis
    plumbing and the doc comments that claim a guarantee it doesn't provide (Rule 2: simplicity).

REGRESSION TEST (must fail on revert): mint a token, exercise whatever revoke path is added,
then assert the same jti is rejected by try_verify_sa_jwt afterward. Today no test exercises
the write side of revoked_jtis because there is no write side.
notes:
DESIGN RESOLVED after upstream source verification (2026-07-27) + operator design conversation. Fetched and read k8s release-1.36 source directly: pkg/serviceaccount/claims.go (the Validator.Validate bound-object liveness check), pkg/registry/core/serviceaccount/storage/token.go and storage.go (the TokenRequest extend-expiration trigger + wiring), pkg/kubeapiserver/options/authentication.go (defaults). CONFIRMED FACTS: (1) upstream has NO JTI-based revocation list anywhere - the jti claim is used ONLY for an audit-log CredentialID, never for a blocklist lookup. u7s revoked_jtis has no upstream analog and must be removed entirely along with its false immediate-invalidation doc claims. (2) upstream's real revocation mechanism is bound-object liveness checking: on EVERY auth attempt, re-verify the ServiceAccount UID matches + not deleted more than jwt.DefaultLeeway=60s ago; if pod-bound, same check against the live Pod; node is only independently checked for STANDALONE node-bound tokens (u7s does not support that binding type - u7s always derives node info alongside a pod-bound token, matching upstream's pod-bound informational-only case, so NO independent node liveness check is needed for u7s). Secret-bound tokens also do not exist in u7s - no secret liveness check needed either. (3) upstream's 1-year MIN_JWT_LIFETIME-equivalent (ExpirationExtensionSeconds) is a NARROW, CONDITIONAL migration safety net (pod-bound AND requested exactly the historical 3607s default AND kube-native audiences AND the --service-account-extend-token-expiration flag which defaults true), paired with a warnafter claim + stale-token audit-annotation/metric so operators can detect when the safety net is masking a real refresh problem. Upstream's own OWN intended lifecycle per the KEP and PR 96273: this is a TEMPORARY per-cluster mitigation meant to be monitored via the stale-token metric then DISABLED once verified unnecessary - not a permanent posture. Real operators (Azure AKS issue 4373, AWS EKS shipping 90 days instead of 1 year) have already pushed back on the 1-year default as excessive. OPERATOR DECISION 2026-07-27: (a) tighten u7s scope to match upstream security expectations - only extend when pod-bound AND kube-native-audience (https://kubernetes.default.svc), NOT unconditionally on every token as today; (b) lower the extension duration to 8 hours, deliberately NOT matching upstream's magic 3607-second trigger value or its 1-year duration - a round, intentionally-chosen number; (c) do NOT gate the extension on the literal requested-value matching a magic constant the way upstream does - gate purely on scope (pod-bound + kube-audience); (d) operator accepts the risk that 8h may be insufficient if the original mayor-tq5y kubelet-refresh-reliability issue is still present, and will personally rerun the full conformance suite after this lands to confirm no regression - if it resurfaces, we will revisit. FULL SCOPE for the implementation: 1) remove revoked_jtis entirely from state.rs, auth.rs, handlers/authorization.rs, including its doc comments. 2) widen SaClaims/KubernetesIoClaims decode in auth.rs to capture kubernetes_io.namespace and kubernetes_io.serviceaccount{name,uid} (currently only pod+node are decoded - the SA identity itself is never read back out for verification). 3) make try_verify_sa_jwt async and store-aware: on every successful signature+expiry check, look up the live ServiceAccount by namespace+name from claims, reject if missing or UID mismatch or deletionTimestamp older than 60s leeway; if a pod claim is present, same UID+deletion-timestamp+60s-leeway check against the live Pod; do NOT independently check node (informational only, matches upstream's pod-bound case). 4) rescope+shorten handlers/tokens.rs's MIN_JWT_LIFETIME_SECS mechanism: only extend to 8 hours (28800s) when pod-bound AND audiences are exactly the kube-native default, otherwise mint exactly the requested (clamped 600-172800s) lifetime with NO extension at all. 5) add a warnafter claim (= now + originally requested expiration_seconds) when the extension applies; in try_verify_sa_jwt, if now is past a token's warnafter but token is still within its real exp, do not reject but increment a new Prometheus counter (e.g. u7s_stale_sa_tokens_total matching the project's existing custom-metric naming convention from mayor-atemy.1) so operators can observe reliance on the safety net, mirroring upstream's stale-token audit-annotation + metric pattern. THIS IS A SECURITY-CRITICAL, HIGH-BLAST-RADIUS CHANGE touching the core authentication path for every request in the cluster - requires live VM verification (mint token bound to a live pod, confirm auth succeeds; delete the pod, confirm the token stops authenticating after the 60s leeway; confirm ordinary kubectl/kubelet flows still work) not just cargo tests, plus ideally a sonobuoy --focus gate on sig-auth ServiceAccount specs before merge given how severe an auth regression would be.
PR opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/910 — implements the 5-piece fix (remove revoked_jtis, widen claims, async store-backed bound-object liveness check, rescoped 8h token-lifetime extension, warnafter+stale-metric). Live VM verification done on lima-node-4:6446 (full bound-token lifecycle incl. 60s grace period, extension scoping, unaffected kubelet/KCM which use mTLS not SA JWTs). cargo test/clippy clean. Do not merge — mayor reviews. Do not close this bead until PR is merged.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #910 (merged 75a83743, all 17 CI checks green, reviewed in full by mayor across all 7 changed files before merge). Implements bound-object liveness checking for SA JWTs matching upstream Kubernetes semantics (release-1.36 pkg/serviceaccount/claims.go verified directly): try_verify_sa_jwt is now async and store-backed, re-verifying the bound ServiceAccount (and Pod, if bound) UID + a 60s post-deletionTimestamp grace period on every authentication attempt. Removed dead revoked_jtis entirely (no upstream analog - jti is audit-only). Rescoped the token-lifetime-extension mechanism to match upstream's real trigger conditions (pod-bound + kube-native audience only, was previously unconditional on every token) with an 8-hour duration - the operator's deliberate choice, NOT upstream's 1-year default, NOT gated on upstream's magic 3607-second value. Added warnafter claim + u7s_stale_sa_tokens_total metric for observability into extension-safety-net reliance, mirroring upstream's stale-token audit pattern. Live-verified on lima-node-4: full bound-token lifecycle (mint bound to live pod -> authenticates -> pod deleted -> still valid within 60s grace -> rejected past 60s), 8h extension confirmed via decoded JWT exp-iat for pod-bound+kube-audience tokens, unbound tokens get exact requested duration, kubelet/KCM unaffected (they use mTLS not SA JWTs). Sonobuoy --focus not run (time-boxed) but operator's planned full conformance re-run will exercise sig-auth ServiceAccount specs as part of the standard 446-spec suite, and will also serve as the check on whether 8h (vs the prior 24h) resurfaces the original mayor-tq5y kubelet-refresh-reliability issue.

title: audit(quality): reflection pass over apiserver + store + scheduler focusing on dead code, drift risks, misplaced comments, visibility, duplication, test-coverage gaps in newly-added code
description:
Read-only Shape-3 audit paired with the security review. Deliverable: ai/findings/code-quality-review-2026-07-24.md plus follow-on beads filed one at a time. Close bead with follow-on IDs enumerated.

TIMING RATIONALE. Nine code PRs merged today; observability + perf work touched many files (admission, watch, scheduler, store, handlers, benches). Time for a critical read looking specifically at cruft that accumulated: functions that landed then never got wired (jdeon-style — prepare_live_event was marked cfg-test-only for 4 weeks before we noticed), overly-permissive pub visibility, tests that describe WHAT the code does instead of WHY it matters, dead code marked with allow-dead-code rather than removed.

SCOPE.
1. DRIFT RISK: any function pair where two paths implement 'the same' logic — post-jdeon we know that leaving prepare_live_event's twin logic inline elsewhere risks divergence. Look for other prepare_live_event-shaped situations: matches_rule vs matches_rule_typed (already confirmed intentional but check for a third), any place a typed and Value-based path do 'the same' filtering, any 'fast path' branch that could go stale relative to the slow path it duplicates.
2. DEAD CODE: cfg-test-only functions that used to be production and were retired without their tests being retired (jdeon-inverse), allow-dead-code annotations that should be deletions, unused enum variants, exports from lib.rs never called externally (post PR 900 the additive-lib pattern was cleaned up but check for any leftover).
3. VISIBILITY: pub versus pub-crate audit — PR 905 narrowed 16 handler functions and 2 admission-cache fields; look for similar cases in the still-pub surface where a bench or test isnt actually calling it and pub-crate would suffice. cross-reference mayor-vocxl notes.
4. COMMENT DEBT: bead-ID references in source (rule violation per CLAUDE.md), used-by-X notes (rule violation), stale line-number references in comments after PRs shifted them.
5. TEST-COVERAGE GAPS in newly-added code: PRs 895-905 added significant surface. Verify each new function has at least one test whose WHY assertion states what breaks for users if it regresses. Skip trivial thin-bin main.rs shim tests — theyre self-documenting.
6. DUPLICATED LOGIC: patterns like the drifted 5th F10 site (opmy6) where same-shape code exists in more than one place and could clearly share. Also: label filtering, resource-key parsing, kubeconfig setup patterns.
7. INCONSISTENT ERROR HANDLING: unwrap/expect on non-boundary code, silent Err swallowing beyond what mil2-F05 already documented, panic-on-bad-input in handlers.

EXPLICIT EXCLUSIONS.
- Do NOT re-audit already-tracked quality work: mayor-mil2 F-05/F-06/F-07 deferred, mayor-8a7b delete_collection swallows non-NotFound resolved, various mayor-gzp5g/opmy6/yc0ou already filed.
- Do NOT propose refactors bigger than 200 LoC unless the pattern appears in 3+ places (economy of scale).
- Do NOT audit test QUANTITY, only test QUALITY (WHY vs WHAT).
- Do NOT propose comment-writing — comments are a smell per CLAUDE.md; the finding should be 'delete this comment' or 'this function needs renaming so the comment becomes unnecessary'.

DELIVERABLE FORMAT.
Follow ai/findings/verbose-debug-log-audit-2026-07-24.md's structure (mayor-o8284) as shape reference. Per finding: file:line, severity HIGH/MED/LOW, one-line 'what breaks or drifts if this stays'. Findings doc first before any bd create.

LOW severity, combined into one small bead.

title: audit(security): reflection pass over apiserver + store + scheduler focusing on auth path, RBAC, admission, webhook handling, tokens, TLS material lifecycle
description:
Read-only Shape-3 audit. Deliverable: ai/findings/security-review-2026-07-24.md plus follow-on beads filed one at a time appending each new ID to this bead's notes. Close this bead with follow-on IDs enumerated.

TIMING RATIONALE. Nine code PRs merged today plus a huge audit-fanout plus a refactor. The heavy day added: auth-related changes (access log carries request_id and user_agent), the /metrics endpoint (auth-gated RBAC endpoint that just got wired), admission chain refactor via jdeon and cef5-F8, thin-bin refactor via vocxl. Time to reflect adversarially before more feature work lands.

SCOPE.
1. Auth path: crates/apiserver/src/auth.rs, main.rs's is_exempt list, all handlers that touch bearer tokens, service-account tokens, JWT signing/verifying (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/tokens.rs).
2. RBAC: crates/apiserver/src/rbac.rs, ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding seed data, aggregation logic, nonResourceURLs enforcement.
3. Admission: crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs (call_webhook TLS/URL handling, SSRF guard, response bounded read, webhook object cloning), quota.rs, limit_range.rs.
4. Token/SA handling: /var/run/secrets projected volumes, JWT lifetime, key rotation, revoked JTIs.
5. TLS material lifecycle: crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs, CA generation/loading, peer certificate handling, kubelet-preferred-address.
6. Recent surface additions: /metrics access-gate (mayor-atemy.1 PR 896), structured access log redaction (mayor-atemy.2 PR 895), the additive lib.rs from PR 900 that gained a narrow re-export set.

title: perf(apiserver): wire prepare_live_event into watch fan-out (serialize once per event, not per watcher)
description:
Discovered 2026-07-24 during mayor-cef5 parallel perf estimation audit (F11 worker finding, see cef5 notes for context).

BACKGROUND. The perf improvement was IMPLEMENTED but NEVER WIRED UP.

- Commit f961ee71 (perf(apiserver): serialize watch events once per event, not per watcher) added crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs::prepare_live_event — a function meant to parse, filter by selector, and serialize each event exactly ONCE, then hand the resulting Bytes to every watcher instead of every watcher redoing the work.
- Commit 4a0a9153 (fix(apiserver): annotate prepare_live_event cfg-test — it is test-only (mayor-18h4)) marked prepare_live_event with #[cfg(test)] because the actual watch_generic_impl fan-out loop was still doing inline parse/filter/serialize per-watcher — prepare_live_event was never called from production code. mayor-18h4's own commit message: 'The fan-out loop in watch_generic already does inline parse/filter/serialize for each Added/Modified event. prepare_live_event duplicates that logic but is never called from production code.'
- Commit 9a8dabcd added dead_code allow before that. Two test-only tests (watch.rs:3899 prepare_live_event_two_watchers_same_event_bytes_get_identical_output and :3958 prepare_live_event_label_selector_watcher_receives_only_matching_events) exist to prove the function's semantics and would gate a future wiring.

CURRENT STATE. crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs live-event fan-out loop parses each event (serde_json::from_str) + reserializes (via encode_watch_event / ndjson_event_value paths) PER WATCHER at ~lines 890 947-961 1015-1078. At N watchers per event, that is N-1 redundant parse+reserialize passes.

WHY THIS MATTERS more than cef5 F11 (which was rank-5 do-not-bother — just the ~5-20 byte api_version/kind clones being dwarfed by the parse+reserialize): eliminating N-1 redundant JSON parse+reserialize passes per event is the STRUCTURAL win F11 alone could not reach. Each parse+reserialize of a small object is on the order of microseconds not nanoseconds; at N watchers x R events per second that adds up (jlzbv audit measured 5 watchers x 200 writes = 1000 delivered events at ~369 events per second aggregate delivery).

APPROACH.
1. First verify prepare_live_event is genuinely a drop-in replacement — walk each of the live-event yield sites (Added/Modified/Deleted arms including the CR-conversion-webhook branches at lines ~890 and ~1015) and check whether the function covers all of them or if any need a variant. Read the two existing cfg-test tests as the semantics oracle.
2. Wire prepare_live_event into watch_generic_impl fan-out. Remove #[cfg(test)] and dead_code annotations. All existing behavior must be preserved.
3. Measure before-after via criterion or the same lima-node-* end-to-end pattern PR 901 established (multi-watcher LIST loop with sustained writes; capture apiserver_watch_events_total rate + write-side latency).

BLAST RADIUS. Watch fan-out path — every controller and sonobuoy smoke exercises it. Not cargo-testable alone; needs Lima VM verification per the vm-operations protocol. Similar to et5o's blast radius. This is a real fix not a spike.

EXPECTED WIN. Per event N-1 parse+reserialize passes eliminated where N is the number of watchers on that resource. At 10 concurrent watchers a 90 percent reduction in per-event fan-out CPU; at conformance scale (typically 2-3 watchers per resource) more modest. Real fix ratio depends on typical watcher-per-resource count in the workload.
notes: PR opened (awaiting mayor review/merge, not yet merged): https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/903
close_reason: PR #903 commit dc666077; measured deltas: criterion watch_fanout_recompute_per_watcher (N independent prepare_live_event calls, what N concurrent watch streams do today) N=5/10/20 = 4.21/8.31/16.58us vs watch_fanout_prepare_once_share_bytes (1 call + Bytes::clone) = 0.855/0.865/0.911us -- 94.5% headroom at N=20 IF a future cache shared output across streams (not wired by this PR -- each watch stream is an independent tokio task, no cross-task sharing exists); end-to-end 10-watcher/200-write scratch-apiserver comparison (baseline 0ff3a99a vs fixed) shows flat wall-clock (+1.9%, expected since write path is untouched) and smaller RSS growth (1344KB->640KB, single-run). VM verified on lima-node-4: kubectl 2-watcher byte-identical ADDED/MODIFIED/DELETED repro, sonobuoy --focus '[sig-api-machinery] Watchers should' 5/5 PASS (had to correct the bead's suggested focus string, which matched 0 real specs).

description:
