title: o11y(debug): scheduler decision-cycle visibility — predicate/preemption/event-emission latency (closes mayor-0ka1z blind spot)
description:
Audit: mayor-o8284 (findings doc: ai/findings/verbose-debug-log-audit-2026-07-24.md, category 5 "Scheduler decision cycle"). Files: crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs, crates/scheduler/src/main.rs.

HEADLINE FINDING: the entire crates/scheduler crate (5,928 lines across lib.rs + main.rs) has ZERO tracing::debug! and ZERO tracing::warn! calls anywhere. Confirmed via grep of every info!(/error!(/debug!(/warn!( call site: 21 total (9 info!, 12 error!, 0 debug!, 0 warn!). Both files `use tracing::{info, error}` only -- debug and warn are never even imported. Every predicate evaluation, every preemption attempt, and every scheduler-to-apiserver HTTP call is invisible even with RUST_LOG=debug today, unlike apiserver/store where at least the primitives exist for some surfaces.

1. [HIGH] lib.rs:1129-1157 (select_node_with_capacity, calls node_qualifies_for_pod at :1060-1068 and resource_fits at :1084-1108) -- the NodeResourcesFit/nodeSelector/affinity/taint predicate core, entirely pure functions, zero logging. When a pod stays Pending there is no record of which nodes were rejected and why (nodeSelector vs taint vs resource exhaustion) -- only the final aggregate Err reaches the caller.

   Fix (immediate, safe): in select_and_reserve_node (lib.rs:1536-1552, already holds the full NodeList and pod), on the Err path from select_node_with_capacity add `debug!(pod = %pod.pod_name, candidates = list.items.len(), "pick_node: no node had capacity")`.
   Stretch goal (larger, note but do not block on it): per-node-rejection-reason tracing would need threading a reason out of node_qualifies_for_pod/resource_fits -- a bigger design change, flag it explicitly in the PR description so it isn't silently dropped, but land the cheap aggregate log regardless.

2. [HIGH] lib.rs:1650-1705 (find_preemption_plan, iterates every qualifying node via select_preemption_victims at :1189-1251, called per-candidate at :1676-1682) -- silent per-candidate. verify_and_reserve_preemption (:1732-1772) can fail (:1758-1763, "capacity may have been claimed concurrently") -- silent. main.rs:123-127's info!("preempting {N} pod(s)...") only fires once a plan is ALREADY chosen -- nothing about how many candidates were evaluated/rejected first, nor about the PreemptionFailure::Skip/Fail paths at main.rs:358-364 (only error! on Skip, :359-361).

   Fix: `debug!(pod = %pod.pod_name, node = %node_name, victims = victims.len(), "find_preemption_plan: candidate evaluated")` inside the `for (index, node) in list.items.iter()` loop (lib.rs:1665) when victims is non-empty; `debug!(node = %plan.node_name, "find_preemption_plan: re-verification failed, capacity claimed concurrently")` at the bail! in verify_and_reserve_preemption (:1758-1763).

3. [HIGH -- directly named in the task brief's context] lib.rs:2001-2029, `emit_scheduling_event` -- the EXACT function mayor-0ka1z's investigation centered on ("silently timing out with no visibility"). Zero logging of any kind, not even on entry. bind_pod (:1842-1856), delete_pod (:2074-2088), patch_pod_status (:2116-2127), and the shared http_get/http_post_json/http_delete/http_patch_status helpers (:29-94) are the same -- the only server-side visibility into ANY of these calls is the terminal info!/error! in main.rs (e.g. :436 "failed to emit {reason} event for {key}: {e}"), which fires on total failure only, with NO latency number even then. PR #833 added a request timeout per mayor-0ka1z's fix, but nothing logs how close to that timeout a call came, or how long a SUCCESSFUL call took -- a creeping latency regression on the events endpoint has no leading indicator before it starts timing out outright again.

   Fix: wrap emit_scheduling_event's http_post_json call (lib.rs:2024) with Instant/elapsed: `debug!(pod = %pod_name, reason, elapsed_ms, "emit_scheduling_event: POST completed")`, logged regardless of outcome. Mirror in bind_pod (:1852-1855), delete_pod's per-iteration http_delete (:2081-2085), and patch_pod_status (:2124-2126) -- all four are the same three-line shape (call, check response, return), so this is mechanical once the first is reviewed.

Scope note: the actual TCP/TLS connect + send/recv happens inside HyperApiClient::request/request_with_content_type (crates/kubeconfig/src/lib.rs:190-292), a SEPARATE crate not in this audit's scope. The proposals above measure at the scheduler's own call sites (in-scope), sufficient to answer "was this specific scheduling HTTP call slow" but not to decompose connect-time vs server-processing-time within it. A future crates/kubeconfig audit is a separate, uncreated item -- do not assume it is covered by this bead.

title: o11y(debug): admission webhook call latency (mutating+validating) + quota/limit-range decision logging
description:
Audit: mayor-o8284 (findings doc: ai/findings/verbose-debug-log-audit-2026-07-24.md, category 4 "Admission chain steps"). Files: crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs, crates/apiserver/src/quota.rs, crates/apiserver/src/limit_range.rs.

1. [HIGH -- single highest-value finding in the whole audit] admission.rs:989-1028, `call_webhook` -- the SHARED HTTP POST helper both the mutating path (invoke_mutating_webhook, calls it at admission.rs:1171) and the validating path (run_validating_webhooks' loop, calls it at admission.rs:3083) route through. Neither call site, nor call_webhook itself, has ANY timing instrumentation on success or failure. The only nearby logging is failure-classification warn!s that fire with no duration (:1208-1211 mutating-Ignore, :3107-3110 validating-Ignore); the Fail/timeout branches (:1213-1225, :3111-3123) return a Status error with NO server-side log at all -- a webhook timeout is only visible to the CLIENT as a 500/504, never logged server-side. This is exactly the shape of blind spot mayor-0ka1z closed for the scheduler's HTTP calls (PR #833) -- it exists identically, unfixed, here.

   Fix: instrument call_webhook itself (one place, covers both call sites for free). Wrap the `client.post(url)...send().await` (:997-1006) and the chunked-read loop (:1010-1023) with Instant/elapsed, and log unconditionally before returning: `debug!(url = %url, elapsed_ms, timed_out, ok = response.is_some(), "admission: webhook HTTP call completed")`.

2. [MED] admission.rs:2557-2600 (run_mutating_webhooks) and :2955-3130 (run_validating_webhooks) -- no entry/exit timing of their own, so even the AGGREGATE "how long did admission take" is invisible before getting to the per-webhook breakdown in #1. Add debug at entry (webhook count in scope) and exit (total elapsed) of both functions. NOTE: the request-path-timing follow-on bead (category 1) also touches these two functions for the same reason from the request-handler's perspective -- sequence/coordinate with that bead so the aggregate log is added once, not twice.

3. [MED] quota.rs:650-780, `check_resource_quota` -- the function that turns a create/update into an HTTP 403 when a ResourceQuota hard limit would be exceeded (three return points: :707-713 service-type quota, :729-734 count-based quota, :755-772 resource-request quota). NONE of the three logs anything -- the 403 reaches the client with no server-side breadcrumb correlating "namespace X's quota Y rejected this request." (The existing warn!s in this file at :287, :371, :470, :559, :603, :611, :632 are infra-failure paths -- "failed to list/count/parse" -- correctly classified, not a gap; do not touch them.)

   Fix: at each of the three rejection points, add `debug!(quota = %quota_name, resource = %quota_resource, requested, used, limit = %limit_str, "quota: request rejected — hard limit exceeded")`.

4. [MED] limit_range.rs:330-371, `apply_limit_ranges` -- either injects default resource requests/limits into a container (inject_defaults, called at :364) or rejects the request (validate_container_resources, called at :365, returns Err on violation). Zero logging either way today. A user whose pod silently gained a resources.limits.cpu they never requested has no server-side trace even at debug level. (The existing warn! at :103, "failed to list LimitRanges," is an infra-failure path, not a gap; do not touch it.)

   Fix: after the per-container loop (:356-368), if inject_defaults actually changed a container's resources, log `debug!(pod_name, container = %name, "limit_range: defaults injected")`; at validate_container_resources' Err return, log the violation before propagating: `debug!(container = %name, err = %e, "limit_range: container rejected")`.

Classification check (additive-only, no rework proposed): admission.rs's existing webhook skip-reason debug!s (:1082-1085, :1102-1105, :1115-1118, :2994-2997, :3014-3017, :3027-3030) are correctly debug-level already -- no change needed there.

Full walkthrough: ai/findings/verbose-debug-log-audit-2026-07-24.md section 4.

title: o11y(debug): SQLite storage-write internals + watch lag near-miss recovery are silent under --verbose
description:
Audit: mayor-o8284 (findings doc: ai/findings/verbose-debug-log-audit-2026-07-24.md, categories 2 "Storage-write internals" + 3 "Watch/broadcast internals" -- clustered into one bead because both live primarily in crates/store/src/sqlite.rs and the write path directly feeds the ring buffer the watch path replays from). Files: crates/store/src/sqlite.rs, crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs.

PART A -- storage-write internals (sqlite.rs), currently zero logging anywhere in the write path:

1. [HIGH] sqlite.rs:378-388, put_sync's no-op short-circuit (`semantically_equal_ignoring_resource_version` -- the fix landed in #893/a11104a7 specifically to stop kubelet's routine unchanged-status re-PATCHes from flooding every watcher). Add `debug!(key, existing_revision, "put_sync: no-op write suppressed")` at the ROLLBACK/return point. This is the highest-value item in this half: the recent fix's own effectiveness under load is currently unverifiable except by inferring from the absence of flood symptoms -- there is no direct "N no-op writes suppressed" signal.

2. [MED] sqlite.rs:159-240, push_event_locked (the sole fan-out point for every write, holds no logging at all): add `debug!(new_horizon, ring_len, "push_event_locked: ring buffer compacted")` guarded on `guard.len() > RING_CAPACITY` actually firing (around :171-177), and `debug!(evicted_key, cap = DELETION_LOG_CAP, "push_event_locked: deletion tombstone log evicted oldest entry")` guarded on the cap eviction actually firing (around :201-208).

3. [MED] sqlite.rs:930-968 (Store::put) and :970-1002 (Store::delete) -- wrap the `spawn_blocking(...).await??` round trip with Instant/elapsed and log `debug!(key, elapsed_ms, is_noop, is_create, "store: write committed")` / `debug!(key, elapsed_ms, "store: delete committed")`. This is the STORAGE-ENGINE-INTERNAL view (blocking-thread-pool + txn-lock-wait time), complementary to the separate request-path-timing follow-on bead's proposal to time the SAME calls from the apiserver handler's caller side -- implement both; they answer different questions (caller-perceived wait vs. internal engine cost).

PART B -- watch/broadcast internals (sqlite.rs watch() + apiserver handlers/watch.rs). Existing coverage is already decent for terminal states (stream-opened at sqlite.rs:1088-1094, compacted-at-connect at :1125-1130, dedup-skip at :1175-1181, yielding-live-event at :1184-1189, compacted-after-lag-recovery at :1266-1271, broadcast-closed at :1285) -- do not re-add these, they exist.

4. [HIGH] sqlite.rs:1199-1279, the `Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(n))` arm. Lag is detected (:1199) and a metric increments (u7s_watch_broadcast_lagged_total, :1201-1203) but there is NO log at the moment of detection, and critically the SUCCESS path -- ring buffer covers the gap, stream continues live without hitting Compacted (implicit fallthrough after the `if current_horizon > last_replayed` check at :1236-1277 does not match) -- has zero trace of any kind, metric or log. This is the exact "lag near-miss recovery attempts" signal named in the task brief; today a near-miss that self-heals is indistinguishable from no-lag-ever-happened. Add one `debug!(prefix = %prefix_owned, missed = n, last_replayed, current_horizon, recovered: bool, "watch: lag detected, ring-buffer recovery attempted")` right after the horizon check resolves (~sqlite.rs:1277), covering both outcomes via the boolean.

5. [MED] sqlite.rs:1088-1094 (the existing "stream opened" debug) -- extend with `receiver_count = tx.receiver_count()` (near-zero cost, value already computed for the u7s_watch_broadcast_receivers metric) so per-open-event fan-out count is visible without a /metrics scrape.

6. [LOW] Per-prefix event RATE (not just per-event) has no signal in any form -- flagged as an open design question (would need new stateful bookkeeping, a ticker or counter map, closer to metric-shaped than a single debug call) rather than a concrete file:line proposal. Whoever picks this bead up should make a call on whether it's in scope or deferred further.

7. [MED] crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs:894-899 and :1015-1020 (convert_watched_cr_object, the CR conversion webhook called per live event) -- success path has zero latency measurement; only failure is logged (correctly, as warn!, at :903-908 / :1039-1044 -- do not touch those). Add `debug!(prefix = %prefix, key = %obj.key, elapsed_ms, "watch: CR conversion webhook call completed")` wrapping the Ok branch.

8. [LOW] crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs:656-668, per-client watch-permit acquisition -- only the 429-rejection path logs/counts; the success path ("watch N/64 opened for user X") has no log. Add `debug!(username = %username, "watch: permit acquired")` after :668.

Scope note: crates/store/src/sqlite.rs is ALSO under live investigation by mayor-z7tuw (RecvError::Closed unreachability, concurrent worktree) -- line numbers here may shift if that fix lands first; reconcile line numbers against HEAD at implementation time, the intent/insertion points described above should still apply.

Full walkthrough: ai/findings/verbose-debug-log-audit-2026-07-24.md sections 2 and 3.

title: o11y(debug): request-path phase timing — LIST body-build + admission/storage-write call-site boundaries invisible under --verbose
description:
Audit: mayor-o8284 (findings doc: ai/findings/verbose-debug-log-audit-2026-07-24.md, category 1 "Request-path timing per verb/resource"). content_type.rs's per-request access log (#895, content_type.rs:121-129, tracing::info!) gives one opaque `latency_ms` per request covering auth+routing+admission+storage+encode combined -- no internal phase breakdown exists anywhere. A perf-regression investigator asking "why did LIST pods tail latency jump 2x" cannot tell from --verbose logs today whether the regression is in the SQLite query, the in-process per-item filtering loop, or JSON response encoding.

Add tracing::debug! at these currently-silent phase boundaries:

1. [HIGH] crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs:136-146 (list_resource, the generic LIST path every non-Pod resource uses) -- wrap `state.store.list(...)` with Instant/elapsed; also log item count (resp.items.len()) and post-filter count from the loop at :153-176.

2. [HIGH] crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:341-351 (list_pods -- Pods bypass resource.rs via a dedicated handler for Pod-specific semantics) -- identical pattern to #1; this is literally the resource named in the task brief's own motivating example question, so it should not be skipped even though resource.rs's fix looks like it "covers" LIST generically.

3. [MED] crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs:327-328 (create_resource) -- the `run_mutating_webhooks(...).await?` / `run_validating_webhooks(...).await?` call site has no timing. Pair this with entry/exit debug logging inside admission.rs:2557 (run_mutating_webhooks) and admission.rs:2955 (run_validating_webhooks) themselves, giving the ADMISSION-CHAIN AGGREGATE latency as one phase of the total request. NOTE: the admission-chain-steps follow-on bead from this same audit proposes PER-WEBHOOK timing inside those same two functions (via admission.rs's shared call_webhook helper) -- coordinate/sequence with that bead since both touch admission.rs:2557-3130; do not implement the aggregate entry/exit log twice.

4. [MED] crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs:341 (create_resource, `state.store.put(&key, obj.to_bytes(), Some(0)).await`) and the equivalent single call site in replace_resource -- wrap with Instant/elapsed. This is the CALLER-SIDE view (how long did the request wait on the store); it is deliberately a different, complementary signal from the storage-internals follow-on bead's proposal to instrument INSIDE crates/store/src/sqlite.rs's Store::put/delete (txn/no-op/broadcast breakdown) -- implement both, they answer different questions, do not conflate into one change.

Scope note: does NOT overlap mayor-atemy.3 (OPEN, P3) -- that bead covers per-pod CONTENT visibility (phase/deletionTimestamp/image) in list_pods' returned items; this bead is about TIMING of the same functions, an orthogonal axis. No proposed change here duplicates atemy.3.

Full walkthrough with additional context: ai/findings/verbose-debug-log-audit-2026-07-24.md section 1.

title: audit(observability): --verbose debug-log coverage across apiserver + store + scheduler — catalog what an operator can see today vs. what's needed to reason about Phase-5 perf work
description:
Gates the Phase-5 perf sprint (per operator directive 2026-07-24 following mayor-atemy Phase 1 merges #895/#896). /metrics endpoint (#896) surfaces WHAT is happening; --verbose debug logs are the operator's tool for WHY. Today they are sparse (~40 tracing::debug! calls across apiserver + store; only 14 files have any) and ad-hoc — some added defensively, some left over from investigations. Need a designed baseline before perf work relies on them.

Audit scope: catalog EVERY tracing::debug!/warn!/info! call across crates/apiserver + crates/store + crates/scheduler. For each call: what it logs, at what level, what happens under --verbose (RUST_LOG=debug). Identify gaps against these categories a perf-regression investigator will need: (1) request-path timing per verb/resource (open, LIST body build, admission chain, storage write, response encode); (2) storage-write internals (SQLite txn boundaries, ring-buffer fills, deletion-tombstone log, compaction horizon movement); (3) watch/broadcast internals (per-subscriber fan-out counts, ring-buffer replay depths, lag near-miss recovery attempts, per-prefix event rate); (4) admission chain steps (mutating/validating webhook call latencies, quota/limit-range effects); (5) scheduler decision cycle (predicate evaluation, preemption attempts, event-emission latency — bearing in mind mayor-0ka1z existed BECAUSE emit_scheduling_event was silently timing out). Cross-reference against ai/findings/observability-watch-events-audit-2026-07-22.md's motivation section for what the operator explicitly wanted to see during past investigations.

Deliverable: ai/findings/verbose-debug-log-audit-2026-07-24.md with per-category gaps + severity + file:line pointers to add each new debug! call. File one small follow-on bead per category (or fewer if categories cluster) for the implementation phase. No code changes in this bead. Bead itself can then be closed by the auditor with the follow-on IDs enumerated in its notes.

EXPLICIT SCOPE NOTE: this audit is ADDITIVE-ONLY analysis — it should propose NEW debug! calls to fill gaps, NOT propose reworking existing tracing infrastructure (structured fields, log format, filter design). Those are separate decisions if the operator wants them. Also, atemy.3 (list/pod-lifecycle debug visibility) is ALREADY a scoped bead in the ready queue — the audit should CROSS-REFERENCE atemy.3 and defer to it for the specific pod-lifecycle scope it covers, not duplicate that work.

title: investigate: RecvError::Closed in SqliteStore::watch() appears structurally unreachable in production
description: Discovered while implementing mayor-atemy.1 (apiserver /metrics endpoint). crates/store/src/sqlite.rs's watch() captures its own clone of the broadcast Sender (tx_clone, kept alive specifically for lag-recovery re-subscription) inside the returned stream's async_stream::stream! generator. Because that clone is captured eagerly and lives for the stream's entire lifetime, a live watch stream always holds at least one Sender handle of its own — meaning tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver::recv() can never return RecvError::Closed for that stream while it is still being polled (Sender refcount can never reach zero while the stream itself holds a handle). Confirmed empirically: a test that dropped the originating SqliteStore while a watch stream was still open timed out waiting for the stream to end, rather than observing Closed.\n\nThe u7s_watch_closed_total{reason="store_closed"} counter (added in mayor-atemy.1) is instrumented at this branch and is harmless, but likely will read zero forever in production given this analysis. Needs investigation: is this branch truly dead code (in which case simplify/remove, or document explicitly), or is there a real teardown path (e.g. simultaneous drop of every outstanding watch task plus the store) that can still reach it? If it's meant to be reachable, tx_clone's retention strategy may need to change (e.g. only clone tx lazily at the point of lag-recovery rather than upfront).
close_reason: PR #897 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/897 — confirmed RecvError::Closed is structurally unreachable (not just empirically); simplified to unreachable!() with regression test, removed dead store_closed metric label

title: investigate: patch_pod_status has no no-op-write suppression, likely floods kubectl -w with meaningless MODIFIED events on every kubelet status re-assertion
description: Operator observed live: kubectl get pods -w against a u7s apiserver produces a continuous stream of lines with no meaningful changes visible. Same command against a live k3s cluster under comparable/heavier public-internet load does NOT show this flood. Code read (not yet live-verified) found a strong candidate root cause: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs patch_pod_status calls apply_status_patch to merge the incoming strategic-merge-patch into the stored object, then UNCONDITIONALLY calls state.store.put with the result inside a retry-on-RevisionMismatch loop -- there is no check anywhere in this path for whether the merged result actually differs from what was already stored. Kubelet posts a status PATCH to this endpoint on every sync-loop tick (a normal, expected kubelet behavior -- it periodically re-asserts current status even when nothing changed, this is not a kubelet bug). If the merged content is byte-for-byte (or semantically) identical to the stored object, this handler still bumps resourceVersion and persists a write, which broadcasts a watch/MODIFIED event to every watcher with no real diff. Real kube-apiserver's generic registry has content-aware update paths that avoid this. Task: (1) Reproduce live -- bring up a stack, create a steady-state pod, capture the ACTUAL PATCH request bodies kubelet sends to /status over a sustained period (e.g. via request logging or a proxy), confirm consecutive ones are content-identical for a pod with genuinely unchanged status. (2) Confirm the resourceVersion bump + watch event fires on each one (kubectl get pods -w or a raw watch client). (3) Research upstream's actual mechanism: does real kube-apiserver's generic registry (or the specific status-subresource strategy) skip persisting/broadcasting a no-op update, and if so how (e.g. comparing old vs new object via reflect.DeepEqual or similar before calling the storage backend)? Check apimachinery/pkg/registry/generic or the relevant REST strategy source on release-1.36. (4) Quantify the actual flood: how many redundant writes per pod per minute in steady state, compared to what real Kubernetes would produce. (5) Propose a fix: likely a semantic-equality check between the pre-patch and post-patch object (ignoring resourceVersion/managedFields naturally) before calling store.put, mirroring whatever upstream's actual mechanism is if a suitable one is found. Do NOT implement the fix in this bead -- audit/root-cause only, then file a properly-scoped fix bead. Operator can provide additional live examples/details if the investigation runs aground -- ask via the bead notes or report back to the mayor rather than guessing.
close_reason: CONFIRMED live on lima-node-4 (port 6446/10253): kubelet PATCHes steady pod's /status every exactly 10.000s; 26/26 and separately 32/32 consecutive steady-state PATCHes were semantic no-ops on .status, yet every one bumped resourceVersion and fired a watch/MODIFIED event (Store::put in patch_pod_status is unconditional, no equality check anywhere in the path or in the Store trait). Clean 5.3-min window, 1 steady pod: 32 watch events observed, 0 reflected an actual status change (~6 meaningless events/min/pod, scales linearly cluster-wide). Reproduces operator's live kubectl -w flood report exactly. Upstream research (release-1.36, staging/.../storage/etcd3/store.go GuaranteedUpdate ~line 553) confirms real kube-apiserver has a generic, resource-agnostic, storage-layer bytes.Equal no-op short-circuit (no write/revision-bump/watch-event on semantically-identical Update) -- this is real k8s' actual architectural defense, not merely 'kubelet dedup', so u7s's lack of an equivalent is a genuine gap. Findings doc (not committed, gitignored): ai/findings/ako44-pod-status-watch-flood-investigation-2026-07-24.md. Filed follow-on fix bead mayor-msf3h (P1, exact fix shape: Store-trait-level no-op suppression mirroring etcd3's mechanism, not a patch_pod_status-only patch). No code changes made in this bead (audit-only); temporary debug instrumentation used for live verification was reverted via git checkout before closing.

title: fix(apiserver): wire CRD schema x-kubernetes-list-type/list-map-keys into strategic_merge_patch for CR instances
description:
Implements the design scoped by mayor-nic50.2 (read-only audit, do not re-investigate --
read ai/findings/nic50-crd-merge-key-plumbing-design-2026-07-24.md first, it has file:line
evidence and exact function signatures). No code was written by mayor-nic50.2; this bead
does the implementation.

## Problem

crates/apiserver/src/patch.rs's merge_key_for_path is a hardcoded literal-path table with
zero CRD-schema awareness, consulted unconditionally by strategic_merge_patch regardless
of resource kind. Every custom resource's list fields get atomic-replace on
strategic-merge-patch, at any nesting depth, unless the field's JSON path coincidentally
collides with one of the built-in literal strings. Real CRDs that embed a
PodTemplateSpec-shaped field (Argo Workflows, Tekton, KEDA ScaledJob, cert-manager, etc.)
are affected right now. x-kubernetes-list-type: map + x-kubernetes-list-map-keys is a real,
documented, GA-since-1.16 CRD structural-schema feature -- this is missing standard CRD
functionality, not a novel ask. Operator-facing requirement: kubectl apply against upstream
and u7s must produce the same result.

## Integration point (already traced)

- handlers/crd.rs:75 -- CustomResourceDefinitionVersion.schema: Option<serde_json::Value>,
  untyped JSON holding the raw openAPIV3Schema.
- handlers/cr.rs::find_crd() (cr.rs:176-274) resolves this per-request into
  CrContext.schema (cr.rs:156). No cache anywhere -- re-fetched/re-scanned from the store
  on every request already, for reasons unrelated to patching (defaulting, validation).
- handlers/cr.rs::patch_cr (cr.rs:2476) and patch_cr_namespaced (cr.rs:2666) both call
  find_crd BEFORE calling crate::patch::strategic_merge_patch(&mut obj, &patch) at
  cr.rs:2584 and cr.rs:2789 respectively -- ctx.schema is already resolved and in memory
  at that point. These are the ONLY two strategic_merge_patch call sites in cr.rs (CR
  status only supports PUT, not PATCH).
- apiextensions_gen_adapter.rs's typed JsonSchemaProps (prost-generated) is NOT the right
  data model to reuse -- it's only used for protobuf-content-type CRD-object
  encode/decode in proto.rs, unrelated to the CR-instance patch path. Write the new
  resolver directly against serde_json::Value, mirroring the existing
  apply_crd_schema_defaults (cr.rs:615) / prune_cr_unknown_fields (cr.rs:719) walking
  convention (properties/items recursion).

## Proposed signatures (from the findings doc -- adjust only if you find a concrete reason to)

  pub fn strategic_merge_patch_for_cr(
      target: &mut serde_json::Value,
      patch: &serde_json::Value,
      schema: Option<&serde_json::Value>,
  ) -> Result<(), PatchError>

  // strategic_merge_patch_at and strategic_merge_array both gain a new
  // `schema: Option<&serde_json::Value>` parameter, threaded through every recursive call.

  fn merge_key_for_path(path: &str, schema: Option<&serde_json::Value>) -> MergeKeyKind {
      if let Some(schema) = schema {
          return crd_merge_key_for_path(schema, path); // never falls through to the
                                                          // built-in table -- that table
                                                          // encodes Pod/Service shapes
                                                          // meaningless for a CRD's own kind
      }
      match path { /* existing hardcoded table, UNCHANGED */ }
  }

  fn crd_merge_key_for_path(schema: &serde_json::Value, path: &str) -> MergeKeyKind {
      // Some("map") + first list-map-keys entry -> MergeKeyKind::Key(String)
      // anything else (absent, "set", "atomic", malformed) -> MergeKeyKind::Unknown
  }

  fn find_schema_node<'a>(schema: &'a serde_json::Value, path: &str) -> Option<&'a serde_json::Value>
      // walks properties.<seg> per dot-separated path segment; when more segments remain
      // and the resolved node has `items`, transparently descends into items first
      // (mirrors how strategic_merge_array flattens array-element paths -- see
      // findings doc section 3 for the full worked example and rationale).

Note: MergeKeyKind::Key currently holds &'static str (fine for the hardcoded literal
table). A CRD-derived key is owned/borrowed from the schema Value, not 'static -- change
Key(&'static str) to Key(String) (small per-array-merge allocation, negligible next to
patch body parsing).

cr.rs call sites change from
  crate::patch::strategic_merge_patch(&mut obj, &patch)
to
  crate::patch::strategic_merge_patch_for_cr(&mut obj, &patch, ctx.schema.as_ref())
at cr.rs:2584 and cr.rs:2789 ONLY. resource.rs and every other built-in-resource caller of
strategic_merge_patch is untouched.

## Answered already (do not re-derive)

- Performance: zero new store round-trips -- ctx.schema is already resolved before these
  call sites run, for unrelated reasons. No caching needed. Staleness is a non-issue: since
  find_crd has no cache today, a kubectl apply that adds list-type to a CRD takes effect on
  the very next PATCH with no invalidation logic required.
- Default (no annotation) behavior: confirmed via patch.rs:118 that MergeKeyKind::Replace
  and MergeKeyKind::Unknown are handled identically (both last-write-wins) -- the
  no-annotation/atomic/set case already gets correct upstream-default atomic-replace
  behavior via Unknown, with zero new logic. Only the "map + list-map-keys present" case
  is the actual gap this bead closes.

## Done-when

- A CR whose CRD schema declares x-kubernetes-list-type: map + x-kubernetes-list-map-keys
  on a list field (including one nested inside an embedded PodTemplateSpec-shaped
  structure, e.g. spec.template.spec.containers-equivalent) gets merge-by-key semantics on
  strategic-merge-patch, matching upstream.
- A CR whose CRD schema has no list-type annotation (or declares atomic/set) continues to
  get atomic-replace, unchanged from today.
- Built-in resource strategic-merge-patch behavior (resource.rs callers) is completely
  unaffected -- regression tests for the existing hardcoded-table paths still pass
  unmodified.
- New unit tests in patch.rs (or cr.rs) cover: a CRD schema with list-type:map merges by
  key at a nested path; a CRD schema with no annotation still atomic-replaces; a CRD
  schema with list-type:set does NOT get merge-by-key (falls to Unknown, not silently
  treated as map).

title: generalize merge_key_for_path's Pod-related entries to suffix-match .template.spec.<field>, not exact-path, so any nesting depth (CronJob and beyond) resolves correctly

description: Discovered via mayor-5x99r investigation 2026-07-23: merge_key_for_path in patch.rs is a hardcoded literal-path-string table, exact-match only. title: replace_pod never completes finalizer drain on PUT (no finalizer_drain_complete check)
description:
Investigation for mayor-2mi3e traced finalizer_drain_complete usage across handlers and found
replace_pod (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:614-689) never calls it (or any equivalent
check) at all on the general PUT path — unlike replace_resource/replace_namespaced_resource
in resource.rs, which do (and were just fixed to read the stored object's deletionTimestamp
instead of trusting the decoded body).

This means a PUT to /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name} that removes a pod's last finalizer
while metadata.deletionTimestamp is set does NOT hard-delete the pod — it just persists the
object as an update, leaving it stuck Terminating forever (the pod never disappears from the
store even though finalizers are empty and deletionTimestamp is set).

This is a pre-existing, independent gap from the protobuf-decode-drops-deletionTimestamp bug
fixed in mayor-2mi3e (it would misbehave even with a perfectly round-tripping JSON PUT), so it
was left out of that fix's scope. Needs someone to add the same finalizer_drain_complete-style
check (hard-delete via the pod's own delete path when deletion_timestamp.is_some() &&
finalizers now empty) to replace_pod, mirroring patch_pod's existing post-patch check at
pods.rs:1002-1024.

title: fix(apiserver): CR orphan-delete (cr.rs) hard-deletes owner BEFORE stripping dependents — same GC race as mayor-74j3.5, worse ordering
description:
delete_cr (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs, ~line 1591-1606) hard-deletes the
owner CR via state.store.delete FIRST, then calls cascade_delete_cr_dependents
(~line 1447) AFTER — which, for orphan=true, synchronously strips each
dependent's ownerReferences one at a time (same in-process store-write pattern
mayor-74j3.5 just removed from resource.rs's RC/Deployment orphan path).

This is the SAME race class mayor-74j3.5 fixed for built-in resources (RC/
Deployment orphan-delete), applied to Custom Resources — and structurally
WORSE: here the owner is already gone from the store before any dependent's
ownerRef is stripped, giving real KCM's GC controller a head start to
cascade-delete a not-yet-stripped dependent (vs. mayor-74j3.5's old code,
which at least attempted the strip before the owner's hard-delete).

Not live-reproduced (no CR-owns-CR fixture handy in this session; found by code
reading while implementing mayor-74j3.5, scoped there explicitly to the
resource.rs built-in-resource call sites only). Fix direction should mirror
mayor-74j3.5: on orphan, add the `orphan` finalizer to the owner CR and defer
to the existing finalizer-drain machinery instead of hard-deleting immediately
and stripping dependents synchronously afterward. Needs its own live-KCM
verification (CR with ownerReferences + --cascade=orphan) before shipping,
same as mayor-74j3.5 required.

title: infra: lima-node-smoke squats hostPort 10251, colliding with worker kubelet-port slot
description:
Discovered while verifying mayor-39z0k (per-node kubelet proxy port fix) on
worker slot lima-node-2 (assigned kubelet port 10251).

~/.lima/lima-node-smoke/lima.yaml and ~/.lima/lima-node-2/lima.yaml both
declare the identical hostPort:10251 -> guestPort:10250 forward. Since
lima-node-smoke was already running before lima-node-2 was (re)provisioned,
lima-node-2's own forward silently lost the bind race: TCP connects to
127.0.0.1:10251 succeeded, but the TLS handshake failed (BadGateway /
websocket close 1006) because the traffic was actually reaching
lima-node-smoke's kubelet (wrong cert/CA), not lima-node-2's.

This is NOT specific to mayor-39z0k's fix -- the OLD (pre-fix) code also
unconditionally dials --kubelet-port for the primary node, so any worker
assigned kubelet port 10251 while lima-node-smoke is running would hit the
identical collision.

Worked around for verification by deleting+recreating lima-node-2 with
kubelet port 10252 (confirmed free across all 6 currently-running lima
VMs at the time). Did not touch lima-node-smoke per dispatch instructions.

Suggest: confirm whether lima-node-smoke is still needed; if not, reap it.
If it needs to stay, reserve its port in whatever doc/convention tracks
worker port-slot assignments (ai/prompts/vm-operations.md or similar) so
10251 is never handed to a live worker again.
close_reason: Fixed directly by the mayor (infra, no code change): lima-node-smoke was live-configured on kubelet-port 10251 (slot 1s documented port) instead of its own 10255 -- a provisioning mistake, not an intentional reservation. Confirmed idle (only an orphaned KCM from a past worker session, endlessly erroring against a stale apiserver cert -- cleaned up as a side effect). Stopped the VM, edited ~/.lima/lima-node-smoke/lima.yaml portForwards hostPort 10251 to 10255, restarted, verified via hostagent log (Found non-static port forward: guest=10250 host=10255) and confirmed 10251 is now free on the host. Updated ~/.config/u7s-workers/lima-node-smoke.kubelet-port cache and docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md with explicit VM-name-to-port mapping plus a live-port verification instruction and this incidents history, to prevent silent drift recurring.

title: fix(apiserver): DeleteCollection has no Custom Resource fallback and ignores field_selector — CustomResourceFieldSelectors still fails after watch-conversion fix
description:
DISCOVERED FROM mayor-tv4ob while doing the mandatory LIVE verification for that bead's fix (CR watch never converts across API versions). After root-cause-2 was fixed (CR watch/sendInitialEvents now convert cross-version events before the field-selector filter — verified both live and via a focused conformance run), the [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourceFieldSelectors conformance test progressed PAST every LIST, WATCH, and informer field-selector assertion (crd_selectable_fields.go:229-267 all pass instantly now) but fails at a NEW, later step:

  STEP: Deleting one custom resources to ensure that deletions are observed
  [FAILED] deleting custom resource: stable.example.com/v2/<generated-crd-plural> "<generated-crd-plural>" not found
  In [It] at: k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/apimachinery/crd_selectable_fields.go:272

This corresponds to upstream's:
  err = v2Client.Namespace(f.Namespace.Name).DeleteCollection(ctx, metav1.DeleteOptions{GracePeriodSeconds: ptr(0)}, metav1.ListOptions{FieldSelector: "host=host1,port=80"})
  framework.ExpectNoError(err, "deleting custom resource")

ROOT CAUSE (two distinct gaps, both in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs):

1. NO CR FALLBACK AT ALL: delete_collection_resource (~2411) and delete_collection_namespaced_resource (~2527) both resolve the resource type via lookup() (handlers/generic.rs:173-188), which only checks state.resource_registry — the static table of built-in (compiled-in) resource types. CRD-backed custom resources are never in that registry (they are dynamic, resolved via handlers::cr::find_crd against stored CustomResourceDefinition objects instead). lookup() returns 404 immediately when the type isn't in the registry, and neither delete_collection_* function has a fallback to cr:: handling — unlike every other verb dispatched from resource.rs (list_resource -> cr::list_cr, get_resource -> cr::get_cr, create_resource -> cr::create_cr, delete_resource -> cr::delete_cr, delete_namespaced_resource -> cr::delete_cr_namespaced, etc., all with an explicit CR-fallback branch — see resource.rs:56,218,274,611-612,1227,1464,2026-2027 for the existing pattern). So ANY DeleteCollection request against a CRD-backed group/version/plural 404s unconditionally, regardless of field/label selector.

2. EVEN WITH A CR FALLBACK, FIELD SELECTORS ARE IGNORED: delete_collection_namespaced_resource's loop only consults query.label_selector (parse_label_selector + apply_label_selector, resource.rs:2545-2549,2576-2581) — query.field_selector is never read at all. The conformance test's DeleteCollection call filters by FieldSelector ("host=host1,port=80"), not a label selector, so even a straightforward 'add a CR fallback that reuses cr::find_crd' fix would still delete either nothing or everything rather than honoring the selector. A correct fix needs both: (a) a CR fallback (find_crd + iterate the CR prefix like list_cr does) and (b) field-selector filtering via cr::cr_matches_field_selector (the same CRD-selectableFields-aware matcher LIST/watch already use), mirroring how mayor-lshow/mayor-tv4ob threaded that matcher into LIST and watch respectively. delete_collection_resource (cluster-scoped) likely has the identical gap for field_selector even for built-in resources — worth checking during the fix.

VERIFY: scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --vm <VM> --port <PORT> --kubelet-port <KUBELET_PORT> --focus "CustomResourceFieldSelectors" — after this fix, the test should progress further (to the post-delete/update re-list and re-watch assertions at crd_selectable_fields.go:274-309) or pass fully if those also already work.

Evidence: temp/e2e/0721-1935-customresourcefieldselectors/podlogs/sonobuoy/sonobuoy-e2e-job-9f1185d6b7304ff9/logs/e2e.txt (lines 17-113) in the mayor-tv4ob worker's worktree.
close_reason: PR #863 opened (https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/863). DeleteCollection CR fallback + field-selector fixed and verified live (before: 404, after: correct partial delete). Focused conformance run advances CustomResourceFieldSelectors past line 272 through line 305 (all LIST/WATCH/DELETE/UPDATE assertions pass); fails at a NEW distinct line-309 informer synthetic-DELETE bug, root-caused and filed separately as mayor-apo6g (discovered-from this bead). mayor-tv4ob should stay open pending mayor-apo6g.

title: perf(apiserver): per-version storage+Cacher for CR conversion so cross-version watch/list converts once per write per version instead of per-object-per-watcher -- upstream apiextensions architecture; do as soon as conformance is green
notes:
Follow-up from mayor-tv4ob Phase-1 design (2026-07-21). Operator decision: implement tv4ob's watch-conversion PER-OBJECT now (get conformance green), then do THIS cache optimization as soon as the suite is green. TRIGGER: conformance suite fully green. Also aligns with the Phase-5 perf phase (correctness-first, then optimize).

WHAT: u7s currently has NO per-version cache for CR conversion. tv4ob's fix converts each cross-version watched event per-object per-watcher via the conversion webhook (same-version watches short-circuit free). Worst case: O(non-storage-watchers x events) webhook calls; a watcher stalled on webhook latency risks 410/resync (store ring buffer 1000/2048, crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:9-10). Fine at conformance scale, unverified for high-churn production.

UPSTREAM ARCHITECTURE to mirror (from tv4ob scout, verified): apiextensions creates one storage+Cacher PER SERVED VERSION (customresource_handler.go:855); each decodes etcd bytes through a version-pinned codec that calls the converter on every read (versioning.go:190). So conversion happens ONCE per write per version, shared by all watchers of that version for free — not a webhook cache, an architectural per-version materialization. Replicating in u7s: a per-served-version view/cache of CR objects (converted at write time or lazily-once-per-version), shared across that version's watchers + LIST. Larger effort — likely its own epic with sub-beads. Cross-ref tv4ob (the per-object interim) + the Phase-5 perf roadmap section.
2026-07-24 measured headroom from mayor-jdeon PR 903: criterion watch_fanout benchmark N=5/10/20 concurrent watchers shows recompute-per-watcher at 4.21us/8.31us/16.58us vs prepare-once-share-bytes at 0.855us/0.865us/0.911us. That is 94.5 percent headroom at N=20 if a cross-task cache like zw0ou proposes shared prepared bytes across the independent tokio tasks each watch stream runs as. Today no such sharing exists - jdeons wiring dedupes within-task duplication and eliminates a double-parse in the DELETED arm but does not cross task boundaries. This measurement is the concrete argument for why zw0ou is architecturally the right thing IF a production workload with high watcher-count materializes. Also captured in jdeons crates/apiserver/benches/watch_fanout.rs as watch_fanout_prepare_once_share_bytes group for repeatable measurement.
Plan doc filed at ai/findings/zw0ou-per-version-storage-cacher-plan-2026-07-29.md (worker agent-a57cef2b033f95739). Awaiting operator review before implementation dispatch. Sub-beads sketched but not created. Summary: upstream (release-1.36) builds one storage+Cacher PER served CRD version, each with a version-pinned versioning.Codec that converts at decode time (versioning.go:190) inside that Cacher's own reflector -- once per write, fanned out to N watchers for free (cacher.go:886-945), plus a SECOND sharing layer caching per-encoder wire bytes via CacheableObject/CacheEncode (cacher.go:947-976). u7s instead converts per-watcher-task per-event via the conversion webhook (watch.rs:959-992). Recommended delta is NOT a full Store+Cacher+reflector rewrite -- it's a lightweight CrConversionCache (RwLock<HashMap<(source_rv,target_version), Arc<Value>>>) mirroring the existing CrSchemaCache precedent (state.rs:200-264, mayor-p8vgj, same HEAD c66c8a0c), wired into the single shared convert_cr_list_items helper (cr.rs:327-352) both LIST and watch already call. 4 sub-beads sketched, ~230-350 LoC production (450-700 incl tests): (1) P2 add CrConversionCache + wire into convert_cr_list_items [load-bearing, low risk, dispatch first]; (2) P3 verify/fix metadata.resourceVersion write-path staleness precondition [likely folds into sub-bead-1 PR]; (3) P3 cache eviction tied to compaction_horizon [optional, memory-hygiene only per monotonic-rv memory]; (4) P3/P4 single-flight coalescing for thundering-herd races [flagged as genuinely separate concurrency mechanism, operator should explicitly decide if worth doing]. KEY CAVEAT surfaced in plan: the cited 94.5% headroom bench (watch_fanout.rs) measures JSON parse/serialize cost via prepare_live_event, NOT the webhook-call cost this bead targets -- it's directional evidence, not a direct prediction; sub-bead 1 should add a webhook-latency-aware benchmark to measure the actual win before deciding on sub-beads 3/4.
Sub-bead 1 filed as mayor-n8bkc (2026-07-29, folded in sub-bead 2's precondition audit + mandatory webhook-latency bench per plan Q5). Operator decision (2026-07-29): dispatch sub-bead 1 now; sub-beads 3 (eviction) and 4 (single-flight) held pending sub-bead 1's bench numbers.
Sub-bead 3 (eviction) filed as mayor-<...>d after n8bkc bench validated the win. Sub-bead 4 (single-flight) still deferred pending concurrent-fanout bench.
close_reason: EPIC done end-to-end. All 4 sub-beads landed on main: sub-bead 1 (mayor-n8bkc / PR #928 CrConversionCache introduction), sub-bead 2 (integrated via n8bkc), sub-bead 3 (mayor-2kuo0 / PR #929 cache eviction on CR + CRD delete), sub-bead 4 (mayor-2ttjh / PR #934 single-flight coalescing via Mutex+Notify). TRIGGER 'conformance suite fully green' met 2026-07-30: 446/446 in 1h45m19s at HEAD c2f74106 (temp/e2e/0730-0222-conformance). Cross-version CR watch/list now converts once per write per version rather than per-object-per-watcher, eliminating the thundering-herd webhook fanout mayor-k7b4w bench proved. Note: one follow-on P3 filed during rr4ja code review — mayor-rguh2 (LeaderClaimGuard zip-truncation on malformed short webhook responses), not a driver for the CRFS investigation, tracked independently.

title: SSA apply-create paths bypass the Terminating-namespace gate: do_patch is_ssa+stored=none at resource.rs:852 (via patch_namespaced_resource) and patch_cr_namespaced at cr.rs:2351 create new objects in a Terminating namespace, unlike the POST create paths -- reintroduces the content-injection wedge class via kubectl apply --server-side
notes: Found by adversarial review of PR #860 (bpmz9) 2026-07-21. bpmz9 added a Terminating-namespace gate to create_pod, and create_namespaced_resource (resource.rs:1435-1448) + create_cr_namespaced (cr.rs:1865-1872) already had one — so POST-create into a Terminating namespace is correctly rejected 403. BUT the SSA APPLY-CREATE paths have NO such gate: do_patch's 'if is_ssa && stored_opt.is_none()' upsert (resource.rs:852, reached via patch_namespaced_resource at resource.rs:2262 for every generic resource type — ConfigMaps/Deployments/ReplicaSets/Jobs/ServiceAccounts) and the identical SSA-upsert block in patch_cr_namespaced (cr.rs:2351, all namespaced CRs). So  (or any SSA-based operator/controller) creating a NOT-yet-existing object in a Terminating namespace SUCCEEDS — reintroducing the 'controller keeps injecting content mid-deletion' wedge class that bpmz9's create_pod gate + KCM-owned deletion was meant to close, just via PATCH+apply instead of POST+create. PRE-EXISTING (not a regression from #860 — #860 is still a net improvement and merged), but it undermines the 'create-gates are sufficient' assumption. FIX: add the same Terminating-namespace check to the SSA-upsert-create branch in do_patch (resource.rs:852) and patch_cr_namespaced (cr.rs:2351) — return 403 'unable to create new content in namespace X because it is being terminated' when is_ssa && object doesn't exist && namespace is Terminating. Sibling to mayor-njkk1 (cluster-scoped delete_collection finalizer bug, also from bpmz9). Verify: kubectl apply --server-side a new configmap into a Terminating namespace -> 403. Cross-ref bpmz9 (PR #860).
close_reason: PR #880 opened - SSA apply-create now rejects new objects in a Terminating namespace at both call sites (resource.rs do_patch and cr.rs patch_cr_namespaced), live-verified with kubectl apply --server-side returning 403 for both a generic resource and a CR

title: fix(apiserver): delete_collection_resource (cluster-scoped) ignores metadata.finalizers, hard-deletes unconditionally
description:
Same class of bug as delete_collection_namespaced_resource and delete_collection_pods (fixed in mayor-bpmz9 / PR #860): delete_collection_resource (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs, the DELETE handler for cluster-scoped collection endpoints like /apis/{group}/{version}/{resource}) calls state.store.delete unconditionally on every listed object, ignoring metadata.finalizers entirely. A cluster-scoped object with a finalizer (e.g. a CustomResourceDefinition, ClusterRole, or PersistentVolume with a legitimate finalizer) gets hard-deleted instead of soft-deleted when removed via DeleteCollection, bypassing the same finalizer protection every single-object DELETE already honors.

Not fixed as part of mayor-bpmz9 because it is not on the namespace-termination path (namespace content lives in namespaced resources, drained via delete_collection_namespaced_resource / delete_collection_pods, not the cluster-scoped variant) so it wasn't required to make that fix work. Same remedy applies: mirror apply_delete_policy's soft-delete-with-deletionTimestamp behavior in the per-object loop, matching what was done for delete_collection_namespaced_resource.
close_reason: PR #880 opened - delete_collection_resource now honors metadata.finalizers via apply_delete_policy, live-verified with a finalizer'd CSINode surviving DeleteCollection

title: CR LIST across versions fails: conversion webhook response JSON parse error 500 on a v1 LIST of a CRD stored as v2 -- blocks CustomResourceFieldSelectors from fully passing after tv4ob root-cause-1
notes: Discovered by the g40rz+tv4ob cluster worker (PR #858) 2026-07-21. After tv4ob root-cause-1 (CR watch selectable-field filtering) landed, CustomResourceFieldSelectors STILL fails: it progresses past both v2 LIST field-selector assertions, then on the v1/hostPort LIST step the apiserver returns a 'conversion webhook response JSON parse error' (HTTP 500) and never reaches the watch assertions. Verified by the worker to be UNRELATED to the #858 diff (no conversion/webhook code touched). This is the CROSS-VERSION CONVERSION half of tv4ob's original title ('CR watch never converts across versions') but manifesting on the LIST path first, via a conversion WEBHOOK response the apiserver can't parse. Likely root cause: u7s's handling of the conversion webhook RESPONSE envelope for CR list conversion (parse error suggests the response shape or the request/response ConversionReview wrapping is off). Needs: reproduce via kubectl (create a CRD with v1+v2 + a conversion webhook, store objects, LIST at v1) on --stack-only, inspect the 500 + apiserver.log for the exact parse failure, then fix the conversion-webhook response parsing. Cross-ref tv4ob (root-cause-1 done in #858; this is root-cause-2). Blocks CustomResourceFieldSelectors + likely CustomResourceConversionWebhook-family tests.
close_reason: PR #861 opened: fixed by sending an explicit Accept: application/json header on the conversion-webhook request (reqwest's default Accept: */* let the real webhook's content negotiation reply non-JSON). Live kubectl repro shows 500->200. Conformance: CustomResourceFieldSelectors now clears ALL 4 LIST assertions (both v1 hostPort steps included); fails later at the v1 cross-version WATCH assertion (crd_selectable_fields.go:259), which is tv4ob's separately-diagnosed root-cause-2 (watch path has no conversion-webhook integration at all) -- unrelated to this fix, tv4ob should stay open for it.

title: Terminating namespace has no async reconciler and cascade retry-exhaustion is indistinguishable from a genuine blocking finalizer, so any create that slips the Terminating gate wedges the namespace forever
notes:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-07-30: A + C combined (transactional guard + typed return). Skip B (periodic sweep) — if A is correct, B has nothing to do; if A were buggy, better to fix A than mask with B.

SCOPE (single PR):
1. Add a store API for transactional guard: something like create_if_namespace_active(ns, key, value) that atomically reads namespace phase (checks status.phase != Terminating) and inserts the object. Extend the Store trait in crates/store/src/lib.rs; implement in crates/store/src/sqlite.rs via a single SQL transaction.
2. Route ALL namespaced create paths through the new API: resource.rs:1441/2226/2856, pods.rs:446, cr.rs:2221/2856, and anywhere else a namespaced create-guard currently reads namespace phase then writes an object non-atomically. Grep for the 'is being terminated' error string as the anchor.
3. Retype cascade_delete_namespace_resources_until_stable (namespaces.rs:810-829) return from bool to enum { CleanEmpty, FinalizerPending, RetryExhausted }. Update the caller (delete_namespace ~line 1033) to distinguish these cases explicitly; RetryExhausted logs at warn level (this should now be unreachable given A closes the create-slip window, but the typed return keeps future refactors from re-introducing a slip via a new create-path that forgot the transactional API).
4. Fail-on-revert tests: (a) reproduce the 74j3.6-style race — spawn a create concurrently with delete_namespace's phase-flip, assert the create gets 403 100% of the time; (b) assert cascade_delete_namespace_resources_until_stable returns FinalizerPending (not RetryExhausted) for a real finalizer'd object, and vice versa.
5. Verify live on lima-node-2 (--stack-only): reproduce the RC/Job repro from 74j3.6, plus try to slip a create through with a curl-race harness; namespace must fully delete within seconds, no wedges.

BLAST RADIUS: ~500-800 LoC. Touches crates/store (Store trait + sqlite impl), 4-6 handler call sites, namespaces.rs cascade return type. Public API change on Store trait.

PERF: single-digit % slowdown on namespaced-create hot path (transactional overhead). No read-path impact.
close_reason: Transactional guard + typed cascade result. Create paths now atomically check namespace phase; cascade retry-exhaustion is distinguishable from real-finalizer-pending. See PR #948 + kubectl verification quoted in PR body.
