title: apiserver drops spec.nodeSelector/spec.affinity on some pod creates under load
description:
Discovered while verifying mayor-oei5x (nodeAffinity) and cross-referencing the
pre-existing NodeSelector predicate fix (mayor-ewnt) during two independent
sonobuoy --focus SchedulerPredicates runs.

Both "validates that NodeSelector is respected if not matching [Conformance]"
and "validates that NodeAffinity is respected if not matching" reproducibly
fail because the conformance-created "restricted-pod" gets BOUND AND RUN despite
carrying a non-matching spec.nodeSelector / spec.affinity.nodeAffinity that no
node satisfies.

Root cause CONFIRMED via kubectl get pod -o json on the live failing pod
(namespace sched-pred-4437, run temp/e2e/0714-2102-schedulerpredicates and
reproduced again in temp/e2e/0714-2159-schedulerpredicates): the PERSISTED pod
object has NO "nodeSelector" key in spec at all -- .spec.nodeSelector and
.spec.affinity are both completely absent/null, even though the e2e test's
create request explicitly set spec.nodeSelector={"label":"nonempty"} (and the
analogous test sets spec.affinity.nodeAffinity with two non-matching
nodeSelectorTerms). The scheduler (crates/scheduler) is NOT at fault here --
its node_selector_matches/node_affinity_matches correctly treat an EMPTY
selector/no-affinity as "matches any node" (standard Kubernetes semantics for
a pod with no restriction), and it faithfully reflects whatever spec it reads
from the watch stream. Manual reproduction via plain `kubectl apply` of an
identical pod (same nodeSelector, in both `default` and a freshly created
namespace) correctly PRESERVES the nodeSelector field and the pod correctly
stays Pending -- so this is NOT reproducible via a simple, low-concurrency
create. It reproduces specifically for the sonobuoy e2e test's pod, which is
created amid heavy concurrent apiserver traffic right after cluster/sonobuoy
bootstrap (many concurrent namespace/serviceaccount/configmap/RBAC creates
from parallel ginkgo workers) -- strongly suggesting a CONCURRENCY bug in
crates/apiserver's pod CREATE path (admission mutation --  e.g. the
ServiceAccount token volume injection that also appears on this pod, which
rewrites/merges the spec -- or the underlying store write) that drops
unfamiliar/optional fields under concurrent load, rather than a nodeSelector-
specific bug.

Reproduction:
1. Bring up a fresh --stack-only stack.
2. sonobuoy --focus "SchedulerPredicates" (or just the NodeSelector/NodeAffinity
   focus) twice in a row -- both times "restricted-pod" gets bound to the sole
   node despite requesting a label no node has.
3. kubectl get pod -n <sched-pred-NNNN> restricted-pod -o json immediately
   after -- .spec.nodeSelector / .spec.affinity are absent.
4. Compare with a manually kubectl-applied pod with the identical
   nodeSelector -- it correctly stays Pending with the field intact.

Fix should live in crates/apiserver's pod create/admission path -- investigate
the ServiceAccount admission/mutation and/or the store's object-merge logic
for a race under concurrent creates that silently drops caller-supplied
optional spec fields.
close_reason: PR #787 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/787 — root cause confirmed (apiserver protobuf pod decoder dropped spec.nodeSelector/spec.affinity.nodeAffinity), fixed, verified live via before/after sonobuoy runs

title: chore(apiserver): extension apiserver CrashLoopBackOff pods still fail RBAC even after RoleBinding creation until fresh restart
description:
Follow-up from mayor-n3yk. Fixed the missing system:auth-delegator ClusterRole + kube-system/extension-apiserver-authentication-reader Role (real bootstrap RBAC gap, confirmed via live manual repro that a FRESH pod started after these objects exist reaches Deployment Available). However, the actual [sig-api-machinery] Aggregator conformance test still times out (302s) in a live sonobuoy --focus run: the sample-apiserver container starts crash-looping (Forbidden on the extension-apiserver-authentication configmap) BEFORE the e2e test's own RoleBinding is created (~2s after pod start, confirmed via apiserver.log: RoleBinding POST at t+2s), and appears to KEEP failing with the identical Forbidden error for 3+ minutes across multiple CrashLoopBackOff restarts, despite the RoleBinding existing well before each restart.

Manually reproducing the EXACT same sequence (deployment create -> few seconds later -> create RoleBinding+ClusterRoleBinding, WITHOUT deleting the pod) DID self-heal within ~26s (2 restarts) in one controlled test. But the live sonobuoy run's pod kept failing past 3 minutes. Root cause NOT confirmed — ruled out: RBAC index key-format/namespace-extraction bug (rbac.rs's apply_object + state.rs's init() correctly reconstruct the namespaced /apis/.../namespaces/<ns>/roles/<name> key format, verified by reading the code and by a passing regression test). Also ruled out: RbacIndex caching/staleness (apply_object is called synchronously in the same request handler that persists the object, no async refresh delay).

Suspected but unconfirmed: something specific to REPEATED requests from the same crash-looping pod/SA-token, or a kubelet/CRI restart-backoff timing anomaly making restarts far less frequent than the standard 10/20/40/80s schedule, or a race between iptables DNAT rule state and pod restarts. Needs live request-level tracing (e.g. --verbose apiserver logs correlated with exact kubelet restart timestamps) to pin down further.

Evidence: temp/e2e/0714-1820-should-be-able-to-support-the-1-17-sample-api-server-using-the-current-aggregator/ (sonobuoy run showing the timeout even with the fix applied), and the mayor-n3yk investigation notes.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED (PR #786, https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/786) — but a
SEPARATE, unrelated bug (mayor-ux65o) now blocks the full focus-PASS, so this bead stays
open per its own gate ("do not close as fixed without a focus-PASS").

## Root cause (two compounding bugs, both in the RBAC/defaulting layer)

1. crates/apiserver/src/auth.rs: AuthzRequest.name was ONLY ever derived from the URL
   path. Every client-go informer that watches a single named object (including the one
   every aggregated apiserver uses to read kube-system/extension-apiserver-authentication)
   does so via LIST+WATCH with `fieldSelector=metadata.name=<name>`, NOT a plain named GET.
   So `name` was always None for this traffic, and rbac.rs's rule_covers() unconditionally
   denies a resourceNames-restricted rule when name=None. Confirmed real Kubernetes derives
   RequestInfo.Name from an exact-match field selector for precisely this reason
   (k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/request/requestinfo.go lines ~247-253, fetched and
   cached at temp/research/requestinfo.go). Fixed by adding field_selector_name() in
   auth.rs, used only for the authz name field (verb stays list/watch, matching upstream).

2. crates/apiserver/src/handlers/defaults.rs: RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding
   roleRef.apiGroup was never defaulted when empty. Real Kubernetes defaults it server-side
   (pkg/apis/rbac/v1/defaults.go: SetDefaults_RoleBinding/SetDefaults_ClusterRoleBinding,
   cached at temp/research/rbac_v1_defaults.go). The upstream aggregator e2e test's
   RoleBinding object (test/e2e/apimachinery/aggregator.go line ~338, cached at
   temp/research/aggregator.go) literally sends `RoleRef{APIGroup: ""}`. Without
   defaulting, the stored apiGroup stayed "", and rbac.rs's resolve_role_rules() exact-match
   check on "rbac.authorization.k8s.io" silently returned zero rules — the binding granted
   NOTHING, no matter how long it existed. This alone fully explains why the manual
   controlled repro "self-healed" (it almost certainly used a plain kubectl-generated
   RoleBinding with the correct apiGroup, and/or a plain named GET) while the live sonobuoy
   run — which uses this exact test object with the empty apiGroup — never did, regardless
   of restart count or timing.

Both bugs independently caused a PERMANENT (not flaky/racy) deny — restart timing, SA token
staleness, kubelet backoff cadence, and iptables/DNAT races (all raised as suspects in the
original bead) were RED HERRINGS. The "identical Forbidden error across every restart for
3+ minutes" was simply because the RoleBinding never actually granted anything, ever, on
this exact request pattern — there was no self-healing to wait for.

## Evidence (three live sonobuoy --focus runs on lima-node-smoke, 6444/10251)

- temp/e2e/0714-1937-.../ — reproduced original bug on latest main + mayor-n3yk's fix
  merged in: pod crash-loops past 300s, e2e.txt confirms `[FAILED] ... error waiting for
  deployment status to match expectation ... 303.487 seconds`. kubelet.log shows 6 restarts
  across the full 5 minutes following the exact 10/20/40/80/160s backoff schedule — so the
  "kubelet backoff anomaly" hypothesis is also ruled out; the schedule was normal.
- temp/e2e/0714-2137-.../ — after fix #1 only (fieldSelector name): STILL fails the same
  way. Pod log (finally captured this run) shows the exact error text:
  "system:serviceaccount:aggregator-6820:default is not allowed to get configmaps" —a
  DIRECT named GET (RunOnce() in requestheader_controller.go, cached at
  temp/research/requestheader_controller.go line ~198), which should have had name=Some(...)
  already — pointing straight at bug #2 (roleRef.apiGroup).
- temp/e2e/0714-2213-.../ — after BOTH fixes: Deployment reaches Available in 24.559s (down
  from a 300s+ permanent failure). Test proceeds to a LATER step ("Registering the sample
  API server" -> creating an APIService object), which now fails for an entirely different,
  unrelated reason: `POST /apis/apiregistration.k8s.io/v1/apiservices` returns 400 "invalid
  JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1" — a protobuf-request-body decoding gap in generic
  resource creation, NOT RBAC. Filed separately as mayor-ux65o since it's a different
  subsystem (content-type negotiation) requiring its own investigation.

## Verification

cargo test --workspace --quiet: 2182 apiserver tests + full workspace pass, including 11 new
regression tests (field_selector_name unit tests, two full AuthService-integration tests
proving the exact bug scenario, and 4 default_role_ref_api_group tests).
cargo clippy --workspace --tests --quiet -- -D warnings: clean.

## Verdict

The mechanism THIS bead describes (permanent RBAC-driven CrashLoopBackOff despite a timely
RoleBinding) is CONCLUSIVELY fixed and merged-ready in PR #786. Full conformance PASS for
this specific test is blocked by a newly-discovered, unrelated bug tracked as mayor-ux65o.
Recommend: merge #786 (fixes a real, well-evidenced bug regardless), then re-run this
bead's focus gate once mayor-ux65o lands; close mayor-fnym9 at that point with the PASS
quote, or re-scope/close now with a cross-reference at the mayor's discretion since the
originally-described mechanism is resolved.
close_reason: Resolved by mayor-vl391/PR #801, landed after this bead's last evidence. The crash-loop was against the extension-apiserver-authentication configmap via a system:auth-delegator SAR check (a non-resource-URL check) -- vl391's PR fixed authorization.rs never parsing spec.nonResourceAttributes at all, so that exact SAR was unconditionally denied no matter how many times the RoleBinding retry happened. This explains why this bead's own RBAC-data/timing investigation (index key-format, RbacIndex staleness) found nothing: the real blocker was the SAR check itself being structurally broken for non-resource URLs, not RBAC role/rolebinding state. vl391's own verification already passed the exact gate this bead was blocked on: sonobuoy --focus 'Should be able to support the 1.17 Sample API Server' PASS (Ran 1 of 7579 Specs in 37.037 seconds, SUCCESS). Closing rather than re-running redundantly -- same test, same passing evidence.

title: investigate(scheduler): nodeSelector predicate ignored for pod scheduled ~10min into sustained e2e load (NodeSelector-not-matching test)
description:
Discovered while fixing mayor-lafgk (scheduler doesn't emit FailedScheduling events).
sonobuoy --focus SchedulerPredicates run temp/e2e/0714-1849-schedulerpredicates shows
"validates that NodeSelector is respected if not matching [Conformance]" STILL failing
at predicates.go:1102 even though:

1. crates/scheduler/'s node_selector_matches/select_node_for_pod/pick_node DO correctly
   implement nodeSelector matching (unit-tested, mayor-ewnt).
2. A manual live repro immediately after a fresh --stack-only bring-up (`kubectl apply`
   a pod with nodeSelector {label: nonempty} against a node with no such label) correctly
   left the pod Pending and produced a FailedScheduling event.
3. But in the actual e2e run, ~10 minutes and several prior SchedulerPredicates tests
   into the SAME long-lived scheduler process's uptime, the identical scenario
   (test creates "restricted-pod" with nodeSelector {label: nonempty}, no node has that
   label — confirmed via `kubectl get node -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels}'` post-run,
   no stray "label" key present) got BOUND anyway:

   scheduler.log:
     09:42:50.974398Z INFO unscheduled pod detected: sched-pred-3956/restricted-pod
     09:42:50.976865Z INFO bound pod sched-pred-3956/restricted-pod -> node lima-node-4

   Only ~2.5ms between detection and bind, with NO intervening "preempting N pod(s)"
   log line — meaning pick_node's FIRST attempt returned Ok directly, i.e. it believed
   the node satisfied the selector on the very first try. This strongly suggests
   needs_scheduling extracted an EMPTY (not `{"label":"nonempty"}`) node_selector for
   this specific watch ADDED event, since an empty selector matches any node
   instantly (node_selector_matches semantics).

Leading hypothesis (unconfirmed): a watch-delivery/parsing race under sustained load —
by this point in the run the scheduler's long-lived pod watch had processed several
prior SchedulerPredicates tests plus a resource-saturation test that created 10+
additional pods with many lifecycle events, i.e. real contention existed by 09:42:50
(unlike mayor-lafgk's own event-emission repro, which was demonstrated in a fresh,
uncontended stack). Possible causes to check: drain_watch_buffer mis-splitting a
multi-frame chunk under load such that this pod's ADDED JSON gets truncated/merged with
an adjacent event and needs_scheduling's serde_json::from_value falls back to its
unwrap_or_else default (which uses PodSpec::default() -> node_selector: None -> empty
map) — see needs_scheduling's fallback path in lib.rs. This is DISTINCT from mayor-sjlw1
(DELETE-tombstone missing apiVersion/kind, already fixed) and mayor-et5o (BOOKMARK
latency) — neither explains a wrong/empty field value in an ADDED event that otherwise
decoded successfully enough to trigger a bind. Needs a scout with RUST_LOG=debug across
a full SchedulerPredicates run correlating the raw watch line for this specific pod.
notes:
Likely superseded by mayor-2rf39's root cause and fix (apiserver protobuf pod decoder
silently dropping spec.nodeSelector/spec.affinity.nodeAffinity — core_gen_adapter.rs's
gen_pod_spec_to_json never read PodSpec.node_selector/affinity off the generated prost
struct). That mechanism fully explains this bead's symptom WITHOUT needing a scheduler-
side watch-parsing race:

- e2e test clients (client-go clientsets) send Pod creates as protobuf; kubectl sends
  JSON. The manual "kubectl apply" repro noted here (and in mayor-lafgk) used JSON, so
  it always worked — it was never exercising the actual bug.
- The apiserver itself persisted restricted-pod with an EMPTY/absent nodeSelector in the
  store (confirmed live via `kubectl get pod -o json` immediately after protobuf-encoded
  create, before any scheduler involvement). Every subsequent watch ADDED event the
  scheduler received for that pod legitimately carried an empty node_selector because
  that's what was actually stored — no truncation/merge/buffer-splitting needed in
  crates/scheduler to explain it.
- The "~10 minutes into sustained load" correlation was very likely just "whichever
  point in that run's test ordering the first protobuf-encoded restricted-pod create
  happened to occur," not a true time/load dependency: verified this directly by running
  a FRESH, minimally-loaded, --focus scoped to ONLY the NodeSelector+NodeAffinity tests
  post-fix — the NodeSelector test ran as the very FIRST spec (seconds after sonobuoy
  bootstrap, no sustained load whatsoever) and correctly preserved nodeSelector /
  correctly stayed Pending.

Recommend closing this as a duplicate/superseded-by mayor-2rf39 unless further
investigation turns up a genuine independent watch-race on top of the now-fixed
decode bug (I did not find evidence of one).

Residual observation (out of scope for mayor-2rf39, not investigated further here):
post-fix, "validates that NodeSelector/NodeAffinity is respected if not matching" STILL
fail at predicates.go:1102 with "STEP: Found 0 events." even though mayor-lafgk (closed,
PR #777) claims FailedScheduling event emission was fixed and verified. The pod itself
is correctly left Pending/Unschedulable with the field intact (confirmed via live
kubectl get pod -o json), so this is purely the event-emission gap, but it may indicate
mayor-lafgk's fix doesn't cover the plain-predicate-mismatch-no-preemption-attempted
code path specifically (as opposed to whatever path its own verification exercised).
close_reason: Duplicate of/fixed-by mayor-2rf39 (PR #787, merged). CONFIRMED via two independent live checks on a fresh --reset stack (lima-node-3, main@933c43ee incl. f33d87b3): (1) a genuine raw-protobuf-wire POST (same bytes as mayor-2rf39's merged unit tests, sent over a real TLS connection to the live running apiserver, not an in-process test) with spec.nodeSelector={label:nonempty} -> kubectl get pod -o json shows spec.nodeSelector correctly preserved and status.phase=Pending/PodScheduled=False/Unschedulable. (2) fresh sonobuoy --focus 'SchedulerPredicates' run (temp/e2e/0715-1015-schedulerpredicates, 32 ran/24 passed/8 failed): for BOTH 'validates that NodeSelector is respected if not matching [Conformance]' and 'validates that NodeAffinity is respected if not matching', e2e.txt's own resource dump shows the real e2e-created restricted-pod (namespaces sched-pred-4397 and sched-pred-2973, also caught live via kubectl mid-run) correctly Pending with PodScheduled=False/Unschedulable/'pod not yet scheduled' -- the scheduling decision itself is now correct. Both tests still FAIL, but via 'context deadline exceeded' at predicates.go:1102 after 'STEP: Found 0 events' -- NOT a recurrence of this bug. Root cause of that residual failure: PR #777 (mayor-lafgk, FailedScheduling/Scheduled event emission) is confirmed OPEN/UNMERGED (gh pr view: mergedAt=null, state=OPEN) -- emit_scheduling_event etc. do not exist anywhere in crates/scheduler on main, so no scheduling-outcome Event is ever emitted for ANY pod yet, which is exactly why the event-watch step times out. mayor-lafgk's bead was closed on PR-open per convention but the PR itself is still pending mayor merge. Recommend mayor prioritize merging PR #777 -- its own gate-results table already predicted both these tests would need it. No code changes made in this dispatch (a throwaway verification harness was added to crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs and fully reverted; git diff is empty).

title: fix(apiserver): PATCH/PUT node extended-resource update returns 409 'Node already exists' (breaks pod-overhead conformance BeforeEach)
description:
Discovered while fixing mayor-lafgk (scheduler doesn't emit FailedScheduling events).
sonobuoy --focus SchedulerPredicates run temp/e2e/0714-1849-schedulerpredicates shows
"validates pod overhead is considered along with resource limits of pods that are
allowed to run [BeforeEach] verify pod overhead is accounted for" failing at
predicates.go:240, NOT at the event-wait line (predicates.go:1102) — this is unrelated
to scheduling/events entirely:

  Unexpected error: unable to apply fake resource to lima-node-4:
  Node "lima-node-4" already exists (409, reason AlreadyExists)

The test's BeforeEach tries to patch a fake extended resource (e.g.
example.com/foo: 5) onto the node's status.capacity/allocatable, and the apiserver
rejects it with a 409 "already exists" — which normally means a CREATE was attempted
against an object that already exists, suggesting the update path is (incorrectly)
routed through create/PUT-as-create logic instead of a real PATCH/subresource update
for the node status. AfterEach then also fails removing the fake resource with the
same error (predicates.go:271).

Fix: find whatever handler processes the fake-resource node-capacity update in this
test (likely a raw PATCH to /api/v1/nodes/{name}/status or similar) and confirm the
apiserver's node PATCH/update handler doesn't fall through to a create path that
collides with the already-existing node. Needs its own reproduction — this bead only
scouted it as a side-finding of mayor-lafgk.
close_reason: PR #782 opened (fix(apiserver): node status PATCH returns spurious 409 AlreadyExists). Root cause: crates/apiserver/src/util.rs parse_resource_version mapped resourceVersion="0" to Some(0) (Store::put create-only semantics) instead of None (unconditional write), so sig-scheduling's node-status BeforeEach/AfterEach (nodeCopy.ResourceVersion="0"; UpdateStatus) against an existing node 409'd. Fixed by mapping "0" to None like an absent RV. Regression tests: util::tests::parse_resource_version_zero_is_unconditional_not_create_only, handlers::status::tests::put_resource_status_explicit_zero_rv_is_unconditional_write_on_existing_object (verified fails-on-revert). Gate: sonobuoy --focus 'validates pod overhead is considered along with resource limits' e2e.txt shows zero AlreadyExists occurrences and both BeforeEach/AfterEach STEPs complete (the [It] body itself still fails at predicates.go:1102, the separate scheduler resource-fit gap tracked in mayor-7duz2, out of scope). cargo test --workspace and cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings both clean.

title: feat(scheduler): NodeResourcesFit must check cpu/memory/ephemeral-storage requests, not just pod count
description:
Discovered while fixing mayor-lafgk (scheduler doesn't emit FailedScheduling events).
sonobuoy --focus SchedulerPredicates run temp/e2e/0714-1849-schedulerpredicates shows
two tests still failing at predicates.go:1102 despite the event-emission fix:
  - "validates resource limits of pods that are allowed to run [Conformance]"
  - "validates local ephemeral storage resource limits of pods that are allowed to run"
Both tests saturate a node's cpu/ephemeral-storage capacity with N pods, then create one
more pod expecting the SCHEDULER to reject it (FailedScheduling event). Instead
crates/scheduler/'s select_node_with_capacity (lib.rs) only tracks pod COUNT against
status.allocatable.pods — it has no notion of cpu/memory/ephemeral-storage requests at
all. So the scheduler binds the extra pod anyway; the KUBELET then rejects it after the
fact with OutOfcpu / OutOfephemeral-storage (see e2e.txt: "Node didn't have enough
resource: cpu, requested: 4000, used: 5600, capacity: 8000"), which is a real-kubelet
event but NOT a scheduler FailedScheduling event, so the test's observeEventAfterAction
watch times out.

Fix: extend pick_node/select_node_with_capacity to sum each candidate node's already-
bound pods' resource requests (cpu/memory/ephemeral-storage) alongside the existing pod-
count check, and skip nodes where the pending pod's requests would exceed
status.allocatable minus already-committed requests — mirroring the real
NodeResourcesFit predicate. See k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/scheduling/predicates.go:129
(ephemeral-storage) for the exact saturate-then-overflow test shape.
close_reason: PR #784 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/784. Fixed in crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs: added ResourceRequests + parse_quantity_milli (mirrors crates/apiserver/src/quota.rs's arithmetic, kept crate-local since these are independent binaries with no shared types crate), extended NodeAllocatable with cpu/memory/ephemeral-storage, and replaced count_non_terminated_pods with summarize_node_pods (same terminal-phase filter, now also summing resource requests from a single JSON parse). select_node_with_capacity now rejects a node when the pending pod's own requests (extracted by needs_scheduling from spec.containers) plus already-committed usage would exceed status.allocatable for cpu/memory/ephemeral-storage, alongside the existing pod-count check. Verified correct via kubectl (a pod requesting more cpu than allocatable stays Pending) and via sonobuoy e2e.txt for BOTH the cpu and ephemeral-storage sub-tests: the 'additional-pod' in each case is shown staying Pending with condition PodScheduled=False/Unschedulable ('pod not yet scheduled'), confirming the scheduler correctly never bound it. HONEST PARTIAL: both conformance tests still fail at predicates.go:1102 -- purely because the scheduler doesn't yet emit a FailedScheduling event for the test's observeEventAfterAction wait, a separate, already-fixed-but-unmerged gap (PR #777, mayor-lafgk). RISK NOTED: summing resource requests requires one extra GET per qualifying candidate node per scheduling decision (same call pattern as before, now also parsing resource requests) -- fine at this project's scale but would need caching/informers at real cluster scale.

title: feat(scheduler): respect non-empty schedulingGates (must not bind gated pods)
description:
Discovered while fixing mayor-lafgk (scheduler doesn't emit FailedScheduling events).
sonobuoy --focus SchedulerPredicates run temp/e2e/0714-1849-schedulerpredicates shows
"validates Pods with non-empty schedulingGates are blocked on scheduling" failing at
predicates.go:831 (WaitForPodsSchedulingGated times out) — a ReplicaSet's pods carry
spec.schedulingGates: [foo, bar] and MUST stay Pending (not even considered "ready to
schedule") until the gates are cleared, but crates/scheduler/'s needs_scheduling has no
concept of schedulingGates at all: it schedules any pod with empty spec.nodeName
regardless of gates, so all 3 ReplicaSet pods get bound and start Running immediately.

Fix: extract spec.schedulingGates from the watch event in needs_scheduling and return
None (do not schedule) whenever the list is non-empty — mirroring how Kubernetes'
scheduler treats non-empty schedulingGates as "not ready for scheduling", distinct from
a normal predicate failure (no FailedScheduling event is expected in this case either;
the pod simply never enters the scheduling cycle). See
k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/framework/pod/wait.go:454-476 (WaitForPodsSchedulingGated) and
predicates.go:810 for the exact test shape.
close_reason: PR #784 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/784. Fixed in crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs needs_scheduling: non-empty spec.schedulingGates now returns None, keeping the pod out of the scheduling cycle entirely (verified: gated pod stays Pending, spec.nodeName empty, both via direct kubectl and sonobuoy). HONEST PARTIAL: the conformance test 'validates Pods with non-empty schedulingGates are blocked on scheduling' still fails because WaitForPodsSchedulingGated (upstream wait.go:475-486) additionally requires a PodScheduled=False/Reason=SchedulingGated status condition that no component in u7s ever writes -- this is a distinct, separate requirement beyond 'don't schedule the pod', filed as mayor-pwf4g.

title: feat(scheduler): enforce taints/tolerations predicate
description:
Discovered while fixing mayor-lafgk (scheduler doesn't emit FailedScheduling events).
sonobuoy --focus SchedulerPredicates run temp/e2e/0714-1849-schedulerpredicates shows
"validates that taints-tolerations is respected if not matching" still failing at
predicates.go:1102: the test taints a node NoSchedule and creates pods with no matching
toleration, expecting them to stay Pending (FailedScheduling event). Instead
scheduler.log shows both "without-toleration" and "still-no-tolerations" pods get bound
immediately to the tainted node — crates/scheduler/ has zero taint/toleration handling
(grep for "taint"/"toleration" in lib.rs/main.rs returns nothing). NodeItem doesn't even
deserialize spec.taints from the node list response.

Fix: add taints to NodeItem/NodeStatus deserialization (or a new NodeSpec struct with
`taints: Vec<Taint>`), extract spec.tolerations from the pod watch event in
needs_scheduling, and gate node selection on toleration-matches-taint (NoSchedule and
NoExecute effects must block scheduling unless a toleration matches key/value/effect,
or the toleration uses operator Exists). See
k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/scheduling/predicates.go:632 for the exact test shape.
close_reason: PR #784 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/784. Fixed in crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs: added Taint/Toleration types, NodeItem now deserializes spec.taints, needs_scheduling extracts spec.tolerations, and node_taints_tolerated gates node selection (NoSchedule/NoExecute blocked unless tolerated; PreferNoSchedule never hard-blocks since this scheduler does no scoring). Folded into a shared node_qualifies_for_pod used by both select_node_with_capacity and find_preemption_plan. Verified correct via kubectl (untolerated pod on a NoSchedule-tainted node stays Pending; tolerated pod binds) and via sonobuoy e2e.txt timeline (the relaunched untolerated pod produces zero container events, confirming it never got bound). HONEST PARTIAL: the conformance test 'validates that taints-tolerations is respected if not matching' still fails at predicates.go:1102 -- purely because the scheduler doesn't yet emit a FailedScheduling event for the observeEventAfterAction wait to see, a separate, already-fixed-but-unmerged gap (PR #777, mayor-lafgk).

title: feat(scheduler): enforce nodeAffinity (RequiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution) predicate
description:
Discovered while fixing mayor-lafgk (scheduler doesn't emit FailedScheduling events).
After fixing event emission, sonobuoy --focus SchedulerPredicates run
temp/e2e/0714-1849-schedulerpredicates showed "validates that NodeAffinity is respected
if not matching" still failing at predicates.go:1102 (context deadline exceeded waiting
for a FailedScheduling event) — but for a DIFFERENT reason than the event gap: the
scheduler (crates/scheduler/) has ZERO handling of spec.affinity.nodeAffinity anywhere
(grep confirms no "affinity"/"Affinity" references in lib.rs or main.rs). It only checks
spec.nodeSelector via node_selector_matches. A pod with a NodeAffinity
RequiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution term that no node satisfies gets bound
anyway (scheduler.log: "unscheduled pod detected" immediately followed by "bound pod"),
so the scheduler emits a "Scheduled" event instead of "FailedScheduling" — the test then
times out waiting for the failure event that (correctly, per the new fix) never comes,
because the pod really was bound.

Fix: extract spec.affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution
from the watch event in needs_scheduling (or a new extraction function) and evaluate its
nodeSelectorTerms/matchExpressions against candidate node labels in pick_node /
find_preemption_plan, mirroring node_selector_matches. See
k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/scheduling/predicates.go:500 for the exact NodeAffinity shape
the conformance test uses (MatchExpressions with In/NotIn operators, multiple terms
ORed together per NodeSelector semantics).
close_reason: PR #784 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/784. Fixed in crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs: added NodeAffinity/NodeSelectorSpec/NodeSelectorTerm/NodeSelectorRequirement types, needs_scheduling extracts spec.affinity.nodeAffinity.requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution, and node_affinity_matches evaluates it (nodeSelectorTerms ORed, matchExpressions within a term ANDed, In/NotIn/Exists/DoesNotExist operators) -- folded into node_qualifies_for_pod alongside nodeSelector/taints, used by both pick_node and find_preemption_plan. Verified correct via direct kubectl repro (a pod with a non-satisfiable required nodeAffinity term stays Pending; the same pod created after labeling a matching node correctly binds) and via unit tests. HONEST PARTIAL, and IMPORTANT FINDING: sonobuoy's 'validates that NodeAffinity is respected if not matching' (and the pre-existing NodeSelector-not-matching test) still fail, but NOT because of a scheduler defect -- confirmed via kubectl get pod -o json on the live failing pod that the apiserver is DROPPING spec.nodeSelector/spec.affinity from the persisted pod object entirely under concurrent load (reproduced across 2 independent full sonobuoy runs; NOT reproducible via a simple low-concurrency kubectl apply of an identical spec, which correctly preserves the field). This is a separate, more serious apiserver bug, filed as mayor-2rf39 -- do not conflate it with this bead's scope.

title: apiserver: hostNetwork pod podIPs patch causes kubelet sandbox-recreate loop (blocks hostNetwork exec pods)
description:
Any hostNetwork:true pod (e.g. an exec/debug pod used by e2e tests) enters a
continuous kubelet "Sandbox for pod has changed. Need to start a new one" loop
and the container is killed and recreated every ~1s indefinitely — it never
stabilizes long enough for `kubectl exec` to reliably run a command inside it.

Discovered while investigating mayor-9dv5 ([sig-network] HostPort 'validates
that there is no conflict between pods with same hostPort but different
hostIP and protocol'). That test's failure is NOT a hostPort/dataplane bug —
CRI-O's own hostports nftables implementation correctly disambiguates by
(hostIP, protocol, port) and connectivity to the actual hostPort-exposed pods
works fine in manual repro. The failure is caused entirely by the test's own
`e2e-host-exec` pod (hostNetwork: true, no args — a plain agnhost container
used only to `kubectl exec` curl/nc from) being killed and recreated by
kubelet every ~1s, so the ExecWithOptions calls the test issues either hit a
container mid-teardown or a fresh container whose shell session dies
instantly, surfacing as "Can not connect ... to serverIP" in the test's retry
loop.

Reproduced twice (2 separate sonobuoy --focus runs, both failing identically
at hostport.go:164 with the same cmdPod1 exec error), and confirmed via a
manual pod (hostNetwork: true, agnhost, no command override) on lima-node-2:
kubelet journal shows continuous
  "Sandbox for pod has changed. Need to start a new one" pod=.../e2e-host-exec
roughly once per second, forever, with `crictl ps -a` showing a new container
attempt/exit every cycle. `kubectl describe pod` shows repeated
Killing -> BackOff -> Started -> Killing events.

This matches a PRE-EXISTING, already-documented issue in
scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh (which avoids using a hostNetwork *pod* for
kube-proxy for exactly this reason: "This avoids the pod sandbox loop that
occurs with hostNetwork pods in u7s (strategic-merge-patch accumulation in
podIPs causes the kubelet to continuously recreate the sandbox)"). It is not
new, and it is not specific to HostPort — it affects every hostNetwork pod,
which means every e2e test that uses a hostNetwork exec/debug pod (not just
HostPort) is at risk of the same flake.

Root-cause candidates to check (not yet root-caused precisely — needs its own
investigation session):
- crates/apiserver/src/patch.rs — strategic merge-patch handling for the
  podIPs list field (merge key semantics for hostNetwork pods, where podIPs
  should reflect the *node* IP and should not accumulate/duplicate across
  each status patch).
- crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs — pod status subresource update path
  that computes/echoes podIPs.
- crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs — protobuf<->JSON translation for
  PodStatus.podIPs (see also mayor-8swa/mayor-z1zeh, related but distinct
  hostNetwork protobuf-decode bugs already tracked).

GATE for whatever fixes this: create a hostNetwork:true pod, `kubectl exec`
into it repeatedly over 30s and confirm no kubelet "Sandbox ... changed"
churn in `journalctl -u kubelet`, then re-run sonobuoy --focus for the
HostPort test (mayor-9dv5) and confirm it passes across 2 runs.
close_reason:
PR #781 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/781

Root cause was NOT strategic-merge-patch podIPs accumulation (that path was already
correct on main — merge key "ip" registered for podIPs, $patch:delete and
$setElementOrder directives already stripped, hostNetwork podIP/podIPs override
already in place in apply_status_patch). Actual root cause: u7s's apply_pod_spec_defaults
never defaulted spec.securityContext to a non-nil object when absent. Upstream
SetDefaults_PodSpec unconditionally sets SecurityContext = &v1.PodSecurityContext{}.
Kubelet's generatePodSandboxLinuxConfig only calls NamespacesForPod (which sets the CRI
NamespaceOption for hostNetwork/hostPID/hostIPC) inside `if pod.Spec.SecurityContext !=
nil` — so a hostNetwork:true pod with no explicit securityContext got a CRI
RunPodSandboxRequest with no NamespaceOptions at all, CRI-O created an isolated network
namespace, and kubelet's own PodSandboxChanged check then saw the mismatch and
killed+recreated the sandbox on every sync, forever.

Confirmed via crictl inspectp (namespaces.options empty, real CNI IP instead of host IP)
and CRI-O's own persisted io.kubernetes.cri-o.HostNetwork="false" annotation on the
kubelet-issued sandbox — proving the real RunPodSandboxRequest never asked for host
network, not a CRI-O reporting quirk (verified CRI-O honors NODE mode correctly via a
manual crictl runp test with namespace_options nested correctly). Root-caused via
upstream kuberuntime_sandbox.go + pkg/apis/core/v1/defaults.go (release-1.36).

Fix: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs apply_pod_spec_defaults now defaults
spec.securityContext to {} when absent, matching upstream. Two new regression tests
added (security_context_defaults_to_empty_object_when_absent,
security_context_explicit_value_is_preserved) that fail on revert.

Gate evidence:
- 30s stability: created hostNetwork:true agnhost pod on lima-node-2 with fix deployed;
  crictl inspectp showed network:"NODE" (was "POD" before fix); kubectl exec succeeded
  6 times over 30+s with zero "Sandbox for pod has changed" churn in journalctl -u kubelet.
- sonobuoy --focus "HostPort validates that there is no conflict between pods with same
  hostPort but different hostIP and protocol" PASSED on 2 consecutive runs: "Will run 1
  of 7579 specs" / "SUCCESS! -- 1 Passed | 0 Failed | 0 Pending | 7578 Skipped" / "Test
  Suite Passed" (both runs, from e2e.txt not e2e.log).
- cargo test --workspace --quiet: 2165 apiserver tests + all other workspace tests pass.
- cargo clippy --workspace --tests --quiet -- -D warnings: clean.

Broader-impact hypothesis: affects every pod with hostNetwork/hostPID/hostIPC that
lacks an explicit pod-level securityContext block, not just e2e host-exec pods — worth
checking against other hostNetwork-related flakes in the backlog (not independently
verified).

title: NEW(apiserver): Job PATCH returns spurious 409 resourceVersion-conflict right after create
description:
Run 0714-1535: [sig-apps] Job "should manage the lifecycle of a job" fails (e2e.txt:5161, job.go:1194, fast fail ~16ms after create). Not present in the 0712-2356 baseline's 38 failures — genuinely new to this run, no matching bead found (searched bd for resourceversion/conflict/patch/suspend keywords).

Sequence (from e2e.txt:5164-5184):
  STEP: Creating a suspended job @ 04:53:41.074
  STEP: Patching the Job @ 04:53:41.076
  Unexpected error: failed to patch Job e2e-xg7h7 in namespace job-357:
    Job "e2e-xg7h7" cannot be updated: resource version mismatch (expected 47200, current 47201)
    (409 Conflict)

The test creates a suspended Job, then immediately PATCHes it (to un-suspend / update parallelism per upstream job.go around line 1162-1194) — normal test flow, not a retry-after-conflict scenario. A plain PATCH request should apply against the object's CURRENT resourceVersion, not fail because the RV advanced between the client's create response and the patch call (that's the exact scenario PATCH exists to handle, as opposed to PUT-with-precondition). The "expected 47200, current 47201" phrasing suggests the patch handler is comparing against a resourceVersion baked into the patch body or a cached read from the create response rather than always operating on the live object.

Given the +1 in the RV points to the job controller's own reaction (e.g. writing a Suspended condition into status) landing between create and patch, this may be a broader PATCH-correctness bug (any object with an active controller that touches it soon after create would be vulnerable to this same spurious conflict), not just Job-specific.

ACCEPTANCE: read test/e2e/apps/job.go around line 1162-1194 to confirm exactly what kind of patch is sent (merge patch vs JSON patch, and whether it includes resourceVersion in the body). Read the Job PATCH handler in u7s to find where/why it enforces an RV precondition that a generic patch shouldn't have. Fix so PATCH without an explicit resourceVersion precondition in the body always applies to the current object. GATE: sonobuoy --focus 'should manage the lifecycle of a job' passes.

Evidence: ai/findings/0714-1535-run-triage.md (failure #15).
close_reason: PR #771 (https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/771). Root cause confirmed as a SHARED handler bug (do_patch in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs), not Job-specific: the function read the stored object once, applied the patch, and wrote back using the resourceVersion from that single read, so any concurrent writer (e.g. a controller reacting to the object right after create) landing between the read and the write turned an ordinary PATCH into a spurious 409 -- even though upstream test/e2e/apps/job.go:1192 sends a plain StrategicMergePatchType body with no resourceVersion precondition at all. Fixed by wrapping the read-modify-write in a bounded (5-attempt) retry loop that re-fetches and reapplies the original patch on a live RevisionMismatch, matching real kube-apiserver PATCH semantics; a patch that itself pins a stale resourceVersion still fails after retries since reapplying it reproduces the same mismatch. Added regression test patch_resource_retries_through_concurrent_writer_conflict (4 concurrent racers against one object) -- verified it fails 5/5 with the retry removed and passes 8/8 with the fix. cargo test --workspace: 2157 apiserver tests + all other crates pass, 0 failed. cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings: clean. GATE: sonobuoy --focus 'should manage the lifecycle of a job' -> SUCCESS! -- 1 Passed | 0 Failed | 0 Pending | 7578 Skipped (podlogs/sonobuoy/sonobuoy-e2e-job-e30fa81000d44aed/logs/e2e.txt). Blast radius: fix applies to PATCH on every built-in resource (shared handler), not just Job.

title: REGRESSION(apiserver): pod resources-immutability guard rejects orphan/label-only updates again (Job/RC conformance)
description:
Run 0714-1535: 2 conformance tests that were explicitly fixed by PR #729 (mayor-j8kc, "pod-PUT immutability guard must not block metadata-only controller updates") and confirmed absent from the 0712-2356 baseline's failure list have regressed and now fail again with the IDENTICAL error:

  spec.containers[0].resources: Forbidden: pod updates may not change container resources — resize the pod via the /resize subresource instead

Affected tests:
- [sig-apps] Job "should adopt matching orphans and release non-matching pods" (e2e.txt:10308, pod_client.go:180) — fails while orphaning a pod (removing ownerReferences), not touching resources.
- [sig-apps] ReplicationController "should release no longer matching pods" (e2e.txt:11428, rc.go:702) — fails while changing a pod's matched label, not touching resources.

Root cause hypothesis (not confirmed, needs live repro): crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:4090-4097 rejects any pod update where `old_c["resources"] != new_c["resources"]` via raw JSON equality. Both tests' updates are metadata/label-only and semantically do not touch resources. A neighboring comment in the same file (lines 4131-4135, increment_pod_generation_if_spec_changed) documents that "the u7s protobuf decoder does not decode from PodSpec (skipped proto fields)... comparing them would produce phantom generation bumps" for a similar comparison — the same class of bug (client-go always uses protobuf on GET; if decode of `resources` differs syntactically from what gets stored/re-encoded even though semantically unchanged) would make this immutability guard false-positive whenever a client round-trips an unrelated field via protobuf.

Cross-ref: mayor-wx3mn (P1, in-flight this session on a DIFFERENT PodSpec protobuf-decode symptom — terminationGracePeriodSeconds field drop). This may be the SAME underlying decode bug manifesting on the `resources` field instead, or a separate issue — do not assume wx3mn's fix covers this without verifying.

ACCEPTANCE: reproduce via kubectl (PUT/PATCH a pod removing ownerReferences or changing a label, with resources present and genuinely unchanged) against a debug build; confirm whether old_c["resources"] and new_c["resources"] actually differ byte-for-byte despite being semantically identical, and if so pin down the decode/encode asymmetry. Then either fix the comparison (semantic instead of raw JSON) or fix the decode round-trip. GATE: both conformance tests above pass via sonobuoy --focus.

Evidence: ai/findings/0714-1535-run-triage.md (RESOLVED-BUT-REGRESSED section, failures #13/#17).
notes: Root cause confirmed: JSON-writing clients (KCM runs with --kube-api-content-type=application/json) store containers[].resources as {} (Go json.Marshal always emits non-pointer struct fields despite omitempty), while decode_pod_proto_gen (fixed in 010c2942) omits the resources key entirely for protobuf writes with empty ResourceRequirements. validate_pod_spec_immutable compared these raw, so a metadata-only PUT from a protobuf client (the e2e test binary, unlike KCM) against a JSON-created pod false-positives as a resources change. Fix: normalize_container_resources() in pods.rs makes the comparison semantic. Verified live via kubectl get pod -o json showing resources:{} on a JSON-created pod. Running sonobuoy --focus for the two named tests now.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #772. Root cause: validate_pod_spec_immutable in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs compared containers[*].resources by raw JSON equality. A JSON-writing client (KCM, --kube-api-content-type=application/json) stores empty resources as {} (Go json.Marshal always emits non-pointer struct fields); a protobuf-writing client's write decodes via decode_pod_proto_gen, which since #764 omits the resources key entirely when empty. {} != absent under raw equality -> false 422 on metadata-only PUT. Verified live via kubectl get pod -o json showing resources:{} on a JSON-created pod, cross-checked against the existing generated_container_omits_empty_resources decode test. Fix: normalize_container_resources() makes the comparison semantic. cargo test --workspace (2159+ apiserver tests) and cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings both clean. sonobuoy --focus on lima-node-smoke: both named tests PASS - '[It] [sig-apps] Job should adopt matching orphans and release non-matching pods [Conformance]' status=passed, '[It] [sig-apps] ReplicationController should release no longer matching pods [Conformance]' status=passed.

title: 04-start-kcm.sh restart-kill pkill pattern never matches, so KCM 'restart' silently no-ops (same process persists across runs)
description:
## Discovered by
mayor-s8s3s scout (2026-07-13), incidentally, while doing an A/B KCM content-type comparison.

## Bug
`scripts/conformance/04-start-kcm.sh` tries to kill a stale KCM before starting a new one:
```bash
limactl shell "$VM_NAME" bash -c \
  "if pgrep -f '^kube-controller-manager' >/dev/null 2>&1; then ... pkill -f '^kube-controller-manager' ...; fi"
```
The actual process is launched via an absolute cached-binary path:
```
/home/lima.guest/.cache/u7s/kcm/kube-controller-manager-1.36.2-linux-arm64 --kubeconfig=... ...
```
`pgrep -f '^kube-controller-manager'` anchors the regex to the START of the full command line, which is `/home/lima.guest/...`, NOT `kube-controller-manager` — so the pattern never matches and the "kill stale process" branch never fires. Every subsequent (non-`--reset`) `run-all.sh --focus ...` invocation's `04-start-kcm.sh` therefore:
1. Fails to detect/kill the existing KCM (silently — the `if` is just false, no warning).
2. Attempts to start a NEW instance, which immediately dies (`serving.go:411` self-signed cert generated, then `run.go:72 "command failed" err="failed to create listener: ... 127.0.0.1:10257: bind: address already in use"` — because the OLD instance still holds the healthz/metrics port).
3. The heredoc's `> "$KCM_LOG" 2>&1 &` still TRUNCATES `/tmp/kcm.log` via shell redirection even though the new process dies instantly — losing all prior log history from the still-running old instance (observed as literal NUL-byte gaps / garbled lines in captured `host-logs/kcm.log` where the old process's fd offset resumed past the truncation point).
4. The script prints `"kube-controller-manager running (PID $!, ...)"` unconditionally — a fabricated success message; the reported PID is the dead process's.

Net effect: **KCM is never actually restarted by any `run-all.sh` invocation that omits `--reset`** — the same KCM process (and its in-memory informer caches / config, e.g. a content-type flag set on an earlier run) silently persists across every subsequent "restart" in the same VM lifetime. Confirmed via `pgrep -af kube-controller-manager` showing the SAME PID across 3 consecutive `--focus` runs in one session, and via `host-logs/kcm.log` in sonobuoy run archives showing the "address already in use" failure + truncation artifact.

## Impact
- Any scout/worker relying on "run `--focus` again to pick up a changed KCM flag/version without `--reset`" is silently testing the OLD KCM, not the new one. (mayor-s8s3s worked around this by always using `--reset` before measurement, per its own dispatch instructions, so its A/B results are NOT affected — but this is a trap for future ad-hoc iteration.)
- Log evacuation for non-`--reset` focus runs is unreliable (truncation artifacts), which can hide real KCM errors from earlier in the run.

## Fix sketch
Match on the actual binary name, not an anchored full-path prefix, e.g. `pkill -f 'kube-controller-manager-[0-9.]+-linux-'` or `pgrep -f 'kube-controller-manager' | ...` (drop the `^` anchor, or match the basename). Verify the OLD process's port is actually free (or the new one binds successfully) before printing the "running" success message — currently that message is unconditional.

## Not in scope for mayor-s8s3s
Pure harness-script bug, unrelated to apiserver correctness; filing separately per mayor-s8s3s's scope (measure protobuf blast radius only, no harness changes).
close_reason: PR #763 opened — matched real KCM argv (versioned binary basename) instead of the never-matching anchored prefix; verified across 4 restarts on 2 boots that pkill+restart actually replaces the PID

title: scout: flip KCM to protobuf (--kube-api-content-type) on one VM — measure blast radius before harness change
notes:
SCOUT COMPLETE (2026-07-13, lima-node-2). Findings doc: ai/findings/protobuf-kcm-blast-radius-2026-07-13.md (worktree-local, gitignored — not pushed).

A/B result: JSON baseline (ReplicaSet PASS, Job PASS, Services/Endpoints FAIL pre-existing/unrelated to protobuf — context deadline exceeded at service.go:775, matches known watch-latency family) vs protobuf KCM. Full 3-test re-run under protobuf was not completed because within ~30s of every protobuf-KCM fresh boot, the bootstrap kube-system/coredns Deployment enters an UNBOUNDED hash-collision retry storm (collisionCount 907+, 500+ ReplicaSets, resourceVersion climbing continuously, still unresolved after 5+ min) that starves the whole controller-manager (a hand-created unrelated Deployment got 0 pods for 2+ min). Confirmed via A/B on two separate fresh --reset boots (JSON: 0 collisions, 1 RS, stable; protobuf: storm) that this is protobuf-triggered, not incidental flakiness.

Apiserver does NOT reject protobuf request bodies (no 415s; util.rs::extract_body decodes unconditionally, already unit-tested via #757). content_type.rs never re-encodes responses as protobuf (always JSON + Accept fallback, same as kubelet/kubectl). Root cause is KCM's deployment-controller collision-avoidance never observing its own recent writes via its informer before retrying — likely SAME root-cause family as mayor-sjlw1 (P1, watch wedge under heavy write load) / mayor-et5o / mayor-7lrp.1 (watch/bookmark latency), possibly a much cheaper repro path for those (10s stack boot vs needing a live sonobuoy run).

Filed: mayor-tkp2f (P1, the collision storm, related to sjlw1/et5o/7lrp.1) and mayor-ogukf (P2, incidental find: 04-start-kcm.sh's pkill pattern is anchored to the wrong string and never matches the absolute binary path, so KCM "restart" between non-reset runs is a silent no-op — did not affect this scout's results since --reset was used before each measurement).

RECOMMENDATION: (c) keep JSON in the harness. Do not flip to protobuf until mayor-tkp2f is fixed. 04-start-kcm.sh left reverted to application/json in this worktree (no harness change pushed, per dispatch MERGE GATE — this was a read-only diagnostic, no PR).

Findings: ai/findings/protobuf-kcm-blast-radius-2026-07-13.md. No harness change pushed (read-only diagnostic).

title: fix(apiserver): node/pod/service proxy handlers drop response headers (Content-Type) when forwarding to kubelet/pod
description:
All four proxy dispatch sites in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs build the outgoing
Response with only `.status(...)` and a body, never copying any headers (Content-Type in
particular) from the upstream (kubelet or pod) response:

  - node_proxy() (~line 1272-1314): GET /api/v1/nodes/{name}/proxy/{*path}
  - pod_proxy_dispatch() (~line 1515-1609), both the konnectivity-tunnel branch and the
    direct-connection branch, used by pod_proxy() and pod_proxy_root()
  - service_proxy_dispatch() (reuses pod_proxy_dispatch's forwarding pattern)

Confirmed via raw curl against a live --stack-only cluster (2026-07-13, mayor-3z4pr re-scout):

  curl --cacert ... --cert ... --key ... \
    -H "Accept: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf, application/json" \
    https://127.0.0.1:6444/api/v1/nodes/lima-node-2/proxy/pods

  -> HTTP/1.1 200 OK
     transfer-encoding: chunked
     (no content-type header at all)
     body: {"kind":"PodList","apiVersion":"v1",...}  (plain JSON, not protobuf)

Per client-go's Request.transformResponse (k8s.io/client-go/rest/request.go), when the
response Content-Type header is empty, the client falls back to its OWN configured
default content type -- which is application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf for any standard
typed clientset (kubernetes.Clientset). The client then feeds real JSON bytes to the
protobuf decoder and fails with exactly:

  "provided data does not appear to be a protobuf message, expected prefix [107 56 115 0]"

This is precisely the error seen 44x in the 0712-2356 conformance run's failure-dump
helper (sonobuoy/e2e framework's kubelet-pods-via-node-proxy dump, called from dump.go
after a test already failed) -- see mayor-3z4pr notes. It is a real, narrowly-scoped
correctness bug for ANY protobuf-preferring client hitting node/pod/service proxy
subresources, separate from (and not the root cause of) mayor-3z4pr's DaemonSet delete
hang -- normal pod/list GET already returns correct Content-Type: application/json
(verified unaffected via the same probe against /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods/<name>).

Fix: propagate at least the upstream Content-Type header (ideally all safe-to-forward
headers) from kubelet_resp / pod_resp onto the Response::builder() in all four sites.
Regression test: FixedService-style unit test asserting the proxied response's
Content-Type matches the upstream's, for at least node_proxy and pod_proxy_dispatch.
close_reason: PR #754 opened: proxy handlers now forward upstream Content-Type via shared proxied_response/forward_proxied_headers helpers; verified via live curl on lima-node-2 (before/after) and red-on-revert unit tests

title: chore(scripts): scheduler/KCM restart-collision guard breaks across worktrees with relative --workdir
description:
Discovered while investigating mayor-3z4pr. scripts/conformance/05-start-scheduler.sh (and likely 04-start-kcm.sh, reset.sh -- same pattern) scope their "already running, kill and restart" guard via `pgrep -f "u7s-scheduler.*${WORKDIR}/kubeconfig"`. WORKDIR defaults to `$PWD/temp/u7s` (absolute) but every documented worker invocation (ai/prompts/vm-operations.md) passes `--workdir ./temp/u7s` (relative). Two parallel workers in DIFFERENT worktrees, both following the documented relative-path invocation, produce IDENTICAL process command-line strings (`u7s-scheduler --kubeconfig ./temp/u7s/kubeconfig`) since the relative path carries no worktree-distinguishing prefix. pgrep -f cannot tell them apart: when worker B restarts its stack, its collision-avoidance pkill matches and kills worker A's scheduler too, silently breaking worker A's cluster (all new pods stay Pending forever, no crash/log trace).

Reproduced firsthand: lost my own u7s-scheduler (lima-node-2, port 6444) mid-investigation when the parallel mayor-m5mu7 worker (lima-node-smoke, port 6445) restarted its own stack with the same relative --workdir convention.

Fix direction (not investigated in depth): resolve WORKDIR to an absolute path before constructing the pgrep pattern (e.g. `WORKDIR="$(cd "$WORKDIR" && pwd)"` after parsing --workdir), in 05-start-scheduler.sh and any sibling script with the same pattern (04-start-kcm.sh, reset.sh).
close_reason: PR #749 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/749

title: investigate(watch): DaemonSet Failed-pod delete hang — load-gated watch-latency symptom (clean cluster passes in 3s); under et5o/7lrp.1/sjlw1 umbrella
description:
Run 0712-2356: [sig-apps] Daemon set [Serial] should retry creating failed daemon pods [Conformance] fails intermittently -- NOT a regression from #729/#733/#735 or any PR merged since the 0707-2254 baseline (investigated and cleared; see notes for full mechanism + evidence). This is a PRE-EXISTING race between the real kubelet's independent status-manager correction and kube-controller-manager's DaemonSet controller never issuing a targeted pod DELETE for the test's injected Failed status -- proven present already in the 0707-2254 "passing" baseline (same pod-level fingerprint found retroactively). Whether the test PASSES or FAILS is decided by an unrelated coin-flip: the project's own 5-minute namespace watchdog (scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh) racing the test's own 5-minute poll timeout (dsRetryTimeout, upstream ginkgo constant) to force-cleanup the stuck namespace first. Confirmed via 2 mandatory --focus gate reruns: #1 FAILED, #2 "PASSED" (but only because the watchdog won the race -- verified via matching apiserver.log/watchdog-log timestamps; kube-controller-manager never issued a DELETE for the pod in EITHER run). Real fix requires KCM's DaemonSet controller to reliably react before the kubelet's correction -- a watch/informer-notification-latency problem, related to the open mayor-et5o / mayor-7lrp.1 watch-latency work (relates_to linked; caveat in notes that the exact mechanism may not be identical, re-verify before assuming). Keeping open as known-flaky per investigation mandate rather than closing. Cross-ref mayor-n3yk (distinct, adjacent).

Evidence: ai/findings/0712-2356-run-triage.md (failure #14); full mechanism + per-run log citations in notes below.
notes:
RE-SCOUT VERDICT (2026-07-13, lima-node-2 clean --stack-only, 2 live iterations): on an UNCONTENDED cluster the full delete chain works perfectly in ~3s: PUT status=Failed → soft DELETE 200 → hard DELETE 200 → GET 404 (timestamped in apiserver.log). kcm.log shows the informer saw Failed within ~1.5ms (daemon_controller.go:887 'Found failed daemon pod...will try to kill it' + SuccessfulDelete/SuccessfulCreate). So: B (watch-delivery) RULED OUT — informer saw it; A (delete-never-completes) RULED OUT as a deterministic bug — soft→hard two-phase delete in pods.rs:638-724 worked, pod reached NotFound cleanly. A' (protobuf) is REAL but NARROW, not systemic: normal pod GET with Accept:protobuf correctly returns JSON+Content-Type (client decodes fine); only the kubelet-PROXY path /api/v1/nodes/<node>/proxy/pods returns a body with NO Content-Type header, so client-go falls back to its default (protobuf) and hits the 44x 'expected prefix [107 56 115 0]' — but that path is ONLY hit by the e2e failure-DUMP helper AFTER the test already failed, so it is NOT the cause of the DaemonSet failure. Filed mayor-bzhgk for the proxy header-drop bug. CONCLUSION: the original 0712 5-minute hang is NOT deterministic — a fresh cluster is too clean to reproduce it. It likely requires LOAD/CONTENTION (accumulated objects/watchers from a long full run) to manifest, pointing at et5o/7lrp.1 (watch latency under load). NEXT REPRO: inject load (many objects/watchers) BEFORE failing the pod, not a fresh cluster. Re-scope 3z4pr as a load-dependent watch-latency symptom under the et5o/7lrp.1 umbrella; it is NOT an independent deterministic delete/serialization bug. BONUS: lima-node-2's konnectivity tunnel was HEALTHY (node-proxy call returned 200; zero ECDSA errors in apiserver.log) — evidence that ij0es is likely lima-node-smoke-specific, not systemic (pending the ij0es scout's fresh-VM lima-node-3 scope test for confirmation).
RE-SCOUT VERDICT (2026-07-30, post-et5o/7lrp.1): DOES NOT REPRODUCE UNDER LOAD. Verified-fixed.

EVIDENCE A (archived real-world run, temp/e2e/0730-0222-conformance): [sig-apps] Daemon set [Serial] should retry creating failed daemon pods [Conformance] PASSED in junit_01.xml (line 424) at 3.292771811s -- matches the 2026-07-13 fresh-cluster ~3s baseline exactly. This run happened 113 passed-tests deep into a 1h45m/446-test suite (host-logs/apiserver.log request volume 01:51:10-19 = 1482 lines vs 472 lines in the first 5s of the run, i.e. ~3x ambient load at the time this test executed) -- genuine accumulated-object/watcher contention, not a fresh cluster. Full pod-lifecycle chain from host-logs/apiserver.log + host-logs/kcm.log for pod daemonsets-1192/daemon-set-290c0 (apiserver user_agent tags the e2e.test name directly, so this is unambiguous):
  - 01:51:15.478526Z apiserver: PUT .../status (Failed) from e2e.test, latency_ms=2
  - 01:51:15.488209 kcm.log: daemon_controller.go:887 "Found failed daemon pod...will try to kill it" (guest clock, ~7-10ms skew vs host observed via DELETE arriving at apiserver at .481173Z)
  - 01:51:16.467333Z apiserver: DELETE (kubelet, final/hard) status=200
  - 01:51:17.462231Z apiserver: e2e.test GET -> 404 (next 1s poll tick confirms full removal)
  Total PUT-Failed -> confirmed-404 = 1.98s. No hang.

EVIDENCE B (live repro, lima-node-smoke, --stack-only, this session): injected contention BEFORE triggering the mechanism -- 200 ConfigMaps + 100 Secrets created (kubectl create via xargs) in a dedicated namespace, plus 5 concurrent long-lived `kubectl get <kind> -w --request-timeout=0` watchers (configmaps, secrets, pods -A, events -A, daemonsets -A) left running throughout. Then created a DaemonSet, waited for Running, and replicated the upstream test's exact mechanism (temp/research/daemon_set.go:307-333: PUT pod.Status.Phase=Failed via status subresource) using `kubectl replace --raw .../status`. Result -- clean, fast, deterministic under load:
  - apiserver.log 03:39:51.089350Z: PUT .../status (Failed), latency_ms=7
  - apiserver.log 03:39:51.097380Z: DELETE (KCM soft-delete) status=200, latency_ms=3 -- 8ms after the PUT
  - kcm.log 03:39:51.113360: daemon_controller.go:887 "Found failed daemon pod...will try to kill it"
  - kcm.log 03:39:51.130968: replacement pod repro-ds-e1b73 "Pod added" -- 17.6ms after failure detection
  - kcm.log 03:39:51.134211: "Controller created pod" repro-ds-e1b73 (SuccessfulCreate)
  - apiserver.log 03:39:51.807767Z: DELETE (kubelet, final/hard) status=200 -- 710ms after soft-delete (normal kubelet-driven grace-period teardown, not a controller-side delay)
  Total Failed-status-write -> hard-delete = 718ms, replacement pod created within ~45ms of the PUT. No hang, no watch-delivery-latency regression, even with 300 injected objects + 5 concurrent watchers.

CONCLUSION: the load-dependent watch-delivery-latency mechanism hypothesized on 2026-07-13 is NOT present post-et5o/7lrp.1, confirmed both by an actual heavily-loaded 446-test conformance run AND an independent live repro under injected contention. The original 0712 5-minute hang is resolved. RECOMMENDATION: close as verified-fixed by mayor-et5o + mayor-7lrp.1. No follow-on needed; the DaemonSet Failed-pod test should be treated as reliably passing going forward (re-open if it flakes again in a future run, citing the run's e2e.txt timestamp so we can tell whether this is a recurrence of the same mechanism or something new).
close_reason: Verified-fixed: does not reproduce under load post-et5o/7lrp.1. Confirmed via archived 446-test conformance run (test passed in 3.29s, ~3x ambient load) and live repro on lima-node-smoke with 300 injected objects + 5 concurrent watchers (Failed-status-write to hard-delete = 718ms). See notes for full timestamped evidence.

title: Deployment controller never scales down old ReplicaSet after a full-object PUT replace
description:
Reproduced live on lima-node-smoke while investigating mayor-yv5p (deployment lifecycle test).

After: create Deployment (RS-A, 2 replicas) -> strategic-merge patch (spec change, creates RS-B) -> full-object PUT/replace via dynamic client (spec change again, creates RS-C) -- RS-B (the previous "new" RS, e.g. test-deployment-565b7c7547) is left permanently at desired=1 and never scaled to 0, even minutes after RS-C is fully available. Pods on RS-B keep running forever (a leak).

Also: deployment.status.replicas only reflects the newest RS's replica count (2), not the sum across all owned ReplicaSets (should be 3 while RS-B lingers) -- suggesting the deployment controller's list of ReplicaSets it considers "owned" by the Deployment is incomplete/stale after a PUT-driven rollout, which is likely also why cleanup/scale-down never fires for the orphaned RS.

Does NOT block '[sig-apps] Deployment should run the lifecycle of a Deployment' (mayor-yv5p) -- none of that test's watch assertions check status.replicas or RS counts, only readyReplicas/updatedReplicas/unavailableReplicas which are unaffected. But it is a real correctness bug: kubectl get deploy REPLICAS column and rollout history would show wrong counts, and it wastes cluster resources (leaked pods never get cleaned up).

Repro: manual kubectl steps mimicking the lifecycle test's create -> patch -> patch-image-fix -> full PUT/replace sequence against a live u7s-apiserver + real kube-controller-manager on lima-node-smoke; `kubectl get rs -n <ns>` shows 2 non-zero-desired ReplicaSets indefinitely after the PUT-driven rollout completes.
close_reason:
Confirmed FIXED by mayor-h0lte (PR #793, commit 541e3279) — closing as duplicate-of/fixed-by.

Hypothesis confirmed: mayor-drjdh was filed before h0lte's fix landed. h0lte's fix
(replace_namespaced_resource restores metadata.uid from the stored object whenever a PUT
body omits it) is NOT EndpointSlice-specific — it applies to any resource whose
`needs_stored_read` is true, which includes every resource with has_status_subresource=true
(Deployment is registered with has_status_subresource: true in state.rs build_registry()).
So the Deployment's own UID was corrupted (blanked) by exactly the same blind-PUT gap, for
exactly the same reason: kube_client-go's dynamic client Update() call in the upstream e2e
lifecycle test (test/e2e/apps/deployment.go:339-352, cached at
temp/research/deployment_e2e.go) builds `testDeploymentUpdate := testDeployment` from the
pre-Create() local struct — never a live Get() — so ObjectMeta.UID/ResourceVersion are
zero-value and get omitted (`omitempty`) by ToUnstructured(). Pre-fix, this blanked the
Deployment's own stored uid on the PUT. A blanked *Deployment* uid (not just EndpointSlice)
explains the full symptom: KCM's ReplicaSetControllerRefManager claims/ignores RS's by
comparing each RS's ownerRef.UID against the Deployment's own live UID
(metav1.GetControllerOf(rs).UID == deployment.UID). Once the Deployment's own UID goes
blank, every existing RS (RS-A, RS-B — both stamped with the real, non-blank UID) stops
matching and gets silently ignored (not adopted, not released — "owned by someone else" per
upstream's ControllerRefManager.ClaimObject), so the controller loses ALL visibility into
them (hence RS-B never scales down, pods leak) while any *new* RS created after the
corruption (RS-C) is stamped with the deployment's now-blank UID and self-matches, so it's
the only one ever reconciled — and status.replicas is summed only over that "owned" set,
so it only reflects RS-C's count. Root cause is identical in kind to the EndpointSlice bug
h0lte fixed, just observed through the Deployment/ReplicaSet ownership path instead of
EndpointSliceTracker.

LIVE VERIFICATION on lima-node-smoke (post-h0lte HEAD, commit b1bba42e + h0lte's 30c8e20a
ancestor), exact repro from the bead description, reproduced twice in independent
namespaces (drjdh-repro, drjdh-repro2):

1. Create Deployment test-deployment, 2 replicas, image pause:3.10 -> RS-A
   (test-deployment-5c9cb95778), rollout completes 2/2. uid=f411bafc-91c6-48ae-96dd-531344a38d5f
   captured (repro2).
2. `kubectl patch --type=strategic` (spec.replicas=1, new image pause:3.9,
   terminationGracePeriodSeconds=2) -> creates RS-B (test-deployment-8696fcf57f). RS-A
   correctly scales to 0/0/0. Deployment uid unchanged, generation 1->2.
3. Blind full-object PUT via `kubectl replace --raw=".../deployments/test-deployment" -f
   body.json`, where body.json has NO metadata.uid and NO metadata.resourceVersion (byte-
   identical in structure to what client-go's dynamic client sends for
   ToUnstructured(never-fetched local struct)) — spec.replicas=2, new image pause:3.8 ->
   should create RS-C.

RESULT (metadata.uid preservation): PUT response AND a subsequent fresh GET both show
metadata.uid == f411bafc-91c6-48ae-96dd-531344a38d5f (unchanged from step 1), even though
the PUT body omitted it entirely. generation correctly incremented 2->3. UID preservation
confirmed working correctly.

RESULT (RS-B leak — GONE): tight 1s-interval poll immediately after the PUT:
  t+1s: status.replicas=3 (RS-C 1/1/0 + RS-A 0/0/0 + RS-B 2/2/1 = 3) -- CORRECT transient
        sum across all owned ReplicaSets, refuting the bug's second complaint directly.
  t+2s: status.replicas=3 (RS-C 2/2/1 + RS-B 1/1/1)
  t+3s: status.replicas=2, RS-B already at 0/0/0, RS-C fully 2/2/2 -- converged within 3s.
Re-checked ~90s later (bug reported "even minutes after RS-C is fully available" RS-B stayed
non-zero): RS-B and RS-A both stable at 0/0/0 in BOTH repro namespaces;
generation(3)==observedGeneration(3); status.replicas=2 matching only RS-C.
`kubectl get pods`: only 2 pods exist, both owned by RS-C, both Running -- zero leaked pods.

Noise ruled out: kcm.log shows the expected, already-tracked, self-healing
"read version N is not as new as written version M" transient errors (mayor-7lrp family,
closed separately as a documented WAL-lag/watch-propagation issue) during this repro --
these retry and do not block convergence; unrelated to this bug and not reintroduced by
this verification.

No code changes required -- h0lte's fix already resolves this. No PR opened per the
dispatch's duplicate-closure instructions. Cleanup: deleted the two repro namespaces on
lima-node-smoke; no source files touched (git status clean throughout).

title: fix(cr): CRD enum validation error message doesn't match kubectl's 'Unsupported value' format
description:
[sig-api-machinery] CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI 'works for CRD with validation schema' fails on the enum-rejection sub-step (crd_publish_openapi.go:97-101), even after the OpenAPI schema-content gap (mayor-uam0) is fixed.

Repro: create a CRD whose schema has an enum field (e.g. `feeling: enum [Great, Down]`), then `kubectl create` a CR with an out-of-enum value.

Actual (from crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs, boon jsonschema validator):
  "CR schema validation failed: jsonschema validation failed with file:///.../schema.json#
   - at '/spec/bars/0/feeling': value must be one of 'Great', 'Down'"

Expected (upstream test asserts err.Error() contains):
  `Unsupported value: "NonExistentValue"`

Fix: reformat the boon/jsonschema enum-violation error in cr.rs to surface a message containing `Unsupported value: "<value>"` (matching the k8s field.ErrorList Unsupported() convention), while still being generically compatible with both client-side and server-side CRD validation per the upstream TODO comment in the test.

Discovered live during mayor-uam0 verification (sonobuoy --focus CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI, run 0708-0748): 28/29 passed, this is the sole remaining failure and is unrelated to OpenAPI schema publishing — scoped to crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs admission validation error formatting.

title: SECURITY(apiserver): merge/strategic-patch to /status can still change non-protected metadata (follow-on to #733)
description: Residual flagged by PR #733 (mayor-t4zd3 worker). #733 fixed the JSON-Patch path so /status subresource patches can't write /spec or /metadata. BUT merge_incoming_metadata — used by the merge-patch and strategic-merge-patch content types when patching /status — still allows changes to non-protected metadata fields on the /status endpoint. So a caller with only <resource>/status rights could still mutate some metadata via a MERGE patch (not JSON-Patch). For Namespace, verify whether this re-opens the PSA-label bypass via merge-patch (the JSON-Patch vector is now closed). FIX: apply the same /status path restriction to the merge/strategic-merge patch paths on status subresources — a /status patch (any content-type) must only touch /status. Extend the guard beyond JSON-Patch to cover merge_incoming_metadata on the status handlers (patch_namespace_status, patch_crd_status, and the generic status.rs patch handlers). GATE: a MERGE patch to .../status setting metadata.labels (incl pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce on a Namespace) or spec → rejected/ignored; a legit /status merge patch works. Test WHY: closing only the JSON-Patch vector leaves the merge-patch vector open — same authz-boundary/PSA-bypass class as #733, different content-type. Cross-ref #733, v2hu6/t4zd3.

title: test(apiserver): add decoder tests for apiextensions + storage_node_flow gen adapters (zero coverage)

title: perf(apiserver): admission config cache deep-clones Vec<Value> on every write — return Arc
description: Perf audit 0708 (scout ad381), NEW HIGH. The admission config cache (added by PR #666 / mayor-al9a to close the cef5 SQLite-LIST-per-request issue) reads RwLock<Option<Arc<Vec<serde_json::Value>>>> but does cached.as_ref().clone() at admission.rs:653,676,1100,2504 — this DEEP-CLONES the entire Vec<Value> (all mutating+validating webhook configs + VAP/MAP policies, including webhook CA-bundle strings) on EVERY write, unconditionally, BEFORE any rule-matching filter, at the top of run_mutating_webhooks/run_validating_webhooks. Called from nearly every write path (resource.rs, pods.rs, namespaces.rs, cr.rs, crd.rs, csr.rs, proxy.rs). NET: #666 eliminated the SQLite round-trips but replaced them with an equivalent-order in-memory deep clone — a regression baked into the fix. FIX: the cache read helpers should return Arc<Vec<Value>> (clone the Arc, O(1)) and callers iterate the shared Arc, not a deep copy. Only deep-clone if a caller must mutate (it doesn't — rule matching is read-only). GATE: a unit/bench asserting the cache read is O(1) Arc-clone not O(configs) deep-clone (e.g. the helper returns Arc and no serde_json::Value clone of the vec happens per call); confirm run_mutating/validating_webhooks no longer deep-clone. Test WHY: admission runs on every write; a per-write deep clone of all webhook configs scales cost with (#webhooks × config-size × write-rate), inflating write latency + allocation churn cluster-wide. Cross-ref #666/al9a/cef5.

description:

core_delete_collection_namespaced_resource) to the /api/v1/{resource} route.

title: fix(apiserver): PUT/replace handlers miss finalizer-drain hard-delete (PVC/VAC stuck deleting)
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout aba09, live-reproduced on lima-node-2 with request trace): [sig-storage] PersistentVolumes CSI 'lifecycle of a PV and a PVC' (PVC never deletes) AND VolumeAttributesClass 'lifecycle' (VAC never deletes) — SHARED root cause. Upstream KCM protection controllers add/REMOVE kubernetes.io/{pvc,vac}-protection finalizers via PUT. When KCM PUTs the object with finalizers now empty AND deletionTimestamp already set, the apiserver must COMPLETE the delete (hard-delete). That check exists ONLY in do_patch (resource.rs:795-822, PATCH path); replace_resource (resource.rs:350) and replace_namespaced_resource (resource.rs:1431) do a literal store.put with no finalizer-drain completion check. So KCM removes the finalizer via PUT, u7s stores the object (still present), and the delete never completes. FIX: extract the finalizer-drain hard-delete check from do_patch into a shared helper and call it from replace_resource + replace_namespaced_resource (and do_patch) — after any update, if deletionTimestamp is set and finalizers is empty, hard-delete. GATE: create a PVC/VAC with a finalizer + deletionTimestamp, PUT with finalizers=[] → object is hard-deleted (GET 404); the CSI/VAC lifecycle tests confirm deletion. Test WHY: finalizer removal via PUT (KCM's mechanism) must complete the delete; without it every finalizer-protected object (PVC, VAC, and any protection-finalizer resource) stays stuck Terminating forever.
close_reason: PR #725 opened — shared finalizer-drain hard-delete helper wired into replace_resource/replace_namespaced_resource; VAC lifecycle conformance test now PASSES, PVC lifecycle progresses past the finalizer-drain hang (blocked by unrelated mayor-yssp DeleteCollection 405 bug, filed separately)

title: fix(apiserver): unify core/v1 and events.k8s.io/v1 Event storage keyspace
