title: fix(apiserver): PodSpec proto decode missing hostNetwork/hostAliases/dnsConfig/ephemeralContainers/automountServiceAccountToken + enableServiceLinks mis-tagged (26→30)
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout af9a8, mayor-verified proto.rs:856-902): the PodSpec proto struct is missing multiple fields, so they are silently dropped on protobuf Pod decode (default wire format for typed/e2e clients). Missing: hostNetwork (tag 11), hostAliases (tag 23), dnsConfig (tag 26), ephemeralContainers (tag 34), automountServiceAccountToken (tag 21). CRITICAL MIS-TAG: proto.rs:895 binds enable_service_links to tag 26 — but tag 26 is dnsConfig upstream; enableServiceLinks is tag 30. So enable_service_links currently mis-decodes dnsConfig bytes. FIXING dnsConfig REQUIRES fixing the enableServiceLinks tag simultaneously (they collide on 26). FIXES conformance: [sig-network] DNS 'configurable pod DNS nameservers' (dnsConfig); [sig-node] Ephemeral Containers 'should update ephemeral containers' (ephemeralContainers — merge logic pods.rs:2239 is correct but never sees the field); [sig-node] Kubelet hostAliases '/etc/hosts entries' (hostAliases); [sig-node] KubeletManagedEtcHosts (hostNetwork — dropped per existing comment proto.rs:2336-2342); [sig-auth] ServiceAccounts 'opting out of API token automount' (automountServiceAccountToken pod-level override of SA default — NOT fixed by #713). FIX: add all 5 fields to PodSpec with correct tags + move enable_service_links to tag 30 + add tag 26 dnsConfig, then emit each in gen_pod_spec_to_json. GATE: unit test decoding a protobuf Pod with each field set → served JSON carries it; enableServiceLinks and dnsConfig both round-trip (no tag collision). Test WHY: these pod fields are silently dropped for all protobuf clients; the tag-26 collision actively corrupts dnsConfig<->enableServiceLinks. Cross-ref memory content-type-determines-decode-path, adapter-objectmeta-per-package-no-delegation. CLUSTER with cfp7 (pod securityContext tag 14) + hdwo (container securityContext tag 15) — all proto.rs PodSpec/Container struct completions → ONE proto.rs+adapter PR.

title: fix(apiserver): CSR spec.request is base64(PEM) but decoded as DER (ASN.1 tag 0x2d)
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout a0ae5): [sig-auth] Certificates API 'should support CSR API operations' — 'spec.request does not contain a valid DER-encoded PKCS#10: unknown/unsupported ASN.1 DER tag: 0x2d'. 0x2d = '-' = the '-----BEGIN' PEM armor. title: fix(apiserver): pods/eviction subresource ignores PodDisruptionBudget and never sets DisruptionTarget condition
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout aaf96, live-verified: eviction of a pod with disruptionsAllowed:0 returned HTTP 201 instead of 429): [sig-apps] DisruptionController 'should block an eviction until the PDB is updated to allow it' ('Expected an error, got nil') AND [sig-apps] Job 'pod failure policy to ignore failure matching on DisruptionTarget condition' — SAME root cause. evict_pod (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:827-873) has ZERO PDB awareness and never sets pod conditions. (b) when an eviction/preemption/disruption proceeds, set the pod's DisruptionTarget condition (status.conditions) so pod-failure-policy consumers (Job controller) can match it. Test WHY: PDBs are the primary safety mechanism against voluntary disruption; ignoring them lets evictions violate availability guarantees, and a missing DisruptionTarget condition breaks Job pod-failure-policy matching. Touches PDB status too (disruptionsAllowed must be computed) — check that PDB status is populated by KCM's disruption controller and readable.

title: fix(apiserver): TokenReview response missing authentication.kubernetes.io/pod-name extra info for bound SA tokens
description:
Live-verified on run 0707-0613 (worker mayor-owhv/mayor-s9u0 session): after the ServiceAccount admission fixes (default serviceAccountName + auto-mount token volume), the token/ca.crt/namespace files ARE correctly present in every pod (verified via kubectl exec: /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/{token,ca.crt,namespace} all populated, kube-api-access-* volume+mount injected). Two conformance tests still fail for a DIFFERENT, deeper reason:

1. [sig-auth] ServiceAccounts 'should mount an API token into pods' fails at k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/auth/service_accounts.go:151 with: 'expected single authentication.kubernetes.io/pod-name extra info item matching <pod>, got []'. This test calls TokenReview on the pod's bound SA token and expects the response's status.user.extra to include authentication.kubernetes.io/{pod-name,pod-uid,service-account-uid} — u7s's token authenticator/TokenReview handler does not populate these extra fields for bound (projected) service-account tokens.

May share root cause with (1) since sample-apiserver's own SA token must also validate/authenticate correctly, or may be an unrelated startup issue (TLS cert secret, flags). Needs a from-scratch repro (kubectl run + inspect pod logs directly, not via sonobuoy) to pin down.

NOT caused by missing SA-name-default or missing token-volume injection — both proven correct via direct kubectl exec verification before this bead was filed. This is a separate authentication-layer gap.
notes: RE-CHECK AFTER the proto.rs securityContext decode cluster (mayor-cfp7/hdwo) lands. pl0h has two parts: (a) TokenReview response missing authentication.kubernetes.io/pod-name extra for bound SA tokens; (b) sample-apiserver crash-loops before reaching u7s. Part (b) may be DOWNSTREAM of the securityContext protobuf-decode P1 bug (extension apiserver pods may have been mis-configured/failing due to dropped securityContext or SA-token mount). Re-verify (b) on a fresh stack once the proto cluster merges — it may already be resolved. Part (a) is a distinct TokenReview extra-info gap regardless. title: feat(apiserver): ServiceAccount admission auto-mount of default token volume into pods
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout ae178, live-reproduced x2): [sig-api-machinery] Aggregator sample-apiserver deployment ReadyReplicas:0 (crash-loops 'failed to get delegated authentication kubeconfig: ... no such file or directory'), and bare pods have no /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount. ROOT CAUSE: no ServiceAccount admission plugin — u7s never auto-injects the default kube-api-access-* projected token volume + volumeMount into every container (upstream ServiceAccount admission controller does this). FIX: implement ServiceAccount admission on pod create: inject a projected volume (serviceAccountToken + configmap ca.crt + downwardAPI namespace) named kube-api-access-XXXXX and mount it at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount in each container (unless automountServiceAccountToken=false). This is the LARGER of the SA beads — likely a new admission module. GATE: create a pod → it gets the kube-api-access volume + mount in every container; with automountServiceAccountToken=false it does NOT. Test WHY: in-cluster clients (incl extension apiservers, the sample-apiserver) read the token/ca from that path; without auto-mount they cannot authenticate and crash-loop → extension-apiserver/webhook deployments never become Ready. UNBLOCKS the Aggregator test and likely reduces contention on webhook-deployment tests. Depends on serviceAccountName defaulting (mayor-<B1>). Cross-ref [sig-auth] ServiceAccounts opting-out-of-automount + mount-API-token tests (may share this).

title: fix(apiserver): emit optional field for ConfigMap/Secret volume and projected sources
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout ae178, live-reproduced): 4 failures — [sig-storage] ConfigMap optional updates reflected in volume, Projected configMap optional updates, Projected secret optional updates, Secrets optional updates — all pods never become running+ready (300s) because the kubelet gets FailedMount 'not found' for an OPTIONAL configmap/secret that should be tolerated. ROOT CAUSE: crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs gen_pod_spec_to_json (lines ~638-659, ~683-708) and gen_projected_volume_source_to_json (~135-166) — the 'optional' bool (proto field 4) on ConfigMap/Secret volume sources and projections is decoded by the generated prost struct but NEVER emitted into JSON. So the kubelet sees a required mount, blocks pod start on a missing optional source. Confirmed via the archived run's captured Pod object (no 'optional' key) + matching kubelet FailedMount event. FIX: emit 'optional': <bool> in those blocks (only when set, matching k8s omitempty semantics — verify how other optional bools are emitted in the same file). GATE: unit test — decode a pod with a ConfigMap volume source optional=true → JSON carries optional:true; same for secret + projected. Test WHY: an optional configmap/secret volume must not block pod startup when the source is absent; dropping 'optional' makes every optional mount behave as required. Cross-ref memory adapter-objectmeta-per-package-no-delegation.

title: fix(apiserver): MicroTime decode drops pre-1970 acquireTime/renewTime on Lease
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout aee89): [sig-node] Lease 'lease API should be available' fails — AcquireTime/RenewTime come back nil (should be set). ROOT CAUSE: gen_microtime_fields_to_rfc3339 (crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs:9-14) does 'if secs <= 0 { return None }', silently dropping the field. The conformance test deliberately uses pre-1970 timestamps (time.Time{}.Add(2s)) which are negative/near-zero as Unix seconds. FIX: secs_to_rfc3339 (and the MicroTime helper) must accept i64/negative values and emit the correct pre-1970 RFC3339 — do NOT just remove the guard (must handle negative seconds correctly). GATE: decode a MicroTime with negative Unix seconds -> correct pre-1970 RFC3339 string, not None. Test WHY: Lease acquire/renew times can legitimately be any instant; dropping non-positive times makes leader-election/heartbeat leases look never-acquired. This helper is shared, so the fix also unblocks the Job/CronJob condition-time beads. Cross-ref memory adapter-objectmeta-per-package-no-delegation.

title: fix(apiserver): replace_resource/replace_namespaced_resource omit kind/apiVersion on PUT response
description: Conformance (run 0707-0454, scout aee89, mayor-verified): [sig-apps] Deployment 'should run the lifecycle of a Deployment' fails 'failed to update the DeploymentStatus: Object Kind is missing'. MISGROUPED as a /status bug — it is actually a general PUT-response bug on the MAIN resource (test uses a dynamic/unstructured client Update). ROOT CAUSE: replace_resource (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs:350) and replace_namespaced_resource (:1429) NEVER call inject_type_meta before responding, unlike GET (225,1145), POST (299,1273), and PATCH (342,867,900,1312) in the same file. Mayor-verified via grep: those two fn bodies are absent from the inject_type_meta call sites. A PUT with kind/apiVersion omitted echoes the omission back -> unstructured-client decode fails (runtime.NewMissingKindErr). FIX: add inject_type_meta(&mut obj.body, &group, &version, &meta.kind) before the final response in BOTH replace_resource and replace_namespaced_resource, mirroring the existing PATCH-path calls. GATE: an existing test idiom exists (resource.rs:5798, 9776, 9851 assert inject_type_meta presence on GET/PATCH) — add the equivalent for PUT: a PUT whose body omits kind/apiVersion must return an object with non-empty Kind; removing the new inject_type_meta call must fail the test. Test WHY: unstructured/dynamic clients require TypeMeta on Update responses to decode; without it every dynamic-client PUT breaks. HIGH VALUE — affects all PUT, not just Deployment.

title: fix(apiserver): add dedicated CRD status subresource route (apiextensions .../customresourcedefinitions/{name}/status)
description: Conformance (1 failure, run 0707-0454, scout aa225): [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourceDefinition getting/updating/patching CRD status sub-resource works — fails with 'getting CustomResourceDefinition status: Resource "apiextensions.k8s.io/v1/customresourcedefinitions" not found'. ROOT CAUSE: no dedicated route for /apis/apiextensions.k8s.io/v1/customresourcedefinitions/{name}/status. main.rs:632-642 registers CRD list/get/put/patch/delete but NOT status; the status request falls to the generic catch-all (main.rs:725-730 -> cr.rs:1984 get_cr_status -> cr.rs:209 find_crd), which searches for a CRD-of-CRDs that can never exist -> 'not found'. title: fix(apiserver): register trailing-slash discovery routes for /api/, /apis/, /apis/{group}/
description: Conformance (2 failures, run 0707-0454, scout aa225): [sig-api-machinery] Discovery should validate PreferredVersion for each APIGroup ('Failed to find /apis/: server could not find the requested resource') and [sig-cli] Kubectl proxy --port 0 ('Expected at least one supported apiversion, got'). ROOT CAUSE: /apis/ discovery IS populated (servergroups.json shows 29 groups incl apiextensions.k8s.io) — the bug is trailing-slash routing. Upstream e2e clients call AbsPath('/apis/'), '/apis/{group}/', '/api/' with a LITERAL trailing slash, but main.rs:383,392,393 register only /api, /apis, /apis/{group} (no-slash). auth.rs:425-438 is_exempt also matches only exact no-slash strings. No path-normalize layer exists. FIX: register trailing-slash route siblings for /api/, /apis/, /apis/{group}/ AND extend the auth is_exempt match to accept the trailing-slash variants. ACCEPTANCE: GET /apis/ and /api/ return the discovery doc (not 404); both conformance tests pass. Test WHY: a client that appends a trailing slash to a discovery path must get the same doc, else kubectl/discovery clients break.

title: apiserver: no validation of securityContext.sysctls[].name format at pod admission (should reject invalid sysctls test)
description: VERIFIED live (h24j scout a18244, 2026-07-07). Conformance 'should reject invalid sysctls' expects the APISERVER to reject malformed sysctl NAMES at pod create (422, message with Invalid value: 'foo-' and Invalid value: 'bar..' — syntactic name validation, independent of allow/deny-listing). u7s ACCEPTS the pod (created, exit 0) and persists the malformed names; the pod is later killed by the KUBELET with 'SysctlForbidden: forbidden sysctl foo- not allowlisted' — WRONG layer + WRONG message (that's the allowlist check for valid-but-unsafe sysctls, a different mechanism). u7s has NO apiserver-side sysctl-name-format validation. FIX: add structural validation of securityContext.sysctls[].name on the pod create/update admission path (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs, near other securityContext validation — scout couldn't locate an existing sysctl validator; may need a new fn). Validate the k8s sysctl name format (segments matching the sysctl naming rules); reject malformed at 422. GATE: create a pod with sysctls [{name:'foo-'},{name:'kernel.shmmax',value:'100000000'},{name:'safe-and-unsafe',value:'100000000'},{name:'bar..',value:'42'}] → REJECTED at create with 422 containing Invalid value: 'foo-' and 'bar..', and must NOT reject/mention kernel.shmmax or safe-and-unsafe (syntactically valid). Split from EPIC h24j.

title: apiserver: pod resize validation conflates 'key absent from patch' with 'key removed' → false-positive QoS/removal rejections (2 InPlaceResize conformance tests)
description: VERIFIED with 2 live repros (h24j scout a18244, 2026-07-07). Both failing InPlaceResize conformance tests ('3 containers various operations', '6 containers various operations') build their resize PATCH via strategicpatch.CreateTwoWayMergePatch, which OMITS unchanged resource keys (a cpu-only change produces a patch section with no memory key — meaning 'memory unchanged', NOT 'remove memory'). u7s misinterprets absent-key as removal. ROOT CAUSE (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs): (1) merge_resize_for_qos (~2055) REPLACES stored_container['resources'][section] WHOLESALE with incoming[section] instead of merging key-by-key → a cpu-only patch drops the existing memory key before QoS is recomputed → false 'QOS class may not change' rejection. (2) validate_resize_patch Rule 3 (~2000) reads incoming['limits'/'requests'][resource] via serde index → Value::Null for BOTH absent (unchanged→preserve) AND explicit null (real removal) → can't distinguish → false 'resource requests cannot be removed'. REPRO A: Guaranteed 3-container pod, PATCH only c1 cpu (memory omitted) → 'QOS Class may not change ... Guaranteed→Burstable' (should be accepted). REPRO B: Burstable pod (requests only), PATCH only requests.memory (cpu omitted) → 'resources.requests.cpu: resource requests cannot be removed' (should be accepted). FIX: merge_resize_for_qos merge per-key (not replace section); Rule 3 use .get() to distinguish None(absent→preserve stored) from Some(Null)(explicit removal); KEEP wholly-absent/null section = 'remove all in section' (the existing passing 'remove cpu&memory limits' test needs that — don't regress). GATE (2 unit tests, reject→accept): (a) Guaranteed 3-ctr, patch touching only c1 cpu → Ok; (b) Burstable requests-only, patch only requests.memory → Ok. HIGHEST-VALUE h24j fix: deterministic, one root cause, both failing tests. Split from EPIC h24j.

title: pods/exec CONNECT webhook denial likely masked the same way as pods/attach (mayor-u6eb)
description:
Same class of bug as mayor-u6eb (fixed via PR #705), NOT yet fixed here.

/exec has the identical get(pod_exec).post(pod_exec) routing (crates/apiserver/src/main.rs), where pod_exec's last extractor is also axum's WebSocketUpgrade. kubectl exec uses the same k8s.io/client-go/tools/remotecommand fallback executor as attach: it dials WebSocket (GET) first, and treats any non-101 handshake response (including a correct admission-webhook 403 denial) as an upgrade failure, silently retrying via POST (SPDY) — discarding the original GET attempt's error/message. Since pod_exec's POST leg hits the same WebSocketUpgrade extractor, it 405s with axum's generic 'Request method must be `GET`' before resolve_exec_target/admission ever runs on the retry — masking a webhook's denial exactly like pods/attach did before mayor-u6eb.

Not verified live — flagged during mayor-u6eb's investigation as the same pattern by inspection, not confirmed with a real kubectl exec + deny-webhook repro. portforward may or may not share this (kubectl port-forward historically defaults to SPDY-first rather than WebSocket-first; needs its own check before assuming the same fix applies).

Suggested fix: mirror mayor-u6eb's approach — a pod_exec_post handler that calls resolve_exec_target (running admission) and returns its Result, falling back to 501 if all checks pass.
close_reason: Merged PR #707 (51c4c1a7). Found more than expected (Rule 8): resolve_exec_target had ZERO admission integration — pods/exec webhooks were never invoked on EITHER GET or POST. Fix: (1) added run_validating_webhooks to resolve_exec_target (resource=pods/exec, operation=CONNECT, mirroring attach); (2) added pod_exec_post (no WS extractor) reusing resolve_exec_target, propagating Status, 501 if all pass; (3) /exec route get(pod_exec).post(pod_exec_post). Live-verified: exec denial now surfaces the webhook message on both GET+POST legs (403 each); webhook received both CONNECT requests. 2 fail-on-revert tests. Completes the attach/exec webhook-denial pair (u6eb #705 = attach).

Fix has two parts: (1) resolve_exec_target had NO admission check at all (unlike resolve_attach_target) -- added run_validating_webhooks for resource pods/exec op CONNECT; (2) added pod_exec_post handler (no WebSocketUpgrade extractor) reusing resolve_exec_target, POST route repointed. title: admission webhooks skipped on deletecollection (delete_collection_resource / delete_collection_namespaced_resource)
description: Follow-up to mayor-w354: single-object DELETE handlers (delete_resource, delete_namespaced_resource, delete_pod, delete_cr(_namespaced), delete_crd, delete_namespace) now run the validating admission webhook chain before deleting. delete_collection_resource and delete_collection_namespaced_resource (DELETE on the collection endpoint, e.g. 'kubectl delete cm --all') were intentionally left out of that fix to keep the change scoped: they loop over every matching object in a single request and none of them extract the caller's UserInfo today. Upstream kube-apiserver's DeleteCollection calls admission per object being deleted. FIX: thread Extension<UserInfo> into both handlers and call run_validating_webhooks per object (with operation=DELETE) inside the deletion loop in resource.rs, matching the per-object semantics of the single-delete handlers; skip/continue objects a Fail-policy webhook denies rather than aborting the whole collection (match upstream: partial failure, not all-or-nothing) — needs a design decision on the aggregate response shape when some objects are denied.
acceptance_criteria: kubectl delete <resource> --all against a namespace/cluster with a Fail-policy validating webhook denies the matching objects (and only those); cargo test -p u7s-apiserver passes; cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings clean.
notes: PR #704 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/704 — awaiting review/merge. Deny semantics deviated from the bead's proposed skip/continue design: used fail-fast (propagate first denial, abort request) to match the existing non-NotFound-store-error handling already in this loop; see PR body for rationale. Live-verified on lima-node-smoke:6444 via raw DELETE to the collection endpoint (kubectl's own --all resolves client-side to per-object deletes, so it doesn't exercise this path).
close_reason: Merged PR #704 (028769fc). Per-object validating admission (operation=DELETE) added to delete_collection_resource + delete_collection_namespaced_resource, mirroring #700's single-delete pattern; UserInfo threaded through core.rs collection handler + 2 router test fixups. Fail-fast deny semantics (task instruction over bead's skip/continue — flagged Rule 7). 2 fail-on-revert tests. Live-verified via raw collection DELETE endpoint (both namespaced+cluster-scoped): Fail-policy VWC -> 500, objects survive; removed -> 200, deleted. Completes the deletecollection half of webhook DELETE admission (w354 did single delete).

title: admission webhook matchConditions not evaluated at invocation (CEL only checked syntactically at registration)
description: VERIFIED live (scout aa9f7278, 2026-07-06): a webhook with matchCondition 'object.metadata.name != "skip-me"' mutated BOTH skip-me AND a normal configmap identically — matchConditions are never evaluated at invocation. WebhookEntry (admission.rs L108-126) has NO match_conditions field. They ARE validated syntactically at config write time (validate_webhook_match_conditions_cel L2047) but ignored at runtime. title: PodTemplate missing from /api/v1 discovery resource list — kubectl get/apply podtemplates fails with 'server doesn't have a resource type'
description:
Found while live-verifying mayor-tw11 (fieldValidation=Strict top-level field fix).

crates/apiserver/src/types.rs V1_RESOURCES (the static list backing GET /api/v1,
served by handlers/discovery.rs::api_v1_resources) has no entry for "podtemplates",
even though:
  - state.rs::build_registry registers ("", "v1", "podtemplates") — the resource IS
    served (POST /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/podtemplates returns 201).
  - main.rs wires generic core routes for it via the {resource} catch-all.

Live repro against a freshly built worktree stack (port 6445):
  $ kubectl get podtemplates -n default
  error: the server doesn't have a resource type "podtemplates"
  $ kubectl get endpoints -n default   # contrast: endpoints IS in V1_RESOURCES
  No resources found in default namespace.

Because kubectl resolves Kind -> resource name via discovery (RESTMapper) before
issuing any request, this means `kubectl apply -f <podtemplate.yaml>` and
`kubectl get podtemplates` never reach the apiserver's create/list handlers at
all — they fail locally in kubectl with "no matches for kind". A direct REST
POST (bypassing kubectl's discovery) works fine and correctly enforces
fieldValidation=Strict (see mayor-tw11).

Fix: add a "podtemplates" ApiResource entry to V1_RESOURCES in types.rs
(name, singular_name: "podtemplate", namespaced: true, kind: "PodTemplate",
verbs: CORE_VERBS, short_names: None) — mirroring the existing entries for
endpoints/events immediately above/below it alphabetically. Add a regression
test following the existing discovery.rs table-driven pattern
(names.contains(&"podtemplates")) so this can't silently regress again.
notes: MAYOR-VERIFIED LIVE (2026-07-06, HEAD 638da558): GET /api/v1 discovery does NOT list 'podtemplates' (confirmed: configmaps/endpoints/events/secrets/etc ARE listed, podtemplates is NOT). So kubectl get/apply/describe podtemplates fails client-side ('the server doesn't have a resource type') before reaching the apiserver — even though a direct curl POST to /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/podtemplates works (201). FIX: add the podtemplates entry to V1_RESOURCES in crates/apiserver/src/types.rs (name=podtemplates, singularName=podtemplate, namespaced=true, kind=PodTemplate, verbs=[create,delete,deletecollection,get,list,patch,update,watch]). Match the existing entries' shape. Trivial. GATE: kubectl get podtemplates -> no discovery error (empty list ok). Pairs with tw11 (#697) which fixes the fieldValidation side; both needed for PodTemplate to be fully usable via kubectl. Likely contributes to a fast-fail conformance failure that touches podtemplates (e.g. the chunking test creates podtemplates). Small, clean, dispatch-ready.
close_reason: Merged PR #698 (42924220). Added podtemplates entry to V1_RESOURCES (types.rs); regression test podtemplates_advertised_in_v1_discovery fail-on-revert; live gate kubectl get/apply/describe podtemplates all work (no 'server doesn't have a resource type'). Pairs with tw11 (#697) fieldValidation fix — PodTemplate now fully usable via kubectl.

title: fieldValidation=Strict falsely rejects non-spec top-level fields on PodTemplate, core/events.k8s.io Event, and CSIStorageCapacity
description:
Follow-up from the known_top_level_fields audit done for mayor-i5x4 (ValidatingWebhookConfiguration/MutatingWebhookConfiguration fix). Same root cause, different resource types: known_top_level_fields (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/json_patch.rs) falls back to the default ["apiVersion","kind","metadata","spec","status"] set for any (group, plural) without an explicit arm. Several REGISTERED (state.rs build_registry) and SERVED types have top-level fields that are neither "spec" nor "status", so fieldValidation=Strict (kubectl's default) falsely 422s "unknown field" for every real field on these types. Verified against the vendored upstream proto (crates/apiserver/proto-include/k8s.io/api/.../generated.proto):

- core/v1 PodTemplate ("", "podtemplates"): real top-level field is `template` (PodTemplateSpec), not `spec`.
- core/v1 Endpoints ("", "endpoints") — NOT EndpointSlice, already fixed separately: real top-level field is `subsets`.
- core/v1 Event ("", "events"): top-level fields are involvedObject, reason, message, source, firstTimestamp, lastTimestamp, count, type, eventTime, series, action, related, reportingComponent, reportingInstance (verify full list against k8s.io/api/core/v1/generated.proto — old-style Event schema, NOT spec/status shaped at all).
- events.k8s.io/v1 Event ("events.k8s.io", "events"): different schema from core Event — eventTime, series, reportingController, reportingInstance, action, reason, regarding, related, note, type, deprecatedSource, deprecatedFirstTimestamp, deprecatedLastTimestamp, deprecatedCount (see crates/apiserver/proto-include/k8s.io/api/events/v1/generated.proto).
- storage.k8s.io/v1 CSIStorageCapacity ("storage.k8s.io", "csistoragecapacities"): top-level fields are nodeTopology, storageClassName, capacity, maximumVolumeSize (see crates/apiserver/proto-include/k8s.io/api/storage/v1/generated.proto:387+).

Confirmed all five (group, plural) pairs are present in state.rs::build_registry and therefore reachable via the generic create_resource handler (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs), which calls apply_field_validation unconditionally per POST — so they are live, reachable 422 false-positives under fieldValidation=Strict, not speculative.

NOT included in mayor-i5x4's fix: that PR is scoped narrowly to the admissionregistration.k8s.io webhook config types per its title/deliverable. This bead tracks the additional gaps found during that bead's required audit step, deliberately kept out of that PR's diff to keep it surgical.

Fix: add match arms to known_top_level_fields for each (group, plural) pair above, verified field-for-field against the vendored proto (do not guess). Add regression tests following the existing endpointslice_top_level_fields_are_not_unknown / webhook_configuration_webhooks_field_is_not_unknown pattern in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/json_patch.rs.

GATE: for each type, curl POST with ?fieldValidation=Strict&dryRun=All using a body containing only its real top-level fields -> assert 2xx (not 422).
notes: MAYOR-VERIFIED LIVE (2026-07-06, HEAD 24027ca6): all reproduce as 422 under fieldValidation=Strict&dryRun=All — PodTemplate(template)->422, Endpoints(subsets)->422, CSIStorageCapacity->422. Same bug class as i5x4 (#696): known_top_level_fields (json_patch.rs:82) lacks arms for these non-spec-shaped types, so they fall to the default {apiVersion,kind,metadata,spec,status} and their real top-level fields get flagged unknown -> breaks kubectl apply under default validation. This likely causes several fast-fail conformance failures: [sig-instrumentation] Events API operations, [sig-node]/[sig-api-machinery] tests that create Events/PodTemplates/Endpoints. FIX (surgical, mirror #696): add known_top_level_fields arms for: ('','podtemplates')=[apiVersion,kind,metadata,template]; ('','endpoints')=[apiVersion,kind,metadata,subsets]; ('','events')=core/v1 Event fields; ('events.k8s.io','events')=events.k8s.io/v1 Event fields (DIFFERENT schema — eventTime,reportingController,reportingInstance,action,reason,regarding,related,note,type,deprecatedX...); ('storage.k8s.io','csistoragecapacities')=[apiVersion,kind,metadata,nodeTopology,storageClassName,capacity,maximumVolumeSize]. VERIFY each field set against the vendored proto (crates/apiserver/proto-include/...) like #696 did. GATE per type: curl POST with ?fieldValidation=Strict -> 2xx not 422. Regression test per type (fail-on-revert). Dispatch-ready — this is the next fast-fail fix after #696 merges.
close_reason: Merged PR #697 (c13983aa). Added known_top_level_fields arms for PodTemplate(template)/Endpoints(subsets)/core-v1 Event/events.k8s.io Event/CSIStorageCapacity — all proto-verified; 6 regression tests fail-on-revert; live gate all 5 types create 201 under fieldValidation=Strict. Side finding: podtemplates missing from /api/v1 discovery → mayor-vtb4 (P2, verified, dispatch-ready).

title: apiserver does not resolve priorityClassName → spec.priority on pod create (blocks scheduler preemption)
description: VERIFIED live (mayor + rsei worker, 2026-07-06): creating a Pod with only spec.priorityClassName set leaves spec.priority NULL/absent after create (priorityClassName is preserved, but not resolved). Setting spec.priority explicitly survives (osuq's wire-decode works). No admission logic resolves priorityClassName -> PriorityClass.value -> spec.priority anywhere (admission.rs, handlers/defaults.rs, handlers/pods.rs all checked, zero hits). GAP: on pod create (and the PriorityClass admission plugin's job upstream), if spec.priorityClassName is set and spec.priority is absent, look up the PriorityClass object by name and copy .value into spec.priority (also handle globalDefault PriorityClass when no className given; and the two built-in system-cluster-critical/system-node-critical classes). BLOCKS preemption: the scheduler's new preemption logic (PR #695, mayor-rsei) keys off spec.priority which is always 0 without this. This is the HIGHEST-LEVERAGE next step to make '[sig-scheduling] SchedulerPreemption validates basic preemption works' reachable. GATE: kubectl create a PriorityClass (value N) + a pod with priorityClassName=it, GET pod -> assert spec.priority == N. Likely small (a create-path defaulting step). Discovered building rsei.
notes: PR #699 REVIEWED + APPROVED (mayor, pending green CI). Resolution in async create_pod handler (store GET of scheduling.k8s.io/priorityclasses) delegating to pure resolve_pod_priority_class(pod, stored_class) — correct semantics: early-return on no/empty className + on explicit priority (preserves osuq's wire value); system-cluster-critical(2000000000)/system-node-critical(2000001000) matched by name BEFORE store (work without seeded objects, verified live); not-found -> Err -> 403 Forbidden (matches upstream + the file's RuntimeClass convention); preemptionPolicy copied only if pod didn't set one. globalDefault deferred (MVP, not needed by preemption tests). Single file +480 (11 tests: 8 pure + 3 integration), clippy clean. Live gate: PriorityClass(12345)+pod -> priority=12345; nonexistent className -> 403; system-cluster-critical -> 2000000000 unseeded. WILL MERGE on green. UNBLOCKS mayor-rsei — after this, the shipped preemption (#695) can see real priorities; SchedulerPreemption basic test becomes reachable (still needs kg2s extended-resource accounting for the specific tests). Survived a port collision (mayor dispatched it + kc54 scout on same :6445 — 2u9x's final gate still ran clean).
close_reason: Merged PR #699 (19ed8bc4). resolve_pod_priority_class in create_pod handler: priorityClassName→spec.priority via store GET, system-cluster/node-critical hardcoded, 403 on not-found, explicit priority preserved; 11 tests, live-verified. UNBLOCKS rsei.

title: proto decode drops Namespace status (decode_namespace_proto_gen ignored ns.status → phase+conditions lost for protobuf clients)
description: VERIFIED (worker a897, PR #694): crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs decode_namespace_proto_gen never read ns.status — any protobuf-encoded Namespace write silently loses status.phase AND status.conditions. Classic proto-decode-drop class (cf dispatch-proto-decode-drop-check). Fix mirrors the existing Service status.conditions decode pattern in the same file + a prost encode->decode round-trip test (namespace_status_put_preserves_phase...). This fix is GOOD and should land — it rode into PR #694 (ftkl) but is UNRELATED to the ftkl panic (that stack uses JSON, not protobuf, for ns writes, so this drop never fired there). Carve it out of #694 (or keep it in #694 but relabel — mayor decides). Gate: prost-encode a Namespace with status.phase=Active + a condition, decode via decode_namespace_proto_gen, assert both survive. Discovered while reviewing ftkl; the worker was right to fix it but flag the disconnect.
notes: CORRECTION (2026-07-07, ftkl PANIC-1 worker a5bd2f2f): my earlier note calling this 'unrelated to the ftkl panic' was WRONG. decode_namespace_proto_gen decoding ns.status (this fix, #694/a1902a96) IS the fix for ftkl PANIC-1. WHY I got it wrong: the e2e client sends UpdateStatus as application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf (e2e framework defaults typed clients to protobuf; 06-run-sonobuoy.sh doesn't override), so the namespace-status PUT goes through the PROTO decoder — which dropped status until this fix. My probe used JSON (+ the mayor's :6443 was cert-drifted anyway), so I saw JSON-path working and wrongly concluded proto-decode was unrelated. The two-client distinction (KCM uses --kube-api-content-type=application/json; e2e uses protobuf) is the crux. So oww6 (#694) and ftkl PANIC-1 are the SAME fix. LESSON: content-type determines the decode path; test the path the FAILING CLIENT uses (protobuf), not the convenient one (JSON).
close_reason: Merged in PR #694 (c92d9d6a). decode_namespace_proto_gen now decodes ns.status (phase+conditions), mirroring the Service pattern; round-trip regression test proven fail-on-revert. Proto-decode-drop class fix.

title: wrap long conformance runs in caffeinate to prevent host-sleep wall-clock inflation
description:
Unattended overnight full-conformance runs on macOS accumulate ~8h of dead wall-clock because the host sleeps (~15min DarkWake cycles freeze apiserver+scheduler+Lima-kubelet together). VERIFIED root cause of the '12h vs ginkgo-4h' discrepancy on runs 0705-1409 + 0706-1152 (see bead d13f, closed). Ginkgo's exec clock is correct (~4-5h); the excess is pure host-sleep.

FIX: prevent sleep for the duration of a run. Options: (a) document + require operators run 'caffeinate -dimsu scripts/conformance/run-all.sh ...' for full runs; (b) have run-all.sh self-wrap in caffeinate when it detects a full (non---focus, non---stack-only) run — spawn 'caffeinate -w $$' as a child so it dies with the script; (c) macOS Energy Saver 'prevent automatic sleeping'. Prefer (b) — automatic, no operator memory required — but keep it macOS-guarded (Linux CI doesn't need it). ACCEPTANCE: a full overnight run's apiserver.log shows NO synchronized multi-minute gaps across apiserver/scheduler/kubelet-lease; wall-clock ~= ginkgo 'Ran in'. Low effort, high value (unblocks trustworthy overnight baselining). Note: keeping the host awake for ~5h is fine; this is local Mac dev only.
close_reason: Full caffeinated conformance run completed 2026-07-07 at temp/e2e/0707-0454-conformance: consistent ~4h wall-clock (14327s), no host-sleep inflation. 92 failures / 2 errors / 7135 skipped / 7586 total. This run is the new true baseline replacing the corrupted overnight runs.

title: Server-Side Apply not supported — apply-patch+yaml content-type returns 400 (blocks ApplyStatus + kubectl apply --server-side, multiple conformance failures)
description:
VERIFIED live (apiserver :6443, HEAD 1fb9c258, 2026-07-06): u7s does NOT support Server-Side Apply. A PATCH with Content-Type 'application/apply-patch+yaml' returns 400 'invalid patch JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1' on BOTH a status subresource (namespaces/X/status) AND a plain resource (default/configmaps/Y) — u7s is parsing the YAML apply body as JSON and failing. So the apply-patch content-type isn't handled at all.

IMPACT: SSA is used pervasively — every e2e ApplyStatus() call, kubectl apply --server-side, and many conformance tests that build objects via Apply configurations. Surfaced via the ftkl panic cluster (Namespaces 'apply changes to a namespace status' panics because ApplyStatus 400s then the client indexes an empty slice), but the blast radius is far wider. Likely one of the highest-leverage single correctness levers.

REPRO / GATE (fast, kubectl+curl, no VM): 
curl -sk --cert <c> --key <k> -X PATCH -H 'Content-Type: application/apply-patch+yaml' --data-binary '<yaml manifest>' '<server>/api/v1/namespaces/default/configmaps/ssa-test?fieldManager=test'
BUG = 400 'invalid patch JSON'. FIXED = 200/201 with the object, and a second apply with a different fieldManager merges/conflicts per SSA semantics.

SCOPE NOTE (pre-alpha): full SSA (managedFields tracking, field ownership, conflict detection, apply-patch+json too) is large. A scout should size it: minimum viable = parse apply-patch+yaml/json, treat apply as upsert (create-or-merge), populate managedFields enough that ApplyStatus round-trips and clients don't panic. Determine whether a reduced SSA satisfies the conformance tests or whether field-ownership/conflict is required. Flag as an EPIC candidate. ARCHITECTURE/API-SURFACE — flag for operator before large build. Root-caused under mayor-ftkl.
notes:
SIZING COMPLETE (scout a54a, 2026-07-06) + MAYOR-VERIFIED. REFRAME: this is a SMALL MVP parser bug, NOT a high-leverage conformance lever, NOT P1 (downgraded to P2). KEY FINDINGS:
1. ROOT CAUSE is precise: ~8 built-in PATCH handlers detect Content-Type application/apply-patch+yaml but parse the body with serde_json::from_slice / Object::from_bytes (JSON-only) -> real multi-line YAML 400s with 'invalid patch JSON'. A YAML-tolerant parser (cr.rs:469 ssa_body_to_json, using yaml_rust2 already a dep) EXISTS and WORKS but is wired into only 2 call sites (CR-create path, fixed by mayor-4xgf/PR#672). title: apiserver returns malformed/missing responses → 5 conformance tests PANIC (namespace status conditions, strict fieldValidation, GC, statefulset)
description:
Run 0706-1152: 5 [PANICKED!] conformance specs. The panic is in the Go e2e CLIENT (runtime/panic.go) — the apiserver did NOT crash (run completed) — but each is a real apiserver correctness bug: the apiserver returns a structurally-wrong or missing response that the client immediately nil-derefs / indexes out of range. Fast panics (0.03-2s) confirm it's a bad RESPONSE, not a hang. All are kubectl-reproducible (good before/after gates). Source pinned release-1.36.

PANIC 1 (CLEAN REPRO) — Namespaces 'should apply changes to a namespace status', namespace.go:365, 'index out of range [-1]'. Test does PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/{name}/status then reads patchedStatus.Status.Conditions[len-1]. u7s returns 0 conditions -> len-1 = -1 -> panic. REPRO: kubectl patch ns <n> --subresource=status --type=merge -p '{"status":{"conditions":[{...}]}}' and GET; assert .status.conditions is present & non-empty. ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: u7s namespace /status subresource doesn't persist/return status.conditions.

PANIC 2 (CLEAN REPRO) — FieldValidation 'should detect unknown and duplicate fields of a typed object', field_validation.go:104, nil deref on err.Error(). Test does POST /apis/apps/v1/namespaces/{ns}/deployments?fieldValidation=Strict with a body containing unknown+duplicate fields, expects a 400 'strict decoding error: unknown field'. u7s returns err==nil (ACCEPTS the invalid body) -> test calls nil.Error() -> panic. REPRO: POST a deployment with a bogus top-level field + ?fieldValidation=Strict; assert HTTP 400 + 'strict decoding error'. ROOT CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: u7s does not implement fieldValidation=Strict (unknown/duplicate field rejection).

PANIC 3 — Namespaces 'should ensure that all pods are removed when a namespace is deleted', namespace.go:247, nil deref. Pod Create response deref'd for Spec fields. Investigate whether Create returns an incomplete Pod.

PANIC 4 — Garbage collector 'should not delete dependents that have both valid owner and owner waiting for dependents', garbage_collector.go:722 (120s then panic). Likely ownerReferences/GC finalizer response shape.

PANIC 5 — StatefulSet 'Burst scaling should run to completion even with unhealthy pods', statefulset.go:836 (70s then panic). Likely related to qrip (statefulset rollout) — may dedupe.

ACCEPTANCE: a scout reproduces PANIC 1 + PANIC 2 via kubectl (highest-confidence, cleanest), confirms the missing behavior (ns status.conditions; strict fieldValidation), and files/rescopes fix beads. PANIC 3/4/5 need the test source read (namespace.go:247, garbage_collector.go:722, statefulset.go:836) to confirm the exact response gap. Split into fix beads by root cause. These are P1 because a malformed apiserver response that panics a well-behaved client is a correctness red flag beyond the specific test.

title: investigate: workload pods never reach awaited status → deployment/job/var-expansion tests hang (~1h wall-clock combined)
description:
Cluster of test-hangs in run 0705-2315 sharing one signature: object exists (GET 200) but never reaches the status the e2e framework polls for, so the test hangs until watchdog reap. Verified from apiserver.log:
- deployment-8597 (331s): polls GET pods/webserver-deployment-… + GET replicasets/… — Deployment rollout never reaches Available (pods PATCHed but rollout not satisfied).
- job-9079 (671s): 1031 PATCH …/pods/fail-once-local-*/status — the Job backoff/'fail once then succeed' test; pods churn status but Job completion never observed.
- var-expansion-7371 (974s): polls GET pods/var-expansion-… every 2s — pod phase transition (env-var substitution / subpath expansion) never completes.
SHARED HYPOTHESIS: a pod-readiness/phase or workload-controller-status gap (KCM writes status but the awaited condition — Available/Complete/Succeeded/Ready — never flips). MAY be one root cause or 3; a scout must split before fix dispatch. Possibly overlaps the pod-lifecycle EPIC h24j (but h24j is scoped to security-context/sysctl/ephemeral/hooks, NOT rollout/job-completion). RELATED to the probe-defaulting class (ct2s) — pods created but never Ready. ACCEPTANCE (scout): kubectl-repro each (Deployment→wait Available; Job fail-once→wait Complete; var-expansion pod→wait Running/Succeeded), identify the missing status transition per case, then file/rescope fix beads. Wall-clock cost ~1h combined (d13f). No existing bead; cross-ref h24j.
notes:
Run 0707-2254 (92→48): the webhook/extension-apiserver deployment set STILL FAILS — AdmissionWebhook deny-attach + mutate-CR (2), Aggregator sample-apiserver, CRD-conversion-webhook (2), CustomResourceFieldSelectors. All depend on an extension-apiserver/webhook Deployment reaching Available. #713 (SA token mount + kube-root-ca) did NOT clear them → the 'workload deployment never Available' driver is still live, OR these need something beyond SA-token. Deployment.status.availableReplicas reconcile? single-node schedulability?). Cross-ref n3yk.

1. Deployment Available (testProportionalScalingDeployment's literal "webserver-deployment" name, the only test using it): create 2-replica Deployment -> Available in ~1s; patch template (rolling update) -> re-Available in ~5s; scaled to 20 replicas + 2nd rolling update under load -> still Available within ~10-20s. kcm.log DOES still show the 7lrp-family "read version N is not as new as written version M" RS-controller errors under the 20-replica burst (confirmed still-live, same signature as mayor-7lrp), but per 7lrp's own prior finding this now only costs single-digit seconds of requeue, not a hang — convergence still completes. NOT reproduced as a hang. Verdict: stale / already fixed (likely ct2s probe-defaulting #692 + the 7lrp/sjlw1 watch-staleness mitigations landed since the 0705-2315 run). Residual WAL-staleness log noise remains tracked under mayor-et5o (P3, open) — did not re-fix here, out of scope.

Re-testing it here would duplicate fnym9's active work.

2. Job Complete (batch/job.go's literal "fail-once-local" name, the only test using it): parallelism=2/completions=4/backoffLimit=6, RestartPolicy=OnFailure, busybox touches /data/foo on an emptyDir then fails, succeeds on in-place restart. All 4 pods restart once and reach Succeeded; Job status.conditions[Complete]=True, succeeded=4, in ~18s total. NOT reproduced. Verdict: stale / already fixed.

3. var-expansion phase (common/node/expansion.go's newPod() "should allow substituting values in a volume subpath" — the case matching this bead's own "env-var substitution / subpath expansion" framing): single busybox pod, RestartPolicy Never, SubPathExpr "$(POD_NAME)" on an emptyDir mounted twice (with + without subpath) -> phase reaches Succeeded (exit 0, subpath dir correctly created/resolved) in ~2s. NOT reproduced. Verdict: stale / already fixed.

GET .../endpointslices?labelSelector=kubernetes.io/service-name=iso-web (filtered) vs GET .../endpointslices (unfiltered) returned byte-identical JSON: same uid 00aa71ad-d64d-4b7e-8c6c-2417475f3af1, same generation, same 3 endpoint addresses, same ready=true. Repro 2 (ns e06u-repro2, timed-web Deployment replicas=4, multi-write scenario matching h0lte's exact trigger): filtered and unfiltered queries again byte-identical (uid 8341c3ad-c3d2-40ab-92b4-d0e5ee5b9f43, generation=5, 4/4 ready) within ~5s of pods going Ready. Sanity check: labelSelector=kubernetes.io/service-name=nonexistent-svc correctly returned 0 items, proving the filter actively discriminates (not a no-op). kcm.log: zero occurrences of "informer cache is out of date" across the session despite 3 log lines confirming KCM processed e06u-repro. Source review of crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs's apply_label_selector/parse_label_selector confirms this is fully generic code shared by every namespaced resource LIST path (no EndpointSlice-specific branching), structurally ruling out an EndpointSlice-only filter bug. title: API list chunking/pagination (?limit + ?continue) — sig-api-machinery chunking tests hang (~31m wall-clock, 2 ns)
description: Two chunking namespaces (chunking-8870 1873s… actually 929s, chunking-4661 944s) hung ~31m combined in run 0705-2315, watchdog-reaped. Verified from apiserver.log: the test creates many podtemplates (POST …/podtemplates ×N) then polls GET …/podtemplates?limit=40 — it was still on the FIRST page (limit=40) and never advanced, indicating the ?continue pagination token isn't honored (either not emitted in the list response's metadata.continue, or a follow-up ?limit=&continue=<token> isn't served correctly). sig-api-machinery '[Chunking] should return chunks of results for list calls' / 'should support continue listing…'. ACCEPTANCE: LIST with ?limit=N returns metadata.continue when more items exist; a follow-up LIST with that continue token returns the next page; the chunking --focus passes. Root-cause with a kubectl-driven repro (create 50 podtemplates, GET ?limit=10, follow continue) before fixing. Wall-clock cost ranked in d13f. No existing bead.
notes: (2026-07-06, adding to prior note) basic ?limit+continue works. The chunking conformance failures may ALSO be partly host-sleep (the '[Slow]' inconsistent-continue test polls). Re-probe the full multi-page + compacted-away continue flow with adequate waits before dispatch. Likely lower-value than first thought.
close_reason: PR #775 opened (https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/775). Root cause: pagination itself (limit/continue/HMAC tokens/remainingItemCount) was already correctly implemented; the bug was that every page reported the store's LIVE global resourceVersion instead of one pinned to the pagination pass, so it drifted upward whenever unrelated resources were written between page fetches -- failing chunking.go's assertion that all pages of one listing share the same resourceVersion. Fix: continue tokens now embed the resourceVersion pinned at page 1 (generic.rs encode_continue/decode_continue), and resource.rs/core.rs/csr.rs list handlers report that pinned rv on every page instead of resp.revision; a fresh rv is only minted on token expiry (matching the inconsistent-list-restart test). New regression test list_namespaced_resource_paginates_all_items_once_with_stable_resource_version (resource.rs) creates 25 objects, pages with interleaved concurrent writes, and asserts all items returned once in order with one shared resourceVersion -- verified it fails on revert. Gate: sonobuoy --focus 'Servers.*API chunking|should return chunks of results for list calls|should support continue listing' -> 'Ran 2 of 7579 Specs in 98.586 seconds; SUCCESS! -- 2 Passed | 0 Failed | 0 Pending | 7577 Skipped'. cargo test --workspace (2159 tests) and cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings both clean.

title: fix(proxy): Service proxy must parse <name>:<port> suffix (named-port proxy syntax)
description:
DETERMINISTIC apiserver bug (NOT environmental/reachability — proven). Follow-on from cyrd.1 (Service proxy route, #686), found by re-running the proxy conformance test tighter (run 0705-2024).

## Symptom
'[sig-network] Proxy version v1 should proxy through a service and a pod' FAILS. The test requests `/api/v1/namespaces/proxy-1014/services/proxy-service-84b98:portname1/proxy/` and gets **404 in ~1-3ms**: `Service "proxy-service-84b98:portname1" not found`.

## Why it's NOT reachability/setup (operator's worry, ruled out)
The 404 returns in ~1ms — nothing was dialed. It's an immediate name-lookup rejection, not a connection timeout / context-deadline / unreachable-pod. The apiserver never tried to reach a pod IP.

## Root cause (mayor-verified)
`resolve_service_proxy_target` (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs:1435-1447) does `object_key("services", ns, svc_name)` with the RAW svc_name including the `:portname1` suffix → Service lookup 404s because the stored Service is named `proxy-service-84b98`, not `proxy-service-84b98:portname1`. k8s proxy URL syntax allows `services/<name>:<port-or-portName>/proxy/` to target a specific service port; cyrd.1 didn't parse the suffix.

## Fix (mirror the EXISTING node-proxy pattern)
proxy.rs ALREADY has `strip_node_port` (line 1000-1009, `rsplit_once(':')`) for exactly this on node proxy. Service names are DNS-1123 (no colons) so the same rsplit is safe. Steps:
1. In resolve_service_proxy_target: split svc_name into (bare_name, Option<port_or_portName>) via rsplit_once(':'); look up the Service by bare_name.
2. USE the parsed port: resolve it to the target endpoint port. The suffix may be a numeric port OR a named port — map a named port through the Service's spec.ports[].name → targetPort, and match the EndpointSlice port by name. (The failing test uses ':portname1' — a NAMED port.)
3. If no suffix, keep current behavior (first ready endpoint + its port).
Add regression tests: services/<name>:<numericPort>/proxy and services/<name>:<portName>/proxy both resolve; bare services/<name>/proxy still works.

## Verify
--focus 'Proxy version v1 should proxy through a service and a pod' → PASS (was 404-loop → 122s timeout). VM.

## Pattern note
Same class as cyrd.6 (label-selector) — an incompletely-parsed k8s URL form failing fast. Cross-ref cyrd.1 (#686), cyrd (epic).
close_reason: PR #688 opened — Service proxy named-port parsing fixed; bare name used for store lookup, port spec resolved via EndpointSlice ports[].name; 2103 tests pass; kubectl repro shows 404→502 (forward attempted, not parse error); conformance run ongoing

title: fix(store): per-prefix bookmark RV — retarget to EnsureReady() RS/DS/SS false-positive retries (not ES tracker)
description:
Scout findings clarify that the per-prefix bookmark fix (cyrd.3) was described as fixing 'EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date' but that error comes from endpointSliceTracker.Has() (object cache generation check), NOT from ConsistencyStore.EnsureReady() which uses LastStoreSyncResourceVersion/bookmarks.

The per-prefix bookmark fix IS valuable, but for a different failure: when a cross-resource global bookmark (e.g. from a Pod write) advances a StatefulSet informer's LastStoreSyncResourceVersion past the most recent StatefulSet write RV, EnsureReady() passes prematurely. This was observed as: 'read version: 391 is not as new as written version: 392 for group resource statefulsets.apps' in kcm.log.

This bead should be closed or retargeted. The per-prefix bookmark work should target:
1. Prevent cross-prefix global bookmarks from advancing LastStoreSyncResourceVersion past the per-prefix write RV
2. Test: StatefulSet write at rv=N; StatefulSet informer bookmark arrives at rv>=N without a Pod write at rv=N driving it

The EndpointSlice tracker convergence issue should be addressed by mayor-cyrd.4 (ring/broadcast capacity) instead.

title: fix(watch): Watch stream 'Watch failed: context canceled' disconnections cause test failures
description: Conformance run 0705-1409 shows 'Watch failed: context canceled' errors firing every 1 second for 5+ minutes during multiple test specs (RS Replace/Patch, DS complex daemon, Kubelet readonly). This is the PRIMARY driver of test failures in the apps/node test areas (distinct from the WAL-lag retry churn). Example: RS Replace/Patch test has retrywatcher errors every 1s for 3+ minutes before the test times out. Needs investigation: why do watch streams disconnect on context cancellation? Is this konnectivity-server dropping connections? Or apiserver HTTP server timeout? The 0703-1822 baseline may not show this - compare.
notes: Very likely RESOLVED by cyrd.6 (set-based label-selector watch delivery). The 'Watch failed: context canceled' cascade is the CLIENT giving up after the awaited event never arrives — and the reason it never arrives is the set-based-selector parse gap (cyrd.6), not a server-side watch-cancel. Verify-close after cyrd.6 lands + a --focus re-run.

The e2e retrywatcher context is canceled after the wait condition resolves; no watch stream ever reaches the apiserver (confirmed: zero watch=true requests for namespaced endpointslices). title: fix(apiserver): investigate namespace termination latency (~8h conformance gap driver)
description: The ~8h wall-clock regression in conformance run 0705-1409 is caused by namespace termination latency (10 large inter-spec gaps totaling 9.13h), NOT the WAL-read-lag controller retry churn. d13f and the 7lrp scout both confirm this. The EndpointSlice->Sysctls gap alone is 163 minutes. Root cause appears to be slow namespace GC/finalizer processing in u7s apiserver. This is a distinct bug from the WAL-lag retry churn (7lrp). Needs separate investigation: profile namespace deletion in apiserver, check finalizer processing loops, GC cascade for EndpointSlice/Service/Pod, and why the 0703-1822 baseline run did NOT show this (~4.76h total elapsed).
notes:
REFRAMED (2026-07-06, from live run 0705-2315 terminal watchdog log + apiserver.log). The title 'namespace termination latency' is MISLEADING — namespace TERMINATION is NOT slow. Proof: the watchdog's own force-delete DELETE completes in seconds (DELETE 200 -> DELETE 404 within ~1-9s for every reaped ns; e.g. cronjob-2149 14:35:17.44 DELETE 200 -> next-second gone). The ~4.5h 'gap' is NOT teardown cost.

REAL MECHANISM: conformance tests HANG mid-execution polling a condition u7s never satisfies, so the test never reaches its AfterEach cleanup DELETE. There is NO test-issued namespace DELETE in apiserver.log for ANY stuck ns before the watchdog's — the tests go silent while polling. The watchdog (06-run-sonobuoy.sh) reaps each at a 5-min-Active / 10-min-Terminating threshold. So each hang costs [test-specific poll time] + [up to 5 min watchdog threshold], serialized against suite progress.

Examples (apiserver.log, verified): cronjob-2149 polled GET cronjobs/suspended every 2s returning 200 until reaped (= 0rc4); statefulset-6615 polled pods?labelSelector=baz= waiting for pods that never appear (= qrip). Each stuck ns maps to a DISTINCT correctness bug, NOT a shared teardown bug.

CONSEQUENCE: the wall-clock regression and the correctness FAILURES ARE THE SAME LIST. Fixing the per-area correctness bugs (gjy0 proxy, 0rc4 cronjob, qrip statefulset, kxht webhook, uam0 crd-openapi, rsei preempt + NEW: chunking/services/var-expansion) buys back the wall-clock directly. This bead (7lrp.2) is therefore largely a DUPLICATE lens on d13f + those beads — recommend CLOSE as superseded by d13f's per-area breakdown, keeping only any residual genuine ns-termination-latency finding (none observed). Wall-clock cost ranking by area is in d13f.
close_reason: Superseded by d13f's per-area breakdown: the 'termination latency' framing was wrong (teardown itself is fast, seconds). Real mechanism is per-area tests hanging mid-poll on conditions u7s never satisfies, then reaped by the watchdog threshold — same list as the correctness bugs already tracked individually (gjy0/0rc4/qrip/kxht/uam0/rsei/25ap). No residual latency finding beyond those. Closing to stop double-tracking.

title: Per-prefix bookmark RV to fix informer cache consistency (endpointslice hot-loop factor B)
description: Global bookmark events advance endpointslice informer RV past last write on that prefix, causing KCM consistency check to fail. Track last-write rv per key prefix in push_event. Emit heartbeat bookmark at max(prefix_last_rv, current_revision()). Test: EndpointSlice write at rv=N; watcher BOOKMARK arrives at rv=N within 60s; no premature cross-prefix bookmark.
notes: SHARPENED DIAGNOSIS (mayor, 2026-07-05) — the '600s timeout' mechanism + a correction to the buffer-eviction theory. The massive durations are NOT slow relists: they are conformance tests' own 'wait for watch notification / wait for condition' loops hitting their HARD ceiling (300s/600s) because an awaited event NEVER ARRIVES. Concrete proof (ConfigMap watch test, watch-8063, all @19:22:23 UTC in host-logs/apiserver.log): label-selector watch opened (GET .../configmaps?labelSelector=watch-this-configmap in (multiple-watchers-A)&watch=true → 200), ConfigMap created (POST → 201) with matching label watch-this-configmap=multiple-watchers-A, but the ADDED event never delivered → test '[FAILED] Timed out waiting for expected watch notification: {ADDED ...configmap-a...}' (e2e.txt:573), namespace idle until 19:39 (~16min later). KEY CORRECTION to the scout's 'buffer eviction under burst' theory: this ConfigMap test is a SINGLE create on a QUIET namespace — NO burst — yet the event still didn't arrive. So buffer capacity (cyrd.4) is NOT the whole story. There appears to be a LABEL-SELECTOR WATCH DELIVERY bug: matching events aren't delivered to label-filtered watch streams on the LIVE path (filtering may only be applied to the initial snapshot — cf core.rs:528 comment + super::watch::object_matches_label_selector). A fix-scout must check: does the live watch-broadcast path apply label-selector matching and deliver matching events? This likely underlies BOTH the ConfigMap watch failures AND EndpointSlice non-convergence (KCM's endpointslice informer uses watches too). Buffer bump (cyrd.4) may help under-load cases but will NOT fix the quiet-namespace label-watch drop. RE-SCOPE cyrd.3 around live label-selector watch delivery.
close_reason: Scout complete: cyrd.3 was misdirected. 'EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date' comes from endpointSliceTracker.Has() (object cache generation check), NOT ConsistencyStore.EnsureReady() (which uses LastStoreSyncResourceVersion). Per-prefix bookmark fix does not address this error. Follow-on: mayor-cyrd.4 (ring/broadcast capacity increase) is the correct fix for ES tracker lag; mayor-cyrd.5 retargets the per-prefix bookmark work to RS/DS/SS EnsureReady() false positives. title: Reduce SQLite WAL read lag (endpointslice hot-loop factor A)
description: EndpointSlice hot-loop is exacerbated by SQLite WAL read lag: after writing rv=N on write connection, read connection sees rv=N-1. Tune wal_autocheckpoint from 100 pages to ~10. Add PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) after write batch in sqlite.rs. Test: write-then-read verifies revision is visible without lag.
notes: MAYOR CORRECTION (2026-07-05): the cyrd scout attributed the EndpointSlice hot-loop to WAL read lag ('is not as new as written') — but log counts show these are DISTINCT loops: 'EndpointSlice for Service X not found' occurs only 44-46× and ALL for ONE service (endpointslice-6289, the single EndpointSlice conformance test) — localized, not run-wide. The 'is not as new as written' WAL-lag signature occurs 204× across replicasets(121)/statefulsets(72)/daemonsets(11) — ZERO for endpointslices. So cyrd.2's WAL-lag work is really about the 7lrp class (workload-controller consistency), NOT the endpointslice loop. RE-SCOPE: cyrd.2 should likely be MERGED INTO / reopened as 7lrp (WAL read lag), not kept as a cyrd child. The endpointslice-6289 loop is a separate localized issue (part of the EndpointSlice sync failure, cyrd's actual scope). Recommend: move cyrd.2 under the 7lrp umbrella; keep cyrd.1 (proxy route) + cyrd.3 (bookmark RV) as cyrd.
close_reason: AUDIT 2026-07-14 (ai/findings/cyrd-service-discovery-audit-2026-07-14.md): already reparented under mayor-7lrp (closed) per its own prior notes; superseded by 7lrp's conclusion that the root cause is watch-event TCP-propagation lag, not WAL read-connection lag — cyrd.2's proposed fix (wal_autocheckpoint tuning + PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE)) targets a mechanism 7lrp's own deeper investigation moved away from. The actual recommended fix (TCP_NODELAY) is tracked at mayor-7lrp.1 (open, P3, possibly already landed via #759/tkp2f pending remeasurement). This audit re-confirmed the 'read version N not as new as written N+1' symptom still reproduces live (transient/self-healing, replicasets.apps) but attributes it to the 7lrp/7lrp.1 mechanism, not WAL tuning. No further cyrd.2-specific work needed.

title: investigate: CronJob 'suspended' disappears after create (GET 200→404) — sig-apps 'should not schedule jobs when suspended' fails
description:
Surfaced by the 0705 conformance diff (mayor-d13f), but MIS-ATTRIBUTED there to protobuf codegen — it is NOT a proto deser bug. Needs a scout to confirm root cause + whether it's pre-existing (NOT proven EPIC-caused; the test was not in the 0703 baseline run set).

## Symptom
[sig-apps] CronJob 'should not schedule jobs when suspended [Slow] [Conformance]' FAILS with: 'Unexpected final error while getting *v1.CronJob: CronJob "suspended" not found'.

## Evidence (preserved host log)
temp/e2e/0705-1409-conformance/host-logs/apiserver.log:
- POST/create of cronjob-3176/cronjobs/suspended succeeds; subsequent GET /apis/batch/v1/namespaces/cronjob-3176/cronjobs/suspended returns 200 at 16:08:48, 16:24:18, 16:24:20 ... then 404 at 2026-07-05T16:24:22.646741Z. The object VANISHED between 16:24:20 and 16:24:22.
So the CronJob was created and readable, then disappeared ~15min later while the test still expected it. Candidate causes: (a) an over-eager GC/orphan sweep deleting the suspended CronJob; (b) a TTL/finalizer bug; (c) namespace/ownership cascade. NOT the proto decode path (create+GET returned valid 200s before the 404).

## NOT the k8s\0 protobuf error
The '[107 56 115 0]' error in the same test's output is a SEPARATE pu5i artifact (dump.go diagnostic hitting the kubelet-proxy) — see mayor-pu5i. Do not conflate.

## Scope for a scout (--stack-only, when a VM is free)
Reproduce: create a suspended CronJob, watch whether it persists or gets deleted (kubectl get -w + apiserver log + kcm.log). Determine what deletes it. Confirm whether baseline (pre-EPIC) had the same behavior (was this test even run/passing before?). Then decide severity + whether it's EPIC-related (unlikely) or a pre-existing CronJob lifecycle bug.

## Cross-ref
mayor-d13f (conformance diff), mayor-pu5i (the proto-prefix red herring).
notes: RE-ROOT-CAUSED LIVE (mayor, 2026-07-06) — NON-BUG on current main (c92d9d6a). Created a suspended CronJob (schedule '* * * * *'), waited 70s past a tick: 0 jobs spawned, suspend honored correctly. The 239s hang of '[sig-apps] CronJob should not schedule jobs when suspended [Slow]' in the ballooned run was a HOST-SLEEP artifact (the test polls for ~1min to confirm no jobs appear; a Power Nap gap during that poll inflated it to 239s and may have tripped a timeout). RECOMMEND: close/park until a CAFFEINATED full run confirms — this likely PASSES clean without host-sleep. Not worth a fix dispatch. Cross-ref tier2-conformance-beads-stale-symptom-framed, conformance-wallclock-ginkgo-vs-realtime.

It raced [sig-apps] CronJob 'should not schedule jobs when suspended' (5min gomega.Consistently). Live-confirmed pre-fix (watchdog fired on a same-age namespace at 468s; real test missed the same tick by ~10-15s and passed by luck) and post-fix (test ran its full 300s window cleanly, no watchdog interference). Fixed in PR https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/798 (thresholds raised 5m/10m -> 20m/30m, regression test added to test-watchdog-logic.sh).

title: apiserver: Export and unify MicroTime timestamp helper across adapters
description:
MicroTime fields are handled correctly in coord_gen_adapter, net_disc_cert_policy_events_gen_adapter, and core_gen_adapter (Event.series), but there's no exported helper.

Each adapter that needs microsecond-precision timestamp formatting imports crate::util::secs_nanos_to_rfc3339_micro directly. Risk: if util function changes, all adapters must be reviewed.

Fix: Create a gen_microtime_to_rfc3339 helper in core_gen_adapter (or shared module) and export it. Have all adapters delegate.

Low priority but indicative of per-adapter reimplementation pattern.

See ai/findings/protobuf-typegen-adapter-quality-audit-2026-07-05.md finding #5.

title: apiserver: Standardize PodTemplateSpec empty-object handling across adapters
description:
core_gen_adapter.rs:905-914 emits { metadata: <json>, spec: <json> } unconditionally, even if both are empty objects.

batch_gen_adapter.rs:245-255 wraps the result with conditional logic that produces { template: {} } if empty.

This inconsistency means a Pod and a Job with the same template can have different JSON representations.

Fix: Decide on behavior (emit always or omit if empty) and standardize across core and batch. If omitting: update gen_pod_template_spec_to_json to return Option, then unwrap_or emit empty.

See ai/findings/protobuf-typegen-adapter-quality-audit-2026-07-05.md finding #4.
close_reason: Non-issue on inspection: core gen_pod_template_spec_to_json and batch gen_job_spec_to_json both emit {} for empty PodTemplateSpec. The conditional wrapper in batch is logically equivalent — both paths produce {}. No code change needed.

title: apiserver: Add test coverage for all adapter decoders + field-omission assertions
description:
Test coverage gaps: only core_gen_adapter (3 tests) and batch_gen_adapter (3 tests) have tests. 7 adapters untested: coord, rbac, admissionreg, apiextensions, net_disc_cert_policy_events, storage_node_flow, apps.

Existing tests are construction-based (verify data survives roundtrip) but not correctness-based (verify JSON is null-free and omits zero/empty fields).

Example: if condition type is None, tests don't catch that JSON emits "type": null instead of omitting the field.

Fix: 
1. Add roundtrip tests for each untested adapter
2. Add explicit field-omission assertions (verify optional fields produce null JSON value, not omitted from dict or serialized as empty)
3. Test with all-defaults proto to verify only required fields are emitted

See ai/findings/protobuf-typegen-adapter-quality-audit-2026-07-05.md finding #3.

title: apiserver: Fix condition type/status null-safety in apps and batch adapters
description:
apps_gen_adapter.rs:145-146 and batch_gen_adapter.rs:163-164 directly serialize condition type/status fields without null-checking:
  
  apps_gen_adapter line 145-146:
    "type": c.r#type,
    "status": c.status,

  This serializes Option<String> directly. If Some(None), produces JSON null, violating K8s spec (conditions require non-null type).

  core_gen_adapter correctly uses unwrap_or_default() to convert None to empty string.

  Fix: Change both adapters to use unwrap_or_default(). Add test verifying condition with None type produces type: "", not type: null.

  See ai/findings/protobuf-typegen-adapter-quality-audit-2026-07-05.md finding #2.
close_reason: PR #684: Fixed unwrap_or_default() on condition type/status in apps macro and batch inline code. Two regression tests added that fail on revert.

title: apiserver: Consolidate gen_object_meta_to_json — delegate from 5 adapters to core_gen_adapter
description:
rbac_gen_adapter (line 10), admissionreg_gen_adapter (line 6), apiextensions_gen_adapter (line 6), net_disc_cert_policy_events_gen_adapter (line 10), storage_node_flow_gen_adapter (line 9) all reimplement gen_object_meta_to_json locally. Drift risk: any bugfix to core_gen_adapter::gen_object_meta_to_json won't propagate.

Fix: Replace local fn gen_object_meta_to_json with delegation to crate::core_gen_adapter::gen_object_meta_to_json. See ai/findings/protobuf-typegen-adapter-quality-audit-2026-07-05.md finding #1.
notes: MERGED #684 (7fed8731). BONUS CORRECTNESS BUG found during consolidation (not in original scope): admissionreg_gen_adapter + apiextensions_gen_adapter were MISSING the owner_references emission block entirely → silent data loss for GC-owned webhooks/CRDs (a ValidatingWebhookConfiguration or CRD with an ownerReference would lose it on decode→JSON). Both now match core. rbac/net_disc/storage_node_flow/coord were already correct. KEY FINDING: function-level ObjectMeta delegation is architecturally IMPOSSIBLE — each adapter's ObjectMeta is a distinct Rust type from its own proto-generated module (prost generates per-package types); the 'consolidation' is keeping the copies byte-identical + correct, not sharing one fn. Future adapter authors: copy core's gen_object_meta_to_json EXACTLY incl owner_references.

title: fix(apiserver): Pod spec update does not bump metadata.generation (is_workload_resource excludes pods)
description:
Split from mayor-40cj (whose proto-drop half was fixed by #675). This is the REMAINING half of the pod-generation conformance failure — a generation-tracking gap, NOT a proto issue.

## Symptom
Conformance test `[sig-node] Pods Extended (pod generation) pod generation should start at 1 and increment per update` FAILS: 3 Passed | 1 Failed. e2e.txt (verified 2026-07-04 on merged main ec8b0a0f, VM lima-node-2): `[FAILED] Expected <int64>: 1 to be equivalent to <int64>: 5 at k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/node/pods.go:530`. The test does 4 spec updates and asserts metadata.generation reaches 5 (starts at 1, +1 per update); it stays at 1.

## Root cause (verified against code)
`is_workload_resource` (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/defaults.rs:84-95) lists apps deployments/replicasets/statefulsets/daemonsets, batch jobs/cronjobs, policy poddisruptionbudgets — but NOT ("", "pods"). The generation machinery is gated on this predicate at:
- defaults.rs:44 (set generation=1 on create)
- resource.rs:729 (spec_before_patch for PATCH generation tracking)
- resource.rs:1460/1496 (spec_before_replace for PUT) → because is_workload_resource is false for pods, spec_before_replace=None, so the increment at resource.rs:1544 (increment_workload_generation_if_spec_changed) never runs for Pods.
The proto-decode of the updated field (tolerations) is already correct post-#675 — the PUT succeeds and carries the new spec; only the generation bump is missing.

## Fix (needs care — Pods are not like workload controllers)
Adding ("", "pods") to is_workload_resource is the obvious first step, BUT verify upstream Pod generation semantics before doing so blindly:
- Upstream (PodObservedGenerationTracking, GA) increments metadata.generation on Pod SPEC updates. Pods are largely immutable post-create — only a specific mutable subset (e.g. activeDeadlineSeconds, tolerations additions, spec.containers[*].image for in-place resize, etc.) can change. Confirm the generation bump fires for exactly the mutable-spec updates the test performs and does not misfire on status-only or metadata-only updates.
- Confirm create-time generation=1 is correct for Pods (it is, upstream).
- Ensure the spec-diff used by increment_workload_generation_if_spec_changed compares the right subtree for Pods (spec, excluding status).

## Verification (MANDATORY — sonobuoy, this is the pods.go:530 test)
Inject Lima VM protocol. Gate: `--focus 'sig-node\] Pods Extended \(pod generation\)'` must go 4/4 (the other 3 already pass). Read e2e.txt (not e2e.log). Read the test source (temp/research/ or WebFetch pods.go from the pinned upstream branch) to confirm the exact update sequence before fixing.

## Regression test
Extract the generation-bump decision into/against a pure function and assert: a Pod spec update bumps generation; a status-only update does not. Must fail on revert.

## Cross-ref
- Proto half: mayor-40cj (closed, fixed by #675).
- BLOCKS mayor-osuq (held pending this + a Pod e2e that exercises priorityClassName end-to-end).
notes: Dispatched 2026-07-04, VM lima-node-smoke/6444/kubelet10251 (needs sonobuoy: pods.go:530). Disjoint from EPIC proto.rs work (touches defaults.rs is_workload_resource:84 + resource.rs generation paths). Parallel-safe with wave-2c.
close_reason: MERGED as PR #681 (8b7119ac, 2026-07-04). Root cause diverged from the is_workload_resource hypothesis (that path is dead for pods — they route through dedicated pods.rs handlers): the real bug was replace_pod/patch_pod accepting a client-supplied lower metadata.generation and downgrading it. Fix (pods.rs only): stamp stored_generation into the incoming body before increment_pod_generation_if_spec_changed. Sonobuoy: [sig-node] Pods Extended (pod generation) now 4/4 (was 3/1); kubectl before/after verified all 8 cases incl client-gen-ignored. 2 regression tests fail on revert. Dead is_workload_resource pods-addition removed pre-merge (mayor review, Rule 2). Unblocks osuq.

title: fix(proto): PodSpec proto decode drops tolerations (field 22) — client-go PUT loses tolerations; pod-generation conformance test still fails
description:
New instance of the proto-decode-drop bug class (see dispatch-proto-decode-drop-check). Surfaced 2026-07-03 by the pod-generation fix worker (PR #670, mayor-h4xw): the conformance test '[sig-node] Pods Extended (pod generation) pod generation should start at 1 and increment per update' does an update that ADDS a toleration and asserts generation bumps. It still FAILS after #670 (latest --focus run: 3 Passed | 1 Failed) because client-go sends the PUT body as protobuf, and u7s proto.rs PodSpec has NO tolerations field (upstream metav1 PodSpec tolerations = field 22). So extract_body silently drops tolerations before the generation compare ever runs — the toleration add looks like a no-op, generation doesn't bump, test fails.

CONFIRMED by the worker: the fix's own unit test client_go_toleration_update_bumps_generation passes at the JSON level, proving the generation logic is correct; the failure is purely the proto decoder not carrying tolerations into the typed spec.

FIX: add tolerations (field 22, repeated Toleration message) to the PodSpec prost struct in crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs with the correct upstream field number, decode it in the pod proto decode path, add a proto-round-trip regression test (encode a pod with tolerations → decode → assert tolerations survive), AND audit sibling PodSpec fields in the same pass for other drops (per dispatch-proto-decode-drop-check — the recurring pattern). This is likely SUBSUMED by the proto EPIC mayor-xmu4 (P2 tkyb migrates core-group structs to generated code, which would carry tolerations by construction) — decide whether to fix discretely now or fold into the EPIC. Filing discretely so it is not lost.

Once fixed, the pod-generation --focus should go 4/4 (the other 3 already pass via #670).

Related: mayor-h4xw (the merged partial fix), mayor-xmu4 (proto EPIC), mayor-osuq (sibling PodSpec proto drop: priorityClassName/priority).
acceptance_criteria: proto.rs PodSpec decodes tolerations (field 22); a proto-round-trip test asserts tolerations survive; the pod-generation --focus conformance run goes 4/4 (the toleration-add-bumps-generation case passes). Sibling PodSpec fields audited for other drops in the same pass.
notes: VERIFICATION on merged main (#675, ec8b0a0f) — 2026-07-04T04:15Z, VM lima-node-2. Result: STILL FAILS, 3 Passed | 1 Failed (UNCHANGED from pre-fix). e2e.txt: temp/e2e/0704-1312-.../logs/e2e.txt line 78-82: '[FAILED] Expected <int64>: 1 to be equivalent to <int64>: 5 at pods.go:530'. (2) SEPARATE, still-broken: metadata.generation never increments on Pod spec updates because is_workload_resource (defaults.rs:84-95) does NOT include ('','pods') — so spec_before_replace=None (resource.rs:1496) and the increment at resource.rs:1544 never runs for Pods. The test asserts generation reaches 5 after 4 updates; stays 1. This generation-bump gap is a DISTINCT bug the proto fix merely unmasked — NOT a proto-typing issue.
