title: fix(apiserver): Job protobuf decode drops successPolicy/podFailurePolicy + zero-valued backoffLimitPerIndex/maxFailedIndexes (3 Job conformance tests hang)
description:
CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (supersedes the earlier "namespace deleted too aggressively" hypothesis, which is WRONG — see below).

The Job's PODS run to completion and the kcm job controller's status PUTs all return 200 (verified: 5x PUT /jobs/<name>/status, all status=200). The namespace is deleted only because the reaper watchdog force-deletes it after 5min — AFTER the expected condition failed to appear. Namespace lifecycle is a symptom, not the cause. Fixing namespace finalizers would NOT fix these tests.

REAL CAUSE: lossy Job protobuf->JSON decode on the CREATE path in crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs (job_spec_to_json, ~line 4312; reached via create_namespaced_resource -> extract_body -> decode_job_proto). When clients send Content-Type: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf (the e2e client and kcm both do — their Job GETs log as `proto`), these JobSpec fields are dropped:
- successPolicy (proto field 16): decoded to raw bytes but NEVER emitted to JSON (no branch). podFailurePolicy (field 11): same.
- backoffLimitPerIndex (field 12) and maxFailedIndexes (field 13): emitted only when != 0, so a legitimate value of 0 is dropped (proto3 zero-value ambiguity).
The stored Job permanently lacks these fields, so the (correct) kcm controller never sees a success policy / per-index limits to evaluate, and never sets the terminal condition the test polls for.

EVIDENCE:
- e2e.log: pods reached Succeeded (e.g. with-success-policy-succeeded-indexed index 0 Succeeded) yet controller emitted BackoffLimitExceeded — only possible if successPolicy is invisible to the controller.
- apiserver.log: /jobs/<name>/status PUTs all 200 (writes accepted; not a rejected-write problem).
- Job CONDITIONS themselves round-trip fine (JobStatus/JobCondition proto field numbers verified correct); only the SPEC decode is lossy. (Separately: JobStatus.uncountedTerminatedPods field 8 is dropped on the status path — latent, not the cause here.)
- The existing test decode_job_proto_handles_job_with_success_policy asserts only kind/name/completions — it CANNOT fail when successPolicy is dropped (violates repo Rule 9).

AFFECTED TESTS (all [sig-apps] Job [Conformance]):
- "with successPolicy should succeeded when all indexes succeeded" (job.go:506) — dropped successPolicy
- "should terminate job execution when the number of failed indexes exceeds maxFailedIndexes" (job.go:662) — dropped maxFailedIndexes=0 / backoffLimitPerIndex=0
- "with successPolicy succeededIndexes rule should succeeded even when some indexes remain pending" (job.go:546) — dropped successPolicy

REPRO FOCUS (Go regexp; passed as sonobuoy --e2e-focus):
  --focus 'with successPolicy|number of failed indexes exceeds maxFailedIndexes'
(covers all three; matches the assembled ginkgo text "[sig-apps] Job with successPolicy ..." etc.)

ACCEPTANCE:
- job_spec_to_json emits successPolicy and podFailurePolicy; backoffLimitPerIndex/maxFailedIndexes use presence tracking (Option<i32>) so 0 is preserved.
- Strengthen the Job proto round-trip test to assert these fields survive.
- The focus tests pass.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #650: typed prost structs for successPolicy/podFailurePolicy, Option<i32> for backoffLimitPerIndex/maxFailedIndexes, all emitted in job_spec_to_json. Tests strengthened to fail on revert.

title: fix(statefulset): StatefulSet rolling update does not apply after patch — pod still uses old image
description:
After patching a StatefulSet's pod template (changing the container image), the running pod continues to use the old image. The test patches the StatefulSet, waits for the rolling update to apply, then asserts the pod image. It fails with: 'statefulset not using ssPatchImage. Is using registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.55' (the old image, not the patched pause:3.10.2).

The kube-controller-manager (upstream, known correct) handles StatefulSet rolling updates by deleting and recreating pods when the template changes. The most likely cause is that the StatefulSet template patch is not being persisted correctly by our apiserver — either the patch is being accepted (200) but the spec.template is not being stored, or the watch notification is not being delivered so kcm never sees the change.

Repro focus:
  --focus='StatefulSet.*should list, patch and delete a collection of StatefulSets'

Acceptance: After patching a StatefulSet's container image, the kcm performs a rolling update and the pod uses the new image. Focus test passes.
notes: RE-ROOT-CAUSED LIVE (mayor, 2026-07-06) — NON-BUG on current main (c92d9d6a). StatefulSet rolling update WORKS: created ss (nginx:1.25), patched image to 1.26, waited 25s -> pod ss-0 recreated with nginx:1.26. Rollout applies correctly. The bead's 'rolling update does not apply, pod still uses old image' is FALSE now (may have been a pre-fix state or a host-sleep timeout in the ballooned run). RECOMMEND: close/park until a caffeinated run confirms. The StatefulSet PANIC (burst-scaling, ftkl PANIC-5) is separate and still open. Not worth a rollout fix dispatch.
close_reason: PR #770 opened (https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/770). Root cause: NOT a rolling-update/watch bug -- a strategic-merge-patch array-ordering bug in crates/apiserver/src/patch.rs shared by all resource PATCH handlers. Upstream apimachinery's mergeSortedSlice interleaves a brand-new (unmatched-by-merge-key) patch array element AHEAD of untouched elements, but our strategic_merge_array appended it at the end -- so the e2e test's patched container (named after the StatefulSet, not the fixture's 'webserver' container) landed at index 1 and Containers[0].Image kept reading the stale image, failing the assertion immediately after PATCH+GET (no controller/rollout involved). Fixed by porting upstream's interleave-reorder algorithm into reorder_merged_array. Regression test test_smp_unmatched_container_lands_before_untouched_container added. Verified live on lima-node-4 (patched container landed at index 0 with new image). cargo test --workspace --quiet: 2158+ tests pass, 0 failed. cargo clippy --workspace --tests --quiet -- -D warnings: clean. sonobuoy --focus 'StatefulSet.*should list, patch and delete a collection of StatefulSets' PASS: 'Ran 1 of 7579 Specs in 22.394 seconds / SUCCESS! -- 1 Passed | 0 Failed | 0 Pending | 7578 Skipped / Test Suite Passed' (from podlogs/sonobuoy/.../logs/e2e.txt).

title: fix(volumes): defaultMode not applied to secret/configmap volume mounts — file permissions are 644 instead of requested mode
description:
When a pod mounts a Secret or ConfigMap volume with a non-default defaultMode (e.g. 0400 = read-only), the files in the mount appear with permissions -rw-r--r-- (0644) instead of the requested -r-------- (0400). The test asserts the file mode matches the requested defaultMode and fails.

The kubelet (upstream, known correct) applies the mode from the pod spec. This suggests the defaultMode field is being lost somewhere in the pod spec decode/re-encode path on our apiserver — the kubelet gets a pod spec without the defaultMode field and falls back to the default 0644.

Likely the same proto-drop pattern as other field-loss bugs: the volume.defaultMode field may not be declared in our proto struct, causing silent drop on decode.

Repro focus:
  --focus='should be consumable from pods in volume with defaultMode set'

(Matches both the Secrets and ConfigMap variants.)

Acceptance: A pod with a Secret or ConfigMap volume mounted with defaultMode=0400 results in files with permissions -r--------. Focus test passes for both variants.
notes: PROTO DROP PATTERN: This is very likely the same silent proto field drop that has hit enableServiceLinks, runtimeClassName, PVC status, PDB status, ownerRefs, and resizePolicy. Check whether Volume.default_mode is declared in our prost struct AND has the correct upstream proto field number (compare against k8s staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/generated.proto). Also audit sibling fields in the same VolumeSource/Volume struct in the same pass. Full pattern documented in ai/extended-context/apiserver-code-gotchas.md (the two ⚠️ PATTERN sections). Regression test must fail on revert (proto round-trip test).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #654: added SecretVolumeSource.default_mode and ConfigMapVolumeSource.default_mode (upstream field 3), emit defaultMode in pod-spec JSON decode. Failing-on-revert tests added.

title: fix(auth): ServiceAccount bound token missing 'credential-id' extra info — token mount conformance test fails
description:
When the apiserver issues a bound ServiceAccount token (POST /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/serviceaccounts/<name>/token), the resulting token's extra info does not include the 'authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id' key. The conformance test mounts an API token into a pod, then verifies this extra info is present and starts with 'JTI='. It fails with: 'expected single authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id extra info item starting with JTI=, got []'.

This is a token issuance bug — the credential ID (JWT ID claim, JTI) is not being added to the token's extra info map when the token is signed.

Repro focus:
  --focus='ServiceAccounts.*should mount an API token into pods'

Acceptance: Tokens issued via the TokenRequest API include 'authentication.kubernetes.io/credential-id' in their extra info, prefixed with 'JTI='. Focus test passes.
close_reason: PR #661 opened — credential-id extra info added to SA token auth

title: fix(leases): Lease object returned with nil renewTime — lease conformance test fails
description:
The Lease object returned by GET /apis/coordination.k8s.io/v1/namespaces/<ns>/leases/<name> has a nil renewTime field even after the kubelet has been updating it via PUT. The kubelet (upstream, known correct) sets renewTime on every heartbeat. The test creates a Lease, waits for renewTime to be populated, then asserts it matches — but the returned object has renewTime=nil.

This is likely a proto decode or serialization issue where the renewTime field is not being persisted or returned. The field is a MicroTime (not Time), which may have a different proto encoding.

Repro focus:
  --focus='Lease.*lease API should be available'

Acceptance: After a Lease is created and updated by the kubelet, GET on the Lease returns a non-nil renewTime that matches the value the kubelet wrote. Focus test passes.
notes: PROTO DROP PATTERN: renewTime on Lease is a MicroTime (not Time), which has a different proto wire format than the regular metav1.Time. Very likely our Lease prost struct has the renewTime field missing or using the wrong field number, causing silent drop on decode. Compare against k8s staging/src/k8s.io/apis/coordination/v1/generated.proto. Also check acquireTime (also MicroTime) in the same struct. Full pattern in ai/extended-context/apiserver-code-gotchas.md.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #654: added secs_nanos_to_rfc3339_micro() in util.rs, updated Lease decode and Event MicroTime sibling fields to include nanosecond precision. Failing-on-revert test decode_lease_proto_preserves_renew_time_nanoseconds added.

title: fix(admission): ValidatingAdmissionPolicy evaluation incorrect — wrong allow/deny outcomes and index-out-of-range panic
description:
ValidatingAdmissionPolicy evaluation produces wrong outcomes in at least two conformance tests:

1. 'should validate against a Deployment' — the policy blocks a Deployment creation that should be allowed ('Internal error! Other namespace should not be allowed'), meaning the CEL expression is being evaluated against the wrong namespace context.

2. 'should support ValidatingAdmissionPolicy API operations' — the updated status is never set ('expect the updated status exist'), indicating the policy status subresource update is not persisting.

Additionally the apiserver.log contains a WARN: "VAP validation expr eval failed: namespaceObject.metadata.name == '...'" — the namespaceObject variable is apparently not being resolved correctly in CEL evaluation context.

A related panic occurs in namespace.go:365 (index out of range [-1]) in the same Serial test block, which may be triggered by the VAP evaluation state.

Repro focus:
  --focus='ValidatingAdmissionPolicy.*should support ValidatingAdmissionPolicy API operations|ValidatingAdmissionPolicy.*should validate against a Deployment'

Acceptance: VAP CEL expressions have access to the correct namespaceObject. Policy status is updated after evaluation. Both focus tests pass.
notes:
RE-PROBED LIVE (mayor, 2026-07-06) — basic VAP evaluation WORKS. Created a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (expression object.metadata.name != 'deny-me') + binding (Deny): configmap 'deny-me' -> 422 'ValidatingAdmissionPolicy denied the request', 'allow-me' -> 201. So allow/deny + CEL eval + binding + matchConstraints all function. The bead's 'evaluation incorrect (wrong allow/deny) + index-out-of-range panic' is therefore NOT the general mechanism — it's a SPECIFIC CEL construct / edge case in a particular conformance test (the panic = index-oob on some expression or variable/param-ref shape). RE-SCOPE before dispatch: read the failing VAP conformance test(s), find the exact expression/feature that mis-evaluates or panics (e.g. variables, params, messageExpression, matchConditions on the policy, or a specific CEL type op), reproduce THAT, then fix. Do NOT dispatch 'fix VAP eval' broadly — it mostly works. Cross-ref tier2-conformance-beads-stale-symptom-framed.

RESOLVED (worker agent-a8eac80f393bdbcf1, 2026-07-06) — PR #706 (https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/706), pushed, NOT merged, bead left open per dispatch instructions.

Root cause pinned: namespaceObject was not a resolvable CEL root in the hand-rolled VAP parser (crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs parse_vap_primary only recognized object/variables/request). Unknown identifiers fell through to a string-literal fallback that left the following .metadata.name tokens unconsumed; eval_cel_bool_expr's final .as_bool() on the leftover string returned None, which run_validating_admission_policies treats as validation failure -> deny. Live-reproduced verbatim on lima-node-smoke:6444 with the exact "should validate against a Deployment" expression: creating a Deployment (replicas=2) in the policy's own target namespace was wrongly denied with "Internal error! Other namespace should not be allowed." — matching the bead's WARN log and failure exactly.

Fix: threaded namespace_object: &serde_json::Value through the parse_vap_* recursive-descent chain (same pattern as object/variables/request), added namespaceObject as a recognized root, and resolve it once per request in run_validating_admission_policies via a new fetch_namespace_object (Null for cluster-scoped, per upstream contract). 2 new regression tests, both verified fail-on-revert with the exact upstream denial message.

The "index out of range [-1]" panic (namespace.go:365) is CONFIRMED UNRELATED to VAP: it's a Go e2e client panic on the core Namespace /status subresource (UpdateStatus not persisting appended conditions), already tracked as mayor-ftkl (PANIC-1). No Rust panic exists anywhere in the apiserver for any VAP CEL construct the conformance suite uses (grep -i panic across a full apiserver.log run: zero matches). The bead's "index-out-of-range panic" framing was stale/conflated, consistent with the NOTES cross-ref to tier2-conformance-beads-stale-symptom-framed.

Item 2 in the bead ("should support ValidatingAdmissionPolicy API operations" / VAP status subresource not persisting) did NOT reproduce in the 0706-1152 run (that test didn't execute in that pass) and is architecturally the same class of bug as mayor-ftkl's PANIC-1 (a generic resource /status PUT not persisting client-supplied fields) rather than a CEL-evaluator bug — it lives in handlers/resource.rs (write_vap_status), not admission.rs, so it's out of scope for this fix and not touched. Recommend the mayor re-verify it live and, if still reproducing, fold it into mayor-ftkl's status-subresource investigation rather than re-opening this bead's CEL scope.

Gates: cargo test --workspace (1977+ apiserver tests, 0 failures), cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings (clean), cargo fmt --check (clean), live before/after gate on own stack.
close_reason: Merged PR #706 (a945eff8). Root cause: VAP CEL variable 'namespaceObject' was not a resolvable root in the hand-rolled parser (parse_vap_primary only knew object/variables/request) -> expressions like 'namespaceObject.metadata.name==X' fell through to a string-literal fallback, left the '.metadata.name' tokens unconsumed, eval'd to non-bool -> None -> treated as validation FAILURE (wrong deny). Fix: thread namespace_object through the parse chain, add namespaceObject root, resolve once via fetch_namespace_object (null for cluster-scoped, per upstream); webhook matchConditions correctly pass Null (no namespaceObject in that spec). Live-verified with the exact upstream expr from validatingadmissionpolicy.go 'should validate against a Deployment'; 2 fail-on-revert tests. IMPORTANT: the 'index out of range [-1]' PANIC in the bead title is a DIFFERENT bug (NOT VAP/CEL — the Rust apiserver never panics, grep confirms) = Namespace /status UpdateStatus not persisting conditions -> recorded on mayor-ftkl (PANIC-1) as its real cause. VAP /status API-operations gap (if still present) is the same /status-persistence class -> also folded to ftkl. This bead's CEL scope is DONE.

title: fix(scheduler): preemption not working — preemptor pod not scheduled after victim eviction
description:
Scheduler preemption is not implemented or not working correctly. The test creates a low-priority victim pod holding the only unit of an extended resource (scheduling.k8s.io/foo), then creates a high-priority preemptor pod requesting the same resource. The preemptor should evict the victim and take its slot. Instead the preemptor stays in OutOfscheduling.k8s.io/foo indefinitely and the test times out after 300s.

Both preemption conformance tests fail:
- 'validates basic preemption works'
- 'validates pod disruption condition is added to the preempted pod'

Repro focus:
  --focus='SchedulerPreemption'

Acceptance: When a higher-priority pod cannot be scheduled due to resource contention with a lower-priority pod, the scheduler evicts the lower-priority pod and binds the higher-priority pod. Both focus tests pass.
notes: UNBLOCKED: 2u9x (priorityClassName→spec.priority) merged in #699 (19ed8bc4). The preemption logic (#695) now sees real pod priorities. REMAINING for the SchedulerPreemption CONFORMANCE tests: kg2s (scheduler extended-resource accounting — the tests fill the node with a fake extended resource, not pod-count). So rsei's basic preemption should now WORK for pod-count-exhaustion scenarios; the specific conformance tests additionally need kg2s. Verify: on a full node (pod-count), a high-priority pod now evicts a low-priority one (spec.priority is populated). Consider closing rsei as 'preemption implemented + priorities resolved' and tracking the conformance-test-specific gap purely under kg2s.
close_reason: Fixed by PR #816. Root cause: scheduler had zero extended-resource accounting (resource_fits/select_preemption_victims only tracked pod-count/cpu/mem/ephemeral-storage), so pick_node always succeeded for nodes saturated only on an extended resource -- the sole contention mechanism all 4 SchedulerPreemption conformance tests use. find_preemption_plan never ran; pods bound onto full nodes, kubelet either rejected outright or picked the wrong victim via its own ambiguous local fallback. Generalized resource_fits + select_preemption_victims to arbitrary extended resources (with a relevance filter so irrelevant pods are never evicted -- caught live evicting kube-system/coredns in the first pass), and added DisruptionTarget/PreemptionByScheduler condition-stamping before eviction to match upstream. Verified live via kubectl repro of all 4 scenarios AND via sonobuoy --focus SchedulerPreemption JUnit results: all 4 target conformance tests pass. Follow-ups filed: mayor-lb60u (concurrent-preemption 409 race, out of gate scope), mayor-myf94 (unrelated priority=0 protobuf-decode drop).

comments.author: Erdos Balint
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-07-15: the 2026-07-06 note claiming preemption 'should now work' for pod-count-exhaustion scenarios is WRONG per real evidence. Conformance run temp/e2e/0714-1535-conformance (2026-07-14, AFTER both 2u9x/osuq priority-decode fixes landed) shows ALL 4 SchedulerPreemption tests still FAILING:
1. 'validates basic preemption works' -- preemptor pod never reaches Running, timeout at predicates.go:1041 (e2e.txt ~line 8792-8798).
2. 'validates pod disruption condition is added to the preempted pod' -- eviction appears to happen (finalizer removed, pod updated) but the DisruptionTarget status-condition assertion fails at resource.go:512 (~line 411).
3. 'validates lower priority pod preemption by critical pod' -- victim pod stays Phase:Running instead of being preempted for a critical-priority pod, fails at preemption.go:309 (~line 7538).
4. 'PreemptionExecutionPath / runs ReplicaSets to verify preemption running path' -- times out waiting for a 2nd ReplicaSet pod creation that preemption should unblock, fails at preemption.go:896 (~line 550-637).
Common thread: every scenario where a preemption-driven evict-then-schedule is expected either doesn't happen at all or doesn't set the right status condition. This is NOT just a stale-bookkeeping bead -- preemption itself needs real root-causing. Do not close without a fresh --focus PASS on all 4 tests.

title: fix(dra): ResourceClaim PATCH response body missing 'kind' field — DRA CRUD conformance test fails
description:
PATCH /apis/resource.k8s.io/v1/namespaces/<ns>/resourceclaims/<name> returns 200 but the response body is missing the 'kind' field. The conformance test performs a json-patch (application/json-patch+json) on a ResourceClaim and validates the returned object; it fails with: "Object 'Kind' is missing in '{...}'".

The access log confirms all DRA PATCHes return 200 — this is a response serialization bug, not a routing/status issue. The returned object is missing TypeMeta (kind/apiVersion), which the conformance harness validates.

Repro focus:
  --focus='DRA.*CRUD Tests.*ResourceClaim'

Acceptance: PATCH on a ResourceClaim returns a complete object with kind=ResourceClaim and apiVersion=resource.k8s.io/v1 in the response body. Focus above passes.
notes: PROTO DROP PATTERN: The missing 'kind' field in PATCH responses is very likely a TypeMeta proto drop — our prost struct for ResourceClaim (or the generic response path) may not be serializing kind/apiVersion back into the response object. Check whether the ResourceClaim proto struct includes TypeMeta fields (kind, api_version) with the correct upstream field numbers (compare against k8s staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/generated.proto). Also audit sibling fields in the same struct in the same pass. Full pattern documented in ai/extended-context/apiserver-code-gotchas.md (the two ⚠️ PATTERN sections). Regression test must fail on revert (proto round-trip test).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #654: added inject_type_meta() at both return paths in do_patch (dry-run and normal). Generic response-path bug affecting ALL resources via do_patch, not only ResourceClaim. Flagged to mayor in PR body. Failing-on-revert test patch_namespaced_resource_response_always_includes_type_meta added.

title: fix(openapi): CRD schema not included in /openapi/v2 response after CRD creation
description:
After creating a CustomResourceDefinition, the GET /openapi/v2 endpoint returns 200 but the response body does not include the new CRD's schema — the definition key is present but the value is an empty object (map[]) instead of the full schema with spec/status/properties. The access log confirms the endpoint is reachable (200 throughout); the problem is content correctness, not routing.

The tests poll /openapi/v2 every 500ms for up to 60s waiting for the schema to appear. It never does.

Repro focus:
  --focus='CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI'

Acceptance: After a CRD is created, the schema defined in spec.versions[].schema.openAPIV3Schema appears correctly in /openapi/v2 within the polling window. Focus above passes.
notes: SCOUT aa225 (2026-07-06T20:34Z, run 0707-0454): CONFIRMED uam0 owns the CRD explain failures — [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI 'works for CRD preserving unknown fields at root / in embedded object / without validation schema' all fail with 'kubectl explain ...: GVR (...) not found in OpenAPI schema'. These are client-side kubectl-explain errors rooted in OpenAPI schema CONTENT, not discovery routing (discovery /apis/ is fine). CAVEAT: uam0 is scoped to /openapi/v2, but /openapi/v3 and /openapi/v3/apis/{group}/{version} already dynamically enumerate CRD groups (existing test openapi_v3_group_returns_crd_schema passes). kubectl explain on modern kubectl uses /openapi/v3. So the fix may need to ensure /openapi/v3 CRD schema CONTENT is complete/correct (not just v2). Confirm which openapi version kubectl explain hits for these CRDs and fix the schema-content gap there. Explain failures to cover: 3 CustomResourcePublishOpenAPI tests.
close_reason: PR #736 opened — fixed /openapi/v3 group CRD schema missing paths+GVK extension (root cause of kubectl explain 'GVR not found' failures) and /openapi/v2 including unserved-version definitions. 4/5 target tests verified passing live (sonobuoy 28/29); 1 residual (enum error message format) filed as mayor-bypo8, out of openapi scope.

title: fix(resourcequota): /resourcequotas/<name>/status subresource returns 404 — kube-controller-manager cannot write quota used counts
description:
PUT /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/resourcequotas/<name>/status returns 404. The access log shows 50 × 404s on this subresource during the conformance run. The kube-controller-manager periodically recalculates quota usage and writes it back via this subresource. Because our apiserver returns 404, the quota's 'used' counters are never updated, so admission always sees zero usage and never blocks pod/service creation — causing the ResourceQuota tests to fail with 'expected error, got nil'.

Repro focus:
  --focus='ResourceQuota should create a ResourceQuota and capture the life of a service|ResourceQuota should verify ResourceQuota with terminating scopes'

Acceptance: PUT /resourcequotas/<name>/status is accepted (200) and persists the updated status. kube-controller-manager quota used counts reflect actual resource usage. Focus above passes.
notes: FRAMING WRONG (scout af69fee4, live-verified): PUT /resourcequotas/<name>/status returns 200 and PERSISTS — the generic status route (main.rs:553) + put_namespaced_resource_status (status.rs:197) work fine. The log 404s were GETs to not-yet-created / deleted quotas (correct). REAL ROOT CAUSE: object_matches_scope (quota.rs:131-138) handles only BestEffort/NotBestEffort; 'Terminating'/'NotTerminating' fall through to always-match → wrong accounting → 'verify ResourceQuota with terminating scopes' conformance test fails. FIX: add Terminating/NotTerminating cases to object_matches_scope (a pod matches Terminating iff spec.activeDeadlineSeconds.is_number()). No route/main.rs change needed. Focus gate: 'ResourceQuota should verify ResourceQuota with terminating scopes'. LATENT/DEFER (not this fix): ResourceQuotaStatus proto struct missing (proto.rs:2747/6129 — only matters if KCM sends proto for status, it uses JSON); status.used ~15s update latency. Evidence: ai/findings/f5p5-lp6i-routing-scout-2026-07-02.md.
close_reason: PR #656 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/656

title: fix(pods): pod resize subresource (/pods/<name>/resize) returns 405 — in-place resize tests fail
description:
GET /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/pods/<name>/resize returns 405 Method Not Allowed. The access log shows 150 × 405s on these paths. The in-place pod resize tests poll this subresource to confirm the resize was applied, and immediately fail with 405.

A separate but related failure: PATCH /pods/<name> with a resize that removes a resource request gets rejected with 'resource requests cannot be removed' — this may be a validation bug in our PATCH handler.

Repro focus:
  --focus='Pod InPlace Resize Container'

Acceptance: GET /pods/<name>/resize returns the current resize status. PATCH to change resource requests (including removing them) is accepted when the resize feature gate is enabled. Focus above passes.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (scout af69fee4, live-verified): /resize route at main.rs:444-446 registers .patch()+.put() but NOT .get() → GET returns 405. FIX: add .get(handlers::pods::get_pod_resize) to the route + add get_pod_resize in pods.rs delegating to get_pod_status (status.resize is embedded in the pod body). The bead's SECOND claim — 'PATCH removing a resource request is wrongly rejected' — is NOT A BUG: real k8s 1.33 also rejects removal, pod_resize.go:390 explicitly asserts 'resource requests cannot be removed', our validate_resize_patch (pods.rs:1872-1936 Rule 3) is CORRECT. Do NOT touch that validation. Scope of fix = the missing GET only. Focus gate: 'Pod InPlace Resize Container'. Evidence: ai/findings/f5p5-lp6i-routing-scout-2026-07-02.md.
close_reason: PR #655 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/655 — added GET handler for pod /resize subresource; get_pod_resize mirrors get_pod_status; route updated with .get(); 2 regression tests pass and fail on revert; 1829 tests pass; VM: GET /resize returns 200 (was 405)

title: fix(pods): pod log subresource returns 500 — lifecycle hook and container probe tests fail at log collection
description:
GET /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/pods/<name>/log returns 500 Internal Server Error. The access log shows 23 × 500s on pods/.../log paths. These are all in test teardown: after the test body times out or completes, the framework collects pod logs as diagnostic evidence — that collection step itself 500s, which causes the test to be marked FAILED even in cases where the underlying behaviour may have been correct.

Affected tests (representative):
  --focus='Container Lifecycle Hook.*should execute prestop'

Also hits container probe tests via the same log-collection path during teardown.

Note: the 400s on pods/.../log are expected (pod not in running state); only the 500s are bugs.

Acceptance: GET /pods/<name>/log successfully proxies to the kubelet log streaming endpoint and returns the container's log bytes. The lifecycle hook focus above passes.
notes:
LIVE EVIDENCE from operator's full conformance run (2026-07-05, verified against temp/u7s/apiserver.log + VM state). NOT a konnectivity crash (server PID 20447 up, ready_backends=1; agent up; kubelet PID 49081 listening on 10250, reachable in 0.16ms HTTP 401 from inside VM). The failure: apiserver returns 500 on GET pods/<name>/log?container=e2e — SUSTAINED window 01:08:48→01:13:56 UTC (~5min of repeated 500s on the sonobuoy-e2e-job pod), then SELF-RECOVERED (status=200 at 01:13:56). NOT a brief transient. BROADER than one pod: at 01:12:56Z the same 500 hit container-lifecycle-hook-7133/{pod-handle-http-request,pod-with-poststart-http-hook}/log AND a /nodes/lima-node:10250/proxy/pods returned 502 in the same instant — so the whole apiserver→kubelet(:10250) leg was intermittently broken during the window while kubelet itself was healthy. ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS: apiserver's kubelet client/proxy path (connection reuse / TLS / dial not retried) hiccups under load, not kubelet death, not konnectivity. IMPACT: per pu5i's own note, these teardown-log 500s mark tests FAILED even when behavior was correct → the operator's run may show SPURIOUS failures / understate real conformance. NEXT: --stack-only scout to reproduce the log-500 and read the apiserver's actual kubelet-dial error stack; do AFTER the operator's run finishes (needs a VM slot). Symptom log: temp/terminal_failure.log.
SCOUT QUEUED (operator 2026-07-05): dispatch a --stack-only scout to reproduce the pod-log 500 + capture the apiserver's kubelet-dial error stack — but ONLY AFTER the operator's in-progress full conformance run on lima-node ends. NOTHING destructive until then (no orphan-process reaping, no VM touches, no --reset). Run-done signal: 'kubectl -n sonobuoy get pods' — e2e-job pod (sonobuoy-e2e-job-dcde5e94bfb041df) currently 2/2 Running; done when its e2e container is Completed/Terminated (not 2/2 Running). Scout gets a FREE VM (lima-node-2 or lima-node-smoke — NEVER lima-node). Scope for the scout: read the pu5i live-evidence note above (sustained 01:08-01:13 UTC self-recovering window, multi-pod, correlates w/ node-proxy 502); reproduce via kubectl logs against a --stack-only stack under load, grep apiserver log for the kubelet-dial/proxy error, root-cause the apiserver kubelet-client path (conn reuse/TLS/dial-retry), findings doc + fix recommendation.
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (scout a9bbc7c6, 2026-07-05, verified by mayor against source). build_kubelet_reqwest_client() is called PER-REQUEST in pod_log (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs:196) AND node_proxy (proxy.rs:1082) — each builds a fresh reqwest::Client with an empty connection pool. Under sonobuoy's concurrent teardown-log load, the burst of simultaneous new TLS handshakes is intermittently reset by kubelet → HTTP 500 (log) / 502 (node-proxy), correlated (both use the same per-request-client path). Fail-latency ~5ms (fast-fail, NO retry). FIX (small, 2 files): add shared kubelet_client: reqwest::Client to AppState (build once in new_with_config, mirroring the existing webhook_client at state.rs:146), use state.kubelet_client in both handlers, delete per-request build_kubelet_reqwest_client calls. Note: the state.rs:150 'Identity: !Clone' comment is STALE — reqwest::Identity derives Clone in reqwest 0.13. SECONDARY: pod_log returns 500 on kubelet-comm failure (proxy.rs:209) — should be 502 to match node_proxy. Findings: ai/findings/pu5i-podlog-500-scout-2026-07-05.md. This is a clean solo fix bead now — ready to dispatch.
close_reason: PR #685 opened: shares kubelet_client on AppState (built once in new_with_config), removes per-request build_kubelet_reqwest_client calls from pod_log and resolve_node_proxy_target, changes pod_log 500→502 on kubelet failure, deletes dead build_kubelet_reqwest_client fn, adds regression tests

title: fix(apiserver): pod proxy over konnectivity uses http:// forward-proxy -> 405; must use CONNECT tunnel (breaks DNS + Proxy conformance)
description:
pod proxy over konnectivity sends plain-HTTP forward-proxy GET; konnectivity only allows CONNECT -> 405.

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed + live-reproduced against the running apiserver, PID that wrote temp/u7s/apiserver.log):
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs:
- pod_proxy_dispatch (line ~1222) builds a PLAIN-HTTP target: http://{podIP}:{port}/{path}
- build_pod_proxy_client (line ~1183-1207) routes it through reqwest::Proxy::all("https://<konnectivity>") when konnectivity_proxy_addr is set.
- reqwest issues an HTTP CONNECT tunnel ONLY for https:// targets. For an http:// target it sends a classic forward-proxy request: `GET http://<podIP>/... HTTP/1.1` directly to konnectivity.
- konnectivity-server (proxy-agent v0.35.0) accepts ONLY CONNECT and replies 405 with body "this proxy only supports CONNECT passthrough".
- Our handler passes the upstream status through verbatim (line ~1263: Response::builder().status(pod_status.as_u16())). Client sees 405.

Contrast that WORKS: node_proxy / pod_log target https:// (proxy.rs:161, 1077), so reqwest issues CONNECT and tunnels fine. That asymmetry is the tell.

EVIDENCE:
- Live repro: GET /api/v1/namespaces/kube-system/pods/<coredns>/proxy/metrics -> 405 MethodNotAllowed on the current apiserver.
- The string "only supports CONNECT passthrough" does NOT exist in crates/ (rg = 0) -> external origin (konnectivity).
- apiserver.log pod-proxy paths: 1616x 405, 0x 200. (The 404s in the log are our own not_found for already-deleted pods, unrelated.)
- REFUTED earlier theories: (a) route/method missing at the router - route IS registered with GET since aadcf9c7; (b) wrong target port - agnhost test-webserver listens on 80, matching our unwrap_or(80); the request never reaches agnhost, konnectivity rejects it first.

Affected tests (all read a pod through pods/proxy):
- ALL [sig-network] DNS conformance tests (they read lookup results via GET /pods/<pod>/proxy/results/<file>): dns-7251,dns-9416,dns-9513,dns-2826 in the failing run.
- [sig-network] Proxy version v1 should proxy through a service and a pod (sends DELETE /pods/<pod>/proxy?method=DELETE, 5997 retries).
NOTE: ReplicaSet failures in this run are NOT primarily this bug - they are the WAL stale-read (see the stale-read bead). ReplicaSet pod-proxy 405 appears only 1x; ReplicaSet stale-read errors appear 544x.

REPRO FOCUS (Go regexp, passed as sonobuoy --e2e-focus):
  --focus 'sig-network\] DNS '        # all 5 DNS conformance tests, fastest signal
  --focus 'should proxy through a service and a pod'   # the Proxy DELETE test
Fastest single check WITHOUT a full run (against a live cluster with any Running pod):
  kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/namespaces/kube-system/pods/<running-pod>/proxy/metrics"   # must NOT be 405

ACCEPTANCE:
- GET/DELETE/POST/PUT on /pods/<name>/proxy[/<path>] tunnel via HTTP CONNECT to the pod IP:port through konnectivity and return the pod's real response (200/404 from the pod), not konnectivity's 405.
- New regression test asserts a pod-proxy request produces a CONNECT (not a forward-proxy GET) toward the konnectivity address. (Existing tests only assert the proxy URL is https:// and the client builds; none exercise a real GET through the tunnel - which is why this shipped.)
- Both focus patterns pass.
close_reason: PR #662 opened: manually establishes CONNECT tunnel to konnectivity via tokio-rustls + hyper http1; no more 405. Live: kubectl pod proxy returns 200. DNS --focus: 11 passed, 0 proxy-405 failures.

title: fix(pods): create_pod ignores ?dryRun=All and missing RuntimeClass
description:
Two bugs in create_pod (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:317):

1. **?dryRun=All is ignored**: create_pod does not accept a CreateQuery parameter and has no is_dry_run() check before state.store.put(). Every pod create is persisted even when the client sends ?dryRun=All. Confirmed in apiserver.log: POST /api/v1/namespaces/runtimeclass-386/pods?dryRun=All returns 201 and the scheduler immediately creates a binding.

2. **RuntimeClass non-existence is not a rejection**: when spec.runtimeClassName references a deleted/missing RuntimeClass, create_pod logs a warning and continues. The real apiserver returns 403 Forbidden. The test 'should reject a Pod requesting a deleted RuntimeClass' (k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/common/node/runtimeclass.go) calls expectPodRejection with DryRun=All and retries via gomega.Eventually until it gets Forbidden. Because we ignore dryRun and never reject, the test creates ~298 real pods, fills the node to capacity=110, and cascades OutOfpods errors into all subsequent tests.

Fix: add CreateQuery param to create_pod, return early when is_dry_run(), and return Status::forbidden when runtimeClassName references a non-existent RuntimeClass. Regression test must fail on revert of either fix.
close_reason: PR #659 opened: create_pod now honors dryRun=All (no store.put) and returns 403 on missing RuntimeClass. Both regression tests fail-on-revert. Conformance test 'should reject a Pod requesting a deleted RuntimeClass': 1 Passed, 0 Failed.

title: apiserver silently drops sonobuoy live progress updates (sonobuoy status frozen at start)
description:
## Summary

During a sonobuoy run, `sonobuoy status` (and `sonobuoy status --json`) freezes at the
initial progress value and never advances until the whole suite completes — e.g. stuck at
`{msg:"Test Suite starting", total:444, completed:0}` for a full run. The apiserver ACCEPTS
the aggregator's progress writes (HTTP 200) but the stored progress annotation does not
reflect the rapid per-test increments — same "200 + silent content loss" shape as the PDB
proto bug, but a different mechanism.

## Mechanism (how sonobuoy reports progress)

The e2e framework POSTs progress to http://localhost:8099/progress (localhost, inside the
pod) -> sonobuoy worker sidecar -> aggregator -> aggregator PATCHes its OWN pod's
`metadata.annotations["sonobuoy.hept.io/status"]` so `sonobuoy status` can read it back via
the apiserver. The lost hop is that final annotation PATCH on the aggregator pod.

## Evidence

REPRODUCED on an isolated cluster (worktree debug/sonobuoy-progress, VM lima-node-2, port
6444, focus "should be consumable"):
- Stored annotation after the suite ran 42 tests: progress = {msg:"Test Suite completed",
  total:42, completed:0}. `completed` stuck at 0 despite 42 tests finishing. Some updates
  land (total 0->42, terminal msg) but the rapid per-test `completed` increments do NOT.
- Live full run (mayor, 6443): frozen at {msg:"Test Suite starting", total:444, completed:0}
  the whole run, while apiserver.log showed 1205 main-resource PATCHes + 408 /status PATCHes
  to /pods/sonobuoy, ALL status=200, over 1h40m. Pod resourceVersion actively churning.

Fingerprint = lost-update: slow/terminal updates survive; rapid ones are lost -> a
read-modify-write clobber between concurrent writers on the same aggregator pod
(aggregator annotation PATCH interleaved with kubelet /status PATCH).

## Write path (narrowed)

The aggregator's main-resource annotation PATCH is served by `patch_pod`
(crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:604), NOT the generic do_patch. patch_pod does
read-whole -> merge -> retry-on-RevisionMismatch -> write-whole. In isolation an annotation
merge-patch persists correctly (verified via kubectl: strategic-merge, merge, and even via
/status all persist a test annotation). So the drop is NOT a blanket annotation-PATCH bug.

## NOT yet root-caused

The exact drop is unconfirmed. Candidate: a concurrent /status write (kubelet) round-trips
the whole object and reverts the annotation, or the merge loses it under a specific
interleaving. Targeted debug logging was added to patch_pod (target: "u7s_sonobuoy", logs
incoming PATCH body + merged annotation before persist) on branch debug/sonobuoy-progress;
next step is to re-run and read those u7s_sonobuoy lines to see the actual bytes.

Also note upstream flakiness exists (vmware-tanzu/sonobuoy#1507: "status intermittently not
reporting"), but our freeze is deterministic across two runs, so this is a u7s bug.

## Impact

Cosmetic/operational: the suite still runs and final results are correct; only live
progress visibility is broken. Makes long conformance runs opaque (can't tell hang vs
progress).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] During a sonobuoy run, `sonobuoy status` advances `completed` as tests finish.
- [ ] Root cause identified from actual PATCH bodies (which writer/merge drops it).
- [ ] Regression coverage for the identified mechanism (fails-on-revert).
- [ ] Temp u7s_sonobuoy debug logging removed.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND — apiserver EXONERATED; this is a sonobuoy config gap, not a u7s bug.

Captured the actual PATCH bodies via targeted logging in patch_pod (target u7s_sonobuoy, branch debug/sonobuoy-progress, isolated cluster lima-node-2/6444). Findings:
- The INCOMING annotation PATCHes from sonobuoy only ever carry completed:0. The progress object jumps from msg='Test Suite starting' (total:42, completed:0) straight to 'Test Suite completed' (total:42, completed:0). There are NO intermediate per-test increments (completed:1..42) on the wire.
- Our apiserver stores exactly what it receives: the 'AFTER merge' values equal the incoming values (total:42/completed:0 in -> same merged -> same stored). merge_patch preserves the annotation faithfully. No drop, no clobber.

So the frozen 'sonobuoy status' counter is UPSTREAM behavior: per-test progress requires the e2e plugin env vars E2E_USE_GO_RUNNER=true and E2E_EXTRA_ARGS=--progress-report-url=http://localhost:8099/progress (per sonobuoy docs). Our invocation in scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh:116 ('run --plugin e2e --wait --e2e-parallel=true ...') sets NEITHER, so the framework only emits suite start/complete events and completed stays 0. This matches the observed behavior exactly.

RECLASSIFY: not an apiserver bug. Options: (a) close as 'not our bug / works-as-configured'; or (b) convert to a low-pri tooling improvement — add the two env vars to 06-run-sonobuoy.sh so 'sonobuoy status' shows live per-test progress during long runs. The earlier lost-update/clobber hypothesis in this bead is REFUTED by the wire evidence.
INDEPENDENTLY RECONFIRMED (fresh live run, lima-node-2, --focus '[sig-apps] Deployment', 30 tests ran) — apiserver exoneration stands, but the earlier 'config gap' narrower claim is WRONG:

1. `sonobuoy gen plugin e2e` on our actual VM (sonobuoy v0.57.3) shows E2E_USE_GO_RUNNER=true and E2E_EXTRA_ARGS=--progress-report-url=http://localhost:8099/progress ARE set by DEFAULT in the built-in e2e plugin manifest that `sonobuoy run --plugin e2e` uses — our script does NOT need to add them. The earlier "missing env vars" theory was incorrect.
2. Confirmed end-to-end plumbing IS working live: worker sidecar log showed "Starting to listen on port 8099 ... relay them to https://[10.85.0.4]:8080/api/v1/progress/global/e2e"; aggregator log showed 5x "received request ... url=/api/v1/progress/global/e2e" POSTs during the run.
3. Despite that, EVERY incoming annotation PATCH body to the aggregator's own pod carried completed:0 — captured via temp u7s_sonobuoy debug logging (now removed), e.g.:
   incoming_patch: progress:{"total":12,"completed":0} (first report)
   ... (no intermediate completed:1..11 ever observed) ...
   final: progress:{"msg":"Test Suite completed","total":0,"completed":0}
4. Zero RevisionMismatch retries occurred during the ENTIRE run (grep -c "revision mismatch, retrying" apiserver.log => 0). This is the decisive falsification of the lost-update/clobber hypothesis: a race cannot cause data loss that never even needed a retry. incoming_patch == merged_annotation == stored_annotation byte-for-byte at every step.
5. Verified statically too: patch_pod/patch_pod_status both already have the RevisionMismatch retry-loop (re-read-fresh + reapply), predating mayor-g50t3's do_patch fix (PR #771, which touched a different file, resource.rs, for generic/CRD resources — patch_pod already had this pattern). SqliteStore::put's CAS is atomic (BEGIN IMMEDIATE txn under a single write-conn async Mutex) — no possible silent overwrite.

CONCLUSION: apiserver has zero bug here. The frozen 'completed' counter is entirely upstream — the e2e Go test runner / ginkgo v2's progress-report client only ever sends completed:0 (start sentinel) then a "Test Suite completed" terminal sentinel; it does not emit real intermediate progress in our invocation (`--e2e-parallel=true`, non-disruptive-conformance mode). Not fixable from u7s; would need upstream ginkgo/sonobuoy investigation or dropping --e2e-parallel (rejected — would drastically slow conformance runs), which is out of scope for this bead.

Added a permanent regression test (patch_pod_annotation_survives_concurrent_status_write_race, crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs) that locks in the CAS+retry invariant that made the leading hypothesis a non-issue: verified fails-on-revert by temporarily replacing the retry `continue` with an unconditional write, confirming the assertion on status.phase fails as expected, then reverted.

Closing as not-a-u7s-bug; apiserver behavior verified correct under real concurrent load.
close_reason: Not a u7s bug — confirmed with fresh live evidence (zero RevisionMismatch retries during a full run, yet freeze reproduced; apiserver stores exactly what it receives). Root cause is upstream sonobuoy/ginkgo progress reporter never emitting incremental completed counts. Regression coverage for the CAS+retry invariant added in PR #785.

title: Container proto decoder drops field 24 (restartPolicy) -> sidecar init containers block forever
description: Root cause of the resize 300s-timeout bulk (found while scouting mayor-ma3q; verified). crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs Container prost struct has resize_policy at tag 23 but NO field at tag 24. Upstream Container field 24 is 'optional string restartPolicy' (KEP-3939 sidecar containers; verified against k8s release-1.34 core/v1/generated.proto). The e2e binary sends pods (via protobuf) with an init container restartPolicy: Always (sidecar). u7s SILENTLY DROPS field 24, converting the sidecar into a traditional BLOCKING init container. The init container runs 'sleep 1d', never exits, pod stays Pending forever, test times out after 300s waiting for Running+Ready. This is the recurring proto-decode-drop pattern (see ai/extended-context/apiserver-code-gotchas.md); ~23 of the 54 resize failures are this (NOT resize-acknowledgment, which the prior wjon-spike correctly found was fine). FIX (size S, identical to #631 resizePolicy/field 23): add #[prost(string, optional, tag = "24")] restart_policy: Option<String> to the Container struct (~line 903, after resize_policy) and emit it in container_to_json (~line 5024). AUDIT in same pass: field 25 = repeated ContainerRestartRule restartPolicyRules (also absent — decide whether to add; newer field). Regression: proto-round-trip test decode_container_proto_preserves_restart_policy (a sidecar init container with restartPolicy=Always survives decode). VERIFY LIVE: run-all.sh --focus 'InPlace Resize Container' should flip ~23 of 54 (15/54 -> ~38/54). kubectl repro (from scout): JSON-created sidecar pod reaches Running+Ready; proto-created (e2e) drops field 24 -> stuck Pending. Findings: ai/findings/0701-resize-acknowledgment-scout.md.
close_reason: Merged: #641 (bh8m — Container proto field-24 restartPolicy decode; resize focus 15->28/69) and #642 (mory — reject container reorder via $setElementOrder; invalid-resize focus 9->10/10). Both live-verified. bh8m follow-up: field 25 restartPolicyRules deferred (needs nested structs).

title: Pod proxy subresource 404s for running pod (blocks RC serve-image conformance connectivity check)
description: Surfaced 2026-07-01 verifying #634 (mayor-n9t6). With the RC runaway fixed, the '[sig-apps] ReplicationController should serve a basic image on each replica' test now advances past pod creation (1 pod, Running, Ready -- verified) but FAILS at rc.go:538 'Trying to dial the pod' / WaitForPodsResponding: the apiserver returns 'the server could not find the requested resource (get pods <podname>)' when the test dials the pod via the pod proxy subresource. The pod EXISTS and is Running (the test read its status one line earlier). SUSPECTED cause: crates/apiserver/src/main.rs:476 registers the pod proxy route as '/api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/pods/{name}/proxy/{*path}' -- requiring a NON-EMPTY trailing {*path}. WaitForPodsResponding dials '/pods/{name}/proxy' (no subpath) or '/proxy/', which does not match the {*path} route -> 404. VERIFY: does the proxy handler need a route for the no-subpath form ('/pods/{name}/proxy' and '/pods/{name}/proxy/')? Also confirm the actual subresource the test uses (proxy GET vs portforward) -- error is a GET returning 404, consistent with proxy, not the portforward POST. Note: exec/attach/portforward are 501 stubs (main.rs:461) pending SPDY/WebSocket; proxy is separately routed (476). This is a DISTINCT bug from n9t6 (selector defaulting) -- n9t6's fix is proven and merges on its own. Repro: on a stack with #634, run-all.sh --focus 'ReplicationController should serve a basic image on each replica' -> 1 pod Running but FAIL at rc.go:538. Fix + regression test (proxy GET to a running pod with and without subpath returns 2xx/routes to kubelet, not 404).
close_reason: Merged: #636 (cokf proto status decode + DS/Job/CronJob audit), #637 (rpcb pod proxy no-subpath routing), #638 (h9fz status-patch no longer namespace-404s, GC loop terminates). All CI-green + verified (cokf unit round-trip, rpcb routing test, h9fz live before/after).

title: Scheduler has no node pod-capacity (NodeResourcesFit) check — binds pods to full nodes
description: crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs pick_node()/select_node_for_pod() (verified ~lines 216-255) selects the first nodeSelector-matching node with NO check of the node's pod capacity/allocatable. NodeItem/NodeList structs (~177-191) don't even capture status.allocatable.pods. Consequence: pods are bound to a node already at its pod cap; the kubelet then fails them with OutOfpods (phase=Failed) instead of the pod staying Pending/Unschedulable. This is the standard NodeResourcesFit predicate, entirely absent. It is a real robustness gap that WILL cause conformance failures independent of the RC-runaway investigation (mayor-n9t6): any test that fills a node expects overflow pods to pend, not fail. FIX: add allocatable.pods to NodeItem; in pick_node, count non-terminated pods on the candidate node (GET /api/v1/pods?fieldSelector=spec.nodeName%3D<node>) and skip/err when at capacity so the pod stays Pending. NOTE: this CAPS the blast radius of n9t6's runaway but is NOT believed to be n9t6's root cause (a bare kubectl apply of the same RC converges; the runaway is triggered by something specific to the conformance test's shape — under active investigation). File separately so it can be fixed on its own merits.
close_reason: Fixed by #635 (merged). Scheduler now skips nodes at pod capacity (NodeResourcesFit); overflow pods stay Pending instead of failing OutOfpods. Worker-demonstrated live.

title: Pod status-patch to deleted namespace hard-404s, trapping KCM pod-GC in infinite retry
description: Conformance run 0701-1407 secondary root cause (the persistent-load driver). KCM's pod-GC controller (gc_controller.go:313) tries to mark an orphaned/terminating pod Failed via a status subresource PATCH; our apiserver returns HTTP 404 'Namespace not found' because the pod's namespace is already deleted; KCM can never finalize the pod, so it RETRIES ~every 2s FOREVER. Evidence: /tmp/kcm.log in lima-node has 2566 'Failed to delete unscheduled terminating pod' errors -- 28% of the entire KCM log -- ALL for namespace validating-admission-policy-6650, spread evenly across 00:24->15:32 UTC (15h, i.e. still going >1h after the run ended). This is why the apiserver stays hot post-run (apiserver.log grew to 7.3GB, still growing at 15:30). Real k8s lets a terminal-status patch on a pod in a terminating/absent namespace succeed or no-op so GC can finalize. FIX: the pod status subresource handler should not hard-404 a status patch that only sets phase=Failed/observedGeneration when the namespace is terminating/gone -- allow it (or return a result KCM treats as 'done') so the GC loop terminates. Needs a regression test on the pod status handler for the deleted-namespace case.
close_reason: Merged: #636 (cokf proto status decode + DS/Job/CronJob audit), #637 (rpcb pod proxy no-subpath routing), #638 (h9fz status-patch no longer namespace-404s, GC loop terminates). All CI-green + verified (cokf unit round-trip, rpcb routing test, h9fz live before/after).

title: Categorize 0701-1407 full conformance run failures
description: Analyze temp/e2e/0701-1407-conformance e2e.txt and produce a categorized failure inventory. Run is TRUNCATED at the 6h sonobuoy aggregator cap (status: timeout, no Ginkgo final summary) — worker must NOT report totals as if the whole suite ran. Deliverable: grouped failure list (by apiserver surface/root-cause family) with per-failure spec name + one-line symptom + evidence pointer. No prioritization (operator+mayor decide). Compare failure families against the 0627-1541 run where possible.

title: fix(apiserver): Container.resizePolicy stripped on proto decode (proto field 23) — blocks 3 resize conformance specs + ~65 others
description: VERIFIED via the resize --focus probe (mayor-abf46122, 2026-06-29): the Container proto struct in crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs is MISSING field 23 (resizePolicy — []ContainerResizePolicy). So a pod's container resizePolicy is STRIPPED on proto decode → after a PATCH /resize, the returned pod is missing resizePolicy → the conformance tests' post-PATCH verification fails. This is the FOURTH+ instance of the proto-decode-drop family (cf enableServiceLinks #605, runtimeClassName #600, PVC status #622, PDB status #627, ownerRefs #626/#629). HIGHEST-LEVERAGE resize follow-up: the probe (run 'Pod InPlace Resize Container' --focus) showed 4 Passed / 66 Failed across 70 specs — the resizePolicy strip is the dominant cause: it fails 2 of the 3 remaining CONFORMANCE specs ('6 containers various operations' + 'increase CPU/mem multi-container', both immediate-fail ~3-4s after PATCH /resize) AND most of the ~65 non-conformance resize specs ('resizePolicy field stripped from GET response'). FIX: add resizePolicy (field 23, ContainerResizePolicy{resourceName, restartPolicy}) to the Container prost struct + decoder in proto.rs, so it survives the proto round-trip. Likely also add it to the typed Container struct (types.rs) if it's reasoned about. cargo-testable (proto round-trip preserves resizePolicy) + verify via the resize --focus.
notes: From the resize conditional-gap probe (mayor-21gi/usz6, PR #630). The probe CONFIRMED the other 2 conditional gaps (allocatedResources synth, PodResize conditions) are NOT needed — resizePolicy is the real remaining blocker. 3rd resize conformance spec ('resize via the replace endpoint') fails for a DIFFERENT reason (init-container 'sleep 1d' never exits init — separate init-container-resize question, file separately if pursued). After this lands, re-run the resize --focus to see how many of the 6 conformance + 65 non-conformance specs flip. Proto-decode-drop family — consider an audit of the Container proto struct for OTHER missing fields while here.
close_reason: PR #631 opened: fix Container.resizePolicy proto field 23 stripped on decode

title: fix(apiserver/GC): cascading deletion not supported for custom resources (CRD ownerRefs)
description:
VERIFIED + DESIGNED (scout, 2026-06-29; ai/findings/0629-cr-cascade-scout.md). Root cause CONFIRMED + BROADER than first thought: the CR delete handlers delete_cr (cr.rs:816) and delete_cr_namespaced (cr.rs:1217) hard-delete the owner with NO apply_delete_policy call, NO DeleteOptions parsing, NO ownerRef cascade. So CRs currently ignore finalizers, propagationPolicy, AND cascade entirely — not just the cascade. Conformance spec '[sig-api-machinery] Garbage collector should support cascading deletion of custom resources' (gc.go:990) fails because a deleted owner CR's dependents (+ canary) are never reclaimed. Root cause = (b): apiserver SHOULD do server-side CR cascade but doesn't (u7s DOES serve CR watches + PartialObjectMetadata, so it's not a KCM-infra gap; it's our missing handler logic).

FIX DESIGN (Medium, ~1-2d):
1. cr.rs: add headers:HeaderMap + body:Bytes to delete_cr (816) and delete_cr_namespaced (1217). Parse DeleteOptions (reuse the DeleteOptionsProto decoder + is_explicit_cascade/is_orphan logic from #617/#625).
2. cr.rs: call apply_delete_policy (so CR finalizers → soft-delete work; this ALSO gives Foreground-compatible soft-delete behavior, helping deferred mayor-kxsk — but the foregroundDeletion finalizer-removal controller loop stays out of scope).
3. cr.rs: add cascade_delete_cr_dependents — enumerate all CRD store prefixes, delete objects whose ownerReferences[].uid matches the deleted owner (recurse for ownership chains). Honor the policy (Orphan → strip ownerRefs instead, per #625 pattern).
4. resource.rs: at the CR-fallthrough call sites (line 492 delete_cr, line 1582 delete_cr_namespaced) propagate the parsed DeleteOptions/headers/body instead of discarding them.

NOTE: a GENERIC ownerRef-scan helper could be shared with mayor-2f5a (CronJob), BUT they wire at DIFFERENT call sites (CronJob = batch branch of delete_namespaced_resource in resource.rs; CR = cr.rs). 2f5a is being fixed separately with the per-kind pattern. Keep the scan helper generic enough to reuse, but this bead = the CR (cr.rs) wiring + cascade.
notes: Scout findings: ai/findings/0629-cr-cascade-scout.md. Now ready to dispatch as a fix (was investigate-first). Medium size. Verify with cargo + the 'cascading deletion of custom resources' GC --focus. Test source: garbage_collector.go:990 (uses Background per scout). Surface: cr.rs (primary) + resource.rs (fallthrough call sites). Reuse #617/#625 DeleteOptions+orphan logic. Foreground finalizer-loop = out of scope (kxsk).
close_reason: PR #629 opened; cascade+ownerRef fix verified PASS on lima-node-smoke. Two commits: cascade+apply_delete_policy (#0ae5), ownerRef preservation in stamp_cr_fields (#8860).

title: feat(apiserver): implement OIDC SA-issuer discovery endpoints (/.well-known/openid-configuration + /openid/v1/jwks)
description: VERIFIED (scout mayor-gobh + mayor-confirmed in source). The routes /.well-known/openid-configuration and /openid/v1/jwks are NOT registered in the axum router (crates/apiserver/src/main.rs) — they return 404 even with admin creds (scout confirmed via kubectl get --raw). The system:service-account-issuer-discovery ClusterRole IS already seeded (main.rs:1088 grants GET on those nonResourceURLs), but the endpoints behind it don't exist. CAPTURED FAILURE (e2e.txt, OIDC discovery conformance): in-cluster discovery gets 403 (cascade from the RBAC bug mayor-a31j), and the endpoints themselves 404. FIX: register both routes + handlers. /.well-known/openid-configuration → OIDC config JSON (issuer, jwks_uri, response_types, subject_types, signing algs). /openid/v1/jwks → JWK Set exposing the SA token-signing public key (the apiserver already has the SA signing key — expose its public half as a JWK). RBAC-protect them (NOT exempt — the seeded ClusterRole gates access). Split from mayor-gobh. NOTE: Lead 2 (kube-root-ca CA mismatch) was REFUTED by the scout — the ConfigMap CA == serving CA; the TLS error in the test was a cascade from the RBAC 403, not a CA bug. Do NOT chase a CA fix.
notes: Source: ai/findings/0629-oidc-discovery-scout.md (Root Cause B). e2e.txt: temp/e2e/0629-1220-oidc-gobh/e2e.txt. Verified: main.rs has the routes ONLY as a ClusterRole nonResourceURL (1088), not as registered routes. DEPENDS on the SA signing key the apiserver uses for projected SA tokens (find where it signs SA tokens → expose the public key as JWK). Both this AND mayor-a31j must land for the OIDC discovery spec to pass. The conformance test is [sig-auth] ServiceAccountIssuerDiscovery should support OIDC discovery of service account issuer.
close_reason: PR #623 opened: implements GET /.well-known/openid-configuration and GET /openid/v1/jwks, RBAC-gated, JWK derived from existing SA key, 1733 tests pass

title: fix(apiserver): honor 'escalate' verb in ClusterRoleBinding/RoleBinding escalation check
description: VERIFIED (scout mayor-gobh + mayor-confirmed in source). check_crb_escalation (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs:511) and check_rb_escalation (:600) go straight to user_holds_all_rules with NO bypass for the 'escalate' verb. Real Kubernetes RBAC: a user may create a binding to ANY (cluster)role if they hold the 'escalate' verb on clusterroles/roles in rbac.authorization.k8s.io — even without personally holding the role's rules. u7s lacks this bypass, so a user with verbs:['*'] on clusterroles (which INCLUDES escalate) is wrongly denied. CAPTURED FAILURE (e2e.txt line 27, OIDC discovery conformance): 'error granting ClusterRoleBinding svcaccounts-2092-system:service-account-issuer-discovery: cannot escalate privileges: user does not hold all rules of the referenced ClusterRole'. title: conformance VM stack (NOT lima-node) leaves pods Pending: scheduler/kubelet/konnectivity setup issue on lima-node-2
description:
CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE (scout + mayor-verified in source). Two independent bugs in the conformance scripts, both of which ONLY bite non-default --workdir/--port runs (every worker run used the default temp/u7s, which is why they all worked):

BUG 1 (PRIMARY — causes the Pending hang): run-all.sh:137 invokes 'bash 05-start-scheduler.sh' with NO args — every sibling step (lines 101/116/128/133/143) passes ${_WORKDIR_ARG}; line 137 is the sole exception. 05-start-scheduler.sh defaults WORKDIR to $PWD/temp/u7s, so with --workdir ./temp/u7s-baseline the scheduler connected to temp/u7s/kubeconfig (the mayor/smoke cluster), NEVER the lima-node-2 apiserver at 6445 → no scheduler watching that cluster → sonobuoy aggregator stuck PodScheduled:False forever. SIDE-EFFECT (scout residual #2): 05-start-scheduler.sh scopes its pkill to u7s-scheduler.*${WORKDIR}/kubeconfig with WORKDIR defaulting to temp/u7s — so a non-default-workdir run's scheduler-start would KILL the mayor's running scheduler (the hung baseline likely disrupted the mayor stack).

BUG 2 (SECONDARY — independent, breaks exec/logs/attach but NOT scheduling): u7s-start.sh:108 hardcodes KONNECTIVITY_PROXY_PORT default to 8135. A non-default run that omits --konnectivity-server-port collides with the mayor's 8135; the 'nc -z 8135' guard (u7s-start.sh:247) then SKIPS the whole konnectivity+apiserver-restart block, so that stack runs with no konnectivity proxy. Benign for scheduling (smoke runs proved it) but breaks exec/logs.

FIX (operator-approved, ONE worker): (1) run-all.sh:137 → 'bash 05-start-scheduler.sh ${_WORKDIR_ARG}' (05-start-scheduler.sh already accepts --workdir). (2) Auto-derive konnectivity port in u7s-start.sh:108 AND lima-start.sh:60: if no override, KONNECTIVITY_PROXY_PORT = 8135 + (PORT-6443)*100 (so 6444→8235, 6445→8335). (3) Add a konnectivity column to the VM-slots tables in dispatch-prompt-template.md + ai/dashboard.md. NOT 'non-default VMs are broken' — it's a workdir-propagation + port-default bug.

title: fix(apiserver): named-targetPort Service yields EndpointSlice with empty/protocol:'' ports — controller can't build slice ports
notes:
Scoped via targeted --focus (run 0626-1632) + kubectl repro on current main (lima-node). The standing lesson: root-caused before filing. This is the GROUP A (controller-populated) endpointslice gap — SEPARATE from mayor-6ipr (Group B, the proto-decode 'invalid JSON' on EndpointSlice CREATE).

GOOD NEWS FIRST: the endpointslice-controller IS now running (the --controllers='*' change in 1a437ce9 enabled it). The failing slice is correctly managed-by endpointslice-controller.k8s.io with both pod endpoints, conditions, targetRef, nodeName. So the controller works; this is a narrower port-resolution bug.

TEST: [sig-network] EndpointSlice 'should create Endpoints and EndpointSlices for Pods matching a Service' (endpointslice.go:144). FAILS (122s) at endpointslice.go:809: 'Expected at least 2 EndpointSlices for Service .../example-named-port, got 1'. The single slice it did produce has "ports":[] (EMPTY).

THE TEST (endpointslice.go:217-228): creates Service 'example-named-port' with Ports:[{Name:http, Port:80, TargetPort: intstr.FromString(\"example-name\"), Protocol:TCP}] — a NAMED targetPort. The assertion helper hasMatchingEndpointSlices (line ~723) requires len(endpointSlice.Ports) == len(svc.Spec.Ports). Our slice has 0 ports vs the service's 1 -> fail. The endpointslice controller resolves a NAMED targetPort by matching it against the pod's container port NAMES; if that resolution yields nothing, the slice gets empty ports.

KUBECTL REPRO (mayor, lima-node, 2026-06-26T~07:1xZ): pod with named containerPort {name:http,containerPort:80}; Service {port:80, targetPort: 'http'} (named). Result: ONE slice produced (count ok for single-port), BUT its port is {"name":"http","port":80,"protocol":""} — protocol is EMPTY STRING, should be "TCP". So the port IS partially built but protocol defaulting is missing, and for the test's intstr.FromString('example-name') targetPort the resolution apparently yields an empty ports list entirely.

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE (apiserver, NOT the external controller):
- Service .spec.ports protocol is not defaulted to TCP when omitted (the slice port shows protocol:'' — Service write-time defaulting gap). AND/OR
- named targetPort resolution: the endpointslice controller needs the pod's container ports (name->number) AND the Service port's protocol to build slice ports. proto Container.ports DOES decode name/containerPort/protocol (proto.rs:775 ContainerPort has all fields), so the decode side looks intact — suspect the EMIT side (proto.rs:~2913 where spec ports serialize) OR Service-port defaulting OR how the apiserver serves the pod's ports to the controller.

INVESTIGATE (worker, VM + verbose):
1. Repro the EXACT test shape: pod with a named container port 'example-name', Service example-named-port with targetPort: 'example-name', protocol omitted. Observe the produced slice's ports.
2. Check each layer: (a) does GET on the Service show .spec.ports[].protocol defaulted to TCP? (b) does GET on the pod show .spec.containers[].ports[] with the name intact (name 'example-name')? (c) does the slice the controller builds have the resolved port? Find which layer drops/empties the port info.
3. Most likely fixes: Service write-time port defaulting (protocol=TCP when absent) in the Service create/update handler; and/or pod container-port emit on the proto round-trip. Compare proto.rs:2913 emit vs the ContainerPort struct.

ACCEPTANCE: (a) kubectl repro: a named-targetPort Service yields a slice whose ports match the Service ports (name+protocol=TCP+resolved number), not protocol:''/empty; (b) sonobuoy --focus 'should create Endpoints and EndpointSlices for Pods matching a Service' PASS (EXTRACT e2e.txt before worktree cleanup). Surface: Service port defaulting handler and/or proto.rs port emit. Needs VM.

NOTE: also re-baseline the OTHER Group A specs (multiport endpoints, multiple-EndpointSlices specs) after this fix — they likely share the named-port/protocol root cause. Do NOT conflate with 6ipr (Group B proto CREATE).
close_reason: PR #610 opened — fixed two defaulting layers: Service port protocol and Pod containerPort protocol. Named-targetPort EndpointSlice now produces correct ports. sonobuoy --focus passes 20/20.

title: fix(proto): EndpointSlice API-operations create fails 'invalid JSON' — decoder returns None on typed-client payload
notes:
Scoped via targeted --focus on current main (run 0626-1608, lima-node) — the standing lesson: root-cause before filing.

TEST: [sig-network] EndpointSlice "should support creating EndpointSlice API operations" (network/endpointslice.go). Pure apiserver CRUD — NO pod/controller dependency. Fails in ~1s, deterministic.

FAILURE (e2e.txt, run 0626-1608): at the 'creating' step (endpointslice.go:348) the apiserver returns 'invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1'. This is the EXACT proto-decode-gap signature fixed 5x this session (#596 CSIDriver, #600 runtimeClassName, #597 Service status, #605 enableServiceLinks): the typed Go client POSTs Content-Type: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf; the apiserver fails to decode it and tries to parse protobuf bytes as JSON -> column-1 error.

WRINKLE — NOT a missing decoder: crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs:6799 ALREADY has decode_endpointslice_proto (added #577), registered at proto.rs:7268 ('EndpointSlice' => decode_endpointslice_proto). The struct (proto.rs:6784) decodes metadata(1), addressType(2), endpoints(3), ports(4). So the 'invalid JSON' means EndpointSlice::decode(data) is returning None (the .ok()? bails) on THIS test's payload, OR the body never reaches this decoder (content-type/dispatch routing).

INVESTIGATE (worker, VM + verbose log):
1. Capture the actual protobuf body the test POSTs (RUST_LOG=debug via --verbose; the apiserver should log the decode attempt).
2. Determine WHICH: (a) decode_endpointslice_proto returns None -> the test sends a field/shape the struct doesn't handle (e.g. a field at a tag we don't decode that makes prost fail? unlikely — prost ignores unknown tags; more likely a nested message shape mismatch in DiscoveryEndpoint/EndpointConditions/ports). OR (b) the request isn't routed to decode_proto_by_kind for EndpointSlice at all (the create handler's extract_body / kind dispatch — check the discovery.k8s.io/v1 endpointslices route wiring vs how kind is resolved). The log line 'getting /apis/discovery.k8s.iov1' suggests discovery works; the CREATE path is the suspect.
3. Compare with a WORKING proto create on current main (e.g. a CSIDriver or Service create via typed client) to see what differs for EndpointSlice.

FIX whatever the repro shows (likely: extend the EndpointSlice proto struct/nested types to handle the test's payload, OR fix the kind dispatch for discovery.k8s.io/v1 EndpointSlice). Same pattern as the prior proto fixes.

ACCEPTANCE: (a) unit test — the test's EndpointSlice payload round-trips through decode (fails on revert); (b) kubectl/typed repro: creating an EndpointSlice via protobuf succeeds (was 'invalid JSON'); (c) sonobuoy --focus 'should support creating EndpointSlice API operations' PASS (e2e.txt — EXTRACT it before worktree cleanup). Surface: proto.rs (+ maybe the discovery.k8s.io create routing). Needs VM.

CONTEXT: this is the pure-apiserver slice (Group B) of the endpointslice frontier. Group A (controller-populates-slices-for-pods specs: 'should create Endpoints and EndpointSlices for Pods matching a Service' etc.) is SEPARATE — may have improved since the endpointslice-controller was enabled in 1a437ce9 (the --controllers='*' change); re-baseline Group A in a later run, do NOT conflate with this bead.

title: decide+enable missing KCM controllers (pod-gc, ttl-after-finished, pv-*) OR switch to default set with exclusions
notes:
Found during mayor-khgv / PR #607. The KCM --controllers allowlist (scripts/conformance/04-start-kcm.sh:109) was hand-curated and missing 'disruption' (fixed #607). The worker spotted 8 MORE standard kube-controller-manager controllers absent from the list. This bead is to DECIDE which to enable for this setup (single static node, no cloud provider) and add the appropriate ones — NOT a blind add-all.

Current list (post-#607): csrapproving, csrsigning, garbagecollector, deployment, replicaset, root-ca-cert-publisher, endpoints-controller, endpointslice-controller, endpointslice-mirroring-controller, namespace, serviceaccount, daemonset, resourcequota, statefulset, job, cronjob, horizontalpodautoscaling, disruption.

ABSENT (worker-spotted) + mayor's tiering for a single-node/no-cloud cluster:

LIKELY-WANTED (conformance-relevant, apply to our setup):
- pod-garbage-collector — GCs pods in terminating/failed states; conformance pod-lifecycle + node tests rely on it. HIGH value.
- ttl-after-finished — deletes completed Jobs after .spec.ttlSecondsAfterFinished; Job conformance tests use it. HIGH value.
- persistentvolume-binder — binds PVCs to PVs; any storage conformance that creates a PVC needs it. Check if storage specs are in scope.
- persistentvolumeclaim-protection (and pv protection) — finalizer protection so in-use PVCs/PVs aren't deleted; storage conformance. MED.
- persistentvolume-expander — PVC resize; only if volume-expansion specs are in scope. MED/LOW.

PROBABLY-NOT (need infra we don't have):
- node-lifecycle — manages node taints/eviction on NotReady; with a single static always-Ready node this may be unnecessary or even cause unwanted eviction behavior. Evaluate carefully.
- service-lb-controller — LoadBalancer Services need a cloud provider; we have none. SKIP unless a stub is wanted.
- ttl (the legacy node-TTL controller) — largely deprecated/no-op in modern clusters. SKIP.

ACTION: decide per-controller (operator input useful for the storage ones — depends whether storage conformance is a goal). Add the wanted ones to 04-start-kcm.sh:109. Verify each enabled controller does something sane via kubectl (e.g. pod-garbage-collector: a failed pod gets GC'd; ttl-after-finished: a Job with ttlSecondsAfterFinished:0 is deleted after completion). Script-only; verify on a VM. Consider also whether the list should instead use the kube-controller-manager DEFAULT set (--controllers='*,-<the ones we explicitly don't want>') rather than an explicit allowlist that keeps drifting out of date — that's the more maintainable pattern and would have avoided BOTH the disruption gap and this one. Surface that as the real recommendation.
