title: fix(apiserver): webhook pod never Ready — container Killed + contradictory pod condition (status=True reason=ContainersNotReady)
notes:
Re-triaged from conformance-triage-2026-06-25 DEFER list (Cluster D). The original "agnhost webhook image is slow / env timing" guess is WRONG — verified via targeted --focus on current main (run 0626-1407, lima-node).

TEST: [sig-api-machinery] AdmissionWebhook "should be able to deny custom resource creation, update and deletion" — fails in BeforeEach (webhook.go:220) after 33s: "waiting for webhook configuration to be ready" never succeeds. (The whole AdmissionWebhook suite shares this setup, so this likely blocks ~all webhook specs.)

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS (e2e.txt, run 0626-1407, UTC 2026-06-26T05:06-05:07):
- sample-webhook-deployment pod: image Pulled OK, Container Created OK, Container Started OK — so NOT an image/env problem.
- Then: "Killing: Stopping container sample-webhook" — the container is killed shortly after starting.
- Readiness probe fails: Get https://10.85.0.19:8444/readyz: dial tcp 10.85.0.19:8444: connect: connection refused (because the container is gone).
- Pod conditions are SELF-CONTRADICTORY (resource.go:158):
    Ready: status=True reason=ContainersNotReady "containers with unready status: [sample-webhook]"
    ContainersReady: status=True reason=ContainersNotReady
  A Ready=True condition must NOT carry reason=ContainersNotReady. status and reason disagree.

ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESES (investigate-first — do NOT assume):
1. Our pod-status handling produces inconsistent condition status vs reason (status=True with a not-ready reason). If the apiserver is merging/defaulting pod status conditions wrong, the kubelet's real "not ready" gets a True status, OR our status write clobbers the kubelet's update. This is the most apiserver-shaped lead. Check how pod /status PATCH/PUT from the kubelet is merged (compare with the Service status fix #597 and finalizer/status-merge work #590).
2. Why is the container Killed right after Started? Could be the kubelet restarting it due to the failing readiness/liveness probe, OR a pod-spec field we mis-decode causing the kubelet to recreate. Check the kubelet log (/tmp/kcm.log is KCM; need kubelet log on the VM) for the kill reason.
3. The readiness probe connection-refused is to the POD IP directly (kubelet-local), not via konnectivity — so probably a consequence (container down), not the cause.

START HERE: reproduce with kubectl on a VM — create a Deployment whose container serves HTTPS on a port with a readiness probe (mirror sample-webhook), watch the pod: does the container get Killed? Are the Ready/ContainersReady condition status+reason consistent? Inspect the kubelet log on the VM for the Killing reason. Pin the root cause BEFORE writing a fix. The contradictory condition (status=True + reason=ContainersNotReady) is the sharpest lead and is almost certainly ours.

SCOPE: likely apiserver pod-status condition handling (+ maybe a pod-spec decode field affecting the kubelet). Could be medium-sized. If the repro shows it's purely kubelet-internal (not reproducible via our status path), report and re-defer with evidence. Needs VM.

ACCEPTANCE: kubectl repro shows a probe-gated pod reaching consistent Ready=True/reason="" (no contradiction) and container not killed; then --focus '\[sig-api-machinery\] AdmissionWebhook' setup succeeds (or at least the target deny test passes BeforeEach).
close_reason: PR #608 opened — fix confirmed: kubelet sends reason:null (not absent) on condition status change; merge_conditions treated null key as present, skipping stale-reason clear; contradictory Ready=True+reason=ContainersNotReady is gone after fix; remaining webhook test failures are pre-existing endpoint slice issue (separate from this bead)

title: fix(apiserver): kubectl create/apply fails default validation — OpenAPI v3 schema fetch returns invalid proto
notes:
Found 2026-06-26T04:51Z (kubectl repro, lima-node) while verifying mayor-8hzp.

SYMPTOM: `kubectl create -f job.yaml` and `kubectl apply -f job.yaml` FAIL by default with:
  error validating data: proto: cannot parse invalid wire-format data; if you choose to ignore these errors, turn validation off with --validate=false
Reproduced on a minimal batch/v1 Job (both create and apply; --validate=false bypasses it and the object is created fine). So it is the CLIENT-SIDE VALIDATION path, not the create handler.

ROOT CAUSE: kubectl validation fetches the OpenAPI schema for the GVK. Our OpenAPI endpoints are empty stubs:
  GET /openapi/v2 -> {"definitions":{},"info":{...}}   (empty definitions)
  GET /openapi/v3 -> {"paths":{}}                        (empty paths)
kubectl 1.3x uses OpenAPI v3 by default; the per-GVK v3 schema fetch returns something that decodes as invalid proto wire-format, so kubectl aborts validation with the error above for EVERY resource (not just Job — Job is just what surfaced it).

IMPACT: any user doing plain `kubectl create/apply` (the most common workflow) hits this unless they pass --validate=false. This is worse than "validation is lax" — it's a hard failure on the default path. Likely also affects some conformance/e2e flows that create via kubectl with validation.

RELATION: mayor-52wo (deferred) is "embed upstream kube OpenAPI v2 spec as static blob" — that would populate /openapi/v2. But the ACTIVE failure is the v3 path returning invalid proto. Two sub-parts:
  (a) why does the v3 (or v2) schema fetch return INVALID PROTO rather than empty-but-valid? An empty-but-valid schema should make kubectl skip/relax validation, not error. Find the openapi v3 handler (grep openapi / v3 in handlers) and see what it serves for a per-GVK schema request and its content-type. Returning a proper (even if minimal) response, or a correct content-type, may stop the proto parse error.
  (b) longer-term, populate real schemas (52wo).

SCOPE THIS BEAD to (a) — make `kubectl create/apply` of a core/batch resource succeed with default validation (no --validate=false needed). VERIFY: kubectl create -f a Job/Pod/Deployment WITHOUT --validate=false succeeds. Investigate-first (find the openapi v3 per-GVK handler and what it returns); the fix may be small (content-type / empty-but-valid schema) or may need 52wo — report which.
close_reason: DUPLICATE of mayor-52wo (verified-redundant). Operator correctly flagged my mis-framing: we DO serve OpenAPI for CRDs (openapi_v3 + openapi_v3_group in discovery.rs:1382/1416, dynamically from the CRD registry; tests at discovery.rs:3074/3358/3389). The kubectl create/apply validation failure on a Job is because we serve OpenAPI ONLY for CRDs, NOT built-in types — /openapi/v3/apis/batch/v1 returns 404 (verified 2026-06-26T04:52Z), so kubectl can't find the Job schema and errors. That is exactly the gap mayor-52wo addresses ('Enables kubectl --validate for core types'). Evidence folded into 52wo. Not a separate content-type/proto bug.

title: fix(apiserver): pod.metadata.generation should be 1 after create, not 2 (node/pods.go:530)
notes:
Dropped scope from mayor-jgwx. That bead bundled QOS class (fixed, PR #600) AND 'investigate pod.metadata.generation starting at 2 not 1'. The PR #600 worker fixed QOS, verified sonobuoy 21/21, and CLOSED jgwx — but did NOT address generation and did NOT split it (Rule 12 miss: closed with half the scope undone). Re-filing so it isn't lost.

Symptom (run 0625-2158, node/pods.go:530, 'should support pod readiness gates' or similar): pod.metadata.generation is 2 after create; the test expects 1 after create (and 2 after a subsequent spec update). Pods ARE generation-tracked in modern k8s (generation increments on spec change), but a freshly created pod must have generation=1, not 2.

Likely cause: our create path increments generation twice — once on initial store write and again via an update/defaulting pass (the same apply_pod_create_defaults / status-set path PR #600 touched may be doing a second write that bumps generation). Investigate: Grep generation handling in handlers/pods.rs create path + the store put path. A pod create should set generation=1 exactly once. Watch for: do we write the pod, then write it AGAIN to set status.qosClass/overhead (PR #600 added status mutation at create)? If so, the second write may be incrementing generation — meaning PR #600 could have made this WORSE. Check generation after a plain create on current main first.

Acceptance: kubectl create a pod, GET it, confirm metadata.generation==1. Then patch its spec, confirm generation==2. Regression test on the create path. cargo + the node/pods.go:530 spec via --focus.
close_reason: VERIFIED-REDUNDANT on current main (kubectl repro 2026-06-26T04:49Z, lima-node). Created a pod: .metadata.generation=1 on create, =2 after a spec patch — exactly what node/pods.go:530 ('pod generation should start at 1 and increment per update') asserts. title: infra: parameterize konnectivity ports per-worker (8135/8132/8133/8134 hard-coded blocks parallel VM verification)
notes:
Surfaced during mayor-52fb / PR #603: the worker could not run its sonobuoy gate because konnectivity-server ports collide. The mayor's konnectivity-server (proxy-server-darwin-arm64) binds fixed ports --server-port=8135, --agent-port=8132, --admin-port=8133, --health-port=8134 on 127.0.0.1. Unlike the apiserver --port and --kubelet-port (which the dispatch protocol assigns per worker: 6444/10251, 6445/10252, ...), the konnectivity ports are HARD-CODED in the startup script. So a second stack (a worker's worktree) cannot stand up its own konnectivity — it collides with the mayor's on 8135 et al.

Impact: any worker fixing a konnectivity-path handler (pod proxy/log/exec — the /pods/{p}/proxy and /pods/{p}/log subresources) CANNOT run a sonobuoy/kubectl gate that exercises the tunnel, because it can't bring up an isolated konnectivity-server. PR #603 (proxy https fix) merged with kubectl 'no-longer-hangs' evidence but NO end-to-end proxy-returns-200 proof for exactly this reason.

Fix: parameterize the konnectivity ports (server/agent/admin/health) the same way --port/--kubelet-port are, with a per-slot assignment table (e.g. slot1: 8235/8232/8233/8234, slot2: 8335/..., etc.), threaded through run-all.sh and the konnectivity startup script and the apiserver's --konnectivity proxy addr. Then parallel workers can each run a full konnectivity stack. Find the startup script (grep server-port=8135 in scripts/) and the apiserver flag that points at the konnectivity proxy addr.

Until fixed: konnectivity-path beads must serialize on the mayor's stack or the operator runs their --focus manually (as for #603).
close_reason: PR #613 opened — konnectivity ports parameterized per-slot (8135+N*100), mayor default unchanged, slot1 verified on lima-node-smoke

title: feat(apiserver): in-place pod resize — /pods/{name}/resize subresource updates container cgroup limits
notes:
Found correcting the hang-investigation mislabel. Run 0625-2158 e2e.txt: common/node/pod_resize.go specs fail because after a resize, the container cgroup shows PRE-resize values: e.g. /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max was 36700160 (35Mi), test expected 41943040 (40Mi); cpu.max was '2000 100000', expected '2500 100000'. Also container status allocatedResources/resources still show old cpu/memory.

This is the InPlacePodVerticalScaling feature (DeclaredFeatures includes InPlacePodLevelResourcesVerticalScaling). The apiserver must support the pods/resize subresource and persist updated resources so the kubelet applies them to the cgroup. This is a LARGER feature, not a one-liner — likely needs: the resize subresource handler, status.resize tracking, and allocatedResources status. Scope/spike before dispatching. Multiple pod_resize.go specs each burn ~hundreds of seconds waiting for the resize that never lands. NOT a kubelet bug — kubelet applies what we persist; we don't persist the resize.

Defer until the QOS/defaulting cluster lands and we have a full-run baseline to see how many resize specs exist.
close_reason: SPIKE complete (ai/findings/0629-inplace-resize-spike.md). MAJOR REFRAME: in-place resize is MOSTLY ALREADY IMPLEMENTED — the /pods/{name}/resize route (main.rs:441) + patch_pod_resize handler (pods.rs:1751, persists container resources + sets status.resize='Proposed') + 3 unit tests already exist. The headline blocker for the resize CONFORMANCE specs was node-cap saturation, now fixed by #617. Remaining gaps are SMALL: (1) patch_pod_resize doesn't bump metadata.generation; (2) pods/resize not advertised in /api/v1 discovery (V1_RESOURCES, types.rs). Two CONDITIONAL gaps (kubelet allocatedResources synthesis; PodResizePending/InProgress conditions) should NOT be pre-built — only if a focused run shows they're needed. Kubelet v1.36.2 DOES advertise+apply in-place resize, so persisting spec.resources should suffice. Split into the 2 small fix beads below; the conditional ones wait on a focused-run.

title: fix(util): secs_to_rfc3339/days_to_ymd off-by-one for some dates after a leap year
notes:
Found during mayor-o67l / PR #599. crate::util::secs_to_rfc3339 (via days_to_ymd) computes the wrong calendar date for certain dates after a leap year within a 4-year block — e.g. 2001-09-09 decodes as 2001-09-10 (off by one day). This affects EVERY timestamp the apiserver emits from a proto/unix-seconds source: creationTimestamp, lastTransitionTime, managedFields times, etc. A wrong creationTimestamp/RFC3339 string could fail client-side validation or break tests that compare timestamps.

Repro: call crate::util::secs_to_rfc3339 with the unix seconds for 2001-09-09T00:00:00Z and observe it returns 2001-09-10. Root cause is in the day-count -> Y/M/D conversion (days_to_ymd) leap-year handling. Fix the date arithmetic and add a table-driven test covering: a leap day (Feb 29), Mar 1 of a leap year, dates just after a leap year (the failing case), year boundaries, and a few known epoch values. The existing util.rs tests use values that happen to land on correct dates, masking the bug — the new test must include a date that currently fails.

Scope: crates/apiserver/src/util.rs only. cargo-testable, no VM. Do NOT change callers — just fix the conversion so all existing call sites become correct.

title: fix(apiserver): inject RuntimeClass overhead into pod.spec.overhead at admission time
notes: Root cause: common/node/runtimeclass.go:153 creates a RuntimeClass with cpu overhead 10m, then creates a pod using that RuntimeClass and expects pod.spec.overhead.cpu to equal 10m. title: fix(apiserver): return 406 for all unsupported Table Accept headers, not just some code paths
notes:
CORRECTED ROOT CAUSE (PR #598 closed — it fixed the wrong path: unsupported table VERSION on LIST handlers, but the test uses v=v1 on a dedicated POST handler).

Source-confirmed (temp/research/table_conversion.go:154, ConformanceIt 'should return a 406 for a backend which does not implement metadata'):
- The test POSTs a SelfSubjectAccessReview to /apis/authorization.k8s.io/v1/selfsubjectaccessreviews with header Accept: application/json;as=Table;v=v1;g=meta.k8s.io
- Line 168: expects err.(APIStatus).Status().Code == 406.
- It expects 406 because selfsubjectaccessreviews is a 'backend which does not implement metadata' (no Table conversion). The VERSION is v1 (supported); the point is the RESOURCE has no table form.

WHY #598 missed it: selfsubjectaccessreviews is a dedicated route (main.rs:537 -> handlers::authorization::self_subject_access_review, a POST handler). It does NOT route through list_resource/list_namespaced_resource. The authorization handler currently ignores the Accept header entirely and returns its object as JSON regardless.

CORRECT FIX: when a request's Accept demands Table (as=Table) and the target handler/resource has no Table conversion, return 406 Not Acceptable. At minimum self_subject_access_review (handlers/authorization.rs:64) must do this. PREFER a shared choke point if one exists cleanly (so subjectaccessreviews, tokenreviews, and other non-Table handlers are also correct) — but do not over-engineer; if no clean choke point, fix the specific handler the test needs and note the rest. Reuse super::table::wants_table / table_accept_version and Status::not_acceptable (already exist).

ACCEPTANCE GATE: kubectl repro — POST a SelfSubjectAccessReview with Accept 'application/json;as=Table;v=v1;g=meta.k8s.io' and confirm HTTP 406 (before: 200/other). Plus sonobuoy --focus 'should return a 406 for a backend which does not implement metadata' PASS.

close_reason: PR #592 opened: watch NDJSON emission reduced to 1 allocation via to_writer helpers; byte-identity tests pass

title: audit: verify metadata-only proto decoders do not silently drop spec for types sent via proto
description: Cluster 5 from duplication-audit-2026-06-25. decode_serviceaccount_proto (proto.rs:4614), decode_persistentvolumeclaim_proto (4625), decode_storageclass_proto (4720), decode_volumeattributesclass_proto (4731) decode only metadata — same pattern as Job template before the #583 fix. If any of these types are ever written via proto, spec is silently dropped and the caller receives 200 OK with a spec-less object. Audit whether kubectl sends these via proto and add spec decoding for any that are at risk.
close_reason: PR #594 opened: verified all 5 suspect decoders drop meaningful fields via proto; fixed ServiceAccount (imagePullSecrets/secrets/automountServiceAccountToken), PVC (spec), StorageClass (provisioner/parameters/reclaimPolicy/etc), VolumeAttributesClass (driverName/parameters), RC (template/containers). One round-trip regression test per type. cargo test: 1683 passed, clippy clean.

title: perf: use prepare_cached in store query_all to avoid SQL re-compilation per list (F5)
description:
query_all in crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:436 calls conn.prepare(sql) which does not cache the compiled statement. Every list operation re-parses and re-compiles the SQL. rusqlite's prepare_cached is an LRU cache with 8 slots per connection — sufficient to cover all list_sync SQL variants.

## Context
Audit finding F5 from ai/findings/perf-audit-2026-06-25.md. File:line = crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:436. Hot-path: YES (every LIST). Impact: MEDIUM. One-line fix.
acceptance_criteria: query_all uses conn.prepare_cached instead of conn.prepare. Existing list tests pass.
close_reason: PR #591 opened: prepare_cached in query_all

title: cleanup: de-duplicate rbac_cluster_key / rbac_namespaced_key between resource.rs and generic.rs
description: Cluster 2 from duplication-audit-2026-06-25. rbac_cluster_key and rbac_namespaced_key are defined identically in both resource.rs (prod, lines 2003+2534) and generic.rs (test-only, lines 545+550). If the key format changes the test copies diverge silently. Fix: make the resource.rs functions pub(crate) and remove the test-only copies from generic.rs.
close_reason: PR #593 opened: de-duplicated rbac_cluster_key/rbac_namespaced_key to single pub(crate) definition in resource.rs

title: fix: promote merge_incoming_metadata to shared helper and add finalizer protection to all status PUT paths
description: Cluster 1 from duplication-audit-2026-06-25. Five copies of identity-field-preservation in status write paths. apply_status_patch (PATCH) protects finalizers+deletionTimestamp but all PUT paths do not, creating a potential livelock for controllers that PUT status on resources with finalizers.
close_reason: PR #590 opened: consolidates merge_incoming_metadata to 8-field helper with finalizer+deletionTimestamp protection; all 4 inline PUT copies replaced; per-path regression tests added; cargo test+clippy green

title: perf: bound deletion_log to prevent unbounded memory growth (F3)
description:
SqliteStore.deletion_log (crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:31,119-122) is an unbounded HashMap<String, Arc<InternalEvent>> that grows with one entry per unique deleted key and is never evicted. Over a long conformance run with namespace lifecycle churn, this retains full object bodies (pod specs, etc.) indefinitely. No pruning occurs even after re-create.

## Context
Audit finding F3 from ai/findings/perf-audit-2026-06-25.md. File:line = crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:31,119-122. Hot-path: YES (write path for inserts, read on compaction replay). Impact: HIGH. Most likely contributor to RSS growth in bench-rss CI checks.
acceptance_criteria: deletion_log is bounded. Entries are evicted when the key is re-created (PUT succeeds) or the map exceeds 2*RING_CAPACITY entries (evict oldest by revision). Regression test verifies deletion_log does not grow past the cap after repeated create/delete cycles.
close_reason: PR #591 opened: bound deletion_log with evict-on-recreate + cap at 2xRING_CAPACITY

title: perf: pre-serialize watch events at broadcast time to eliminate per-watcher deserialize (F2)
description:
Each live watch event in watch_generic (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs:507-534) independently deserializes the event bytes, applies defaults, and re-serializes to NDJSON. With N active watchers for the same resource prefix, this is N full serde_json parse+serialize cycles per write. Event bytes are shared via Arc<InternalEvent> but the deserialized form is not.

## Context
Audit finding F2 from ai/findings/perf-audit-2026-06-25.md. File:line = crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs:507-534. Hot-path: YES (every ADDED/MODIFIED event, multiplied by watcher count). Impact: HIGH. This is the highest-fanout hot path.
acceptance_criteria: Watch events are serialized to NDJSON bytes once per event (not once per watcher). All N watchers share the same pre-built bytes. Label/field selector filtering still works (lazy deserialize only when selector is present).
close_reason: PR #592 opened: prepare_live_event() extracts parse-once-filter-serialize with tests for two-watcher identity and selector filtering

title: perf: fix double JSON parse in store put_sync (F1)
description:
put_sync in crates/store/src/sqlite.rs calls stamp_resource_version (full deserialize+reserialize) then immediately deserializes the stamped value again to extract metadata.namespace and metadata.name for indexed columns. This is two full serde_json round-trips per write on the blocking thread.

## Context
Audit finding F1 from ai/findings/perf-audit-2026-06-25.md. File:line = crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:183-262. Hot-path: YES (every PUT). Impact: HIGH.
acceptance_criteria: put_sync extracts ns/obj_name from the original or stamped value without a second full deserialization cycle. Regression test verifies ns and obj_name are correctly set after a put.
close_reason: PR #591 opened: eliminate double JSON parse in put_sync

title: store: KCM RS controller stale-read requeueing under high write bursts
description:
KCM logs show persistent 'read version N is not as new as written version M' errors for the ReplicaSet controller, causing unnecessary requeueing. Root cause hypothesis: wal_autocheckpoint=1000 (sqlite.rs:168) causes the WAL read connection to lag behind the write connection under high write bursts during conformance runs.

Evidence: KCM kcm.log shows RS controller stale-read requeueing throughout the run. The stale-read guard exists in both get() (sqlite.rs:756-769) and list() (sqlite.rs:788-798) but the checkpoint threshold may be too high, causing prolonged lag under sustained write pressure.

Investigate: (1) lower wal_autocheckpoint threshold or switch to PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE) on writes, (2) measure how often the stale-read guard triggers vs how often it successfully retries, (3) check whether requeueing rate correlates with write burst size during conformance.

This does not cause object deletion (KCM GC not implicated in any test failure) but does cause unnecessary controller churn and may mask real failures by introducing spurious reconciliation noise.
notes: PR #574 open — wal_autocheckpoint 1000→100, regression test added. CI in progress.
close_reason: fixed: PR #574 merged — wal_autocheckpoint lowered 1000→100, regression test added

title: apiserver: EndpointSlice POST returns HTTP 400 invalid JSON — request body not decoded
description:
Test: [sig-network] EndpointSlice [It] should support creating EndpointSlice API operations [Conformance]

Failure: failed in 40ms at STEP: creating — 'HTTP 400 BadRequest: invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1'

When the test POSTs a new EndpointSlice to discovery.k8s.io/v1, u7s returns HTTP 400 with 'invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1'. This indicates the request body is being read as empty or the handler for this group/resource is returning an error before parsing the body.

The namespace was not reaped — this is a genuine u7s bug. Investigate the EndpointSlice create handler in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/ for the discovery.k8s.io group.
close_reason: fixed: PR #577 merged — regression tests for EndpointSlice POST proto decode (fix was already in #565)

title: apiserver: kubectl validation fails — openapi/v2 or v3 endpoint returns wrong Content-Type
description:
Test: [sig-cli] Kubectl client Kubectl label [BeforeEach] should update the label on a resource [Conformance]

Failure: kubectl create -f - exits immediately (64ms) with: 'error validating data: the server was unable to respond with a content type that the client supports'

kubectl sends a schema-fetch request to /openapi/v2 or /openapi/v3 for server-side validation before creating resources. u7s returns a response with an unexpected or missing Content-Type header, causing kubectl to reject it and abort resource creation. The BeforeEach failure means the entire test fails before any assertions run.

Investigate: what does GET /openapi/v2 and GET /openapi/v3 return from u7s? Check Content-Type header and response body. Kubectl expects application/com.github.proto-openapi.spec.v2@v1.0+protobuf or application/json with correct schema content.
close_reason: fixed: PR #575 merged — removed 406 on /openapi/v2, added /openapi/ passthrough in ContentTypeLayer

title: apiserver: MutatingWebhookConfiguration not intercepting creates — AdmissionWebhook timeout test fails
description:
Test: [sig-api-machinery] AdmissionWebhook [Privileged:ClusterAdmin] [It] should honor timeout [Conformance]

Failure: 'waiting for webhook configuration to be ready: timed out waiting for the condition' after 33s. The test registers a MutatingWebhookConfiguration with a 1s timeout (slower than the 5s webhook latency). The readiness probe works by creating a sentinel object and expecting a webhook-injected annotation — that annotation never appeared.

Root cause: u7s either (1) does not route create requests through registered MutatingWebhookConfigurations, or (2) does not enforce webhook timeout semantics, or (3) the admission webhook dispatch loop is not implemented.

The namespace was not reaped — this is a genuine u7s bug. The test failed at 21:21:08 UTC, ~2.5h before the watchdog reaped its namespace.
close_reason: fixed: PR #576 merged — konnectivity proxy now applied regardless of caBundle presence; regression test added

title: conformance: run logrotate hourly to cap syslog mid-run
description:
The size 2G trigger in /etc/logrotate.d/rsyslog (added in #571) is only checked when the logrotate systemd timer fires — currently daily at midnight. A 10-hour conformance run starting at 00:39 generates ~2GB/hour, hitting 20GB before the next midnight check. The run is evicted by the kubelet at ~10h due to ephemeral storage exhaustion.

Fix: change the logrotate timer to run hourly (or every 2 hours) inside the VM, OR call logrotate --force from the watchdog loop in scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh periodically. Also verify that the size 2G configuration written by lima-start.sh actually took effect in the VM (the earlier fix was applied to the provisioning script but the current VM was reset since — confirm the drop-in is present post-reset).

Preferred fix: add a systemd timer override in lima-start.sh that runs logrotate every 2 hours, alongside the existing size 2G config. This is self-contained in the provisioning script and does not require changes to the run script.
close_reason: fixed in PR #573

title: conformance: VM syslog grows to 12GB per run due to CRI-O info verbosity
description:
During a 6-hour --reset conformance run, /var/log/syslog grows to ~12GB. Root cause: CRI-O runs at default info log level, emitting ~40M lines per run (pod sandbox stop/start/CNI check events). logrotate is functional but runs daily via systemd timer — it fires once per 24h, too infrequent to cap mid-run growth. The --reset path (reset.sh) deletes the VM entirely, so logrotate never accumulates history across runs either.

Investigated options:
- CONTAINER_LOG_LEVEL=warn: eliminates 90% of volume but blinds CRI-O debugging
- size limit in logrotate config + higher trigger frequency: preserves full logs, caps disk impact

Fix scope: find the VM provisioning path in run-all.sh or the Lima template; add a size-based logrotate trigger (e.g. size 2G, rotate 2) to /etc/logrotate.d/rsyslog so rotation happens mid-run. Optionally also invoke logrotate --force at VM start to ensure clean slate. Do NOT suppress CRI-O log level — we need full logs for active debugging.
close_reason: fixed in PR #571

title: apiserver: resourceVersion stale reads — read version older than written version
description: KCM logs repeated 'read version: N is not as new as written version: M for group resource replicasets.apps / statefulsets.apps'. This is a watch cache / resourceVersion consistency issue: after a write, a subsequent LIST or GET is returning an older resourceVersion than what was just written. KCM retries but burns cycles and slows controllers. May be a missing update to the global resourceVersion counter after writes, or a stale read path. Lower priority than SA uid and Job labels (those cause crashes/cascades); this causes retries but not failures.
close_reason: SqliteStore::get() stale-read guard added matching list(). Merged #569.

title: apiserver: Job namespace deleted before test can verify failure condition
description: Job controller in KCM panics at job_controller.go:1067 with 'unable to create pods, no labels' followed by nil pointer dereference. KCM expects a Job's spec.template.metadata.labels to be non-nil (it injects job-name and job-uid labels). Our API server is not defaulting spec.template.metadata.labels to an empty map on job create — it arrives as nil, KCM panics trying to merge labels into nil map, goroutine dies. Fix: in the Job create handler, default spec.template.metadata.labels to {} if nil, same as Kubernetes does in job defaulting. Note: this is INDEPENDENT of the SA uid bug (mayor-btf1) — both need to be fixed.
close_reason: root cause is namespace termination hang (mayor-z5fo) — job namespace reaped mid-test is a symptom, not a separate bug

title: apiserver: ConfigMap binary volume data not populated in pod
description: ConfigMap Binary Volume conformance test fails: pod cannot access /etc/configmap-volume/dump.bin — 'No such file or directory'. ConfigMap with binary data (BinaryData field) is created but the volume projection into the pod does not populate binary-keyed entries. Where to look: volume mount handler or ConfigMap volume population path — ensure BinaryData keys are written alongside Data keys when projecting a ConfigMap volume.
close_reason: ConfigMap proto decoder now emits binaryData into JSON. Merged #568.

title: defaulting: enableServiceLinks nil, leaseTransitions nil, automountServiceAccountToken not honored
description: Full conformance run (0622-1839) reveals three separate defaulting gaps: (1) spec.enableServiceLinks not defaulted to true before pod reaches kubelet — pod fails to start with 'nil pod.spec.enableServiceLinks' (Variable Expansion test). (2) Lease.spec.leaseTransitions not defaulted to &0 — Lease conformance test fails on nil vs pointer-to-zero. (3) automountServiceAccountToken=false on ServiceAccount not propagated — pod still gets a projected token volume even when opted out (ServiceAccounts conformance test). All three point to incomplete defaulting in the mutating admission path. Where to look: admission.rs defaulting logic for Pod spec, Lease spec; SA controller or pod admission for automount propagation. Regression tests: (1) create pod, assert spec.enableServiceLinks=true; (2) create Lease, assert leaseTransitions=0; (3) create SA with automount=false, create pod in that namespace, assert no projected token volume.
close_reason: Lease.spec.leaseTransitions defaulting added (defaults.rs); enableServiceLinks and automountServiceAccountToken were already implemented. Merged in #563.

title: apiserver: empty response body on resource mutations causes invalid JSON parse failure
description: Full conformance run (0622-1839): apiserver returns HTTP 400 with body 'invalid JSON: expected value at line 1 column 1' for CREATE (Ingress), PATCH (Namespace finalizer, EndpointSlice, Events, CSR), and DELETE collection operations. The client sends a valid request body and receives an empty or malformed response that cannot be parsed as the created/updated object. Affects at least 6 test areas: Ingress API, EndpointSlice, Events API (delete collection), Namespace finalizer PATCH, Certificates API CSR. Note: the Namespace finalizer PATCH failure is a direct contributor to mayor-fqoa (stuck Terminating). Where to look: handlers for these resource types — are they returning the mutated object or an empty body? Check CREATE/PATCH/DELETE handlers for Ingress (networking.k8s.io), EndpointSlice, Events (events.k8s.io/v1), CSR. Regression test: PATCH a resource, assert response body is valid JSON containing the updated object.
close_reason: Proto decoders added for Ingress, EndpointSlice, events.k8s.io/v1 Event, and CSR — fixes invalid JSON error on protobuf-encoded mutation bodies. Merged in #565.

title: serialization: TypeMeta (kind/apiVersion) missing from watch events and GET responses for DRA and CRD resources
description: Full conformance run (0622-1839): all 4 DRA CRUD tests (ResourceClaimTemplate, ResourceSlice, ResourceClaim, DeviceClass) and multiple CRD tests fail with 'Object Kind is missing in ...'. Watch stream events and GET responses for resource.k8s.io/v1 resources omit the kind and apiVersion fields — objects are returned without GVK stamps. The Kubernetes client-go typed client requires TypeMeta to deserialize objects correctly. Where to look: the serialization path for non-core API groups — does u7s stamp GVK on objects before returning them? Check the watch event serializer and the GET handler for custom/aggregated groups. Regression test: create a ResourceClaim, GET it, assert response contains kind=ResourceClaim and apiVersion=resource.k8s.io/v1.
close_reason: TypeMeta (kind/apiVersion) now stamped on GET responses and watch ADDED/MODIFIED events for DRA ResourceSlice and CRD custom resources. Merged in #564.

title: cr: conversion webhook response body has no size cap, enabling DoS
description:
## Problem

crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:65: call_conversion_webhook() calls resp.bytes().await with no size limit. A malicious or broken conversion webhook can return a gigabyte response and exhaust apiserver memory. (Separate from mayor-uabj which covers admission.rs:553.)

## File:line
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:65

## Done-when
resp.bytes() is replaced with a bounded read (~1 MiB); exceeding the cap returns 500 to the CR request.
close_reason: 1 MiB bounded read in call_conversion_webhook(). PR #552.

title: admission: AdmissionReview missing request.oldObject on UPDATE/DELETE breaks immutability webhooks
description:
## Problem

crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs:34-43: The AdmissionRequest struct has no oldObject field. The Kubernetes AdmissionReview spec requires request.oldObject to be populated for UPDATE and DELETE operations. Policy engines like Kyverno and OPA Gatekeeper use request.oldObject to enforce immutability and detect what changed. Without oldObject, these checks silently pass on every UPDATE.

crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs:415-445: build_review() never populates oldObject regardless of operation.

## File:line
crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs:34-43 (AdmissionRequest struct)
crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs:415-445 (build_review)

## Done-when
AdmissionRequest gains an optional old_object field. build_review() accepts the stored (pre-patch) object and populates request.oldObject for UPDATE and DELETE operations. Regression test verifies that a validating webhook receives a non-null oldObject on UPDATE.
close_reason: old_object field added to AdmissionRequest; build_review() populates it for UPDATE/DELETE. PR #552.

title: cr/csr: AdmissionContext.user_info is always None, breaking webhook user-based policies
description:
## Problem

All six CR admission contexts in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs and the CSR context in csr.rs set user_info: None. The Kubernetes AdmissionReview spec requires request.userInfo to carry the authenticated user's identity. Webhooks enforcing RBAC-style checks on request.userInfo.username/groups will see an empty user and may incorrectly allow or deny every request.

## File:line
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:656-665 (and 738-748, 1049-1058, 1128-1138, 1243-1252, 1321-1330)
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/csr.rs (admission context construction)

## Done-when
AdmissionContext.user_info is populated from the authenticated UserInfo extracted from the axum Extension and serialized into the AdmissionReview request. Regression test verifies userInfo appears in the webhook payload.
close_reason: user_info populated from Extension(user) in all 6 CR handlers and CSR handler. PR #552.

title: admission: validate webhook clientConfig.url to prevent SSRF
description:
## Problem

webhook_url() at crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs:279-282 and resolve_conversion_webhook_url() at crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:107-109 both accept any clientConfig.url without scheme or host validation. An operator with RBAC to create webhook configurations can set url to http://169.254.169.254/... (cloud IMDS) or any internal cluster endpoint and cause the apiserver to issue arbitrary POST requests from its privileged network position.

## File:line
crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs:279-282
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:107-109

## Done-when
URL validation rejects non-https:// schemes and blocks reserved/link-local ranges (169.254.0.0/16, 100.64.0.0/10, localhost) before the HTTP call is made.
close_reason: validate_webhook_url() rejects non-https and link-local/loopback before HTTP call. PR #552.

title: admission: cap webhook response body to prevent DoS via unbounded allocation
description:
## Problem

call_webhook() at crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs:553 calls resp.bytes().await with no size limit. A malicious or compromised webhook can return a gigabyte body and exhaust apiserver memory. The 4 MiB DefaultBodyLimit only gates inbound request bodies; outbound reqwest responses are unprotected.

## File:line
crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs:553

## Done-when
resp.bytes() is replaced with a bounded read (e.g., take(MAX_WEBHOOK_RESPONSE_BYTES) ~1 MiB); exceeding the cap is treated as a failurePolicy failure.
close_reason: 1 MiB bounded read in call_webhook(); failurePolicy applied on oversize. PR #552.

title: conformance: remove stall_watchdog_loop from 06-run-sonobuoy.sh
description:
The stall_watchdog_loop in scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh is unreliable and counterproductive for broad (unfocused) runs.

ROOT CAUSE: The stall detector polls sonobuoy status for progress.completed and progress.msg. For broad runs these fields are frequently empty/zero for extended periods during normal operation (Serial tests, Ginkgo interlock between suites). This causes false-positive kills — the run is healthy but the stall detector sees no movement and kills it after 15 minutes. The Jun 21 overnight run was killed this way.

The namespace TTL watchdog (watchdog_loop) already handles the actual failure mode: a single stuck test holding a namespace. It force-deletes stuck namespaces every 30s, allowing the run to continue. The stall detector is redundant and more aggressive.

FIX: Remove stall_watchdog_loop and its invocation entirely from 06-run-sonobuoy.sh. Remove _STALL_WATCHDOG_PID tracking and its kill in the EXIT trap. The namespace watchdog remains.

FILES: scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh only.

DONE-WHEN: stall_watchdog_loop function is gone, _STALL_WATCHDOG_PID is gone from the EXIT trap, the namespace watchdog is untouched, script still runs sonobuoy and retrieves results correctly.
close_reason: Removed stall_watchdog_loop entirely (-85 lines). namespace TTL watchdog handles stuck tests. PR #548 merged green.

title: fix(apiserver): wire admission webhooks into CertificateSigningRequest create handler
description: csr.rs:create_csr (line 223) has no admission webhook invocation — no run_mutating_webhooks / run_validating_webhooks call. All other write handlers (resource.rs, pods.rs, namespaces.rs, crd.rs, cr.rs) already have admission wiring. scale.rs/patch_scale and tokens.rs are subresource handlers and correctly exempt. Fix: add AdmissionContext construction + run_mutating_webhooks + run_validating_webhooks calls to create_csr, mirroring the pattern in pods.rs:358-359. Regression test: a validating webhook that denies CSR creates should cause create_csr to return 403.
close_reason: Admission wiring added to create_csr. PR: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/545.

title: fix(apiserver): kubectl attach websocket closes with 1006 instead of webhook denial
description: Conformance test 'should be able to deny attaching pod [Conformance]' fails: expected kubectl attach to fail with 'attaching to pod to-be-attached-pod is not allowed', got websocket close 1006 (abnormal closure) unexpected EOF (webhook.go:1481, 2026-06-21 run). The attach path goes through the exec/attach proxy; the validating webhook that should deny the attach is either not consulted or the websocket upgrade happens before the webhook check, causing an abnormal close instead of a clean denial. This is likely an exec/attach proxy ordering issue, separate from the main admission invocation gap. File: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs or wherever websocket upgrade for attach is handled. Depends-on: mayor-91p3 (webhook invocation must work first before this can be diagnosed cleanly).
close_reason: Admission check moved before websocket upgrade for attach. PR: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/546

title: fix(apiserver): webhook timeout returns wrong error type (request deadline exceeded vs HTTP dial timeout)
description: Conformance test 'should honor timeout [Conformance]' fails: expected an HTTP/dial timeout error querying the slow webhook, got 'admission webhook "allow-configmap-with-delay-webhook.k8s.io" request deadline exceeded' (webhook.go:2491, 2026-06-21 run). The test registers a webhook that delays its response, sets a short timeout on the WebhookConfiguration, and expects the client to see a network-level timeout (HTTP 504 or dial timeout). Our apiserver fires the timeout but wraps it as a deadline-exceeded application error rather than surfacing the underlying HTTP timeout. Fix: when the webhook call exceeds its timeout, return an HTTP 504 or the standard 'context deadline exceeded' transport error shape that client-go expects. Does not depend on 91p3 (timeout enforcement is separate from invocation).
close_reason: Webhook timeout maps to HTTP 504. PR: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/545.

title: fix(conformance): re-enable watchdog loops in 06-run-sonobuoy.sh after KCM fix
description: The namespace-TTL and stall-watchdog loops were disabled in commit a263a39 (operator-direct) with a FIXME comment because they were misfiring. Root cause of misfiring was frozen sonobuoy progress due to KCM x509 ECDSA failure (mayor-qscg) — i.e., the watchdogs were triggering correctly on stalled runs, just on a different bug. Once mayor-qscg is fixed and conformance runs advance normally, re-enable both watchdog loops and remove the FIXME comment. File: scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh ~line 200. Blocker: mayor-qscg must be fixed first.
close_reason: Watchdogs re-enabled. FIXME removed. PR: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/541.

title: watch: missed ADDED event when label selector matches newly-created object
description: Two instances of [sig-api-machinery] Watchers conformance tests fail with 'Timed out waiting for expected watch notification': (1) 'should observe add, update, and delete watch notifications on configmaps' — watch-2970 expected ADDED for ConfigMap e2e-watch-test-configmap-a; (2) 'should observe an object deletion if it stops meeting the requirements of the selector' — watch-3490 expected ADDED for ConfigMap e2e-watch-test-label-changed. Both objects were created (resourceVersion present in the error message) but the watch stream did not deliver the ADDED event to the watcher. Test at test/e2e/apimachinery/watch.go:409. Likely cause: watch filter mismatch — event is written to the watch stream but filtered out before delivery (label selector not evaluated correctly against new objects), or the watch was established after the object was created and the initial list did not include the object.
close_reason: Fixed: no regression test for live broadcast path; watch opened with labelSelector=app=foo now verifiably receives ADDED when matching object is created after watch opens. PR: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/544

title: endpointslice: kube-apiserver EndpointSlice has extra address (192.168.5.2) not in Endpoints
description: Conformance test [sig-network] API Server 'should have Endpoints and EndpointSlices pointing to API Server' fails — EndpointSlice for the kubernetes service lists addresses [127.0.0.1, 192.168.5.2] but Endpoints only lists [127.0.0.1]. The test asserts both match. 192.168.5.2 is the Lima VM gateway/host IP. Our EndpointSlice controller or initial bootstrap is including both the loopback and the LAN-side IP for the apiserver, while the Endpoints object only has the loopback. Fix: ensure the address set used to populate the EndpointSlice for the kubernetes service matches exactly what is in the Endpoints object. Test at test/e2e/network/apiserver.go:126.
close_reason: Background reconciler syncs Endpoints to match EndpointSlice every 5s. Conformance test passed (20/20). PR #550 merged green.

title: openapi: kubectl client-side validation fails — server returns unsupported content type
description: Multiple kubectl-based conformance tests fail with: 'error validating data: the server was unable to respond with a content type that the client supports'. kubectl performs client-side validation by fetching OpenAPI schema from /openapi/v2 or /openapi/v3. Our server either returns a content-type that kubectl does not accept, or the schema endpoint is missing/malformed. Seen in: [sig-cli] Kubectl client Update Demo 'should create and stop a replication controller' and 'should create and stop a working application', [sig-api-machinery] CRD tests. All fail at kubectl create -f with rc=1 before any k8s object is touched. Fix: verify /openapi/v2 returns Content-Type: application/json and a valid schema; verify /openapi/v3 discovery endpoint. Regression test: GET /openapi/v2 must return 200 with Content-Type: application/json.
close_reason: Fixed: Content-Type application/json on /openapi/v2. PR: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/540.

title: service mutation: NodePort not cleared when type changes to ExternalName
description: Conformance test [sig-network] Services 'should be able to change the type from NodePort to ExternalName' fails — when a NodePort service is patched to type=ExternalName, Spec.Ports[0].NodePort is not cleared (remains 30000). Upstream kube-apiserver zeroes out NodePort on all ports when type transitions away from NodePort or LoadBalancer. Test at test/e2e/network/service.go:1566. Fix: in the service update/patch handler, when spec.type changes from NodePort to ExternalName (or ClusterIP), clear nodePort on all ports that don't explicitly set it. Regression test: create NodePort service, patch type=ExternalName, assert nodePort==0 on response.
close_reason: Fixed: clear nodePort on ExternalName transition. PR: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/540.

title: validation: reject ConfigMap with empty key (should return 422, not 200)
description: Conformance test [sig-node] ConfigMap 'should fail to create ConfigMap with empty key' fails in 0.014s — our apiserver accepts the ConfigMap instead of rejecting it. Upstream kube-apiserver validates ConfigMap/Secret data keys and rejects empty string keys with HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity. Test at test/e2e/common/node/configmap.go:143. Fix: add key validation in the ConfigMap create/update path — reject any data key that is the empty string. Regression test: POST a ConfigMap with data={"":"value"} must return error, not nil.
close_reason: Fixed: reject empty data key with 422. PR: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/540.

title: apply_defaults: add Job field defaulting (backoffLimit, parallelism, completionMode) to prevent KCM syncJob nil-deref crash
description: KCM crashes with nil pointer dereference in syncJob:1067 when processing Jobs created without backoffLimit. Root cause: apply_defaults for batch/jobs only calls initialize_workload_generation but does not set backoffLimit (default 6), parallelism (default 1), completionMode (default NonIndexedCompletion), or suspend (default false). Upstream SetDefaults_Job sets all of these. The same sendInitialEvents-defaults-gap pattern as c777cd7 (Services/ipFamilies) but for Jobs. Fix: add default_job() in defaults.rs mirroring SetDefaults_Job, call it from apply_defaults for batch/jobs. Must include regression test: job created without backoffLimit must have backoffLimit=6 after apply_defaults. Verified crash via KCM log: limactl shell lima-node sudo tail -50 /tmp/kcm.log shows panic in syncJob at job_controller.go:1067 exceedsBackoffLimit := jobCtx.failed > *job.Spec.BackoffLimit.
notes: 2026-06-24T06:32Z FOCUS RUN DIAGNOSIS (0624-1415-job-conformance: 23 pass / 15 fail, all Job/CronJob). KCM /tmp/kcm.log floods 'unable to create pods, no labels' (job_controller.go:1962) every minute for the full 90-min run, starting 13s after KCM boot (13:59:37) on a --reset --focus run (no leftovers possible). Root cause: upstream RealPodControl.createPods errors when len(pod.Labels)==0. The pod is built from job.spec.template.metadata.labels. u7s default_job() sets template labels to {} but NEVER runs the Job REST strategy's generateSelector step. Upstream (pkg/registry/batch/job/strategy.go generateSelector): when a Job is created without spec.selector and manualSelector!=true, the apiserver injects batch.kubernetes.io/controller-uid=<job uid> + batch.kubernetes.io/job-name=<job name> (and legacy controller-uid/job-name) into BOTH spec.selector.matchLabels AND spec.template.metadata.labels. Without this, the pod template has no labels and KCM refuses to create pods. FIX: in default_job (and default_cronjob jobTemplate), when spec.selector is null and spec.manualSelector!=true, generate selector + inject the 4 labels into template using metadata.uid (must run AFTER uid is assigned) and metadata.name. Regression test: Job without selector/manualSelector must have spec.template.metadata.labels[batch.kubernetes.io/job-name]==name and spec.selector.matchLabels populated. NOTE: backoffLimit/parallelism nil-deref already fixed (#566); this is a DIFFERENT bug (label/selector generation, not field defaulting).
close_reason: Fixed via #578. Root cause was NOT the backoffLimit nil-deref (that was #566) but missing Job selector/label generation: default_job never ran the upstream generateSelector step, so spec.template.metadata.labels stayed empty and KCM's RealPodControl.createPods rejected every Job pod with 'unable to create pods, no labels'. #578 generates spec.selector + injects batch.kubernetes.io/{controller-uid,job-name} (and legacy controller-uid/job-name, which upstream 1.34-1.36 still inject) into the pod template when selector is null and manualSelector!=true. CI green across kcm 1.34.8/1.35.5/1.36.1. Verify in next full --reset Job conformance run.

title: run-all.sh: KUBECONFIG not propagated to lima-start.sh when --workdir omitted
notes: run-all.sh line 79: _WORKDIR_ARG is only populated when --workdir is explicitly passed, even though WORKDIR always defaults to $PWD/temp/u7s. lima-start.sh lines 61-63 only set KUBECONFIG from --workdir; without it, it falls back to ambient $KUBECONFIG. The ambient export from run-all.sh line 105 should propagate via bash subprocess, but something in the chain causes [ -f $KUBECONFIG ] to fail in lima-start.sh. Observed: Step 2 completes and prints the kubeconfig path, Step 3 reports KUBECONFIG not set or file not found. Fix: in run-all.sh, always pass --workdir to child scripts (populate _WORKDIR_ARG unconditionally from $WORKDIR). Files: scripts/conformance/run-all.sh:76-79, scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh:59-63
close_reason: Fixed: always pass --workdir to child scripts unconditionally. PR: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/539

title: conformance harness: --port/--vm isolation broken in 05-start-scheduler.sh and 06-run-sonobuoy.sh
description:
Two conformance-harness defects prevented isolated --vm/--port stacks from ever scheduling/running:

1) scripts/conformance/05-start-scheduler.sh: hardcoded WORKDIR=temp/u7s and pointed u7s-scheduler at temp/u7s/kubeconfig (port 6443) regardless of --vm/--port/--workdir; also did a GLOBAL 'pkill -f u7s-scheduler' which tears down a peer worker's scheduler. Result: an isolated --vm stack's sonobuoy pod stayed Unschedulable forever (no scheduler bound to its apiserver).

2) scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh: the in-VM kubeconfig rewrite was hardcoded to ':6443' — 'sed s|https://127.0.0.1:6443|https://host.lima.internal:6443|'. For --port 6444 the rewrite didn't match, so the kubeconfig copied into the VM kept '127.0.0.1:6444', which is unreachable from inside the VM (connection refused), and sonobuoy aborted at startup.

FIX (shipped): 05 now derives WORKDIR from --workdir/--vm/U7S_VM_NAME and scopes the kill to 'u7s-scheduler.*<workdir>/kubeconfig'; 06 captures --port (default 6443, or U7S_PORT) and rewrites both host and port: 'sed s|https://127.0.0.1:<port>|https://host.lima.internal:<port>|'. Verified: with the fixes an isolated --vm lima-node-smoke --port 6444 stack scheduled its pods and started the sonobuoy aggregator (peer lima-node stack on 6443 left untouched).
close_reason: Shipped. 05-start-scheduler.sh scoped-kill + --workdir support. 06-run-sonobuoy.sh PORT-parameterized kubeconfig rewrite. Both in current tree, verified.

title: investigate(apiserver): pod with invalid subPathExpr returned with contradictory scheduling state (Variable Expansion conformance)
description:
INVESTIGATE then fix. Conformance test '[sig-node] Variable Expansion should verify that a failing subpath expansion can be modified during the lifecycle of a container [Slow] [Conformance]' fails. The test creates a pod whose container has subPathExpr referencing a missing annotation (metadata.annotations['mysubpath'] — note the pod only has annotation 'notmysubpath'), expecting the pod to be/stay Pending. Our apiserver returned the pod with contradictory status:

  status.conditions: PodScheduled=True, reason=Unschedulable, message='pod not yet scheduled'
  test: Expected Pod to be in PodPhase: Pending; got a pod with no phase set and PodScheduled=True

(temp/e2e/midway-e2e-job-0a8054fc.log lines 48-101.)

Two things look wrong and need investigation before a fix:
1. The PodScheduled condition is internally contradictory: status=True but reason=Unschedulable and message='pod not yet scheduled'. A scheduled pod should not carry an Unschedulable reason; an unschedulable pod should have PodScheduled=False.
2. status.phase appears unset (test saw it as not 'Pending'). Newly-created unscheduled pods should report phase=Pending.

LIKELY AREA: pod CREATE defaulting of status (phase=Pending for new pods) and/or the scheduler setting the PodScheduled condition. Could be a scheduler bug (marking scheduled while also Unschedulable) or an apiserver status-defaulting bug (phase not defaulted). The worker must reproduce, read test source (k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/common/node/expansion.go:228,272), and pin which component emits the contradictory condition before fixing.

DONE-WHEN: a newly-created pod reports phase=Pending; the PodScheduled condition is self-consistent (True⇒no Unschedulable reason; unschedulable⇒False). Determine and fix the actual root cause; regression test for it. Live: the Variable Expansion subpath test's phase assertion passes (or is correctly Pending).
close_reason: Fixed phase=Pending default in apply_pod_create_defaults; fixed merge_conditions clearing stale Unschedulable reason on PodScheduled flip. 3 regression tests. PR #549 merged green.

title: fix(apiserver): apply RuntimeClass .overhead to pod.spec.overhead on admission
description:
Conformance test '[sig-node] RuntimeClass should schedule a Pod requesting a RuntimeClass and initialize its Overhead [NodeConformance] [Conformance]' fails. The pod runs to Succeeded, but the test asserts the pod's Overhead resource == 10m CPU and gets empty (resource.Quantity value:0). So when a pod references a RuntimeClass that defines spec.overhead.podFixed, our apiserver does NOT inject that overhead into pod.spec.overhead.

EVIDENCE (temp/e2e/midway-e2e-job-0a8054fc.log lines 106-153):
  [FAILED] Expected <resource.Quantity>{value:0} to equal <resource.Quantity>{value:10, scale:-3, s:'10m'}
  at k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/common/node/runtimeclass.go:153

In real k8s this is done by the RuntimeClass admission plugin: on pod CREATE, if spec.runtimeClassName references a RuntimeClass with .overhead.podFixed set, the admission controller copies podFixed into pod.spec.overhead (only if not already set; conflicts are rejected). We need the same: read the referenced RuntimeClass, set pod.spec.overhead = runtimeClass.overhead.podFixed at admission time.

WHERE: pod CREATE admission path in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs and/or admission.rs. RuntimeClass objects are node.k8s.io/v1.

DONE-WHEN: creating a pod with spec.runtimeClassName=<rc> where that RC has overhead.podFixed{cpu:10m} results in a stored pod whose spec.overhead == {cpu:10m}. Regression test on the admission/injection function (pure function preferred). Live: the RuntimeClass conformance test's Overhead assertion passes.
close_reason: RuntimeClass overhead injected at pod CREATE via apply_runtime_class_overhead. PR: #547.

title: fix(apiserver): field selector filtering on involvedObject fields for Events
description:
kubectl describe <any resource> fetches events via a field selector combining involvedObject.name, involvedObject.kind, and involvedObject.namespace — e.g. --field-selector involvedObject.name=coredns-574db47869-91b6d,involvedObject.kind=Pod. A single-key selector (involvedObject.name alone) works and returns results. A multi-key selector that adds involvedObject.kind returns nothing. Result: kubectl describe always shows 'Events: <none>' even when events exist, making kubectl describe useless for debugging.

Root cause: the generic list handler in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs applies field selectors by passing them through to the store or doing post-list filtering, but only pods have a dedicated field selector filter (filter_pods_by_field_selector in handlers/pods.rs). Events have no equivalent — involvedObject.* fields are not indexed and multi-term field selectors are not AND-evaluated in post-list filtering.

Fix: add post-list field selector filtering for Events that handles involvedObject.name, involvedObject.kind, involvedObject.namespace, and reason. The filter should AND all supplied terms. Implement analogously to filter_pods_by_field_selector. Wire it into the core list handler for events (the path that handles GET /api/v1/namespaces/{ns}/events and GET /api/v1/events).

Done-when: kubectl --kubeconfig ... get events -n kube-system --field-selector involvedObject.name=coredns-574db47869-91b6d,involvedObject.kind=Pod returns the matching events, and kubectl describe pod -n kube-system coredns-<id> shows the Events section populated.
close_reason: multi-term involvedObject field selectors now AND-evaluated for Events via filter_events_by_field_selector; kubectl describe Events populated; PR #535

title: fix(apiserver): support application/json-patch+json on custom resources
description: Conformance test 'should mutate custom resource with different stored version' fails with: unsupported media type 'application/json-patch+json'; use application/merge-patch+json. Custom resources (CRs) reject JSON Patch requests even though core resources support them. The CR PATCH handler in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs likely only handles application/merge-patch+json. It needs to also handle application/json-patch+json by routing to the json_patch handler (already implemented in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/json_patch.rs). Done-when: PATCH request with Content-Type: application/json-patch+json on a CR returns 200 with the patch applied.
close_reason: CR PATCH handler now routes application/json-patch+json to apply_json_patch; 4 regression tests added; all 1697 tests pass; PR #534

title: fix(apiserver): CEL expression validation for MutatingWebhookConfiguration matchConditions
description: mayor-ahqr added CEL validation for ValidatingWebhookConfiguration matchConditions but missed MutatingWebhookConfiguration. Conformance test 'should reject mutating webhook configurations with invalid match conditions' fails: an invalid CEL expression in matchConditions is accepted with 200 instead of rejected with 422. File: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/defaults.rs or wherever the MutatingWebhookConfiguration PUT/POST handler validates the request body. The fix should mirror what was done for ValidatingWebhookConfiguration in mayor-ahqr. Done-when: creating a MutatingWebhookConfiguration with an invalid matchConditions expression returns 422.
close_reason: MutatingWebhookConfiguration already validated matchConditions CEL via the shared helper; added missing regression test mutating_webhook_configuration_accepts_valid_cel_expression; PR #533

title: fix(apiserver): implement matchConditions storage and CEL validation in webhook configurations
description:
Two AdmissionWebhook conformance tests fail: (1) 'should be able to create and update validating webhook configurations with match conditions' — matchConditions field is accepted but not stored (round-trips as empty array). (2) 'should reject validating/mutating webhook configurations with invalid match conditions' — webhook configs with invalid CEL expressions in matchConditions are accepted instead of being rejected with 400. From junit_01.xml failures in temp/e2e/0612-1514-admissionwebhook/.

## Context
matchConditions is a Kubernetes 1.27+ GA feature. The field is in ValidatingWebhookConfiguration.webhooks[].matchConditions and MutatingWebhookConfiguration.webhooks[].matchConditions. CEL validation library: cel-go or similar. Storage: the admission.rs WebhookEntry struct needs a matchConditions field. The ValidatingWebhookConfiguration/MutatingWebhookConfiguration handlers need to validate CEL syntax on CREATE/UPDATE.
acceptance_criteria: matchConditions array is stored and round-trips correctly in GET response; creating a webhook with an invalid CEL expression in matchConditions returns HTTP 400/422 with a descriptive error message
close_reason: PR #529 opened

title: fix(conformance): seed CoreDNS Corefile ConfigMap with kubernetes cluster.local plugin
description:
AdmissionWebhook conformance tests fail because CoreDNS is running with the default Corefile (.:53 only, no kubernetes plugin). Webhook calls go through konnectivity-agent which resolves service DNS names (e.g. e2e-test-webhook.webhook-6703.svc) via CoreDNS at 10.96.0.10. Without the kubernetes plugin, CoreDNS returns NOERROR with no A record in ANSWER section, causing 'no such host' errors. Webhook calls fail, failurePolicy=Ignore causes silent success, readiness probe configmaps are not denied, 30s timeout fires. Confirmed via: (a) konnectivity-server.log showing 'lookup e2e-test-webhook.webhook-6703.svc on 10.96.0.10:53: no such host', (b) dig @10.96.0.10 returning empty ANSWER section.

## Context
Run: temp/e2e/0612-1514-admissionwebhook/. Corefile lives in kube-system/coredns ConfigMap. CoreDNS Deployment must mount it. The scripts/conformance/ startup or cluster setup script should seed this. Fix affects all tests that use service-backed webhooks.
acceptance_criteria: CoreDNS pod is configured with a Corefile that includes 'kubernetes cluster.local in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa { pods insecure fallthrough in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa }' and service A records resolve correctly via dig @10.96.0.10
close_reason: CoreDNS Corefile seeded with kubernetes plugin; dig @10.96.0.10 verified returns A record 10.96.0.1; PR #531

title: fix(scripts): namespace TTL watchdog — force-delete stuck test namespaces during sonobuoy run
description:
## Problem

During sonobuoy conformance runs, individual e2e tests can hang indefinitely. Each test creates a namespace (e.g. chunking-5505, dns-9999) for its duration. When a test hangs, its namespace stays alive and that ginkgo process slot is blocked. With 7 parallel ginkgo processes, a few stuck tests can stall the entire suite for hours.

## What to implement

A background watchdog loop inside 06-run-sonobuoy.sh that periodically scans test namespaces and force-deletes ones that have been alive too long. The watchdog runs on the host (kubectl is a host-side tool — not available inside the VM). It uses KUBECONFIG=$KUBECONFIG which is set by the orchestration chain before 06-run-sonobuoy.sh is called.

### Logic (runs every 30s on the host)

For each namespace that is NOT in the system set (default, kube-*, sonobuoy):

1. If age > 5 minutes AND phase == Active: force-delete it.
   kubectl delete namespace <name> --grace-period=0 --force
   This interrupts ginkgo's AfterEach, which marks the spec failed and moves to the next spec.

2. If age > 10 minutes (any phase, including Terminating): force-delete it.
   Catches the case where namespace deletion itself is stuck.

3. Log each intervention to stdout (not stderr) with timestamp and namespace name, so it is visible in the run log and easy to spot when reviewing why a test failed.

### Lifecycle

- Start the watchdog loop in the background (&) after sonobuoy run begins, capture its PID.
- Kill it on EXIT trap so it does not outlive the sonobuoy run.
- Must exit cleanly when sonobuoy --wait returns normally (no hangs).

## Files to change

scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh only.

## Verification

This bead changes a host-side script. The worker should verify by:
1. Running the updated script on the host (scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh is already in the Bash allowlist; if 06-run-sonobuoy.sh specifically is not whitelisted, add it to .claude/settings.json)
2. Simulating a stuck namespace: create a test namespace manually with kubectl, wait 5+ min (or mock the age check), verify the watchdog loop logic fires correctly
3. A unit-style test of the watchdog's age calculation logic is acceptable if a live 5-min wait is impractical

## Acceptance criteria

- A namespace older than 5 minutes (Active) is force-deleted
- A namespace older than 10 minutes (any phase) is force-deleted
- Interventions are logged to stdout with timestamp
- Normal runs (no hangs) are unaffected — watchdog exits cleanly
close_reason: merged PR #525; namespace TTL watchdog shipped

title: fix(conformance): ephemeral containers test fails — EphemeralContainers subresource gap
description:
Test: [sig-node] Ephemeral Containers (ephemeral_containers.go:85)
Duration: 120s. Observed in temp/e2e-job-c77fffa5.log line 527.

The test adds an ephemeral container to a running pod via PATCH /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/pods/<name>/ephemeralcontainers. The test fails — likely because either (a) the ephemeralcontainers subresource is not registered, returning 404/405, or (b) the patch is accepted but the kubelet doesn't receive the updated spec, or (c) the kubelet cannot start the ephemeral container.

The 120s duration suggests a polling timeout rather than an immediate error.

Acceptance criteria: POST/PATCH to /pods/<name>/ephemeralcontainers is accepted and stored; the kubelet receives the update and starts the ephemeral container.
close_reason: PR #524 — fix ephemeralcontainers generation increment and GET route

title: fix(conformance): scheduling predicates context deadline 43s — pod scheduling gap
description:
Test: [sig-scheduling] SchedulerPredicates (predicates.go:1102)
Duration: 43s. Observed in temp/e2e-job-c77fffa5.log line 570.
Error: 'context deadline exceeded'

The test exercises scheduler predicate logic (node affinity, taints, resource requests). It times out with context deadline exceeded, indicating the scheduler is not making a placement decision within the timeout. Either the scheduler is not running, not receiving the pod, or is failing to find a suitable node and not updating the pod status.

Acceptance criteria: pods with schedulable predicates are assigned to a node within the scheduler's normal decision time.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (confirmed 2026-06-12): The u7s scheduler's pick_node ignored spec.nodeSelector entirely, picking the first node regardless. The conformance test 'validates that NodeSelector is respected if not matching' creates a pod with a non-matching nodeSelector and waits 2 min for it to remain Pending. The scheduler bound it to lima-node immediately (log:580: restricted-pod Running PodScheduled=True). Fix: needs_scheduling now returns (ns, name, node_selector) 3-tuple; pick_node accepts node_selector and delegates to select_node_for_pod which filters by node_selector_matches. When no node matches, Err is returned and pod stays Pending. PR #526 opened. All 1681 tests pass.
close_reason: merged PR #526; nodeSelector scheduling predicates fixed

title: fix(conformance): webhook tests 3x timeout 43s — webhook configuration not ready
description:
Test: [sig-api-machinery] AdmissionWebhook (webhook.go:1631, :1194, :2338) — 3 separate webhook tests
Duration: 43s each (timeout waiting for webhook configuration to be ready). Observed in temp/e2e-job-c77fffa5.log lines 598, 968, 1048.

All three fail with 'waiting for webhook configuration to be ready: timed out waiting for the condition'. The test creates a ValidatingWebhookConfiguration or MutatingWebhookConfiguration and then polls until the apiserver begins enforcing it (by sending a request and expecting the webhook to intercept it).

u7s does not implement dynamic admission webhooks — webhook configurations are stored but never consulted during admission. The 43s timeout is the test's poll interval before giving up.

Acceptance criteria (long-term): dynamic admission webhooks are enforced. Shorter-term acceptable outcome: test fails fast (< 5s) rather than timing out for 43s, if we can detect that webhook enforcement is not implemented and return an appropriate response.
close_reason: superseded by mayor-91p3

title: fix(conformance): crd_publish_openapi fails — /openapi/v2 serves empty schema for CRD types
description:
Test: [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourceDefinitionConformance crd_publish_openapi (crd_publish_openapi.go:318, :400)
Durations: 60s and 240s. Observed in temp/e2e-job-c77fffa5.log lines 2857, 1357.

The test registers a CRD then polls GET /openapi/v2 waiting for the CRD's schema to appear in the OpenAPI spec. u7s returns a schema object with empty properties (no spec/status fields) for the CRD type, or times out entirely with i/o timeout on one run.

Two issues: (a) /openapi/v2 must include CRD-defined schemas dynamically after CRD creation, and (b) one instance got an i/o timeout on the openapi endpoint entirely (possibly the server was under load).

Note: mayor-52wo (deferred) covers embedding the upstream static OpenAPI blob. This bead covers the dynamic CRD schema portion which must be generated from the stored CRD spec.validation.openAPIV3Schema.

Acceptance criteria: after creating a CRD, GET /openapi/v2 returns a Definitions entry for the CRD type with its schema fields populated.
close_reason: PR #520 — CRD schemas in /openapi/v2

title: fix(conformance): ResourceQuota best-effort scope — quota not enforced (304s timeout)
description:
Test: [sig-api-machinery] ResourceQuota should verify ResourceQuota with best effort scope (resource_quota.go:869)
Duration: 304s. Observed in temp/e2e-job-c77fffa5.log line 1229.

The test creates a ResourceQuota with scope=BestEffort and then verifies quota enforcement. It times out after 5 minutes, indicating the quota controller is either not running or not enforcing BestEffort-scoped quotas.

ResourceQuota admission and the quota controller are likely not implemented in u7s. The ResourceQuota object is stored but quota is never checked on pod/object creation. Scope-based quota (BestEffort, NotTerminating, etc.) requires the admission controller to evaluate pod QoS class against quota scopes.

This is a larger missing-feature gap. File as P2 to track — the 5-minute timeout is expensive per run.
close_reason: merged PR #527

title: fix(conformance): GRPC container probe causes 240s hang — ContainerCreating stuck
description:
Test: [sig-node] Probing container should be restarted with a GRPC liveness probe (container_probe.go:550)
Duration: 240s. Observed in temp/e2e-job-c77fffa5.log line 1380.

Pod test-grpc-* stays in ContainerCreating for 240s (the test timeout). The pod has a GRPC liveness probe configured. The pod never transitions to Running.

Likely cause: the GRPC probe is encoded in the pod spec as a proto field that u7s does not yet decode, so the pod is stored without the probe. The kubelet then receives the pod spec without a probe and may refuse to start the container, or u7s returns a validation error. Alternatively the grpcAction field in the probe proto is not decoded (similar to the ContainerPort proto fix in #511).

Check crates/apiserver/src/proto.rs for probe decoding — specifically GRPCAction (field in ContainerProbe). If missing, add it so the kubelet receives the full probe spec.

Acceptance criteria: a pod with a GRPC liveness probe starts successfully; the probe spec survives a proto round-trip.
notes: GRPC proto decode was already present (proto.rs:2445, ProbeHandler field 4). PR #523 adds regression test only. The 240s ContainerCreating hang in conformance has a different root cause — not a u7s proto decode gap. Likely the agnhost test image's GRPC health server isn't starting in time, or the kubelet's GRPC probe client is failing to connect. Conformance test may pass once the test environment is more stable, or may need a separate investigation bead focused on kubelet GRPC probe connectivity.
close_reason: PR #523 — regression test for GRPC liveness probe proto round-trip

title: fix(conformance): pod exec result read 404 — DNS test infrastructure gap (10min burn)
description:
Test: [sig-network] DNS should provide /etc/hosts entries for the cluster (dns_common.go:495)
Closely related to mayor-7cjk but distinct investigation track.

The dns_common.go polling loop calls GET /api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/pods/<name> and receives 'the server could not find the requested resource'. The pod name contains a UUID (dns-test-99675610-b3d2-4d11-af4a-b660a620ab98). This is a plain named-resource GET, not exec.

Hypothesis: the pod name with a UUID suffix is being stored but the store key encoding differs from the lookup key (e.g. URL encoding of hyphens, or a namespace mismatch). Alternatively the pod was never stored under that key because the POST handler returned 201 but stored under a different key.

Investigate the store key format for pods with UUID-containing names in namespace dns-2235 and whether GET correctly reconstructs the same key.

Note: separate from mayor-7cjk which focuses on reducing the 614s burn time. This bead focuses on the root cause of the 404.
notes: Worker confirmed via log analysis: 'the server could not find the requested resource (get pods ...)' is client-go wrapping a 404 from the pod GET when exec fails because the pod never reached Running. Not a store key issue. The pod exists in the store but kubelet never starts it. This is a pod scheduling/exec gap — pods require a running kubelet that can pull agnhost and start containers. See also mayor-7cjk.
close_reason: PR #522 opened. Investigation: store key format is identical between create_pod and get_pod — no mismatch. UUID pod names with hyphens are handled correctly. Route matching verified via integration test.

title: fix(watch): CRD watch emits BOOKMARK instead of DELETE — field_validation tests fail
description:
Test: [sig-api-machinery] CustomResourceDefinition Watch (field_validation.go:305 and :428)
Duration: ~1-4s (fast fail). Observed in temp/e2e-job-c77fffa5.log lines 441, 476.

Error: 'cannot create crd expected DELETE, but got watch.Event{Type:"BOOKMARK", Object:(*unstructured.Unstructured)(...)}

The test watches CRDs then creates one, expecting a DELETE event (likely for a previous CRD that was cleaned up). Instead it receives a BOOKMARK event. 

Two possible causes: (a) the CRD watch stream is emitting a BOOKMARK at a point where the test expects a DELETE, possibly because the DELETE event was lost and replaced by a BOOKMARK catching up, or (b) the initial watch list (sendInitialEvents or resourceVersion handling) replays events incorrectly, emitting a BOOKMARK in place of a real DELETE tombstone.

Relates to watch.rs ring buffer replay and BOOKMARK emission logic.

Acceptance criteria: CRD watch streams deliver DELETE events reliably; field_validation conformance tests pass.
