title: Bump Lima base image from Ubuntu 24.04 to 26.04+ for systemd 256+: enables Lima vsock SSH forwarder, ends fleet-wide usernet-crash SSH-loss hazard
description:
SIGNAL

mayor-f7wxy scout (findings ai/findings/vsock-ssh-fallback-investigation-2026-08-06.md, closed) confirmed all 6 Lima VMs run Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS with systemd 255. Lima requires systemd 256+ to start its vsock SSH forwarder (verified in Lima source pkg/driver/vz/vm_darwin.go:124-137, cached at temp/research/lima-templates/).

Consequence: every VM falls back to routing SSH through the shared limactl usernet daemon. Any usernet incident (crash under host memory pressure, restart, hang) simultaneously kills SSH port-forwards to ALL Lima VMs.

Observed 2026-08-06T05:00:20Z: usernet daemon crashed, SSH died on all VMs at once, guest kernels remained healthy (proven by vsock heartbeat still alive). Recovery required manual limactl stop plus limactl start per affected VM, which wiped VM state.

Operator direction 2026-08-06: 'We are not under incident pressure now. We know this can happen and can recover by restarting the VM. Let us bump image version or systemd version if that can make our test setup more reliable. We do not really do anything OS-specific - I do not think such an update has much risk at all.'

FIX

Bump the two image URLs at lima/kubelet.yaml:28 and lima/kubelet.yaml:30 from Ubuntu 24.04 to current-LTS - specifically 26.04 if available (Noble follows Jammy, Oracular, Plucky, Questing... Ubuntu LTS ships every 2 years so 26.04 lands April 2026). Confirm systemd 256+ is in the new image before merging.

If 26.04 is not yet available at the time of implementation, options:
1. Use latest interim release (26.04-nonLTS if odd-year cadence) - systemd 256+ likely present
2. Ubuntu 24.04.4 backports repo - install systemd 256 via ppa - fragile, not recommended
3. Debian trixie (systemd 256) - larger base-image change, likely more surface disturbance

Prefer option 1: bump to whatever the current stable image with systemd 256+ is.

SCOPE

2 LoC change in lima/kubelet.yaml. Plus:
- Full reprovision of all 6 VMs (~15-20 min each per lima-start.sh:189, sequential is ~2 hrs, parallel possible)
- Revalidation conformance run (20 min per bd memory conformance-suite-is-iterable-for-profiling-purposes) to confirm nothing OS-specific breaks

Total operator time: ~2.5 hours of clock time, most of it unattended.

TESTS

Post-image-bump verification:
1. limactl shell lima-node-X systemctl --version returns 256+
2. limactl shell lima-node-X ls /sys/class/vsock/... shows vsock interfaces
3. Restart usernet daemon deliberately, confirm SSH survives (this is the acceptance criterion - vsock fallback works)
4. Full certified-conformance suite passes with pattern-identical results to the 0806-0917 baseline (483/483)

RISK

Low per operator assessment. u7s does not depend on any OS-specific behavior of the guest.

Points where subtle risk lives:
- kubelet YAML defaults may differ across Ubuntu versions in obscure ways (cgroups v2 defaults, systemd-networkd behavior, apparmor profiles)
- CRI-O install path via distribution package repo may point to a stale channel if 26.04 is very new - verify apt sources
- lima-start.sh assumptions about VM shell environment (bash version, coreutils behavior) - Ubuntu is generally stable here

CROSS-REFS

- Investigation: ai/findings/vsock-ssh-fallback-investigation-2026-08-06.md
- Related shipped: mayor-v82ej PR #1028 persistent journald (belt-and-suspenders even with vsock working)
- Bd memory: all-lima-vms-share-vsock-fallback-limitation (documents the current failure mode until this bead lands)

Shape-1 solo dispatch. Files: lima/kubelet.yaml, possibly scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh if any Ubuntu-version-specific tuning was in there.

title: Investigate why mcpls LSP crashes in scout worktrees: hypothesis is rust-analyzer needs prior cargo build to warm target/ before semantic queries work
description:
OBSERVED 2026-08-06 across 3 scout tasks (mayor-32uy1 JWT signature-cache scout, mayor-6sbvc JWT sig-cache implementation start, mayor-7e8jf JSON serde scout): mcp mcpls tools get_hover and get_definition and get_references crashed with MCP error -32603 LSP server process terminated unexpectedly, forcing grep-plus-Read fallback per Rule 12.

OPERATOR HYPOTHESIS 2026-08-06: LSP semantic queries via mcpls require a live rust-analyzer process backing the workspace. In the mayor checkout that process is likely already spawned from prior editor use. In a fresh scout worktree - especially scouts that do only Read-tool operations without any cargo build/cargo check - rust-analyzer either never spawns or crashes on its first query because target/ is empty / dependency graph unbuilt.

If confirmed, the fix is simple: scout dispatch prompts should either (a) require a cargo check in the worktree before any mcpls LSP call, or (b) document this expectation as a common preamble line, or (c) mcpls itself should auto-warm on first query (probably out of our scope).

2. Test the warming hypothesis. In the SAME fresh worktree, run cargo check (or cargo build) once, then retry mcp mcpls get_hover. Does it now succeed?

3. If step 2 succeeds, verify: is it target/ that mattered, or is rust-analyzer spawning independently? Check ps aux for rust-analyzer processes before/during/after the cargo run.

4. Report the minimum action needed to make mcpls reliably work in a scout worktree. Cheapest possible answer wins - e.g. if a bare cargo check is enough (no build), that is a ~10-second per-scout cost.

RETURN under 150 words: reproduced yes/no, warming step needed, proposed preamble text if any.

title: Lima VM provisioning falls back to usernet SSH forwarding when vsock SSH unavailable, breaking recovery from usernet crashes
description:
PROBLEM

lima-node was provisioned without vsock-based SSH forwarding. Evidence in the host-side hostagent log ~/.lima/lima-node/ha.stderr.log recorded at VM boot time:

    Failed to start vsock forwarder (systemd is older than v256?)
    SSH server does not seem to be running on vsock port, using usernet forwarder

Because the vsock fallback failed, lima-node's SSH port-forward routes exclusively through the shared limactl usernet daemon. When usernet crashed at 05:00:20 UTC on 2026-08-06, lima-node's SSH became permanently unreachable with no recovery path.

Confirmed in the same session: a separate vsock-only channel used by the guest agent for time-sync and port-discovery heartbeat kept working through and after the usernet crash. This proves the guest kernel was healthy; the failure was purely at the SSH-forwarding layer.

IMPLICATIONS

- Any usernet daemon incident (crash, restart, hang) permanently kills SSH to all lima VMs on this host until manual limactl stop and start
- Post-hoc forensic recovery of VM state after usernet incidents becomes impossible without wiping the ring buffer via VM restart
- Recovery costs on this platform are real: mayor-v82ej PR 1028 addressed journal-retention; this is the SSH-transport-availability sibling

MECHANISM (per operator dmesg-recovery scout 2026-08-06)

Lima's hostagent tries vsock SSH first because it survives usernet daemon incidents. Vsock forwarding requires systemd v256 or newer on the guest. The Ubuntu images our lima VMs are built on ship an older systemd, so vsock provisioning fails silently at bring-up time and falls through to usernet. There is no runtime signal of this fallback -- it appears normal until usernet crashes.

INVESTIGATION NEEDED (scout scope)

1. What is the exact systemd version on our lima VMs today? Check /etc/os-release and systemctl --version inside a live lima VM to confirm.
2. What lima base image are we using in scripts/conformance/lima-start.sh and scripts/worker-vm.sh? Is a newer image with systemd v256 plus available upstream?
3. If no newer image exists, is manual vsock-forwarder provisioning possible on the current systemd, e.g. install a newer systemd via backports, or bind-mount a working vsock socket?
4. What is the smallest change that would give us reliable vsock SSH forwarding without breaking the current stack?

RELATED

- Findings doc appended to ai/findings/operator-csi-hostpath-run-2026-08-06.md, section VM-side kernel recovery
- mayor-v82ej closed with PR 1028, addressed journal-retention on VM restart
- mayor-mjt51 and mayor-biy31 closed, related SYN-drop-under-load hypothesis, may reopen based on separate operator decision

PRIORITY

P3 today. This bug does not cause runtime failures on its own -- it only manifests when the usernet daemon dies. Its severity is proportional to how often usernet crashes, which we now believe to be tied to host-side memory pressure with all 6 Lima VMs running.

title: u7s apiserver missing VolumeSnapshot API group -- all csi-hostpath snapshot specs fail deterministically
description:
csi-hostpath conformance snapshot specs all fail with a client-side error before any u7s-side handler is reached:

    Resource snapshot.storage.k8s.io/v1/volumesnapshotclasses not found

The apiserver has ZERO references to that API group anywhere in the code. This is a legitimate gap, not a bug in an implemented handler.

## What is missing

Upstream Kubernetes ships the VolumeSnapshot CRDs (VolumeSnapshotClass, VolumeSnapshot, VolumeSnapshotContent -- all in group snapshot.storage.k8s.io/v1) as an AGGREGATED-CRD-style API, packaged with the external-snapshotter component. It is used by any CSI driver that supports snapshotting -- csi-hostpath in particular declares snapshot capability and its conformance specs exercise the whole snapshot lifecycle.

Because these are conformance-required for the Kubernetes storage e2e suite, u7s must serve the API group to pass any csi-hostpath focused run beyond the trivial provision/mount tests.

## Discovery

Discovered by ai/findings/operator-csi-hostpath-run-2026-08-06.md (scout on the operators --procs=4 csi-hostpath run 2026-08-06). Explicit citation in that findings doc under New bug candidate: snapshot family fails deterministically.

## Scope decisions the operator needs to make FIRST

This is a design bead, not an implementation bead yet. Options include but arent limited to:

1. Ship the VolumeSnapshot CRDs plus the external-snapshotter controller (upstream approach, replicates real k8s exactly).
2. Serve the API group natively in u7s (like our existing built-in resources -- consistent with u7s stance of not shipping controllers we can absorb, but a real amount of code).
3. Skip snapshot conformance entirely (would need --e2e-skip or --label-filter narrowing to exclude the snapshot family from any focused csi-hostpath run and from --all-e2e).

The current state is effectively option 3 by accident (the specs 404 immediately, sonobuoy records them as failing not skipping).

## Scout task

Read-only scout to estimate work for each of the 3 options: LoC/complexity, upstream references to mirror (external-snapshotter version + interfaces), interaction with existing csi-hostpath and CRD-serving code in u7s. Produce ai/findings/snapshot-api-scoping-2026-08-06.md with a per-option cost/blast-radius estimate.

Cross-refs: mayor-w44wg (DiskPressure) also touches csi-hostpath but is a different symptom class; mayor-f5sv4 (OOM) is independent.
notes: Cross-ref from mayor-6q2v2 triage (run 0807-0450, 4-proc, e2e.log): 7 failures in this run hit exactly this 'Resource snapshot.storage.k8s.io/v1/volumesnapshotclasses not found' signature, confirming the gap is still live and applies across all snapshot Testpatterns: [Testpattern: Pre-provisioned Snapshot (delete policy)] snapshottable ... check deletion (persistent) (L6845); [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (default fs)] provisioning should provision storage with snapshot data source [Feature:VolumeSnapshotDataSource] (L10337); [Testpattern: Ephemeral Snapshot (delete policy)] snapshottable ... check deletion (ephemeral) (L10621); [Testpattern: Ephemeral Snapshot (retain policy)] snapshottable ... check deletion (ephemeral) (L13080); [Testpattern: Pre-provisioned Snapshot (retain policy)] snapshottable ... check deletion (persistent) (L13924); [Testpattern: Dynamic Snapshot (delete policy)] snapshottable ... check deletion (persistent) (L14806); [Testpattern: Dynamic Snapshot (retain policy)] snapshottable ... check deletion (persistent) (L15057). NOTE anomaly worth a follow-up: [Testpattern: Dynamic PV (block volmode)] provisioning should provision storage with snapshot data source [Feature:VolumeSnapshotDataSource] (L3420) did NOT hit this 404 -- it got past the snapshot-data-source step entirely and failed later on a 'test -b /opt/0' device check (filed under mayor-rcujn). Worth checking whether block-volmode's snapshot-data-source path in provisioning.go takes a different route that doesn't touch the VolumeSnapshot API the same way default-fs does.

title: u7s_watch_broadcast_lagged_total prefix label is unbounded cardinality (Prometheus footgun)
description:
Discovered 2026-08-06 by mayor-drs2a Phase-1 observability audit (bed a11ac814, doc ai/findings/mayor-drs2a-observability-plan-2026-08-06.md).

`u7s_watch_broadcast_lagged_total{prefix}` (crates/store/src/metrics.rs:14-28, incremented at crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:1366-1368) has used the RAW, un-canonicalized (namespace-including) prefix as its label since it was added. This is a pre-existing unbounded-cardinality Prometheus footgun.

Impact: every distinct namespace × resource-type prefix that trips a Lagged event creates a new Prometheus time series. On a cluster that runs many namespaces (e.g. sonobuoy conformance runs create 100s), each namespace's Pod/Service/etc. watch prefixes each become their own label value. A single Lagged burst produces N new series that persist for the entire Prometheus retention window.

The observability plan proposes a new `u7s_watch_lag_recovery_duration_seconds{prefix_bucket}` histogram that uses a coarse first-two-path-segments `prefix_bucket()` heuristic to bound cardinality. The SAME canonicalization should be applied to the existing `u7s_watch_broadcast_lagged_total` counter's `prefix` label -- currently unrelated to the new plan, but same class of bug.

Fix scope: refactor the label to use the same `prefix_bucket()` helper (once introduced by the drs2a observability implementation). Trivial refactor -- ~5 LoC. Best done as a follow-up commit within the drs2a Phase-1 observability PR to avoid churning the metric contract twice.

Priority: P3 -- real footgun but currently latent (Lagged events are rare per bd memory watch-replay-is-global-ring-buffer-not-per-resource-relist; a real cardinality explosion has not been reported).

Cross-references:
- mayor-drs2a (parent -- Stage-2 ring sharding + observability that this bead's fix will piggy-back on).
- ai/findings/mayor-drs2a-observability-plan-2026-08-06.md (source of the finding).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1025 (piggy-backed on mayor-drs2a Phase-1 observability commit)

title: CRD-backed resources have no scale subresource — CRD-targeted HPA gets immediate 404
description:
Untriaged sub-finding surfaced while investigating mayor-4mxi3 Signature #6 (not
independently live-reproduced — time-boxed per mayor-4mxi3's dispatch instructions,
which called this out as only a "time-permitting bonus" after the primary target).
Recorded here as a scoped, actionable follow-up rather than left buried in the parent
bead's notes.

mayor-4mxi3's own Signature #7 (1/31 in the original aggregate run): a CRD-targeted HPA
gets a near-instant 404 ("Told to stop trying after 0.022s...the server could not find
the requested resource") when reading the CRD-backed target's replica count — the
~0.022s response time (vs the multi-minute timeouts elsewhere in the same run) is
itself evidence this is a hard "route does not exist" 404, not a data/timing/contention
issue like Signature #1 turned out to be.

CODE-LEVEL CONFIRMATION (grep only, not live-verified): crates/apiserver/src/handlers/
cr.rs implements the `status` subresource for CRDs (see `has_status_subresource`,
gated on `subresources.status` being present on the CRD's version) but has no
equivalent for `subresources.scale` anywhere — no route, no handler, no reference to
`specReplicasPath`/`statusReplicasPath`/`labelSelectorPath` (the three JSONPath fields
upstream's CRD scale-subresource spec requires) in the file or anywhere else in
crates/apiserver/src. apps/v1 workloads (Deployment/ReplicaSet/StatefulSet/RC) DO get a
scale subresource (handlers/scale.rs), but that implementation is hardcoded to those
resource kinds' known JSON shape (`spec.replicas`/`status.replicas`) — it is not
reachable for, nor written to be generic over, arbitrary CRD-defined replica/selector
field paths.

This is a materially smaller, more clearly-scoped gap than the metrics.k8s.io finding
(mayor-x0i0f): implementing generic CRD scale-subresource support requires reading the
three JSONPath-ish config fields from the CRD's `subresources.scale` spec and doing
get/set through them generically (rather than assuming `spec.replicas`/
`status.replicas` field names), then wiring GET/PUT/PATCH routes for it analogous to
the existing apps/v1 scale.rs handlers. Worth checking whether a JSONPath-subset parser
already exists anywhere in this codebase (e.g. for CEL/webhook match conditions) before
reaching for a new dependency — minimal-dependencies stance applies.

NEXT STEP FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: live-reproduce first (a minimal CRD with
`subresources: {scale: {...}}` + an HPA targeting it, on a fresh single-VM stack) before
implementing — this bead's own root-cause is grep-derived, not live-confirmed, per
mayor-4mxi3's explicit re-verify-live guidance.

Cross-reference: mayor-4mxi3 (parent characterization bead, Signature #7 — 1/31
original-run failures). Distinct from mayor-7ki1k/PR #989 (Scale.status.selector fix
for apps/v1 workloads, predates and does not touch CRDs at all).

title: scheduler: NodeTally::assume doesn't record hostPort claims (race window)
description: NodeTally::assume (the fast-path recording a scheduler-decided bind before its HTTP call completes) leaves TalliedPod.host_ports empty — only NodeTally::apply_event (a real watch event) populates it, since assume()'s current 5-arg signature is called directly by crates/scheduler/src/main.rs's own test module and widening it was out of scope for mayor-9b7t1 (lib.rs-only). This leaves a narrow race: a hostPort a scheduling decision just reserved on a node is invisible to the NodePorts filter for other concurrent decisions until the real bind's watch event round-trips back — analogous to the read-after-write race 'requests' already closed for cpu/memory. Not exercised by the sequential conformance test (predicates.go:706), but could let two pods requesting the same hostPort get bound to the same node under concurrent scheduling load. Fix: thread host_ports through assume()'s signature (and both main.rs call sites) once a coordinated main.rs edit is in scope.
close_reason: PR #1009 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/1009

title: cleanup(store): list_sync leaves read_conn transaction open on early-return error path, no rollback
description: Discovered mayor-z1p1u worker session while investigating an unrelated admission-webhook conformance failure (that bug turned out NOT to be caused by this). crates/store/src/sqlite.rs list_sync (roughly lines 694-939) can early-return with a question-mark operator between its BEGIN DEFERRED and COMMIT, leaving the read connection mid-transaction with no rollback. The existing last_written_revision staleness guard in Store::get() was confirmed (via a targeted, since-reverted unit test) to correctly recover from this specific wedge by falling back to write_conn, so this is not currently causing observable bugs -- but it is a latent correctness smell worth closing so a future change to that guard does not silently reintroduce a stale-read hazard. Fix: ensure list_sync rolls back (or the transaction is scoped so Rust drop semantics roll back automatically) on every early-return error path, not just the success path.
close_reason: PR #1001 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/1001

title: fix(apiserver): mutating-webhook namespaceSelector never matches a namespace label patched after namespace creation
description:
Conformance run temp/e2e/0804-1447-conformance failed sig-api-machinery AdmissionWebhook listing mutating webhooks should work Conformance at k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/apimachinery/webhook.go:689. NOT the same spec PR #999 fixed (that was should be able to deny pod and configmap creation, a connect_timeout truncation bug). Evidence in the run is present that #999s fix IS active in this binary (apiserver.log:205666 shows elapsed_ms=10001 timed_out=true for a timeout=10s webhook call, i.e. connect_timeout correctly scaled, not capped at 5s), so this is a different, newly surfaced root cause, not a #999 regression.

Failure: creating a configMap in the tests own namespace webhook-5969 never gets mutated by the tests own mutating webhook adding-configmap-data-stage-1.k8s.io, which times out after 15318ms with a 500 (apiserver.log:1473161). Root apiserver.log evidence: the webhook is scoped with NamespaceSelector MatchLabels f.UniqueName=true (see temp/research/webhook-test.go:2739-2741, newMutateConfigMapWebhookFixture). The test framework PATCHes namespace webhook-5969 successfully at 14:29:16.394592Z (apiserver.log:1305539, status=200) which should set that label. But every single admission evaluation of this webhook against namespace webhook-5969 -- 14515 occurrences total, including ones as late as 14:29:41.64, seven seconds after the test already failed at 14:29:34 -- logs skipped: namespace webhook-5969 does not match namespaceSelector (admission.rs:1230). The label match never succeeds even long after the patch landed.

Suspect code: crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs fetch_namespace_labels (line 409-431) does a fresh state.store.get per call, so it is not an obviously-cached snapshot -- but something between the successful PATCH and this read is not seeing the new label. Three hypotheses a worker should verify directly against a live repro rather than guess: (a) store.get has read-after-write staleness for the namespace object relative to a concurrent PATCH commit, (b) label_selector_matches (grep admission.rs) has a matching bug e.g. only checks MatchLabels keys that already existed at object-fetch time or mishandles a single-key selector, (c) the 14:29:16.394592Z PATCH was not actually the label-setting patch (verify its request body) and the framework labels the namespace via a different call this repo may be missing or mishandling -- check how the e2e framework normally applies this label (CreateNamespace helper, or a later Patch) and confirm our apiserver actually persists it by reading the namespace object back from sqlite directly.

This is a sonobuoy/admission-webhook-exercised code path -- Lima VM protocol applies, kubectl-first diagnosis per ai/prompts/vm-operations.md, cargo tests alone are not sufficient.

Fix-verification requirement (project standing policy, see bd memory fix-verification-required-before-merge): reproduce the failure live via kubectl against a MutatingWebhookConfiguration with a NamespaceSelector keyed to a label applied via a namespace Patch AFTER namespace creation, confirm it fails before the fix and passes after, then run sonobuoy --focus for this exact spec as the final gate. Do not just patch the code and assume -- prove the before/after against the real bug.
notes:
INVESTIGATION SUMMARY (worker session, could not confirm root cause -- reporting back per bead instructions rather than forcing an unverified fix):

1. Hypothesis 1 (wrong/missing PATCH) -- DISPROVEN with direct evidence. Fetched
   k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/apimachinery/webhook.go@release-1.36. Confirmed
   `labelNamespace(ctx, f, f.Namespace.Name)` (line ~2404-2416, using
   types.StrategicMergePatchType) runs in the shared `BeforeEach` (line ~91-97) for
   ALL AdmissionWebhook tests, before any webhook configs are created. This IS the
   exact 14:29:16.394592Z PATCH cited in the bead. f.UniqueName == f.Namespace.Name
   for this suite (SkipNamespaceCreation=false), so the namespaceSelector key really
   is the namespace's own name.

2. Hypothesis 2 (store read-after-write staleness) -- could NOT reproduce live
   despite an extensive matrix of kubectl-level repros against a real file-backed
   (WAL-mode) apiserver on lima-node-4: single webhook, 2/6/7/8 duplicate-named
   MutatingWebhookConfigurations (matching the real test's 10x duplicate shape),
   webhook-config names sharing the namespace's own name as prefix (exact upstream
   naming collision), timing gaps from milliseconds to 8+ seconds between patch and
   create, a 40x rapid serial burst, and a genuine 8-way TRUE PARALLEL stress (xargs
   -P8, 5 rounds of concurrent create+delete across 8 namespaces). In every case the
   correctly-scoped webhook fired and only genuinely non-matching webhooks were
   skipped -- never a false skip of the intended match.

   Also ran a targeted unit-test experiment (not committed -- reverted) that
   deliberately leaves the store's read_conn mid-transaction (BEGIN DEFERRED, one
   query, then an error before COMMIT -- exactly what an early `?`-return in
   list_sync would do) and then verifies get() after a later write. The existing
   `last_written_revision` staleness guard in Store::get() DOES correctly recover
   in this scenario (falls back to write_conn), so a wedged read-connection
   transaction from list_sync's missing rollback-on-error (a real, separate code
   smell I found in crates/store/src/sqlite.rs list_sync, lines ~694-939) does NOT
   explain this bug either.

3. Hypothesis 3 (label_selector_matches bug) -- code review + all of the above live
   repros show correct matching in every tested shape (single key, namespace name as
   key, multiple selectors evaluated in the same admission pass).

4. Ran the ACTUAL failing spec via sonobuoy --focus "listing mutating webhooks
   should work" against current main (includes #999) on lima-node-4: SUCCESS, 1
   Passed / 0 Failed / 0 Pending. Result:
   temp/e2e/0804-2316-listing-mutating-webhooks-should-work (worker-local, not
   committed -- gitignored).

CONCLUSION: could not reproduce via any means available to a single worker
(kubectl-level synthetic load, true parallel stress, or a solo focused sonobuoy
run). The original failure came from a FULL certified-conformance run with
--procs=16 -- i.e. 16 OTHER ginkgo specs' worth of concurrent system load/CPU
contention that a focused single-spec run does not reproduce (ginkgo still passes
--procs=16 to a focused run, but with only 1 spec active there is no genuine
contention). Recommend: (a) treat as possibly load-dependent/flaky pending a
repeat sighting in a fresh full conformance run, and/or (b) if it recurs, capture
the FULL raw apiserver.log from that run (not just excerpted line numbers) so a
future worker can reconstruct the exact request interleaving instead of
re-deriving hypotheses from scratch. No code changes made or committed this
session (worktree left clean).
MAYOR REVIEW: worker findings verified (worktree confirmed clean/no commits, mayor checkout unaffected). No fix shipped -- reclassifying as suspected load-dependent flake, not a confirmed regression. Downgrading P1 -> P3 and unclaiming pending a repeat sighting in a fresh FULL conformance run (per worker recommendation, capture the complete raw apiserver.log if it recurs, not excerpts). Do not re-dispatch on kubectl-level or focused-run repro attempts alone -- those are proven insufficient to reproduce this. Worktree agent-a53ad08b6b7a05cd4 removed after this review (clean, no PR).

title: apiserver: ResourceClaim DeviceRequest.Exactly.Count never defaults to 1 (ExactCount mode)
description:
Discovered while investigating mayor-wp3wj (DRA allocation never happens).

Upstream contract (staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go, AllocationMode doc comment on DeviceRequest): "If the mode is ExactCount and count is not specified, the default count is one." Real kube-apiserver applies this via SetDefaults_ExactDeviceRequest during admission/defaulting.

u7s's apiserver registers ResourceClaim (and ResourceClaimTemplate) as a generic CRUD resource (crates/apiserver/src/state.rs ~line 1372, rm("ResourceClaim", true, true)) with no type-specific defaulting pass. A ResourceClaim created via the typed Go client with Devices.Requests[0].Exactly = {DeviceClassName: "..."} (Count left as its Go zero value, omitted on the wire) round-trips through u7s's generic JSON store and is persisted/served with count effectively 0/absent instead of being defaulted to 1 -- confirmed live via `kubectl get resourceclaims -o yaml` showing spec.devices.requests[0].exactly.count: 0 for a claim that upstream Kubernetes would show as count: 1.

This is a real, narrow, standalone correctness bug independent of whether allocation itself is implemented (see mayor-wp3wj for that much larger gap) -- any consumer that reads spec.devices.requests[].exactly.count and assumes upstream defaulting occurred (e.g. a future DRA scheduler plugin, or any client polling this field) will silently see 0 instead of 1.

Fix should live wherever u7s does other generic per-Kind defaulting/admission (if such a mechanism exists) or as a small ResourceClaim-specific normalization step in the create/update path in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs or resource_gen_adapter.rs. Needs investigation into whether u7s has ANY existing defaulting-on-create precedent to follow (Rule 11) before picking an implementation site.

Regression test (Rule 14): create a ResourceClaim with Exactly.DeviceClassName set and Count omitted; GET it back; assert count == 1, not 0.
close_reason: PR #1066 opened. default_resourceclaim added to handlers/defaults.rs, wired into apply_defaults for (resource.k8s.io, resourceclaims). Also added default_resourceclaimtemplate for (resource.k8s.io, resourceclaimtemplates) since upstream's SetObjectDefaults_ResourceClaimTemplate runs the identical defaulting over the template's embedded spec.spec.devices.requests[]. Mirrors upstream SetDefaults_ExactDeviceRequest semantics, including the allocationMode==ExactCount guard. Fail-on-revert test added and verified. Does NOT touch DRA allocation logic (mayor-wp3wj/8qcaw scope, separate).

title: [Feature:LoadBalancer] e2e tests can never pass — no cloud-controller-manager / LB provisioner in u7s; consider skip-list
description:
During the --all-e2e conformance run (temp/e2e/0803-1624-conformance,
2026-08-03), 2 loadbalancers-* namespaces (loadbalancers-9693, loadbalancers-1424)
were reaped by the 10-minute watchdog while running
"[sig-network] LoadBalancers [Feature:LoadBalancer] ..." specs
(test/e2e/network/loadbalancer.go, basename "loadbalancers").

u7s runs no cloud-controller-manager in this conformance setup (only
kube-controller-manager is started — see scripts/conformance step 4/6) and
has no LoadBalancer status/ingress-IP synthesis logic anywhere in the
apiserver (grepped crates/apiserver for LoadBalancer-status-related code:
only generated proto message types exist, no controller/handler that ever
populates status.loadBalancer.ingress). Any `type: LoadBalancer` Service
test therefore spins forever waiting for an external IP that will never be
assigned, guaranteeing it gets force-reaped by the conformance watchdog
regardless of [Slow]/[Flaky] tagging.

This isn't a hang bug to fix in u7s (no cloud provider means no LB, by
design, until such support is added) — it's a scope gap in what --all-e2e's
E2E_SKIP currently excludes (E2E_SKIP=[Disruptive]|[Flaky]|[Slow] does not
exclude [Feature:LoadBalancer]).

Suggested options:
(a) Add [Feature:LoadBalancer] to the standard --all-e2e E2E_SKIP list until
    u7s implements a LoadBalancer provisioner (even a fake/local one).
(b) Document as a known, permanent non-conformant gap and accept the
    resulting watchdog reaps as expected noise (worse: they burn ~10 min of
    watchdog time each, real wall-clock cost during future runs).

Findings doc (not committed, local only):

title: DEFER (unverified) — watchdog threshold vs. generic storage testsuites: apparent 15min need was actually an unrelated scheduler re-bind bug (mayor-4526p), re-measure after that's fixed
description:
During the --all-e2e conformance run (temp/e2e/0803-1624-conformance,
2026-08-03), the "ephemeral" basename accounted for 14 of the 26 non-OOM-
adjacent namespace reaps by scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh's
watchdog_loop (10-minute Active threshold), and "provisioning" for 1 more —
by far the largest groups. Both are generic storageframework.TestSuite base
names (test/e2e/storage/testsuites/ephemeral.go and .../provisioning.go)
shared across dozens of driver x volume-mode combinations, not one
repeatedly-hanging test.

Representative evidence that these are legitimately slow, not hung:
- ephemeral-6126 ("CSI Volumes [Driver: csi-hostpath] ... ephemeral should
  support multiple inline ephemeral volumes", created 14:39:16, watchdog
  reaped it at 14:49:21/604s) — the test's OWN cleanup calls (DELETE
  csidrivers/csi-hostpath-ephemeral-6126, DELETE namespace) don't happen
  until 14:54:20, ~5 minutes AFTER the watchdog already force-deleted it —
  both return 404 (already gone). The test was still making real progress
  toward a natural ~15min total runtime.
- provisioning-1338 ("In-tree Volumes [Driver: nfs3] ... provisioning should
  provision storage with mount options", created 14:51:43, watchdog reaped
  it at 15:01:46/601s) — same pattern: the test's own AfterEach cleanup
  sequence runs at 15:06:44 (~5 min after the reap), every delete returning
  404.

scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh's watchdog_loop already documents
exactly this class of problem for one specific known case (the CronJob
5-minute gomega.Consistently check, which is why the threshold is 10 min
rather than a tighter value) — but that precedent doesn't cover the
ephemeral/provisioning generic storage testsuites, which routinely need
noticeably longer than 10 minutes for some driver/pattern combinations
(NFS server startup + PV binding + pod scheduling + write/verify + cleanup)
without being upstream-tagged [Slow].

Options to consider (not decided here):
(a) Raise the Active threshold specifically for namespaces whose basename is
    in a known-slower set (ephemeral, provisioning), similar to how the
    15-minute any-phase threshold already differs from the 10-minute Active
    one.
(b) Raise the global Active threshold (simpler, but weakens the "genuine
    hang gets reaped promptly" property the comment already calls out).
(c) Determine whether these specific driver/pattern combinations should
    upstream-carry [Slow] in a newer k8s release and are just missing it in
    the pinned e2e.test binary version here — if so, no watchdog change
    needed, just wait for a version bump or don't run --all-e2e against this
    combination.

Findings doc (not committed, local only):
ai/findings/all-e2e-watchdog-reap-analysis-2026-08-04.md, section 4c.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-04 (operator asked directly, investigated properly this time): the ephemeral/provisioning reaps in the 0803-1624 --all-e2e run are NOT a watchdog-timing issue at all -- confirmed via the archived apiserver.log + sonobuoy's own resources/ns/*/core_v1_events.json snapshots.

ephemeral-6126 (and the same-pattern ephemeral-654): the test polls GET .../pods/inline-volume-tester-* every ~2 seconds, UNIFORMLY, for its ENTIRE lifetime (30 requests/minute, 15 straight minutes, confirmed via apiserver.log bucketed by minute) -- this is a wait-loop that never progresses, not a slow-but-advancing test. ephemeral-654's own kubelet event confirms why: FailedMount x26, 'failed to get Plugin from volumeSpec for volume "my-volume-0" err=no volume plugin matched' -- the CSI driver that would register this volume plugin was never available.

Traced further to ephemeral-654's companion namespace ephemeral-654-1772 (where the CSI driver itself deploys, per this test suite's own setup convention): csi-hostpathplugin-0's events show 'Failed to pull image registry.k8s.io/sig-storage/{livenessprobe:v2.18.0,csi-attacher:v4.11.0,csi-provisioner:v6.1.1}: RegistryUnavailable ... dial tcp 34.96.108.209:443: connect: connection refused'. The CSI driver's own sidecar containers never started because their images never pulled -- a network connectivity failure to registry.k8s.io from inside the Lima VM, NOT a u7s bug.

provisioning-7014 shows the matching downstream symptom for the OTHER large reap group: ProvisioningFailed, 'storageclass.storage.k8s.io "provisioning-7014" not found' x26 -- same root (the driver's controller-side component that creates the StorageClass never came up).

Conclusion: no watchdog threshold change would fix this -- the underlying dependency (CSI driver image pull) never succeeds, so the test would poll forever regardless of timeout. This is a concrete, high-value data point for the ALREADY-TRACKED image-pull reliability problem (mayor-5fkx5's pre-pull retry, the broader usernet-burst mitigation thread) -- cross-referencing there. Closing this bead's original 'raise the threshold' framing as moot; the watchdog was doing exactly the right thing by reaping these.
close_reason: Notes already conclude this is moot (root-caused 2026-08-04): the ephemeral/provisioning reaps were CSI driver image-pull failures (registry.k8s.io connection refused from the Lima VM), not a watchdog-timing issue -- the watchdog was correctly reaping tests that would have polled forever regardless of threshold. Cross-referenced to mayor-5fkx5 (image pre-pull). Closing now since the investigation was already complete but never formally closed.

title: feat(scheduler): enforce inter-pod affinity/anti-affinity (InterPodAffinity Filter)
description:
u7s's scheduler has ZERO matching logic for spec.affinity.podAffinity /
spec.affinity.podAntiAffinity anywhere in crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs
(confirmed via grep across the whole file). Only spec.affinity.nodeAffinity
is implemented (node_affinity_matches, required-only). A pod that sets
podAffinity/podAntiAffinity is scheduled as if it had no affinity
constraints at all.

This is worse at the apiserver layer than topologySpreadConstraints: the
protobuf decode path (crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs,
gen_node_affinity_to_json, line 994) explicitly documents "Only nodeAffinity
is decoded here -- podAffinity/podAntiAffinity are dropped from the returned
JSON" -- a protobuf-encoded pod create/update (the default wire format for
client-go clientsets: e2e test binaries, controllers) that sets ONLY
podAffinity/podAntiAffinity (no nodeAffinity) round-trips as
spec.affinity: {} -- total silent data loss, not just an unenforced field.
The JSON path (kubectl apply -f) is unaffected since pod specs are stored
as generic JSON there and podAffinity/podAntiAffinity survive untouched --
only the strict protobuf decoder has this narrower drop.

CONFORMANCE STATUS (verified against upstream release-1.36 source, not
assumed): NOT a conformance gap for the scheduler-enforcement half.
Checked test/e2e/scheduling/priorities.go's "Pod should be scheduled to
node that don't match the PodAntiAffinity terms" -- plain `ginkgo.It`, not
`framework.ConformanceIt`. A comment in predicates.go ("TODO: upgrade calls
in PodAffinity tests when we're able to run them") corroborates upstream
itself treats pod-affinity e2e tests as not reliably conformance-required.
The only other ConformanceIt+PodAffinity co-occurrence found repo-wide
(test/e2e/apps/deployment.go) uses PodAntiAffinity purely as an internal
pinning mechanism inside a LoadBalancer rolling-update helper, not as a
directly-asserted feature, and that test path isn't itself a ConformanceIt
block. This is a real, user-facing PodSpec API completeness gap, not a
conformance blocker.

SCOPE (two parts, can be split further if picked up):
1. (Scheduler) Implement a Filter-phase check for
   requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution podAffinity/podAntiAffinity
   terms against pods already tallied per node (reuse NodeTally). Treat
   preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution as a Score-phase concern
   deferred until a Score phase exists (there is none today).
2. (Apiserver, smaller/independent) Fix gen_node_affinity_to_json's
   protobuf-decode drop of podAffinity/podAntiAffinity -- this is a pure
   data-loss bug independent of whether the scheduler acts on the fields yet
   (matches the pattern mayor-w5eoy fixed for topologySpreadConstraints and
   other fields). Could be split into its own smaller apiserver-only bead
   if whoever picks this up wants to land the decode fix first.

Related: mayor-pxm9c (in-flight) is the separate, minimal least-loaded
tie-break fix for load-spreading -- do not duplicate; this bead is a
distinct Filter dimension (explicit user-declared pod-to-pod placement
rules), not general spreading.

title: feat(scheduler): enforce topologySpreadConstraints (PodTopologySpread Filter)
description:
u7s's scheduler has ZERO handling of spec.topologySpreadConstraints anywhere
in crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs (confirmed via grep across the whole file: no
matches for topologySpreadConstraints/topology_spread). The apiserver DOES
correctly decode and round-trip this field end-to-end though -- both the JSON
path and, since PR #794 (mayor-w5eoy), the protobuf wire path
(crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs:1407-1468), and the strategic-merge
patch key "topologyKey" is registered (crates/apiserver/src/patch.rs). The
apiserver's own code comment at core_gen_adapter.rs:1407-1410 already
documents the gap: "scheduler-enforced pod spreading... dropping this makes
the scheduler treat a pod... as unconstrained" -- the field survives
`kubectl get pod -o yaml` faithfully, but nothing in the Filter phase acts on
it, so a pod that asks to be spread across zones/hostnames can land
arbitrarily (in practice, thanks to the current first-fit
select_node_with_capacity, it piles onto whichever node is tried first).

CONFORMANCE STATUS (verified against upstream release-1.36 source, not
assumed): NOT a conformance gap. Checked
test/e2e/scheduling/predicates.go's "PodTopologySpread Filtering" ->
"validates 4 pods with MaxSkew=1 are evenly distributed into 2 nodes" (the
only e2e coverage for this field) -- it's a plain `ginkgo.It`, not
`framework.ConformanceIt`. Kubernetes conformance policy deliberately
excludes scheduler behaviors that assume multi-node topology since a
conformant cluster may be single-node. This is a real, user-facing PodSpec
API completeness gap (an explicit field a workload owner can set and have
silently ignored), not a conformance blocker -- prioritize accordingly, below
anything gating conformance.

SCOPE: implement a Filter-phase check in crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs (likely
alongside select_node_with_capacity / node_qualifies_for_pod) that, for each
constraint in spec.topologySpreadConstraints, computes per-topology-domain
pod counts (using the existing NodeTally/node-usage infrastructure
mayor-pxm9c is adding to for load-spreading) and rejects candidate nodes that
would push skew beyond maxSkew when whenUnsatisfiable=DoNotSchedule (the
ScheduleAnyway case can be treated as a soft/no-op preference given there is
no Score phase yet). Do NOT duplicate mayor-pxm9c's pod-count tie-break scope
-- this is a distinct Filter dimension keyed by topologyKey + labelSelector,
not general load-spreading.

Related: mayor-w5eoy (closed) fixed the protobuf decode-drop at the apiserver
layer only; scheduler enforcement was explicitly out of scope there.
Related: mayor-pxm9c (in-flight) is the separate, minimal least-loaded
tie-break fix -- do not duplicate.

title: investigate(perf): podtemplate create latency climbs 50ms to 97ms over ~400 sequential creates in API chunking conformance test
description: DEFER severity - needs more data before deciding if this is real. Follow-on from a clean-run perf audit of temp/e2e/0803-1139-conformance (483/483 passed, no correctness impact). The sig-api-machinery API chunking conformance test creates about 430 podtemplates in one namespace (chunking-2157) to exercise LIST continue tokens. Request-level latency_ms for the POST .../podtemplates calls climbs from about 50ms early in the sequence to about 97ms late (example: apiserver.log line 42033, latency_ms=97, request_id=2403cb07). Ruled out store-layer cost as the driver: the corresponding u7s_store::sqlite namespaced-create-committed lines for the same keys stay at 3-5ms elapsed_ms throughout, not growing. The surrounding log context around the slow request (apiserver.log lines 42010-42033) shows it interleaved at sub-millisecond granularity with dozens of unrelated concurrent requests from other parallel-running conformance tests, which is at least as plausible an explanation (general scheduling and queueing jitter under N-way ginkgo parallelism) as a real O(n)-per-insert algorithmic cost specific to the podtemplates create path. Not confident enough either way from this data alone to call it a bug. Next step if picked up: reproduce with an isolated non-parallel run (ginkgo --focus matching just this test, no other concurrent tests) and see whether the same latency growth appears in isolation - if it does, this points to a real per-insert cost that scales with existing object count in a namespace or resource type (worth checking indexing/lookup patterns in the create path); if it does not reproduce in isolation, this was concurrent-load noise and can be closed as non-issue. Findings doc: ai/findings/conformance-clean-run-perf-audit-2026-08-03.md in worker worktree agent-a86fbfa20f37d32fa (gitignored).

title: fix(scheduler): tracing_subscriber init missing .with_ansi(false), scheduler.log still has embedded ANSI escape codes
description: LOW severity. Follow-on from a clean-run perf audit of temp/e2e/0803-1139-conformance. crates/apiserver/src/lib.rs line 173 calls tracing_subscriber::fmt().with_ansi(false) per the closed mayor-upts bead and PR 267 (apiserver.log full of ANSI escape sequences making it unreadable in files and log viewers). crates/scheduler/src/main.rs line 703 has its own separate tracing_subscriber::fmt() init that never got the same treatment: it calls .with_env_filter(...).init() with no .with_ansi(false) call at all. Confirmed empirically during this audit: scheduler.log lines look like 2026-08-03T11:17:44.601796Z ESC[34mDEBUGESC[0m ESC[2mu7s_schedulerESC[2m:ESC[0m bind_pod: POST completed ESC[3mpodESC[2m=ESC[0mcoredns... elapsed_ms is split by escape codes from its own value, so a plain grep -oE elapsed_ms=[0-9]+ against scheduler.log silently matches nothing and requires stripping ANSI codes first to extract structured fields. Fix: add the same .with_ansi(false) call used in crates/apiserver/src/lib.rs to the tracing_subscriber::fmt() chain in crates/scheduler/src/main.rs around line 703. One-line change, same shape as PR 267. Regression test: none needed beyond a quick manual verification the resulting scheduler.log has no ESC bytes, consistent with how mayor-upts was verified (this is cosmetic/observability, not behavior-affecting). title: MISDIAGNOSED — see notes + follow-on: kubelet exec/log proxy TLS BadSignature was a stale-VM cert/CA mismatch, not a proxy.rs bug
description:
Live-forensics audit (mayor-rqqee, findings doc ai/findings/conformance-2node-novznat-regression-2026-08-03.md in worker worktree agent-a96a37f2aff439554, gitignored) of a 2-node conformance run (temp/e2e/0803-1011-conformance, 157 failures/483 executed, vs baseline temp/e2e/0803-0053-conformance at 1 failure/483) found the DOMINANT failure cluster (70+/157 directly, likely 100+/157 counting timeout/context-deadline variants) is caused by kubelet exec/log proxy TLS connection failures, not test flakiness.

apiserver.log (this run) shows:
- 2318x `WARN u7s_apiserver::handlers::proxy: exec proxy error: kubelet exec connect failed: IO error: invalid peer certificate: BadSignature`
- 1520x `GET .../pods/{name}/log?container=...` responses with `status=502`
- Steady rate throughout the run's ~50min wall-clock (89-288/min), not a single spike.

These surface to ginkgo as e.g. `[FAILED] failed to get logs from POD for CONTAINER: an error on the server ("unknown") has prevented the request from succeeding (get pods POD)` across secrets/configmap/downwardAPI/projected/subpath volume tests (sig-storage), and `Unexpected error getting pod logs: timed out waiting for the condition` (sig-auth ServiceAccountIssuerDiscovery) — i.e. it hits every test that uses the framework's pod-logs helper, cutting across multiple sig-* areas, not just sig-storage.

CONFIRMED NEW vs baseline: the baseline run's own preserved apiserver.log (temp/e2e/0803-0053-conformance/host-logs/apiserver.log, 666MB, full run) has ZERO occurrences of "BadSignature", "exec proxy error", or log-endpoint 502s.

RULED OUT as a recent-merge regression: the only commits landing between baseline (00:53 UTC) and this run (09:21 UTC) are #978 (store RING_CAPACITY), #979 (replace_pod status), #980+#981 (pre-pull added+reverted) — none touch crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs. The one PR touching kubelet TLS, #975 "HTTP/2 (ALPN h2) for kubelet watch multiplexing" (6ba2982f), landed well before baseline (already present when baseline ran clean) and only touches crates/apiserver/src/lib.rs + src/tls.rs (server-side ALPN for INBOUND kubelet watch connections) — not the outbound exec/log client-dial path this bug lives in.

Implicated code: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs — build_kubelet_tls_config (~line 577-621) and its callers: run_exec_proxy (~1049-1071, fresh TLS dial per exec call via tokio_tungstenite::connect_async_tls_with_config, NO retry on failure) and the plain GET-log kubelet-proxy dial path (~line 1656). Each exec/log/attach request establishes a brand-new short-lived TLS connection to the kubelet with no retry/backoff.

Working hypothesis (NOT yet isolated — needs a dedicated repro, not more log archaeology): this is a load/concurrency-dependent reliability bug in the per-request kubelet TLS dial that reproduces once concurrent connection volume/timing crosses some threshold this run hit (2908s wall-clock, likely amplified by cross-VM host contention per mayor-igjn1's measured 20-40x failure-rate jump under concurrent multi-VM load) and baseline (1233s wall-clock) never did. Candidate mechanisms to investigate: TLS session-cache collision across concurrent dials, TCP segment reordering under host contention truncating what rustls reads before it declares the signature invalid, or a connection-pool/reuse bug despite each call intending a fresh connection.

Next step: reproduce by ramping concurrent exec/log calls against a live kubelet (kubectl exec/logs in a loop, or a targeted load test) and watch for BadSignature onset at a specific concurrency threshold, OR instrument proxy.rs to log the actual peer cert bytes/length on BadSignature to see if it's truncated. Add retry/backoff on kubelet TLS dial failure regardless of root cause (defense in depth — a single retry would likely absorb most of these given the errors are logged as WARN and evidently often self-heal on the next attempt, going by how few of the 2318 warnings become the ~70 hard test failures).

Severity: HIGH — this is the majority root cause of the 157-failure regression.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-03: original 'latent load-dependent TLS reliability bug' diagnosis is WRONG. Actual root cause found via live cert inspection during a follow-up run: lima-node's kubelet serving cert (openssl s_client 127.0.0.1:10250) has notBefore=Aug 3 07:06:39 2026, predating this run's own reset/provisioning by 3.5h, while lima-node-3's cert (127.0.0.1:10261) has notBefore=Aug 3 10:40:04 matching this run's provisioning exactly. openssl verify -CAfile temp/u7s/ca.crt against lima-node's cert FAILS with 'certificate signature failure' (exact match to the apiserver's BadSignature error); lima-node-3's cert verifies OK. This is deterministic per-node (kubelet is presenting a cert signed by a now-defunct prior CA key), not load/concurrency-dependent -- proxy.rs is behaving correctly by rejecting a genuinely invalid cert. Real bug is in scripts/conformance/reset.sh:129 teardown_vm(): 'limactl delete --force "$vm" 2>/dev/null || true' silently swallows any delete failure, so if the VM is busy/held and delete fails, the OLD VM (with its OLD kubelet cert) survives into the next run while the host-side CA is freshly regenerated independently, producing exactly this CA/cert mismatch. See new bead for the actual fix. In-flight retry/backoff fix worker was stopped before completion -- retry cannot fix a 100%-deterministic per-node cert mismatch.
close_reason: Investigation was already complete and superseded -- notes already record the correction: real root cause was scripts/conformance/reset.sh's silent-swallowed limactl delete leaving a stale kubelet cert (mayor-zdrjr, fixed via PR #982, merged). This bead itself was never closed after filing that follow-on. Closing now as part of session-end hygiene.

title: reset.sh silently fails to kill multiple processes on same port (embedded newline in kill args)
description:
Discovered during mayor-5fkx5 dispatch (worker a0298869dc4dad845).

In scripts/conformance/reset.sh around lines 78-82: when lsof -ti tcp:\$PORT
returns multiple PIDs (newline-separated), the subsequent 'kill \$API_PID'
receives a single arg with embedded newlines. kill fails silently — process
is NOT actually killed despite the log message claiming success.

Symptoms: orphan processes accumulate across --reset cycles. Discovered because
the worker had to manually pkill -f leftover processes on its worktree-specific
path pattern.

Fix: pass the PID list to kill as multiple separate arguments — e.g.
'kill \$API_PIDS' after 'API_PIDS=(\$(lsof -ti tcp:\$PORT))' array assignment,
or 'echo "\$API_PID" | xargs kill'.

Low-severity, but worth fixing before we accumulate hard-to-track orphans
after many conformance cycles.

title: gen_pod_status_to_json drops PodStatus.observedGeneration on protobuf status decode
description:
Found in passing while investigating mayor-82wpg (see
ai/findings/pod-observed-generation-2026-08-03.md,
worker/agent-ac79efa5d567fb62d).

crates/apiserver/src/core_gen_adapter.rs::gen_pod_status_to_json decodes a
protobuf-encoded PodStatus message into the JSON shape u7s stores/serves.
It maps PodCondition.observedGeneration (per-condition, proto field on
PodCondition) but does NOT map the top-level PodStatus.observedGeneration
(proto field 17, api-core-v1-generated.proto:4821) to JSON
`status.observedGeneration`.

This function is only reached when a client sends a protobuf-encoded write
to the /status subresource (the function doc comment says this is for
"client-go typed clients' UpdateStatus, which defaults to protobuf content
type" hitting replace_pod_status via PUT). Kubelet's own status updates use
JSON PATCH (application/strategic-merge-patch+json), so this gap does not
affect the kubelet path and is NOT the cause of mayor-82wpg's reported
failure — confirmed via live repro that kubelet's JSON PATCH path works.

Fix: add the same `if let Some(v) = status.observed_generation.filter(|&v|
v != 0) { m.insert("observedGeneration", v.into()); }` pattern already used
elsewhere in this file (e.g. the ReplicationController status decoder at
~line 2985) to gen_pod_status_to_json. Small, should ship with a regression
test asserting a protobuf PUT .../status carrying observedGeneration
survives decode (mirroring the existing "status.observedGeneration must
survive" test pattern in core_gen_adapter.rs around line 3327, which
currently only covers a different resource type).
close_reason: PR #983 opened: https://github.com/valerauko/u7s/pull/983

title: Re-verify [sig-node] pod generation/observedGeneration conformance test post-EMFILE fix
description:
mayor-82wpg claimed pod.status.observedGeneration was never populated,
breaking the [sig-node] "pod generation should start at 1 and increment
per update" test (test/e2e/node/pods.go:531, upstream release-1.36).

Investigation (see ai/findings/pod-observed-generation-2026-08-03.md in
worker/agent-ac79efa5d567fb62d) found NO code or config bug: the feature
gate (PodObservedGenerationTracking) is GA-locked-on since k8s 1.35, and
u7s's generic JSON status-patch merge (apply_status_patch in
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs) passes observedGeneration through
untouched with no allowlist to go stale. Live reproduction on current main
(stack brought up via scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --stack-only) showed
metadata.generation and status.observedGeneration converging correctly
end-to-end within 1-15s per spec update, well inside the test's 20s-per-step
timeout.

The likely explanation: the original failing run (0802-2344-conformance)
predates the apiserver FD/EMFILE crash fix (commit a0867a92 / PR #965,
PR #962). Apiserver instability under sustained load could plausibly drop
kubelet's status PATCH or the watch event carrying the generation bump,
producing the "stuck at 0" symptom without any gap in the observedGeneration
code path itself.

## Action needed

Re-run conformance with --focus 'pod generation should start at 1 and
increment per update' (or a fuller run including [sig-node] Pods specs)
against current main to confirm the test now passes reliably. If it still
flakes under full-suite load (not just a quiet manual repro), the real bug
is watch/status-patch latency under system load — a different, narrower
investigation than mayor-82wpg assumed.
close_reason: verified-fixed by 0806-1542-conformance run. The test '[sig-node] Pods Extended (pod generation) Pod Generation pod generation should start at 1 and increment per update [Conformance]' passes with status=passed, time=37.694s (see temp/e2e/0806-1542-conformance/plugins/e2e/results/global/junit_01.xml). Bead hypothesis confirmed: original 0802-2344 failure was masked by pre-EMFILE-fix apiserver instability (PR #965/#962), not a real observedGeneration code gap.

title: Evaluate alt Lima network driver / VM isolation as fallback usernet mitigations (mayor-mjt51 sub-questions 2/3, not run)
description:
Follow-on to mayor-mjt51's usernet-mitigation audit (findings:
ai/findings/usernet-mitigation-audit-2026-08-02.md, worker worktree
agent-a16f32c3c371fb6b8).

mayor-mjt51's dispatch specified 3 sub-questions to investigate in order,
stopping once one clearly won. Sub-question 1 (kubelet HTTP/2
multiplexing) produced a clear, well-evidenced, code-level answer inside
budget: the apiserver never supports HTTP/2, which is the primary
amplifier turning kubelet's per-reflector watch reconnects into a
150-200-connection SYN burst. Per the dispatch's own stopping rule,
sub-questions 2 and 3 were NOT run -- no new VM was provisioned, no VMs
were stopped, no code touched for this bead's scope. This is a deliberate
scoping decision (see the findings doc), not an oversight, and this bead
exists so that work isn't silently dropped.

Only pick this up if the HTTP/2 fix (tracked in the companion "Enable
HTTP/2..." bead) doesn't fully eliminate the blackhole once measured --
e.g. because non-kubelet clients (sonobuoy/ginkgo CLI traffic) don't
benefit from apiserver-side h2 the same way a long-lived kubelet process
does, or because the residual multiplexed connection count still exceeds
whatever usernet's internal limit turns out to be.

## Sub-question 2 (from mayor-mjt51, not run)
Does an alternative Lima network driver (vzNAT, socket_vmnet) eliminate
the blackhole? Method: read Lima's docs on network drivers for 4-VM
Mac-arm64 compatibility; provision a NEW test VM (do not touch
lima-node/lima-node-2/lima-node-3, the mayor's live stack) with the
alt driver; run the mayor-biy31 instrumentation
(scripts/conformance/instrument-vip-capture.sh) against a short
`--focus 'Guestbook application should create and stop a working

title: [Serial]-tagged conformance specs never actually run serially in our sonobuoy invocation (go-runner skip-filter gap)
description: mayor-xz6fg's parallelism experiment found that test/conformance/image/go-runner/cmd.go (release-1.36) only prepends the Serial skip pattern to ginkgo when E2E_SKIP is completely empty. sonobuoy's own e2e-skip default is never empty (Disruptive or NoExecuteTaintManager), so this fallback never fires in our deployment: neither the historical serial baseline (skip was empty but no parallel flag was set anyway, so moot) nor the 16-way experiment (parallel flag was dropped entirely) ever filtered Serial specs out. Net effect: Serial-tagged Kubernetes conformance specs, which rely on ginkgos skip=Serial convention rather than an actual ginkgo Serial decorator for mutual exclusion, run interleaved with everything else at both 1-way and 16-way concurrency. This looks pre-existing, not introduced by the 16-way experiment: the 16-way runs failure list includes a Serial-tagged Daemon set rollback spec, and the historical baselines two failures were both Serial-tagged too (garbage collector, scheduler preemption) suggesting Serial-spec interference may be a standing source of flakiness regardless of parallelism level. Action: decide whether to explicitly pass an e2e-skip value that prepends Serial for any future parallel run (mirroring the deprecated bash run_e2e.sh convention), or accept running Serial specs concurrently as a known tradeoff for our single-VM setup and document it. See ai/findings/parallelism-experiment-16-way-2026-08-02.md in mayor-xz6fg's worker worktree for full details.

title: docs: add scheduler.log to ai/prompts/vm-operations.md Logs table (host-side, temp/u7s/scheduler.log)
description:
## Bug

\`ai/prompts/vm-operations.md\` Logs table at L374-380 lists apiserver (host), konnectivity-server (host), KCM (VM), kubelet (VM), konnectivity-agent (kubectl logs) — but **omits scheduler**. Result: mayor dispatch briefs have been telling workers to grep \`limactl shell <vm> sudo grep ... /tmp/scheduler.log\` (matching the VM convention for KCM), when scheduler actually runs on the host and writes to \`temp/u7s/scheduler.log\` (matching the apiserver convention).

Verified live 2026-07-31: \`limactl shell lima-node ls /tmp/scheduler.log\` → \`No such file or directory\`; \`ls temp/u7s/scheduler.log\` → present. Same is true for apiserver (in table). KCM stays in-VM at \`/tmp/kcm.log\` (in table, correct).

## Impact

Workers dispatched with the wrong path get empty grep output — silent failure mode. Discovered when the h61va 2-node re-scout (2026-07-31) noted the dispatch brief's \`/tmp/scheduler.log\` path was wrong and corrected it to \`temp/u7s/scheduler.log\` on the host. Mayor-i4mwr's scout and this session's other scheduler-touching briefs may have gotten misleading (empty) log output but not noticed. Scheduler is a hot component for the recent sched-preemption regression class; getting its log path wrong in dispatch briefs is a real diagnosis-blocker.

## Fix

Add one row to the Logs table in ai/prompts/vm-operations.md:

| scheduler | \`temp/u7s/scheduler.log\` |

Also worth a one-line note under the table clarifying the convention: **components that run on the host (apiserver, scheduler, konnectivity-server) log to \`temp/u7s/*.log\`; components that run in the VM (KCM, kubelet) require \`limactl shell <VM>\` access** — so future mayors and workers understand the pattern rather than looking it up per-component.

## Acceptance criteria

- vm-operations.md Logs table includes scheduler with the correct host path.
- One-line "convention" clarifier added under the table.
- No other file changes.

## Not in scope

- Any code changes.

title: apiserver GC: propagationPolicy=Foreground doesn't add foregroundDeletion finalizer; RC hard-deletes before dependents drain, pre-existing conformance flake
description:
## Failure **Test:** \`[sig-api-machinery] Garbage collector should keep the rc around until all its pods are deleted if the deleteOptions says so [Serial] [Conformance]\` **File:** \`k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/apimachinery/garbage_collector.go:711\` **Run:** temp/e2e/0731-0640-conformance **Result:** RC's pods (simpletest.rc-*) stuck in \`Phase: Pending\` with \`ContainersNotReady\` at test timeout. From e2e.txt tail: - pods scheduled to lima-node with \`PodScheduled=True\`, \`NodeName: lima-node\` - containers stuck \`Waiting\` with \`ContainerStateWaiting\` populated - test wanted them to be either Running (then GC'd via foreground deleteOptions) or already gone ## Corrected regression scope Both today's failures were passing in 0730-1446 (444/446, only i4mwr + 0agv5 failing) and 0730-0222 baseline (446/446). Both are [Conformance]-tagged + [Serial] — always in the certified-conformance selection. This is a genuine regression between 0730-1446 SHA and HEAD \`af319a20\` (post-#956/#957/#958/#959). ## Suspects - **#957 (mayor-i4mwr, deferred-bind)** — TOP suspect. Pods stuck Pending after PodScheduled=True but before container start is the classic "scheduler bound them but kubelet never got the signal / bind didn't propagate" shape. If the deferred-bind path has a subtle propagation bug where the bind commits to the scheduler's in-memory state but the actual apiserver PATCH is delayed, pods sit Pending exactly like this. Note: sched-preemption critical-pod test (P1 sibling bead) is ALSO regressing on HEAD — high probability both share a root cause in #957. - **#956 (mayor-0agv5, webhook retry)** — weak. The webhook retry code only fires on connect-refused; wouldn't affect regular pod admission timing. - **#958/#959 (ClusterIP derivation)** — no obvious connection to pod lifecycle. ## Reproduction \`\`\` scripts/conformance/run-all.sh --vm --port

--kubelet-port \\ --workdir ./temp/u7s --reset \\ --focus 'should keep the rc around until all its pods are deleted' \`\`\` ## Scout task (SCOUT-ONLY) 1. Live-repro on HEAD, confirm the "pods stuck Pending" symptom. 2. **Fast hypothesis test**: revert #957 locally on top of HEAD, re-run the focus. If green → #957 is the shared root cause with the sibling P1 bead; both can be fixed together. 3. If #957 not the cause, check kubelet-side: are the pods actually being reported bound by the apiserver? Grep \`/tmp/apiserver.log\` for the RC pods; grep \`/tmp/kcm.log\` for GC + finalizer activity; grep \`/tmp/scheduler.log\` for bind events. 4. Findings doc at \`ai/findings/-gc-rc-pending-diagnosis-2026-07-31.md\`. Fix options with concrete code sketches. 5. **If sibling P1 bead's scout also finds #957 is the root cause**, coordinate: one fix probably covers both. Note the dependency in the findings doc. ## Acceptance criteria (for the eventual fix PR) - Live-repro on HEAD; kubectl + log evidence of the mechanism. - Fix + regression test that fails on revert. - Sonobuoy focus passes. - The mayor-i4mwr target test (\`validates basic preemption works\`) MUST still pass. - Sibling P1 sched-preemption test MUST also pass (if the fix covers both). ## Labels rationale P2: Conformance regression, but the P1 sched-preemption test is the more direct signal into the same suspected root cause. If #957 is the shared cause, both close together; if not, this needs its own investigation.
