title: conformance: add --all-e2e flag to run-all.sh that widens beyond [Conformance]-tagged specs
description:
## Background Today `scripts/conformance/06-run-sonobuoy.sh:150` invokes sonobuoy with `--mode=certified-conformance`, which restricts execution to specs whose ginkgo body wraps `framework.ConformanceIt(...)` (the `[Conformance]`-tagged subset). Plain `ginkgo.It(...)` and `framework.It(...)` specs — everything from field-manager tests in `test/e2e/apimachinery/apply.go` to non-Conformance-tagged variants across most sig areas — are never touched by our runs. The subset is smaller than it looks: for example, `test/e2e/apps/deployment.go` has ~40 specs but only 9 are `ConformanceIt`. Discovered while briefing operator on mayor-u6ju (SSA EPIC) — the SSA-semantics tests (conflict/force/field-removal/managedFields) are plain `ginkgo.It`, so u7s's SSA gaps are invisible to conformance today. Same shape likely holds for other subsystems we care about (rich admission-webhook cases, watch-bookmark-under-load, chunked LIST edge cases). Running the wider set once gives a real picture of "what actually breaks" beyond the certified-conformance surface — highly valuable both as a Phase-5 perf baseline (more diverse latency shapes) and as a discovery pass for follow-on beads. ## Fix Add a `--all-e2e` flag on `run-all.sh` (default OFF — certified-conformance stays the default gate). When set, `06-run-sonobuoy.sh` replaces the `--mode=certified-conformance` line with an explicit focus/skip pair: ``` sonobuoy $SONOBUOY_BASE_ARGS \ --e2e-focus=".*" \ --e2e-skip="\[Disruptive\]|\[Flaky\]|\[Slow\]" ``` Rationale for the skip set: - `[Disruptive]` — kills node processes to verify recovery; some tests structurally require multi-node infra u7s's lima setup doesn't have (cordon/uncordon, host-network, planned reboot). - `[Flaky]` — upstream-known-flaky, not signal. - `[Slow]` — >5min individual specs. Excluding these matches upstream's own release-qual practice; without the skip the wall-clock balloons unpredictably. ## Not in scope - Making `--all-e2e` the default (this is opt-in for discovery / periodic full runs, not the per-PR CI gate). - Any change to how results are parsed downstream (e2e.txt path, PASS/FAIL counting) — same sonobuoy output shape. - Running / triaging the results — the point of this bead is the runner change so the *operator can* trigger such runs; interpreting the first all-e2e run's output is a separate initiative (expect many new failures, most legitimate discovery, some lima-precondition noise). ## Acceptance criteria - `run-all.sh --all-e2e --vm --port

--kubelet-port --workdir ./temp/u7s [--reset]` invokes sonobuoy with the widened focus/skip, not `--mode=certified-conformance`. - Bare `run-all.sh` (no --all-e2e) unchanged from today's behavior — same certified-conformance flow, same protection against runaway invocations per existing docs. - `--all-e2e` composes correctly with `--stack-only` (--stack-only wins, same as the existing `--focus` interaction — see run-all.sh's existing flag composition). - `--all-e2e` and `--focus ` are mutually exclusive — either error out with a clear message, or one wins with a warning (match existing --stack-only+--focus precedent). - Small doc update in `ai/prompts/vm-operations.md` naming the new flag and its wall-clock expectation (~6-12h vs certified's ~2h). ## Notes on cost / expected first-run outcome - Wall-clock: certified takes ~2h at current state; expect ~6-12h for --all-e2e. Not for iterative dev; a periodic discovery / perf-baseline run. - Disk: podlogs balloon from ~1GiB (certified) to probably 5-10GiB. Existing evacuation loop in 06-run-sonobuoy.sh already handles the volume; verify but don't rework. - Failure count: expect a large number of new failures on the FIRST such run — most are legitimate "we've never exercised this code path" gaps, some are lima-preconditions we can't fix. Do NOT triage in this bead; that's separate follow-up work. ## Discovered Operator briefing on mayor-u6ju (SSA EPIC), 2026-07-31. The observation that `[Conformance]` is a strict subset generalized to "we should be able to opt into the wider set when we want it".
notes: Fresh dispatch 2026-07-31 12:XX after prior worker's worktree discarded.
close_reason: shipped via PR #962 -- --all-e2e flag added; certified-conformance remains default; --focus mutually exclusive (hard error), --stack-only wins over --all-e2e

title: apiserver: TLS server-SAN hardcodes 10.96.0.1 for kubernetes ClusterIP, doesn't derive from --service-cluster-ip-range
description:
## Bug

`crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs::build_server_sans` hardcodes `10.96.0.1` as a required TLS SAN, and its own assertion at ~L583-595 enforces this. Comment at L252-583 explains why: in-cluster clients set `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST=10.96.0.1` from the Downward API and need the apiserver's cert to validate at that IP.

This is a coherence gap alongside mayor-pjjb4 (PR #958). #958 fixed the *Service* ClusterIPs to derive from `--service-cluster-ip-range`, but the *TLS SAN* still hardcodes `10.96.0.1`. If an operator runs with e.g. `--service-cluster-ip-range 172.20.0.0/16`, #958 correctly seeds the kubernetes Service with `172.20.0.1`, but tls.rs's SAN list still contains `10.96.0.1` — an IP no Service actually owns — and DOESN'T contain `172.20.0.1`, so in-cluster clients would fail TLS validation.

## Discovered

Worker's scope-catch in pjjb4 dispatch return (2026-07-31). Flagged as coherent-with-pjjb4 territory but outside its four-site boundary.

## Fix

Derive the required TLS SAN from `--service-cluster-ip-range` (first host, same as pjjb4's `kubernetes` Service ClusterIP). Reuse the `ServiceIpAllocator::nth_host` helper pjjb4 added in `state.rs`. Update the assertion at ~L583-595 to reference the derived IP, not the literal `10.96.0.1`.

Also update the 5 test setups in tls.rs that pass `service_cluster_ip_range: "10.96.0.0/12"` explicitly — those stay unchanged (default range still yields `10.96.0.1`).

## Acceptance criteria

- With `--service-cluster-ip-range 172.20.0.0/16`, `build_server_sans` emits `172.20.0.1` as a SAN (not `10.96.0.1`).
- Existing default (`10.96.0.0/12`) still emits `10.96.0.1` — no observable regression for the current lima setup.
- Regression test that fails on revert.

## Not in scope

- Any change to sonobuoy's own `KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST` value (Downward API is populated by the kubelet from the actual Service's clusterIP, so as long as pjjb4's Service derivation is coherent with the TLS SAN, sonobuoy Just Works on both default and non-default ranges).
- Anything else related to non-default service-cluster-ip-range coherence (script-side hardcodes remain deferred per pjjb4's operator decision).
notes: dispatched 2026-07-31 as Shape-1 solo — consumes ServiceIpAllocator::nth_host shipped in PR #958
close_reason: shipped via PR #959 — TLS SAN derives from --service-cluster-ip-range via #958's ServiceIpAllocator::nth_host, closing coherence gap

title: apiserver: kubernetes/kube-dns Service ClusterIPs hardcoded to 10.96.0.1/10.96.0.10, don't derive from --service-cluster-ip-range
description:
## Bug

`--service-cluster-ip-range` is a proper CLI flag (`args.rs:53`, default `10.96.0.0/12`). It seeds the `kubernetes` ServiceCIDR object at startup (`lib.rs:4941`). BUT the two Service ClusterIPs the apiserver hardcodes for its own bootstrap Services don't derive from that flag:

- `kubernetes` Service — hardcoded `10.96.0.1` at `lib.rs:2173`, again at `handlers/defaults.rs:1069`, admission default at `handlers/defaults.rs:2496`.
- `kube-dns` Service — hardcoded `10.96.0.10` at `lib.rs:2202`.

## Impact

Not a live bug — nothing in u7s ever passes `--service-cluster-ip-range` to a non-default range that doesn't contain 10.96.0.1/10.96.0.10. But it's a coherence gap: if an operator ever wanted to run u7s with e.g. `--service-cluster-ip-range 172.20.0.0/16`, the seeded kubernetes and kube-dns Services would still get 10.96.x.x ClusterIPs — outside the configured range — breaking:
- The startup coherence check (a seeded Service outside the ServiceCIDR is a validation error).
- kubelet's /etc/resolv.conf pointing at a nameserver IP that no Service actually owns.
- kube-proxy programming a DNAT for 10.96.0.1:443 that the apiserver Service doesn't advertise.

## Fix

Derive both bootstrap ClusterIPs from `--service-cluster-ip-range`:
- `kubernetes` Service ClusterIP = first host in the range (typically `.1`)
- `kube-dns` Service ClusterIP = tenth host in the range (matches kubeadm convention)
Thread the value through to the three defaults.rs sites so admission defaulting and roundtrip tests use the derived value, not the hardcode.

Also check if there are analogous script-side hardcodes that would need to move to a corresponding `run-all.sh` flag — but that's a separate concern (per operator: script-side hardcodes are fine for the test rig; only address if someone wants to run u7s outside the concrete lima setup).

## Acceptance criteria

- Passing `--service-cluster-ip-range 172.20.0.0/16` seeds `kubernetes` with clusterIP `172.20.0.1` and `kube-dns` with clusterIP `172.20.0.10`.
- Existing default (`10.96.0.0/12`) still seeds the same `10.96.0.1` / `10.96.0.10` values (no observable regression).
- Regression test that fails on revert.

## Discovered

Discussion with operator 2026-07-30 about pgm5q.8's "widen clusterCIDR" prescription — turned out kube-proxy's clusterCIDR is script-side (`lima-start.sh:559`, correctly `10.85.0.0/16` for our CRI-O convention). The bead's mis-diagnosed "widen" led to auditing the apiserver's own configurability; `--service-cluster-ip-range` IS a flag, but two derived values weren't wired to it. Filing here so it doesn't get lost.
notes: dispatched 2026-07-31 as Shape-1 solo from :18 dispatch loop
close_reason: shipped via PR #958 — derive kubernetes/kube-dns Service ClusterIPs from --service-cluster-ip-range instead of hardcoding 10.96.0.1/10.96.0.10

title: PATCH /apis/apiextensions.k8s.io/v1/customresourcedefinitions/{name} has no SSA create-on-missing (upsert) support
description:
Discovered as a byproduct of mayor-8beb1's related-defaulting sweep (Namespace
apply-create status.phase divergence).

## Finding

`patch_crd` (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/crd.rs) always does
`state.store.get(&key).await?.ok_or_else(|| Status::not_found(...))?` before
applying any patch — unlike `do_patch` (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs),
which has an explicit `is_ssa && stored_opt.is_none()` upsert branch that creates
the object when a `application/apply-patch+yaml` PATCH targets a name that does
not yet exist. `patch_namespace` routes its SSA branch through `do_patch` and gets
this upsert behavior for free; `patch_crd` has its own bespoke PATCH handler and
never implemented the equivalent.

Real Kubernetes Server-Side Apply is documented to create the object on first
apply if it doesn't exist yet (this is core SSA semantics, not an edge case) —
`kubectl apply --server-side -f my-crd.yaml` for a brand-new CRD sends a PATCH
with `Content-Type: application/apply-patch+yaml` and relies on the apiserver to
create it. Against u7s, this PATCH currently 404s instead.

## Impact

Any CRD applied via `kubectl apply --server-side` (not just plain `kubectl apply`,
since CRDs are rarely re-applied identically) when it does not already exist fails
outright with 404, rather than being silently mis-defaulted (a different, worse
failure mode than the Namespace bug in mayor-8beb1, which at least created the
object with `status: {}`).

## Suggested fix

Add an upsert branch to `patch_crd` mirroring `do_patch`'s
`is_ssa && stored_opt.is_none()` branch: parse the YAML apply body, run
`create_crd`'s defaulting/admission/status-stamping, and persist via `put(..., Some(0))`.
This is a larger change than a one-line defaulter fix (CRD has its own bespoke
admission/validation/status-stamping pipeline in `create_crd`, distinct from the
generic resource.rs create path), so it was filed separately rather than folded
into mayor-8beb1's surgical Namespace fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- `kubectl apply --server-side -f <new-crd.yaml>` (or an equivalent PATCH with
  `application/apply-patch+yaml` on a CRD name that does not exist) creates the
  CRD with the same status-stamping (`Established`/`NamesAccepted` conditions)
  as plain `kubectl create -f <crd.yaml>`, instead of 404ing.
- Regression test covering the create-on-missing PATCH path for CRDs.
close_reason: patch_crd now upserts on missing CRD for SSA (application/apply-patch+yaml), matching upstream SSA create-if-missing semantics. See PR #951.

title: PATCH on immutable ConfigMap/Secret blanket-rejects metadata-only changes
description:
Found during mayor-rwbd storage/volume audit (ai/findings/storage-volume-audit-2026-07-30.md).

crates/apiserver/src/handlers/resource.rs do_patch's immutability guard (~line 1026-1035) rejects ANY patch when the stored Secret/ConfigMap has immutable:true, regardless of what the patch actually touches:

    if group.is_empty() && (plural == "secrets" || plural == "configmaps")
        && current.body["immutable"] == serde_json::Value::Bool(true)
    {
        return Err(Status::unprocessable_entity(...));
    }

This is a real deviation from upstream: real kube-apiserver only rejects changes to data/binaryData/stringData (or clearing the immutable flag) — it allows patching labels/annotations on an immutable object. The PUT path three lines below in the same file (replace_namespaced_resource, ~line 1892-1915) already gets this right by checking data_changed/binary_data_changed/string_data_changed/immutable_cleared instead of blanket-rejecting.

No currently-known conformance test exercises PATCH on an immutable object (the immutable conformance tests only call Update()/PUT), so this doesn't explain any of the 9 sig-storage failures — it's a standalone correctness bug found while auditing.

Acceptance criteria:
- PATCH on an immutable Secret/ConfigMap that only touches metadata (labels/annotations) succeeds.
- PATCH that touches data/binaryData/stringData, or that clears immutable:true, still returns 422.

title: fix(apiserver): CrConversionCache LeaderClaimGuard zip-truncation leaks in_flight entries on short conversion webhook response
description:
In [convert_cr_list_items](crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs#L430-L440), the leader-resolve loop uses `leader_indices.into_iter().zip(converted).zip(leader_keys)` which Rust-`zip`s to the shortest iterator. If `call_conversion_webhook` returns a NON-EMPTY but SHORT converted array (e.g. 2 items requested, 1 item returned by a malformed webhook), the trailing leader entries are silently dropped.

`call_conversion_webhook` at [handlers/cr.rs:133](crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs#L133) only checks `converted.is_empty()`, not `converted.len() == requested.len()`, so this partial-length case slips through as "success".

Consequence: `guard.keys.clear()` at [handlers/cr.rs:440](crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs#L440) unconditionally runs after the loop regardless of how many pairs were actually processed, disabling the Drop-based safety net for exactly the keys that need it. Those `(rv, apiVersion)` keys are then orphaned in `in_flight` forever, and any future concurrent caller on the same key will hang on a Notify that nobody will ever fire.

FIX SKETCH (~5-10 LoC):
1. In `call_conversion_webhook`, add an assertion that `converted.len() == objects.len()` before returning Ok; if mismatched, return a `Status::internal` describing the shape mismatch (this matches upstream's [conversion webhook contract](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/extend-kubernetes/custom-resources/custom-resource-definitions/#webhook-conversion), where the webhook MUST return one converted object per requested object).
2. Add a regression test in `crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs` tests: mock a conversion webhook that returns `convertedObjects` with 1 item when 2 were requested; assert the response is a `Status::internal` AND that `state.cr_conversion_cache.in_flight` has no leftover entries.
3. The fix will FAIL on revert (add `#[cfg(test)] pub fn in_flight_len(&self) -> usize` on CrConversionCache so the test can assert the map is empty after the failed call).

DISCOVERED BY: mayor-rr4ja code review of 9110c9a4. Not the driver for the CustomResourceFieldSelectors regression under investigation, but a real correctness gap in the single-flight coalescing.

LABELS: apiserver, conversion-webhook, correctness
close_reason: PR #938 opened: call_conversion_webhook now enforces converted.len() == requested.len(), with a regression test asserting both the Status::internal error and empty in_flight afterward

title: perf(apiserver): CrConversionCache single-flight coalescing (zw0ou sub-bead 4)
description:
Justified by mayor-k7b4w's thundering-herd bench (crates/apiserver/benches/cr_conversion_fanout.rs, group cr_conversion_fanout_thundering_herd). N tokio tasks released together via a Barrier, all hitting the SAME cold (source_rv, target_apiVersion) key on a plain RwLock<HashMap> cache (mirrors CrConversionCache's exact get/insert shape, no coalescing):

RAW N=100 NUMBERS (10 criterion samples each, unless noted):
- 5ms webhook delay, N=100: wall-clock [7.61ms, 7.66ms, 7.70ms] (median), webhook_calls = 100.00/100 (avg over 30-40 sample iterations, exactly deterministic every run)
- 20ms webhook delay, N=100: wall-clock [22.88ms, 23.05ms, 23.21ms] (median), webhook_calls = 100.00/100 (avg over 20 sample iterations, exactly deterministic every run)

Full table (N x delay): webhook_calls == N at EVERY (N, delay) combination tested (N in 1/5/10/20/50/100, delay in 5ms/20ms) -- zero coalescing benefit, 100% thundering herd, perfectly reproducible (no run showed less than N calls).

IMPORTANT CAVEAT for whoever implements this: wall-clock in the bench does NOT scale with N (stays ~flat: ~7.2-7.7ms at 5ms delay, ~22.5-23.2ms at 20ms delay, regardless of N) because the mock webhook is a bare tokio::time::sleep, and tokio's timer wheel runs arbitrarily many concurrent sleeps for free. A real conversion webhook is not free like that -- it consumes a real HTTP connection/thread/CPU cycle on an external service, may be rate-limited, and may cost money per call. So the pathology this bead fixes is REDUNDANT WEBHOOK LOAD (N calls where 1 would do), not client-observed latency amplification -- don't let a "wall-clock looks fine" read of a future benchmark talk you out of this; the call-count amplification is the real, measured problem.

RECOMMENDED PRIMITIVE: DashMap<CrConversionCacheKey, ...> + per-key tokio::sync::oneshot (hand-rolled single-flight), OR moka::future::Cache::try_get_with if the project is willing to add the moka dependency (it has a mature, well-tested single-flight implementation purpose-built for exactly this cache-stampede scenario -- concurrent gets on a missing key block on the first caller's in-flight compute rather than all recomputing). Given the project's "resist adding crates" stance, evaluate a minimal hand-rolled DashMap+oneshot approach first; only pull in moka if the hand-rolled version proves fiddly to get race-free (e.g. panicking in-flight futures need to release the per-key slot for the next caller, which oneshot senders being dropped handles automatically, but audit this carefully).

Scope: production code change (unlike the bench-only k7b4w that justified this). Wire into CrConversionCache (crates/apiserver/src/state.rs) and convert_cr_list_items (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs).
close_reason: PR #934 opened: single-flight coalescing via Mutex<HashMap<Key, Arc<Notify>>> claim/resolve (not DashMap/moka — matches existing state.rs WatchLimitState/QuotaAdmissionLocks convention, zero new deps); thundering herd N=100 @ 20ms webhook: 100 calls -> 1

title: task
description:
Third sub-bead of the zw0ou EPIC (plan at ai/findings/zw0ou-per-version-storage-cacher-plan-2026-07-29.md). Follows n8bkc (PR #928) which added the CrConversionCache as correct-but-leaky: it grows unbounded because there's no eviction, only structural correctness (monotonic-rv key never collides).

PROBLEM: On a long-running cluster with many CR writes across many CRDs, the cache accumulates every (source_rv, target_apiVersion) tuple ever converted. Memory grows without bound. Not a correctness concern (per zw0ou-plan-is-cache-not-cacher-architecture + store-revision-counter-monotonic-never-reused memories), but a memory-hygiene concern.

FIX SHAPE per plan sub-bead 3 (~30-50 LoC):
1. On CR DELETE (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs delete paths) — evict any entries with this object's rv from the cache. Small mechanical addition; grep for the delete handler and mirror n8bkc's insertion pattern in reverse.
2. On CRD DELETE (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/crd.rs delete_crd) — evict all cache entries for CRs whose target_apiVersion matches any of the deleted CRD's versions. Broader sweep. Precedent: p8vgj's CrSchemaCache eviction pattern at crd.rs already does this same shape for schema-compile cache.
3. Optional (only if plan-sub-bead-3 explicitly suggests it): bounded max entries (e.g. 10_000) with LRU eviction on insert. Read the plan doc before deciding; if it doesn't suggest LRU, don't add it — Rule 2 simplicity.

Rule 14 tests (extend the tv4ob/n8bkc conversion-test scaffold):
- cr_conversion_cache_evicts_on_cr_delete_removes_matching_rv_entries
- cr_conversion_cache_evicts_on_crd_delete_removes_all_entries_for_that_crds_versions
- cr_conversion_cache_no_regression_on_conversion_correctness_after_eviction (positive control: after evicting, a subsequent conversion works and produces the same result)

CORRECTNESS NOTE: eviction is memory-hygiene only, NOT correctness-critical. If eviction has a bug (evicts too aggressively, too little, wrong keys), the WORST case is redundant conversion webhook calls on entries that should have been cached — same failure mode as any cache miss, no wrong data. This gives eviction bugs a soft failure mode; still worth testing but calibrates severity.

QUALITY GATE:
- cargo test --workspace + clippy must stay green.
- No new benchmark required for this sub-bead (n8bkc's cr_conversion_fanout bench already validates the underlying cache; eviction doesn't change the hit-path perf).
- Do NOT re-add invalidation on WRITE — the monotonic-rv guarantee means old entries under a bumped rv are unreachable-but-harmless (memory pressure aside). Only DELETE evicts.

title: task
description:
mayor-lm71q investigated whether patch.rs's registration of merge key \"name\" for
containerStatuses/initContainerStatuses/ephemeralContainerStatuses (patch.rs:559-567)
matches real kubelet/kube-apiserver strategic-merge-patch behavior, or is stale.

Verdict: STALE. Evidence (kubernetes/kubernetes release-1.36):
- staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go:5403,5415,5433 -- the real Go struct tags for
  these three fields carry NO patchStrategy/patchMergeKey (contrast PodIPs/HostIPs at
  lines 5385/5370, which do).
- staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/strategicpatch/patch.go:320-343
  (handleSliceDiff, used by kubelet's CreateTwoWayMergePatch to build its status patch)
  and :1477-1489 (mergeSliceHandler, used by kube-apiserver to apply an incoming
  patch) both key off patchStrategy=="merge"; with no tag present, both sides fall to
  the default/else branch and treat the field as a plain whole-array value (construct:
  replace-if-changed: apply: replace verbatim). Neither kubelet's outgoing patch nor a
  real apiserver's patch application merges containerStatuses by name -- confirming the
  vendored proto's +listType=atomic (core/v1/generated.proto:4918-4919,4929-4931,
  4947-4949) with no patchMergeKey is accurate, and patch.rs's "name" registration is a
  stale artifact from db2ab919 (added by incorrect analogy to the podIPs fix in the same
  commit; podIPs genuinely has patchStrategy=merge/patchMergeKey=ip and is unaffected).

Full findings: ai/findings/containerstatuses-merge-key-vs-listtype-atomic-2026-07-29.md
(gitignored local doc from the investigation, not committed -- reproduce via the file:line
citations above if needed).

Fix:
1. Remove the three-field match arm at patch.rs:559-567 entirely (let containerStatuses/
   initContainerStatuses/ephemeralContainerStatuses fall through to MergeKeyKind::Unknown,
   i.e. whole-array-replace).
2. Add a regression test with TWO containers in the target's containerStatuses where the
   incoming patch only mentions one -- assert the unlisted container's status entry is
   DROPPED (matching real kube-apiserver's replace semantics), not silently preserved
   (which today's merge-by-name incorrectly does). This is the multi-container case none
   of the existing tests (container_state_is_replaced_not_merged_on_status_patch,
   init_container_state_is_replaced_not_merged_on_status_patch,
   test_smp_allocated_resources_status_merge_preserves_existing) actually exercise --
   they all use a single container name so merge and replace are indistinguishable.
3. Verify should_replace_object() (patch.rs, the containerStatuses[].state
   discriminated-union special case) and the allocatedResourcesStatus nested merge-key
   entry (patch.rs ~493-500, keyed by the containerStatuses ELEMENT's field, not the
   array itself) are unaffected -- they operate one level deeper, inside a single
   ContainerStatus object, and don't depend on the outer array's merge-vs-replace
   behavior.
4. Note in a doc comment (matching this file's convention) why this now correctly falls
   through to Unknown, citing the evidence above, so a future audit doesn't re-flag the
   now-absent entry as a gap.

Low risk in practice: kubelet always resends its full in-memory containerStatuses
snapshot (never a partial/sparse array), so real kubelet traffic is unaffected either
way. The divergence only matters for non-kubelet clients sending partial
containerStatuses patches (e.g. `kubectl patch --subresource=status`), where u7s
currently (incorrectly) preserves stale entries a real apiserver would drop.
notes: STOP-AND-REPORT (bead's own step-3 trigger fired): removed patch.rs:559-567 arm as scratch experiment, ran cargo test -p u7s-apiserver --lib patch:: -- test_smp_allocated_resources_status_merge_preserves_existing FAILED (left=1, right=2, 'gpu' dropped). Root cause: should_replace_object's containerStatuses[].state check AND the .allocatedResourcesStatus merge-key arm (~493) are ONLY ever reached via strategic_merge_array's per-element recursion (strategic_merge_patch_at(target_elem, patch_elem, path, schema) at patch.rs:291), which is ONLY invoked when merge_key_for_path returns MergeKeyKind::Key for the OUTER array (containerStatuses/init/ephemeral). Removing the outer arm makes the outer array MergeKeyKind::Unknown, so strategic_merge_array (and hence ALL per-element recursion into a matched container, including allocatedResourcesStatus merging and the .state discriminated-union special case) never fires for these 3 fields again -- they become unreachable. This matches real upstream (no element-wise merge at all for containerStatuses since there's no patchMergeKey), so the outer-arm removal itself is correct -- but the EXISTING regression test test_smp_allocated_resources_status_merge_preserves_existing (same container name 'app' both sides, only allocatedResourcesStatus differs) was written under the premise that the outer array merges by name, and now fails because a real apiserver would ALSO drop the old 'gpu' entry (whole containerStatuses element gets replaced, no field-level merge survives). title: task
description:
Discovered during mayor-6hgd9's ReDoS-cap research 2026-07-28. Upstream K8s (release-1.36, apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apis/apiextensions/validation/validation.go:1493-1494) unconditionally rejects patternProperties in every v1 CRD structural schema:

  if len(schema.PatternProperties) != 0 {
      allErrs = append(allErrs, field.Forbidden(fldPath.Child(patternProperties), patternProperties is not supported))
  }

u7s does NOT replicate this. crates/apiserver/src/apiextensions_gen_adapter.rs:261-271 serializes pattern_properties straight through to the JSON handed to boon (the JSON-schema validator), and crates/apiserver/src/handlers/crd.rs has no rejecting check.

Consequence for u7s: even after mayor-cmtwm lands the per-pattern 512-byte cap (which the mayor-6hgd9 doc shows is sufficient on its own to bound the aggregate DoS cost at ~0.26s per request via the linear-in-K argument), keeping patternProperties enabled at all is a divergence from upstream's structural-schema simplicity rule that (a) admits a bunch of odd validation semantics upstream deliberately excludes, and (b) means u7s accepts CRDs upstream would 422 — a conformance/portability concern separate from the DoS one.

FIX SHAPE: in the CRD create/update handler (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/crd.rs), walk the submitted openAPIV3Schema and reject any node with a non-empty patternProperties map with 422/Forbidden matching upstream error text. Regression test: a CRD with patternProperties is rejected; a CRD without one is accepted.

PRIORITY: P3 defense-in-depth, files AFTER mayor-cmtwm's per-pattern cap lands (that fix already caps patternProperties KEYS at the same 512 bytes as pattern values, which per mayor-6hgd9's Q5 calculation is sufficient for the DoS). This bead brings u7s into structural-schema parity with upstream. Not urgent — waiting on cmtwm to land first makes the sequencing clean (cmtwm handles DoS + partial parity via per-key cap; this bead completes parity via outright rejection).

Full evidence: ai/findings/crd-pattern-size-upstream-and-real-world-2026-07-28.md Q5.

FEEDS FROM: mayor-cmtwm (P2 HIGH ReDoS fix). File this bead AFTER cmtwm lands, not before.
close_reason: PR #924 opened: patternProperties rejected outright at any schema depth, matching upstream K8s validation.go:1493-1494

title: task
description:
Audit: ai/findings/redos-and-user-controlled-pattern-audit-2026-07-28.md, finding F1 (MEDIUM).

PROBLEM: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs::validate_cr_schema (lines 476-499) builds a brand
new boon::Schemas + boon::Compiler and re-parses/re-compiles the CRD's ENTIRE openAPIV3Schema
(including every `pattern`/`patternProperties` regex.rs::Regex::new call inside boon-0.6.1's
compiler.rs:472 and :385) from scratch on EVERY SINGLE CR create/update/patch/apply request --
8 production call sites in cr.rs (lines 1300, 1398, 2114, 2211, 2521, 2611, 2726, 2816).

Neither of boon's two Regex::new call sites sets RegexBuilder::size_limit()/dfa_size_limit(),
so each compile relies on the regex crate's own built-in 10MB default size limit. That's a real
bound (kept this at MEDIUM not HIGH), and the request body itself is capped at 4 MiB
(MAX_BODY_BYTES, crates/apiserver/src/lib.rs:61,318) which is an upstream length bound per the
audit's rubric. But paying up to that bounded-but-non-trivial parse+compile cost on EVERY CR
write (not just on CRD install/update) is architecturally wasteful and is a DoS amplification
factor: a CRD needs a malicious/complex pattern installed only ONCE (a comparatively higher-
privilege action), after which ANY principal with mere create/update RBAC on that Custom
Resource kind can retrigger the full recompile cost repeatedly with ordinary CR writes.

Verified against upstream Kubernetes (release-1.36's kube-openapi dependency,
k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/validation/validate/rexp.go, fetched via gh api and cached at
temp/research/kube-openapi-rexp.go): upstream's compileRegexp/mustCompileRegexp/cacheRegexp
memoize every compiled *regexp.Regexp in a process-wide map[string]*regexp.Regexp, so a given
schema's pattern is compiled ONCE per process lifetime, never per-request. u7s has no equivalent
cache.

FIX SHAPE: cache the compiled boon::Schemas (or at minimum the compiled schema index returned
by compiler.compile) per CRD version in CrContext/AppState, keyed by (group, version,
resourceVersion) or a hash of the raw openAPIV3Schema JSON. Invalidate/rebuild only when the
CRD's schema actually changes (CRD update). This mirrors upstream's compile-once-reuse-forever
behavior and removes the repeat-compile amplification vector.

NOTE: this fix does NOT by itself cap the worst-case cost of the FIRST compile after a CRD
schema change -- pair with the companion HIGH bead (F2, mayor-cmtwm) which adds a length
pre-check on pattern/patternProperties to bound that first-compile cost directly.

Regression test: after caching, repeated CR writes against the same CRD version must not
re-invoke boon::Compiler::compile (assert via a call counter or timing delta versus a
schema-change case that DOES re-trigger a rebuild).
close_reason: PR #925 opened: cached boon::Schemas per CRD (group, version, resourceVersion) with invalidation on write + eviction on delete

title: Root-cause the exact mechanism by which content_type.rs header mutation on chunked responses caused client-go watch cancellation
description: Follow-up to mayor-ido0r (RESOLVED via PR 907, postmortem in ai/extended-context/conformance-header-mutation-postmortem-2026-07-27.md). We fixed a P1 conformance regression by making the x-request-id header insertion in content_type.rs ContentTypeService::call conditional on NOT being a chunked Transfer-Encoding response, matching the files existing is_chunked exemption for body re-encoding. The fix is confirmed via bisection (proven at the commit level, verified across 4 clean live runs) and via the retrywatcher-context-canceled correlation (0 occurrences on every clean binary, up to 300 on every broken binary). HOWEVER the exact runtime mechanism connecting the header mutation to client-go watch clients seeing context canceled was never proven with a minimal repro or a stack trace. MAYOR REASONING WORTH RECORDING: resp.headers_mut().insert(...) mutates the HeaderMap inside http::Response Parts before the Response is returned up through the Tower and hyper stack, meaning nothing has been written to the wire yet at that point. http::Response Body and Parts are separate fields with no unsafe pinning coupling in the http or axum crates, so under ordinary safe-Rust semantics this specific operation should not affect a streams behavior once hyper starts polling it. The fix ALSO left the tracing::info call site repositioning and the reencode_proto_response extraction untouched, meaning the header insert really is the single differentiating operation between the confirmed-broken and confirmed-fixed binaries, per the fix diff itself. This means the puzzle is real: we know THAT the header insert is causal, we do not know WHY. SCOPE FOR THIS INVESTIGATION: build a minimal STANDALONE axum plus tokio reproduction, decoupled from the full apiserver and the conformance harness. A synthetic watch-like endpoint backed by a broadcast Receiver stream, wrapped in a middleware doing the exact old-vs-new header-insert sequence, driven by a REAL client-go based watch client if feasible (since retrywatcher.go context-canceled behavior is client-go internal machinery reacting to something specific about server behavior, a naive curl or raw-socket client may not trigger whatever it actually responds to) rather than more log archaeology on the full system. EXPLICITLY ALLOWED TO FAIL OR BE INCONCLUSIVE: there is a real chance a minimal repro will not reproduce the issue at all, which would itself be a valuable finding meaning the mechanism needs a precondition only present in the full system such as concurrent watch load, connection reuse, or TLS layering. Report an honest inconclusive result rather than forcing a conclusion. PRIORITY: optional, best-effort, non-blocking assurance work on an already-fixed and already-confirmed issue. Not urgent, pick up whenever there is slack. TIME BUDGET: time-box to a single dispatch, report findings either way. If a mechanism IS found, fold the finding back into the postmortem doc as an addendum (ai/extended-context/conformance-header-mutation-postmortem-2026-07-27.md) rather than writing a new standalone doc.
close_reason: Investigation completed 2026-07-28, closed as well-argued inconclusive (allowed per bead scope). Tier 1 (source-level read at pinned versions axum 0.8.9/axum-core 0.5.6/hyper 1.11.0/http 1.4.0) confirmed no coupling between Parts and Body. Tier 2 (minimal axum/tokio repro driven by real client-go@v0.36.2 RetryWatcher) reproduced ZERO cancellations in both broken and fixed modes. Two untested preconditions remain (TLS layering + concurrent watch load) — filed as follow-on. Addendum appended to ai/extended-context/conformance-header-mutation-postmortem-2026-07-27.md. Memory: content-type-header-mutation-mechanism-mo96q-inconclusive.

title: test(apiserver): add regression test proving header-value CR/LF injection is rejected at the HTTP layer before reaching the access-log
description:
Found by mayor-rl86n (2026-07-24 security reflection audit). Doc: ai/findings/security-review-2026-07-24.md section 6 (Recent surface additions / log-injection sub-check), LOW/DEFER tier.

The structured access log (content_type.rs's single tracing::info! call site, PR #895
mayor-atemy.2) logs `user_agent` (from the User-Agent header) and `uri`
(req.uri().to_string(), still percent-encoded) verbatim via Display (%field) with no escaping
performed by this crate's own code.

Reasoned-but-not-empirically-proven safety argument (this audit is read-only, no cargo
test/run):
- `user_agent` is an HTTP header value; http::HeaderValue's wire-parsing rejects CR/LF and
  other C0 control bytes (0x00-0x08, 0x0A-0x1F, 0x7F) before the value is ever exposed to
  application code — hyper/axum should reject the whole request at the HTTP layer if a header
  value contains one of these bytes, closing both classic newline-log-injection and
  ANSI/terminal-escape-injection vectors via User-Agent.
- `uri` stays percent-encoded in its logged form, so an attacker-supplied %0a/%1b sequence
  remains three literal printable characters, never becomes a raw control byte, in the logged
  string.

This is believed safe BY CONSTRUCTION of the http/axum dependency stack, not by any escaping
this crate performs — confidence is high but not proven, since verifying it would require
actually sending such a request through the full axum/hyper stack (out of scope for a
read-only audit).

ASK: add one specific, cheap integration/unit test (not a fuzzing harness) that builds a
Request with a header value containing a literal "\r\n" and asserts either (a) the request is
rejected before reaching any handler (if http::HeaderValue::from_str is used to construct it,
this should already fail to construct — assert that), or (b) if constructed via a lower-level
path that bypasses that validation, assert the access log line does not get split/forged. This
converts the "reasoned" safety argument in the audit doc into a proven, regression-tested
invariant.

Not urgent (LOW) — this is a confirming test for a control that is already believed correct,
not a known-broken code path.
close_reason: PR #915 opened: added test proving http::HeaderValue::from_str rejects CR/LF in header values, converting the audit's reasoned log-injection safety claim into a regression-tested one; no production code gap found

title: chore(apiserver): narrow remaining 65 pub handler functions to pub(crate) in resource.rs/pods.rs/namespaces.rs/core.rs
description:

Every handlers::* submodule is `pub mod` (handlers/mod.rs), so every remaining `pub fn` inside is a genuine (if accidental) external API surface point that a careless future bench addition could silently start depending on.

title: fix(apiserver): run_validating_webhooks's Arc-sharing invariant relies on a non-local expect() that could turn into a live panic
description:
From the 2026-07-24 code-quality audit (mayor-98p78, F1). PR #905 added Arc-sharing of the admitted object across N configured-webhook calls to both run_mutating_webhooks and run_validating_webhooks (crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs) -- the same problem, solved two different ways:

- run_mutating_webhooks (line ~2598): `if all_webhooks.is_empty() { return Ok(object); }` early-return, then unconditionally Arc-wraps -- the empty case is structurally impossible past that point.
- run_validating_webhooks (line ~3018): computes `has_webhooks` once into a bool, builds `object_arc: Option<Arc<Value>>` from it, then separately iterates `all_webhooks.iter()` in the loop below and unwraps object_arc via `.expect("all_webhooks is non-empty inside this loop, so object_arc was built")` (line ~3122).

has_webhooks/object_arc's Some-ness and the loop's non-emptiness are two independently-computed facts about the same all_webhooks value, kept in sync only by both being derived at adjacent lines today. A future edit that filters, reorders, or early-continues within all_webhooks between the has_webhooks computation and the loop (e.g. a new "disabled" flag, or hoisting a filter) would silently decouple them -- the .expect() would then panic on EVERY validating-webhook-configured request, not just malformed input.

WHY THIS MATTERS: no test today pins the invariant itself (only the current always-holds happy path is tested) -- see the audit's Category 5 notes. A refactor that looks locally correct could turn on a live panic for every admission-controlled write with no compiler or test signal.

FIX SHAPE: make run_validating_webhooks match run_mutating_webhooks's early-return shape -- `if all_webhooks.is_empty() { return Ok(()); }` before building object_arc, then wrap unconditionally, removing the Option<Arc<_>> and the .expect(). Mechanical, likely under 15 LoC.

VERIFY (Rule 14): a regression test that would fail if the .expect() panics -- e.g. a test that configures a ValidatingWebhookConfiguration whose rule/selector causes the webhook to be skipped via `continue` for every entry (so the loop runs 0 effective webhook calls despite all_webhooks being non-empty), confirming the code path that reaches the object_arc access doesn't rely on ordering. cargo test --workspace and cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings must stay green.

Full audit: ai/findings/code-quality-review-2026-07-24.md (Category 1, F1).
close_reason: PR #916 opened: scoped object_arc/old_object_arc construction to the same if !all_webhooks.is_empty() block as the loop, removing the Option<Arc<_>>+.expect() decoupling risk; CEL policy step left running unconditionally (deviation from literal bead suggestion, explained in PR).

title: chore(apiserver): consider a real lib+thin-bin split to avoid double-compiling the crate for benches/tests
description: PR #899 (mayor-08xro) added an additive src/lib.rs to crates/apiserver purely so benches/list_filter.rs could link against apply_label_selector, since main.rs had no lib target at all and Cargo cannot make ANY code in a bin-only crate reachable from an external bench crate regardless of visibility. Not urgent -- current cost is compile time only.

Decide whether the double-compile cost is worth eliminating given how many more apiserver benches/tests are expected. title: cleanup(apiserver): rewire watch.rs:1219/1231 to read revision via state_for_conversion.store, then drop redundant _store_keepalive
description: Discovered during mayor-z7tuw investigation (PR #897). The _store_keepalive dance in crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs was added in commit 0bfd47db to prevent the store's broadcast Sender from being dropped mid-watch-stream. Since then, SqliteStore::watch() itself captures tx_clone into the returned stream's generator, providing the exact same guarantee at the store layer (see PR #897's comment on the unreachable! arm). _store_keepalive is now belt-and-suspenders; safe to remove for clarity. Zero-harm cosmetic redundancy, not a defect. P4 because there is literally no observable effect — but the code is misleading in that a future reader may think _store_keepalive is load-bearing when it isn't.
notes:
WORKER FINDING (small-hygiene cluster, 2026-07-28): bead description does not match the code. Verified via direct source read of crates/apiserver/src/handlers/watch.rs (LSP tools unavailable in this session, used equivalent grep+Read inspection per the bead's own fallback instruction).

_store_keepalive (watch.rs:769, re-bound at :786) is `Arc::clone(&state.store)` — a clone of the whole SqliteStore, not specifically the broadcast Sender. It is NOT inert belt-and-suspenders: it is actively read via `.current_revision()` at watch.rs:1219 and :1231 to compute the BOOKMARK event's global revision (KCM ConsistencyStore compat — see the surrounding comment). Removing the binding as literally described would not compile.

Confirmed separately (crates/store/src/sqlite.rs:1091-1330): SqliteStore::watch()'s own generator does capture `tx_clone` and this genuinely makes the RecvError::Closed arm at sqlite.rs:1313 unreachable — that half of the bead's premise (PR #897's comment) is correct. But that only proves the *Sender*-liveness guarantee is now redundant at the store layer; it says nothing about the *revision-lookup* usage the handler-level variable also serves.

Per the bead's own instruction ("If the LSP shows _store_keepalive is doing anything OTHER than binding a clone of the store's sender for the stream lifetime, STOP and report"), stopping here rather than performing the described removal. A correct fix would need to first rewire watch.rs:1219/1231 to read the revision from `state_for_conversion.store.current_revision()` (already captured in the same generator for CR conversion) before the `_store_keepalive` binding could be dropped — that's a different, slightly larger change than what this bead describes, and out of surgical scope for a mechanical cleanup bead. Left unclaimed for re-scoping. No code changes made for this bead.

title: fix(apiserver): x-kubernetes-list-type: set needs dedupe-by-value merge semantics, not atomic-replace
description:
Follow-up flagged by mayor-nic50.2's investigation (see
ai/findings/nic50-crd-merge-key-plumbing-design-2026-07-24.md section 4, written in that
worker's worktree -- gitignored, may not exist in your checkout; this description has the
load-bearing content inline). Depends on mayor-nic50.3 landing first (that bead introduces
crd_merge_key_for_path/find_schema_node, which this one extends).

## Problem

x-kubernetes-list-type has three values upstream: atomic (whole-array replace -- already
correct via MergeKeyKind::Unknown), map (merge by named key(s) -- mayor-nic50.3), and set
(merge by WHOLE-ELEMENT VALUE EQUALITY -- dedupe, not clobber). mayor-nic50.3's design
deliberately collapses `set` into MergeKeyKind::Unknown (atomic replace) as the safe,
conservative choice for that bead's scope -- but that is not upstream-faithful: a `set`
field should have new patch elements added, existing ones deduped by value, not have the
whole array wholesale replaced on every patch.

## Scope

- Add MergeKeyKind::Set (or equivalent) alongside Key/Replace/Unknown.
- crd_merge_key_for_path (from mayor-nic50.3) returns Set when
  x-kubernetes-list-type == "set" (currently it returns Unknown for this case -- narrow
  that fallback once this variant exists).
- strategic_merge_array (patch.rs) needs a Set-handling branch: append patch elements not
  already present by value equality, rather than the current Key/Replace/Unknown branches'
  behavior.
- Only applies to CRD-schema-resolved paths (schema: Some(..)) -- built-in resources have
  no x-kubernetes-list-type: set fields registered in the hardcoded table today, so
  resource.rs's call sites are unaffected.

## Done-when

A CR whose CRD schema declares x-kubernetes-list-type: set on a scalar (or object) list
field merges by value equality on strategic-merge-patch (dedupes, doesn't replace the
whole array), with a regression test proving a patch that adds one new set element leaves
pre-existing elements intact.

## References
- Parent epic: mayor-nic50
- Scoped by: mayor-nic50.2
- Depends on: mayor-nic50.3

title: scheduler never re-patches PodScheduled=False on a failed scheduling attempt after pod creation, unlike upstream which sets it every cycle
notes: Surfaced by mayor-d2242 Phase-1 (2026-07-21). u7s's scheduler emits a FailedScheduling Event on a failed scheduling attempt (main.rs:401-424) but NEVER patches the pod's own status.conditions PodScheduled=False. Consequence: status.conditions stays frozen at the pod-creation-time default, so tools/tests that poll for {type:PodScheduled,reason:Unschedulable} (some conformance waits do) can't observe the failure, and there's no self-generated MODIFIED event either (which is part of why d2242's requeue gap bites -- though d2242's fix, periodic re-sync, addresses the requeue independently). title: feat(scheduler): SchedulerAsyncPreemption 10-way contention test fails -- deeper fairness/nomination gap under concurrent preemption, no Conformance test exercises it
notes: Surfaced by mayor-ouuo5 (PR #842). After the pick_node/find_preemption_plan check-then-commit race was fixed, all 5 [Conformance]-tagged SchedulerPreemption tests pass, but the non-conformance, feature-gated SchedulerAsyncPreemption 10-way test still fails: a deeper fairness/nomination gap under concurrent preemption contention (10 pods contending). Not exercised by any [Conformance] test, so it does NOT affect the conformance floor. Worker (PR #842) explicitly scoped it out. Lower priority than conformance work. When picked up: reproduce via the async-preemption e2e (feature gate SchedulerAsyncPreemption); the gap is likely in how multiple preemptors nominate/contend for the same victims fairly rather than first-come serialization -- crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs find_preemption_plan / verify_and_reserve_preemption + main.rs preemption loop. Cross-ref mayor-ouuo5 close reason + PR #842 body.
close_reason: REPRODUCED live on lima-node-4 (2026-07-30). Primary mechanism: u7s scheduler never writes status.nominatedNodeName (zero hits in crates/scheduler/) -- the upstream SchedulerAsyncPreemption e2e test hard-blocks on NominatedNodeName != "" at its FIRST wait step, deterministically, at ANY contention level, not just 10-way. This is a missing-feature gap, not a subtle race. No feature-gate infra needed: SchedulerAsyncPreemption is Beta+Default:true since k8s 1.33, and upstream's WithFeatureGate is a pure Ginkgo CI-filter label (confirmed by reading ginkgowrapper.go), not a runtime cluster-gate check -- u7s has zero feature-gate infra anywhere, which turns out not to matter here. Secondary, live-confirmed (but not yet proven harmful) mechanism: concurrent find_preemption_plan calls compute overlapping/nested victim sets (filler-2 was DELETEd by all 3 concurrent preemptors' eviction loops in a live 3-way repro) because victim selection has no visibility into another in-flight plan's claims -- harmless in the balanced case reproduced (idempotent 404s, correct final state) since verify_and_reserve_preemption's aggregate-capacity recheck still serializes real slot ownership; whether this causes genuine starvation under real over-subscription (combined with the backoff-free 5-attempt retry in preempt_and_pick_node) was not independently verified (time-boxed) and needs re-checking once nomination unblocks the test far enough to reach that scenario. Findings doc: ai/findings/scheduler-async-preemption-fairness-scout-2026-07-30.md (gitignored, not committed). Follow-on filed: mayor-efhom (set status.nominatedNodeName on preemption-plan commit -- the clear, small, necessary first fix; further scope intentionally deferred pending live re-test after that lands).

title: proxy: https: scheme prefix in pod/service proxy URLs should connect to the backend over TLS
description:
Discovered while verifying mayor-caskz (scheme:name:port proxy parsing) via the [sig-network] "Proxy version v1 should proxy through a service and a pod" conformance test on lima-node-4 (run 0716-1715). Upstream k8s's scheme:name:port proxy addressing (`net.SplitSchemeNamePort` / `net.JoinSchemeNamePort`) uses the scheme not just to disambiguate the name/port split but to select the wire protocol used for the apiserver-to-backend connection: an `https:<name>:<port>` proxy URL must connect to the pod/endpoint IP with TLS (skipping cert verification, since arbitrary workload pods have no known CA), not plain HTTP.

mayor-caskz's fix (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs: split_scheme_name_port) correctly parses and strips the scheme for the name/port lookup, matching that bead's explicit scope ("strip an optional leading http:/https: scheme token"). It intentionally does not thread the scheme into the backend connection. pod_proxy_dispatch/service_proxy_dispatch always build `http://{ip}:{port}/...` regardless of the requested scheme.

Effect: an `https:`-prefixed proxy request to a pod/service port that is actually a TLS listener gets a plaintext HTTP request, and the TLS server correctly rejects it — observed as a 400 "Client sent an HTTP request to an HTTPS server" instead of the proxied TLS response.

Repro (from e2e.txt, run 0716-1715): all 5 https-scheme table-test cases (services tlsportname1/tlsportname2, pods 443/460/462) get this 400 instead of the expected proxied body ("tls baz" / "tls qux" / rewritten HTML). Confirmed unrelated to name/port parsing: zero 404s in the same run; these are pure protocol-selection failures.

Fix direction: resolve_pod_proxy_target / resolve_service_proxy_target need to return the parsed scheme (or a bool) alongside (ip, port, proxy_addr); pod_proxy_dispatch / service_proxy_dispatch need an https branch that connects with a TLS client that skips backend cert verification (matching upstream's InsecureSkipVerify behavior for pod-target TLS, since pod TLS certs are self-signed/unknown to the cluster CA).
close_reason: PR #859 opened — https-scheme pod/service proxy now connects to the backend over TLS (direct branch: reqwest danger_accept_invalid_certs; konnectivity tunnel branch: second inner TLS session to the pod). Verified live on lima-node-4: kubectl repro against an agnhost TLS backend returns 200 (no more 400 'HTTP request to HTTPS server'); focused conformance run for 'Proxy version v1 should proxy through a service and a pod' passes (1 Passed, 0 Failed). Companion fix mayor-rmqrl (HTML link rewrite) landed in the same PR — both were required for the aggregated Proxy conformance spec to go green.

title: proxy: pod/service proxy does not rewrite relative HTML links to include the proxy path prefix
description: Discovered while verifying mayor-caskz (scheme:name:port proxy parsing) via the [sig-network] "Proxy version v1 should proxy through a service and a pod" conformance test on lima-node-4 (run 0716-1715). That test's aggregated table includes cases where the proxied backend (agnhost porter) returns HTML containing a relative link, e.g. `test`. Upstream kube-apiserver's proxy rewrites such relative hrefs to be prefixed with the full proxy subresource path (so the link still resolves through the proxy when followed), e.g. expected `test`. u7s's pod_proxy_dispatch / service_proxy_dispatch (crates/apiserver/src/handlers/proxy.rs) stream the backend response body through unmodified (`Body::from_stream(...)` / `Body::from(body)`) — there is no HTML content rewriting anywhere in proxy.rs (confirmed: zero matches for "rewrite"/"text/html" in the file). This is NOT related to mayor-caskz's scheme:name:port name/port parsing fix (which is verified correct: all 320 proxy attempts in the same run had zero 404s). It reproduces even on the plain bare pod-proxy-root form (`pods//proxy/`), which never had a parsing bug. Repro (from e2e.txt, run 0716-1715): path .../pods//proxy/: wanted `test`, got `test` 3 of the 16 table-test cases fail on this (pod bare root, pod :1080, pod http:...:1080 — all serving the SERVE_PORT_80/1080 env body). Fix direction: kube-apiserver's UpgradeAwareProxy wraps text/html responses with a Transport that rewrites href/src attributes referencing absolute-path URLs to be relative to the proxy request's own path. u7s would need an equivalent rewrite step in pod_proxy_dispatch/service_proxy_dispatch when the upstream Content-Type is text/html.
close_reason: PR #859 opened — pod/service proxy now rewrites root-relative href/src links in text/html responses to include the proxy path prefix, matching upstream's proxy Transport. Verified live on lima-node-4: kubectl repro against an agnhost HTML backend returns the correctly-rewritten <a href=".../proxy/rewriteme"> link for both pod-proxy and service-proxy forms; focused conformance run for 'Proxy version v1 should proxy through a service and a pod' passes (1 Passed, 0 Failed). Companion fix mayor-vkkma (https TLS backend) landed in the same PR — both were required for the aggregated Proxy conformance spec to go green.

title: fix(scheduler): find_preemption_plan conflates 'no viable preemption target' with 'GET nodes failed' — same typed-error gap as pick_node
description:
Follow-on from mayor-zf07r (pick_node's typed PickNodeError fix).

find_preemption_plan (crates/scheduler/src/lib.rs) issues its own live GET
/api/v1/nodes and `bail!`s with an untyped anyhow::Error on a GET/parse
failure, exactly like pick_node used to. It has the same latent gap:
main.rs's preemption arm does `find_preemption_plan(...).await?`, so a
transient GET failure there is indistinguishable from "no node can fit the
pod even after preempting every eligible lower-priority pod" — both surface
as the outer Err, which main.rs turns into a FailedScheduling event.

Why this wasn't folded into mayor-zf07r: fixing pick_node only needed one
early-return guard ahead of the existing 2-arm match (first_pick captured
once, `should_retry_without_preempting` gates a bare `return;` from the
tokio::spawn body before the `outcome` async block is even entered).
find_preemption_plan's call sits one level deeper, INSIDE that `outcome:
anyhow::Result<String>` async block, after victims may already have been
evicted. A bare early-return doesn't type-check there (the block's declared
type is anyhow::Result<String>, not unit), so a correct fix needs the
`outcome` slot itself to gain a third "skip, no event" state (e.g.
`Option<anyhow::Result<String>>`) threaded through both the Ok/Preempt arms
and the final reason/message/event_type derivation — a materially bigger,
still-worth-doing change, not a one-match-arm tweak.

Suggested shape: either reuse PickNodeError (rename NoCapacity if needed to
cover "no viable preemption plan" too) or add a small analogous
FindPreemptionPlanError{NoViablePlan, ApiError(anyhow::Error)}; thread a
skip-vs-fail distinction through main.rs's outcome computation for the
preemption arm specifically. Blast radius: one pod's scheduling attempt
transiently marked FailedScheduling instead of retried, same P3 class as
the parent bead.
