title: task
description:
Follow-on to mayor-cmtwm/PR #924 (CRD ReDoS defense, 1024-byte cap on pattern/patternProperties keys) + n8bkc's empirical bench.

CONTEXT: PR #924 shipped a 1024-byte cap on the operator's decision after mayor-6hgd9's research showed real-world CRDs top out at 113 bytes (9x headroom). During #924's implementation, a bounded timing PoC measured that a single 1024-byte \d-repeated pattern compile takes ~657ms (memory boon-1024-byte-pattern-empirical-657ms) — much higher than the 6hgd9 audit doc predicted (which assumed sub-millisecond). At 1024 bytes, a schema with 10 patterns near cap could take ~6.5s per CR write.

OPERATOR DECISION (2026-07-29): keep the 1024-byte cap as-is for now. Reasoning: the DoS reachability requires a cluster-admin (or trusted Helm chart) to install a malicious/careless CRD *first*; after that, non-admin CR-write RBAC principals can retrigger the compile cost. But: the person paying the retrigger cost is themselves the CRD author (or their trusted delegate), so this is primarily a self-DoS scenario. Not worth the tighter restriction when real-world CRDs are 9x smaller than the cap already.

TRIGGER: file this bead to preserve the option if it ever escalates into a practical bottleneck. Concrete escalation signals:
- A supply-chain incident where a Helm chart installs a CRD with >256-byte patterns and downstream CR writes get slow.
- A conformance test surfacing >100ms delays on CR writes traceable to boon compile cost.
- A production observability dashboard showing tail-latency amplification on CR paths.

If any of those happen, revisit this bead: tighten MAX_CRD_PATTERN_BYTES from 1024 to 256 (2x headroom over 113-byte real-world max, drops worst-case single-compile to sub-100ms). ~5 LoC fix: one constant change in patch.rs + adjust boundary tests + PR body sentence.

CAVEAT: DO NOT lower below 256 without re-running the mayor-6hgd9 real-world survey — there could be a legitimate operator pattern that's ~200-500 bytes we didn't sample. 256 was chosen as 2x the observed max; anything tighter risks rejecting a legitimate future CRD.

title: task
description: Follow-on to mayor-mo96q (closed inconclusive 2026-07-28). The Tier-1/Tier-2 investigation ruled out both source-level coupling (http 1.4.0 / axum-core 0.5.6 have no Parts↔Body coupling) and single-connection client-go RetryWatcher reproduction (0 cancellations in both broken/fixed modes over 8s runs). The two most plausible untested preconditions per the addendum in ai/extended-context/conformance-header-mutation-postmortem-2026-07-27.md are: (1) TLS layering (real apiserver serves over tokio-rustls; the repro used plain HTTP; TLS record buffering/flushing sits exactly at the boundary between 'headers committed' and 'bytes on wire' that safe-Rust otherwise rules out); (2) concurrent watch load (conformance has dozens of simultaneous long-lived watches sharing one ContentTypeService + store Arc; repro tested one connection at a time). P4 optional, pick up if slack. If TLS alone reproduces without concurrent load, that's a P2-worthy finding (means any middleware Response mutation on a chunked TLS response is a landmine). If concurrent load reproduces without TLS, likewise. Fold any positive finding into the postmortem doc as a second addendum, don't create a new doc.

Full matrix (TLS-only, concurrent-only, TLS+concurrent) x (broken/fixed) x up to N=50, 15-20s/run: 0 cancellations/restarts in every cell, including the combined precondition. Neither hypothesis reproduces. Recommend closing the mechanism investigation; draft addendum text handed to mayor for ai/extended-context/conformance-header-mutation-postmortem-2026-07-27.md, not committed by this task per instructions. - crates/controller-manager/src/lib.rs:188 (WatchEvent<ClusterRoleObject>)
- crates/controller-manager/src/endpoint_slice_mirroring_controller.rs:128 (WatchEvent, generic)
- crates/controller-manager/src/namespace_controller.rs:91 (NsWatchEvent, in parse_ns_event)

WHY THIS MATTERS (or rather, doesn't, much): nothing correctness-wise -- same "invisible end-to-end, dwarfed by I/O" characterization PR #902 itself gave F10's scheduler sites. If anything, lower priority here since namespace/ClusterRoleBinding/EndpointSlice-mirroring watch volume is lower than the scheduler's pod-watch loop. Verify serde_json's &Value Deserializer impl produces identical results at each site (same verification F10's PR #902 did) before/after via existing tests -- PR #902 required zero test changes for its 4 sites since the deserialize semantics are equivalent; expect the same here.

title: chore(apiserver): finish AdmissionConfigCache field narrowing + verify build_review/AdmissionContext/AdmissionReview visibility
description:
From the 2026-07-24 code-quality audit (mayor-98p78, F3 + F4). Two small, related pub-visibility items found alongside mayor-2zh15 (the larger handler-visibility sweep), both in admission-cache/admission-review code:

F3 (crates/apiserver/src/state.rs:154-158): PR #900/#905 narrowed AdmissionConfigCache's mutating_webhooks/validating_webhooks fields from pub to pub(crate). The struct's 3 other fields -- mutating_policies, validating_policies, validating_policy_bindings -- remain pub. Confirmed (grep, whole crate + all 3 benches) they are read only from crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs, never externally. Fix: pub -> pub(crate) on the 3 fields. 3-line diff.

F4 (crates/apiserver/src/admission.rs:799-801, lib.rs:1, lib.rs:49): build_review/AdmissionContext/AdmissionReview are marked `pub` with a doc comment claiming this (not pub(crate)) is required so benches/admission_review.rs can call them via the crate-root pub use re-export. But `mod admission` itself is a PRIVATE module (lib.rs:1, not `pub mod`) -- unlike `handlers` (mayor-2zh15's context), which is `pub mod` at every level. Because the only external path to build_review is the explicit `pub use admission::{build_review, AdmissionContext, AdmissionReview};` re-export at the crate root (lib.rs:49), and pub(crate) items are visible crate-wide (including at the crate root where the re-export lives), marking these pub(crate) instead of pub would produce an IDENTICAL external surface -- the `pub use` line alone controls external reachability here. Zero functional difference either way, but the comment teaches the wrong lesson about why pub was chosen, which risks being copied into the next similarly-shaped (but actually-needs-real-pub) case, like handlers::generic::apply_label_selector, where pub genuinely is load-bearing.

FIX SHAPE: for F4, either (a) narrow the 3 signatures to pub(crate) and verify via cargo build --workspace + cargo bench --package u7s-apiserver --no-run that the admission_review bench still links, or (b) if the implementer finds a reason pub(crate) does NOT work here (verify empirically, this audit did not run cargo per its Shape-3 read-only constraint), leave pub but fix the comment to not claim pub(crate) would fail. Either outcome is acceptable; the goal is comment accuracy, not a specific visibility keyword. Low priority/low value -- bundle with mayor-2zh15's file if convenient, otherwise standalone.

cargo test --workspace and cargo clippy --workspace --tests -- -D warnings must stay green.

Full audit: ai/findings/code-quality-review-2026-07-24.md (Category 3, F3 + F4).

title: quota: ResourceQuota status.used never updated, kubectl describe quota shows stale usage
description:
## Problem

crates/apiserver/src/quota.rs: check_resource_quota() live-counts objects correctly for enforcement but never writes back status.used to the ResourceQuota object. kubectl describe quota always shows 0 used (or last human-written value), breaking observability.

## Implementation shape — IMPORTANT

Do NOT update status.used inline inside check_resource_quota() or from a post-write hook in the handler pipeline. Inline writes from the admission path risk reentrancy (a quota status PUT could itself trigger admission) and produce incorrect results if the CREATE succeeds admission but fails storage.

Instead, implement a background reconciler task in crates/apiserver/src/main.rs following the same pattern as reconcile_kubernetes_endpointslice():
- Spawn a tokio task that periodically (every 30s is fine) iterates all ResourceQuota objects in the store.
- For each quota, live-count the matching resources (reuse the counting logic already in check_resource_quota or extract it into a pure function).
- If status.used differs from the live count, call store.put() with the stored revision (optimistic concurrency — same pattern as the EndpointSlice reconciler after PR #551).
- Wire a shutdown signal via tokio::sync::watch following the same pattern used for the EndpointSlice reconciler.

This is purely observability — enforcement correctness is unchanged. The reconciler runs asynchronously and tolerate a ~30s lag in displayed counts.

## Files
crates/apiserver/src/quota.rs — extract counting logic into a reusable pure function
crates/apiserver/src/main.rs — spawn reconciler task (follow EndpointSlice reconciler pattern)

## Done-when
After creating a pod against a quota, within 30s status.used.pods reflects the live count in the stored ResourceQuota object. Regression test: create a pod, call the reconciler directly (not via the background loop), verify status.used.pods incremented. Shutdown signal wired and tested.
close_reason: count_quota_usage() pure function extracted; background reconciler in main.rs updates status.used every 30s with optimistic concurrency and shutdown signal. 3 regression tests. PR #558.

title: generic: validate_name allows names starting/ending with hyphens or dots for core resources
description:
## Problem

crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs:69-93: validate_name() does not check that the first and last characters are alphanumeric. Names like '-foo', 'foo-', '.bar' pass for all core resources. The real kube-apiserver rejects these with 422. (mayor-f26s covers cr.rs validate_cr_name; this is the shared validate_name used by generic resource handlers.)

## File:line
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/generic.rs:69-93

## Done-when
validate_name checks name[0] and name[len-1] are in [a-z0-9]; returns 400 otherwise. Regression test covers '-foo', 'foo-', 'foo.'.
close_reason: validate_name checks first/last char is [a-z0-9]; 4 regression tests. PR #554.

title: cr: validate_cr_name permits uppercase letters, accepting names kube-apiserver rejects
description:
## Problem

crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:332: validate_cr_name uses is_ascii_alphanumeric() which matches A-Z. CR names like 'MyWidget' pass but real kube-apiserver rejects them with 422 per DNS label rules (lowercase only). Note: mayor-f26s fixes start/end character check but not the uppercase case.

## File:line
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:332

## Done-when
Character check requires only [a-z0-9] for alphanumeric positions. Uppercase names return 422. Regression test covers 'MyWidget' -> 422.
close_reason: validate_cr_name uses is_ascii_lowercase()||is_ascii_digit() blocking uppercase. 2 regression tests. PR #554.

title: cr: validate_cr_name allows names starting/ending with hyphen or dot
description:
## Problem

crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:324-339: the implementation only checks that all characters are [a-zA-Z0-9.-]. Names like '-foo', 'foo-', '.bar', 'bar.' pass validation. The real kube-apiserver rejects these with 422 Unprocessable Entity per DNS label rules.

## File:line
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/cr.rs:324-339

## Done-when
Validation checks that name[0] and name[len-1] are alphanumeric; returns 422 otherwise. Regression test added.
close_reason: validate_cr_name checks first/last char is [a-z0-9]; 3 regression tests. PR #554.

title: pods: merge_conditions ignores $patch:delete directive
description:
## Problem

crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:1506-1544: merge_conditions() does not check for the '$patch: delete' strategic-merge directive. A PATCH with {type: Ready, $patch: delete} stores the literal $patch key inside the condition object rather than removing the condition.

## File:line
crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs:1506-1544

## Done-when
merge_conditions checks for $patch == 'delete' on a condition entry and removes the matching condition by type rather than merging it.
close_reason: merge_conditions checks $patch==delete, retains matching condition by type removal. 1 regression test. PR #555.

title: refactor: type SecretData in controller-manager SA token construction
description: controller-manager/src/lib.rs constructs kubernetes.io/service-account-token Secrets via serde_json::json!() macro (write-only, no field reads). A typo produces wrong field names in the stored Secret silently. Low urgency today (no internal consumer reads these fields back), but introduce typed SecretData { token: String } and ServiceAccountTokenSecret struct for correctness. Promote to higher priority if pod token injection is added.
close_reason: implemented: typed SecretData in controller-manager. PR #158 merged 2026-05-22.
